programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the practical evidence problem is that school assessment calendars differ widely between British-curriculum schools, so one child's mock is another child's ordinary week. That makes internally generated evidence, marked by the tutor against the published descriptors, more reliable for month-to-month comparison than school marks, which arrive on the school's timetable rather than yours.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE History (0470/0977)
programmes.description: The alternative route in the UAE. Content overlaps heavily, but paper structure and source question conventions differ enough that a mark gained on one board's paper is not evidence of readiness for the other. If evidence is the point, the paper it came from has to match the entry.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai families often hold mixed revision material because children move schools inside the city. Before trusting any mark as evidence, check that the practice paper carried the same code as the entry. A strong score on the wrong board's paper is the most misleading single document in a Dubai student's folder.

programmes.name: A Level and IB Diploma history after Year 11
programmes.description: Both post-16 routes raise the writing demand sharply and both assess extended independent work. The evidence habits built at IGCSE transfer directly: a student who is used to receiving a band and a single change to make will handle Diploma or A Level feedback far better than one used to being told it was fine.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Year 11 students choose between the two routes in the spring term, and the choice is better made on evidence than on preference. A student whose source answers have climbed steadily and whose essays still narrate is telling you something useful about which course will suit them, and that pattern is visible in a folder of marked work.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-history-4hi1-home-tu.subjectsIntro: These are the 4HI1 options a Dubai school may enter, described here by the evidence each one produces when it is going well. Your child sits a selected combination.

subjects.name: Germany: development of dictatorship, 1918-45
subjects.description: Progress shows as precision: named legislation and dates appearing in paragraphs that previously said the government. If the reproduced timeline is accurate and the essays still narrate, the problem is structure rather than knowledge.

subjects.name: Russia and the Soviet Union, 1905-24
subjects.description: The clearest early evidence here is a blank-paper timeline with 1905, February 1917 and October 1917 correctly placed. Students who cannot produce that sequence cannot write causation, and the gap is visible in one twelve-minute exercise.

subjects.name: The USA, 1918-41
subjects.description: Watch for the shift from listing New Deal agencies to assessing their effect. That single change usually moves a band, and it is easy to see in two marked essays side by side without knowing the period.

subjects.name: Colonial rule and the nationalist challenge in India, 1919-47
subjects.description: Frequently entered in UAE schools. Progress shows as the student weighing competing pressures on British policy rather than recounting campaigns, and as named legislation replacing general description of unrest.

subjects.name: Changes in medicine, c1848-c1948
subjects.description: A development study where the measurable improvement is argument about the pace of change. An essay that opens by claiming something about speed or cause of change is already in a different band from one that opens with a discovery.

subjects.name: South Africa: union to the end of apartheid, 1948-94
subjects.description: Source-rich, so the early evidence tends to appear in utility judgements before it appears in essays. A student distinguishing phases of resistance rather than treating it as one movement is the signal to look for.

subjects.name: A world divided: superpower relations, 1943-72
subjects.description: Progress is visible as restraint: answering a question about one crisis with one crisis. If marked essays still import three, the issue is question focus, which is a planning problem and fixable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: The origins and course of the First World War, 1905-18
subjects.description: Breadth evidence means comparison across years. A marked answer that cites 1905, 1914 and 1917 to argue about change is scoring differently from one that explains 1914 thoroughly, whatever the content quality.

subjects.name: The changing nature of warfare, 1919-1991
subjects.description: Look for secure examples from at least three distinct conflicts and for an argument about continuity as well as change. The continuity half is the one most candidates never produce, and its appearance is a reliable progress marker.

subjects.name: The Middle East: conflict, crisis and change, 1917-2012
subjects.description: Commonly entered in UAE schools and the option where students arrive with the most prior opinion. Progress shows as attributed specifics replacing general assertion, which a parent can check by looking for names and dates in the paragraphs.

subjects.name: Source investigation skills
subjects.description: The most measurable part of the course. Three things either appear in an answer or do not: the enquiry named, the provenance used, and a judgement about usefulness. A tick against each, session by session, is a progress record on its own.

subjects.name: Extended writing and timing
subjects.description: Measured by band on a marked essay and by the per-question timing log from a full paper. These two numbers, tracked monthly, carry more information about an IGCSE history grade than any report comment.

sections.heading: What a tutor leaves behind, and why that is the thing to compare
paragraphs: Parents choosing between an in-home tutor and an online one usually compare the wrong attribute. Presence is easy to verify and tells you almost nothing. Output is harder to insist on and tells you everything. So the first question to put to any provider in Dubai, before rates or availability, is what document exists at the end of each hour, and whether you will be sent it without asking.

For history the answer can be concrete, because the subject produces writing. A session that worked ends with an extended answer or source answer that has been marked, with the band identified, with annotations showing where the band was lost, and with one named change for next time. That artefact is comparable across weeks, survives a change of tutor, and can be read by a parent who last studied history at school. A verbal summary at the front door has none of those properties.

There is one honest point in favour of the visit. A younger or more easily distracted student sometimes works better with an adult physically present, and some households want the reassurance of seeing the lesson happen. Those are real reasons, and neither is about history. If they decide it for your family, choose the visit with your eyes open and then insist on the written output anyway, because the tutor who cannot produce a band against the descriptors is the problem whichever room they are sitting in.

sections.heading: The four measurements that show a 4HI1 grade actually moving
paragraphs: Four numbers are enough. The first is the band of a marked extended answer, judged against the published descriptors rather than against a percentage. Bands move in steps, and a step is unambiguous: it means the answer did something it previously did not, usually reach a judgement or sustain an argument. The second is the per-question timing log from a full paper, which exposes the most common hidden failure in this subject, namely a final answer half the length of the first.

The third is retrieval, measured by blank-paper reproduction. Ask the student to reproduce a one-page timeline for an entered option from memory in twelve minutes, then count the gaps against the original. This is the only one of the four a parent can administer personally without knowing the period, and it is the quickest way to tell whether a student's knowledge is retrievable or merely familiar. The fourth is the position of each weakness on the ranked list drawn up in the first session, revisited at half term.

What makes these four work together is that they fail differently. A band can rise because the student wrote about a topic they happen to know well. A timing log can improve because the paper was easier. Retrieval can be strong while the writing stays narrative. The ranked list can move because a weakness was avoided rather than fixed. Taken individually, each is gameable. Taken together over two months, they are difficult to fake, and the pattern across them tells you whether to continue, change the plan or stop.

sections.heading: Reading a marked 4HI1 script when you never studied history
paragraphs: You do not need the period knowledge to audit the writing, because the descriptors reward structural moves that are visible to anyone. Read the first sentence of each paragraph. If those sentences are claims, the essay is arguing. If they are dates or events, the essay is narrating, and narration caps the band however accurate the content. That single check takes thirty seconds and identifies the most common reason a Dubai history script sits in the middle.

Then read the final paragraph and ask whether it decides anything. A judgement is a sentence that states which factor mattered most, or how far a statement holds, in terms the question used. A summary of both sides is not a judgement, and its absence is the second most common capped mark. If the last paragraph restates the introduction, the answer has stopped short of the band the student was capable of.

For a source answer, look for three things in order: is the enquiry named in the opening sentence, is the provenance used rather than merely stated, and does the answer say what the source is useful for and what it cannot show. Each of those either appears or does not. Ticking three boxes per source answer, week by week, produces a progress record that requires no subject knowledge at all, and it is more informative than most school report comments.

None of this makes you the marker, and it is not meant to. It makes you able to ask one precise question at the review: the first sentences are still dates rather than claims, so what is the plan for that. A tutor who can answer that question concretely is doing the work. A tutor who answers that your child is making good progress and enjoys the sessions has told you what the term will produce.
bullets: Read the first sentence of each paragraph: claim or date?
Read the last paragraph: does it decide, or does it summarise?
In a source answer, is the enquiry named in the first sentence?
Is provenance used to judge, or only described?
Are people, laws and bodies named, or referred to generally?

sections.heading: What the first eight weeks should actually produce
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the right review horizon for a history grade, and the artefacts should arrive on a predictable schedule rather than in a rush before the review. The purpose of fixing this in advance is that it removes the awkward conversation in week seven: either the documents exist or they do not, and the decision to continue is made on the file rather than on goodwill.

The sequence below is what we commit to, and it is deliberately front-loaded. The diagnosis arrives in week one because everything else is calibrated against it. The three artefacts per option come next, written by the student rather than supplied, because a timeline a tutor hands over proves nothing about retrieval. Marked essays begin from week four, when there is a plan to mark against, and the first timed paper sits at week seven so that the eight-week review has a timing log in it.

If a provider cannot describe their equivalent of this schedule before you pay, that is informative. The common pattern in this market is a strong first session followed by a drift into content coverage with no written output, which feels productive and leaves nothing to judge. Insisting on the schedule up front costs a parent one email and converts the eight-week review from an impression into a reading of documents.

Two things will disrupt the schedule legitimately, and both should be planned for in week one rather than treated as failures in week five. School assessment weeks absorb the student's writing capacity, so the session in such a week is better spent reading the school's own marked script than adding to it. And Ramadan shifts the evening, so the slot moves to a post-Iftar time by agreement. Neither changes the artefact list; both change which week each artefact lands in.

sections.heading: Signals that look like progress and are not
paragraphs: Confidence is the first false signal. A student who has spent six hours with an engaging tutor talking about the Middle East will feel better about the Middle East, and feeling better is not a band. We have seen scripts unchanged in structure after a term of enjoyable sessions, which is a teaching failure rather than a student one, and it is invisible unless somebody is marking.

The second is familiarity dressed as mastery. Rereading notes produces recognition, and recognition collapses under exam pressure. This is why the retrieval check matters: a student who insists they know the period and cannot reproduce fifteen anchor dates on blank paper is telling you something true about their revision method. The third is mock inflation, where a score rises because the paper was the one the class had already worked through, or because the marking was generous relative to the descriptors.

The fourth is the predicted grade, and it deserves a blunt sentence. A tutor cannot predict a 4HI1 grade and should not offer one. What a tutor can say is which band an answer currently reaches and what would move it. Any provider showing you a satisfaction percentage, a success rate or a proportion of students achieving a grade owes you the sample size, the date and the method on the same page, and in this market that information is almost never supplied.

The fifth is volume. A folder thick with completed past papers looks like diligence and frequently records nothing, because self-marking rewards content and the descriptors reward structure. Four papers marked properly against the descriptors, with one answer rewritten afterwards, carry more information and more improvement than a dozen sat casually. Ask how many of the papers in the folder were marked by somebody other than the student.

sections.heading: Why evidence, not proximity, should pick your 4HI1 tutor
paragraphs: 4HI1 schools choose which depth and breadth studies they teach, so the single most useful attribute in a history tutor is having taught your child's entered options. The second is being able to mark extended writing against the descriptors in a way you can read. Neither of those attributes correlates with living near your community, and the in-home filter removes most of the people who have both.

Work through the arithmetic. Start with history tutors available in Dubai, narrow to those with Edexcel rather than Cambridge experience, narrow again to those who have taught the entered periods, then to those free at seven on a Tuesday. Finally narrow to those willing to drive to your community in exam-term traffic. The last filter has no educational content, and it is usually the one that eliminates the specialist, leaving a capable generalist whom families later describe as fine.

Online delivery also makes a wrong match survivable, which is an evidence argument rather than a convenience one. A mismatch discovered in week three costs three weeks if another tutor can take the same hour, and costs a term if the replacement has to live nearby. Because the diagnosis and the marked file transfer with the student, a new tutor starts from the ranked weakness list rather than from scratch. That continuity is impossible to replicate when the binding constraint is who will make the drive.

There is a version of the in-home argument we accept, and it is worth naming rather than arguing past. A student who will not sit down without an adult in the room is a real phenomenon, and for that student presence is doing something teaching cannot. Even then, insist on the marked answer and the band, because the attendance problem and the writing problem are separate and only one of them is solved by a tutor arriving at the door.

sections.heading: Who is teaching your child, and how to verify it
paragraphs: Evidence about the work is one half; evidence about the person is the other. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service via its smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you see quoted on a tutoring site as unsourced. Separately, a tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, renewed annually. IB Gram claims no regulator approval of any kind and you should be sceptical of any provider that does.

One boundary is worth stating because families sometimes see it as a shortcut. Do not arrange for your child's own school history teacher to tutor them privately. The permit carries a code of conduct addressing tutors serving students affiliated with their own school, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Beyond the rules, the person marking the school assessment should not also be paid to prepare the student for it, because it destroys the independence of exactly the evidence this page is about.
bullets: Ask the tutor directly about their MoHRE private tuition work permit
Ask which entered options they have taught and in which series
Ask for one marked answer with its band before you commit a term
Avoid any arrangement involving your child's own class teacher

sections.heading: When the evidence says continue, change or stop
paragraphs: Continue when the band has stepped on two different questions, the timing log shows the final answer holding up, and the week-one weakness has dropped out of the top three. That is tuition working, and the sensible next move is to keep the rhythm and let the plan run to the next review rather than adding hours.

Change the plan when the measurements disagree with each other. Strong retrieval with narrative essays means the work should shift to structure and planning. Good structure with weak retrieval means the artefacts are not being rehearsed and the between-session task needs rewriting. Rising essay bands with flat source answers means the source checks are not being drilled separately, which is a specific fix rather than a general effort problem.

Stop when nothing has moved in eight weeks despite the documents existing. That is a genuine outcome and we will say it rather than sell another term. Sometimes the right answer is a different tutor, sometimes a different subject deserves the slot more, and occasionally the honest answer is that the student needs a term of ordinary school work and sleep rather than more tuition. A provider who cannot describe the conditions under which they would recommend stopping has told you how they intend to handle your eight-week review.

Timing matters in the decision as much as the evidence does. A flat eight weeks in Year 10 is cheap information and leaves plenty of time to act on it. The same eight weeks ending in March of Year 11 is expensive, which is the practical case for starting the measurement early rather than waiting for a mock to raise the alarm. Families who run the first review in the autumn term almost always have more options than those who begin after the mocks.

process.title: Send one marked essay and one source answer
process.description: Two documents, both marked by the school if possible. They separate a narrative-structure problem from a source-technique problem, and those two have different remedies, different costs and different timescales. The school's latest report comment helps but is the weaker signal.

process.title: Get the entered options in writing
process.description: Email the humanities lead for the depth studies, the breadth study and the exam series. Without that list no mark means anything, because a strong score on a period your child will not sit is the most misleading document in the folder.

process.title: Take a first session and keep the diagnosis
process.description: One session per student at no charge, ending in a ranked weakness list and one annotated answer with its band. That document is the baseline for every later comparison, so file it rather than reading it once.

process.title: Agree the artefact schedule before paying
process.description: Which document arrives in which week across the first eight weeks. Ask any provider for their version in writing. The answer, or the absence of one, tells you how the eight-week review is going to go.

process.title: Review on the four measurements at week eight
process.description: Band, timing log, retrieval count, weakness rank. Continue, change the plan or stop, decided on the file rather than on how the sessions felt. We will recommend stopping when the evidence says so.

whyPoints.title: A document after every session, by default
whyPoints.description: An annotated answer, a mark, a band and the one change that would move it. Not on request, not at half term, and not as a verbal summary. That artefact is what makes a parent's supervision possible without subject knowledge.

whyPoints.title: Measurements that fail differently
whyPoints.description: Band, timing, retrieval and weakness rank are each gameable alone and hard to fake together. Reporting all four is a deliberate constraint on us as much as a service to you, because it leaves nowhere for a flat eight weeks to hide.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the entered options
whyPoints.description: Because 4HI1 schools choose their periods, a general history tutor can be good and still not have taught what your child sits. Tutors state plainly which options they have taught, and we will not describe a generalist as an option specialist.

whyPoints.title: Honest about delivery
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one to one and online over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; that service exists only in India. Several providers in this market leave that question unanswered until a parent has paid.

whyPoints.title: Continuity when a tutor changes
whyPoints.description: The diagnosis and the marked file belong to the student, so a replacement tutor starts from the ranked weakness list rather than from scratch. With an in-home arrangement, a change of tutor usually means a change of method as well.

whyPoints.title: We will tell you to stop
whyPoints.description: If eight weeks of documents show no movement, the recommendation is to change the tutor, change the subject or stop, and we would rather say it than sell another term. No predicted grades, no satisfaction statistics, no guarantees.

faqs.question: Can we hire a home tutor in Dubai for Edexcel IGCSE History 4HI1?
faqs.answer: In-home history tuition is advertised widely in Dubai by independent tutors and by agencies that place them, so the market exists. IB Gram is not part of it: we do not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, and home visits are a service we run only in India. What we provide to Dubai families is one-to-one online tuition over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For 4HI1 that trade is favourable, because the tutor can be chosen for having taught your child's entered options rather than for driving distance.

faqs.question: How do I know the tutoring is working before the next school report arrives?
faqs.answer: By tracking four things monthly: the band of a marked extended answer against the published descriptors, the per-question timing log from a full paper, the number of gaps when your child reproduces an option timeline from blank paper, and the position of the week-one weakness on the ranked list. The first and second come from the tutor, the third you can run yourself in twelve minutes, and the fourth is a comparison against the first session. None requires you to know any history. Together, over eight weeks, they are difficult to fake.

faqs.question: What document should arrive after each paid history session?
faqs.answer: An extended answer or source answer that has been marked, with the band identified, annotations showing where the band was lost, and one named change for next time. Not a verbal summary at the door, and not a message saying the session went well. In a written subject the artefact costs the tutor nothing extra, because marking is the teaching. If a provider treats written output as an optional extra, that tells you what the eight-week review will look like.

faqs.question: My daughter says the sessions are going brilliantly. Is that evidence?
faqs.answer: It is worth having and it is not evidence of movement. A student who spends six hours with an engaging tutor on an interesting period will feel better about that period, and feeling better is not a band. We have seen scripts unchanged in structure after a term of thoroughly enjoyable sessions, which is a teaching failure rather than a student one. Enjoyment keeps a teenager turning up, which matters. Judge the tuition on the marked work, and keep the enjoyment as the reason the marked work keeps arriving.

faqs.question: Should I trust a predicted grade from a private tutor?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor cannot predict an IGCSE history grade and should not offer one, because the grade depends on the paper sat, the cohort and the boundaries set afterwards. What a tutor can legitimately state is which band an answer currently reaches against the published descriptors and what would move it. If a provider shows you a success rate, a satisfaction percentage or a proportion of students achieving a particular grade, ask for the sample size, the date and the method. In this market that information is almost never available.

faqs.question: How long before a 4HI1 grade actually moves?
faqs.answer: Structural work shows in marked bands within four to six weeks, because fixing narrative paragraphs and a missing judgement changes every extended answer at once. Retrieval takes longer, perhaps eight to twelve weeks, because it depends on the student rehearsing artefacts rather than on the tutor teaching. Content gaps take a term. This is why the diagnosis matters: it tells you which of the three you are buying, and therefore when to review. Eight weeks is the right first horizon, with one review at week four to check the documents are arriving.

faqs.question: What does a band on a marked essay tell me if I never studied history?
faqs.answer: More than a percentage does. Bands are defined by what an answer does rather than by how much it contains, so a band step means the writing performed a move it previously did not, usually sustaining an argument or reaching a judgement. You can audit it yourself: read the first sentence of every paragraph and check whether each is a claim or a date, then read the final paragraph and check whether it decides anything. Those two checks take under a minute and identify the commonest reason a Dubai script sits mid-paper.

faqs.question: Is a better mock score real progress or just a familiar paper?
faqs.answer: Ask which paper it was. A score that rises on a paper the class has already worked through measures familiarity, and self-marked practice inflates for the same reason: students mark content and descriptors mark structure. Real movement shows up on an unseen paper, marked by someone against the published descriptors, with a timing log attached. If a mock improvement cannot be reproduced on a fresh question from the same option, treat it as encouraging rather than conclusive and keep the review date where it was.

faqs.question: Do tutors come to houses in Dubai for IGCSE history lessons?
faqs.answer: Independent tutors and agencies do offer that in Dubai, and the rates reflect the travel. IB Gram does not: there are no home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE, and that service exists only in India. Our sessions are one to one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. The practical gain is that the screen share puts the marked essay, the descriptors and the source booklet in front of both people at once, which is awkward with one paper copy between two heads at a dining table.

faqs.question: How many sessions before we should expect something in writing?
faqs.answer: One. The first session should end with a ranked weakness list and one annotated answer carrying its band, and that document is the baseline every later comparison is made against. Weeks two and three should produce essay plans and the student's first timeline page. Marked essays start from week four, when there is a plan to mark against, and the first timed paper sits at week seven so the eight-week review has a timing log in it. Ask any provider for their version of that schedule before paying.

faqs.question: Can we see the mark scheme the tutor is marking against?
faqs.answer: You should see how the descriptors are being applied, and a tutor should be able to walk you through why an answer sits in one band rather than the next. What no provider should do is reproduce or supply board documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads, because those are the board's copyright and the correct practice is to reference and link the official source. Ask the tutor to show the reasoning on your child's own script; that is more useful than a document and it is the thing you are paying for.

faqs.question: What if the evidence shows no movement after eight weeks?
faqs.answer: Then the plan changes or the tuition stops, and we will say which we think it is. The diagnostic question is whether the measurements disagree. Strong retrieval with narrative essays means the work should shift to structure. Good structure with weak retrieval means the between-session task is not being done and needs rewriting. Flat on everything, with the documents existing, usually means a different tutor or a different subject deserves the slot. A provider who cannot describe when they would recommend stopping has answered a different question.

faqs.question: Who will actually be teaching my child, and can we meet them first?
faqs.answer: You meet the tutor in the first session, which is one per student at no charge, and the person who teaches that session is the person who continues. Ask them which specification and which entered options they have taught, in which series, and whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is granted free of charge for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. If the match is wrong, say so and we propose someone else, and the diagnosis from the first session transfers to them.

faqs.question: Can we pause the sessions during mock weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and often you should. Mock weeks and school assessment weeks are not revision weeks, and a schedule that treats them as though they were is the commonest reason a plan slips by a fortnight. The useful pattern is to pause teaching during the week itself and bring the mock script to the next session, where it becomes the most valuable single piece of evidence available: a full paper, marked by someone else, under timed conditions. Ramadan is handled the same way, with sessions moved to post-Iftar slots by prior agreement.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-history-4hi1-tutor.tutorsIntro: These tutors work on Pearson Edexcel International GCSE History and the humanities subjects beside it. They are matched to the depth and breadth studies your child's school actually entered, which in this subject is the difference between useful help and general interest.

intro.heading: History rewards a planned argument, and most mid-paper scripts contain an unplanned one
paragraphs: Families looking for an Edexcel IGCSE History 4HI1 tutor in Dubai usually arrive with a specific frustration. Their child reads widely, remembers a great deal, talks about the material with genuine interest, and scores in the middle of the paper. The marked script tells you why within a minute. The essays run chronologically rather than analytically, the source answers describe what a source says rather than judging what it is worth, and the final paragraph summarises instead of deciding. None of that is a knowledge problem, which is why it responds quickly to the right work.

The first thing an honest tutor establishes is which options your child is sitting. Paper 1 is built on depth studies and Paper 2 on a source investigation and a breadth study in change, and schools choose from a bank of options: Germany 1918-45, Russia and the Soviet Union 1905-24, the USA 1918-41, colonial rule and the nationalist challenge in India 1919-47, changes in medicine, South Africa, superpower relations, and breadth studies on the First World War, the changing nature of warfare, the Middle East 1917-2012 and China 1900-89. Confirm the entry with the school before anyone teaches anything.

Tuition for Dubai families is delivered one to one and online, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India. For history that arrangement is an advantage rather than a concession, because option coverage is the scarce resource. The tutor who has taught the India depth study and the Middle East breadth study is not usually the tutor who lives near your community, and over a screen share the marked essay, the source booklet and the mark scheme are visible to both people at once.

Dubai adds two practical pressures worth naming early. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in all private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, so a Year 11 week here carries more compulsory content than the equivalent British timetable. And history, being an optional humanity, is usually the subject whose independent writing time disappears first when a timetable is full. A plan that assumes four free evenings a week will not survive to half term in this city.

What follows is written to be used rather than admired. It sets out the option combinations Dubai schools enter and what each demands, the three-minute essay plan we drill until it is automatic, the source moves that separate a middling answer from a strong one, the small body of knowledge that has to be retrievable rather than recognisable, the Pearson calendar counted backwards, and the line a tutor may not cross with work a student submits.

programmes.name: Where 4HI1 history leads after Year 11

dubai/edexcel-igcse-history-4hi1-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the 4HI1 options a Dubai student may meet, with what each one actually demands. Your child will sit a selected combination; the two skills rows at the end apply to every entry.

subjects.name: Germany: development of dictatorship, 1918-45
subjects.description: Dense on political detail and heavily populated with dates. Strong candidates distinguish consolidation from seizure of power; weaker ones narrate the 1930s. The commonest lost mark is treating every event as inevitable rather than contingent.

subjects.name: Russia and the Soviet Union, 1905-24
subjects.description: Two revolutions, a civil war and a new state in under twenty years, which makes chronology the main failure point. Students who can place 1905, February 1917 and October 1917 confidently answer far better than those who revise themes without a timeline.

subjects.name: The USA, 1918-41
subjects.description: Boom, Depression and New Deal, with strong opportunities for causal chains. Marks are lost on the New Deal, where students list agencies instead of assessing effect, and on the 1920s, where social change gets described rather than explained.

subjects.name: Colonial rule and the nationalist challenge in India, 1919-47
subjects.description: Commonly entered in UAE schools because of cohort interest, and commonly over-narrated. The examinable skill is weighing competing pressures on British policy, not recounting the sequence of campaigns. Specific legislation and dates carry real marks here.

subjects.name: Changes in medicine, c1848-c1948
subjects.description: A development study where change over time is the examined concept. Students need to argue about pace and cause of change rather than catalogue discoveries, and the strongest answers connect public health legislation to scientific advance rather than treating them separately.

subjects.name: South Africa: union to the end of apartheid, 1948-94
subjects.description: Rich in source material and in opportunities for judgement on causation of change. Weak answers treat resistance as one continuous movement; strong answers distinguish phases and assess which pressures mattered most at which point.

subjects.name: A world divided: superpower relations, 1943-72
subjects.description: Crisis-driven and well suited to causal analysis. The frequent error is answering a question about one crisis with the story of three. Precision about who acted, when and with what consequence is what the mark scheme rewards.

subjects.name: The origins and course of the First World War, 1905-18
subjects.description: Breadth questions examine change across the period, so a student who revises only 1914 cannot answer them. Comparative judgement across years, not depth in a single year, is the skill being tested.

subjects.name: The changing nature of warfare, 1919-1991
subjects.description: Technology, tactics and the civilian experience across seven decades. Students need secure examples from at least three distinct conflicts and the ability to argue about continuity as well as change, which is the half most candidates neglect.

subjects.name: The Middle East: conflict, crisis and change, 1917-2012
subjects.description: Frequently entered in UAE schools, and the option where students bring the most prior opinion and the least precision. The mark scheme rewards attributed detail and balanced judgement, so the work is sharpening the argument without flattening it.

subjects.name: Source investigation skills
subjects.description: Provenance, content and context, then a judgement about utility for a stated enquiry. The dominant error across Dubai cohorts is describing a source accurately and never answering how useful it is for the specific purpose named in the question.

subjects.name: Extended essay writing and timing
subjects.description: Planning in three minutes, arguing in paragraphs that each advance a claim, and reaching a judgement that refers back to evidence already supplied. This is the most transferable work in the course and typically the fastest grade movement available.

sections.heading: Which options your Dubai school entered, and why nothing starts before you know
paragraphs: 4HI1 is a specification with choices in it. Paper 1 examines depth studies and Paper 2 pairs a source investigation with a breadth study in change, and the school selects which periods it teaches from the bank the specification offers. The consequence in Dubai is that two students in the same compound, both sitting 4HI1 in the same series, can share no examined content at all. One may be examined on Germany and the USA with a First World War breadth study; the other on India and South Africa with the Middle East.

This is why we ask for the entry before anything else. One email to the humanities lead or the exams officer, naming the depth studies and the breadth study, saves the first three sessions. It also prevents the most expensive mistake in this subject, which is buying a revision guide or inheriting a folder for the wrong period. Families routinely spend a term working on content their child will never see on a paper, and the error is invisible until a mock.

Option choice also changes what the tutoring should prioritise. A narrative-heavy depth study such as Russia punishes weak chronology. A development study such as medicine punishes students who catalogue rather than argue about pace of change. A breadth study punishes anyone who revised one year in depth and nothing across the period. sections.heading: The three-minute essay plan, and why it is the highest-value habit in the course
paragraphs: Students resist planning because it feels like writing time surrendered. The fastest way to end that argument is evidence from their own work: two essays on the same question, one planned and one not, marked against the same descriptors. The planned one is almost always a band higher, and it is usually shorter. Examiners reward an argument that advances, and an unplanned essay advances by accident at best.

The plan we teach fits in three minutes and has four moves. Underline the command and the focus in the question, so the answer addresses the actual claim rather than the topic. Decide the judgement first, in six words, because an essay that knows where it is going writes itself in a straighter line. List three paragraph claims that support or qualify that judgement, each with one specific piece of evidence attached. Then write, and keep the judgement in the final paragraph where a marker expects to find it.

Paragraph discipline follows from the plan. Each paragraph should open with a claim rather than a date, supply specific evidence, explain how the evidence supports the claim, and connect back to the question. Students who have never been taught this write chronological paragraphs that begin with when and end with then, which can contain excellent history and still score in the middle band. Rewriting one such paragraph properly in a session teaches more than reading three model answers.

The habit transfers, which is the other reason it is worth drilling early. A Dubai Year 11 sitting history is usually also sitting English and often geography or business studies, and all of them reward the same move: a claim stated, evidence supplied, a link made back to the question. Families who buy four sessions of planning work in Year 10 frequently find the benefit appears in three subjects rather than one, which changes the arithmetic of whether the tuition was worth it.

sections.heading: Source work: judging usefulness instead of retelling content
paragraphs: The single most common capped mark in 4HI1 source answers across Dubai cohorts is the confident description. A student reads the source accurately, explains what it says, notes who wrote it, and never answers the question that was asked, which is how useful the source is for a particular enquiry. Utility is a judgement about fitness for a stated purpose, and it cannot be reached without naming that purpose explicitly in the answer.

We teach it as three separate reads of the same source, done in order, until the sequence is automatic. First the provenance: who produced this, when, for whom, and with what reason to shape it. Second the content: what specific claims does it make that bear on the enquiry. Third the context: what do you know from your own study that corroborates, qualifies or contradicts it. Only then the judgement, which must state what the source is useful for and what it cannot tell you.

The last part is where strong candidates separate themselves. A source with obvious bias is not useless; it is useful evidence of the view it represents, which is a sentence most mid-band answers never write. Equally, limitation is not a ritual apology about one person's opinion. It is a specific statement of what the enquiry still needs and this source does not supply. Students who practise naming that gap stop writing the generic caveat that costs them nothing and earns them nothing.

sections.heading: What a 4HI1 student must be able to retrieve, not merely recognise
paragraphs: Parents often ask how much a history candidate has to memorise, and the honest answer is less than students fear and more specifically than they manage. Recognition is not retrieval. A student who nods at the Enabling Act when they read it but cannot produce the year under exam pressure has knowledge that will not convert into marks. The fix is not more reading. It is a small, structured store, rehearsed by production rather than by review.

We build three artefacts per entered option. A one-page timeline with roughly fifteen anchor dates, which is enough to place any question in sequence. A terminology sheet of maybe twenty terms the mark scheme uses, defined in the student's own words, because precise vocabulary is where examiners see command of a period. And a specifics card of named individuals, named legislation, named organisations and figures where figures matter. Three pages per option, written by the student, rehearsed by covering and reproducing.

Rehearsal is where most revision schedules fail. Rereading a page produces familiarity, which feels like learning and is not. Reproducing a timeline from memory onto blank paper produces retrieval, which is what the exam asks for. Twelve minutes of blank-paper reproduction twice a week per option outperforms an hour of rereading, and students find it faster, which matters when a Dubai Year 11 timetable already runs long.

The artefacts also solve a parental problem, which is knowing whether revision is happening. A page reproduced from memory is visible evidence in a way that an hour in a bedroom is not, and it can be checked by someone who knows no history at all: cover the original, read what the student produced, count the gaps. Parents who ask for one reproduced timeline a week get a reliable progress signal without having to interrogate their child about what they studied.

sections.heading: Marks lost in Dubai history scripts, ranked by what they cost
paragraphs: First and most expensive is the narrative essay. A chronologically organised answer to an analytical question can contain every relevant fact and still sit two bands below its content, because the mark scheme rewards an argument rather than a sequence. This is also the quickest thing to improve, which is why a diagnosis that finds it is good news rather than bad.

Second is the missing judgement. Students weigh two positions carefully and then stop, or summarise both in a closing paragraph that decides nothing. Third is the described source, discussed above. Fourth is the unfinished paper: across marked scripts we see, the final extended answer is frequently much shorter than the first, which is a timing problem masquerading as a knowledge gap. Fifth is imprecision, where a student writes the government or the nationalists instead of naming who acted.

A sixth pattern belongs specifically to transfers, and Dubai sees many. A student who studied history under another board or in another country often has strong content in the wrong shape: Cambridge-style structures for an Edexcel paper, or inquiry-led paragraphs from a middle-years programme. That student needs translating rather than teaching, and one marked essay shows precisely which habits transfer and which have to be retired before the mocks.

The ranking matters because it dictates sequence. Fixing narrative structure and the missing judgement costs four to six sessions and lifts every extended answer on both papers. Fixing imprecision costs a term, because it means rebuilding the specifics cards. A family told to start with content teaching when the diagnosis says structure is paying for the slow repair before the fast one, and in a Year 11 that is the difference between a grade moving before the mocks and a grade moving after the papers are sat.

sections.heading: The Pearson calendar counted backwards from the written papers
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so build any plan against the live timetable on qualifications.pearson.com rather than a date copied from a tutoring page.

Counting backwards rather than forwards is what makes a plan survive. A forward plan covers content and then discovers that the practice which converts content into marks has nowhere to go. A backward plan forces the uncomfortable decision in week twelve: which entered option gets deep work and which gets consolidation only. Parents sometimes dislike making that choice early, and it is still better made in week twelve than discovered in a mock.

Two Dubai-specific adjustments. Mock weeks and school assessment weeks are not revision weeks, and treating them as such is the commonest reason a schedule slips by a fortnight. And Ramadan changes the rhythm of the UAE working day, with families routinely moving sessions to post-Iftar slots. If the exam term overlaps Ramadan in a given year, place timed full papers outside the heaviest weeks and keep those weeks for lighter consolidation.

One further note on retakes, because families ask after results rather than before. The gap between a results date and the next available entry deadline is short, and the decision is usually made in the fortnight after results arrive. Knowing the published pattern in advance makes that fortnight calmer: results reach students in late August for a June series and in January for a November one, and the entry for the following series closes months ahead of the papers themselves.

sections.heading: KHDA, Social Studies and the Dubai Year 11 timetable
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. For a parent choosing history support, the inspection report is worth reading for one narrow reason: it describes how the school's provision was judged. It says nothing about any individual tutor, and no tutoring provider can hold a KHDA endorsement.

The rule that shapes the week is the mandatory subject requirement. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, and schools may vary lesson length provided total weekly time is met.

Parents sometimes assume UAE Social Studies overlaps usefully with IGCSE History. It does not, in examinable terms. Social Studies follows a Ministry-set curriculum, and for the mandatory subjects the use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is prohibited, so it is not a place to practise 4HI1 essay technique. The overlap is in time rather than content: both subjects want writing hours from the same student in the same week. Planning as if the Year 11 week looks like a British one is how a good schedule quietly fails.

sections.heading: Equivalency, academic honesty, and what to ask before paying for a term
paragraphs: Equivalency decides which IGCSE results count later, and the British-track rule is published. The Ministry of Education requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among those five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. History counts as one of the accredited subjects. Verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae, because this is the authority's process and not something a tutoring provider performs or guarantees.

On academic honesty the boundary is simple and we state it rather than imply it. A tutor teaches, questions, demonstrates on other material and gives feedback on a draft the student has already produced. A tutor does not supply sentences for submission or restructure a submitted piece on the student's behalf. Everything a student hands in is theirs. That protects the candidate, who is the person a board would penalise, and it is a genuine point of difference in a market where at least one operator sells completed assessed work outright.

Which leaves the five questions worth asking any history tutor in this market. Which specification and which options have you taught, and in which series. Can you mark one extended answer against the descriptors while I watch. What arrives in writing after each session. What happens if no specialist in our entered options is free at our hour. And do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is the permit an individual tutoring in the UAE needs.
bullets: Ask for specification code and entered options, not just the subject
Ask to watch one extended answer marked against the descriptors
Ask what written evidence arrives after every session
Ask about the MoHRE private tuition work permit
Verify equivalency rules on moe.gov.ae, not on a tutoring page

process.title: Send two marked essays
process.description: The two most recent marked extended answers, plus the school's latest report comment on history. Two scripts separate a narrative-structure problem from a content gap from a timing problem, and those three have completely different remedies and completely different costs.

process.title: Confirm the entered options
process.description: Email the humanities lead for the depth studies, the breadth study and the exam series. In a specification with school-chosen periods, this is the most valuable single piece of information a parent can obtain, and it takes a day.

process.title: Take a first session with an option specialist
process.description: One session per student at no charge, in which the tutor marks an extended answer with your child and produces a written diagnosis ranking the weaknesses. If the match is wrong, we propose someone else rather than defending the first choice.

process.title: Fix the slot and the weekly writing task
process.description: One recurring online slot in Gulf Standard Time, agreed around school, activities and prayer times, plus one three-minute essay plan or one source answer between sessions. The between-session task is what makes the hour compound rather than reset.

process.title: Review on marked bands at half term
process.description: Compare the ranked weakness list from the first session against current marked work. If the top item has not moved, the plan changes. That is the review that decides whether the tutoring has earned its continuation.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the entered options
whyPoints.description: Because 4HI1 schools choose their periods, a general history tutor can be excellent and still not have taught what your child sits. Tutors are matched to the entered depth and breadth studies, and will say plainly which periods they have not taught.

whyPoints.title: Marked writing, every session
whyPoints.description: You receive the annotated answer, the mark, the band and the single change that would move it. In an essay subject that is the only progress signal available before a report arrives, and a parent who does not teach history can still read a band moving.

whyPoints.title: Honest about delivery
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one to one and online over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; that service exists only in India. Stating it here is more useful than letting a search term imply something we do not sell.

whyPoints.title: Technique before content, when the diagnosis says so
whyPoints.description: Most capped history grades are writing problems rather than knowledge problems, and four to six sessions on planning and source utility often buys more than a term of content teaching. We will recommend the cheaper option when it is the right one.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty stated as a boundary
whyPoints.description: Teaching, questioning and feedback on the student's own work. Nothing a student submits is supplied by a tutor. In a market where completed assessed work is openly sold, this is worth putting in writing rather than assuming.

whyPoints.title: No guarantees and no invented numbers
whyPoints.description: No promised grade, no claim of regulator or board endorsement, no satisfaction statistic without a sample size, a date and a method. If no specialist in your entered options is free at your hour, you are told before you commit.

faqs.question: What does an Edexcel IGCSE History 4HI1 tutor in Dubai do in the first fortnight?
faqs.answer: Session one marks a recent extended answer with your child and ranks the weaknesses, which usually produces a short, uncomfortable list. Session two teaches the three-minute essay plan and applies it to a question from an entered option, then rewrites one paragraph properly. Between the two, we confirm the entered depth and breadth studies with the school. You should finish the fortnight holding a written diagnosis, one rewritten paragraph and a clear statement of which option gets deep work. Content teaching begins after that, because before it the teaching is guesswork.

faqs.question: My son knows a great deal of history but his essays score in the middle. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly because the essays are organised chronologically rather than analytically. An answer that moves through events in order can contain every relevant fact and still sit two bands below its content, because the descriptors reward an argument that advances and a judgement a marker can find. The remedy is structural and fast: decide the judgement in six words before writing, open each paragraph with a claim instead of a date, and put the judgement in the final paragraph. Students usually move a band within a month of weekly practice on this alone.

faqs.question: How many dates does a 4HI1 candidate actually need to hold in their head?
faqs.answer: Fewer than students fear, but they must be retrievable rather than merely recognisable. We build roughly fifteen anchor dates per entered option on a single page, enough to place any question in sequence, alongside about twenty mark-scheme terms and a card of named people, laws and bodies. The rehearsal method matters more than the quantity: reproducing the timeline onto blank paper for twelve minutes twice a week beats an hour of rereading, because the exam asks for production and rereading only produces familiarity.

faqs.question: Which depth and breadth studies do Dubai schools usually enter for 4HI1?
faqs.answer: It varies by department specialism, which is exactly why you have to ask. Across UAE schools the commonly seen depth studies include Germany 1918-45, Russia and the Soviet Union 1905-24, the USA 1918-41 and colonial rule and the nationalist challenge in India 1919-47, with breadth studies on the First World War, the changing nature of warfare, the Middle East 1917-2012 and China 1900-89. Two students in the same Dubai community can share no examined content. One email to the humanities lead settles it in a day and saves three sessions.

faqs.question: What is the difference between describing a source and using it?
faqs.answer: Describing tells the examiner what the source says. Using it answers how useful it is for the specific enquiry the question names. A full answer reads the source three times in order: provenance, who made it, when and with what reason to shape it; content, the specific claims that bear on the enquiry; and context, what your own knowledge corroborates or contradicts. Then it judges, stating what the source is useful for and what the enquiry still needs. A biased source is useful evidence of the view it represents, which most mid-band answers never say.

faqs.question: How many essays a week should a Dubai Year 11 history student be writing?
faqs.answer: One properly marked extended answer a week is more useful than three written casually and never read closely. The value sits in the marking and the rewrite, not in the volume. Our usual rhythm is one full essay a fortnight plus one three-minute plan in the alternate week, rising to one essay a week across the final six weeks. In a Dubai timetable that already carries Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the IGCSE options, a plan that demands three essays a week will be abandoned by half term.

faqs.question: Does Dubai's mandatory Social Studies requirement overlap with Edexcel IGCSE History?
faqs.answer: Not in examinable terms. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, and for those mandatory subjects the use of different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is prohibited, so Social Studies is not a place to practise 4HI1 technique. The real overlap is in time: both subjects want writing hours from the same student in the same week, and instructional time for the mandatory subjects is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. Plan the history schedule around a fuller week than a British timetable.

faqs.question: Is Edexcel 4HI1 harder than the Cambridge IGCSE history route?
faqs.answer: Neither is harder in the abstract; they reward different preparation. The papers differ in structure, in how source questions are framed and in the position of coursework, so a student revising from Cambridge material for an Edexcel entry writes historically sound answers in a format the mark scheme does not reward. That mismatch is common in Dubai because families move between schools inside the city and inherit material. The code on the exam entry slip is the one that matters, and a tutor should be able to tell you which code they have taught.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a history coursework task the school has set?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the skills it requires, question the student's reasoning, demonstrate technique on different material and give feedback on a draft the student has already produced. A tutor cannot supply sentences for submission or restructure the piece on the student's behalf. Whatever is handed in has to be the student's own. That boundary protects your child, because a board penalises the candidate rather than the tutor, and it is worth stating plainly in a market where at least one provider sells completed assessed work.

faqs.question: Should my daughter sit 4HI1 in the November series if she is behind?
faqs.answer: It depends whether the extra months buy teaching or only more revision. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. The cost is timing: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which matters if a sixth-form place depends on them. Entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers, so this is a decision for the school and the exams officer, taken against the live timetable on the board's own site.

faqs.question: Which five IGCSE subjects count for UAE equivalency, and does history qualify?
faqs.answer: For the British track the Ministry of Education requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. History counts as one of the accredited subjects. The same route also requires one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject figure; the sourced rule is five. Verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae before relying on it.

faqs.question: My child runs out of time before the last extended answer. How is that fixed?
faqs.answer: By budgeting time against marks and fixing question order before the exam, then rehearsing both under a clock. The usual cause is over-writing the first answer, which leaves ten minutes for one worth far more. We log per-question timing on practice papers so the pattern is visible rather than asserted, then set a rule: planning time ring-fenced for the extended answers, nothing spent beyond the tariff on short ones, and a hard stop that forces the final answer to be started. Three timed papers normally shift it, because it is a habit.

faqs.question: What should we ask a 4HI1 tutor before paying for a term?
faqs.answer: Five questions. Which specification and which options have you taught, and in which series. Will you mark one extended answer against the descriptors while I watch. What arrives in writing after each session. What happens if no specialist in our entered options is free at our hour. And do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. A tutor who answers those five plainly is a different proposition from one who answers with testimonials.

faqs.question: How do online history sessions fit around a Dubai school week and Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Most Dubai private schools run Monday to Friday with a lighter Friday, so the workable slots are weekday evenings between five and eight and Saturday mornings. Online delivery removes the journey, which in exam term is often what decides whether a session happens at all. We fix one recurring slot in Gulf Standard Time and hold it, because a moving slot becomes a fortnightly one. During Ramadan families commonly shift to post-Iftar timing, and that is agreed in advance rather than improvised, with timed full papers placed outside the heaviest weeks.

faqs.question: What happens if no 4HI1 option specialist is free at our preferred hour?
faqs.answer: You are told before anything is committed. The realistic options are a different hour with the specialist, a fortnightly rhythm with longer written tasks in between, or a tutor with adjacent option experience who states exactly which periods they have and have not taught. What we will not do is place a general history tutor and describe them as an option specialist. In a specification where schools choose the periods, that mismatch surfaces in the first marked essay, after a family has already paid for a month of approximate help.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-history-4hi1-tutor.closingHeading: Start with one marked essay and the entry list
dubai/edexcel-igcse-history-4hi1-tutor.closingBody: If your child sits Pearson Edexcel International GCSE History in Dubai and the grade has settled in the middle of the paper, two documents will tell you more than any consultation: a recent marked extended answer, and the list of depth and breadth studies the school entered. Send the first, email the humanities lead for the second, and take a first session at no charge, one per student, with a tutor who has taught those options. You will leave holding a ranked list of what is costing marks and a plan for the first month. Lessons are online, one to one, in Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below publish the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects they teach and the session lengths they work in, so a family comparing quotes is comparing the same thing twice rather than two different products with one price each.

intro.heading: The number on the quote is not the number you pay
paragraphs: Families searching for an Edexcel IGCSE home tutor in Dubai are usually trying to answer one question: what will this cost over a year, and is it worth it. That question is harder than it should be, because most providers in this market do not publish a price. Of the six best-ranking tutoring pages fetched for this research, three carry no figure at all and two quote in US dollars. One of them even has a FAQ that asks what tutoring costs and then declines to answer it.

So here is the market, in dirhams, with sources. Budget online tutoring from students and early-career tutors is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one with travel priced in runs AED 180 to 500: Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts the band at 180 to 350, and independent home tutors advertise up to 500. Specialists in IB, IGCSE and A Level are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase listing AED 270. Premium named tutors are advertised at AED 500 to 650 and above, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

The gap between the online band and the in-home band is not a quality gap. It is a travel gap. A tutor who drives to three households in an evening across Dubai spends well over an hour in the car, and that hour is paid for by somebody. In a city where an afternoon crossing from Mirdif to the Marina can take forty minutes each way, the premium is simply the cost of the road, converted into an hourly rate and handed to the family who booked the slot furthest from the tutor's own home.

There is a second cost, less visible and usually larger. Geography shrinks the pool. The set of people who can teach Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1 properly is small; the subset of those who live within a reasonable drive of your community is smaller still. Families who insist on proximity are often buying a worse match at a higher rate, which is the most expensive combination available in this market.

IB Gram's position is stated plainly because it changes what you are comparing. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. We do not sell home visits in the UAE; that is a service offered only in India. What that buys is a tutor chosen for the specification rather than the postcode, with no travel inside the rate and no forty-minute buffer around every session.

Published online rates for a qualified subject tutor: AED 150-300
