dubai/edexcel-igcse-physics-4ph1-home-tu.programmesIntro: A 4PH1 budget looks different depending on which route the entry sits in. A two-year school course, a November resit and a private-candidate entry carry different hour counts and different fixed costs, and families are rarely told which one they are in until the entry statement arrives.

programmes.name: Two-year 4PH1 course through a Dubai school
programmes.description: The standard route. The school holds the Pearson centre registration, makes the entry, submits forecast grades and receives the results. Tutoring here is a top-up rather than a replacement, which usually means one hour a week across two years or a heavier block in the term before the series. The cost question is how many of those weeks are genuinely needed, and a marked script answers it better than a sales conversation.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools differ on when 4PH1 teaching starts. Some begin in Year 9 and run three years, which spreads the tutoring need thinly; others compress the specification into two years, which concentrates it. Ask the head of science which model applies, because a three-year course makes a single weekly hour in Year 9 far cheaper than the same work bought under pressure in February of Year 11.

programmes.name: November series retake
programmes.description: Pearson International GCSE runs in November as well as May and June, so a disappointing summer physics grade does not cost a full year. A retake block is short, intensive and comparatively easy to cost: six to ten weeks of two sessions a week, aimed squarely at the categories the previous script lost marks on. The hour count is finite, which makes this the most predictable spend of the three routes.
programmes.countryNote: The November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, which places the preparation window across the first term of the Dubai academic year. Check with the school whether it enters candidates for the November series at all; not every Dubai centre does, and a family may need the private-candidate route instead, which changes the fixed costs.

programmes.name: Private candidate entry
programmes.ageRange: Any age, outside a school cohort
programmes.description: Used by home-educated students, by those whose school does not enter the November series, and by students who have moved mid-course. The entry is made through an approved examination venue rather than through a school, and the venue sets its own administrative charges on top of the Pearson entry fee. Tutoring costs the same per hour, but the fixed costs are visible rather than buried inside school fees.
programmes.countryNote: Ask any Dubai examination venue for its fee schedule in writing before committing, including the per-subject administrative charge and the deadline after which late entry fees apply. These are centre charges rather than Pearson charges, they vary between venues in the same emirate, and they are the part of a private-candidate budget families most often discover late.

programmes.name: What follows 4PH1, and what it costs to be ready
programmes.description: International A Level Physics and IB Diploma Physics both assume the equation handling and the mathematical fluency that 4PH1 only begins. Families who spend a modest amount in Year 10 on arithmetic habits typically spend less in Year 12, because the alternative is paying specialist post-16 rates to fix a problem that cost less to fix at fifteen. That is the one genuine saving available in this market.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai had 387,441 private-school students across 227 schools in 2024-25, with 37% on a UK curriculum and 7% in the International Baccalaureate, so most 4PH1 students in the emirate face a real choice at sixteen rather than an automatic continuation. Specialist post-16 tutoring is quoted at the top of the bands on this page, which is a reason to treat Year 10 physics as the cheaper intervention.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-physics-4ph1-home-tu.subjectsIntro: Few households tutor physics alone. The list below is what a 4PH1 family in Dubai most often adds, and what each addition does to the monthly figure. Use it to work out the total before committing to the first subject rather than after.

subjects.name: Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: The subject on this page. Two untiered written papers, 180 marks, no coursework. Priced at the subject-specialist band rather than the general-tutor band, because the paper split and the equation recall expectation are specific to this code. Usually one weekly hour, rising to two in the final term.

subjects.name: Mathematics A 4MA1
subjects.description: The most common addition, and the one that reduces physics hours rather than adding to them. Maths A is tiered, unlike the sciences, so the tier decision is a real conversation. Students whose physics marks go on rearrangement and standard form are often better served by a maths hour than a second physics hour.

subjects.name: Chemistry 4CH1
subjects.description: Same two-paper, 180-mark shape as physics, with the mole calculation as the load-bearing skill. Households taking three separate sciences normally stagger the tutoring rather than running all three at once, which keeps the monthly figure flat and spreads the work across the two years.

subjects.name: Biology 4BI1
subjects.description: The science families most often postpone, because it reads as though it can be revised late. The postponement is what makes it expensive: a late start converts a term of weekly hours into an intensive block at the point in the year when every provider's diary is full and rates are least negotiable.

subjects.name: Science Double Award 4SD0
subjects.description: The alternative to three separate sciences, worth two International GCSEs. Tutoring is cheaper in total than three single-subject courses but harder to target, because a weak area in one science sits inside a qualification covering all three. Check the entry statement to see which your child actually sits.

subjects.name: English Language A 4EA1
subjects.description: Priced at the general rather than specialist band in most of this market, and frequently the subject a family drops first when the monthly total gets uncomfortable. Worth keeping if the equivalency count is tight, since five accredited subjects at no less than grade 3 is the threshold that matters.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed for. Rarely included in a family's tutoring budget at the planning stage and often the reason the budget is exceeded. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, so the starting point varies sharply between students in the same year group.

subjects.name: Islamic Education
subjects.levels: Mandatory for Muslim students in Dubai
subjects.description: Taught in Standard Arabic for Arab students and in the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs, under KHDA's mandatory-subject requirements. Schools must ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the relevant KHDA approval, which is a useful question to ask before paying for outside support in these subjects.

subjects.name: UAE Social Studies and Moral Education
subjects.description: Delivered in Arabic for Arab students and in the licensed-curriculum language for others. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises no mandatory lesson be shorter than 25 minutes. Additional or different content needs prior Ministry of Education permission, which limits what any outside tutor may legitimately use.

subjects.name: International A Level Physics
subjects.description: Where the same family often returns two years later, at the top of the rate bands on this page. Modular, mathematically heavier, and far less scaffolded than 4PH1. Mentioned here because it is the cost argument for fixing arithmetic habits at fifteen rather than at seventeen.

Read the table by column rather than by row. The rate column is the one families look at; the two that actually explain the rate are travel and specification knowledge. An in-home specialist and an online specialist may have identical qualifications, and the difference between their quotes is almost entirely the ninety minutes of evening the visiting tutor spends in a car. The last column is the one worth arguing about with any provider. Replacement policy sounds like small print until the match is wrong in week three, at which point it decides whether a family loses a term being polite or changes tutor in a week. Ask it explicitly, in writing, before the first paid session, and ask what happens to the diagnosis when the tutor changes. sections.heading: The travel arithmetic behind the in-home premium
paragraphs: An in-home hour is not an hour. For a tutor driving from Jumeirah to Dubai Marina at five in the afternoon, it is an hour of teaching inside two hours and a quarter of working time, plus fuel and parking. Price that evening rationally and the in-home rate has to carry the journey, which is exactly what the published bands show: AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's Dubai table against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor working online, with individual home tutors advertising up to AED 500.

The second effect is less obvious and matters more. Travel does not only raise the rate; it shrinks the pool. A tutor can fit two or three visits into an evening if they are in adjacent communities, and one if they are not. That means the in-home physics tutors genuinely available to a family in Nad Al Sheba at 17:00 on a Tuesday are those who already work nearby, which has nothing to do with whether they have taught 4PH1. Families in the eastern districts feel this least and families in the newer interior communities feel it most.

This is where the honest comparison sits. IB Gram does not arrange home visits in Dubai; lessons run one to one over live video, and the saving is not presented as the main argument. The main argument is that removing the journey removes the constraint on who can teach your child. A Dubai family choosing online is choosing a tutor who knows how Pearson words a plan-an-investigation question, instead of choosing whoever could reach the villa before the student's concentration ran out.

sections.heading: Five things that move a 4PH1 quote, and two that should not
paragraphs: Quotes for the same subject in the same emirate vary by a factor of ten, and most of the variation is explicable. The starting point is the biggest single driver: a student three grades below target across six topics needs a different volume of work from one losing eleven marks to unit conversion, and an honest provider will price those differently after seeing a script rather than identically after a phone call. The second is timing. Diaries fill before a series, and the same tutor is both more expensive and less available in the eight weeks before papers than in September.

Session length changes the effective rate more than families expect. A ninety-minute session is not half again as useful as a sixty-minute one for a fifteen-year-old, and a forty-five-minute session can be better value than either for arithmetic drilling. Marking between sessions is the fourth driver and the one most often hidden: a tutor who marks a full paper properly spends forty minutes on it, and that time is either in the rate, billed separately, or not happening. Ask which. The fifth is subject count, since a second or third subject in the same household usually attracts a lower effective rate per hour.

Two things should not move the quote. A school's KHDA inspection band says nothing about an individual student's need and should never be used to justify a higher rate for families at a particular school. Nor should any claim of regulatory approval: IB Gram holds no permit, accreditation or endorsement from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Pearson or Cambridge, and neither do the overwhelming majority of providers advertising in this market. A rate premium attached to an unevidenced badge is a premium for nothing.

sections.heading: Per hour, per session or per month: how Dubai providers actually price
paragraphs: Comparing two quotes in this market is harder than it should be because they are rarely quoted in the same unit. One provider gives an hourly rate, another a per-session rate for ninety minutes, a third a monthly package of eight sessions, a fourth a term fee. Converting them all to dirhams per taught hour is the only way to see the difference, and doing so sometimes reverses which looks cheaper. A monthly package at AED 799 for eight sessions is about AED 100 a session, which is only comparable if the sessions are an hour and are one to one.

Packages carry a second question: what happens to unused sessions. A family that travels for two weeks in the middle of a monthly package has either lost those sessions, rolled them forward or paid for nothing, and which of the three is a term in the agreement rather than a courtesy. Dubai families travel more than most, across the summer and the winter break, so this clause matters here more than it would elsewhere. Get it in writing before the first payment, along with the cancellation notice period.

The third thing to pin down is what counts as a session. Marking a past paper, writing feedback, a short message answering a question between lessons and a parent call at the end of a block are all real work, and providers treat them differently. sections.heading: Physics tuition in the context of a Dubai school bill
paragraphs: A tutoring figure means little in isolation. It means something next to the rest of a Dubai education budget, and 2026-27 is an unusually clear year in which to do that comparison. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private-school fees in the emirate would not increase for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For the first time in several years, a family's school bill is a fixed quantity while they decide what to add to it.

The supply side is also moving. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four on a UK curriculum and three offering the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places; six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. The emirate had 387,441 private-school students across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering 17 curricula, with 37% on a UK curriculum. More places tends to mean more competition for teaching staff, which is one of the quieter pressures on private tutoring rates in any market.

It is deliberately conservative: it uses the published market bands from this page rather than any figure of ours, and it leaves school fees as a range because they vary by an order of magnitude across the emirate. The point of the comparison is not that tutoring is cheap. sections.heading: What the rate should include, and the extras that appear later
paragraphs: The most common unpleasant surprise in this market is not the hourly rate. It is discovering that the rate covers the taught hour and nothing else. Marking a past paper properly takes a tutor something close to forty minutes, and a provider quoting a low rate has either absorbed that time, excluded it, or is not doing it. All three are legitimate business models and only the third is a problem, but a family cannot tell which they have bought unless they ask.

The same applies to written feedback, to answering a question between lessons, to a short progress call with a parent at the end of a block, and to rescheduling. A provider that reschedules without charge once a term and one that charges for any change under forty-eight hours are offering materially different things at the same headline price. Dubai families travel more than most and should weight rescheduling terms accordingly rather than treating them as boilerplate.

On value-added tax, this page says only what it can source. The treatment of tuition fees under UAE tax rules is a question for the Federal Tax Authority and not for a tutoring provider's marketing page, and any provider telling you confidently that tuition is or is not subject to tax should be asked for its source. The question a parent can get a straight answer to is narrower and more useful: is the figure you have been quoted inclusive of any tax, and will the invoice show it.

sections.heading: Why the search says home tutor and the invoice says online
paragraphs: Parents type home tutor because that is the shape of the need: a child at home in Dubai, a physics grade going the wrong way, and an assumption that help arrives at the door. The phrase is worth answering rather than deflecting. The in-home market exists, it is well supplied in the eastern districts and thin in the newer interior communities, and it costs what this page says it costs. IB Gram does not operate in it. Lessons are one to one over live video, and home visits are a service offered only in India.

Said plainly rather than defensively, the trade is straightforward. An in-home hour buys presence: a person in the room, a phone that goes away, a parent who can see the lesson happening. Those are real goods, particularly for a younger student or one who will not work without supervision. An online hour buys selection: the tutor is chosen because they know the 4PH1 paper split and the equation recall list, not because they live twenty minutes away. For a specification-specific problem at sixteen, selection usually matters more than presence.

There is a third difference that gets no attention in this market and should. An online session leaves a record. The annotated script, the written feedback referenced to a specification point, and the session recording all remain afterwards, which means a parent who was not in the room can still see what changed. A visiting tutor leaves whatever is in the student's own exercise book. For a family spending AED 800 to 1,800 a month, that difference in accountability is worth something concrete.

sections.heading: Permits, licensing and the questions that make a quote comparable
paragraphs: Before comparing two prices, establish that both tutors may lawfully teach. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so disregard any figure quoted to you as fact.

MoHRE's own service listing is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two-working-day completion time, applied for through the ministry's app, website and e-services system. Because the permit is free and quick, a tutor who does not hold one has no cost-based reason not to, which makes it a reasonable thing to ask about before money changes hands. A tuition operation with premises and staff is a different matter again, requiring a KHDA Educational Services Permit, and no provider lacking that permit should present itself as holding any form of KHDA endorsement.

In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct points the same way. The practical reading for a Dubai parent is to be wary of any arrangement offering your child's own class teacher privately. Ask instead for the three things that make quotes comparable: the taught-hour rate, what is included beyond the taught hour, and what happens if the match is wrong.

process.title: Say what you are comparing against
process.description: The most useful opening message names the other quotes on the table and their units: an in-home tutor at a per-visit figure, a centre at a term fee, a platform at a monthly package. A specialist can then convert them to dirhams per taught hour and tell you honestly where the comparison actually sits, including where another option is the better buy.

process.title: Send the marked physics script
process.description: Volume of work drives price more than anything else, and the only honest way to estimate it is to look at the student's own marked paper. Three photographed pages are enough. Without them, any quote is a guess dressed as a number, which is how families end up buying a term of hours for a problem that needed five sessions.

process.title: Free thirty-minute trial, then a written quote
process.description: The trial is diagnostic rather than a sample lesson, and no card details are taken. What follows is a quote with the hour count, the session length, what marking is included and the replacement terms, in writing. A verbal rate with unspecified inclusions is not a quote and cannot be compared with anything.

process.title: Fix the unit and the period before the first paid hour
process.description: Agree whether you are buying hours, sessions, a month or a block, and what happens to unused sessions when the family travels. Dubai households travel across summer and winter breaks more than most, and this single clause accounts for most of the disputes families report with tutoring providers in the emirate.

process.title: Review the spend after the first block
process.description: At the end of four to six sessions, the named problem has either closed or it has not, and the written feedback should make that visible without interpretation. That is the point to decide whether to continue, stop or change subject. An open-ended monthly arrangement nobody reviews is how a tutoring budget quietly doubles.

whyPoints.title: Figures with a source and a date, or no figures
whyPoints.description: Every dirham band on this page names the provider or rate table that published it and the month it was read. Three of the six top-ranking pages in this market publish no price at all and two quote in dollars. Showing the working is cheaper for us than inventing a comparison and is the only version a parent can check.

whyPoints.title: The in-home premium explained rather than disparaged
whyPoints.description: In-home tutoring in Dubai is a legitimate service that costs more because it carries a journey. This page says so, prices it from published sources, and does not pretend the difference is quality. IB Gram simply does not sell it, and the comparison table exists so a family can decide rather than be steered.

whyPoints.title: Priced after a diagnosis, not from a list
whyPoints.description: A quote follows a free thirty-minute trial in which a specialist reads the marked script and estimates the hours the problem actually needs. Pricing before seeing the work is how a five-session problem becomes a two-term commitment, which is comfortable for the provider and expensive for the family.

whyPoints.title: Inclusions stated in writing
whyPoints.description: Marking, written feedback, messages between lessons, rescheduling and replacement terms are all set out before the first paid hour. Two quotes at the same headline rate can differ by several hours of real work a month, and the only way a family sees that is if both providers are asked the same questions.

whyPoints.title: One specification, not physics in general
whyPoints.description: Tutors are matched on Pearson Edexcel 4PH1: the two untiered papers, the content examined only in Paper 2P, the equation recall expectation and the absence of a practical examination. Paying a specialist rate for general physics teaching is the most common way money is wasted in this subject.

whyPoints.title: No badges we do not hold
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Pearson or Cambridge, and says so. A rate premium attached to an unevidenced regulatory badge is the most expensive thing a parent can buy in this market, because it costs money and provides nothing.

faqs.question: How much does a home tutor for Edexcel IGCSE Physics 4PH1 cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: In-home one-to-one tutoring in Dubai is published at AED 180 to 350 an hour in Bestimate's 2026 rate table, with individual home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. Monthly in-home packages of four two-hour visits are advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799. Those are market figures from October 2026, not ours. Online one-to-one with a qualified subject tutor runs AED 150 to 300, and specialists AED 200 to 450 and above. IB Gram teaches 4PH1 online only and quotes after a free thirty-minute trial, with no card details taken.

faqs.question: Why is in-home physics tutoring in Dubai more expensive than online?
faqs.answer: Mostly because of travel. A tutor driving from Jumeirah to Dubai Marina for a five o'clock lesson spends over two hours of working time for one taught hour, plus fuel and parking, and a rational rate carries that. The published gap between AED 180 to 350 in-home and AED 150 to 300 online is close to what the journey is worth. The second effect is availability rather than price: a journey limits a tutor to two or three visits an evening, so the pool a family can actually book from shrinks to those already working nearby.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a physics tutor to a villa or apartment in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not arrange home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. 4PH1 tuition is delivered one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The in-home rates quoted on this page are the market's, included so a family can compare properly rather than be steered. The trade is that a tutor is matched on knowing this specification, including how Paper 2P differs from Paper 1P, rather than on living within driving distance of the community.

faqs.question: What is a realistic monthly budget for one 4PH1 student in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's 2026 estimates for a single weekly hour are AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist support in an examination year. Advertised monthly online packages of eight sessions sit around AED 799. Three sciences at one mid-range hour each therefore implies AED 1,800 to 3,600 a month, which is the arithmetic most families do after committing to the first subject rather than before. Plan the total in September.

faqs.question: Is a ninety-minute session better value than two shorter ones?
faqs.answer: Not usually, for a fifteen-year-old. A ninety-minute physics session at AED 400 converts to about AED 267 a taught hour, which looks efficient until you account for concentration: the last twenty minutes of a long session frequently produce no usable work. Two shorter sessions in a week also give a gap for independent practice, which is where the learning consolidates. Forty-five minutes can be the best value of all for arithmetic drilling. Convert every quote to dirhams per taught hour first, then decide what length suits the student.

faqs.question: Does the hourly rate normally include marking a past paper?
faqs.answer: Ask, because it varies and it is the largest hidden variable in this market. Marking a full physics paper properly takes a tutor close to forty minutes. A provider quoting a low rate has absorbed that time, excluded it, or is not doing it, and all three exist. Two quotes at the same headline figure can differ by several hours of real work a month. The same question applies to written feedback after each session, to messages between lessons, and to a progress call with a parent at the end of a block.

faqs.question: What happens to a monthly package if we travel for two weeks?
faqs.answer: That depends entirely on the agreement, so get it in writing before the first payment. Unused sessions are variously forfeited, rolled forward or credited, and Dubai families travel across summer and winter breaks more than most, which makes the clause worth more here than elsewhere. Ask about the rescheduling notice period in the same conversation: a provider that allows a free change once a term and one that charges for any change inside forty-eight hours are offering different things at the same advertised rate.

faqs.question: Are budget online tutors at AED 50 an hour worth considering for 4PH1?
faqs.answer: For some purposes, yes. Providers advertise from AED 33 to 65 an hour, usually with university-student tutors, and for supervised practice or arithmetic drilling that can be perfectly sensible. What you are unlikely to get at that rate is specification knowledge: how Pearson words a plan-an-investigation question, which content is examined only in Paper 2P, and what the mark scheme awards for an explain question. If the marked script shows lost marks on question technique rather than on content, the cheaper option will not address it.

faqs.question: Does a 4PH1 quote get worse in the eight weeks before a Pearson series?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens, which has the same effect on a family as a rise. In the six to eight weeks before a Pearson series, specialist diaries fill, the convenient slots go first, and there is little room to negotiate on either rate or timing. Booking a pre-series intensive before the autumn half-term for a November series, or before the winter break for the summer, is the practical response. The same hours bought in September cost the same per hour and are far easier to schedule around a Dubai school week.

faqs.question: Does the quoted price for tutoring in Dubai include tax?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider directly and expect the answer on the invoice. The treatment of tuition fees under UAE tax rules is a question for the Federal Tax Authority rather than for a tutoring company's marketing page, and any provider stating it confidently should be asked for its source. What a parent can reasonably settle is narrower: whether the figure quoted is inclusive, whether an invoice will be issued, and whether any tax registration number appears on it. Vague answers to those three questions are themselves informative.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to tutor three sciences together or one at a time?
faqs.answer: Staggering is usually cheaper in practice, even though the per-hour rate is the same. Running physics, chemistry and biology simultaneously at one mid-range hour each implies AED 1,800 to 3,600 a month on the published bands, which most families cannot sustain for two years. Taking one subject for a term, closing the named problem, then moving to the next keeps the monthly figure flat and spreads the work across Years 10 and 11. The exception is the final term before a series, when staggering no longer leaves enough time.

faqs.question: Are Dubai school fees going up in 2026-27, and does that change the tutoring decision?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private-school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. For a family budgeting a tutoring commitment, that makes the school bill a fixed quantity for once. The supply side is still moving: seven new private schools join the 2026-27 intake, four UK curriculum and three IB, adding 16,846 places.

faqs.question: Does a tutor in Dubai need a licence, and does that affect what they charge?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and it is free, so it should not affect the rate at all. The MoHRE private tuition work permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. Any premium charged for holding a free document is a premium for nothing.

faqs.question: How many 4PH1 sessions should we buy to start with?
faqs.answer: Four to six, aimed at one named problem taken from the marked script, with a re-test a fortnight after the block ends. That is enough to see whether the diagnosis was right and whether the student works with that tutor, and it is a finite spend rather than an open commitment. A meaningful number of families stop there, because the named problem has closed and the rest is school work. Buying a term before anyone has looked at a marked paper is how a five-session problem becomes a two-term invoice.

faqs.question: What should a written quote for physics tutoring actually contain?
faqs.answer: Six things: the rate expressed per taught hour, the session length, the number of sessions and over what period, what marking and written feedback are included, the rescheduling and cancellation notice, and the replacement terms if the match is wrong. Ask also whether the diagnosis carries across to a replacement tutor, because a provider that restarts the assessment is charging twice for the same work. A verbal rate with unspecified inclusions is not a quote and cannot be compared against anything.

faqs.question: Can we pay for a short block before a November resit rather than a full term?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a retake it is usually the right structure. Pearson runs International GCSE in November as well as May and June, and the November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, so the preparation window sits in the first term of the Dubai year. A retake block is finite and easy to cost: six to ten weeks of two sessions a week, aimed only at the categories the previous script lost marks on. Confirm first that your child's school enters the November series, since not every Dubai centre does.

Each works one to one over live video with Dubai families.

intro.heading: What a 4PH1 tutor in Dubai is actually for
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics is a specific qualification with a specific code: 4PH1. That code matters more than it looks. It tells you the entry is untiered, that there are two written papers rather than three, that there is no coursework and no separate practical examination, and that the whole grade rests on 180 marks sat inside roughly three and a quarter hours. A tutor who teaches physics in general will cover most of the content. A tutor who teaches 4PH1 knows which of that content is examined only in the second paper, which equations a candidate is expected to recall unaided, and which question stems reliably produce a blank answer space.

Most Dubai families arrive at this search after a mock. The report comes back with a grade one or two bands below where the student sat in Year 10, and the comment says something like inconsistent application. That comment is accurate and useless. What a parent needs is the diagnosis underneath it: whether the marks went on unit conversion, on reading a gradient off a graph, on explaining a circuit instead of calculating it, on rounding part way through a multi-step answer, or on answering a six-mark question with three marks of content. Those five failure modes behave differently and need different work.

Physics is also the science where strong arithmetic hides a weak understanding for longer than in biology or chemistry. A student who can rearrange an equation can pass Year 10 on substitution alone. The 4PH1 papers break that habit, because a substantial share of the marks ask why rather than how much: why the current divides at a junction, why a transformer needs alternating current, why the count rate falls to a quarter after two half-lives. A student who has only ever practised the numerical versions meets those questions for the first time in the exam hall.

What a session can realistically do is narrow. It can rebuild the arithmetic of one topic in an hour. It can teach a student to read a Pearson mark scheme and see that the two marks for an explanation sit in two separate statements, not one longer sentence. It can take a marked mock, sort the lost marks into categories, and put the largest category first. Over a term it can move a student's script from something that earns partial credit everywhere to something that finishes questions. No tutor can promise a particular grade, and anyone who offers one should be treated with real scepticism.

Delivery is online, one to one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For 4PH1 that trade is a good one. The pool of physics specialists who know this exact specification is small in any single emirate, and a Dubai family that restricts itself to tutors who can drive to Al Barsha by five o'clock is choosing from a fraction of it. Over video a student shares a screen, a worked script and a graph in real time, and the session happens at the hour the family actually has free.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-physics-4ph1-tutor.programmesIntro: 4PH1 sits in the middle of a British-curriculum route that most Dubai schools run from Year 7 to Year 13. Knowing what comes before and after changes what a tutor should spend time on, because a student heading for International A Level Physics needs different habits from one who will drop the subject at 16.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary Science (Years 7 to 9)
programmes.description: The three years before the specification starts. Physics here is taught inside a combined science course, usually without formal equation recall and with calculations kept to single steps. The gap that matters is mathematical: ratio, proportion, rearranging a formula, standard form and unit prefixes. A student who leaves Year 9 unable to convert centimetres to metres under time pressure will lose marks in 4PH1 for three years running, and the fix takes weeks in Year 9 but months in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools vary widely in when they begin Pearson content. Some British-curriculum schools start 4PH1 teaching in Year 9 and run a three-year course; others keep Year 9 general and compress the specification into two years. Ask the head of science which model your child's school uses, because it changes whether Year 9 is a preparation year or already an examined one.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics
programmes.description: The qualification this page is about. Eight topics, two written papers, 180 marks, graded 9 to 1, with no tiering decision to make and no coursework to submit. Paper 1P is the longer paper at two hours and 110 marks; Paper 2P runs an hour and a quarter for 70 marks and reaches content the specification identifies as examined only there. Candidates are expected to recall a defined set of equations rather than read them off a sheet.
programmes.countryNote: A Dubai cohort sitting 4PH1 is usually entered through the school as a registered Pearson centre, with the entry made months before the paper. Private candidates sit at an approved examination venue in the emirate instead, and the venue list and fee structure come from the centre rather than from Pearson. Check your child's exam entry statement for the exact codes: a school can enter Pearson for physics and Cambridge for another science.

programmes.name: International A Level Physics
programmes.description: The most common next step for a 4PH1 student who performs well. International A Level Physics is modular, mathematically heavier, and assumes the equation handling that 4PH1 only begins. Students arrive expecting more content and find instead that the same content is examined with far less scaffolding: a question that gave you the formula at 16 now expects you to choose it. The habit that transfers best is writing physics in steps that a marker can follow.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run International A Level alongside the IB Diploma and ask students to choose in Year 11. The physics question is usually about mathematics: an A Level physicist wants to be comfortable with algebra and trigonometry, while a Diploma physicist also carries five other subjects plus the core. A 4PH1 grade is one input into that choice, not the whole of it.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: The other route out of 4PH1, and the one with the sharpest step up at Higher Level. Diploma physics adds an internal assessment, a quantitative emphasis on uncertainty and error, and a breadth of topics that 4PH1 does not touch. Students who coped with 4PH1 by memorising worked examples struggle here, because the Diploma asks them to design and defend a measurement. Students who learned to reason about mechanisms at 16 move across comfortably.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has a substantial IB cohort: International Baccalaureate accounted for 7% of private-school enrolment in the emirate in 2024-25, against 37% on a UK curriculum. Several of the new schools opening for 2026-27 are IB schools. A Year 11 student in a dual-pathway Dubai school is often deciding between the two routes in the same term as the 4PH1 mocks, which is precisely the wrong term to be undecided.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-physics-4ph1-tutor.subjectsIntro: The eight topics below are the Pearson 4PH1 specification as it is actually taught, with the mark-loss pattern that recurs in each. Confirm the current content and the equation list against the live specification on qualifications.pearson.com for your child's cohort, because Pearson revises specifications between series.

subjects.name: Topic 1: Forces and motion
subjects.description: Speed, acceleration, distance-time and velocity-time graphs, Newton's laws, moments, momentum, Hooke's law. The largest single source of early marks and of late confusion. Students lose marks reading gradients and areas off graphs, and by treating weight and mass as interchangeable in a calculation that distinguishes them.

subjects.name: Topic 2: Electricity
subjects.description: Current, voltage, resistance, series and parallel circuits, power, energy transfer, mains electricity and static charge. The topic that most reliably separates grades. Numerical questions are manageable; the explanation questions on why current or voltage divides in a particular circuit are where the marks go.

subjects.name: Topic 3: Waves
subjects.description: Wave properties, the wave equation, reflection, refraction, total internal reflection, sound and the electromagnetic spectrum. Refraction diagrams cost marks because the normal is drawn carelessly or the angle is measured from the surface instead of from the normal. Critical angle calculations need the inverse sine handled confidently.

subjects.name: Topic 4: Energy resources and energy transfer
subjects.description: Energy stores and transfers, conduction, convection, radiation, work, power, efficiency and generating electricity. Efficiency questions are routinely lost by using the wrong pair of energy values, and by giving a percentage greater than one hundred without noticing the answer is impossible.

subjects.name: Topic 5: Solids, liquids and gases
subjects.description: Density, pressure, pressure in liquids, the gas laws, kinetic theory and specific heat capacity. Unit handling dominates the mark loss here: pascals against kilopascals, kelvin against degrees Celsius, cubic centimetres against cubic metres. One conversion error removes every mark that depends on it.

subjects.name: Topic 6: Magnetism and electromagnetism
subjects.description: Magnetic fields, electromagnets, the motor effect, electromagnetic induction, transformers and the generator. Students who learn the left and right hand rules as gestures rather than as statements about direction get the orientation wrong in the exam. Transformer calculations are easy marks that are lost to ratio errors.

subjects.name: Topic 7: Radioactivity and particles
subjects.description: Atomic structure, isotopes, alpha, beta and gamma radiation, half-life, nuclear equations, fission and fusion. Half-life questions are the classic trap: a candidate halves the activity the wrong number of times, or confuses the half-life with the total elapsed time. Nuclear equations need both numbers balanced, not one.

subjects.name: Topic 8: Astrophysics
subjects.description: Orbits, the solar system, stellar life cycles, the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram, red shift and the expanding universe. Often taught last and revised least. The content is comparatively small and the marks are comparatively cheap, which makes it the most efficient topic to repair in the final weeks before a series.

subjects.name: Mathematics inside physics
subjects.description: Standard form, unit prefixes, rearranging equations with the unknown in the denominator, significant figures, gradients, areas under graphs and inverse trigonometric functions. None of this is examined as mathematics, and all of it is examined. A weak week here costs marks in every topic simultaneously.

subjects.name: Practical and investigative skills
subjects.description: Apparatus selection, method description, independent and dependent variables, control variables, repeat readings, anomalous results, precision and sources of error. There is no separate practical paper in 4PH1, so these marks appear inside ordinary written questions and are routinely under-practised as a result.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-physics-4ph1-tutor.regionsIntro: 4PH1 is taught across Dubai's British-curriculum schools, and online delivery means the practical question is scheduling rather than distance. The notes below are about session timing: when a student in each part of the emirate is realistically free, awake and able to work through a past paper.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Lakes Towers

sections.heading: What 4PH1 is, and what each of the two papers asks
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics is examined through two written papers and nothing else. Paper 1P runs for two hours and carries 110 marks. Paper 2P runs for one hour and fifteen minutes and carries 70 marks. Together they make 180 marks, which means Paper 1P is 61.1% of the subject total and Paper 2P is 38.9%. The qualification is reported on the 9 to 1 scale and, unlike Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, it has no Foundation or Higher tier. Every candidate sits the same two papers.

That structure has a practical consequence families often miss. Because there is no tier, there is no grade ceiling to negotiate and no decision to make in Year 10 about which paper to enter for. What there is instead is a body of content the specification identifies as examined only in Paper 2P. A student who has revised evenly across the eight topics but has never practised that subset walks into the shorter paper least prepared, and the shorter paper is the one with less time to recover in.

There is also no coursework and no separate practical examination in 4PH1. Practical and investigative skills are assessed inside the written questions: naming apparatus, describing a method, identifying variables, explaining why repeats were taken, spotting an anomalous reading. Schools still set practical work internally, and that work is genuinely useful preparation, but it carries no Pearson marks. Confirm the current paper structure and the content split against the live 4PH1 specification on qualifications.pearson.com for your child's series, because Pearson revises specifications and the version in use is the one that counts.

sections.heading: The eight topics, and the specific way each one loses marks
paragraphs: A marked 4PH1 script almost never shows marks lost evenly. It shows clusters. A student will hold full marks through a mechanics question and then drop four marks across two efficiency calculations, or answer every numerical electricity question correctly and earn nothing on the one that asks why the lamps dim when a third is added in series. Sorting those clusters by topic is the first thing a session should do, because the repair for each one is different and the cheapest repairs are not the ones a student feels worst about.

The table below is the pattern we see most often in Dubai cohorts, topic by topic. It is diagnostic rather than exhaustive: the point is that each topic has a signature error, and once a parent can name the signature error they can tell whether a tutor is working on it. Graph reading in Topic 1, explanation structure in Topic 2, the normal line in Topic 3, paired energy values in Topic 4, unit prefixes in Topic 5, direction in Topic 6, the number of halvings in Topic 7, and simple under-revision in Topic 8.

The ordering also tells you where to start with limited time. Topic 8 Astrophysics carries comparatively few marks but is taught last and revised least, which makes it the highest return per hour in a short block. Topic 2 Electricity carries the most marks and the hardest explanation questions, so it deserves the long term rather than the final fortnight. A tutor who begins with the first topic in the specification and works forwards is following a book, not a script.

sections.heading: Command words in a Pearson physics paper, and what each one pays for
paragraphs: A large share of the marks a 4PH1 candidate loses are not knowledge marks at all. They are marks for answering a different question from the one asked. State, describe, explain, calculate, determine, deduce and suggest are not synonyms in a Pearson mark scheme, and each has a shape of answer that earns credit. A student who writes a beautiful explanation where the paper asked for a state is writing for nothing; a student who states a fact where the paper asked for an explanation has earned one of the two available marks and stopped.

This is the single most teachable thing on the page, and the thing schools have least time for. It takes one session to go through a past paper with the mark scheme open and highlight, question by question, the command word and the number of distinct statements the scheme is looking for. Most students have never seen a mark scheme. When they do, the structure becomes obvious: two marks means two things, a because in the stem means a causal chain is wanted, and a calculate instruction means the final line needs a number and a unit.

The habit to build is mechanical. Underline the command word. Count the marks. Write that many distinct points. Check the unit. For explanation questions, write in links rather than in sentences: the resistance increases, so the current decreases, so the lamp is dimmer. Three links, three marks, no prose. Dubai students who have come from curricula with a different examination culture benefit from this more than anyone, because they often write at length and are marked on precision.

sections.heading: Equation recall, standard form and the arithmetic that quietly costs grades
paragraphs: 4PH1 expects candidates to recall a defined set of equations. Which ones, and whether anything is printed in the paper, is set out in the live specification, and it is worth reading that list with your child rather than assuming. The practical effect is that a student who can rearrange an equation but cannot remember it loses the whole question, and a student who remembers it but rearranges it badly loses most of it. Both failure modes look identical on a report: careless.

The arithmetic underneath is where Dubai cohorts diverge most, because students in any one Year 11 physics class may have come from four different curricula. Standard form is the common weakness: a student who writes a nanosecond as ten to the minus nine will handle a wave calculation, and one who does not will produce an answer out by a factor of a thousand and still earn the method mark while losing the rest. Unit prefixes, significant figures and rounding discipline behave the same way.

The repair is a drill, not a lecture. Five minutes at the start of every session on cold equation recall and unit conversion, with nothing written down in advance, builds the automatic layer that the papers assume. It feels unglamorous and it is the single highest-yield use of tutoring time in the first term of Year 11. By the February mocks the student should be converting prefixes without pausing, which frees the whole of their working memory for the physics the question is actually testing.
bullets: Cold equation recall at the start of each session, written from memory
Unit prefix conversions drilled until they need no thought: nano, micro, milli, kilo, mega
Standard form practised on the calculator the student will actually take into the exam
Rounding held to the end of a multi-step calculation, never applied part way through
Every final answer checked for a unit before the question is left

sections.heading: Practical physics with no practical examination
paragraphs: 4PH1 has no separate practical paper and no coursework, which creates a quiet problem. The practical skills are still examined, inside the written papers, as questions about apparatus, method, variables, repeats, anomalies and precision. Because there is no practical examination on the timetable, these marks often get no dedicated revision at all. A student can arrive at a six-mark plan-an-investigation question having never written one under timed conditions.

Those questions have a reliable structure and can be prepared in exactly the same way as any other question type. Name the independent variable. Name the dependent variable. Name two things kept constant. Say what is measured and with what instrument. Say how many repeats and why. Say how the result will be processed. A student who writes those six elements in that order earns most of the marks available on most plan questions, regardless of whether they have ever handled the apparatus.

Online delivery makes no difference to this, and it is worth saying plainly because it is the first objection a parent raises. IB Gram does not run laboratory sessions in Dubai and does not send tutors to a UAE address; the practical work belongs to the school, which has the equipment and the technicians. What a tutor can do over video is open the school's own practical write-up on a shared screen, mark it against the way Pearson words these questions, and turn a laboratory afternoon the student has already had into examination marks.

sections.heading: What one 4PH1 session actually changes, in order
paragraphs: The first session is diagnostic and should not feel like a lesson. The student brings the most recent marked script, whatever it is: a mock, a topic test, a set of past-paper questions the school has returned. The tutor sorts the lost marks into the categories above, counts them, and tells the parent which category is largest. That is a short, specific statement a family can act on, and it is usually not what the school report said. A report saying inconsistent effort often resolves to eleven marks lost on unit conversion.

Sessions two to four attack the largest category. If the answer is explanation structure, the work is writing two-mark and three-mark explanations until the student stops writing prose. If it is arithmetic, it is drills. If it is a genuine content gap in one topic, it is teaching, and that is the only case where teaching from scratch is the right use of the hour. Each repair finishes with a re-test using questions the student has not seen, set two weeks later rather than at the end of the same session.

From roughly session five, the pattern becomes maintenance plus timing. A timed section each week, marked by the tutor against the real scheme, with the categories tracked so the family can see whether the original problem has actually gone or has simply moved. This is also the point where a student starts arriving with their own questions, which is the signal worth waiting for. Progress in physics shows up first as better questions and only later as a better grade.
bullets: Session 1: marked script sorted into mark-loss categories, largest named
Sessions 2-4: the largest category only, with a delayed re-test
Session 5 onwards: timed practice, marked against the real scheme
Written feedback after each session, referenced to a specification point
Priorities re-set after every school mock, not kept from the start of term

sections.heading: Why the search says tutor in Dubai and the lesson happens over video
paragraphs: Parents search for a physics tutor in Dubai because that is how the need presents itself: a child in Dubai, a subject they are losing marks in, and an assumption that help arrives at the door. The honest answer is that IB Gram delivers 4PH1 tuition as one-to-one online lessons and does not arrange home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, because home visits are a service offered only in India. That is worth knowing before a trial lesson rather than after one.

The market for an in-home physics tutor in Dubai is real and families use it. Rates quoted in the market sit higher than online rates largely because travel is paid for: Bestimate's Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500, against qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150 to 300 and specialist IGCSE and IB tutors at AED 200 to 450 and above. The gap is not a quality gap. It is a car.

For a specific specification code the case for video is stronger than the general case. There are not many physics tutors in any single emirate who know the 4PH1 paper split, the equation recall list and the way Pearson words a plan question. Restricting the search to those who can reach Dubai Hills by 17:00 on a Tuesday shrinks that group sharply. Over video the student shares their actual script, the tutor annotates it live, and the recording and written feedback remain afterwards, which a visiting tutor cannot leave behind.

sections.heading: The Pearson series counted backwards from the entry deadline
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in two series each year, in May and June and again in November. That second series is the thing almost no competitor page mentions and the thing that most changes a family's options, because it means a disappointing result in the summer does not cost a full year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, which puts the useful revision window squarely across the first half of the Dubai academic year.

The dates that matter to a parent are not the examination dates. They are the dates that precede them. Entries are made by the centre months in advance, forecast grades are submitted before the papers are sat, and results reach centres a day before they reach students. For the June 2026 series Pearson released results to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Count the May and June series backwards from there and the shape is clear: the papers sit in a window that opens in May, the entry that fixes the subject codes closes in the spring before it, and the school's mock cycle has to finish early enough to feed a forecast grade that is submitted weeks ahead of the first paper. A 4PH1 student who waits for the final timetable to appear before planning has lost the only two decisions that were still open.

Two practical rules follow. First, ask the examinations officer at your child's school for the entry deadline rather than the examination date, because the entry decision is the one that cannot be undone later. Second, treat published timetables as provisional until the final version is out: Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including the November series a year out, and the live PDF on qualifications.pearson.com is the only version worth planning around.
