sections.heading: KHDA, the tutoring permit and the five-subject equivalency rule
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually on a six-band scale and publishes the reports. A rating tells you about the school; it tells you nothing about whether one student needs help with Topic 2. Abu Dhabi schools answer to ADEK, Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. IB Gram holds no permit, licence or endorsement from any of them, and nobody should tell you otherwise.

Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists a two-working-day completion time and is the route to check. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules additionally bar school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school.

On equivalency, the British track is documented and worth knowing early. Students must show five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. A 4PH1 grade can be one of the five. One competitor page currently states six subjects; the sourced figure is five. No IB points threshold has been verified for equivalency, so do not accept one from any tutoring provider without a moe.gov.ae source, and treat the process as something to verify with the authority rather than something a tutoring platform performs for you.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, past papers and what a physics tutor may not do
paragraphs: 4PH1 has no coursework, which removes the most common academic-honesty risk in international qualifications at a stroke. There is no internal assessment to supervise and no essay to be ghost-written. What remains is school-set practical work, mock papers and homework, and the line there is still worth stating: a tutor teaches, questions, marks and gives feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor who offers to produce assessed work on a student's behalf is selling the student a problem, and several providers in this market do exactly that.

Past papers and mark schemes are a related issue that families get wrong in good faith. Pearson owns that material. A tutor should reference it, name the series and the paper, and point you to the official source rather than distributing scans. Where a school has issued a paper to its own cohort, working through that paper in a session is ordinary teaching. Reproducing and supplying secure or unreleased material is not, and for an unreleased paper it is a malpractice exposure for the student as well as the provider.

The same caution applies to claims about examiners. A tutor may be an experienced teacher of 4PH1; describing anyone as a current Pearson examiner requires evidence, and examiner status should never be used to suggest access to marking, boundaries or paper content. The useful question for a parent is simpler and harder to fake: ask the tutor to mark a page of your child's physics and explain, mark by mark, where the scheme would and would not award credit. Someone who knows the specification can do that in ten minutes.

process.title: Send the marked script, not a description
process.description: The useful first message contains a photograph of the most recent marked physics work and the year group. A mock, a topic test or a returned past paper all work. A description of the problem is less useful than three pages of the student's own writing, because the lost marks are visible in the writing and are usually not what the report says.

process.title: Free thirty-minute trial, diagnostic rather than teaching
process.description: A specialist works through the script with the student, sorts the lost marks into categories and names the largest. No card details are taken for the trial. The output is a short written statement of the priority and a realistic view of how many weeks it will take, which is useful whether or not the family continues.

process.title: Agree the slot and hold it for the term
process.description: Physics tutoring that moves every week does not build the automatic arithmetic layer that 4PH1 assumes. The slot is set on Gulf Standard Time around the school run and homework load for that part of Dubai, and it stays fixed, including a post-Iftar alternative agreed in advance for Ramadan rather than negotiated during it.

process.title: Work the largest category, then re-test cold
process.description: Two to four sessions on the single biggest source of lost marks, finishing with questions the student has not seen, set a fortnight later rather than at the end of the same hour. A repair that survives two weeks is real. A repair tested immediately only shows that the student remembers the last hour.

process.title: Re-prioritise after every school assessment
process.description: Each mock resets the order. Categories that have closed drop out, new ones appear, and the remaining weeks are re-allocated by marks available per hour of work rather than by specification order. Written feedback after each session keeps a parent able to see the change without having to sit in the room.

process.title: Change the tutor if the match is wrong
process.description: A physics specialist who suits one student will not suit another, and two or three sessions is enough to know. Say so and a different tutor picks up the same diagnosis and the same priority list. Nothing is restarted, and no family should spend a term being polite about a match that is not working.

whyPoints.title: The specification code is the unit of expertise
whyPoints.description: 4PH1 is not interchangeable with Cambridge 0625 or with a double award entry. The paper split, the equation recall expectation and the absence of a practical paper are all specific to this code. Matching on the code rather than on the word physics is the single thing that makes a session land in the first hour instead of the third.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before teaching, every time
whyPoints.description: The first session reads a marked script and names the largest category of lost marks. Teaching content a student already knows is the most common way tutoring hours are wasted, and it is also the most comfortable, because it looks like a lesson. A diagnosis is less comfortable and shortens the work considerably.

whyPoints.title: Marks, not adjectives, in the feedback
whyPoints.description: Written feedback after each session names the specification point and the number of marks at stake, so a parent can see whether the problem identified in week one has actually closed. Progress reported as encouraging is not reportable. Eleven marks lost on unit conversion falling to two is.

whyPoints.title: Honest about delivery and about the market
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one to one over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses, and the in-home rates on this page are the market's, attributed to the sources that published them, not ours. A page that tells you what the alternatives cost is easier to trust than one that refuses to mention a number.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled around a Dubai week, not a London one
whyPoints.description: Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time and are set around the school run for the specific community, the Friday and Saturday weekend, and Ramadan timings agreed before the month begins rather than during it. A slot that fits the family's week is the slot that survives to the exam series.

whyPoints.title: No guarantees, no invented numbers
whyPoints.description: No tutor can promise a particular grade, and no figure appears on this page without a source and a date. Every AED band is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, and every regulatory statement is traceable to u.ae, KHDA, MoHRE or Pearson. Claims that cannot be checked are not claims worth making.

faqs.question: What does an Edexcel IGCSE Physics 4PH1 tutor charge per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates rather than ours: qualified online subject tutors in Dubai sit around AED 150 to 300 an hour, with IGCSE and IB specialists quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150, TutorChase quotes about AED 270, and budget online providers advertise from AED 33 to 65. In-home one-to-one runs higher at AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table, largely because travel is inside the rate. All figures are as published by those providers in October 2026. IB Gram quotes after a free thirty-minute trial, with no card details taken.

faqs.question: Is Edexcel IGCSE Physics 4PH1 tiered like Mathematics A?
faqs.answer: No. 4PH1 is a single untiered entry: every candidate sits the same Paper 1P and Paper 2P and the full 9 to 1 grade range is available to all of them. Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A is different, with a Foundation tier capped below the top grades and a Higher tier, which is why the tiering question comes up so often in British-curriculum schools. For physics there is no tier decision for a Dubai school to make in Year 10, and no ceiling to negotiate. Confirm the structure against the live specification for your child's series on qualifications.pearson.com.

faqs.question: How are Paper 1P and Paper 2P weighted in 4PH1?
faqs.answer: Paper 1P runs two hours for 110 marks and Paper 2P runs one hour fifteen minutes for 70 marks, so the two papers total 180 marks. That makes Paper 1P 61.1% of the subject total and Paper 2P 38.9%. The weighting matters less than the content split: the specification identifies a body of material examined only in Paper 2P, and a student who has revised the eight topics evenly without practising that subset is least prepared for the shorter paper. Check the current structure on the live 4PH1 specification, since Pearson revises specifications between series.

faqs.question: Which 4PH1 topics do Dubai students lose the most marks on?
faqs.answer: Electricity and forces and motion carry the most marks and produce the most loss, but the loss is specific rather than general. In electricity it is explanation questions answered with a calculation. In forces and motion it is gradients and areas read incorrectly off a graph. Solids, liquids and gases loses marks to unit prefixes, energy transfer to the wrong pair of values in an efficiency calculation, and radioactivity to halving an activity the wrong number of times. Astrophysics loses marks simply because it is taught last and revised least, which also makes it the fastest topic to repair.

faqs.question: Does my child have to recall every equation in the 4PH1 specification?
faqs.answer: The specification sets out which equations candidates are expected to recall, and that list is worth reading with your child rather than assuming either way. Confirm on qualifications.pearson.com what, if anything, is printed in the paper for your child's series. In practice the distinction between recall and rearrangement is where the marks go: a student who cannot remember an equation loses the whole question, while one who remembers it but rearranges it badly usually keeps a method mark and loses the rest. Five minutes of cold recall at the start of each session fixes the first problem within a term.

faqs.question: Is there a practical exam in Edexcel IGCSE Physics 4PH1?
faqs.answer: No. 4PH1 has two written papers and no separate practical examination or coursework component. Practical and investigative skills are still examined, inside the written papers: naming apparatus, describing a method, identifying independent, dependent and control variables, justifying repeats, handling anomalous readings and commenting on precision. Because no practical paper appears on the timetable, these marks are often the least revised on the whole specification. Plan-an-investigation questions have a reliable six-part structure and can be prepared under timed conditions in the same way as any other question type.

faqs.question: What does the command word explain earn in a Pearson physics mark scheme?
faqs.answer: Explain asks for a causal chain, and the mark scheme awards each link separately. A two-mark explain question wants two distinct statements, not one longer sentence containing the idea once. The answer that scores looks like a sequence: the resistance increases, so the current decreases, so the lamp is dimmer. Three links, three marks, no prose around them. State wants a single fact, describe wants a sequence without causes, and calculate wants working, a value and a unit. Underlining the command word and counting the marks before writing is the cheapest habit a 4PH1 candidate can build.

faqs.question: My child understands the physics but keeps losing marks on units. Is that fixable before the series?
faqs.answer: Yes, and faster than almost anything else on the specification. Unit and prefix errors are an arithmetic habit rather than a knowledge gap, so the repair is a drill: a few minutes of cold conversions at the start of every session, with nothing written down in advance, until kilopascals, cubic centimetres, nanoseconds and kelvin need no thought. Pressure and gas-law questions in Topic 5 are where this shows up most, but the loss is spread across every topic. Rounding discipline belongs in the same drill, since rounding part way through a multi-step calculation costs marks in the final line.

faqs.question: How long does 4PH1 tutoring usually run before the mocks?
faqs.answer: It depends on what the marked script shows, which is why the first session is diagnostic. A single category of lost marks, such as explanation structure or unit conversion, is usually a block of four to six weekly sessions with a re-test a fortnight after the work finishes. A genuine content gap across two or three topics is a term. A student starting Year 10 with weak mathematical habits benefits most from a full year at one hour a week, because the habit layer is cheap to build early and expensive to build in February of Year 11.

faqs.question: Does a 4PH1 tutor travel to a Dubai address, or are lessons online?
faqs.answer: Lessons are one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not arrange home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. The in-home market in Dubai is real and families use it, at rates published between AED 180 and 500 an hour depending on the provider. For a single specification code the video format gives access to a wider pool of 4PH1 specialists than any one emirate holds, and it leaves behind an annotated script, written feedback and a recording that a visiting tutor cannot.

faqs.question: How do online 4PH1 lessons handle circuit diagrams and graph work?
faqs.answer: On a shared screen with a drawing surface both people can write on. The student draws the circuit, the tutor annotates it, and the annotated version is saved and sent afterwards. Graph work is better over video than on paper in one respect: a velocity-time graph can be redrawn with different axes in seconds, which is exactly the practice a student needs when their error is reading a gradient rather than understanding motion. Refraction diagrams, ray paths and free-body force diagrams all work the same way, and the student keeps every version.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child's Dubai school entered Pearson 4PH1 or Cambridge 0625 for physics?
faqs.answer: The exam entry statement the school issues carries the exact codes, and it is the only document that settles it. Ask the examinations officer rather than the physics teacher if you want the codes in writing. The distinction matters because the two specifications examine differently: 4PH1 is two untiered papers with no practical examination, while Cambridge IGCSE Physics has a different paper structure and a practical component. It is also common for a Dubai school to enter Pearson for one science and Cambridge for another, so check each subject separately rather than assuming one board throughout.

faqs.question: Can a 4PH1 tutor give us Pearson past papers and mark schemes to work from?
faqs.answer: A tutor should reference that material and point you to the official source rather than distributing scans, because Pearson owns it. Where your child's school has already issued a past paper to its cohort, working through that paper in a session is ordinary teaching and is exactly what the hour is for. Reproducing or supplying secure or unreleased material is a copyright problem and, for unreleased papers, a malpractice exposure for the student as well. Any provider offering a library of mark schemes as a selling point is describing something it should not be distributing.

faqs.question: Is a work permit required before someone teaches 4PH1 privately here?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted figure with suspicion. MoHRE's service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists a two-working-day completion time. Ask any tutor whether they hold the permit; it is a fair question and a free document.

faqs.question: Does a 4PH1 grade count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: It can be one of the five. The British track requires five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. One competitor page states six subjects; the sourced figure is five. No IB points threshold has been verified, so do not accept one without a moe.gov.ae source. Equivalency is handled by the authority, not by a tutoring provider, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

faqs.question: Can 4PH1 sessions be scheduled around a Dubai school-bus timetable?
faqs.answer: That is the usual reason a slot gets chosen. A Year 11 student bussing from Arabian Ranches to a coastal school is rarely settled before half past four, so a 19:00 session after a proper break produces better work than one squeezed in on arrival. Mirdif and Dubai Silicon Oasis families with short runs often do better at 16:30 while concentration is still available. Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time, the slot is held for the term rather than moved weekly, and a post-Iftar alternative for Ramadan is agreed before the month starts.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-physics-4ph1-tutor.closingBody: If your child sits Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1 at a Dubai school and the last mock came back lower than expected, the useful next step is small. Send a photograph of the marked paper and the year group. A 4PH1 specialist will sort the lost marks into categories in a free thirty-minute trial session, name the largest one, and tell you honestly how many weeks of work it represents. No card details are taken for the trial. Lessons run one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. If the first tutor is not the right match, say so and another picks up the same diagnosis without starting again.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-science-double-award.tutorsIntro: Tutors below teach Pearson Edexcel International GCSE science and have marked work at this level. When you make contact, lead with the paper rather than the subject. The useful opening sentence is not that your child needs science help but that the chemistry paper dropped to a 4 while biology held at a 6.

intro.heading: Three papers, two grades, and the four or five places marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Science Double Award carries the Pearson code 4SD0. It is one qualification assessed by three written papers, one in each of biology, chemistry and physics, each worth about a third of the whole, and it reports two International GCSE grades on the 9 to 1 scale. There is no coursework and no separately examined practical. That structure is the first thing worth understanding properly, because almost every bad tuition decision at this level comes from treating 4SD0 as three subjects rather than as one qualification with three revision streams.

The practical consequence is that a reported grade hides what you need to know. Two students can both be reported at grade 5 and have nothing in common. One is sitting at 7 in biology, 5 in physics and 3 in chemistry. The other is flat at 5 across all three. The first child has one broken paper and two sound ones, and the fix is narrow, specific and short. The second child has a shared problem running through everything, and that is usually not a science problem at all but a problem with reading questions or with the arithmetic underneath them.

Across the three papers, marks disappear in a small number of recognisable places. In biology, the content is known and the explanation is written out of order, so a mechanism answer worth four marks collects two. In chemistry, a multi-step calculation breaks at step one and the student still writes three more lines, collecting nothing. In physics, the equation is right and the unit conversion is not. In all three, questions describing an experiment are answered from theory rather than from the data printed on the page. None of those is a knowledge gap, and all four respond to different work.

This is what a home tutor is usually being asked to fix, and it is worth being clear about the format question. In-home tuition is a genuine service in Dubai with genuine advantages, particularly for younger students. IB Gram does not place a tutor at a Dubai address: home visits are a service offered only in India, and UAE delivery is one-to-one over live video. For 4SD0 specifically that trade is favourable, because the constraint on this qualification is finding someone who is strong on the chemistry paper, not finding someone who lives nearby.

The sections below work through the three papers in turn, then through the experiment questions that sit inside all of them, then through command words, which are the single most repairable loss at this level. After that comes the part most pages skip: an honest account of what one session can fix, what takes six, and what cannot be fixed in the eight weeks before a series. Knowing which category your child is in matters more than any choice of tutor.

A final framing point. Double Award covers less content per science than the separate 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 qualifications, which means the ceiling on this course is reached by technique more often than by knowledge. Students who have learned the content and are stuck at a 5 are usually losing between eight and fifteen marks a paper to things that are not science: question reading, answer order, unit handling and timing. Those marks are available, and they are the cheapest marks on the course to recover.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-science-double-award.programmesIntro: The same student meets 4SD0 content at four different points, and the work a tutor does at each point is different in kind. Knowing which point you are at tells you whether to buy teaching, technique repair, or a route conversation.

programmes.name: Lower secondary science before 4SD0
programmes.description: The foundations that 4SD0 assumes rather than teaches: particle ideas, the structure of an equation, reading a scale, drawing a line of best fit. A student who reaches Year 10 without secure number handling will meet it again as a chemistry problem, and the diagnosis will be wrong, because the symptom will look like moles and the cause will be ratio.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai British-curriculum schools vary widely in how much quantitative work they build into Years 7 to 9, and students arriving mid-key-stage from another system often have a different balance of practical and numerical experience. That gap is invisible on a report and very visible in the first timed 4SD0 paper.

programmes.name: Year 10 of Science Double Award
programmes.description: The teaching year. Content is new, assessments are internal, and the work worth doing is building the habits that the papers reward: writing explanations in mechanism order, setting out calculations so a marker can follow them, labelling axes without being asked. Technique learned here is free; the same technique taught in Year 11 costs a term of revision time.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools typically run their first full internal 4SD0 assessments late in Year 10, which is the earliest honest signal of the strand split. That paper, marked, is the single most useful document a Dubai family can bring to a first tutoring conversation.

programmes.name: Year 11 and the exam series
programmes.description: Content finishes, mocks arrive, and the plan becomes triage. The work is timed papers, marked properly, with the losses categorised and attacked in order of size. A student losing twelve marks a paper to answer structure and six to content should be spending two thirds of the available time on structure, which is the opposite of what most revision plans do.
programmes.countryNote: The Dubai spring term compresses mocks, internal deadlines and the entry window into a short run, often with Ramadan inside it. Finishing content before that compression and reserving the compressed weeks for timed-paper work is the scheduling decision that most changes outcomes.

programmes.name: Moving between Double Award and a single award
programmes.description: A real option with a real cost. Moving into separate Biology, Chemistry or Physics means closing a content gap, not a technique gap, and content takes contact hours. The decision should be made from the strand marks and the intended post-16 course, and it should be made with the school, because timetable and laboratory capacity are part of the answer.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the switch is most often driven by medicine or engineering ambitions surfacing in Year 10. Sixth forms in the city read Double Award and separate sciences differently for their own entry thresholds, so ask the specific school what it requires before committing to a move.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-science-double-award.subjectsIntro: Each entry below names what the strand assesses and where the marks are most often lost, because that pairing is what a first session needs to establish. The pattern is consistent enough across Dubai students that a tutor can usually predict the loss from a grade and then check it against the script.

subjects.name: Biology strand: cells, transport and exchange
subjects.description: Assesses whether a student can explain a process in the order it happens. Osmosis, diffusion and active transport answers typically lose marks because the direction of movement and the reason for it are stated in the wrong sequence, or because water potential is described without naming the membrane.

subjects.name: Biology strand: inheritance and variation
subjects.description: Genetic cross questions are among the most reliably available marks on the paper and among the most commonly half-collected. The loss is almost always a missing key, an unlabelled Punnett square, or a ratio stated without the phenotypes it refers to. Pure technique, fixable in two sessions.

subjects.name: Chemistry strand: moles and reacting masses
subjects.description: The hardest marks on the whole qualification, and sequential. A student who cannot convert mass to moles cannot start, so the three later steps are unreachable. This needs teaching hours rather than practice sheets, because practice on an unreachable question teaches nothing.

subjects.name: Chemistry strand: rates, equilibria and energy
subjects.description: Assesses whether a student can link a particle explanation to an observed change. Marks go on answers that describe what happened without saying why in terms of collisions, frequency or energy. The fix is a vocabulary discipline more than a content one.

subjects.name: Chemistry strand: separation, tests and the reactivity series
subjects.description: High-yield recall content that students under-revise because it feels easy. Ion tests, gas tests and the order of reactivity carry predictable marks every series, and a short recall programme usually banks several of them within a fortnight.

subjects.name: Physics strand: forces, motion and energy
subjects.description: Assesses equation selection and rearrangement more than conceptual understanding. The classic loss is a correct equation with an unconverted unit, or a calculated answer given without units at all, which is a mark given away after the hard part was done correctly.

subjects.name: Physics strand: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Where series and parallel reasoning is tested. Marks disappear when a student calculates total resistance correctly and then applies the supply voltage to one component. Circuit work rewards drawing the circuit again before touching a number.

subjects.name: Physics strand: waves and radioactivity
subjects.description: Narrower content than in separate 4PH1, and mark-dense. Half-life questions and wave calculations are formulaic once the method is secure. The loss here is usually standard form handling rather than physics, which points the work back at Mathematics A.

subjects.name: Experimental and data skills across all three papers
subjects.description: Assessed inside the written papers. Students are asked to identify independent, dependent and control variables, judge whether a method is valid, read values accurately and draw a conclusion from the data printed on the page rather than from what they already believe about the theory.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (4MA1) underneath the science
subjects.description: Rearrangement, ratio, standard form, percentage change and graph gradients appear in both the chemistry and physics papers. When a student's dropped marks survive having the science removed from them, the intervention belongs here, and treating it as a science problem wastes a term.

sections.heading: What a Dubai family is really choosing between when they search for a home tutor
paragraphs: The phrase home tutor describes a delivery format, and parents searching it are usually after something else: a tutor who knows this qualification, can read a marked script and will be there every week. Those two things are separable, and for 4SD0 they pull in opposite directions, because the specialism the qualification needs is narrower than the pool any single Dubai community can supply.

A visiting tutor has real strengths that online cannot replicate. A younger student stays in a familiar room. A parent can hear the session. Nobody has to manage a screen, a microphone or a shared document. For a Year 7 student who needs supervision and reassurance as much as teaching, those strengths are decisive and worth paying a travel premium for.

For a Year 11 student with a broken chemistry paper, they are not decisive. What matters is whether the person across the table has marked chemistry at this level recently enough to know that the moles chain breaks at the conversion step, and whether they will set the right unseen question afterwards. Geography does not predict that. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all, so the choice here is made on specialism rather than on distance, and the table below sets out what each format actually gives a 4SD0 student.

The honest summary is that the format question matters less than parents expect and the diagnosis question matters more. A visiting tutor who teaches all three sciences generically will not move a stalled grade, and neither will an online tutor who does the same. What moves it is someone who starts from the script.

sections.heading: The three papers, and what each one is really testing
paragraphs: Each of the three 4SD0 papers carries roughly a third of the qualification, and the two reported grades are derived from the whole. That symmetry on paper hides an asymmetry in difficulty: for most students the three papers are not equally hard, and more importantly they are not hard for the same reasons. Treating them as interchangeable blocks of revision time is why so much revision produces so little movement.

The biology paper rewards knowledge expressed in order. A student who knows what osmosis is will still lose marks if the answer names the effect before the cause, because the mark scheme follows the mechanism. The chemistry paper rewards an unbroken chain of working. The physics paper rewards accuracy in handling units and equations more than it rewards insight. Three different skills, three different kinds of preparation.

The table sets out what each paper tests, where the marks most often go, and what the first intervention should be. Read the last column carefully, because it is the one parents most often get backwards: the correct first move on a weak biology paper is usually not more biology, and the correct first move on a weak chemistry paper is almost never more past papers.

One further point about the structure. Because experimental skill is assessed inside these three written papers rather than in a separate practical, the experiment questions are distributed across all of them. A student who skips those questions in revision is skipping marks in three places rather than one, which is why that single habit shows up so clearly in a mock total.

sections.heading: Biology: four places the marks disappear, and what each one needs
paragraphs: Biology is the strand where Dubai students most often have the knowledge and the lowest return on it. The pattern is consistent: content revision is thorough, recall is good in conversation, and the written answers score around sixty per cent of what the knowledge should earn. That gap is almost entirely structural, and it is the cheapest gap on the course to close.

The first place marks go is mechanism order. A mark scheme for an osmosis or transpiration question awards points for naming the gradient, naming the direction of movement, naming the structure involved and linking them causally. A student who writes a true paragraph in the wrong order often satisfies two of four. The repair is to practise writing the four elements as a numbered sequence before writing prose, and it takes about two sessions to become automatic.

The second is the specificity of biological vocabulary. Water moves is not osmosis. Gets energy is not respiration. Mark schemes at this level accept a surprisingly narrow set of terms, and a student who has learned the idea in their own words will reliably under-score. The repair is a terminology list built from the student's own lost marks rather than from a textbook glossary, which makes it short and relevant.

The third is genetics presentation: crosses attempted without a key, Punnett squares drawn without labels, ratios stated without the phenotypes attached. These are marks available every series and lost on layout. The fourth is the experiment questions, where a student explains what should happen instead of reading the table printed in front of them. All four are technique, all four are diagnosable from one marked paper, and together they are frequently worth more than a term of additional content teaching.
bullets: Write the four mechanism elements as a numbered list before writing the answer
Build the terminology list from lost marks, not from the glossary
Never attempt a genetic cross without a key and labelled square
Answer experiment questions from the printed data, not from the theory

sections.heading: Chemistry: the calculation chain, and where it breaks
paragraphs: The chemistry strand is the one that justifies paid teaching hours on 4SD0, and the reason is structural rather than conceptual. Quantitative chemistry is a chain. Mass converts to moles, moles relate through the balanced equation, moles convert back to mass or volume or concentration. Every link depends on the one before it. A student who cannot do the first conversion reliably cannot attempt anything that follows, no matter how many past papers they are given.

This is why practice sheets fail here when they work elsewhere. In biology, attempting a question you cannot fully answer still earns partial marks and still teaches something. In a four-mark calculation, a wrong first step earns nothing and teaches the student only that chemistry is impossible. Confidence collapses faster in this strand than in any other, and by the spring of Year 11 the avoidance is often a bigger problem than the chemistry.

The work that moves it starts behind the visible problem. Establish that mass to moles is secure, twice, on unseen numbers. Then the balanced-equation ratio, twice. Then the return conversion. Only then the exam question that exposed the gap. This feels slow to a parent watching the calendar and it is the only sequence that holds, because each link has to be reliable before the next one can be built on it.

Alongside the chain sit two other chemistry losses worth naming. Rates and equilibria answers lose marks for describing an observation without explaining it in terms of particle collisions, frequency or energy, which is a vocabulary discipline rather than a content gap. And the recall content, ion tests, gas tests and the reactivity series, is routinely under-revised because it feels too easy to bother with, while carrying predictable marks in every series. A fortnight of structured recall usually banks several of them.
bullets: Test the mass-to-moles conversion on unseen numbers before anything else
Each link must be right twice before the next is introduced
Rates and equilibria answers must name collisions, frequency or energy
Schedule a fortnight of recall work on ion tests, gas tests and reactivity

sections.heading: Physics: right method, wrong number
paragraphs: The physics strand produces the most frustrating script to read, because the thinking is usually visible and correct and the mark is not awarded. A student selects the right equation, rearranges it correctly, substitutes carefully and loses the mark to a kilometre that should have been a metre, a milliamp that should have been an amp, or an answer written without units at all. These are not physics errors.

Unit discipline is a habit and it is taught by enforcement rather than explanation. Every quantity written down carries its unit, every substitution happens in base units, every final answer is checked for a unit before the pen moves on. A student who does this for three weeks stops losing the marks permanently. A student who is told about it once in a session loses them in the mock.

The second physics loss is standard form, which is really a maths loss wearing a physics costume. Wave calculations, radioactivity and electrical work all involve numbers in standard form, and a student uncomfortable with it will produce answers out by a factor of a thousand and not notice. If removing the physics from a dropped question leaves an arithmetic problem, the intervention belongs in Mathematics A, and spending that time on physics content is spending it in the wrong place.

The third is circuit reasoning. Series and parallel questions reward redrawing the circuit before touching a number, and most students do the opposite. A total resistance calculated correctly and then combined with the wrong voltage is a very common three-mark loss. Graph work completes the list: axes labelled with units, a line of best fit rather than a dot-to-dot, and a gradient read from two widely separated points on the line rather than from two printed data points.
bullets: Every quantity written down carries its unit, every time
Convert to base units at substitution, not at the end
If the dropped mark survives removing the physics, the work belongs in maths
Redraw the circuit before calculating anything

sections.heading: Experiments without a practical exam: how 4SD0 tests laboratory thinking
paragraphs: 4SD0 has no separately examined practical and no coursework, which parents often read as good news and students often read as permission to skip the experiment questions. Both readings are wrong. The practical thinking is still assessed; it has simply moved onto the written papers, where it appears as a described method, a table of results, or a graph, and asks the student to reason about it.

These questions follow a small number of forms, which makes them unusually learnable. Identify what was changed and what was measured. Name something that had to be kept the same and say why. Judge whether the method answers the question asked. Read a value off a table or a graph accurately. Draw a conclusion that refers to the data on the page. Suggest one specific improvement. That list covers most of what appears, across all three papers.

The characteristic failure is answering from theory. Asked what the results show, a student writes what the results should show according to the textbook, sometimes in direct contradiction of the table printed above the question. Mark schemes reward the data. This single habit, corrected, often returns four to eight marks across a full paper set, and it takes less time to correct than almost anything else on the course.

The second failure is vagueness in improvements. Repeat the experiment is not a mark. Repeat at each temperature and take a mean to reduce the effect of random error usually is. Specificity is the whole skill, and it is practised by writing improvements for experiments the student has never seen rather than by discussing the one they did in class.

sections.heading: Command words: the most repairable loss on the whole qualification
paragraphs: Command words are the verbs at the start of a question, and they are instructions rather than decoration. Describe asks what happens. Explain asks why it happens. Compare asks for a linked statement about both things, not two separate statements. Calculate asks for working. Suggest invites reasoning in an unfamiliar context and does not require a remembered fact. A student who treats all of these as write what you know will under-score across all three papers simultaneously.

The loss is large and nearly invisible on a report. A student who describes when asked to explain can write a long, accurate, well-spelled paragraph and collect one mark out of three. The script looks like a student who does not understand the topic. It is actually a student who did not read the verb, and the two need completely different responses from a tutor.

The repair is an audit. Take one full marked paper, mark every command word in the questions, and compare what each one asked for with what the student supplied. The pattern is usually narrow: most students misread one or two verbs consistently rather than all of them randomly. Once the pattern is named, it is corrected by writing answers to the verb for two or three sessions until the habit sticks.

A related discipline is mark allocation. A question worth four marks is asking for four distinct points, and a question worth one is not asking for a paragraph. Students who write three lines for every question regardless of value run out of time in the final third of the paper, which produces a loss that looks like a knowledge gap in the last topics and is really a pacing failure. Looking at the mark in brackets before writing is, unglamorously, one of the highest-return habits available.
bullets: Describe is what happens; explain is why it happens
Compare requires a linked statement, not two separate ones
Suggest rewards reasoning in an unfamiliar setting, not recall
Read the mark allocation before deciding how much to write

sections.heading: What one session can fix, what takes six, and what will not move in eight weeks
paragraphs: Tutoring is sold without timescales far too often, and the result is families buying the wrong product for the time they have. Some 4SD0 losses genuinely move in a single session. Others need a block. A few will not move at all in the weeks before a series, and knowing that in advance lets a family spend those weeks on the marks that are actually available.

Single-session repairs are the presentation problems: labelling a Punnett square, writing units on every answer, reading the mark allocation, structuring a four-mark explanation as four numbered points. These are rules, not skills. A student can be told, practise five examples, and have the mark back the same evening. Any provider who cannot name a few of these in the first conversation is not reading scripts.

Block-length repairs are the habits and the chains: the mass-to-moles sequence, the unit discipline, the command-word pattern, the experiment-question reflex. Four to six sessions with a timed paper at the end is the normal shape, and the evidence of success is a mark change on an unseen paper rather than a confident feeling at the end of a session.

What will not move in eight weeks is a two-year content deficit across all three strands. A student at grade 3 flat, who has not secured the Year 10 foundations in any paper, cannot be taken to a 6 by intensity, and pretending otherwise wastes both the money and the student's remaining confidence. The honest plan in that case targets the recoverable marks: recall content, experiment questions, command words, presentation, and the single strongest strand. That plan reliably moves a grade. It just does not move it as far as the family wanted, and saying so in week one is better than discovering it in results week.

sections.heading: Double Award or a single award: reading the strand marks before you decide
paragraphs: Families reach this question in Year 10, usually because an ambition has surfaced: medicine, engineering, a specific university route. The decision is treated as a matter of aspiration and it is really a matter of evidence, and the evidence sits in the strand marks that most parents have never seen because the reported grade hides them.

Ask the school for the per-paper breakdown. A student at 7 in biology and 4 in chemistry who wants to study medicine has a chemistry problem to solve before any route decision is meaningful, and moving into separate Biology while chemistry sits at 4 solves nothing. A student flat at 6 across all three who wants engineering has a genuine choice, because the foundation is even and the question becomes one of timetable and appetite.

Understand what the move costs in work. Separate Biology, Chemistry and Physics cover more content per science than the Double Award strands, and a mid-course switch means closing a content gap, which takes contact hours rather than technique sessions. A switch agreed in the first term of Year 10 is manageable. The same switch in the spring of Year 10 is a substantial undertaking, and in Year 11 it is rarely wise.

Finally, ask the destination rather than guessing it. Dubai sixth forms set their own entry thresholds and read Double Award and separate sciences differently for their own A Level and IB Diploma courses. An email to the sixth-form admissions lead naming your child's intended subjects will get a specific answer in writing, and it costs nothing. Tutoring aimed at a threshold that turns out not to apply is the most avoidable waste in this whole process, and no tutoring service should be the source of that threshold.
bullets: Get the per-paper breakdown before discussing routes at all
An uneven split is a repair job, not a route decision

process.title: Send one marked paper, not a summary
process.description: A marked 4SD0 script with the examiner or teacher annotations visible tells a tutor more in ten minutes than a full report does. Where the school publishes per-paper marks, send those too. A description of the problem is useful context; the script is the evidence the plan is built from.

process.title: The trial session is a diagnostic
process.description: The tutor sets questions drawn from the weakest paper and watches how the student approaches them, where they stop and what they write when unsure. The output is a written note naming the loss categories in order of size, which you keep regardless of whether you continue.

process.title: One loss category at a time
process.description: Sessions attack the largest category first rather than working through the syllabus. If the audit says command words are costing more than content, command words get the time. Each session ends with unseen questions targeting the same category so the gain can be checked rather than assumed.

process.title: A timed paper between sessions
process.description: From the spring of Year 10 onward, the student sits a timed paper or section between sessions and it is marked against the published criteria. Progress is measured as a mark change on work the student had not seen, which is the only measure that survives contact with an exam hall.

process.title: Review, then decide
process.description: At the end of a block the categories are re-audited on a fresh marked paper. The next decision follows from that: continue on the same category, move to the next largest, switch paper, or stop. Sessions run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

whyPoints.title: The diagnosis comes from a script
whyPoints.description: Every plan starts with marked work rather than with a conversation about how the term has felt. The loss categories are named and ranked in writing, and the session order follows that ranking rather than the order of the syllabus.

whyPoints.title: One tutor across all three papers
whyPoints.description: 4SD0 is one qualification. A single lead tutor can see that the physics loss is a standard-form problem and the biology loss is a sentence-order problem, and can decide which of the two deserves the next hour. Three separate bookings cannot make that call.

whyPoints.title: Technique before content, where the script says so
whyPoints.description: Most stalled 4SD0 grades are losing more marks to answer order, units and command words than to missing knowledge. Where the evidence shows that, sessions start there, because those are the fastest marks on the course to recover.

whyPoints.title: Experiment questions get deliberate time
whyPoints.description: Because 4SD0 assesses practical thinking inside the written papers, those questions are practised as their own category rather than absorbed into content revision. That single habit is worth several marks across a full paper set.

whyPoints.title: An honest timescale, stated in week one
whyPoints.description: Some losses move in a session, some in a block, and a two-year content deficit does not clear in eight weeks. The plan says which case your child is in before you commit, and names the marks that are genuinely recoverable in the time available.

whyPoints.title: The student's own work stays their own
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question, mark and give feedback on responses the student has written. Nothing is supplied for submission under a student's name, and Pearson papers and mark schemes are referenced and linked rather than distributed.

faqs.question: Can we get a home tutor for Edexcel IGCSE Science Double Award 4SD0 in Dubai?
faqs.answer: In-home tuition does exist in Dubai and the market serves it, so the honest answer is yes, families can find one. IB Gram is not that provider: home visits are a service offered only in India, and UAE delivery is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For a Year 10 or 11 student on 4SD0 that trade usually works in your favour, because what this qualification needs is someone strong on the specific paper the script names, and that person is unlikely to be the one who happens to cover your community on a Tuesday afternoon.

faqs.question: What exactly do the three 4SD0 papers test?
faqs.answer: Each of the three written papers covers one science and carries roughly a third of the qualification, with two International GCSE grades reported from the whole. The biology paper tests recall plus explanation written in the order a process happens. The chemistry paper tests an unbroken chain of quantitative working. The physics paper tests equation selection, rearrangement and unit handling. Experimental thinking and command-word accuracy are tested across all three. Those are four different skills, and revision that treats them as one block of science is why effort often fails to show up in the mark.

faqs.question: How are experiments assessed in 4SD0 if there is no practical exam?
faqs.answer: Practical thinking moves onto the written papers. Questions describe a method, print a table of results or show a graph, and ask the student to identify the variables, name a control and justify it, read values accurately, judge whether the method answers the question, draw a conclusion from the printed data and suggest a specific improvement. There is no coursework and no separate practical to prepare. The marks are learnable because the question forms repeat, and the usual loss is answering from the textbook instead of from the data in front of them.

faqs.question: Which command words cost 4SD0 students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Describe and explain, confused in both directions, account for the largest share. A student who describes what happens when the question asked why it happens can write a long, accurate paragraph and collect one mark of three, which on a report looks exactly like not understanding the topic. Compare is the next most expensive, because it needs a linked statement about both things rather than two separate statements. Most students misread one or two verbs consistently rather than all of them randomly, so an audit of one marked paper usually finds a narrow, correctable pattern.

faqs.question: My child knows the biology but keeps losing explanation marks. What fixes that?
faqs.answer: Answer order, almost always. Mark schemes for mechanism questions award points for naming the gradient or cause, the direction of the effect, the structure involved and the causal link between them. A true paragraph written in the wrong sequence often satisfies two of four. The repair is to write the required elements as a numbered list before writing prose, practise it on the student's own marked responses, and check it on unseen questions. It typically becomes automatic within two sessions, which makes it among the cheapest marks on the course to recover.

faqs.question: Where does the chemistry calculation chain usually break for Double Award students?
faqs.answer: At the first conversion, from mass to moles. Quantitative chemistry is sequential: mass to moles, moles through the balanced equation, moles back to mass, volume or concentration. If the first link is unreliable, nothing after it is reachable, and handing the student more past papers teaches only that chemistry is impossible. The work has to start behind the visible problem, establish each link twice on unseen numbers, and only then attempt the exam question that exposed the gap. Four to six sequential sessions is the normal shape for that rebuild.

faqs.question: Why does my child get the physics content right and the numbers wrong?
faqs.answer: Two causes, and they need different work. The first is unit discipline: a correct equation and a correct rearrangement lose the mark to a kilometre that should have been a metre, or to a final answer with no unit written. That is a habit, fixed by enforcement over about three weeks. The second is standard form, which is a maths problem wearing a physics costume and shows up in wave, radioactivity and electrical questions as answers out by a factor of a thousand. If removing the physics leaves an arithmetic problem, the work belongs in Mathematics A.

faqs.question: How are two grades worked out from three 4SD0 papers?
faqs.answer: Science Double Award is a single qualification that reports two International GCSE grades on the 9 to 1 scale, derived from performance across all three written papers rather than from any one of them. The practical consequence for revision is that strengthening the weakest paper moves the overall outcome further than polishing the strongest, which is the opposite of what students naturally do. Ask the school for the per-paper marks, because the reported grades hide the internal split and that split is what a tuition plan should be built from.

faqs.question: Is a 4SD0 grade enough for A Level or IB Diploma science in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Often, and it depends entirely on the individual school and the individual course. Many sixth forms accept Double Award grades for science A Levels and IB Diploma science courses, while some ask for a separate science for a Higher Level or A Level course in that same discipline. Dubai sixth forms set their own thresholds and read the two routes differently. Email the sixth-form admissions lead naming your child's intended subjects and get the requirement in writing. No tutoring service should be your source for that threshold, including this one.

faqs.question: Should my child move from Double Award to a single-award science?
faqs.answer: Decide it from the strand marks, not from the ambition. A student at 7 in biology and 4 in chemistry who wants medicine has a chemistry repair to make before any route question is meaningful. A student flat at 6 across all three has a real choice. Understand the cost in work: the separate sciences cover more content per subject, so a switch means closing a content gap with contact hours rather than technique sessions. A move agreed early in Year 10 is manageable; the same move in Year 11 rarely is.

faqs.question: How many marks are actually recoverable in the eight weeks before a series?
faqs.answer: It depends on what kind of loss the script shows, which is why an honest answer needs the script first. Presentation and command-word losses, experiment-question habits, unit discipline and recall content are all genuinely available in that window, and together they often total more than families expect. A two-year content deficit across all three strands is not available in eight weeks, and a provider promising otherwise is selling intensity rather than a plan. The useful move is to name the recoverable marks in week one and spend the window entirely on those.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for 4SD0 when so much of it involves experiments?
faqs.answer: It works well, partly because of how 4SD0 assesses practical work. There is no separate practical exam: experimental thinking is tested through methods, tables and graphs printed on the written papers, which is screen-based work by nature. A tutor can annotate a results table live, cover the theory to force a data-only answer, and save the annotated version for the student to re-read. The laboratory work your child does at school remains the school's job. The exam skill is reading and reasoning about experiments on paper.

faqs.question: Can one tutor really cover biology, chemistry and physics properly?
faqs.answer: For Double Award, yes, and it is usually better. 4SD0 covers less content per science than the separate 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 qualifications, so the depth required in each is within reach of a science teacher who has taught at this level. The decisive advantage is cross-paper judgement: one tutor can see that a physics loss is really standard form and a biology loss is really sentence order, and decide which deserves the next hour. For separate sciences at the top end, specialist tutors per subject make more sense.

faqs.question: What should we send before the first 4SD0 session?
faqs.answer: One marked paper with the annotations visible, the per-paper marks if the school publishes them, and the school's scheme of work or current topic list if you have it. Three documents, no covering essay needed. The marked paper is the one that matters, because it shows where marks went rather than what the total was. If the only thing available is a reported grade, send that and the tutor will set a diagnostic paper in the trial session instead, which costs a session but produces the same evidence.

faqs.question: How do we tell whether the problem is science or maths?
faqs.answer: Take the chemistry and physics questions your child dropped and mentally strip out the science. If what remains is rearranging a formula, handling a ratio, converting units or reading a gradient, the blockage is Mathematics A and science tuition will not clear it. This test takes about twenty minutes with a marked paper and regularly redirects a whole term of planned work. It is also the question a tutor should raise in the first conversation rather than the fifth, and an unwillingness to raise it is worth noticing.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-science-double-award.closingHeading: Start with the script, not the grade
dubai/edexcel-igcse-science-double-award.closingBody: A reported 4SD0 grade tells you that something is wrong. A marked paper tells you what, and the two lead to very different plans. Send one marked script and the per-paper marks, take the free trial as a diagnostic session, and read the written note that comes back: it will name the loss categories in order of size and say which of them move in one session, which need a block, and which will not clear before the next series. If the answer is that Mathematics A deserves the first six hours rather than science, you will be told that. Sessions run one-to-one over live video, scheduled around the Dubai school day.

intro.heading: What a 4SD0 tutor costs in Dubai, and what that price is actually attached to
paragraphs: Start with the number, because that is why you are here. Across Dubai, International GCSE science tuition is advertised from roughly AED 45 an hour at the university-student end up to AED 650 at the named-examiner end. EdFlik publishes rates from AED 45 to AED 65. Tutopiya lists sessions from AED 33 to AED 52. Unitors quotes International GCSE tuition from AED 150. TutorChase quotes AED 270. BartyED quotes AED 650. Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to AED 350, and specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Those are their published figures, not ours, and the range is wide enough that an hourly rate on its own tells a parent almost nothing useful.

What the rate is attached to matters more than the rate itself. Science Double Award, Pearson code 4SD0, is a single qualification assessed by three written papers covering biology, chemistry and physics, and it reports two International GCSE grades on the 9 to 1 scale. Parents who read that as three subjects go looking for three tutors and get quoted three times over. It is one timetable problem. In most cases one tutor holding all three papers is both cheaper and more useful than three specialists who each see a third of the picture and none of whom owns the revision plan.

The second thing the price attaches to is diagnosis. A quote given before anyone has read a marked script is a guess wearing the clothes of a plan. Two students sitting on the same grade 5 can need entirely different work. One is losing marks on chemistry calculations and needs real teaching hours. The other knows the biology perfectly and is giving away explanation marks on answer order, which is a two-to-four-session fix. The first student's year costs several times the second's. Any provider quoting a package before seeing evidence is pricing the average student, and your child is not the average student.

Dubai's own school market is the third variable, and this one is specific to the emirate. KHDA inspects 227 private schools serving 387,441 students across seventeen curricula, with UK-curriculum schools accounting for 37 per cent of enrolment, the largest single block in the city. That depth means a wide local pool of teachers who know Pearson International GCSE science well, which keeps the qualified-tutor tier genuinely competitive on price. It also means Year 11 demand arrives in one concentrated wave each spring, and the tutors with the strongest chemistry reputations are committed by January.

The fourth and fifth variables are format and timing, and they are the two you control outright. Online one-to-one strips out the travel component that in-home rates exist to recover, and it widens the pool from whoever lives within a sensible drive of your community to whoever is genuinely strongest on the chemistry paper. Timing is the other lever. The same tutor booked in September of Year 10 costs less per mark gained than the same tutor booked in March of Year 11, because the work available in September is teaching and the work available in March is triage.

IB Gram delivers this as one-to-one online tuition over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the Dubai school day. Home visits are an India-only service and are not sold anywhere in the UAE. dubai/edexcel-igcse-science-double-award.programmesIntro: Science Double Award sits inside a decision chain that starts in Year 9 and does not finish until a Year 12 subject choice is signed off. Each stage below has a different cost profile, and knowing which stage your child is in tells you whether you are buying teaching hours, marks-recovery hours, or a single conversation about route choice.

programmes.name: Choosing science at the end of Year 9
programmes.description: The cheapest intervention available in the whole chain, and the one almost nobody buys. A single session reading the Year 9 science reports against the Double Award and separate-science routes can save a family a year of unnecessary tuition. The question is not which route is harder. It is which route matches how your child's marks currently split across biology, chemistry and physics, and what they intend to study after 16.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai British-curriculum schools typically ask for option choices between January and March of Year 9, with places on separate sciences capped by laboratory and timetable capacity rather than by ambition. If the school has already allocated your child to Double Award, that is a timetable fact to plan around, not a verdict on ability, and it does not close a science A Level route by itself.

programmes.name: Science Double Award (4SD0)
programmes.description: Three written papers, one each in biology, chemistry and physics, each worth about a third of the whole, reported as two International GCSE grades. There is no coursework component and no separately examined practical, so experimental skill is tested through descriptions of experiments on the page. For costing purposes, treat it as one subject with three revision streams rather than as three subjects with one tutor.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this is the most common science route for students who intend to carry one science, not three, into Year 12. It is the route that lets a student protect timetable room for a strong humanities or business subject, which matters in a city where business and engineering degrees pull most of the post-16 traffic.

programmes.name: Separate sciences: 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1
programmes.description: Three distinct qualifications, three sets of papers, three reported grades. Content goes deeper than the Double Award equivalent in each science, and the tuition bill behaves accordingly, because a weak strand cannot be carried by the other two. Families comparing routes on cost alone should compare total tuition hours across two years, not hourly rates, since the separate route tends to need more of them.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools running the Pearson separate sciences often set an internal attainment threshold in Year 9 before allowing all three. A student moving from Double Award into a single award mid-Year 10 is the scenario where tuition cost spikes, because the gap is content, not technique, and content takes contact hours.

programmes.name: November resit and private-candidate entry
programmes.description: Pearson International GCSE subjects are examined in a May or June series and again in November each year, so a disappointing summer grade is not a year lost. A resit plan is a short, specific, paper-level piece of work rather than a fresh two-year course, and it should be priced that way: a block of sessions aimed at the weakest paper, not a general science course repeated.
programmes.countryNote: A student no longer enrolled at a Dubai school sits as a private candidate through a centre that accepts external entries, and the centre sets both its own entry fee and its own registration cut-off. Confirm that cut-off before buying tuition hours, because the entry deadline, not the exam date, is what fixes your calendar.

programmes.name: What a Double Award opens after 16
programmes.description: Two science grades from 4SD0 are accepted for many A Level and IB Diploma science entries, though individual schools set their own thresholds and some ask for a separate science for a Higher Level or A Level course in that discipline. This is a conversation to have with the sixth-form admissions lead in Year 11 autumn, not in results week, and it costs nothing but an email.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai sixth forms split sharply between A Level and IB Diploma, and the two read a Double Award differently. Ask the specific school what it accepts, in writing, before paying for tuition aimed at a grade threshold that may not be the threshold that applies to your child's intended course.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-science-double-award.subjectsIntro: Cost follows the strand, not the subject label. The list below prices the work rather than the content: which parts of 4SD0 absorb real teaching hours, which parts respond to a short technique block, and which neighbouring Pearson subjects a family usually ends up buying alongside it.

subjects.name: Biology strand within 4SD0
subjects.description: Usually the least expensive strand to support. The content is largely factual, so marks go missing on writing rather than on understanding, and explanation questions wanting a mechanism in sequence are the main leak. A short technique block on answer order typically moves this paper further than a term of content teaching would.

subjects.name: Chemistry strand within 4SD0
subjects.description: The strand that justifies paid hours. Moles, equation balancing, reacting masses and concentration calculations are sequential: a gap three steps back makes the visible question unanswerable. This is where a specialist block earns its rate, and where buying the cheapest available hour reliably costs more over a year.

subjects.name: Physics strand within 4SD0
subjects.description: Priced between the other two. The physics content is narrower than a separate 4PH1 course, but the marks depend on unit handling, equation rearrangement and reading values off a graph accurately. Numeracy work bought for this paper usually pays a second time on the chemistry calculations.

subjects.name: Experimental skills across the three papers
subjects.description: Assessed inside the written papers rather than in a separate practical, which removes a cost line that families expect to see. The marks hang on identifying independent and dependent variables, spotting what was controlled, and writing a conclusion that refers to the data rather than to the theory.

subjects.name: Separate Biology (4BI1)
subjects.description: The route for a student aiming at medicine, dentistry or biomedical science. Deeper content than the Double Award biology strand, and the tuition profile shifts from technique to content coverage, which means more hours at the same rate rather than a higher rate.

subjects.name: Separate Chemistry (4CH1)
subjects.description: The most common upgrade request from Double Award families, and the most expensive one to execute mid-course. Organic chemistry and quantitative work carry the extra load. Budget a content block rather than weekly maintenance if the switch happens after Year 10 has started.

subjects.name: Separate Physics (4PH1)
subjects.description: Mathematically the heaviest of the three separate sciences at this level. Students who cope well with the 4SD0 physics strand sometimes still struggle here, because the algebra density rises. A joint physics and Mathematics A plan is usually better value than two unconnected bookings.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (4MA1)
subjects.description: The subject that quietly determines the 4SD0 chemistry and physics grades. Rearranging formulae, ratio, standard form and percentage change appear in both. Families often buy science tuition when the actual blockage is the maths underneath it, which is a cheaper problem to fix.

subjects.name: English Language A (4EA1)
subjects.description: Relevant to a science grade more than parents expect. Extended explanation answers in 4SD0 are marked on whether the reasoning is legible, and a student who writes loosely in English writes loosely in biology. A shared booking across both subjects is common in Dubai.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Runs alongside the Pearson curriculum rather than inside it. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed international curriculum, and the weekly hours they take are part of the time budget any science plan has to fit around.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-science-double-award.regionsIntro: Where a family lives in Dubai changes the logistics of a tuition plan rather than the syllabus. The notes below are about session timing, school-run patterns and local demand, because those are the things that decide whether a 16:00 slot is realistic and whether an in-home rate is worth its premium in your community.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches
regions.note: Villa community with a long school-run tail. Families here commonly book from 16:30 onward, after the second drop-off wave. An in-home tutor crossing from Deira or Bur Dubai prices the return leg into the hour, which is exactly the component an online slot removes.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Dense in British-curriculum families and short of weekday evening availability, because the local demand wave is concentrated. Online booking widens the pool beyond tutors already committed in this postcode, which matters most for the chemistry strand.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle
regions.note: Apartment-heavy, with students travelling out to schools in Al Barsha and Dubai Hills. The commute eats the window between 15:00 and 16:30, so sessions here tend to settle at 17:00 or later, and weekend mornings carry more of the plan than they do in villa districts.

regions.name: Mirdif
regions.note: Established family district feeding several large British-curriculum schools. Year 11 demand here peaks early in the spring term, which is the practical argument for booking science support in the autumn rather than after the mocks are returned.

regions.name: Al Barsha
regions.note: School-dense, which means traffic rather than convenience between 13:30 and 16:00. A tutor who would spend forty minutes each way reaching a Barsha address is charging for seventy minutes of road time inside a sixty-minute lesson fee.

regions.name: Dubai Marina
regions.note: Apartment living with limited quiet study space during family evenings. Shorter, more frequent online sessions tend to work better here than a single long block, and the saving on travel usually funds the extra contact point.

regions.name: The Springs and The Meadows
regions.note: Short internal commutes but a narrow pool of locally resident science specialists. Families here are the clearest beneficiaries of a wider online pool, because the constraint is specialist availability rather than distance.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Mixed school catchment with high demand for exam-series intensives. Pre-mock blocks book out here first, so the November and spring windows need to be reserved a term ahead if a specific tutor matters to you.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai Hills, Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: A cluster of large British-curriculum secondaries where Pearson and Cambridge International GCSE entries sit side by side, sometimes within the same science department. Students we support in this cluster most often arrive with a chemistry-strand problem and a Year 11 mock result that has just landed.

schoolClusters.city: Arabian Ranches, Mirdif and Dubai Silicon Oasis
schoolClusters.note: Villa-belt and eastern Dubai schools with large Year 11 cohorts and a strong separate-science tradition in some departments. The route conversation here is often about moving between Double Award and a single award, which is a cost question as much as an academic one.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School, Arabian Ranches
