sections.heading: Scheduling an evening slot that survives the term
paragraphs: A slot that collapses in week five has cost more than it delivered, and the collapse is almost always predictable. Three things kill a Dubai evening slot: an activity that starts at the same time in the second half of term, a parent's travel pattern that was not accounted for, and a slot chosen in the first week of September before the bus timetable settled. The fix is to provisionally book for two weeks and then fix the term slot once the real return time is known.

Ramadan reshapes the evening entirely. School days shorten, the useful study window moves to after Iftar, and the early evening becomes impractical for fasting households. The two patterns that work are a post-Iftar slot on weekdays and a late-morning slot at weekends. Booking the change a fortnight ahead matters because the post-Iftar window is the single most contested hour in the Dubai tutoring calendar, and it does not expand to meet demand.

The other predictable disruptions are the winter break in December, the spring break in late March or April, and the examination series itself. Most families keep the slot through the breaks at a reduced frequency rather than stopping, because restarting in January means re-establishing a routine from nothing. During the examination series itself the pattern usually inverts: sessions move to mornings between papers, and the evening slot is released. Telling us that a fortnight ahead costs nothing and means the slot can be held for the following year rather than lost.

sections.heading: Rates, coverage and how evening delivery actually works
paragraphs: Published 2026 market rates in Dubai put a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and a subject specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more, with budget online tutoring from around AED 45 to 150 and in-home visits at AED 180 to 500 with travel included. Published monthly figures include AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those come from published 2026 rate cards and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 survey, and they are market figures rather than IB Gram's price list.

The day and the hour do not generally change an online rate, which is worth knowing because the in-home market does charge differently for an evening visit, since the tutor is driving in peak traffic for one hour of work. What does change the number is the level of specialist you need: a Standard Level content gap and a Higher Level option topic are different purchases, and paying specialist rates for the former is a common and avoidable mistake.

Sessions run online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared whiteboard and screen sharing, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India. Coverage is stated before anything is booked: common Diploma subjects at both levels are matched within a few days, Higher Level option topics and second language A subjects take longer, and where the available tutor is based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time we say so rather than implying a local presence.

process.title: Watch the first two weeks before fixing a slot
process.description: Note what time your child is actually home, fed and able to sit down, and what nights have activities in the second half of term. A provisional booking for two weeks costs nothing and prevents the week-five collapse that is the commonest failure in evening tutoring arrangements.

process.title: Free 45-minute diagnostic lesson
process.description: One session, no card details taken, no obligation to continue. The tutor marks work your child has already done and returns the two or three specific recurring losses in writing. That list then becomes the source of every weekly objective rather than a general sense that a subject is hard.

process.title: Match the objective to the hour
process.description: New content needs 16:30 to 18:30. Practice and marking work at any point up to 20:00. Review, planning and core-component discussion survive a late slot. Choosing the hour to fit the work rather than the diary is the difference between twelve things fixed and twelve pleasant conversations.

process.title: One objective per session, written down
process.description: Each hour starts with the objective already agreed and ends with a note naming what to do before the next one. If a session opens with what shall we do today, fifteen minutes of a paid hour has gone on deciding. The notes also make the term reviewable, which a parent cannot do from memory.

process.title: Add a weekend block when measurement is needed
process.description: The evening hour cannot hold a full timed paper. Once a baseline is needed, usually by the end of the first month, book one longer weekend block to sit and mark a paper. Keep the evening hour for teaching and use the long block as the measurement point.

whyPoints.title: One objective per hour, agreed in advance
whyPoints.description: The failure mode of evening tutoring is not the sixty minutes, it is arriving without a plan. Every session has a named objective set from the loss list and ends with a written note. Twelve weeks of that is twelve specific things fixed rather than twelve agreeable hours.

whyPoints.title: The hour matched to the work
whyPoints.description: New content taught at 16:30 lands; the same content taught at 21:00 usually does not survive the night. We say which work suits which slot rather than taking whatever booking is offered, including declining a late booking for first-time teaching of a Higher Level topic.

whyPoints.title: Gulf Standard Time works in your favour late
whyPoints.description: A 19:00 Dubai slot is mid-afternoon in the United Kingdom and early evening in South Asia, so the later Dubai hours draw on a wider specialist pool than the early ones. Families flexible about 19:00 or 20:00 are usually offered a stronger subject match.

whyPoints.title: No travel cost on either side of the hour
whyPoints.description: A tuition centre class costs the drive in both directions in the evening peak, and an in-home tutor prices that travel into the rate. An online hour costs sixty minutes of the evening and gives sixty minutes of attention to one student's own work.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here is attributed to a published 2026 rate card or Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 survey, with the format it applies to. They are the market's figures, not ours. Most pages ranking for this query publish no price at all.

whyPoints.title: Honest boundaries on coursework
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, explains criteria and asks questions; the student writes every sentence of their own internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge work. The school supervisor remains the official process. We state this plainly because the alternative puts the candidate at risk.

faqs.question: What time do evening IB sessions start in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Slots run from about 16:30 to 21:00 Gulf Standard Time, Sunday to Thursday, with weekend options separately. The practical earliest depends on your community: school buses return between roughly 15:15 and 16:30, so a 16:30 start works in communities where the school is close and a 17:30 start is more realistic in the outer developments. The 18:00 to 20:00 window is the most contested in the emirate, which is why early and late slots usually come with a wider choice of specialist.

faqs.question: Can my child really learn anything in one hour after a full school day?
faqs.answer: One thing, done properly. A single technique drilled to fluency, one question type practised until the pattern changes, one section of an internal assessment draft read against its criteria, or a set of six past-paper questions marked and understood. What an hour cannot do is cover a term's backlog, prepare three subjects at once or hold a two-hour timed paper. Sessions that try to do those produce thirty minutes of conversation and thirty of skimming, which is where evening tutoring usually goes wrong.

faqs.question: Is a 21:00 slot worth booking at all?
faqs.answer: Only for the right work. New material taught at that hour rarely survives to the next morning, because there is no consolidation time before sleep, and sleep debt in the Diploma years degrades exactly what the papers test: working memory under time pressure and accuracy late in a long paper. What does survive a late hour is reviewing a script already marked, planning the next week's work, choosing a Theory of Knowledge exhibition object or discussing an Extended Essay research question. A tutor should decline a late booking for first-time teaching.

faqs.question: Why are late Dubai slots sometimes easier to fill than early ones?
faqs.answer: Because of the clock. Dubai runs on Gulf Standard Time, four hours ahead of Coordinated Universal Time, so a 19:00 Dubai session is 15:00 in London, 16:00 in continental Europe and 20:30 in Mumbai, all of which are ordinary working hours for a subject teacher. A 16:30 Dubai session is lunchtime in the United Kingdom, which is harder to staff. Families who can take 19:00 or 20:00 are drawing on a wider pool of specialists and usually get a better subject match for the same money.

faqs.question: Should we book two subjects on the same evening?
faqs.answer: No. The second hour of concentration on a school night produces notes rather than learning, and the student usually arrives at the second session already finished. Two subjects belong on two evenings, and three evenings a week is the practical ceiling for a Diploma student carrying homework in six subjects. Beyond that the homework suffers, which costs more than the tutoring gains. Where two subjects must share an evening, 45 minutes each with a break is better than two full hours.

faqs.question: How does an evening online hour compare with a tuition centre class?
faqs.answer: On arithmetic rather than quality. A 90-minute centre class with 25 minutes of driving each way in the Dubai evening peak costs about two hours and twenty minutes of a school night and delivers 90 minutes of teaching shared across a group, in which a student might ask two questions. An online one-to-one hour costs sixty minutes and delivers sixty minutes directed at that student's own losses. Centres are cheaper per hour and suit content delivery where a whole group has the same gap.

faqs.question: What does an evening session cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published 2026 market rates put a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and a subject specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more. Budget online tutoring runs around AED 45 to 150. In-home visits are AED 180 to 500 with travel built in, and the evening premium is real in that market because the tutor is driving in peak traffic for one hour of work. Online rates generally do not change with the hour. Those bands come from published rate cards and the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 survey.

faqs.question: How do I know the hour is being used properly?
faqs.answer: Ask for two artefacts. The objective, agreed before the session rather than decided during it, and a written note afterwards naming what was done and what to practise. Keep the notes. After six weeks you can read them in sequence and see whether the same problem is still being addressed, which is the single most useful review a parent can do. A session that opens with what shall we do today has already spent fifteen minutes of a paid hour deciding.

faqs.question: Can an evening hour be used for internal assessment work?
faqs.answer: It is one of the best uses of the hour, particularly in Year 12. One session with the published criteria and a draft section in front of the student, asking which band the section currently sits in and what the band above requires, moves a mark more than a month of general content revision. The student makes every change themselves. A tutor who rewrites a section has created a malpractice risk that falls on the candidate, and the school-appointed supervisor remains the official process throughout.

faqs.question: What happens to our evening slot during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: It moves, and the change is worth booking a fortnight ahead. School days shorten, the early evening becomes impractical for fasting households and the useful window shifts to after Iftar, with late-morning slots at weekends as the alternative. The post-Iftar hour is the most contested slot in the Dubai calendar and does not expand to meet demand. Timed practice is harder during fasting hours, so Ramadan evenings are usually better spent on draft work and consolidation than on new content.

faqs.question: Do we keep the slot through the winter and spring breaks?
faqs.answer: Most families do, at a reduced frequency, because restarting in January means rebuilding a routine from nothing. During the breaks the useful change is to move the session to a morning, where a student can take new content properly rather than at the end of a long day. The spring break in particular is the highest-value fortnight before the May series, and the families who use it are the ones who booked those slots in February.

faqs.question: My child's slot collapsed after a month. What went wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost always one of three things: an activity that started at the same time in the second half of term, a parent's travel pattern nobody accounted for, or a slot chosen in the first week of September before the school bus timetable settled. The fix is to book provisionally for two weeks, observe the real return time and the real activity schedule, then fix the term slot. That costs nothing and prevents the commonest failure in evening arrangements.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take two of my children in consecutive evening hours?
faqs.answer: Yes, where the subjects allow it, and online delivery is what makes it practical: two consecutive hours cost two hours, with no travel gap between them and no second travel charge. Each child gets a separate objective and a separate written note. Where the subjects do not overlap, two tutors can be booked back to back in the same window, which is common in households with a Middle Years student and a Diploma student.

faqs.question: Do I need a weekend block as well as the evening hour?
faqs.answer: Eventually, yes, if you want a measurement. The evening hour cannot hold a full timed paper plus the marking conversation, and without a timed paper there is no baseline to judge progress against. The usual arrangement is a weekly evening hour for teaching plus one longer weekend block a month to sit and mark a paper. The hour does the work; the block measures it. In the final term that ratio often reverses.

faqs.question: Where do evening lessons take place?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared whiteboard and screen sharing, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India. In the evening that distinction has a practical edge: nobody is driving anywhere, the hour starts on time, and the tutor is chosen for teaching your child's subject at the right level rather than for being able to reach your community before 18:00.

dubai/evening-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Fix the hour, then fix the objective
dubai/evening-ib-tutor.closingBody: Watch two weeks of real return times before committing to a slot, then take the free 45-minute diagnostic, which takes no card details and carries no obligation. The tutor marks work your child has already done and returns two or three specific recurring losses in writing. Those become the weekly objectives, one per hour, each written down before the session and reviewed after it. If you want a number to judge the term by, add one longer weekend block a month and sit a full paper in it. The hour teaches; the block measures.

dubai/experienced-ib-tutor.tutorsIntro: Each tutor profile below names the subject, the level, the papers that tutor teaches to and the components they have marked. Those four facts are the ones worth comparing. You approve the proposed match before anything is scheduled, and the first session is the free one.

intro.heading: Four kinds of experience, and only two of them mark papers
paragraphs: The word experienced appears on almost every tutoring page in this city and it is doing four separate jobs. It can mean years in a classroom teaching this syllabus. It can mean having sat the Diploma recently and scored well. It can mean having taught many students in this subject without ever having taught it in a school. Or it can mean having marked work against the published assessment criteria often enough to know where an examiner stops giving credit. These are genuinely different capabilities and they are worth very different amounts to a particular student.

A recent graduate with a 7 in Higher Level Chemistry has something real: a fresh memory of what the course felt like, current familiarity with the material and credibility with a seventeen-year-old. What they usually do not have is a sense of the distribution. They know how they answered a question, not how two hundred students answered it, and the difference matters because the common failure modes are a population fact rather than a personal one. A teacher who has taken five cohorts through the same paper has seen the same mistake eighty times and knows which explanation finally lands.

The capability that actually changes grades, though, is marking. A tutor who routinely reads student work against the published criteria develops a specific skill: locating the exact point in a written answer where the credit stops. That is not the same as knowing the subject, and plenty of people who know the subject extremely well cannot do it. It is also the capability least visible in any advertisement, which is why this page is built around how to test for it rather than around claims about it.

What a parent can do about all this is more than it seems. Experience is testable in a short conversation and in a single free session, provided you ask for the right things. Send a marked script in advance and watch what the tutor does with it. Ask which component the student is losing most in and how they know. Ask what the commonest mistake is on that paper and what they do about it. The answers separate the four kinds of experience almost immediately, and none of the questions requires you to know the subject.

One point about how this works in practice. Every IB Gram match in the UAE is one student with one tutor, delivered over live video with the student writing on a shared whiteboard. There are no premises in Dubai and no home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service offered only in India. Any dirham figure quoted on this page is a market rate with its publisher named, and the only commitment made is a free first lesson, one per student and one student per family, with no card details collected.

dubai/experienced-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: Experience is programme-specific in a way families rarely check. A tutor who is excellent with Diploma papers may never have read a Middle Years criterion descriptor, and a primary specialist is doing a different job entirely. These are the three programmes Dubai schools run, with the kind of experience each genuinely requires.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: There is no external examination and no published assessment criteria to mark against, so relevant experience here is early-years pedagogy rather than IB expertise. What matters is whether the tutor can teach reading accurately, hear a child decode and intervene at the right moment, and build number fluency without destroying confidence. A Diploma specialist is usually the wrong match for a seven-year-old regardless of how well they know their subject.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai primary cohorts include many children who have changed curriculum mid-year, so the most valuable experience in this emirate is having seen that pattern often enough to tell a genuine difficulty from a sequencing difference between systems. KHDA's mandatory Arabic streams also start in these years, taught separately for Arab and non-Arab students, and support must follow the school's own stream.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Every Middle Years subject is marked against four criteria labelled A to D, each out of 8, with the school converting criterion totals into a 1-7 grade. Relevant experience here means having read those descriptors closely enough to tell a parent which strand is capping their child, in that subject, from their child's own written work. A tutor who has only taught Diploma content will often miss this entirely, because the Diploma does not work that way.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai continuum schools frequently run Middle Years to Grade 10 before offering a Diploma or British route, so experience of both destinations is genuinely useful here. The most valuable thing an experienced tutor does for a Grade 9 family in this emirate is give an honest read on whether writing stamina and algebraic fluency will survive Higher Level, which is a judgement built from having seen students make that jump.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects on a 45-point total, internally assessed work in every one, plus Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. This is where marking experience separates tutors decisively, because Diploma marks are lost in the structure of written answers and in criterion wording rather than in missing facts. A tutor who cannot tell you which component a student is losing in, from the student's own scripts, has not done this work before whatever their subject knowledge.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's Diploma provision sits in fewer schools than the surrounding British sector, and each runs its own internal assessment calendar. An experienced tutor in this emirate asks which school before anything else, because the same subject needs different phasing depending on whether that school sets its internal deadlines in October or in January. Tutors new to the UAE market frequently do not know to ask.

dubai/experienced-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: This is where experience becomes concrete. For each subject, the thing a student most often loses marks on at Higher Level, and the question an experienced tutor will ask to find out whether that is what is happening with your child. If a tutor cannot answer in these terms, they know the syllabus rather than the paper.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Marks go on working presented out of the order the mark scheme rewards, on proof structure, and on calculus set up correctly then executed carelessly. An experienced tutor asks to see the student's own working on a long question rather than their answer, because the diagnosis is in the layout. Standard Level fails differently, usually on algebraic fluency under time pressure.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The recurring loss is a correct statistical procedure with no interpretation attached, and weak discussion of validity. Experience shows in whether a tutor teaches calculator technique explicitly rather than assuming it. Students who transferred from Analysis and Approaches arrive confident and lose marks steadily on the written commentary around their numbers.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Long answers need a sequence and most students do not have one: define, state the relationship, substitute, evaluate. Unit and significant-figure discipline costs marks quietly across every paper. An experienced tutor will ask whether the student has ever been shown that sequence explicitly, which is usually the fastest available gain in the subject.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry most of the lost marks at Higher Level. The diagnostic is one unfamiliar mechanism: a student who has memorised arrows cannot start it, and one who understands electron behaviour can. Experience shows in a tutor's willingness to go back and rebuild bonding rather than press on with past papers.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command terms separate a 4 from a 6 here more than content does. Students who write everything they know about a topic land in the middle every time. An experienced tutor sorts lost marks by command term rather than by topic, and will usually find that explain and evaluate questions are carrying the damage while state and describe are fine.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the final evaluation sentence are where marks disappear without the student noticing. Higher Level adds quantitative work that rewards arithmetic care. For the internally assessed commentaries, experience shows in whether the tutor insists on article selection early, because an article too broad or too old cannot support the required diagram later.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The unseen non-literary paper rewards an explicit analytical method that most students have never been taught. Vocabulary is rarely the problem for Dubai students; the structure of a comparative argument usually is. The individual oral needs a global issue narrow enough to defend with two extracts, which is a judgement built from having supervised several.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source work is a technique rather than a talent: provenance, purpose, value and limitation each earn marks and each is routinely omitted. Essays lose bands for narrative that never argues. The historical investigation is marked substantially on method and source evaluation, which students consistently underprepare relative to the history itself.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools and theories have to be applied to the stimulus rather than recited, and the pre-released Higher Level case study rewards structured work spread across months. Quantitative content including ratio and investment appraisal is where careless students concede the easiest marks. Experience shows in how early a tutor starts the case study work.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Students who code well frequently write loose prose answers and lose marks on precise terminology and algorithm tracing. The internally assessed solution needs a genuine client and a documented development cycle. An experienced tutor asks who the client is in the first session of Grade 11 rather than in the panic of Grade 12.

dubai/experienced-ib-tutor.regionsTitle: Dubai communities and the experience each cluster needs
dubai/experienced-ib-tutor.regionsIntro: Experience is partly local. Which schools a community feeds decides which internal assessment calendars a tutor has to work around, and which subjects that cluster is routinely short of. These are the Dubai communities where enquiries concentrate, with the kind of experience each one tends to need most.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Umm Al Sheif
regions.note: The densest IB cluster in the emirate, so the most useful experience here is having worked across several schools' differing internal deadlines at once. Higher Level sciences and Analysis and Approaches dominate requests, which is also where marking experience matters most.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and Arabian Ranches
regions.note: Large established Diploma cohorts where students often want help with the same paper in the same week. Experience of the specific paper matters more than general subject knowledge here, because the students have usually already had the content taught competently at school.

regions.name: Mirdif and Nad Al Sheba
regions.note: Continuum schools with Middle Years cohorts that are large relative to the rest of Dubai, so criterion-descriptor experience is the differentiator rather than Diploma expertise. A tutor who has only taught Diploma will frequently misread what is capping a Grade 8 grade here.

regions.name: Jumeirah, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: A mix of continuum and British provision on neighbouring streets, which produces a steady stream of students moving between systems. The valuable experience in this cluster is having handled that transition often enough to map coverage rather than guess at it.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Lakes Towers
regions.note: High turnover and frequent mid-year arrivals part way through the first Diploma year. Experience here means knowing how to establish what a student has actually covered against the subject guide before teaching anything, which is a distinct skill from teaching the course.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Tilal Al Ghaf
regions.note: Newer communities with younger cohorts and newer school provision, including first Diploma cohorts at recently opened schools. External marking as a second opinion is most often wanted here, and that is specifically a marking-experience purchase rather than a teaching one.

regions.name: Business Bay and Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Working households buying short, efficient sessions late in the evening. The relevant experience is being able to diagnose quickly and teach into the gap inside a single hour, which is a different discipline from running a long weekend session.

regions.name: Al Furjan, JVC and Dubai South
regions.note: Minority Higher Level subjects are rarely covered locally at all, so the question is not how experienced the nearest tutor is but whether a subject specialist exists within reach. Online matching is what makes experience in the subject available rather than experience in the area.

schoolClusters.city: Established Diploma schools
schoolClusters.note: Long-running Diploma cohorts with settled teaching teams, where the content is usually taught well and the marks are lost in technique. Tutoring here is mostly marking and command-term work, so a tutor's marking record matters far more than how many years they have been in a classroom.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.city: Newer and expanding IB provision
schoolClusters.note: Dubai added seven private schools for the 2026-27 intake, three of them International Baccalaureate, which means new Diploma teaching teams and first cohorts. A first cohort is unproven rather than poor, and an external second reader on internally assessed work is a reasonable thing for a family to want.

dubai/experienced-ib-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways experience gets used, all one-to-one over live video. The distinction is which capability the hour draws on, because a tutor can be the right choice for one of these and the wrong choice for another even within the same subject.

modes.title: Marking and technique work
modes.description: The student's own written work read against the published assessment criteria, with teaching drawn from the marking rather than from the syllabus. This is the arrangement that requires marking experience specifically, and it is the one that moves grades in subjects where the content is already being taught competently at school. Most Diploma requests in Dubai should start here.

modes.title: Content repair and sequence rebuilding
modes.description: Going back to a foundation that was never secure and rebuilding it, which can mean three sessions of apparently backwards work. This draws on classroom experience rather than marking skill, because knowing the order in which a topic has to be rebuilt is something learned from teaching it many times to different students.

modes.title: Component supervision
modes.description: Structured feedback across an exploration, investigation, commentary, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay, scheduled backwards from the school's own internal deadlines. The experience that counts here is having supervised several of these to completion, because the common failures are process failures rather than subject ones.

sections.heading: The four kinds of experience, and what each one buys
paragraphs: Separating the four kinds makes the hiring decision tractable. Classroom years give pattern recognition across many students. Recent high attainment gives current familiarity and credibility. Volume of private students gives practised explanation without necessarily any sense of the mark scheme. Marking against the published criteria gives the ability to locate exactly where credit stops in a written answer, which is the capability most directly connected to a grade moving.

None of the four is worthless and none of them is sufficient alone. The best matches usually combine classroom years with marking, which is why practising or former subject teachers tend to be the strongest option for Diploma work where the school is already teaching the content well. The worst matches are not inexperienced people; they are experienced people deployed on the wrong job, such as a Diploma specialist asked to fix a Grade 8 criterion problem they have never read a descriptor for.

The verification column in the table is the point of the whole exercise. Each kind of experience has a question that reveals it, and none of those questions requires subject knowledge from the parent. Taken together they take about ten minutes and they are far more informative than any biography, because a biography is a claim and these are demonstrations.

A note on what cannot be verified. Current examiner status is not something a parent can confirm, and it should never be used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. Any tutor described as an examiner should be able to evidence it; absent that, treat the claim as decoration and judge the marking you actually see.

sections.heading: Six questions that test an IB tutor in ten minutes
paragraphs: These questions work because each has a recognisably good answer and a recognisably vague one, and none of them requires the parent to understand the subject. They can be asked on a call or in the first free session, and the shape of the answer is more informative than its content.

The first is which component the student is losing most marks in and how the tutor knows. A good answer references the student's own scripts and names a category. A weak answer describes the subject in general. The second is what the commonest mistake is on that specific paper. A tutor with population experience answers instantly and specifically; a tutor with only personal experience describes their own approach instead.

The third is what they would do in the first three sessions, and the useful signal is whether the plan starts with reading the student's work or with the tutor's own material. The fourth is which school the student attends and why that matters, which tests UAE-specific experience: internal assessment calendars differ across Dubai and an experienced local tutor knows to ask. The fifth is what they will not do, which tests whether academic honesty boundaries are understood as rules or as negotiables.

The sixth is the one most parents skip and it is the most revealing: what would make them say this is not working. A tutor who cannot describe the conditions under which they would recommend stopping has no measurement framework, which means the next three months will be unauditable. An experienced tutor has usually given that advice before and can tell you what it sounded like.
bullets: Which component is losing the marks, and how do you know?
What is the commonest mistake on this specific paper?
What happens in the first three sessions, and what do you read first?
Which school, and what does that change about the plan?
What will you not do with an internally assessed draft?
What would make you tell us this is not working?

sections.heading: Where marks are actually lost, subject by subject
paragraphs: Experience shows up as specificity. A tutor who has taken several cohorts through a paper can name the failure point that carries the most marks in that subject and describe the question that diagnoses it. A tutor who has not will describe the syllabus. The table below is written in the form an experienced answer takes, which also makes it a checklist a parent can use against whatever they are told.

The pattern across subjects is consistent and worth noticing. In most IB subjects the marks a capable student loses are not content marks. They are structural: the wrong command term answered, a procedure performed without interpretation, an argument assembled without a judgement, a diagram drawn imprecisely. That is why marking experience outranks subject depth for most Dubai Diploma students, whose schools are generally teaching the content competently.

The diagnostic column is the one to use in a trial session. Each of these is a single question or task that separates two different underlying problems, and watching a student attempt it tells a tutor more than twenty minutes of conversation. If a tutor does not ask something like it, they are planning to teach a course rather than respond to a student.

Where a subject is not listed here, the method transfers. Ask which component carries the most lost marks for this student, ask for the diagnostic task that distinguishes the two likely causes, and ask what a session would do about each. An experienced tutor in any subject can answer those three in that form.

sections.heading: Assessment structure, and why the level changes the plan
paragraphs: An experienced tutor talks about components rather than about subjects, because the grade is assembled from components and each one fails differently. Most IB subjects are assessed through two or three written papers plus an internally assessed component, with the Higher Level course adding content, usually adding a paper, and marking against higher demand. Knowing which component a student is losing in is the whole of the diagnosis.

Exact weightings differ by subject and change between syllabus cycles, so the honest move is to read the current subject guide rather than to publish a percentage that may be out of date. Your school holds the guide and can show you, and an experienced tutor will quote your child's subject guide rather than a general figure. A tutor who gives you a confident percentage without naming the guide is reciting something they half remember.

What does transfer across subjects is the structural logic. A paper of short structured questions fails on precision and command terms. A paper of extended responses fails on argument and judgement. A data or source paper fails on reading the stimulus. An internally assessed component fails on design and on criterion coverage rather than on content. Matching the work to the component is what an experienced plan looks like.

The table sets out the component types and what each needs, with a column pointing at where to confirm the current weighting. It is deliberately structural, because a plan built on the right component with an approximate weighting beats a plan built on the wrong component with a precise one.

sections.heading: Criterion letters, and what experienced feedback sounds like
paragraphs: Internally assessed work in the IB is marked against lettered criteria, and almost nobody competing for this search names a single one. That absence is informative, because criterion literacy is the difference between feedback that improves a mark and feedback that improves a paragraph. An experienced tutor talks in criterion letters because the mark is awarded in criterion letters.

In the Middle Years Programme every subject is marked against four criteria labelled A to D, each out of 8, and the strand a student is losing is usually consistent across their work in that subject. In the Diploma the lettered criteria differ by subject and component, and both the letters and their mark allocations have to be read from the current subject guide rather than assumed. Any tutor quoting allocations without naming the guide is guessing.

What experienced feedback sounds like is narrow and recognisable. It names the criterion, quotes the descriptor language, points at the place in the student's own text where the descriptor is not yet satisfied, and asks a question rather than supplying a sentence. It does not say the introduction is weak. It says the criterion asks for a justification of the method and this paragraph describes it without justifying it, then asks what the alternative method was and why it was rejected.

The boundary sits in the same place. Feedback against criteria is teaching. Supplying sentences, restructuring on the student's behalf, handing over a research question, or editing a draft into a higher band is not, and a student submitting work produced that way faces an academic honesty investigation reaching beyond one subject grade. Feedback given here is logged with a date so a school supervisor can see its shape if they ask.

sections.heading: Examiner claims, and what a parent should do with them
paragraphs: Examiner status is the most common experience claim in this market and the least verifiable. It is also frequently used to imply something it cannot deliver. No tutor has advance access to grade boundaries, to live mark schemes or to unreleased paper content, and any suggestion otherwise should end the conversation rather than start a negotiation about price.

Where current examiner experience is genuine it does give something real: a developed sense of how credit is awarded and withheld on a specific component. That is valuable and it is also something a tutor can demonstrate directly by marking your child's work in front of you. The demonstration is better evidence than the claim, which is why the free first session is more useful than any biography.

The practical advice is to ask for evidence once, politely, and then stop relying on the answer either way. Judge the marking you can see. Does the tutor locate the exact point where credit stops? Do they reference the published criteria rather than their own preference? Can they predict, before marking, which category of mark this student will lose? Those are observable and they are what examiner experience is supposed to produce.

The same scepticism should apply to statistics. Any provider publishing satisfaction percentages, average scores or improvement figures without the number of students, the date and the method behind them is publishing decoration. Experience is demonstrable in a session. It is not demonstrable in a percentage with no method attached.

sections.heading: Experience of the transition into the Diploma
paragraphs: Dubai moves students between curricula more than most cities, and transition work is a distinct expertise that experience in teaching the Diploma does not automatically include. A student arriving from IGCSE has been rewarded for recall. One arriving from the Middle Years Programme has criterion habits and may have met less content. One arriving from an American high school has breadth and often a gap in algebraic fluency. These need different first terms.

An experienced tutor handles a transition by mapping before teaching. Two or three sessions spent establishing what has actually been covered against the subject guide saves a term of teaching in the wrong order, and it is the single most valuable thing available to a mid-year arrival into the first Diploma year. Tutors without transition experience tend to start teaching the current topic and discover the gaps by accident over several weeks.

The three gaps that most often need explicit teaching rather than time are algebraic manipulation, scientific notation with unit discipline, and extended writing under timed conditions. All three are cheap to fix in the first term and expensive to fix in the second year. A tutor who asks about all three in a first conversation has done this before.

The transition question also runs the other way in Dubai, where students sometimes move from the Diploma into A Levels or back. An experienced tutor will be honest about which subject content transfers and which does not, rather than reassuring a family that the work carries across when a substantial part of it does not.

sections.heading: Experience of the UAE context, which is not the same as subject experience
paragraphs: A tutor can be excellent in a subject and inexperienced in this market, and the gap shows up in practical ways. Dubai private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi has the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

Local experience also means knowing about the mandatory subjects. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, with KHDA's guidance stating that requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 where a school's year begins in April. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in these subjects, stating that combined classes are strictly prohibited because expectations and language of instruction differ.

A tutor new to the UAE will not know to ask which stream a child is in, which school calendar applies, or that the private tuition work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 is granted free of charge for two years through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. None of that is subject knowledge and all of it changes how a plan is built, which is why it belongs in a page about experience.

One boundary belongs here too. Naming a regulator and explaining what it does is accurate; implying that a regulator approves or accredits a tutoring provider is not. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and any provider claiming otherwise should be asked for a permit number.

sections.heading: The graduate with a 7 against the teacher with five cohorts
paragraphs: This is the choice most Dubai families are actually making, often without framing it. A recent graduate with a top grade in the subject is cheaper, more available, culturally closer to the student and genuinely knowledgeable about the current material. A practising or former teacher with several cohorts behind them costs more and brings population knowledge and usually marking skill. Both are legitimate purchases for different jobs.

The graduate is the better buy when the job is content company: working through material the student has been taught, keeping momentum, answering questions, building confidence with someone who sat the same paper recently. For a Standard Level subject where the student is broadly on track and needs practice and encouragement, that is often exactly right and the price difference is substantial.

The teacher is the better buy when the job is diagnosis or technique, which is to say whenever nobody yet knows why the marks are going. Knowing how two hundred students failed a question is a different kind of knowledge from knowing how you passed it, and it is the knowledge that locates a problem quickly. For Higher Level work, for internally assessed components and for any student whose grade has stalled despite effort, it is worth the difference.

The mistake is buying on price without naming the job, and the second mistake is assuming the more expensive option is always better. A seventeen-year-old who has disengaged may respond to a recent graduate and refuse to engage with anyone who reminds them of school. Experience includes knowing that, which is why the match conversation asks about the student rather than only about the subject.

sections.heading: What experience cannot do
paragraphs: No amount of experience can promise a particular grade, and any provider offering one is making a claim they cannot honour. Experience shortens diagnosis, improves the quality of marking and makes the plan better aimed. It does not replace the work the student has to do, and it cannot compress two years of missing content into a final term.

Experience also cannot fix a problem that is not academic. A Grade 12 student sleeping five hours with three overdue components does not have a subject weakness, and the most experienced tutor available will not change that with a weekly session. The first conversation on every match asks what else is happening, and sometimes ends in a recommendation not to buy tutoring at all, which is worth more than a booking.

Availability is the last limit and it is stated rather than hidden. Coverage is deep in Diploma mathematics, the sciences, economics, business and English, and thinner in several group two languages, some arts subjects and minority options. Where no suitably experienced specialist is free, we give a realistic wait rather than offering someone who teaches the adjacent subject, because marked work exposes that substitution inside a fortnight.

What happens next is short. Send the subject, the level, the school and a recent piece of marked work, and ask us the six questions on this page. We come back with a named tutor, what they teach to and what they have marked, plus a slot in Gulf Standard Time, usually within two working days. The first lesson is free for one student per family with no card details taken, and it is spent on the work you sent.

process.title: Name the job before you assess the tutor
process.description: Content company, diagnosis, technique work, content repair or component supervision. Experience is only assessable against a job, and the commonest hiring mistake in this market is deploying a genuinely experienced person on the wrong one. Tell us which of the five you think you need and we will say if we disagree.

process.title: Ask the six questions
process.description: Which component is losing marks and how do you know; what is the commonest mistake on this paper; what do you read first; which school and why does it matter; what will you not do with a draft; and what would make you say this is not working. Ten minutes, no subject knowledge required.

process.title: Send a marked script in advance
process.description: The free session becomes a test with a known answer. Watch whether the tutor opens your evidence or their own placement material, whether they locate where credit stopped, and whether they reference the published criteria rather than their own preference. That is experience demonstrated rather than claimed.

process.title: Judge the written note, not the conversation
process.description: After the session you get a note naming the most expensive error class and the task set. An experienced tutor's note is specific and slightly dull. A vague note after a charming session is the clearest early warning available, and it costs nothing to act on at that point.

process.title: Review at four sessions
process.description: A written continue, change or stop recommendation with the evidence behind it. Changing the match costs one session because the record travels, and stopping is a legitimate outcome. An experienced tutor has given that advice before and will tell you what it sounded like if you ask.

whyPoints.title: Experience stated as four separate capabilities
whyPoints.description: Classroom years, recent attainment, volume taught and marking against the published criteria are different things with different uses. Each profile names the subject, the level, the papers taught to and the components marked, so a family can match the capability to the job rather than to an adjective.

whyPoints.title: Verification handed to the parent
whyPoints.description: Six questions with recognisably good and recognisably vague answers, none requiring subject knowledge. Publishing the test rather than the claim is the opposite of how this market usually works, and it is the only way a word like experienced becomes checkable before money changes hands.

whyPoints.title: Criterion literacy as the standard
whyPoints.description: Feedback names the criterion, quotes the descriptor's language, points at the place in the student's own text and asks a question. Almost nobody competing for this search names a single criterion letter, which is why criterion-led feedback is the clearest available marker of real experience.

whyPoints.title: No unverifiable claims
whyPoints.description: No examiner status without evidence, no implied access to boundaries or marking, no statistics without the number of students, the date and the method, and no regulator approval claimed. IB Gram holds no accreditation from any board or authority and says so plainly.

whyPoints.title: Local experience treated as a skill
whyPoints.description: Knowing to ask which Dubai school, which Arabic stream, which internal assessment calendar and which permit position applies is not subject knowledge and it changes the plan. A tutor new to this market is missing something real even if their subject depth is excellent.

faqs.question: How can I tell whether an IB tutor in Dubai is genuinely experienced?
faqs.answer: Ask six things and watch the shape of the answers. Which component is your child losing marks in, and how do they know. What the commonest mistake is on that specific paper. What they read first in the first three sessions. Which school your child attends and what that changes. What they will refuse to do with an internally assessed draft. And what would make them tell you it is not working. None of these needs subject knowledge from you, and vague answers to the first two are decisive.

faqs.question: Is a recent IB graduate with a 7 good enough to tutor my child?
faqs.answer: For some jobs, yes, and the price difference is substantial. A recent high scorer brings current material knowledge, credibility with a teenager and useful company through content the student has already been taught. What they usually lack is population knowledge: they know how they answered a question, not how two hundred students got it wrong. For diagnosis, for Higher Level technique and for internally assessed work, someone who has marked many students' scripts finds the problem faster, which is what you are paying the difference for.

faqs.question: Why does marking experience matter more than years in a classroom?
faqs.answer: Because most marks a capable Dubai student loses are structural rather than factual. The wrong command term answered, a procedure done without interpretation, an argument assembled without a judgement, a diagram drawn imprecisely. Locating the exact point where credit stops in a written answer is a distinct skill, and plenty of people with deep subject knowledge cannot do it. Years in a classroom give pattern recognition, which is valuable too. The strongest matches combine both, which is why practising and former subject teachers tend to be the best fit for Diploma work.

faqs.question: What should an experienced tutor ask me before the first session?
faqs.answer: Which school, because internal assessment calendars differ across Dubai and the answer changes the whole autumn plan. The level and the specific components in play. What the student thinks is going wrong, which is often more accurate than the grade suggests. Whether there is recent marked work they can read in advance. And what else is happening, because exhaustion, an unidentified difficulty or three overdue components all present as a subject weakness and none responds to weekly subject teaching.

faqs.question: Should I pay more for a tutor who says they are an IB examiner?
faqs.answer: Ask for evidence once, then judge the marking in front of you rather than the claim. Genuine current examiner experience does give a developed sense of how credit is awarded on a specific component, and a tutor who has it can demonstrate it by marking your child's work. What no tutor has is advance access to grade boundaries, live mark schemes or unreleased paper content, and any suggestion otherwise should end the conversation. Examiner status used to imply inside knowledge is a warning about everything else being said.

faqs.question: Does experience with the Diploma mean a tutor can handle Middle Years work?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, and the gap trips up Dubai families regularly. Middle Years subjects are marked against four lettered criteria out of 8 each, converted to a 1-7 grade by the school, and the strand that is capping a student is specific to their own writing. A tutor who has only taught Diploma content will often diagnose a content problem where the real issue is a criterion never addressed. Ask whether they have read the descriptors for your child's subject, and ask them to name which strand they would check first.

faqs.question: What does criterion-led feedback actually sound like?
faqs.answer: Specific and slightly dull. It names the criterion, quotes the descriptor's language, points at the place in the student's own text where the descriptor is not yet met, and asks a question rather than supplying a sentence. Not the introduction is weak, but the criterion asks for the method to be justified and this paragraph describes it without justifying it, so what was the alternative method and why was it rejected. If feedback does not reference a criterion, it is improving a paragraph rather than a mark.

faqs.question: Which Dubai-specific things should an experienced tutor already know?
faqs.answer: That Dubai private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority while Abu Dhabi has ADEK, Sharjah has SPEA and the Ministry of Education supervises Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. That Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, taught in separate streams for Arab and non-Arab students. That internal assessment calendars differ by school. And that private tutoring here requires the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation permit, free for two years.

faqs.question: My child's grade has stalled despite a good tutor. What does experience add here?
faqs.answer: A different diagnosis rather than more hours. A stalled grade with real effort behind it usually means the work is aimed at the wrong component, or the same error class is being treated as effort rather than technique, or a foundation three topics back was never secure. An experienced tutor tests all three from marked scripts instead of increasing frequency. Ask for the ranked error list from the last month: if the top item is unchanged from the first week, the teaching has not reached it and the approach needs to change.

faqs.question: How much do experienced IB tutors charge in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market bands put qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and IB or IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more, with premium named coaches quoted up to AED 650. Those are figures from providers' own pages read in October 2026, not an IB Gram quote. The useful question is what sits inside the hour: whether marking of your child's own written work against the published criteria is included, or whether you are paying a specialist band for explanation alone.

faqs.question: Can an experienced tutor tell me whether Higher Level is realistic?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the most valuable judgements available. The method is evidence rather than opinion: prior attainment in the specific skill the Higher Level course depends on, plus a diagnostic task at Higher Level demand, plus an honest read on writing stamina. A tutor who has taken several cohorts through the jump has seen which students survive it. Ask for the judgement in writing, with the evidence, and read it alongside what the school says rather than instead of it.

faqs.question: What will an experienced tutor refuse to do with my child's Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Supply sentences for insertion, restructure the draft on the student's behalf, hand over a research question for the student to adopt, or edit the work from one band into another. What they will do is explain what each criterion asks for in its own language, read what the student has written and say which criterion is unmet and why, ask the questions the criteria ask, teach the method the work needs, and hold the schedule. Your school's own rules on drafts take precedence over any tutor's preference.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who has taught in a Dubai school better than one who has not?
faqs.answer: Often, for a specific reason: they know the local calendar, the mandatory-subject arrangements and how predicted grades tend to be set in this market, and they know to ask which school. That is real and it changes a plan. It is not a substitute for subject and marking experience, though, and a family should not trade a strong specialist for a weaker one simply because the weaker one is local. The best available combination is subject depth plus marking skill plus knowing the questions this market requires.

faqs.question: What would make you tell us that tutoring is not the answer?
faqs.answer: Several things, and we would rather say them than take a booking. A student carrying several overdue internally assessed components and severe sleep deprivation has a workload problem, not a subject problem. A student who cannot yet read fluently needs a different kind of assessment altogether. A family wanting two years of missing content covered in a final term is being sold hope by anyone who agrees. And if no suitably experienced specialist is free for the subject, we give a realistic wait rather than a substitute.

faqs.question: How many sessions does it take to see whether an experienced match is working?
faqs.answer: Four, and they should produce artefacts rather than impressions: four dated notes, at least one marked script with lost marks sorted by category, a named recurring error class and a written recommendation to continue, change or stop. If the top error class after four weeks is the same one identified in week one with nothing done about it, the match is not working regardless of how experienced the tutor is. Changing at that point costs one session because the record travels with your family.

dubai/experienced-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE one-to-one. What is worth asking each of them is narrower than a CV: which specification code, how many series of it, which papers they have marked most often, and what their annotated feedback on a student's written answer actually looks like.

intro.heading: Experience is a claim, not a credential
paragraphs: Nobody advertises an inexperienced tutor. The word appears on every profile in this market, attached to nothing checkable, which makes it the least useful filter a Dubai parent has. Years of teaching correlate only loosely with the thing you need, which is whether this person can look at your child's written answer, say precisely which marks were available and why they were not awarded, and then teach the difference. Some tutors acquire that in two years. Some never acquire it at all and have been teaching for fifteen.

There is a version of experience that is specific enough to verify. Which specification: Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1, Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher tier. How many series: Cambridge runs March, June and November, so a tutor working steadily sees three cohorts a year rather than one. Which papers: a Physics tutor who has repeatedly marked Paper 6 practical questions knows things about where candidates lose marks that a tutor who has only taught theory does not. Which boundary cases: Core-to-Extended moves, private candidates, mid-year arrivals from CBSE or an American curriculum.

This page is built around evidence rather than reassurance, because the brief for it was evidence. It sets out the questions that separate a real track record from a long one, what marked work should look like when it comes back, how a twelve-week record should read, and the points at which you should expect a tutor to tell you their own analysis was wrong. IB Gram is an independent IB and IGCSE tutor-matching platform with no affiliation to Cambridge International, Pearson, or any Dubai school named here.

Delivery matters to the evidence question in one specific way. Tuition for families in the UAE runs online, one-to-one, over live video; IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and home visiting is a service offered only in India. Because the match is not limited by who will drive to your community, the experience you are selecting for can be narrow: not a science tutor, but someone who has taught Cambridge Chemistry 0620 Extended across several series and knows what the mole questions do to a grade 5 candidate.

One caution before the detail. Examiner status is the most commonly asserted and least commonly evidenced claim in this market. IB Gram does not describe tutors as Cambridge or Pearson examiners, because current examiner status is not something a platform can verify on a parent's behalf, and because examiner status would not grant access to marking, boundaries or paper content in any case. Where a tutor's background includes examining, the right response is to ask for the series and the board and to treat the answer as you would any other claim.
bullets: Ask for specification codes and series taught, not years in teaching
Ask to see a marked piece of written work with its annotations
Expect a named review point in week six, with a decision attached
Treat examiner claims as claims: ask which board and which series
Online delivery means the match can be specification-specific, not radius-specific

dubai/experienced-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Experience is worth different amounts at different points in a British-curriculum school career in Dubai. The further into the IGCSE course a child is, the more the specific specification and paper experience matters relative to general teaching ability.

programmes.name: Years 8-9, before the IGCSE course
programmes.description: At this stage general teaching quality outweighs specification experience. The work is building algebraic fluency, scientific vocabulary and written accuracy that the IGCSE course will assume and not re-teach. A good tutor at this stage needs to diagnose a missing foundation, which is a teaching skill rather than a board-specific one.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools take in new arrivals across the year, so Year 9 classes hold children who have come from CBSE, from an American curriculum, or from a different British scheme of work. The gaps are rarely general weakness; they are specific topics that nobody taught in that sequence. Ask a tutor how they would find those gaps in one hour, and listen for a diagnostic method rather than a syllabus overview.

programmes.name: Year 10, first teaching of the IGCSE course
programmes.description: This is the year the tier decision gets made and where specification experience starts to pay. A tutor who has taught the specification across several series knows which Year 10 topics quietly determine the Year 11 grade, and which ones look hard but carry few marks. Weekly work that tracks the school's sequence costs fewer hours than catching up later.
programmes.countryNote: Because Dubai entries are submitted months before the papers, the Core-or-Extended conversation has to happen in the autumn term of Year 10 or it stops being a real choice. An experienced tutor should be willing to give you an evidenced opinion on that in writing after a handful of sessions, and to say what the Extended content would cost in hours from where your child currently is.

programmes.name: Year 11, the examination year
programmes.description: In the exam year, paper-specific experience outweighs almost everything else. The useful tutor is the one who knows the mark distribution of each paper, which command terms recur, and where a given grade band leaks marks. Progress is measurable weekly from marked timed work, which means the twelve-week evidence trail this page describes is available to you from the first fortnight.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai centres enter candidates across Cambridge's March, June and November series and Pearson's May/June and November series, so two children in the same Dubai year group can be working to deadlines months apart. A tutor should ask which series your child is entered for before anything else, because it changes the entire plan and the entry deadline sits well ahead of the papers.

programmes.name: Post-IGCSE transition at 16
programmes.description: The experience that matters here is of the gap itself: what A Level or the IB Diploma assumes that IGCSE did not teach. A tutor who has taken students across that transition several times can name the specific prerequisites, rather than discovering them in November of Year 12 when the first assessment comes back.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai sixth forms publish their own subject entry requirements rather than working to a national threshold, and because many campuses run both A Level and the Diploma, the same IGCSE grade can be sufficient for one route and short for the other. Ask your child's school for its published per-subject requirements, then ask a tutor what the gap to that threshold looks like in hours.

dubai/experienced-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: The experience worth asking about is subject-specific and paper-specific. For each of these, there is a particular place marks go missing, and a tutor who has taught the specification across several series will name it before you do.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Ask which board and tier. The question to test experience: where do Extended candidates at grade 5 most reliably lose method marks? A specific answer names unwritten working and multi-step problems rather than a topic list.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: The useful experience is on the practical component. A tutor who has marked Paper 6 answers knows that candidates lose marks on graph axes, significant figures and describing a control rather than naming one, which is not knowledge you acquire from teaching theory.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Experience shows in how fast a tutor locates mole weakness. A grade 5 Chemistry candidate is usually not weak at Chemistry; they are unable to move between mass, moles and concentration without prompting, and that single gap spreads its losses across several papers.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: Biology is marked strictly against command terms, and an experienced tutor spends more time on the difference between describe, explain and suggest than on content. Ask how they would teach a student who knows the material and still writes answers that score half marks.

subjects.name: English Language (0500 / 0510 / 4EA1)
subjects.levels: First language and second language routes
subjects.description: Specification experience matters here more than parents assume, because 0500, 0510 and the Pearson equivalents reward different things. Ask which route your child is entered for and what that route's reading-response marks actually require.

subjects.name: Economics (0455) and Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Both are lost on the long questions, where candidates define terms correctly and then fail to apply them to the stimulus material. An experienced tutor can show you, on a marked script, where the evaluation marks were available and went unclaimed.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: The experience test is pseudocode. A tutor who programs well is not the same as one who has taught Paper 2 answers to the published conventions, and students fluent in Python routinely lose marks for writing Python where pseudocode was required.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: A scarce specification and the clearest case for asking about series rather than years. The syllabus assumes fluency that 0580 only introduces, so a tutor whose experience is entirely 0580 will be teaching 0606 for the first time on your child.

subjects.name: Geography (0460) and History (0470)
subjects.description: Source-and-skills subjects dressed as content subjects. Experienced tutors talk about case-study specificity and arguing from the source; inexperienced ones talk about covering the syllabus, which is the wrong unit of work for these papers.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (0508) and Foreign Language (0544)
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the international curriculum in Dubai private schools under KHDA requirements, and the two routes are different courses with different demands. Children are sometimes placed by nationality rather than competence, and an experienced tutor will raise that before teaching anything.

dubai/experienced-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: Because sessions run online, the area a family lives in changes when a session can start rather than who is available to teach it. That matters to the evidence question: a tutoring plan evaluated at week six needs six weeks of sessions that actually happened at a workable hour.

regions.name: Dubai Marina, JBR and Bluewaters
regions.note: Apartment living with a school bus arriving late in the afternoon, so a realistic start is from 17:00 and a 90-minute session in exam term needs the earlier of two possible slots. High relocation turnover means mid-year starts, and mid-year starts need a sharper diagnostic.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Mizhar
regions.note: Villa communities with schools close by and children home early, so 16:00 starts hold. Large IGCSE cohorts here and strong demand for Maths and the sciences, which means the evidence trail is usually built around marked timed papers from week two.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Arabian Ranches
regions.note: Long internal distances and school runs feeding the Al Qudra and Umm Suqeim corridors. Families here often book two subjects in one evening, which makes the week-six review easier to read because both subjects have the same number of sessions behind them.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1, 2 and 3
regions.note: The shortest school runs in the city and the earliest feasible session starts, often competing with established swimming and music commitments. Where the evening is already full, the evidence trail works better on two shorter sessions than on one long one.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle, Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens

sections.heading: What experienced should mean on an IGCSE tutor's profile
paragraphs: Experience becomes checkable the moment it is stated as a number of series and a specification code rather than a number of years. Which board, which code, which tier, how many cohorts, which papers most often. A tutor who answers Cambridge 0620 Extended, eleven cohorts, mostly Paper 2 and Paper 4, some Paper 6 has told you something you can test in a session. A tutor who answers over ten years of experience in science has told you nothing that distinguishes them from anyone else on the page.

Years are a weak proxy because the IGCSE cycle is fast. Cambridge runs three series a year, in March, June and November, and Pearson runs May/June and November, so a tutor working steadily sees several cohorts a year rather than one. Two years of continuous IGCSE teaching across those series can involve more marked scripts than a decade of occasional work, and specification content is revised periodically, which means older experience can be experience of a version your child is not sitting.

The table below is the audit. It is not a hostile list of demands; most good tutors answer all of it in a few minutes and are pleased to be asked, because the alternative is competing on adjectives. What it is designed to surface is the difference between someone who has taught this specification repeatedly and someone whose experience is adjacent to it: a Maths teacher who has never taught 0606, a Physics graduate who has never marked a Paper 6 answer, a tutor whose track record is on a different board's version of the same subject.

sections.heading: The twelve-week evidence trail
paragraphs: Tuition that is working produces a record whether anyone intends it to or not. Twelve weekly sessions generate twelve marked question sets, and if those sets are comparable, the trend in them is the only honest measure of whether the money is doing anything. What makes them comparable is deliberate: timed, from past papers, at consistent difficulty, marked against the published criteria rather than impressionistically. A tutor who sets easier work as the term goes on produces a rising line that means nothing.

The schedule below is the shape a readable trail takes. The important feature is week six, which carries a decision rather than a report. By session six there has been enough marked work to know whether the original diagnosis was right, and the professional response to a flat line at that point is to say the analysis was wrong and change it, or to say tuition is not the intervention this child needs. Families in Dubai most often lose money not to bad tutors but to arrangements with no review point, which run for terms because nobody ever set a date to ask.

Parents do not need to read mark schemes to use this. Three questions cover it. Is the work the same difficulty as it was in week two? What was the mark then and what is it now? And what did the tutor say would happen by now at week one? If a tutor cannot produce comparable scripts, the trail does not exist, and reported progress is a recollection rather than a measurement.
