sections.heading: The MYP eAssessment question, and whether it changes your budget
paragraphs: Some Dubai schools enter Year 5 students for the IB's optional external MYP eAssessment, which leads to the MYP Certificate; many do not. The first thing to establish is whether your child's school does, because the answer changes what Year 5 preparation looks like and families routinely spend money against the wrong model.

Where a school does not enter students, Year 5 assessment remains internal and criterion-based, and preparation means criterion coaching: understanding the descriptors, producing work of the type the criterion rewards, and getting written feedback against it. That is the work described everywhere else on this page.

Where a school does enter students, there is an external examination component on top, and preparing for it is a different activity. Examination preparation means timed practice, recognising question types, and writing to time — skills that are only loosely related to criterion coaching and that are typically bought as a short block before the window rather than across the year. A student can be strong on criteria and still underperform under examination conditions, which is precisely the thing timed practice addresses.

The budget implication is that a family in an eAssessment school has one more purchase in the spring term and should plan for it rather than meeting it as a surprise. The family in a non-eAssessment school does not, and should not be sold examination preparation for an examination that does not exist. Ask the school in writing whether their Year 5 cohort is entered, and for which subjects, before agreeing to anything described as exam preparation.

sections.heading: The MYP to Diploma gap, and why the summer term is the cheapest place to close it
paragraphs: This is the central cost argument of the page. There is a real gap between MYP Year 5 and DP1, it is specific and nameable, and it costs far less to close in the summer term of Grade 10 than in the autumn of Grade 11. Almost nobody does it, which is why DP1 tutoring demand in Dubai spikes in October.

In mathematics the gap is fluency under time plus notation. MYP criterion work rewards investigation and justification; Diploma Paper 1 in Analysis and Approaches is sat without a calculator and rewards fast, accurate, correctly notated manipulation. A student can be excellent at MYP mathematics and slow at exactly that. Six sessions in the summer term on non-calculator technique is cheap; the same work in DP1, alongside five other subjects and an internal assessment, is not.

In the sciences the gap is the internal assessment genre and the quantitative step. The MYP criterion B and C structure prepares a student conceptually for the Diploma investigation, but the Diploma expects more sophisticated uncertainty treatment and a far longer, more formal write-up. A student who has seen what a Diploma-standard investigation looks like before September approaches their first one differently from one meeting the format cold in November.

In the humanities and English the gap is command terms and volume. The Diploma's instruction words set scopes the MYP does not use in the same way, and the reading load steps up substantially. In Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay there is no MYP equivalent at all beyond the Personal Project, which is why a student who did the Personal Project properly has a genuine advantage and one who outsourced it has a double disadvantage.

sections.heading: Online, in-home or group: what the premium actually buys
paragraphs: In the year with the largest middle-years budget, the delivery decision has real financial consequence and it is usually made on instinct. The instinct says a tutor in the room is better. The arithmetic says the difference is the commute.

Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor. Across a Year 5 that includes a Personal Project block, a single-subject term and a summer transition block, that premium compounds into a significant sum for no additional subject expertise. What it buys is proximity, and in Year 5 proximity is not the binding constraint.

The binding constraint is specialism. What a Grade 10 student needs is somebody who can read a Year 5 criterion descriptor against their work, or who knows what a Diploma-standard investigation write-up looks like. The pool of people who can do that in one Dubai community, at the hour the student is home after a long Year 5 day, is narrow. Over video it is not, and it does not shrink when the family changes address or travels.

Group formats deserve a word because they are genuinely cheaper and genuinely limited. An online small group costs less per student and works reasonably for shared content. It does not work for a Personal Project, which is by definition individual, and it does not work for criterion diagnosis, which is about one student's specific work. IB Gram's position on delivery is fixed: all UAE tuition is one-to-one, live over video, and we do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are an India-only service, and if presence in Dubai is your requirement we will say we are not the provider.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and why it is a financial question too
paragraphs: In the year a family is spending most, somebody will offer to solve the problem rather than teach it. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at Diploma level. That is an IB malpractice trigger and the consequence falls on the student, who can be excluded, not on the seller, who keeps the fee. The Personal Project is the Grade 10 equivalent and the pressure is the same.

What a tutor may legitimately be paid for is substantial: teaching the content, explaining each criterion letter by letter with the marks attached, modelling how a piece of that type is structured using a different example, interrogating the student's research question or project goal, challenging an investigation design, reading the student's own drafts and journal entries and saying what is missing, and teaching notation and referencing. That is the work this page prices.

What a tutor may not be paid for is writing any part of a submitted piece, dictating a general rule or an evaluation, designing the investigation, producing the process journal, or correcting a draft into a finished state. The practical test is whether the student could explain every decision in the work unaided, to their supervisor, without notes. If not, the family has bought a liability.

On materials: we do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. We reference them and link the official source, because the official source is correct and legally ours to point at. A provider offering a private library of mark schemes as an inducement is telling you how they handle the rest of it.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: a Grade 10 decision with a Grade 12 consequence
paragraphs: If there is any prospect of a UAE university application, the Ministry of Education equivalency requirements should be read before options are chosen in Grade 10, not in the final year. Parts of the requirement concern which subjects were taken, and by Grade 12 that is settled.

For the British track the published requirements are specific: passes in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. At least one page ranking in this market states that six IGCSE subjects are required, which is wrong.

For the American track, English proficiency is met by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB we will not publish a points threshold, because we have not read one on moe.gov.ae and an unsourced number here would be a liability rather than a service. Ask the Ministry or the school's university counsellor and get the answer in writing.

Two cautions. Equivalency and attestation are processes the Ministry and the emirate attestation authority run; they are not services IB Gram performs, influences or guarantees. And nothing about tutoring is required for equivalency, admission or progression — any provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process they have no part in.

sections.heading: Permits, availability and the Dubai Year 5 calendar
paragraphs: On the legal position of whoever you pay: private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted amount as unverified. A provider building a permit fee into a rate is inventing it.

There is a restriction worth knowing while comparing quotes. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. So an arrangement built around your child's own teacher is not one to seek. This is press-reported rather than read from the policy document, so verify against current ADEK guidance.

On availability, the honest position: Year 5 demand concentrates in the same months across the whole Dubai market, which means the autumn Personal Project window and the pre-options spring are when specialist slots are hardest to get. Mathematics, English and the sciences at Year 5 level are reasonably covered; a specific evening hour in a loaded month sometimes cannot be filled immediately. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, matching extends to our wider base including IB specialists in India, delivered identically by live video on Gulf Standard Time. No home visits happen in the UAE.

On the calendar, the UAE working week runs Monday to Friday with a Saturday-Sunday weekend, so Friday evening is a school night. During Ramadan the school day shortens and the productive window moves, for many families to after Iftar, which is better agreed in advance than renegotiated weekly. And the summer term, after options are settled, is the window this page keeps returning to: it is the cheapest place in four years to close the Diploma gap, and it is almost entirely unused.

process.title: Get the Personal Project checkpoint dates in writing
process.description: Not the IB submission window, the school's own internal checkpoints. They determine when the autumn block runs and when it ends. Without them the project block has no end date and tends to drift into an undiagnosed general slot by spring.

process.title: Decide which of the four Year 5 purchases you are making
process.description: Personal Project coaching, a single-subject block for the MYP grade, options sessions, or the summer Diploma transition block. They are different purchases in different terms. Buying them as one open-ended weekly slot is how a Year 5 budget doubles quietly.

process.title: A free trial lesson before any payment
process.description: One session, no charge, with the tutor matched to the subject and the job. By the end of it you should have a named criterion or a named gap, not a general impression. If the match is wrong you say so, and we match again before any money changes hands.

process.title: Ask whether your school enters the eAssessment
process.description: In writing, and for which subjects. If it does, there is an extra short block of timed practice in the spring. If it does not, nobody should be selling you examination preparation for an examination your child will not sit.

process.title: Book the summer transition block when options are settled
process.description: Six to ten sessions in the final term, targeted at the gaps between Year 5 and DP1 in the subjects actually chosen. This is the highest-return money in the year, because the same work in DP1 sits in the exam-year band alongside five other subjects.

process.title: Close each block on its date
process.description: The Personal Project block ends at submission. The subject block is reviewed on criterion evidence at the end of term. The transition block ends when DP1 starts. Named end dates are what separates a Year 5 plan from a standing subscription.

whyPoints.title: We publish the AED bands with sources
whyPoints.description: Three of the six competitor pages measured in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote dollars. Every figure here is attributed to whoever published it, with the review date, because a family comparing quotes needs the market rather than a brochure.

whyPoints.title: Four purchases, four terms, four end dates
whyPoints.description: Year 5 is expensive because families buy everything in October. Sequenced properly — project in the autumn, subject and options in the spring, Diploma transition in the summer — it is the same work at a far lower monthly peak.

whyPoints.title: We will say when a better grade is not available
whyPoints.description: By Year 5 a mathematics route move is rarely granted and some criterion ceilings are genuine. Saying so is more useful than taking a term's fees for a campaign that will not land, and it redirects the budget to the transition block where it does work.

whyPoints.title: The summer term argument, made plainly
whyPoints.description: The MYP to DP1 gap is specific: non-calculator fluency, the Diploma investigation format, command-term scope, research process. Closing it in the Grade 10 summer costs a block. Meeting it in DP1 costs the exam-year band alongside five other subjects.

whyPoints.title: Honesty where the pressure is highest
whyPoints.description: The Personal Project is the artefact most likely to be bought rather than produced, and a journal written by someone else loses marks on its own terms as well as being a malpractice exposure. The boundary is on the page: coached, read, fed back, never written.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what we are not
whyPoints.description: No home visits anywhere in the UAE, no KHDA approval or regulator accreditation, no UAE office. We publish no IB session or results date anywhere on these pages, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and a wrong date is worse than none.

faqs.question: How much should a Dubai family budget for a Grade 10 MYP year?
faqs.answer: Plan by term rather than by hour. Market rates for a qualified subject tutor working online run AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150, and Bestimate's Dubai monthly estimates for a weekly session run AED 240-600 at the budget end and AED 600-1,200 in the middle. Year 5 typically involves a Personal Project block in the autumn, a single-subject block in the spring, two or three options sessions, and a summer transition block. Bought in sequence, the monthly peak is far lower than buying all four in October.

faqs.question: Why is Grade 10 the most expensive year of the MYP?
faqs.answer: Because four things are purchased at the same time, not because the rate is higher. Year 5 carries the Personal Project on school-set deadlines, the most demanding criterion B and C work in the programme, the options decision, and in some schools an external eAssessment. Families who did nothing in Grades 6 to 9 meet all four at once in October and buy them in a hurry, which is always at the top of the band. The same work spread across the three terms is markedly cheaper and produces better results.

faqs.question: Can I pay someone to help finish the Personal Project?
faqs.answer: You can pay for process coaching and you cannot pay for the project. A tutor may explain each criterion letter by letter with the marks attached, test whether the goal is viable, sharpen a vague specification, read your child's own journal entries and report drafts and say what is missing, and teach referencing. A tutor may not write the report, produce the journal, design the project or correct a draft to completion. The journal is the specific trap: the criteria reward running evidence of planning and reflection, so a reconstruction loses marks on its own terms.

faqs.question: Is the MYP eAssessment something we need to prepare for?
faqs.answer: Only if your school enters students for it, and many Dubai schools do not. Ask in writing whether your Year 5 cohort is entered and for which subjects. Where it is, there is an external examination component and preparing for it means timed practice, question-type recognition and writing to time — a different activity from criterion coaching, usually bought as a short block before the window. Where it is not, nobody should be selling you examination preparation for an examination your child will not sit.

faqs.question: What is the single best use of money in Grade 10?
faqs.answer: The summer term transition block, after options are settled, and almost nobody buys it. Six to ten sessions on the specific gaps between MYP Year 5 and DP1 in the subjects actually chosen: non-calculator fluency and notation for Analysis and Approaches, the Diploma investigation format and uncertainty treatment for the sciences, command-term scope and reading volume for English. The same work met in DP1 sits in the exam-year band that Bestimate puts at AED 1,000-2,000 or more a month, alongside five other subjects and a first internal assessment.

faqs.question: What is the actual gap between MYP Year 5 maths and DP1 maths?
faqs.answer: Speed, notation and the calculator. MYP criterion work rewards investigation and justified generalisation, which is valuable and slow. Diploma Paper 1 in Analysis and Approaches is sat without a calculator at both levels and rewards fast, accurate, correctly notated manipulation under time. A student can be excellent at MYP mathematics and genuinely slow at that, and the fix is non-calculator technique practised repeatedly. Six to eight sessions in the Grade 10 summer term is cheap; the same hours in DP1 compete with five other subjects.

faqs.question: Does choosing the IB Diploma over A Levels cost more in tutoring?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, for a structural reason rather than a quality one. The Diploma means six subjects with an internal assessment in every one, plus Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, which creates more parallel tutoring opportunities than three or four examined A Levels. Unitors' own published rates reflect the same pattern, with IGCSE from AED 150 against IB from AED 200. That is not a reason to choose A Levels — fit matters far more than cost — but it belongs in the conversation honestly rather than being discovered in DP1.

faqs.question: Can my child still move up a maths route in Grade 10?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and it is better to know that before paying for a campaign. By Year 5 the standard and extended routes have diverged in content rather than only in pace, and most Dubai schools decline moves on those grounds rather than on ability. If a route move is what you want, Grade 8 or Grade 9 was the time. What is still worth buying in Year 5 is a strong grade in the current route plus the summer transition block, which protects the Diploma options that remain genuinely available.

faqs.question: Do you come to our home in Dubai for Grade 10 sessions?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. All UAE tuition is one-to-one, live over video, on Gulf Standard Time. The cost side is worth seeing plainly: Bestimate puts in-home visits at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor. Across a Year 5 with three separate blocks that premium compounds into real money, and what it buys is proximity rather than subject expertise.

faqs.question: Is an online group class a cheaper option for Year 5?
faqs.answer: It is cheaper per student and it is limited in ways that matter in Year 5. A small online group works reasonably for shared content delivery. It does not work for the Personal Project, which is individual by definition, and it does not work for criterion diagnosis, which is about one student's specific marked work against a specific descriptor. If the budget is tight, the better economy is fewer sessions of one-to-one targeted at a named criterion than more sessions of group content the student may already have.

faqs.question: Which subjects should we read the equivalency rules for before options?
faqs.answer: All of them, before the choices are made rather than in Grade 12. The published British-track requirements are five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no lower than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade — with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. For the IB track we will not publish a points threshold we have not read on moe.gov.ae. The Ministry runs this process; IB Gram has no part in it and nothing about tutoring is required for it.

faqs.question: When in the Grade 10 year do tutor slots get hardest to find?
faqs.answer: The autumn Personal Project window and the pre-options spring, because Year 5 demand concentrates in the same months across the whole Dubai market. Mathematics, English and the Year 5 sciences are reasonably covered overall, but a specific evening hour in a loaded month sometimes cannot be filled immediately, and we will say so rather than booking a generalist. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, matching extends to our wider base including IB specialists in India, delivered identically by live video on Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: Should a Year 3 science gap be fixed now or left alone?
faqs.answer: Fixed now, and it is usually cheaper than it looks. Year 5 quantitative chemistry rests entirely on being able to write a correct balanced equation first, and Year 5 physics rests on automatic formula rearrangement. A student struggling with either is often paying Year 5 prices for a Year 3 gap. Four to six sessions taking the earlier skill to automaticity frequently recovers more Year 5 marks than twenty sessions of Year 5 content, because the Year 5 content was being attempted on a foundation that would not hold it.

faqs.question: How do we avoid a Year 5 tutoring slot drifting on after it is needed?
faqs.answer: Name the end date before the first session. The Personal Project block ends at submission. The subject block is reviewed on criterion evidence at the end of term. The transition block ends when DP1 starts. The commonest waste in Year 5 is an open weekly slot bought in September for the project and still being paid for in March, by which point nobody has diagnosed what it is for. A block with a session count and a date is a purchase; an open slot is a subscription.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai have to be licensed, and does it affect the price?
faqs.answer: They need a permit and it is free, so it should not appear in a quote. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through a MoHRE private tutor work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: How does the Dubai school fee freeze change our tutoring decision?
faqs.answer: It makes the biggest number in the budget predictable for a year and leaves tutoring as the variable one. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. With the fee held flat, the Year 5 question becomes where in the year to place the tutoring spend rather than whether to make it, and the answer this page keeps returning to is the post-options summer term.

dubai/grade-10-ib-myp-tutor.closingHeading: Sequence the four purchases rather than buying them in October
dubai/grade-10-ib-myp-tutor.closingBody: Grade 10 is the most expensive year in the middle years, and most of the excess comes from timing rather than from rates. The Personal Project belongs in the autumn as a block with a submission date. The subject work and the options decision belong in the spring. And the Diploma transition block belongs in the summer term, where six to ten sessions do work that costs the exam-year band if it waits until DP1. Book a free trial lesson, bring two pieces of marked work and the school's Personal Project checkpoint dates. Sessions are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time; we do not send tutors to UAE homes.

dubai/grade-11-ib-dp-tutor.tutorsIntro: DP1 tutors are matched to one subject at one level, because that is how the budget usually works and because a tutor spread across three Diploma subjects is a generalist in all of them. The first conversation is about which subject earns the hour.

intro.heading: Six subjects, one hour a week, and a decision nobody helps you make
paragraphs: A Grade 11 student in a Dubai IB school is carrying six subjects at once, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the Creativity, Activity, Service strand. Each subject has an internal assessment marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB. Almost no family can fund tutoring in six subjects, and almost every family tries to decide which one to fund on the basis of which report line looks worst. That is the wrong criterion and it is the most expensive mistake in DP1.

Start with the market, since nobody else in this search result publishes it. A qualified subject tutor working online in Dubai sits at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Below that, EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52, which buys supervision rather than Diploma-level subject diagnosis. Above it, named specialists run AED 200-450 and upwards, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 at the examiner-positioned end. In-home visits carry a travel premium: Bestimate puts them at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors at AED 200-500.

In monthly terms, which is what families actually plan against, Bestimate's published Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages visible in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Three of the six competitor pages measured here publish no price at all; the two that do quote US dollars, which is not a currency a Dubai family transacts in.

Now the decision. The right subject to fund is not the lowest grade. It is the subject where an hour moves the most points, and that is determined by three things: the level, because Higher Level carries more teaching hours and deeper content and therefore more recoverable marks; the weighting of the component that is weak, because a paper worth 35 per cent of the grade is worth more attention than one worth 20; and whether an internal assessment is in play, because internal assessment marks are produced over months rather than in three hours and are therefore the most tractable marks in the Diploma.

The second decision is timing, and it favours acting now. The final two terms of DP2 sit in the exam-year band Bestimate puts at AED 1,000-2,000 or more a month, and they are the least productive hours in the programme because the student is simultaneously finishing coursework, sitting mocks and applying to universities. The same budget spent in Grade 11, when a habit can still be retrained rather than patched, buys more points per dirham. That is the whole argument of this page.

All IB Gram tuition in the UAE is delivered one-to-one, live over video, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is an India-only service, and if presence in Dubai is your requirement we will say we are not the right provider.

dubai/grade-11-ib-dp-tutor.programmesIntro: Grade 11 is the first of two Diploma years. The cost structure of DP1 differs from DP2 in ways worth seeing before committing a budget to either.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, Year 1
programmes.description: Six subjects begun simultaneously across six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, with Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay process starting alongside. Internal assessments are introduced and in several subjects a first draft is due within the year. Subject grades run 1 to 7, with up to three bonus points from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, DP1 is also the year subject changes are still possible — just. A student who finds a Higher Level choice unsustainable can usually drop to Standard Level or switch early in the year, and the school's deadline for that is internal and rarely advertised. Asking for it in writing in the first term is worth more than any amount of tutoring on a subject that should not have been taken.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, Year 2
programmes.description: The final year: internal assessments completed and submitted, the Extended Essay finished, Theory of Knowledge assessed, mock examinations sat, and external examinations in the May session for UAE schools. University applications run through the same months.
programmes.countryNote: The expensive year, and the reason this page argues for spending in Grade 11. Bestimate puts specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000-2,000 or more a month, and the hours are competing with coursework deadlines, mocks and applications. A family that funds one subject properly in DP1 usually needs less in DP2, not more.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: At least two Diploma subjects paired with a career-related study, plus a personal and professional skills course, a reflective project, service learning and a language development strand. Fewer Diploma subjects than the full Diploma and a different core.
programmes.countryNote: Rarely offered in Dubai, so a family interested in it has a short list rather than a choice. Worth knowing about in Grade 11 for one reason: a student genuinely unable to sustain six Diploma subjects has an option other than failing at them, and in cost terms it carries a much lower parallel-tutoring load. Check the IB's programme finder and then the school directly.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, Year 5
programmes.description: The final MYP year, with the Personal Project, the most demanding criterion B and C work in the programme, and in some schools an optional external eAssessment. Subjects are assessed against four lettered criteria scored 0-8 and converted to a 1-7 grade.
programmes.countryNote: Mentioned here because the single cheapest version of DP1 support is bought in the Grade 10 summer term, before DP1 starts. Non-calculator fluency for Analysis and Approaches, the Diploma investigation format for the sciences, command-term scope for English: six to ten sessions then does work that costs the exam-year band later.

dubai/grade-11-ib-dp-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the DP1 subjects Dubai families most often fund, each with the component the money should actually target. The ranking logic is weighting and tractability rather than current grade.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most-funded DP1 subject in Dubai and usually correctly so at Higher Level. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator at both levels, which is where the recoverable marks sit: technique and notation under time rather than additional content.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics and modelling led with a graphical calculator assumed throughout. The marks cluster in interpretation questions, which ask what a result means in context and are short compositions wrapped around a calculation. Cheaper to improve than AA, for the same grade movement.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Physical chemistry carries the load: enthalpy cycles, entropy and equilibrium constants. Higher Level is the right place to spend if funding one science, because the content depth is where the recoverable marks are. The scientific investigation is the tractable component.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Uncertainty treatment separates IB Physics from most national syllabuses and is consistently where marks go. Higher Level adds rotational dynamics, the quantum topic and harder field theory, and the written explanation marks are as heavy as the calculation ones.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Broad syllabus and precise command terms, so the cheapest marks are in answer discipline rather than content. 'Outline', 'explain' and 'evaluate' set different scopes, and a student who writes everything for every term loses marks and time together.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three internal assessment commentaries, each on a news article published inside a defined window, each applying a different syllabus unit. The commentaries are the single most tractable marks in the subject and they are deadline-shaped, so they are bought as blocks.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Approachable content and an unforgiving assessment structure. Higher Level requires a research project on a real organisation with supporting documents, and Paper 1 uses a pre-released case study, which rewards early preparation more than late revision.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is a guided analysis of an unseen non-literary text, so advertisements, speeches and infographics are examinable. Technique on Paper 1 is the recoverable mark for most students; the Paper 2 comparative essay depends on reading that cannot be bought late.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Assessed on productive and receptive skills against defined text types, so register and form carry the marks rather than fluency. A good-value subject to fund because text-type conventions are finite and teachable in a defined number of sessions.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a working solution for an identified client, documented across a development process, and the documentation carries most of the criteria marks. Students who build well and document poorly are the standard pattern and the standard fix.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed by an exhibition of three objects with commentaries and a prescribed-title essay, together worth up to three bonus points with the Extended Essay. Low hours, real points, and routinely the last thing a family funds.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay with a supervisor and three formal reflection sessions. Process coaching in DP1 — question narrowing and methodology — is a few sessions that prevent a lost term in DP2. A tutor coaches and feeds back; the writing is the student's.

dubai/grade-11-ib-dp-tutor.regionsTitle: Dubai communities and the DP1 evening

sections.heading: What a Grade 11 IB tutor costs in Dubai
paragraphs: A qualified online IB subject tutor in Dubai costs AED 150-300 an hour at market rates, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. That band is where almost all useful DP1 work sits. Below it you are buying supervision; above it you are buying either a travel premium or a specialism you may not need in Grade 11.

The supervision band has a legitimate use even in the Diploma. EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. For a DP1 student whose problem is that six subjects of homework never gets started, that band buys structure, and paying four times more for syllabus expertise the student is not yet using would be waste. The diagnosis matters: a student losing marks on Chemistry HL equilibrium needs the middle band; a student losing marks because nothing is handed in needs the lower one.

The travel premium is the band DP1 families pay most often without choosing to. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors at AED 200-500. The difference from the online band is the commute rather than the teaching, and in DP1 that difference is particularly poor value, because the subjects where help is most needed — Maths AA HL, Chemistry HL, Physics HL, HL Economics — have the thinnest local pools at any price.

The specialist band at AED 200-450 and upwards, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and BartyED AED 650, earns its premium for a narrow set of DP1 jobs: a Higher Level science where the content depth is the problem, and an internal assessment that is genuinely going wrong. Outside those, the same money placed as a second mid-band subject usually moves more total points. And a caution from the research: do not pay a premium for examiner positioning you cannot verify.

sections.heading: Which of six subjects deserves the hour
paragraphs: This is the decision the whole page exists for, and the honest criterion is marks moved per hour rather than lowest current grade. A 4 in a Standard Level subject with no internal assessment pending may be far less tractable than a 5 in a Higher Level subject with a weak component carrying 35 per cent of the grade.

Three tests, in order. First, level: Higher Level subjects carry more teaching hours, deeper content and more components, which means more recoverable marks for the same hour of work. If a family can fund only one subject, funding a Higher Level one is usually right, even where the Standard Level grade is lower. Second, component weighting: find out which paper or component is weak and what percentage of the grade it carries. An hour spent on a 35 per cent component is worth nearly twice an hour on a 20 per cent one.

Third, tractability. Internal assessment marks are the most tractable in the Diploma because they are produced over months, with drafts, against published criteria, rather than in three hours in May. A student with a weak internal assessment in progress has marks genuinely available. A student whose weakness is accumulated content across two years of a Higher Level science has fewer available marks per hour, and a family should know that before paying for twelve sessions.

There is a fourth consideration that is not about marks: the bonus points. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together carry up to three points, which is the difference between 34 and 37 on a Diploma total, and they are consistently the last thing a Dubai family funds. Three or four sessions of process coaching in DP1 is among the cheapest point movement available in the entire programme, and nobody buys it because it does not appear as a weak line on a report.

sections.heading: Higher and Standard Level: what the weighting difference means for a budget
paragraphs: Families treat Higher Level as simply harder, which is true and not the useful part. The useful part is structural: Higher Level courses carry more prescribed teaching hours, additional content beyond the Standard Level syllabus, and in several subjects an additional component. That means more assessment surface, and more assessment surface means more places where targeted work can move a grade.

It also means the same subject at the two levels is a different purchase. A Standard Level science has fewer components and a shallower syllabus, so the realistic ceiling on what tutoring can add is lower — not because the student is less able but because there is less to recover. A Higher Level science has the extra content, the additional paper in several subjects, and the same internal assessment, which is more room to work in.

The practical move is to ask the school, or read the subject guide, for the component weightings in the specific subjects funded. Every Diploma subject publishes how much each paper and the internal assessment contributes to the final grade, and the numbers differ between subjects and between levels. A family that knows a component is worth 35 per cent and that their child is weak in it has a real basis for a decision. A family working from a report grade has none.

One warning about levels and money. Where a student is in a Higher Level subject they genuinely cannot sustain, no amount of tutoring is the right answer and the honest advice is to ask the school about dropping to Standard Level while the internal change deadline is still open. That deadline is set by the school, is rarely advertised, and usually falls early in DP1. Asking about it is free and occasionally saves two years.

sections.heading: The internal assessment calendar, which is where DP1 money clusters
paragraphs: Internal assessment is the DP1 spending event, and it does not spread evenly. Each subject has coursework marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB, and the deadlines are set by the school rather than by the IB. That has two consequences for a budget: the work arrives in clusters, and nobody tells you when until it is close.

The first action is administrative and free. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the internal deadline calendar for the whole of DP1 and DP2, in writing. Most Dubai schools have one. With it, internal assessment support can be bought as defined blocks against known dates, which costs less and works better. Without it, the pattern is a panic purchase three weeks out, at whatever rate is available at short notice.

The subjects where this bites hardest in Grade 11 are Economics, with three commentaries each tied to a news article published inside a defined window; the sciences, where the scientific investigation has a long lead time and a first draft often falls in DP1; and the Extended Essay, which has three formal reflection sessions spread across the Diploma and a question that should be settled in DP1 rather than DP2. Mathematics has the exploration, usually later.

A note on value. Internal assessment marks are, hour for hour, the best marks in the Diploma to work on, because they are produced over months with drafts against published criteria rather than in an examination hall. Process coaching on them is also the help most constrained by academic honesty rules, which is why the next section sets the boundary out explicitly: what is bought is criteria understanding, question interrogation and written feedback on the student's own drafts, and nothing else is available at any price.

sections.heading: Online, in-home or group in DP1
paragraphs: In a year where a family may be funding one subject for twelve months, the delivery decision has real money attached. The honest arithmetic: Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor. The premium is the commute.

In DP1 that premium is worse value than at any earlier stage, because the subjects most often needing help are the ones with the thinnest local pools. A family wanting Chemistry HL, Maths AA HL, Physics HL or HL Economics in one Dubai community at the hour a Grade 11 student is home is drawing from a very small set of people. Paying a travel premium does not enlarge it; it only increases the cost of whoever is available.

Group formats are genuinely cheaper and genuinely limited. An online small group costs less per student and works for shared content revision. It does not work for internal assessment coaching, which is about one student's own question and drafts, and it does not work where the weakness is a specific component technique rather than content. In DP1 most of what is worth buying is individual by nature.

IB Gram's position is fixed rather than preferential. All UAE tuition is one-to-one, live over video, on Gulf Standard Time, and we do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE — home visits are a service we offer only in India. If physical presence in Dubai is your requirement, we are not the right provider and will say so rather than arguing the point.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what no amount of money buys
paragraphs: In a year where internal assessments are the most valuable marks available, somebody will offer to produce them. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. That is an IB malpractice trigger and the consequence falls on the student, who can be excluded, not on the seller, who keeps the fee. This belongs on a page about cost because cost is the mechanism.

What can legitimately be bought is substantial and is where this page's prices apply. A tutor may teach the subject content, explain each assessment criterion letter by letter with the marks attached, interrogate and narrow a research question, teach the methodology, read the student's own drafts and give written feedback against the criteria, and teach referencing conventions. That is the help that genuinely moves an internal assessment mark.

What cannot be bought is writing any part of the work, dictating sentences for the student to transcribe, supplying a methodology or dataset as the student's own, editing a draft into a finished state, or handing over a model to be adapted. The test is whether the student could explain and defend every line of the work in an oral examination. If not, the family has bought a liability rather than a grade.

The same applies to materials. We do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; we reference them and link the official source. A provider offering a private library of mark schemes or unreleased material as an inducement is creating both a copyright problem and a malpractice exposure that lands on the student.
bullets: Allowed: criteria by letter, methodology taught, feedback on the student's own drafts

sections.heading: The exam calendar in DP1, and the one date error to avoid
paragraphs: UAE IB schools sit the May session, and a Grade 11 student's examinations are therefore a year away. That distance is why DP1 money is better value: there is time for a habit to change rather than for an answer to be patched. What is not a year away is the internal deadline calendar, which is the live constraint in Grade 11 and which the school sets.

We do not publish a specific IB exam or results date on these pages. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so any date printed here would be second-hand, and a wrong date in a family's planning is worse than no date at all. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the entered session and the internal deadline calendar in writing, and verify against ibo.org.

For students also sitting Cambridge or Pearson qualifications alongside — which happens in Dubai, particularly for additional subjects — the board calendars are sourced and usable. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series, and the February/March series is offered to India only, so a Dubai family should not plan around it. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November; its November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the correct practice is always to work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

sections.heading: Permits, availability and the Dubai DP1 calendar
paragraphs: On whoever you are paying: private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so any amount quoted to you is unverified.

There is a restriction worth knowing while comparing DP1 quotes. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. So an arrangement built around your child's own Diploma teacher is not one to pursue. This is press-reported rather than read from the policy document, so verify it against current ADEK guidance.

On availability, the honest position: Higher Level sciences, Maths AA HL and HL Economics are the thinnest subjects in this market, and a specific evening hour on Gulf Standard Time in one of them sometimes cannot be filled immediately. When that is the case we say so rather than booking a generalist against a Higher Level syllabus. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, matching extends to our wider base including IB specialists in India, delivered identically by live video. No home visits happen in the UAE in either direction.

On the calendar, the UAE working week runs Monday to Friday with a Saturday-Sunday weekend, so Friday evening is a school night. During Ramadan the school day shortens and the productive window moves, for many families to after Iftar, which is better agreed in advance than renegotiated weekly. And one piece of budget context: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, which makes tuition the variable line and its placement across the two Diploma years the decision that matters.

process.description: Early in DP1 and in writing. Where a Higher Level choice is genuinely unsustainable, no amount of tutoring is the right answer, and the school's internal change deadline usually falls early and is rarely advertised. Asking costs nothing and occasionally saves two years.

process.title: Review on component evidence each term
process.description: The question at the end of each term is whether the targeted component has moved, with marked work to show it. Where it has and holds, the right advice is often to pause and keep a block in reserve for DP2 rather than to carry the slot forward automatically.

whyPoints.title: We publish the AED market with its sources
whyPoints.description: Three of the six competitor pages measured in this market publish no price at all and the two that do quote dollars. Every figure here names the provider who published it and the review date, because a family choosing between six subjects needs the market rather than a brochure.

whyPoints.title: The funding decision made on weighting, not on the lowest grade
whyPoints.description: Level, component weighting and tractability decide where an hour moves the most points. An hour on a 35 per cent component beats an hour on a 20 per cent one, and an internal assessment in progress beats two years of accumulated content gaps.

whyPoints.title: We will say when tutoring is the wrong purchase
whyPoints.description: A student in an unsustainable Higher Level subject needs the school's change deadline, not twelve sessions. A student not handing work in across six subjects needs the lower supervision band, not a specialist. Saying so costs us a booking and is the useful answer.

whyPoints.title: The bonus points taken seriously
whyPoints.description: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay carry up to three Diploma points for a handful of coaching sessions in DP1, and almost nobody buys them because they do not show as a weak report line. On a points-per-dirham basis they are the best value in the programme.

whyPoints.title: Honesty where the marks are most tractable
whyPoints.description: Internal assessment marks are the best in the Diploma to work on and the most constrained by academic honesty rules. Criteria explained, questions interrogated, drafts read, feedback written, nothing authored — stated on the page rather than buried in terms.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what we are not

faqs.question: Which of my child's six Diploma subjects should we actually pay for?
faqs.answer: Not the lowest grade. Fund the subject where an hour moves the most points, which is decided by three things in order: level, because Higher Level carries more content and components and therefore more recoverable marks; component weighting, because an hour on a paper worth 35 per cent of the grade is worth nearly twice an hour on one worth 20; and tractability, because an internal assessment in progress has marks genuinely available while two years of accumulated content gaps do not. Get the component weightings from the school before deciding.

faqs.question: How much does a Grade 11 IB tutor charge in Dubai?
faqs.answer: A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Below that, EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52, which buys supervision rather than Diploma-level diagnosis. Above it, named specialists run AED 200-450 and upward with TutorChase at AED 270. Bestimate's published Dubai monthly estimates for one weekly session run AED 600-1,200 in the middle band. These are market figures with sources; our own quote follows a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Is it better to fund a Higher Level or a Standard Level subject?
faqs.answer: Higher Level, usually, even where the Standard Level grade is lower. Higher Level courses carry more prescribed teaching hours, additional syllabus content beyond the Standard Level core, and in several subjects an extra component. That is more assessment surface, which means more places targeted work can move a grade. A Standard Level subject has fewer components and a shallower syllabus, so the realistic ceiling on what tutoring can add is lower — not because of the student but because there is less to recover from.

faqs.question: Why are internal assessment marks the best ones to pay for?
faqs.answer: Because they are produced over months rather than in three hours in an examination hall. Each Diploma subject carries coursework marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB, written against published criteria, with drafts along the way. That means a weakness is visible and addressable while the marks are still being earned, which is not true of an examination paper. The constraint is academic honesty: what can be bought is criteria understanding, question interrogation and written feedback on the student's own drafts, and nothing beyond that at any price.

faqs.question: Should we spend in Grade 11 or save it for the final year?
faqs.answer: Grade 11, on a points-per-dirham basis. Bestimate's published Dubai estimates put specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000-2,000 or more a month against AED 600-1,200 for the same weekly session in the mid-band. The final two terms are also the least productive hours in the programme, because the student is simultaneously finishing coursework, sitting mocks and applying to universities. In DP1 there is still time for a habit to be retrained rather than an answer patched. Keep a block in reserve for before mocks.

faqs.question: What should we ask the Diploma coordinator before buying any tutoring?
faqs.answer: Three things, all free. The component weightings for each subject, so the funding decision is made on assessment surface rather than on a report line. The internal deadline calendar for the whole of DP1 and DP2, because internal assessment deadlines are set by the school and arrive in clusters, and a known date turns a panic purchase into a planned block. And the school's internal subject-change deadline, which usually falls early in DP1 and is rarely advertised.

faqs.question: Our child is in a Higher Level subject they cannot cope with. Is tutoring the answer?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Where a Higher Level choice is genuinely unsustainable, twelve sessions will produce an exhausted student and a modest grade, while dropping to Standard Level produces a better outcome in that subject and relieves the other five. The school sets an internal deadline for subject and level changes, it usually falls early in DP1, and it is rarely advertised. Ask about it in writing in the first term. Two consultation sessions to establish honestly whether the level is sustainable is sometimes the most valuable money in the Diploma.

faqs.question: Are Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay worth paying for?
faqs.answer: On a points-per-hour basis they are the best value in the Diploma and families fund them last or not at all. Together they carry up to three bonus points, which is the difference between 34 and 37 on a Diploma total. Three or four sessions in DP1 on narrowing the Extended Essay question, choosing a methodology deliberately, and understanding how the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and prescribed-title essay are assessed is a small, finite purchase. They get skipped because they do not appear as a weak line on a report.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to our home in Dubai for DP1 sessions?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. All UAE tuition is one-to-one, live over video, on Gulf Standard Time. The cost case is plain: Bestimate puts in-home visits at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors at AED 200-500 against AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and the premium is the commute. In DP1 it is especially poor value, because the Higher Level subjects most often needed have the thinnest local pools at any price.

faqs.question: Can a group class work for a DP1 subject?
faqs.answer: For shared content revision, reasonably. For most of what is worth buying in DP1, no. Internal assessment coaching is about one student's own research question and their own drafts, which cannot be done in a group. Component technique — Paper 1 non-calculator work in Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1 guided analysis in English A — is about one student's specific errors. If the budget is tight, fewer one-to-one sessions targeted at a named component is a better economy than more group sessions covering content the student may already hold.

faqs.question: What does uncertainty treatment have to do with a Physics HL budget?
faqs.answer: It is where the marks are, which makes it where the money should go. Uncertainty treatment — propagating an error, drawing sensible error bars, justifying the precision of a stated result — separates IB Physics from most national syllabuses and is thin in many students' prior preparation. It is also finite: a nameable set of techniques rather than a volume of content. That makes it the highest-return target in a Physics HL budget, well ahead of revising topics the student can already describe but cannot quantify.

faqs.question: When will the IB exams be, and should we plan the budget around them?
faqs.answer: UAE IB schools sit the May session, and we do not publish a specific IB exam or results date on these pages because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and a wrong date is worse than none. Ask your Diploma coordinator for the entered session in writing and verify against ibo.org. For budgeting, the examinations are not the live DP1 constraint anyway — the school's internal assessment deadlines are, and those are the dates to plan spending against because they are where the tractable marks sit.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a UAE licence, and should it appear in the price?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and it is free, so it should not appear in any quote. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through a MoHRE private tutor work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published fine schedule.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for Chemistry HL at the hour we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you instead of substituting. Higher Level sciences, Maths AA HL and HL Economics are the thinnest subjects in this market, and a specific evening hour on Gulf Standard Time in one of them sometimes cannot be filled immediately. Booking a generalist against a Higher Level syllabus wastes a term, which in DP1 is the term that mattered. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, matching extends to our wider base including IB specialists in India, delivered identically by live video. No home visits occur in the UAE in any case.

faqs.question: Can we buy an IA to take the pressure off?
faqs.answer: No, and the reason matters more than the refusal. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. That is an IB malpractice trigger, and the consequence falls on the student — who can be excluded — not on the seller, who keeps the fee. What is legitimately available is criteria explained letter by letter with the marks attached, the research question interrogated, methodology taught, and written feedback on the student's own drafts. The test is whether the student could defend every line in an oral examination.

faqs.question: How does the Dubai school fee position affect a DP1 tutoring budget?
faqs.answer: It makes the largest number predictable and leaves tuition as the variable one. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. For a Diploma family that converts the question from whether to spend into where across two years to place it — and the answer this page argues for is DP1, with a reserve block held back for the weeks before mocks.

dubai/grade-11-ib-dp-tutor.closingHeading: Decide which subject earns the hour, then buy it in DP1
dubai/grade-11-ib-dp-tutor.closingBody: Six subjects and one budget is the real Grade 11 problem, and it is solvable with three free pieces of information: the component weightings for each subject, the school's internal assessment deadline calendar, and the subject-change deadline. With those, the funding decision is made on marks-per-hour rather than on whichever report line looks worst. Add three or four sessions on the Extended Essay question and Theory of Knowledge, because up to three points for that little work is the best value in the programme. Book a free trial lesson in the chosen subject. Sessions are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time; we do not send tutors to UAE homes.

intro.heading: What is still movable, and what is already fixed
paragraphs: The honest starting point for a Grade 12 family in Dubai is that some of the year is already decided. Predicted grades have been submitted and university offers rest on them. Internal assessment marks in several subjects are submitted or close to it. The Extended Essay is written or nearly. Theory of Knowledge is largely done. What remains genuinely movable is examination performance in specific components, and that is a smaller target than families assume and more tractable than they fear.

This matters because the final year is the most expensive in the programme. Bestimate's published Dubai 2026 estimates put specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000-2,000 or more a month, against AED 600-1,200 for the same weekly session in the mid-band and AED 240-600 at the budget end. A qualified subject tutor working online in Dubai sits at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Named specialists run AED 200-450 and upwards, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and BartyED AED 650. In-home visits add a travel premium Bestimate puts at AED 180-350, with independent home tutors at AED 200-500.

Spending at that band only makes sense if it is aimed at something that can move. A student weak on Paper 1 technique in Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, which is sat without a calculator at both levels, has real marks available: technique and notation under time is a finite, trainable thing. A student whose Chemistry HL weakness is two years of unlearned content across the whole syllabus has far fewer marks available per hour in March, and a provider who implies otherwise is selling hope.

The second thing a Grade 12 family needs is the shape of what comes after the examinations. Results day, the enquiry-about-results window, and the retake route are all real options with real deadlines, and almost nobody plans for them in advance. The enquiry window in particular is short, it opens on results day, and a family discovering it for the first time on results day has already lost days of it.

Third, the practical constraint that defines the year: everything happens at once. Mock examinations, final internal assessment submissions, university applications and interviews, and then the examinations themselves. A tutoring plan that ignores that calendar will be abandoned by February. One built around it — triage after the mocks, one subject at a time, in the weeks that are actually available — survives.

All IB Gram tuition in the UAE is delivered one-to-one, live over video, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is an India-only service. We publish no IB exam or results date on these pages, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and a wrong date in a final-year plan is worse than no date at all.

dubai/grade-12-ib-dp-tutor.programmesIntro: Grade 12 is the second Diploma year and the last. What follows it — results, remarks, retakes or an alternative route — has its own structure, and knowing it changes decisions made in March.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, Year 2
programmes.description: The final year: internal assessments completed and submitted, the Extended Essay finished, Theory of Knowledge assessed, mock examinations sat, then external examinations. UAE schools sit the May session. Subject grades run 1 to 7, with up to three bonus points from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, for a maximum of 45.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the final-year calendar is compressed by university applications running through the same months, often to several systems at once. A student applying to the UK, the United States, the UAE and sometimes India simultaneously is managing four different deadline structures on top of six subjects, which is the real reason final-year tutoring plans collapse.

programmes.name: Diploma retake and the November session
programmes.description: A candidate may retake subjects in a subsequent session to improve a Diploma result, registering through a school as an examination centre. Internal assessment marks can in some circumstances be carried forward rather than redone, which is a question for the coordinator rather than a tutor.
programmes.countryNote: The route Dubai families most often discover too late. A retake is a registration made through a school, with its own deadline, and a candidate who has left school needs a centre willing to enter them. Asking the coordinator before results day what the retake process would look like costs nothing and converts a panic into a plan.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, Year 1
programmes.description: Six subjects begun simultaneously, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, with internal assessments introduced and the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge processes beginning. Subject changes are usually still possible early in the year.
programmes.countryNote: Included for one reason: almost everything expensive about Grade 12 would have been cheaper in Grade 11. The same technique work in DP1 sits in the mid-band at AED 600-1,200 a month per Bestimate's estimates rather than the exam-year band, and there is time for a habit to change rather than be patched. For a family with a younger child, that is the usable lesson.

programmes.name: IGCSE and A Level, as the alternative route
programmes.description: Single-subject qualifications assessed largely by external written examination, taken individually. Cambridge International runs June and November series for UAE candidates; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with published final and provisional timetables per series.
programmes.countryNote: Relevant to a small number of Grade 12 families for a specific reason: a student whose Diploma result will not support their intended destination sometimes has an A Level or single-subject route available as a recovery option. It is a conversation for a school counsellor rather than a tutor, but it exists, and the board calendars above are the sourced dates to plan it against.

dubai/grade-12-ib-dp-tutor.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is listed with the component where final-year marks are realistically recoverable. In Grade 12 the question is never the subject; it is the component and the question type.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is sat without a calculator at both levels, and it is the most recoverable component in the Diploma: technique, notation and speed under time are finite and trainable in weeks. Content gaps across the whole syllabus are not.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The recoverable marks are in interpretation questions, which ask what a result means in context and are short written compositions. Students who can compute and cannot comment lose heavily, and that is a writing fix rather than a mathematics one.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Physical chemistry questions — enthalpy cycles, entropy, equilibrium — are where final-year marks cluster, and they are topic-shaped rather than diffuse, so they can be targeted. Broad syllabus gaps in March are a volume problem with low marks per hour.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Uncertainty treatment is the highest-return final-year target: propagating errors, error bars, justifying stated precision. It is a nameable set of techniques rather than a body of content, which is exactly what makes it recoverable late.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Answer discipline rather than content. Command terms set different scopes — 'outline' against 'explain' against 'evaluate' — and a student who writes everything for every term loses marks and running time together. Fixable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Final-year marks sit in data-response and extended-answer technique: diagram accuracy, evaluation paragraphs that reach a judgement, and application to the stimulus rather than a general account of the theory.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Paper 1 uses a pre-released case study, which makes it one of the few genuinely preparable components in the Diploma. Students who treat the pre-release as background reading rather than as preparation leave marks on the table.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is a guided analysis of an unseen non-literary text, and technique on it is recoverable late because it is a repeatable procedure. Paper 2 depends on reading that cannot be bought in the final term.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Text types and register carry the marks, and the conventions of each assessed text type are finite. That makes English B one of the better final-year purchases, because the target is a list rather than a body of knowledge.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Largely complete by the final term. Where the prescribed-title essay is still in progress there are bonus points available, and a tutor can explain the assessment structure and give feedback on the student's own draft, but not write any of it.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Usually finished. Where it is not, the realistic help is process coaching and written feedback on the student's own drafts against the criteria. Nothing is drafted, edited to completion or supplied, at any price and at any point in the year.

sections.heading: What the last twelve weeks can actually change
paragraphs: The single most useful thing a Grade 12 family can know is which kinds of weakness respond to late work and which do not, because the difference decides whether exam-year money is well spent or wasted. The dividing line is technique against volume.

Technique responds to late work, reliably and sometimes dramatically. Paper 1 in Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches is sat without a calculator at both levels, and non-calculator fluency, correct notation and speed under time are a finite set of trainable behaviours. Uncertainty treatment in Physics is a nameable list of procedures. Command-term discipline in Biology is answer-length control. Guided analysis technique in English A Paper 1 is a repeatable procedure. All of these can move several marks in six to ten focused sessions, because the student already holds the knowledge and is losing marks in the execution.

Volume does not respond in the same way. A student who has not learned two years of a Higher Level science syllabus has a volume problem, and twelve weeks of tutoring will cover part of it at a low rate of marks per hour. That is not a reason to do nothing; it is a reason to be told the truth and to triage ruthlessly, picking the topics with the heaviest exam presence rather than attempting the lot.

There is a third category worth naming: the already fixed. Predicted grades have gone and conditional offers rest on them. Internal assessment marks that have been submitted cannot be revisited. Reading for English A Paper 2 cannot be done in April. Spending exam-year money on any of these is spending on something that has closed, and a provider who takes the booking without saying so is not helping.

sections.heading: Predicted grades: what they are, and what they are not
paragraphs: Predicted grades are produced by the school, subject by subject, and submitted to universities as the basis for conditional offers. They are a professional judgement about likely performance, not a negotiation and not a target. Understanding that saves a great deal of final-year distress in Dubai households, where the predicted grade is often treated as either a promise or an insult.

The practical consequences are three. First, a conditional offer is conditional on the final result, not on the prediction, so a student holding an offer built on a prediction they are currently below has work to do rather than a guarantee. Second, a student predicted below what an offer requires generally cannot have the prediction raised by lobbying; what can change is the evidence base, which means performance on school assessments and mocks. Third, universities differ in how they treat a shortfall, and that is a counsellor question rather than a tutor one.

Where tutoring legitimately interacts with predictions is through the evidence. Schools predict from performance data, and the mock examinations are usually the most heavily weighted piece of it. A student who improves component technique before the mocks is improving the data the prediction rests on. That is a real and legitimate route, and it is a reason to spend in the autumn term of Grade 12 rather than in the spring.

A caution that belongs here. No provider can promise a grade, a prediction, a point total or an admission outcome, and anybody who does should be disbelieved on that basis alone. What can be described honestly is which components have recoverable marks and roughly how many sessions a technique fix usually takes. Beyond that, the examination is the examination.
