sections.heading: Triage after the mocks: reading the papers rather than the grades
paragraphs: The mock examinations are the most useful diagnostic event in the Diploma and most families use them only as a scoreboard. A mock grade tells you roughly where a student stands. The marked mock papers tell you exactly which components and which question types lost the marks, and that is the information the final term should be planned around.

The pattern is consistent across students: marks are lost in two or three identifiable places rather than spread evenly. A Chemistry HL student might lose most of their marks on equilibrium calculations and on extended-response questions that ask for justification, and almost none on the recall questions everyone assumes are the problem. A Maths AA student might be losing twelve marks on Paper 1 to notation and arithmetic slips and four to genuine content gaps. Those two students need entirely different final terms.

The triage process is simple and takes two or three sessions. Go through each marked paper, categorise every lost mark by component and question type, count them, and rank. Then allocate the remaining weeks against the ranking, stating explicitly what will not be covered — because a plan that implies everything will be covered is not a plan. A family who has done this knows exactly what they are buying and can tell at the end whether it worked.

One further use of the mocks that families miss: running time. A student who leaves a question blank in a mock has a timing problem, not a knowledge problem, and timing is among the fastest things to fix. Blank final questions on a paper almost always mean the earlier answers were too long, which traces back to command-term discipline and is worth more than any content revision.

sections.heading: What the final year costs in Dubai, and which weeks are worth buying
paragraphs: This is the most expensive band in the market and the one where value varies most. Bestimate's published Dubai 2026 estimates put specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000-2,000 or more a month, against AED 600-1,200 in the mid-band and AED 240-600 at the budget end. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Named specialists run AED 200-450 and upwards, TutorChase publishing AED 270 and BartyED AED 650.

The weeks worth buying are not evenly distributed. The autumn term is worth buying because it feeds the mock performance that feeds the predicted grades. The weeks immediately after the mocks are worth buying most of all, because that is when the diagnosis exists and there is still time to act on it. The weeks immediately before the examinations are worth less than families assume, because by then the student is at capacity and additional input displaces consolidation.

The weeks genuinely not worth buying are the ones consumed by university applications and interviews, where a tutoring slot is simply one more thing the student will miss, and the final fortnight, where what helps is rest, timed practice and the student's own revision rather than new teaching. Booking at the exam-year band through those weeks is the commonest way a Grade 12 budget is wasted.

One more thing on value. In-home visits in this market carry a premium Bestimate puts at AED 180-350, with independent home tutors at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor. In the final year that premium buys the commute while the binding constraint is finding someone who knows a specific Higher Level component intimately — a pool that does not grow because you are willing to pay for travel.

sections.heading: Results day, enquiries and remarks: know this in advance
paragraphs: Almost no Dubai family plans for results day, and the one feature of it that matters most is a deadline. The enquiry-about-results window — the process by which a result can be reconsidered — is short, opens on results day, and runs through the school rather than through the family. A family learning about it on results day has already lost days.

Understand what an enquiry does and does not do. It is a reconsideration of marking, not a second chance at the examination and not an appeal against the paper's difficulty. It can change a mark and therefore a grade, in either direction in some systems, and it costs money. It is most worth considering where a result is well below both the prediction and the student's demonstrated performance, and least worth considering where the result matches the mock and the prediction. The school is the right source on cost, process and advisability.

For students sitting Cambridge or Pearson qualifications alongside the Diploma, the board timings are sourced and usable. Pearson's pattern: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates — the February/March series is offered to India only. For IB dates, ask the coordinator and verify on ibo.org; we publish none here.

Then the retake route. A candidate may retake subjects in a later session to improve a Diploma result, registering through a school as an examination centre, and in some circumstances internal assessment marks can be carried forward rather than redone. That is a question for the Diploma coordinator, and the right time to ask it is before results day, not after. A family who knows the answer in advance can make a decision on results day instead of spending a week finding out what their options are.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in the year the pressure peaks
paragraphs: The final year is when somebody will offer to produce the work rather than teach it, and when a stressed family is most likely to accept. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. That is an IB malpractice trigger and the consequence falls on the student — who can be excluded, losing the Diploma and any offers resting on it — not on the seller, who keeps the fee.

What a tutor may legitimately do, including in April, is substantial. They may teach content, explain each assessment criterion letter by letter with the marks attached, interrogate a research question, teach methodology, mark the student's work against the official mark scheme, give written feedback on the student's own drafts, and teach referencing. For examination components they may set timed papers, mark them and categorise the errors, which is the core of everything this page recommends.

What a tutor may not do is write any part of submitted work, dictate sentences for transcription, supply a dataset or methodology as the student's own, edit a draft into a finished state, or provide a model answer to be adapted. The test remains whether the student could explain and defend every line of the work in an oral examination. In the final year that test has teeth, because an investigation flagged at moderation is flagged when there is no time left to remedy it.

On materials, the position is unchanged by urgency: we do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. We reference them and link the official source. A provider offering unreleased material in the final term is offering a malpractice exposure wrapped as an advantage.
bullets: Allowed: timed papers set and marked, criteria by letter, written feedback on the student's own drafts

sections.heading: MoE equivalency and the UAE university route
paragraphs: For a Grade 12 student applying to a university in the UAE, the Ministry of Education equivalency process converts a school certificate into something a UAE institution can accept. It is an administrative process and it has its own timeline, which is worth establishing in the final year rather than after results.

The published requirements for the British track are specific: passes in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. At least one page ranking in this market states six IGCSE subjects are required, which is wrong.

For the American track, English proficiency is met by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB track we will not publish a points threshold, because we have not read one on moe.gov.ae and an unsourced number in a final-year family's planning would be a serious liability. Ask the Ministry or the school's university counsellor and get it in writing.

Two cautions. Equivalency and attestation are processes the Ministry and the emirate attestation authority run; they are not services IB Gram performs, influences or guarantees, and we describe them only so that a timeline can be planned. And nothing about tutoring is required for equivalency, admission or progression — any provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process they have no part in.

sections.heading: Permits, availability and the final-year calendar in Dubai
paragraphs: On whoever you pay at the most expensive point in the programme: private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and MoHRE's service page lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published fine schedule, so treat any quoted amount as unverified.

There is a restriction worth knowing in a year when families will try anything. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. An arrangement built around your child's own Diploma teacher — who also writes the prediction and marks the internal assessment — is not one to pursue. This is press-reported, so verify against current ADEK guidance.

On availability, the final-year squeeze is real and it is seasonal. Demand for Higher Level science, Maths AA HL and HL Economics specialists peaks across the whole Dubai market in the weeks after the mocks, which is exactly when families decide they need them. A specific evening hour in one of those subjects frequently cannot be filled at short notice, and when that is the case we say so rather than booking a generalist against a Higher Level component. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, matching extends to our wider base including IB specialists in India, delivered identically by live video.

On the calendar, the UAE working week runs Monday to Friday with a Saturday-Sunday weekend, so Friday evening is a school night. During Ramadan the school day shortens and the productive window moves, for many families to after Iftar — and in the final term that shift matters more than at any other point, because displaced revision does not get made up. Agree in advance that the slot moves rather than renegotiating it weekly.

process.title: Start from the marked mock papers
process.description: Not the mock grades. Every lost mark categorised by component and question type, counted and ranked. Two or three sessions produce a written list, and that list is what the remaining weeks are allocated against, including an explicit statement of what will not be covered.

process.title: Separate technique from volume honestly
process.description: Technique — notation, timing, command-term scope, uncertainty treatment, guided analysis procedure — moves in six to ten sessions. Two years of unlearned content does not, and should be triaged to the heaviest-weighted topics with expectations stated upfront rather than discovered in April.

process.title: A free trial lesson in the identified component
process.description: One session, no charge, with a tutor matched to that subject and that component. By the end of it you should have a named question type and a plan for it. If the match is wrong you say so, and we match again before any payment at exam-year rates.

process.title: Protect the weeks that are not worth buying
process.description: Application and interview weeks, and the final fortnight. A slot booked through those is a slot the student will miss or cannot use, and at the exam-year band that is the most expensive waste available. Plan the gaps deliberately rather than letting them happen.

process.title: Ask the coordinator about results day before it arrives
process.description: The enquiry-about-results window and its deadline, what a remark reconsiders, the retake registration route, and whether internal assessment marks can be carried forward. All free to ask, all much harder to find out in the week the results land.

process.title: Stop at the examinations
process.description: The plan ends when the papers do. Where a retake becomes relevant after results, that is a new and separate decision made against a specific subject and a specific session, not a continuation of a slot that was running anyway.

whyPoints.title: We say what the final term cannot change
whyPoints.description: Submitted internal assessment marks, predicted grades and the reading for English A Paper 2 are closed. Spending exam-year money on them is spending on something that has shut, and saying so costs us the booking and is the only useful answer.

whyPoints.title: Triage from the papers, not the grades
whyPoints.description: Mock grades are a scoreboard; marked mock papers are a diagnosis. Students lose marks in two or three identifiable places rather than evenly, and the final term should be allocated against that list with what is being skipped stated explicitly.

whyPoints.title: Weeks ranked by value, including the ones to skip
whyPoints.description: The weeks after the mocks are worth most. Application weeks and the final fortnight are worth nothing and are where final-year budgets are typically wasted. Planning the gaps deliberately is part of the plan rather than a failure of it.

whyPoints.title: No promises about grades or admissions
whyPoints.description: No provider can promise a grade, a point total, a prediction or an admission outcome, and anybody who does should be disbelieved on that basis. What can be described is which components have recoverable marks and roughly how long a technique fix usually takes.

whyPoints.title: Honesty with the pressure at its highest
whyPoints.description: The final year is when completed coursework is offered for sale, at AED 3,750 in one documented case. The consequence falls on the student. Our boundary does not move with the calendar: marked papers, criteria explained, feedback on the student's own drafts, nothing authored.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what we are not
whyPoints.description: No home visits anywhere in the UAE, no KHDA approval or regulator accreditation, no UAE office. We publish no IB session or results date because the IB's site blocks automated checking, and where we cannot match a Higher Level component at your hour we say so.

faqs.question: Can anything realistically change in the last twelve weeks of the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Technique can, substantially. Non-calculator fluency and notation for Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Paper 1, uncertainty treatment in Physics, command-term scope and answer-length control across every subject, and guided analysis procedure in English A Paper 1 are all finite trainable behaviours where the student already holds the knowledge and is losing marks in execution. Six to ten focused sessions can move several marks. What does not change in twelve weeks is two years of unlearned content, reading for the Paper 2 comparative essay, or a submitted internal assessment mark.

faqs.question: How much does a Grade 12 IB tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The final year sits in the most expensive band. Bestimate's published Dubai estimates put specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000-2,000 or more a month, against AED 600-1,200 in the mid-band. A qualified subject tutor working online is AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200, while named specialists run AED 200-450 and upward with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home visits add a travel premium Bestimate puts at AED 180-350. These are market figures with sources; ours follows a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Can a predicted grade be changed if it is below our offer?
faqs.answer: Not by lobbying. A predicted grade is the school's professional judgement submitted to universities, and a conditional offer rests on the final result rather than on the prediction. What can legitimately change is the evidence base the school predicts from, and the mock examinations are usually the most heavily weighted part of it. That is a real route and it is a reason to spend in the autumn term rather than the spring. Where a shortfall persists, how a university treats it is a counsellor question rather than a tutor one.

faqs.question: What should we do with the marked mock papers?
faqs.answer: Read them rather than the grade. Go through each paper, categorise every lost mark by component and question type, count them and rank. The pattern is consistent: marks are lost in two or three identifiable places rather than spread evenly. A Chemistry student losing most marks on equilibrium calculations and extended-response justification needs a different final term from one losing them on recall. The triage takes two or three sessions and produces a written list that the remaining weeks are then allocated against.

faqs.question: Which weeks of the final year are not worth paying for?
faqs.answer: The university application and interview weeks, and the final fortnight. In the application weeks a tutoring slot is simply one more commitment the student will miss, and at the exam-year band that is the most expensive waste available. In the final fortnight the student is at capacity and new input displaces consolidation; what helps then is rest, timed practice and their own revision. Plan those gaps deliberately rather than letting the slot run and be missed.

faqs.question: Why is a blank final question on a mock paper important?
faqs.answer: Because it is a timing problem rather than a knowledge problem, and timing is among the fastest things to fix. A blank last question almost always means the earlier answers were too long, which traces back to command-term discipline: writing a full explanation for a question that asked for an outline. Two to four sessions of answer-length control, with timed practice, typically recovers more marks than the same hours spent revising content. It is also the single most overlooked diagnostic in the marked mock paper.

faqs.question: What is an enquiry about results and when do we have to decide?
faqs.answer: It is the process by which a result can be reconsidered, and the window is short, opens on results day and runs through the school rather than the family. It is a reconsideration of marking, not a second attempt at the examination and not an appeal against difficulty. It can change a mark and therefore a grade, and it costs money. It is most worth considering where a result is well below both the prediction and demonstrated performance. Ask your coordinator about the process and the deadline before results day, not on it.

faqs.question: How does an IB retake work from Dubai?
faqs.answer: A candidate may retake subjects in a later session to improve a Diploma result, registering through a school acting as an examination centre, and in some circumstances internal assessment marks can be carried forward rather than redone. Both of those are questions for the Diploma coordinator rather than for a tutor, and the right time to ask is before results day. A student who has left school needs a centre willing to enter them, which takes time to arrange. Knowing the answer in advance turns a bad number into a decision rather than a week of research.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for a specialist rather than a regular subject tutor in the final year?
faqs.answer: For a narrow set of jobs, yes. A Higher Level component where the problem is genuine content depth, or an internal assessment still open and going badly, justifies the AED 200-450 and upward band where TutorChase publishes AED 270. For technique work — timing, notation, command terms, uncertainty procedure — a qualified subject tutor at AED 150-300 does the same job, and the extra money would move more total marks as a second subject. One caution from the research: do not pay a premium for examiner positioning you cannot independently verify.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to our home in Dubai for final-year revision?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. All UAE tuition is one-to-one, live over video, on Gulf Standard Time. In the final year the travel premium is particularly poor value: Bestimate puts in-home visits at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors at AED 200-500 against AED 150-300 online, and the binding constraint is finding someone who knows a specific Higher Level component intimately. That pool does not grow because you will pay for travel.

faqs.question: Can a tutor still help with an internal assessment that is nearly due?
faqs.answer: Within the same boundary as at any other point in the year, which urgency does not move. A tutor may explain each criterion letter by letter with the marks attached, interrogate the research question, teach methodology, read the student's own draft and give written feedback against the criteria, and teach referencing. A tutor may not write any part of it, dictate sentences, supply a dataset or methodology, edit a draft to completion, or provide a model to adapt. An investigation flagged at moderation in the final year arrives when there is no time left to remedy it.

faqs.question: When do IB results come out and should we plan around that date?
faqs.answer: We do not publish a specific IB exam or results date on these pages. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so any date here would be second-hand, and a wrong date in a final-year family's planning is worse than none. Ask your Diploma coordinator for the entered session and the results date in writing and verify against ibo.org. For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications sat alongside, the dates are sourced: Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

faqs.question: What does UAE equivalency require if our child applies to a university here?
faqs.answer: For the British track, passes in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no lower than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. For the American track, SAT Math 450 or above plus English via IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT reading and writing 450. For the IB we will not publish a points threshold we have not read on moe.gov.ae. The Ministry runs this process; IB Gram has no part in it.

faqs.question: Why is it hard to book an HL science tutor right after the mocks?
faqs.answer: Because the whole Dubai market reaches the same conclusion in the same fortnight. Demand for Higher Level science, Maths AA HL and HL Economics specialists peaks immediately after the mocks, which is precisely when families decide they need one. A specific evening hour in one of those subjects often cannot be filled at short notice, and when that is the case we say so rather than booking a generalist against a Higher Level component. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, matching extends to our wider base including IB specialists in India.

faqs.question: How should the final term be scheduled around Ramadan?
faqs.answer: By agreeing the change in advance rather than renegotiating weekly. During Ramadan the school day shortens and the productive window moves, for many families to after Iftar, and in the final term displaced revision does not get made up later because there is no later. Fix the revised slot once, for the month. The UAE working week runs Monday to Friday with a Saturday-Sunday weekend, so Friday evening remains a school night, and Eid breaks are announced rather than fixed far ahead, which argues for a plan with some slack in it.

faqs.question: Can a Dubai DP tutor promise a grade improvement in Grade 12?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody honestly can. What can be described is which components have recoverable marks, why, and roughly how many sessions a particular technique fix usually takes — six to ten for non-calculator technique or uncertainty treatment, two to four for answer-length control and timing. What cannot be offered is a promised grade, a promised point total, a promised prediction or a promised admission outcome. A provider offering any of those is making a claim about an examination they do not mark, and it is a reason to discount everything else they say.

dubai/grade-12-ib-dp-tutor.closingHeading: Buy the weeks after the mocks, and skip the ones that cannot work
dubai/grade-12-ib-dp-tutor.closingBody: The final Diploma year is the most expensive point in the programme and the one where value varies most, so the plan matters more than the rate. Read the marked mock papers rather than the grades, separate technique from volume honestly, put the money into the weeks right after the mocks, and protect the application weeks and the final fortnight from a slot nobody can use. Ask the coordinator about the enquiry window and the retake route before results day. Book a free trial lesson in the component the papers actually name. Sessions are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time; we do not send tutors to UAE homes.

dubai/grade-6-ib-myp-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors matched for Grade 6 work in the MYP's own assessment language rather than translating it into percentages. That matters because a parent's real question — is my child actually improving — can only be answered criterion by criterion in this programme.

intro.heading: Why a Grade 6 report is so hard to read
paragraphs: In Grade 5 a Dubai parent got a portfolio, a teacher comment and, in many schools, a clear sense of where their child sat. In Grade 6 the same parent receives a grid. Each subject carries four criteria lettered A to D, each marked on a 0-8 scale, and the four are converted to a single grade from 1 to 7 by published boundaries. A child can score 6, 6, 3 and 5 and come out with the same subject grade as a child who scored 5, 5, 5 and 5, and the two children need entirely different help.

This is not an accident of reporting; it is the design. The MYP assesses four distinct competencies per subject rather than one aggregate performance, and the four are deliberately unlike each other. In mathematics, criterion A is knowing and understanding, which looks most like what primary rewarded. Criterion B is investigating patterns, criterion C is communicating, and criterion D is applying mathematics in real-life contexts. A child who is fluent at arithmetic and weak at describing a pattern in words will score 7 on A and 3 on B, and no percentage can express that.

Which leads to the specific thing this page is about. The only honest answer to 'is my child making progress' in Grade 6 is criterion-level evidence: which criterion was scored, on what task, against which descriptor, and whether the same criterion scored higher on the next task. A tutor who cannot talk in those terms is guessing, and so is a parent. Three criterion points on criterion B across a term is real, visible, defensible progress. 'Seems more confident' is not.

There is a Dubai layer on top of this, and it is worth knowing in the first term rather than the third. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited, and calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit while advising at least 25 minutes for any mandatory subject lesson. So a Grade 6 child in Dubai is carrying eight MYP subject groups plus those requirements, which is a real timetable.

All IB Gram tuition in the UAE is delivered one-to-one, live over video, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is an India-only service. For a Grade 6 student that is rarely a constraint, because the help needed is specific and short rather than pastoral, and because a session that survives a Dubai school run matters more than a tutor who lives nearby.

Two children with the same subject grade can need opposite kinds of help
Progress in the MYP is measurable only at criterion level, task by task

dubai/grade-6-ib-myp-tutor.programmesIntro: Grade 6 sits at the start of the MYP, immediately after the PYP and four years before the DP decision. Each neighbouring programme explains something about why Grade 6 feels the way it does.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, Year 1
programmes.description: Eight subject groups: language and literature, language acquisition, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics, arts, physical and health education, and design. Each is assessed against four lettered criteria scored 0-8, converted to a 1-7 subject grade. Learning is organised around key and related concepts and a global context, and students are also assessed on Approaches to Learning skills.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, Grade 6 is usually the first year in the secondary section of the school, so the criteria change arrives at the same time as a new building, more teachers and a longer day. Families routinely attribute a dip to the assessment system when it is partly the transition, or to the transition when it is partly the criteria. Separating the two is the first useful thing a tutor does.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary and inquiry-led, organised around units of inquiry, with no external examinations. Assessment is by portfolio plus the Grade 5 Exhibition, a substantial group inquiry presented to the school community. Learning is reported through comments and evidence rather than through criterion scores.
programmes.countryNote: The PYP Exhibition is the best predictor of a comfortable Grade 6, and parents can use it as such. A child who planned, researched, presented and reflected independently in the Exhibition has already met most of what criterion B and criterion D demand in MYP subjects. A child who was carried by a strong group has not, and that gap shows up in the first MYP criterion scores rather than in the content.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher Level and three Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries internal assessment and external examinations, with grades from 1 to 7 plus up to three bonus points, for a ceiling of 45.
programmes.countryNote: Four years away, and the reason Grade 6 criterion habits matter. The DP's internal assessments ask for exactly what MYP criterion B and C ask for in miniature: investigate something, communicate it in a defensible structure, evaluate it honestly. A student who learns that in Grade 6 arrives in DP1 able to do it. A student who learns it in DP1 is learning it under deadline pressure.

dubai/grade-6-ib-myp-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the Grade 6 subjects where parents most often ask for help in Dubai, each with the criterion where the marks actually go missing rather than a general description of the course.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criterion A, knowing and understanding, usually scores highest because it resembles primary work. Marks go missing on criterion B, investigating patterns, where a child must describe a general rule in words and justify it, and on criterion C, communicating, where working has to be readable.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: The big change from primary is criterion B, inquiring and designing: choosing a variable, controlling the others, and explaining why. Criterion C, processing and evaluating, asks a Grade 6 student to say what went wrong with their own experiment, which is a new genre of writing for most.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Criterion A, analysing, is where the step up bites: a child used to retelling a story is asked how the writer produces an effect. Criterion D, using language, rewards range and accuracy, which is where a strong reader with careless punctuation loses marks.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.levels: MYP phases, Arabic, French or Spanish
subjects.description: Marked in phases rather than year groups, which surprises families. A child can be in Grade 6 and in a low phase, and the phase is what determines the descriptor their work is marked against. Worth checking which phase your child is actually in and why.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criterion B, investigating, requires a research question and a plan, which is the single most common Grade 6 struggle across any subject. Criterion D, thinking critically, asks for evaluation of a source, not a summary of it.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Four criteria across a design cycle: inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. Children who build something excellent and document nothing score poorly, because three of the four criteria are about the documented process.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first or additional language
subjects.description: Required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, with Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for first-language Arabic. The stream a child is placed in now shapes their options in Grade 10.

subjects.name: Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies
subjects.description: Taught alongside the licensed curriculum, with KHDA specifying the language of instruction for Arab and non-Arab streams separately. Support works from the school's own material, because additional or different content requires prior Ministry of Education permission.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criterion-marked like everything else, which catches parents out: a developing artist is marked partly on a process journal and a reflection rather than on the finished piece. The journal is where most Grade 6 marks are lost in this subject group.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Includes planning for performance and reflecting on it, so a physically capable child can still score in the middle if the written reflection is thin. Rarely tutored, but worth knowing about when reading a report that seems inconsistent.

sections.heading: How a Grade 6 MYP grade is actually produced
paragraphs: Each MYP subject is assessed against four criteria lettered A to D. Every criterion is marked on a 0-8 scale against published descriptors that describe what work at each band looks like. At reporting time the four criterion scores are combined and converted to a single subject grade from 1 to 7 using boundaries the school applies. That is the whole mechanism, and understanding it answers most of the questions a Grade 6 parent has.

Two consequences follow immediately. First, the subject grade hides the shape of the performance. A child scoring 7, 7, 2 and 4 and a child scoring 5, 5, 5, 5 can land on the same number, and they need opposite interventions: the first needs one specific skill built, the second needs general consolidation. Any conversation about a Grade 6 report that stops at the subject grade has thrown away the useful information.

Second, criterion scores are not percentages and should not be read as such. A 5 out of 8 is not 62 per cent of anything. The descriptor at band 5 describes a quality of work — for instance, an explanation that is mostly complete and uses some subject terminology accurately — and the way to move from 5 to 6 is to produce the thing the band 6 descriptor describes. That is a concrete, nameable change in how a piece of work is written, not an instruction to try harder.

The practical move for a parent is to ask the school for the criterion descriptors for the subjects that matter, and to ask which criterion each returned task was marked against. Most Dubai schools publish them or will send them on request. Put the descriptor next to the child's marked work and the gap is usually obvious within ten minutes.

sections.heading: What a term of real progress looks like, in evidence
paragraphs: Parents of Grade 6 students in Dubai are often told their child is settling in well, and have no way to test that. Here is the testable version. Progress in the MYP is a criterion score that was lower on one task and higher on a comparable later task, with a nameable reason for the change. Everything else is impression.

A worked example. A Grade 6 mathematics student scores 3 on criterion B on an investigation about number patterns, with the descriptor indicating that they applied a pattern but did not describe a general rule. Over six weeks the work targets exactly that: spotting a pattern, stating the rule in words, then in symbols, then justifying why it holds. On the next criterion B task the same student scores 5. That is progress, it is documented, and nobody has to take anybody's word for it.

The same logic applies to criterion C in the sciences, which is where Grade 6 students most consistently underperform in Dubai schools. Processing and evaluating asks the student to present their data clearly and then discuss its limitations. Children who have never been asked to criticise their own work write 'the experiment went well'. Teaching three sentence patterns — what went wrong, why it affected the result, and what would fix it — moves the criterion within a term. It is small, specific and completely measurable.

What does not constitute evidence: a higher subject grade with no criterion detail, since it can come from a different task mix; increased confidence, which is welcome and unmeasurable; more homework completed, which is a process not an outcome; and a tutor's general report that the child is doing better. Insist on criterion-level evidence, from us and from the school. It is the only language the programme actually speaks.

sections.heading: The PYP to MYP step: what actually changes
paragraphs: The content change between Grade 5 and Grade 6 is modest. The assessment change is large, and the organisational change is larger still. Separating those three is the first useful thing to do when a Grade 6 report disappoints, because the three need different responses and families usually treat all of them as an academic problem.

Organisationally, Grade 6 in a Dubai school usually means the secondary building, eight or more subject teachers instead of one or two, a longer day, homework from multiple sources arriving on the same evening, and lockers, timetables and room changes to manage. A capable eleven-year-old can be defeated by the logistics alone while understanding every lesson. The MYP calls these Approaches to Learning skills and assesses them explicitly, which is helpful, because it means the school is already looking at them.

Assessment-wise, the shift is from evidence-and-comment reporting to four criterion scores per subject. In the PYP, a child's capability showed in a portfolio and a teacher's description. In the MYP it shows as a number against a descriptor, and a child who has never been told the descriptor cannot aim at it. This is the single most common cause of a disappointing first MYP report for a child who did well in primary: they are producing good Grade 5 work in a system that is asking for something slightly different.

The PYP Exhibition is the best available predictor of how the step will go, and parents can use it retrospectively. A child who chose their own line of inquiry, planned it, gathered information, presented it and reflected honestly on what they would change has already practised criterion B and criterion D behaviour in several subject groups. A child who contributed to a strong group without doing those things has not, and that is where the first MYP criterion scores will land.

sections.heading: Grade 6 in a Dubai school: the subjects nobody warned you about
paragraphs: A Grade 6 MYP student in Dubai carries eight subject groups plus the UAE mandatory subjects, and the mandatory subjects are the part families most often under-plan. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements that had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year.

The organisational rules are specific and worth knowing. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. KHDA requires Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic as the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

There is a Grade 6 reason to care about this beyond the timetable. The Arabic stream a child is in now is the stream they will still be in at Grade 10 options, and that is what determines whether Arabic A is available to them in the Diploma. A dialect-fluent child placed in the non-Arab additional-language stream in primary, and left there, will arrive at options evening without the written register that Arabic A requires. Grade 6 and 7 are when that placement can still be raised usefully.

On teaching time, KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and advises that any mandatory subject lesson is at least 25 minutes. And on content, the use of any different or additional content for these subjects without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited — which is exactly why support for them works from the school's own material rather than a scheme a tutor has written.

sections.heading: What Grade 6 tutoring costs in Dubai, and when it is worth it
paragraphs: Grade 6 is the cheapest useful place in the whole MYP to intervene, and the most commonly skipped. Market rates for a qualified subject tutor working online in Dubai run AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Bestimate's Dubai 2026 monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240-600 at the budget end and AED 600-1,200 in the middle. Those are market figures from published sources, not our price list.

For Grade 6 specifically, the lower bands are more often appropriate than they are later. EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33-52, which buys supervision and structure. If the actual problem is a child who cannot start their homework, that is the right product and paying four times more is waste. If the problem is criterion B in mathematics, it is not, because reading a band descriptor against a child's work requires someone who knows the programme.

The argument for spending now rather than later is arithmetic. A criterion habit built in Grade 6 is used for five MYP years and then again in every Diploma internal assessment. The same habit taught in DP1 is taught under deadline pressure at the exam-year specialist band, which Bestimate puts at AED 1,000-2,000 or more a month. Families who treat Grade 6 as too early frequently buy the same understanding in Grade 11 at several times the price.

One context figure worth having: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. With the fee held flat, the tuition line is the variable one in a family's education budget, which makes the question of when to spend it the one that matters.

sections.heading: Online or in the room for an eleven-year-old
paragraphs: This is the honest objection to an online session for a Grade 6 student, and it deserves a real answer rather than a sales one. A younger child benefits from a person in the room in ways a sixteen-year-old does not: attention is easier to hold, a glance catches a confusion that a video call misses, and the social cost of admitting you do not understand is lower.

Against that, three things. First, what a Grade 6 MYP student needs is specific rather than pastoral: someone who can read a band descriptor against their work and say what to change. The pool of people who can do that for MYP criteria, in a given Dubai community, at the hour the child is home, is narrower than the pool available online. Second, the travel premium is real — Bestimate puts in-home visits at AED 180-350 against AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor — and it buys the commute, not the expertise.

Third, the practical reliability. A Grade 6 session that starts at 4pm from Arabian Ranches or 6pm from Business Bay has to survive a term of traffic, activities and family travel. A video slot survives all three, and it survives the family changing address, which Dubai families do more than most.

IB Gram's position is fixed rather than a preference: we deliver UAE tuition one-to-one, live over video, and we do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we offer only in India. If what you want for an eleven-year-old is a person at the dining table in Dubai, we are not the provider and will say so rather than talking you out of it.

sections.heading: Academic honesty starts in Grade 6, not in the Diploma
paragraphs: It is worth setting this out on a Grade 6 page because the habits formed here are the ones a student carries into the Personal Project in Grade 10 and the internal assessments in the Diploma. The IB's rules on academic honesty apply throughout the MYP, and the behaviours that get a sixteen-year-old into serious trouble usually started as a parent helping a eleven-year-old a little too much.

What a tutor may do for a Grade 6 student is substantial: teach the content, explain the criterion descriptors and what the band above looks like, model how a task of that type is approached, discuss and challenge the child's own ideas, read the child's draft and say what is missing against the criterion, and teach how to record where information came from. Referencing taught in Grade 6 is a gift to the Grade 12 version of the same student.

What a tutor may not do is write any part of a submitted task, dictate sentences for the child to copy, produce the investigation or the design documentation, or correct a draft into a finished state. The same applies to parents, and in Grade 6 that is the more common route. A beautifully presented piece of work that an eleven-year-old did not actually produce teaches them nothing about criterion C and costs them the feedback that would have helped.

One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at Diploma level. That is where this road ends, and the consequence falls on the student, who can be excluded. Teaching an eleven-year-old that their own imperfect work is the thing being marked is the single most useful piece of academic-honesty education available, and Grade 6 is exactly when it lands.

sections.heading: Scheduling a Grade 6 week in Dubai
paragraphs: Grade 6 is the first year where the school day, homework from multiple teachers and after-school activities compete for the same evening, and the scheduling decision matters more than it did in primary. The UAE working week runs Monday to Friday with a Saturday-Sunday weekend, so Friday evening is a school night — families arriving from countries where it is not routinely book their heaviest session there and lose half of them.

The realistic start time depends on the community. A family inside Dubai Hills Estate with schooling in the community can hold a 4pm weekday slot. A family in Arabian Ranches or Nad Al Sheba usually finds 5pm is the earliest that survives a term, and a Business Bay family with a school in Al Barsha is looking at 6pm. For an eleven-year-old, 6pm after a long secondary day is near the edge of useful, which is a genuine argument for a weekend session instead.

During Ramadan the school day shortens and the household rhythm changes, with the productive study window moving for many families to after Iftar. For a Grade 6 student the better answer is often to reduce rather than reschedule: one session instead of two for the month, at a time that works, rather than two sessions a child is too tired to use. Eid breaks are announced rather than fixed far ahead.

The best Grade 6 scheduling decision available is also the least used: the two or three weeks after a long break, before assessments restart, are when a criterion can be consolidated without competing with homework. Families almost always spend them on holiday. Using one of them deliberately is worth more than a month of sessions squeezed between a long school day and bedtime.

faqs.question: What do the four letters on my child's Grade 6 MYP report mean?
faqs.answer: They are the four assessment criteria for that subject, each marked on a 0-8 scale against published band descriptors, and combined into a single 1-7 subject grade. In mathematics, for example, criterion A is knowing and understanding, B is investigating patterns, C is communicating and D is applying mathematics in real-life contexts. The letters matter more than the final number, because a child scoring 7, 7, 2 and 4 and one scoring 5, 5, 5, 5 can land on the same grade while needing opposite help. Ask the school for the descriptors.

faqs.question: Why did my child go from strong in Grade 5 to average in Grade 6?
faqs.answer: Usually because three things changed at once and only one of them is academic. The content step is modest. The assessment step is large: evidence-and-comment reporting becomes four criterion scores against descriptors the child has often never read. The organisational step is largest: eight subject teachers, a longer day, room changes and homework from several sources arriving the same evening. A capable eleven-year-old can be defeated by logistics while understanding every lesson. Separating the three is the first useful thing to do, because each needs a different response.

faqs.question: How can I tell whether Grade 6 tutoring is actually working?
faqs.answer: By criterion, not by impression. Ask which criterion was targeted, what the band descriptor said at the starting score, and what the same criterion scored on a comparable later task. A move from 3 to 5 on criterion B in mathematics, with a nameable reason — the student now states a general rule in words and justifies it — is documented progress. A higher subject grade on its own is not evidence, because the task mix may have changed. Neither is increased confidence, which is welcome and unmeasurable. Insist on the criterion-level version from any tutor.

faqs.question: Which criterion do Grade 6 students in Dubai most often lose marks on?
faqs.answer: Criterion B in mathematics and criterion C in the sciences, for the same underlying reason. Both ask a child to write about their own thinking rather than produce a correct answer. Criterion B wants a pattern described as a general rule and justified; criterion C in sciences wants the student to process their data and then evaluate it, which means saying honestly what went wrong and why. Children who have never been asked to criticise their own work write 'the experiment went well'. Teaching three sentence patterns for that moves the criterion within a term.

faqs.question: Is Grade 6 too early to start tutoring in the MYP?
faqs.answer: It is the cheapest useful place in the programme to intervene, and the most commonly skipped. A criterion habit built now is used across five MYP years and again in every Diploma internal assessment. The same habit taught in DP1 is taught under deadline pressure at the exam-year band, which Bestimate's published Dubai estimates put at AED 1,000-2,000 or more a month against AED 240-1,200 for a single weekly Grade 6 session. The caveat is that it should be short: target one criterion, re-test it, and stop when it holds.

faqs.question: My child understands the work but cannot organise themselves. Is that a tutoring problem?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the MYP already names it. Approaches to Learning skills are assessed explicitly in the programme, and the ones that bite in Year 1 are planning a task, managing several deadlines at once, taking usable notes and checking work before submitting it. These are worked on using the child's actual assignments rather than in the abstract, and the checking routine in particular recovers criterion C marks very cheaply. If that is the whole problem, a supervision-band tutor at the lower market rate may be a better fit than a subject specialist.

faqs.question: Does my Grade 6 child have to study Arabic in a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements due for implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Grade 6 is a good moment to check in writing which stream your child is recorded in, because it shapes their Grade 11 options.

faqs.question: What is an MYP phase, and why is my child in a low one?
faqs.answer: Language Acquisition in the MYP is organised in phases rather than year groups, so a child's work is marked against the descriptors for their phase rather than for Grade 6. Phases are set by the school based on prior learning, which means a child who arrived without that language, or who was placed in a particular stream in primary, can sit in a low phase while performing well within it. That is not a problem in itself, but it is worth understanding, because the phase a child is in through the MYP influences which language routes are open to them in the Diploma.

faqs.question: How much does a Grade 6 MYP tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates for a qualified subject tutor working online run AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. For Grade 6 specifically the lower supervision band is often appropriate: EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52, which buys structure for a child who will not start homework. Bestimate's published Dubai monthly estimates for one weekly session run AED 240-600 at the budget end and AED 600-1,200 in the middle. These are market figures with sources, not our price list; ours follows a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Can an eleven-year-old really learn well over video?
faqs.answer: For this specific job, yes, with the honest caveat that a person in the room has real advantages for a younger child. What a Grade 6 MYP student needs is narrow: someone who can read a band descriptor against their work and say what to change. The pool of people who can do that in a given Dubai community at the hour the child is home is far narrower than the pool available online, and the in-home travel premium — Bestimate puts visits at AED 180-350 — buys the commute rather than the expertise. We do not offer UAE home visits in any case.

faqs.question: Should I just fix my child's work for them before they hand it in?
faqs.answer: No, and in Grade 6 this is the commonest route past the academic honesty line — a well-meaning parent rather than a tutor. A beautifully presented piece an eleven-year-old did not produce teaches them nothing about criterion C and costs them the feedback that would have helped. What is legitimate is reading the descriptor with them, asking what is missing, and letting them make the change. The habit matters because it is the same boundary that governs the Grade 10 Personal Project and every Diploma internal assessment, where the consequences are serious.

faqs.question: How does the Grade 5 PYP Exhibition predict how Grade 6 will go?
faqs.answer: Quite well, and parents can use it retrospectively. A child who chose their own line of inquiry, planned it, gathered information independently, presented it and reflected honestly on what they would change has already practised what criterion B and criterion D ask for across several MYP subject groups. A child who contributed to a strong group without doing those things has not, and that gap shows up in the first MYP criterion scores rather than in the content knowledge. If the Exhibition was carried by others, expect criterion B to be the first thing to address.

faqs.question: What time can a Grade 6 session realistically start in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It depends on the community and it is worth deciding honestly before booking. Inside Dubai Hills Estate with schooling in the community, 4pm works through term. From Arabian Ranches or Nad Al Sheba, 5pm is usually the earliest that survives. From Business Bay with a school in Al Barsha, 6pm — which for an eleven-year-old after a long secondary day is near the edge of useful, and a weekend session is often the better answer. Remember the UAE week runs Monday to Friday with a Saturday-Sunday weekend, so Friday evening is a school night.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Grade 6 student need?
faqs.answer: Usually one, in one subject, for a defined period. Grade 6 problems are typically a single criterion or a set of organisational habits, and both respond to a weekly hour with written work in between. Two sessions a week is occasionally right at the start, if two subjects are both scoring low on the same underlying skill, but it should step down. What is almost never right is a standing two-session slot across the whole year, because the targeted criterion either moves within a term or the diagnosis was wrong and more hours will not fix it.

faqs.question: Do you tutor Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies for Grade 6?
faqs.answer: Yes, worked from the school's own material and the official curriculum. KHDA states that for the mandatory UAE subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so nothing parallel is introduced. KHDA also specifies the language of instruction separately for Arab and non-Arab streams, and requires that school teachers of these subjects hold appropriate KHDA approval — a question a parent is entitled to ask the school. Support here is about written expression and terminology rather than content a tutor has chosen.

faqs.question: When in the Dubai year is the best time to work on a weak criterion?
faqs.answer: The two or three weeks after a long break, before assessments restart. Nothing is competing with homework, a two-hour session is realistic on a weekday, and a criterion can actually be consolidated rather than patched. Families almost always use those weeks for travel, which is reasonable, but using one of them deliberately is worth more than a month of sessions squeezed between a long secondary day and bedtime. During Ramadan the better move is usually to reduce frequency rather than push a tired child later, since the productive window shifts after Iftar.

intro.heading: The year nothing happens, and why that matters
paragraphs: Every other year of the Middle Years Programme has a reason to pay attention. Grade 6 is the move into criterion-based assessment and a secondary building. Grade 8 is where subjects begin to specialise. Grade 9 starts the final two-year MYP cycle and brings the Diploma decision into view. Grade 10 carries the Personal Project and the options evening. Grade 7 has none of that, which is exactly the problem: nothing forces a family to look closely, so nobody does.

What actually happens in Grade 7 is consolidation of the things Grade 6 introduced and the introduction of the things Grade 8 will assume. In mathematics that means negative numbers and directed number operations become routine, ratio and proportional reasoning arrive properly, algebraic manipulation moves beyond substitution into solving, and the geometry of angles and basic transformations is formalised. None of it is dramatic. All of it is assumed from Grade 8 onwards and never taught again.

In the sciences, Year 2 is where the three disciplines start to be distinguishable inside an integrated course and where quantitative work enters: units, simple calculations, graph conventions, and the beginnings of variable control in criterion B. In language and literature it is where analysis stops being optional, and where a student who still retells the plot stops scoring in the upper bands. In language acquisition it is the year a child either moves up a phase or settles into the one they will be in at Grade 10 options.

The consequence for tutoring is a different brief from any other MYP year. In Grade 6 you diagnose a criterion. In Grade 10 you work to a deadline. In Grade 7 you audit: you find the topics that were covered quickly and not secured, and you secure them, because the cost of not doing so arrives two years later wearing a different label. A Grade 9 student who cannot rearrange an equation is almost always a Grade 7 student who met it in a busy half-term.

There is a Dubai timetable layer on top. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements due for implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, and advises that any mandatory subject lesson should be at least 25 minutes. A Grade 7 week is fuller than it looks.

A word on delivery, because a Grade 7 audit only works with the student's own working in front of both people. All IB Gram tuition in the UAE is one-to-one and live over video, on Gulf Standard Time, so a page of half-secured ratio or directed-number work can go on screen and be gone through line by line in the hour it was written. We send a tutor to no home anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run in India only.

dubai/grade-7-ib-myp-tutor.programmesIntro: Grade 7 sits between the year of adjustment and the year of specialisation. Understanding what each neighbouring stage assumes is how a parent works out whether Year 2 was actually secured.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, Year 2
programmes.description: Eight subject groups continuing from Grade 6, assessed against four lettered criteria per subject scored 0-8 and converted to a 1-7 grade. Learning is framed by key and related concepts and a global context, with Approaches to Learning skills assessed alongside subject content and service as action running through the year.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai schools, Grade 7 is the year the novelty of secondary has worn off and the programme's own structure takes over. Reports look much like the Grade 6 ones, which makes a slow drift easy to miss: a criterion that sat at 5 all year is not a problem on any single report and is a problem by Grade 9. Compare criterion scores across the year rather than reading each report alone.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, Years 3 to 5
programmes.description: The same eight subject groups with growing subject specialisation, more quantitative demand in sciences and mathematics, and increasing independence in criterion B investigations. Year 5 carries the Personal Project with its process journal and report, and in some schools an optional external eAssessment route.
programmes.countryNote: The reason Grade 7 matters. From Grade 8 the sciences separate in substance even where they share a timetable slot, mathematics assumes fluent algebraic manipulation, and individuals and societies expects a research question without scaffolding. Nothing in Years 3 to 5 re-teaches Year 2 content, so an unsecured Grade 7 topic becomes an invisible drag for three years.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across three Higher Level and three Standard Level choices, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. programmes.countryNote: Four years on, and the place where Grade 7 arithmetic and algebra gaps resurface most expensively. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches assumes complete fluency in manipulation, and Paper 1 is sat without a calculator at both levels. A student who was never secure with directed numbers and fractions in Year 2 pays for it in DP1 at the exam-year tutoring band rather than the Grade 7 one.

sections.heading: What Grade 7 actually covers, topic by topic
paragraphs: Parents of Grade 7 students in Dubai rarely have a clear picture of the content, because the reports describe criteria rather than topics and the schemes of work are not always published. Here is the practical version, and the useful thing about it is that it is short enough to audit.

In mathematics, Year 2 formalises directed number operations and the relationship between fractions, decimals and percentages as a single system rather than three. It introduces ratio and proportional reasoning properly, moves algebra from substitution into solving linear equations, and formalises angle rules and basic transformations. Four or five topics, each of which Grade 8 onwards treats as automatic.

In the sciences, Year 2 brings quantitative work: units and measurement, simple calculation, graph conventions including choice of axes and scale, and the first genuine variable control under criterion B. In language and literature, the demand shifts from understanding a text to explaining how it achieves its effect, and criterion D begins rewarding sentence variety and accurate punctuation rather than volume. In individuals and societies, source work begins and research questions appear with scaffolding still attached.

The audit question for each of these is not 'was it taught' but 'is it secure'. A topic is secure when the student can do it unprompted, two weeks after the lesson, without reference to a worked example. Almost every Grade 7 student in a Dubai school has a handful of topics that were taught, understood at the time, and are not secure — and the ones that matter are the ones with the longest downstream dependency.

sections.heading: Where each Year 2 topic resurfaces, and what it costs then
paragraphs: The argument for working in Grade 7 is a dependency argument rather than a performance one. A Year 2 topic that is not secure does not cause a bad Grade 7 report. It causes a bad Grade 9 report, a struggle in DP1, and in the worst case a subject choice narrowed at Grade 10 options by a weakness nobody traced.

The clearest chain runs through algebra. A student who cannot reliably rearrange a linear equation in Grade 7 can usually still pass Grade 8 by pattern-matching. By Grade 9 the equations have two steps more and the pattern-matching fails. By Grade 10 they are choosing between Diploma mathematics routes with a false picture of their own ability, and by DP1 they are in Analysis and Approaches sitting a Paper 1 with no calculator. The original gap is two hours of work in Grade 7 and a term of work in DP1.

The science chain is shorter but just as reliable. Graph conventions and variable control are Year 2 skills that every subsequent practical assumes. A student who never secured them produces criterion B and criterion C work that loses marks for reasons the content revision will not touch, through Grades 8, 9 and 10, and then again in the Diploma internal assessment where the criteria are the same shape but worth a quarter of the subject grade.

The language chain is the quietest and the most consequential. The shift from retelling to analysing happens in Year 2. A student who never makes it writes competent, accurate, well-punctuated summaries for four more years and cannot understand why criterion A sits at 4. Nothing in the content is missing. The genre of the answer is wrong, and it is easiest to change at twelve.

sections.heading: Language acquisition phases: the Grade 7 decision nobody schedules
paragraphs: MYP Language Acquisition runs in phases rather than year groups, and a child's work is marked against the descriptors for their phase. Phases are set by the school on the basis of prior learning. The important structural fact for a Grade 7 family is that phase movement, if it happens at all, usually happens around Year 2, and after that a student tends to stay where they are.

That matters because the phase a student occupies through the MYP shapes which Diploma language routes are realistically open to them. A student who moves up in Year 2 arrives at Grade 10 options with a wider set of choices. A student who settles into a low phase at twelve arrives with a narrower one, often without anyone having made a decision about it.

In Dubai this interacts with Arabic specifically. Arabic is mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. A child placed in the non-Arab additional-language stream in primary, and never reviewed, reaches Grade 10 without the written register that Arabic A requires in the Diploma.

The practical action is a conversation, not a tutoring purchase. Ask the school which phase your child is in, what the criteria for moving up are, and what they would need to demonstrate. Most schools will answer plainly. Where the answer suggests the phase is a holdover from a primary placement rather than a current judgement, that is worth pressing in Grade 7, because it is considerably harder to press in Grade 10.
bullets: Phases are marked against phase descriptors, not against the student's grade
Phase movement typically happens around Year 2 or not at all
The phase held through the MYP narrows or widens Diploma language routes

sections.heading: Interdisciplinary units, service as action, and the parts of the report that confuse
paragraphs: Grade 7 reports in Dubai schools carry elements that look peripheral and are not. Interdisciplinary units are assessed in the MYP with their own criteria, and they ask students to combine understanding from two subject groups to address a problem. A student who is solid in both subjects can still score mid-band here, because the skill assessed is the synthesis rather than either subject.

Service as action runs through the MYP and is reported on, and it is a genuine part of the programme rather than an extracurricular note. It is not usually a tutoring matter, but it is worth knowing about when a report seems to contain comments unrelated to subject performance. The same goes for Approaches to Learning, which the programme assesses explicitly and which in Year 2 centres on self-management: planning, meeting deadlines and organising materials.

The reason to pay attention to these in Grade 7 rather than later is that they are rehearsals. The interdisciplinary unit rehearses the kind of thinking Theory of Knowledge will ask for in the Diploma. Service as action rehearses the Creativity, Activity, Service strand. The self-management strand of Approaches to Learning rehearses every coursework deadline a student will ever meet. None of them are assessed harshly at twelve, which makes Year 2 a cheap place to learn them.

For a parent reading a Grade 7 report, the useful discipline is to separate the subject criteria from everything else, respond to the subject criteria with subject work, and respond to the rest with habits. Buying subject tutoring for a self-management problem is the commonest misdirection of money in this year, and it does not work, because the lessons are not where the problem is.
bullets: Interdisciplinary units assess synthesis, not either subject individually
Service as action and Approaches to Learning are reported on and are real programme elements
Year 2 is the cheap place to learn self-management, because it is not yet assessed harshly

sections.heading: What Grade 7 support costs in Dubai, and the shape to buy
paragraphs: Market rates for a qualified subject tutor working online in Dubai run AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Bestimate's published Dubai 2026 monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240-600 at the budget end and AED 600-1,200 in the middle. Those are market figures from named sources rather than a price list of ours.

The shape matters more in Grade 7 than the rate. An audit is a short, finite purchase: two or three sessions to test the Year 2 topic list and produce a written secured-or-not list, followed by however many sessions the list actually requires. For most students that is a block of six to ten sessions in total, not a year-long slot. Buying a standing weekly hour in Year 2 without an audit first is buying a solution before anyone has described the problem.

The lower market band has a legitimate Grade 7 use. EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33-52, which buys supervision and structure. If the audit shows the content is secure and the issue is self-management, that band is the right fit and paying specialist rates for homework supervision is waste. The audit is what tells you which of the two you are buying.

On the longer-run arithmetic: a Year 2 topic secured now takes a couple of hours. The same topic reached in DP1, where it has compounded through three years of dependent work, is addressed at the exam-year specialist band that Bestimate puts at AED 1,000-2,000 or more a month. One context figure helps here: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, which makes tuition the variable line in a family's education budget and the timing of it the decision that matters.
