sections.heading: The KHDA layer in a Grade 7 Dubai week
paragraphs: A Grade 7 student in a Dubai private school carries eight MYP subject groups plus the UAE mandatory subjects, and families consistently underestimate how much of the week that is. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements that had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year — April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and advises that the length of any mandatory subject lesson should be at least 25 minutes. The practical effect in Year 2 is that the timetable is dense, and a family adding two tutoring sessions to it without looking at the week as a whole is likely to get neither.

On organisation, KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. It requires Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic as the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies. It also requires that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval.

On content, KHDA states that for the mandatory UAE subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. That is why support for these subjects works from the school's own material and the official curriculum rather than from a scheme a tutor has built, and it is a constraint worth knowing before anyone offers you a parallel Arabic programme.
bullets: Eight MYP subject groups plus the KHDA mandatory subjects in a Year 2 week
Instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit; 25 minutes advised as a minimum
Separate Arab and non-Arab classes required; combined classes strictly prohibited
Additional or different content for mandatory subjects needs Ministry permission

sections.heading: Academic honesty in a year of documented process
paragraphs: Grade 7 is where the documentation habit forms in design, arts and investigative work, and that is exactly where the academic honesty boundary gets blurred by well-meaning help. The MYP's rules on honesty apply throughout the programme, and the behaviours that cause serious problems at Diploma level almost always start as small conveniences in the middle years.

What a tutor may do is substantial. They may teach the content, explain each criterion descriptor and what the band above requires, model how a task of that type is approached using a different example, discuss and challenge the student's own ideas, read the student's draft and say what is missing against the criterion, and teach how to record where information came from. Referencing taught in Year 2 is a direct gift to the Grade 10 Personal Project and every Diploma internal assessment.

What a tutor may not do is write any part of a submitted task, dictate sentences for the student to copy, produce the process documentation or the design journal, or correct a draft into a finished state. In the MYP specifically, the process journal is the easiest thing in the programme to ghostwrite and the most damaging, because three of the four criteria in some subjects depend on it and the student learns nothing about the one skill the task existed to build.

At Diploma level this road ends with operators who sell completed Internal Assessments, which is an IB malpractice trigger where the consequence falls on the student, not the seller. Teaching a twelve-year-old that their own imperfect documented process is the thing being marked is the cheapest academic-honesty lesson available, and Year 2 is when it lands without drama.
bullets: Allowed: content taught, descriptors explained, drafts read, referencing taught
Not allowed: writing, dictating, producing a process journal, correcting to completion
The process journal is the easiest MYP artefact to ghostwrite and the most damaging
Official syllabus documents and past papers are linked, never reproduced or supplied

sections.heading: Scheduling Grade 7 in a Dubai year
paragraphs: A Grade 7 week in Dubai is fuller than a Grade 6 one: the same eight subject groups plus the mandatory subjects, more homework arriving from more teachers, and usually more activities. The UAE working week runs Monday to Friday with a Saturday-Sunday weekend, which means Friday evening is a school night — a detail that reliably catches out families whose instincts were formed elsewhere.

Realistic start times vary by community. From Dubai Hills Estate with schooling in the community, 4.30pm holds. From Arabian Ranches or Mudon along the Al Khail corridor, 5pm or later. From Business Bay with a school in Al Barsha, 6pm, which after a full secondary day is near the limit of usefulness for a twelve-year-old and is a real argument for a weekend session instead.

During Ramadan the school day shortens and the productive window moves, for many families to after Iftar. For Grade 7 the better response is usually to reduce frequency for the month rather than push a tired student later. Eid breaks are announced rather than fixed far in advance, so a plan with some slack in it survives better than a rigid one.

The single best scheduling decision available in Year 2 is the holiday audit block. With no homework competing, two-hour sessions across a few days can audit the topic list and secure several items, which term time simply does not allow. The two or three weeks after a long break, before assessments restart, are the most productive period in the whole Grade 7 year, and almost nobody uses them.
bullets: Friday evening is a school night in the UAE; keep the heavy session away from it
Realistic weekday start is 4.30pm, 5pm or 6pm depending on the community

process.title: Ask the school for the Year 2 scheme of work
process.description: Not the report. The scheme of work, or at minimum the topic list for mathematics and sciences. It is the document the audit runs against, and most Dubai schools will provide it on request. Without it the audit is guesswork about what was covered.

process.title: Run the audit in the first two or three sessions
process.description: Short diagnostic questions across the whole Year 2 topic list, testing recall rather than whether the student can follow a worked example. The output is a written list of secured and unsecured topics, ranked by what Grade 8 onwards assumes.

process.title: Read the list before buying anything further
process.description: The list tells you what to buy. Unsecured topics with long downstream dependency need a securing block. Secure content with weak self-management needs a supervision slot at a lower market band. Sound foundations and pacing trouble need a weekly subject slot. They are three different purchases.

process.title: Secure topics in dependency order, then re-test
process.description: One topic per session, taught and then practised independently, with a re-test a fortnight later — because a topic that can be done once with help is not secure. The order follows what later years assume rather than the school's current sequence.

process.title: Raise the language acquisition phase separately
process.description: Ask the school which phase your child is in, what the criteria for moving up are, and what they would need to demonstrate. This is a conversation rather than a purchase, and Grade 7 is a realistic last point to have it usefully.

process.title: Use a holiday block, then stop
process.description: Finish the list in a holiday block if term time is too full, update the written list, and stop. Grade 7 support should be finite. A standing weekly slot with no audit behind it is a subscription, and the year does not justify one.

whyPoints.title: We audit before we sell lessons
whyPoints.description: Grade 7 has no milestone, so there is nothing forcing anyone to find out what is actually missing. The audit produces a written secured-or-not topic list in two or three sessions, and sometimes it says the foundations are fine and a cheaper supervision band is the right fit.

whyPoints.title: Topics traced to where they are needed
whyPoints.description: Securing a Year 2 topic is a dependency argument rather than a performance one. The order of work follows what Grade 8, Grade 10 and DP1 actually assume, which is why a quiet year's gap is worth fixing before it acquires three years of dependent work on top of it.

whyPoints.title: Progress reported as topics closed
whyPoints.description: Not 'improving'. A named topic moved from unsecured to secured, demonstrated by unprompted recall a fortnight later. That is checkable by a parent who was not in the session, which is the only standard worth reporting against.

whyPoints.title: We separate content from organisation
whyPoints.description: A self-management problem does not respond to subject tutoring, and buying subject hours for it is the commonest misdirection of money in Year 2. The audit tells the two apart, and we will say when the cheaper band is the correct answer.

whyPoints.title: The KHDA requirements quoted from source
whyPoints.description: The 40-minute lesson unit, the 25-minute advised minimum, separate Arab and non-Arab classes, and the prohibition on additional content without Ministry permission. These shape a Grade 7 week and they constrain honestly what any tutor can offer for the mandatory subjects.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what we are not
whyPoints.description: No home visits anywhere in the UAE, no KHDA approval or regulator accreditation, no UAE office. Market rates here are attributed to whoever published them rather than presented as ours, and where we cannot match a subject at a workable hour we say so.

faqs.question: What does a Grade 7 student actually cover in MYP mathematics?
faqs.answer: Year 2 formalises directed number operations and treats fractions, decimals and percentages as one system rather than three. It introduces ratio and proportional reasoning properly, moves algebra from substitution into solving linear equations, and formalises angle rules and basic transformations. That is four or five topics, which is short enough to audit in a couple of sessions. The important point is that Grade 8 onwards treats every one of them as automatic and does not re-teach them, so a topic understood at the time but never secured becomes an invisible drag for years.

faqs.question: Why is Grade 7 a risky year if nothing happens in it?
faqs.answer: Because nothing forces anyone to look. Grade 6 brings the move into criterion assessment, Grade 8 brings specialisation, Grade 9 starts the final MYP cycle, Grade 10 carries the Personal Project and options. Grade 7 has no external milestone at all, so a criterion that sits quietly at 5 all year never looks like a problem on any single report and is a problem by Grade 9. The response is an audit rather than a weekly slot: test the Year 2 topic list, find what is unsecured, and secure it before three years of dependent work is built on top.

faqs.question: What does it mean for a topic to be 'secure' rather than just covered?
faqs.answer: A topic is secure when the student can do it unprompted, roughly two weeks after the lesson, without reference to a worked example. Most Grade 7 students in Dubai schools have between four and ten topics across mathematics and sciences that were taught, understood at the time, and are not secure by that test. The distinction matters because the school's records show the topic as covered, the report shows no particular problem, and the gap only surfaces when a later topic assumes it. Re-testing after a fortnight is the whole of the method.

faqs.question: Can a Grade 7 algebra gap really cause a problem in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Reliably, and the chain is predictable. A student who cannot confidently rearrange a linear equation in Year 2 can usually still pass Grade 8 by pattern-matching. In Grade 9 the equations gain a step or two and the pattern-matching fails. At Grade 10 options they are choosing a Diploma mathematics route on a false picture of their own ability, and in DP1 they are in Analysis and Approaches where Paper 1 is sat without a calculator at both levels. The original fix is two hours of Grade 7 work; the later fix is a term at the exam-year band.

faqs.question: My child is in a low MYP language phase. Can that be changed in Grade 7?
faqs.answer: This is the right year to ask. Language Acquisition runs in phases rather than year groups, phases are set by the school on prior learning, and movement between them tends to happen around Year 2 or not at all. The phase held through the MYP then shapes which Diploma language routes are realistically available at Grade 10 options. Ask the school in writing which phase your child is in, what the criteria for moving up are, and what they would need to demonstrate. Where the phase looks like a holdover from a primary placement, press it now.

faqs.question: What is an interdisciplinary unit and why did my child score low on it?
faqs.answer: Interdisciplinary units are assessed in the MYP with their own criteria and ask students to combine understanding from two subject groups to address a problem. The skill being marked is the synthesis, not either subject, so a student who is solid in both can still land mid-band. It is worth paying attention to in Year 2 because it rehearses the kind of thinking Theory of Knowledge asks for in the Diploma, and because at twelve it is assessed without serious consequence, which makes it a cheap place to learn the move.

faqs.question: Should I buy a weekly tutoring slot for a Grade 7 student?
faqs.answer: Not before an audit. A standing weekly hour is buying a solution before anyone has described the problem, and in Year 2 the problem is often not what the family assumes. The audit takes two or three sessions and produces a written secured-or-not topic list. That list then tells you which of three different purchases you need: a securing block for unsecured topics, a lower-band supervision slot if the content is fine and self-management is the issue, or a weekly subject slot if the foundations are sound and pacing is the trouble.

faqs.question: How much does Grade 7 MYP tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates for a qualified subject tutor working online run AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150, while Bestimate's published Dubai monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240-600 at the budget end and AED 600-1,200 in the middle. In Year 2 the shape usually costs less than a year-long slot, because an audit plus a securing block is typically six to ten sessions in total. Where the audit shows self-management is the real issue, the AED 33-65 supervision band is the correct fit.

faqs.question: My child is disorganised rather than struggling. Will subject tutoring help?
faqs.answer: No, and buying it is the commonest misdirection of money in this year. The MYP already names the issue: Approaches to Learning skills are assessed explicitly, and in Year 2 the self-management strand — planning a task, meeting several deadlines, organising materials — is what bites. That responds to work on the student's actual assignments and to a checking routine before submission, not to more subject content. It is also cheaper, because supervision sits at the lower end of the Dubai market band rather than the specialist end.

faqs.question: How many Dubai subjects is a Grade 7 student really carrying?
faqs.answer: Eight MYP subject groups plus the UAE mandatory subjects, which is more week than most families count. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements due for implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises at least 25 minutes for any mandatory subject lesson. Adding two tutoring sessions without reviewing the whole week often produces neither.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write up my child's design process journal?
faqs.answer: No, and in the MYP it is the single most damaging thing a tutor or parent can do. Three of the four criteria in some subjects depend on the documented process, so a ghostwritten journal removes exactly the feedback the task existed to produce. What is legitimate is modelling how a journal entry of that type is written using a different example, explaining the criterion descriptor, reading the student's own entry and saying what is missing. The student makes the change. That boundary is the same one that governs the Diploma internal assessment four years later.

faqs.question: Is a holiday block better than term-time sessions in Grade 7?
faqs.answer: For audit and securing work, considerably. With no homework competing, two-hour sessions across a few days can test the Year 2 topic list and secure several items, which term time does not allow. The two or three weeks after a long Dubai school break, before assessments restart, are the most productive period in the whole year and almost nobody uses them. Term-time weekly sessions are better suited to keeping pace with current work; the audit and the securing of back topics belong in a block.

faqs.question: What time does a Grade 7 session realistically start in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It depends on the commute, and it is worth testing a slot for a fortnight before committing to it. From Dubai Hills Estate with schooling inside the community, 4.30pm holds through term. From Arabian Ranches or Mudon along the Al Khail corridor, 5pm or later. From Business Bay with a school in Al Barsha, 6pm, which after a full secondary day is near the limit for a twelve-year-old and makes a weekend session the better option. The UAE week runs Monday to Friday with a Saturday-Sunday weekend, so Friday evening is a school night.

faqs.question: Do you teach the UAE mandatory subjects for Grade 7, and how?
faqs.answer: Yes, from the school's own material and the official curriculum. KHDA states that for the mandatory UAE subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so no parallel scheme is introduced. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, specifies the language of instruction for each stream, and requires that school teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education hold appropriate KHDA approval. Support focuses on written expression and terminology rather than content selection.

faqs.question: How do I know the audit found real gaps rather than manufactured ones?
faqs.answer: Because it is written down and testable by you. The output is a named list of topics marked secure or not secure, each tested by a short unprompted question rather than by whether the student could follow a worked example. You can re-test any item yourself a fortnight later. If a topic was listed as unsecured and the student can now do it cold, the work happened. If the list is vague, or describes attitudes rather than topics, it is not an audit and it should be challenged on exactly that basis.

faqs.question: Does service as action affect my child's Grade 7 subject results?
faqs.answer: Not directly, but it appears on the report and it is a genuine part of the MYP rather than an extracurricular note, which is why a Grade 7 report can contain comments that seem unrelated to subject performance. It rehearses the Creativity, Activity, Service strand that students meet in the Diploma. For a parent the useful discipline is to read the subject criteria separately from the rest: respond to subject criteria with subject work, and respond to service, self-management and organisation comments with habits rather than with tutoring hours.

dubai/grade-7-ib-myp-tutor.closingHeading: Audit the quiet year before it costs you a loud one
dubai/grade-7-ib-myp-tutor.closingBody: Grade 7 is the only MYP year with nothing at the end of it, which is why gaps form here unnoticed and surface two years later wearing a different label. The fix is not a standing weekly slot but a short audit: get the Year 2 topic list from the school, test each item for unprompted recall, and secure the ones that later years assume. That is usually six to ten sessions in total, and it is considerably cheaper than meeting the same gap in DP1. Book a free trial lesson and bring the scheme of work. Sessions are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time; we do not send tutors to UAE homes.

intro.heading: The year a snapshot turns into a label
paragraphs: Grade 8 is where most Dubai MYP schools begin to sort. Mathematics splits into a standard and an extended route. The integrated sciences, which have been one subject on the timetable, start to behave like three in content and in the criterion B work they set. Individuals and societies withdraws the research scaffolding it provided in Year 2. And in a good number of schools, a set list is drawn up, reviewed at intervals, and in practice becomes the student's track for the next two years.

The academic content of Year 3 is a step rather than a leap. In mathematics it is indices and standard form, linear graphs and gradient, simultaneous equations, Pythagoras, and the first real work with probability and data handling. In the sciences it is particle theory applied properly, forces and energy quantitatively, cells and systems in more depth, and chemical change written as equations. In language and literature it is sustained analytical writing rather than paragraph-level analysis.

What makes Year 3 consequential is not the content but the sorting. A student placed in a standard mathematics set in Grade 8 will usually still be there in Grade 10, and will arrive at Diploma options having been told, implicitly, which mathematics route is realistic. That can be entirely correct. It can also be the result of one weak term, a missed topic from Year 2, or a criterion the student never understood the demands of. Those three look identical on a set list and need completely different responses.

So the honest brief for Grade 8 support is narrow and specific: find out whether the set is a fair reflection of capability or an artefact, and if it is an artefact, build the evidence that gets it reviewed. Schools review sets on performance against criteria, not on parental conviction, which means the work has to be the kind that produces criterion scores a head of department can look at.

The Dubai layer continues. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements due for implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and requires that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

One further thing is worth saying to a parent reading a mid-table Year 3 report. The integrated science grade in particular hides more than it shows. A student can be genuinely strong in the biology strand, adequate in physics and lost in chemistry, and still land on a single middling number with four criterion scores behind it. That number tells you nothing about what to do next, and the diagnosis has to happen at strand level and at criterion level before any money is spent. The same applies to a mathematics grade produced partly in a set whose demands differ from the set next door.

On delivery, which matters here because the object is evidence a head of department will actually read. Every IB Gram lesson in the UAE is one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time, so marked criterion work accumulates in one place across a term instead of in a notebook that gets left at school. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE: in-home tutoring is an India-only service, and nothing on this page should be read as offering it in Dubai.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, Year 3
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four lettered criteria per subject, each scored 0-8 and converted to a 1-7 subject grade. programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, Year 3 is also where school populations are most mobile: families arrive and leave mid-year, and new students are placed into sets on the basis of a transfer report from a different system. programmes.description: The final two-year MYP cycle, with increasing independence in criterion B investigations, the Grade 10 Personal Project and its process journal and report, and in some schools an optional external eAssessment route. This is also where the Diploma or A Level decision is made.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. A student who spent Years 3 to 5 in a standard MYP mathematics set is rarely steered towards Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, which is the route most engineering and physics degrees expect. That is the real stake in a Grade 8 set decision.

dubai/grade-8-ib-myp-tutor.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is listed with what Year 3 adds and the criterion where Grade 8 students in Dubai most often lose marks. This is the diagnostic list, not a syllabus summary.

subjects.name: Mathematics (standard route)
subjects.description: Indices and standard form, linear graphs and gradient, Pythagoras, probability and data handling. Criterion A is usually secure; criterion B, investigating patterns, is where a standard-set student is most often capped, because the generalisation step is where the extended work begins.

subjects.name: Mathematics (extended route)
subjects.description: The same core plus simultaneous equations handled algebraically, more demanding manipulation, and investigations requiring a justified general rule. The step is in criterion B and C rather than in topic count, which is why topic coverage alone does not move a student between routes.

subjects.name: Biology strand
subjects.description: Cells, systems and transport in more depth, with quantitative handling of data from experiments. Criterion C, processing and evaluating, is the recurring loss: students describe results instead of evaluating the reliability of their own method.

subjects.name: Chemistry strand
subjects.description: Particle theory applied properly, chemical change expressed as word and symbol equations, and the beginnings of quantitative reasoning about reactions. A Year 3 student who cannot balance an equation confidently carries that into every later chemistry topic.

subjects.name: Physics strand
subjects.description: Forces, energy and motion handled with numbers rather than descriptions, plus graph work where gradient means something physical. The gap is usually unit handling and rearranging a formula, which traces back to Year 2 algebra rather than to physics.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Sustained analytical writing across a whole essay rather than a single paragraph. Criterion B, organising, becomes a real constraint: a student with good insights and no structure scores below one with ordinary insights arranged well.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Scaffolding is withdrawn: students are expected to form a research question, select sources and evaluate them. Criterion B and D carry most of the loss, and a student who always worked from a given question in Year 2 feels this immediately.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Still marked against phase descriptors rather than grade level. By Year 3 the phase a student occupies is usually settled, and it is the main constraint on which Diploma language routes will be open at Grade 10 options.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: A fuller design cycle with more independence in the inquiring and analysing stage. Three of the four criteria depend on documented process, so the journal habit built or missed in Year 2 determines most of the Year 3 mark.

sections.heading: Standard or extended mathematics: what actually separates them
paragraphs: Dubai parents consistently believe the difference between standard and extended MYP mathematics is topic coverage, and therefore that a tutor covering extra topics will move a child between them. That is not what separates the routes. The routes differ in what criterion B and criterion C demand, which is a different kind of work rather than more of the same.

Both routes cover indices and standard form, linear graphs and gradient, Pythagoras, and probability and data handling in Year 3. The extended route handles simultaneous equations algebraically rather than graphically, carries more demanding manipulation, and above all expects an investigation to end in a justified general rule rather than a described pattern. That last point is the actual boundary: a standard-route student says 'the numbers go up by three each time'; an extended-route student says 'the nth term is 3n minus 1, because each step adds one more group of three', and then shows it.

The practical consequence for a student in the wrong route is that covering more content will not move them. Producing an investigation with a justified generalisation will. That is why Grade 8 support aimed at a set review should spend its time on generalisation and algebraic method rather than on racing ahead through topics the student will meet anyway.

The second practical consequence is a diagnostic one. Where a student cannot reach a justified general rule because their algebra is unsecured — they cannot reliably manipulate an expression — the honest answer is that the Year 2 algebra has to be secured first, and a set review this term is unrealistic. Saying that is more useful than six weeks of investigation practice on a foundation that will not hold it.

sections.heading: Which Grade 8 decisions are reversible, and which are not
paragraphs: Families treat all Year 3 decisions as provisional because nothing formal is signed. In practice they vary a great deal in how reversible they are, and it is worth knowing which is which before deciding where to spend effort.

Mathematics set placement is reversible, but the window narrows every year. Moving up in Grade 8 means making up pace and a handful of method differences. Moving up in Grade 10 means making up two years of genuinely divergent work, and most schools will decline it on those grounds rather than on ability. If a set is going to be challenged, Year 3 is the cheap time.

Language acquisition phase placement is close to fixed by Year 3. Phases are set on prior learning and movement typically happens around Year 2, so a Grade 8 student in a low phase will usually finish the MYP there. That constrains which Diploma language routes are realistic, and it is a conversation to have with the school rather than a tutoring purchase.

The KHDA Arabic stream is effectively fixed, because it follows from whether the student is recorded as an Arab or non-Arab learner and KHDA requires the two groups to be taught separately. Science strand strengths are entirely reversible, because the sciences do not formally split until later and a weak strand in Year 3 is simply a weak strand. And the Diploma or A Level direction remains fully open in Grade 8, which is worth saying to anxious parents: nothing has been decided about Grade 11 yet.

sections.heading: The sciences in Year 3: one grade, three different problems
paragraphs: In most Dubai MYP schools the sciences appear on the report as one subject with four criterion scores, while in substance Year 3 is teaching three distinguishable disciplines. A student can be genuinely strong in biology, adequate in physics and lost in chemistry and still receive a middling integrated grade, which tells a parent nothing about what to do.

The chemistry problem in Year 3 is almost always equations. Particle theory is handled conceptually and most students cope; writing chemical change as a word equation and then a balanced symbol equation is a procedural skill that either gets secured or does not. A student who cannot balance confidently at thirteen carries that into every later chemistry topic, and no amount of revising reaction types compensates.

The physics problem is usually not physics. Forces, energy and motion in Year 3 are handled with numbers, which means unit conversion and rearranging a formula. A student who struggles here is normally a student whose Year 2 algebra is unsecured, and the correct intervention is algebra rather than more physics content. This is the most common misdiagnosis on a Grade 8 report.

The biology problem is criterion C. The content is accessible and students generally understand it; the marks go on processing and evaluating, where they are asked to present data properly and then evaluate the reliability of their own method. Students describe what happened instead. Three taught sentence patterns — what limited the result, why it mattered, what would improve it — move the criterion within a term, and the same move pays again in the Diploma internal assessment four years later.

sections.heading: How to get a set reviewed, and what evidence a school will accept
paragraphs: This is the practical heart of a Grade 8 page, because it is the thing families most often attempt and most often attempt badly. Schools review sets on performance evidence against criteria. They do not review them on a parent's assessment of their child, on a tutor's letter, or on effort. Understanding that converts a frustrating conversation into a workable plan.

Start by asking the school three questions in writing: how often sets are reviewed, what evidence the review uses, and whether movement up can happen mid-year or only at year end. The answers vary considerably between Dubai schools, and they determine the timeline. There is no point building evidence for a review that happens in June if the decision for the following year is taken in April.

Then build the right evidence. In mathematics that means completed investigations in which the student states and justifies a general rule, and criterion C work with correct notation, because those are the criteria that distinguish the routes. In the sciences it means criterion B and C work: a designed investigation with controlled variables and an honest evaluation. Topic tests matter less than families assume, because they mostly test criterion A, which is rarely where the set boundary sits.

Finally, be prepared for the honest answer. Sometimes the set is a fair reflection, the student is working at their genuine current ceiling, and the right advice is to do well in the set they are in rather than to spend a year and a tutoring budget on a move that will not happen. A provider who tells you this is more use than one who takes the booking. And a student who finishes Year 3 strong in the standard route has lost nothing: nothing about the Diploma has been decided in Grade 8.

sections.heading: What Grade 8 support costs in Dubai, and the cheaper alternative
paragraphs: Market rates for a qualified subject tutor working online in Dubai run AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Bestimate's published Dubai 2026 monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are market figures, attributed, rather than our price list.

A set-review campaign in Grade 8 is a defined block rather than a standing slot: typically eight to twelve sessions aimed at producing specific criterion evidence before a known review date. Bought that way it is a predictable cost with a date attached. Bought as an open-ended weekly hour 'to help with maths' it drifts into a year of expenditure with no decision point, which is the pattern most Dubai families fall into.

There is a cheaper alternative that families rarely consider, and it is often the correct one. Where the real obstacle is an unsecured Year 2 topic — algebraic manipulation above all — the intervention is a short securing block on that topic rather than a year of Year 3 support. Four sessions on rearranging expressions can recover more Year 3 marks than twenty sessions on Year 3 content, because the Year 3 content assumes the Year 2 skill.

The longer arithmetic favours acting now. A set challenged in Grade 8 costs a defined block. The same conversation attempted in Grade 10 is usually declined, and the consequence shows up as a Diploma mathematics route that was never genuinely on the table. One piece of budget context: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, which makes tuition the variable line and its timing the decision that matters.

sections.heading: Online or in the room for a thirteen-year-old
paragraphs: A reasonable objection, and worth a straight answer. For a thirteen-year-old a person in the room has advantages: attention is easier to sustain, a glance catches confusion a camera misses, and some students admit to not understanding more readily face to face. Those are real and this page is not going to pretend otherwise.

Set against them, the Grade 8 requirement is unusually specific. What this student needs is somebody who can mark an investigation against the extended-route criterion B descriptor and say precisely what is missing from the generalisation. The pool of people who can do that in a given Dubai community at the hour the child is home is far narrower than the pool available over video, and the in-home travel premium — Bestimate puts visits at AED 180-350 against AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor — buys the commute rather than that expertise.

There is also a reliability argument that matters more in Year 3 than earlier. A set-review campaign depends on regular, dated output across eight to twelve sessions before a fixed review date. A video slot survives traffic, activities, family travel and a change of address. An in-home arrangement typically loses two or three sessions to those over the same period, which in a timed campaign is the difference between having the evidence and not.

IB Gram's position is fixed rather than preferential: all UAE tuition is one-to-one, live over video, and we do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we offer only in India. If physical presence is your requirement for a thirteen-year-old, we are not the right provider and will say so plainly rather than arguing you out of it.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when the work is being used as evidence
paragraphs: This matters acutely in Grade 8 and for a reason specific to the year. If a student's investigations are being produced partly to support a set review, the temptation to improve them beyond what the student actually did is at its strongest, and the result would be worse than useless: a student moved into a route they cannot sustain on the basis of work they did not produce.

What a tutor may do is substantial. They may teach the content, explain the criterion descriptors and what the band above requires, model how an investigation of that type is structured using a different problem, discuss and challenge the student's reasoning, read the student's own draft and say what is missing against the criterion, and teach notation and referencing conventions.

What a tutor may not do is write any part of the submitted work, dictate the general rule or its justification, produce the investigation, or correct a draft into a finished state. For a set-review campaign specifically, the test is whether the student could sit with the head of department and explain every line of the investigation unaided. If not, the evidence is false and the review it produces is a disservice.

The same principle governs materials. We do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; we reference them and link the official source. At Diploma level this road ends with operators selling completed Internal Assessments, which is an IB malpractice trigger where the consequence falls on the student. Grade 8 is a good place to establish that the student's own work is the thing being judged.
bullets: Allowed: descriptors explained, structure modelled on a different problem, drafts read
Not allowed: writing, dictating the generalisation, producing the investigation
For a set review the test is whether the student could explain it unaided to a head of department

sections.heading: The KHDA layer and the Grade 8 timetable
paragraphs: A Grade 8 student in a Dubai private school carries eight MYP subject groups plus the UAE mandatory subjects, and in Year 3 the academic load inside those subjects has also grown. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements due for implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year.

KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. It requires Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic as the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies. It also requires that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

On instructional time, KHDA calculates mandatory-subject time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that any mandatory subject lesson should be at least 25 minutes. The practical point for a Year 3 family planning a set-review campaign is that the week is already full, and adding two sessions without removing anything usually produces worse work rather than more of it.

On content, KHDA states that for the mandatory UAE subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Support for Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies therefore works from the school's own material and the official curriculum rather than from a parallel scheme, and a provider offering you their own Arabic programme for these subjects is offering something that rule does not permit.

process.title: Ask the school how sets are reviewed
process.description: Three questions in writing: how often, on what evidence, and whether movement up can happen mid-year or only at year end. The answers set the timeline for everything else, and there is no sense building evidence for a June review if next year's decision is taken in April.

process.title: Diagnose whether the set is a ceiling or an artefact
process.description: The trial session and one follow-up establish which. A student capped at the generalisation step with secure algebra is an artefact; a student who cannot manipulate an expression is not ready for a set move this term, and saying so is more useful than six weeks of practice on a weak foundation.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the matched tutor
process.description: One session, no charge, with a tutor who teaches the extended route and knows its descriptors. By the end the tutor should be able to say which criterion caps the student and what the band above requires. If the match is wrong you say so, before any payment.

process.title: Build the evidence the review will actually use
process.description: Completed investigations with justified general rules, criterion C work with correct notation, and in the sciences a designed investigation with controlled variables and an honest evaluation. Topic tests matter less, because they mostly demonstrate criterion A, which is rarely where the set boundary sits.

process.title: Fix the prior-year gap if that is the real obstacle
process.description: Four to six sessions on Year 2 algebraic manipulation often recovers more Year 3 marks than twenty sessions of Year 3 content, because Year 3 assumes the Year 2 skill. This is cheaper and faster than a set campaign, and sometimes it is the whole answer.

process.title: Stop at the review, whichever way it goes
process.description: The block ends at the review date. If the move happens, support shifts to holding the new route. If it does not, the right advice is usually to do well in the current set rather than repeat the campaign — nothing about the Diploma has been decided in Grade 8.

whyPoints.title: We name what actually separates the routes
whyPoints.description: Not topic coverage. Standard and extended MYP mathematics differ in whether an investigation must end in a justified general rule, which means covering extra content will not move a student between them. Working on the right thing is most of the value here.

whyPoints.title: We will tell you when the set is fair
whyPoints.description: Sometimes a student is working at their genuine current ceiling and a year of effort will not produce a move. Saying so is more useful than taking the booking, and a student who finishes Year 3 strong in the standard route has lost nothing — Grade 11 is still open.

whyPoints.title: Evidence of the kind a school will accept
whyPoints.description: Reviews run on criterion performance, not on parental conviction or a tutor's letter. The work produced is the type a head of department looks at: investigations with justified generalisations, criterion C work with correct notation, designed experiments with honest evaluations.

whyPoints.title: Prior-year gaps checked before Year 3 content is sold
whyPoints.description: The most common misdiagnosis on a Grade 8 report is a physics problem that is actually unsecured Year 2 algebra. Four sessions on manipulation can recover more marks than twenty on Year 3 content, and it is cheaper, so we look there first.

whyPoints.title: Honesty, especially when work is evidence
whyPoints.description: A set move built on work the student did not produce puts them in a route they cannot sustain. The test is whether the student could explain every line to a head of department unaided, and that standard is stated here rather than buried in terms.

whyPoints.description: No home visits anywhere in the UAE, no KHDA approval or regulator accreditation, no UAE office. Every AED figure here is attributed to whoever published it, and where we cannot match a subject at a workable hour we say so rather than substituting.

faqs.question: What is the difference between standard and extended MYP mathematics in Grade 8?
faqs.answer: Not topic coverage, which is what most families assume. Both routes cover indices and standard form, linear graphs, Pythagoras and probability in Year 3. The extended route handles simultaneous equations algebraically, carries harder manipulation, and crucially expects an investigation to end in a justified general rule rather than a described pattern. A standard-route answer says the numbers increase by three each time; an extended-route answer states the nth term and shows why it holds. That is the real boundary, which is why covering extra content does not move a student between routes.

faqs.question: Can my child move up a maths set in Grade 8, and how?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and Year 3 is the cheap time to try, because by Grade 10 the two routes have genuinely diverged in content and most schools decline moves on those grounds. The method is evidence: completed investigations in which the student states and justifies a general rule, plus criterion C work with correct notation. Ask the school in writing how often sets are reviewed, what evidence the review uses, and whether movement can happen mid-year. Topic tests matter less than families expect, because they mainly demonstrate criterion A.

faqs.question: My child has one science grade but is only weak in chemistry. What now?
faqs.answer: Target the strand, not the subject. In most Dubai MYP schools the sciences report as one grade with four criterion scores while Year 3 teaches three distinguishable disciplines, so a middling integrated grade can conceal one weak strand entirely. In Year 3 chemistry the issue is almost always equations: writing chemical change as a word equation and then a balanced symbol equation is a procedural skill that either gets secured or does not. Four to eight sessions on exactly that is usually more effective than general science support.

faqs.question: Why is my child struggling with Grade 8 physics when they understand the concepts?
faqs.answer: Because Year 3 physics is quantitative and the obstacle is usually algebra rather than physics. Forces, energy and motion are handled with numbers, which means unit conversion and rearranging a formula. A student who cannot reliably rearrange an expression — a Year 2 skill — will struggle with every numerical physics question regardless of how well they understand the concept. This is the most common misdiagnosis on a Grade 8 report, and the correct intervention is a short securing block on manipulation rather than more physics content.

faqs.question: Which Grade 8 decisions can still be changed later?
faqs.answer: Science strand weaknesses are fully reversible at any point, and the Diploma or A Level direction remains entirely open — nothing about Grade 11 is decided in Year 3. Mathematics set placement is reversible now and rarely by Grade 10, because the routes diverge in content. Language acquisition phase placement is close to fixed by Year 3, since movement typically happens around Year 2. The KHDA Arabic stream is effectively fixed, because it follows from the Arab or non-Arab distinction and KHDA requires the two groups to be taught separately.

faqs.question: How long does a set-review campaign take in Grade 8?
faqs.answer: Typically eight to twelve sessions aimed at a known review date, which is why the first step is asking the school when the review happens. Bought that way it is a defined cost with an end point. Bought as an open-ended weekly hour to help with maths generally, it drifts into a year of expenditure with no decision moment, which is the pattern most families fall into. If the diagnosis shows a prior-year algebra gap is the real obstacle, a four to six session securing block comes first and the campaign is deferred.

faqs.question: What if the set is actually a fair reflection of my child's ability?
faqs.answer: Then the honest advice is to do well in the set they are in rather than spend a year and a budget on a move that will not happen. A student who finishes Year 3 strong in the standard route has lost nothing concrete: the Diploma or A Level direction is decided at Grade 10 options on Years 4 and 5 performance, not in Grade 8. What is worth doing in that case is securing criterion B and C habits, which are the cheapest things to change at thirteen and the ones every later year assumes.

faqs.question: Does a Grade 8 maths set affect which IB Diploma maths course is available?
faqs.answer: Indirectly but significantly, which is the real stake. The Diploma offers Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each at Higher or Standard Level, and Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is what most engineering and physics degree routes expect. A student who spends Years 3 to 5 in a standard MYP mathematics set is rarely steered towards it at options. That is not a rule anywhere, but it is the pattern, and it is why a set that is an artefact rather than a ceiling is worth challenging in Year 3.

faqs.question: How much does Grade 8 MYP tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates for a qualified subject tutor working online run AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Bestimate's published Dubai monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240-600 at the budget end and AED 600-1,200 in the middle. A set-review block of eight to twelve sessions is the common Grade 8 purchase. Where organisation rather than content is the issue, the AED 33-65 supervision band — Tutopiya from AED 33-52, EdFlik from AED 45-65 — is the correct and cheaper fit.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring suitable for a thirteen-year-old working towards a set review?
faqs.answer: For this job, yes, with the honest caveat that a person in the room has real advantages for a younger student. The Grade 8 requirement is specific: someone who can mark an investigation against the extended-route criterion B descriptor and say what the generalisation is missing. That pool is far narrower in a single Dubai community at a fixed hour than online. A review campaign also needs regular dated output across eight to twelve sessions, and a video slot survives traffic, activities and travel that typically cost an in-home arrangement two or three sessions.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help write the investigation we are using as set-review evidence?
faqs.answer: No, and here the boundary matters more than usual. A set move built on work the student did not produce places them in a route they cannot sustain, which is worse than no move at all. A tutor may explain the criterion descriptor, model how an investigation of that type is structured using a different problem, challenge the student's reasoning, read their own draft and say what is missing, and teach notation. The test is whether the student could sit with the head of department and explain every line unaided.

faqs.question: What does criterion C ask for in Grade 8 sciences?
faqs.answer: Processing and evaluating: presenting data properly and then evaluating the reliability of the student's own method. This is where Year 3 biology marks are most consistently lost, because students describe what happened rather than evaluating it. Three taught sentence patterns usually move the criterion within a term — what limited the result, why that mattered, and what would improve it. The same move pays again four years later in the Diploma internal assessment, where the criteria have a similar shape and are worth roughly a quarter of the subject grade.

faqs.question: How does research work change between Grade 7 and Grade 8?
faqs.answer: The scaffolding is withdrawn. In Year 2 individuals and societies gives students a research question and often a source set; in Year 3 they are expected to form the question, select sources and evaluate them, with criterion B and D carrying most of the loss. A student who always worked from a given question feels this immediately and often reads it as a drop in ability. It is not — it is a new skill, and forming a workable question from a broad topic is the single hardest part of it to learn late.

faqs.question: Do you teach Arabic and Islamic Education for a Grade 8 student in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, from the school's own material and the official curriculum. KHDA states that for the mandatory UAE subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so no parallel scheme is introduced. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, specifies Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for first-language Arabic and for Islamic Education for Arab students, and requires that school teachers of these subjects hold appropriate KHDA approval — a reasonable question to ask the school.

faqs.question: My child joined a Dubai school mid-year and was put in a lower set. Is that permanent?
faqs.answer: It should not be, and it is worth raising early. Transfer placements are often made on a report from a different system in the first week of term, which is a weak basis for a track that tends to persist to Grade 10. Ask the school in writing how and when the placement will be reviewed and what evidence the review will use. Then build that evidence: investigations with justified general rules in mathematics, designed and evaluated experiments in the sciences. A placement made from a transcript is exactly the case where a review is most justified.

faqs.question: Should we add two sessions a week in Grade 8 to make up ground?
faqs.answer: Usually not without removing something. A Year 3 week already carries eight MYP subject groups plus the UAE mandatory subjects, and KHDA calculates mandatory-subject time on a 40-minute lesson unit with a 25-minute advised minimum per lesson. Adding two sessions to a full week tends to produce worse work rather than more of it. The better pattern is one weekly session during term plus a holiday block, since the weeks after a long break — with no homework competing — are the most productive period available.

dubai/grade-8-ib-myp-tutor.closingHeading: Find out whether the set is a ceiling or an artefact
dubai/grade-8-ib-myp-tutor.closingBody: Grade 8 is the year a snapshot becomes a label, and almost everything worth doing follows from one question: is the set a fair reflection of capability, or the residue of a weak term, a mid-year transfer or an unsecured Year 2 skill? Ask the school how sets are reviewed and on what evidence, then build that evidence — investigations with justified general rules, criterion C work with correct notation. Book a free trial lesson and bring two pieces of marked work. If the set turns out to be fair, we will tell you, because nothing about Grade 11 has been decided yet. Sessions are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time; we do not send tutors to UAE homes.

dubai/grade-9-ib-myp-tutor.tutorsIntro: Grade 9 tutors plan across two years rather than one term, because Year 4 and Year 5 are a single assessment cycle. That changes what the first sessions are for: establishing independence in investigative work rather than patching last week's test.

intro.heading: Year 4 is the first half of something, not a year on its own
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme treats Grades 9 and 10 as a single final cycle, and Dubai schools plan them that way even when the reporting looks year by year. What that means in practice is that Year 4 is where several long processes start and none of them finish. The scaffolding on criterion B investigations is withdrawn for good. Research questions have to be formed rather than received. The Personal Project is introduced, often lightly, with a deadline that lands a year later. And the school starts gathering the evidence it will use when it advises on the Diploma or an A Level route.

That makes Year 4 the year families most often misread in the opposite direction from Grade 7. In Grade 7 nothing happens and nobody looks. In Grade 9 quite a lot happens, none of it has an immediate consequence, and so a family can reasonably conclude there is nothing to do yet. The reports look like Year 3 reports. The options evening is a year away. The Personal Project has a title and no urgency. Meanwhile the student is being formed into the candidate who will walk into that options evening.

The content in Year 4 is a genuine step up. Mathematics moves into quadratics, algebraic fractions, trigonometry in right-angled triangles and more demanding graph work, with the extended route expecting algebraic method rather than numerical trial throughout. The sciences carry quantitative reasoning in all three strands with real calculation and unit discipline. Language and literature expects sustained analytical essays with a defensible structure. Individuals and societies expects a research question, a source selection and an evaluation, all from the student.

What a tutor can usefully do here is narrower than in earlier years and more valuable. It is to build independence in the specific things the Diploma will later demand: forming a question, designing an investigation, evaluating one's own work honestly, and writing an argument that holds its shape over several pages. Those four are the whole of the Diploma internal assessment skill set in miniature, they are assessed in Year 4 with low stakes, and they are considerably cheaper to learn now than in DP1.

The Dubai context continues to apply. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements due for implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ.

How this is delivered follows from what Year 4 is for. Independence is poorly served by an adult sitting at the same table, so all IB Gram tuition in the UAE is one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time: the student forms the research question and drafts the investigation, and the tutor reads it back and questions it. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, Dubai included; home visiting exists only within our India service.

dubai/grade-9-ib-myp-tutor.programmesIntro: Grade 9 sits at the start of the last MYP cycle, with two destinations a year away. Understanding what each one assesses is how a family reads Year 4 performance correctly.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, Year 4
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four lettered criteria per subject, each scored 0-8 and converted to a 1-7 grade. Year 4 withdraws investigative scaffolding, raises quantitative demand across mathematics and the sciences, and introduces the Personal Project process that concludes in Year 5. Approaches to Learning skills remain assessed alongside subject content.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, Year 4 is also when some schools begin running MYP and an IGCSE track in parallel, so two students in the same year group can be on genuinely different assessment paths. A family should establish in writing which path their child is on, because the Year 5 destination and the options conversation differ substantially between them.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, Year 5
programmes.description: The second half of the final cycle, carrying the completed Personal Project with its process journal and report, the most demanding criterion B work in the programme, and in some schools an optional external eAssessment route. It ends with the options decision for the Diploma, A Level or another post-16 route.
programmes.countryNote: Everything started in Year 4 lands here. A student who learned to form a research question in Year 4 writes a workable Personal Project question in Year 5; one who did not spends a term circling. Dubai schools set their own Personal Project checkpoints, which means the real deadlines are internal and are rarely communicated to parents until they are close.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject carries an internal assessment marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB, with external examinations in the May session for UAE schools and grades from 1 to 7 plus up to three bonus points.
programmes.countryNote: One of the two destinations. The Diploma rewards exactly what Year 4 is rehearsing: an independently formed question, a designed investigation, honest evaluation and sustained argument. A student who is comfortable with those four by the end of Year 4 is a strong Diploma candidate regardless of their current grades, which is a more useful predictor than a report average.

programmes.name: IGCSE and the A Level route
programmes.description: Single-subject qualifications taken at 16, assessed largely or wholly by external written examination, followed by three or four A Levels with deeper specialisation and less breadth. Cambridge International offers Core and Extended tiers in many IGCSE subjects; UAE candidates sit the June and November series.
programmes.countryNote: The other destination, and widely available in Dubai because British-curriculum schools dominate the market by enrolment. The honest comparison is about assessment style rather than difficulty: A Levels reward depth in three subjects assessed mostly by examination, the Diploma rewards breadth across six plus coursework in every one. Year 4 performance in criterion B is a reasonable guide to which suits a student.

dubai/grade-9-ib-myp-tutor.subjectsIntro: Each subject below names what Year 4 adds and the specific independence the student is now expected to show. The pattern across all of them is the same: scaffolding removed, judgement required.

subjects.name: Mathematics (extended route)
subjects.description: Quadratics, algebraic fractions, right-angled trigonometry and more demanding graph work, with algebraic method expected throughout rather than numerical trial. Criterion B now requires a general rule, justified, from an investigation the student has set up themselves.

subjects.name: Mathematics (standard route)
subjects.description: The same core topics at a different depth, with investigations expecting a described and applied pattern. The honest question in Year 4 is whether the route still fits, because by Year 5 a move between them is considerably harder to make.

subjects.name: Biology strand
subjects.description: Genetics, ecology and physiology with quantitative data handling, plus criterion B investigations designed by the student. The marks sit in evaluating one's own method honestly, which is the same skill the Diploma internal assessment weights most heavily.

subjects.name: Chemistry strand
subjects.description: Quantitative chemistry arrives properly: moles in outline, reacting masses, rates and energy change. Students who never secured balancing in Year 3 hit a wall here, because every calculation depends on a correct equation first.

subjects.name: Physics strand
subjects.description: Waves, electricity and energy handled with real calculation and unit discipline, plus graph work where gradient and area both carry physical meaning. Formula rearrangement must be automatic by now rather than something worked out each time.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Sustained analytical essays rather than paragraph responses. Criterion B, organising, becomes decisive: an essay that holds a line of argument across several pages scores above one with better individual observations arranged poorly.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: A research question, a source selection and an evaluation, all produced by the student. This is the closest thing in the MYP to Extended Essay practice, and a student who can do it in Year 4 has a substantial advantage two years later.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: A full design cycle with the client or user identified by the student, documented through all four criteria. The specification-writing step is where most Year 4 marks are lost, because a vague specification cannot be evaluated against.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Still assessed against phase descriptors. By Year 4 the phase is settled for most students and is the main determinant of which Diploma language routes are realistic, which makes it worth a direct question to the school this year rather than next.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies
subjects.description: Required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and KHDA-specified languages of instruction. Support works from the school's own material, since additional content requires prior Ministry of Education permission.

sections.heading: What Year 4 starts and Year 5 finishes
paragraphs: Treating Grade 9 as a standalone year is the central planning error in the MYP, because the programme does not treat it that way and neither do Dubai schools. The final cycle runs across two years, and several of the things that determine a Year 5 outcome are set in motion now, quietly, with no immediate consequence attached.

The clearest example is the Personal Project. It is introduced in Year 4 in most Dubai schools, with a goal chosen and a process journal begun, and it is completed and submitted in Year 5 against checkpoints the school sets internally. A student who chooses a viable goal and builds a journal habit in Year 4 writes a decent project in Year 5 without drama. A student who chooses an unviable goal — too broad, dependent on resources they will not have, or not actually interesting to them — spends a term of Year 5 discovering that and starting again.

The second is investigative independence. Scaffolding on criterion B is withdrawn in Year 4 and is not reinstated. Year 5 assumes the student can form a question and design an investigation, because Year 4 was where they learned to. The student who never learned faces the hardest criterion B work in the programme without the underlying skill, and that reads on a report as a drop in ability rather than as a missing habit.

The third is the evidence base for the options conversation. Schools advise on post-16 routes using performance across the final cycle, and much of what they look at is generated in Year 4. That means Year 4 criterion scores are not a dress rehearsal; they are part of the record the advice will rest on. None of this requires panic. It requires knowing that Year 4 work has downstream weight and spending effort accordingly.

sections.heading: The Personal Project clock, which is already running
paragraphs: The Personal Project is the MYP's culminating piece: a self-directed project with a goal the student sets, a process journal kept throughout, and a report assessed against lettered criteria. It is submitted in Year 5. It is chosen and begun in Year 4, and the single most useful thing a Grade 9 family can do is treat the goal choice as a decision rather than as an enthusiasm.

A viable goal has four properties. It is narrow enough to be finished, it depends only on resources the student will actually have, it produces something that can be evaluated against a specification the student writes, and it holds the student's interest for a year. Most unviable goals fail the first or second test: a project to build something requiring equipment or permissions that will not materialise, or a goal so broad that no specification can be written for it.

The process journal is where the marks sit and where Year 4 habits matter most. The criteria reward evidence of planning, decision-making and reflection across the whole project, not a tidy account written afterwards. A student who keeps a running journal from Year 4 has that evidence. A student who reconstructs it the week before submission has an artefact that reads exactly as what it is, and loses marks across more than one criterion.

There is a hard boundary worth stating here because this is the project most exposed to it. A tutor may explain each criterion letter by letter with the marks attached, test whether a goal is viable, ask the questions that make a specification sharper, read the student's own journal entries and report drafts and say what is missing, and teach referencing. A tutor may not write the report, produce the journal, design the project or correct a draft into a finished state. The test is whether the student could explain every decision in the project unaided.
bullets: A viable goal is narrow, resourced, specifiable and genuinely interesting to the student

sections.heading: The Diploma or A Level fork, judged on assessment style
paragraphs: A year out from options, Dubai families start asking which route is better. The question has no general answer and a very good specific one, because the two routes assess differently and a student's Year 4 criterion profile is a reasonable guide to which suits them.

The Diploma asks for breadth: six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject carries an internal assessment marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB. It rewards a student who can carry many things at once, who writes well across subjects, and who can run an independent piece of work to a deadline. UAE schools sit the May session.

The A Level route asks for depth: three or four subjects after IGCSE, assessed largely or wholly by external written examination, with far less coursework and no compulsory core. It rewards a student who is strong in a narrow band of subjects, who performs well under examination conditions, and who would find six subjects plus coursework in all of them a dilution rather than an opportunity. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in June and November for UAE candidates; the February/March series is offered to India only.

The useful Year 4 read is this. A student whose criterion A scores are strong and whose criterion B and C scores lag is often better served by an examination-led route, because criterion A is closest to what examinations test. A student whose criterion B and C scores are strong — who forms good questions, designs sound investigations and evaluates honestly — is a natural Diploma candidate even if their topic-test performance is unremarkable, because that is what the internal assessments and the Extended Essay reward. Neither profile is better. They are different, and the match matters more than the reputation of either qualification.

sections.heading: Where Year 4 marks actually go in each subject group
paragraphs: The Year 4 content step is real, but marks are lost in patterned, nameable places rather than across the board. Knowing where means a term of work can target something specific instead of revising generally.

In mathematics the two losses are quadratics handled by trial rather than method, and criterion B investigations that describe a pattern without justifying a general rule. The second matters more, because it is the criterion that separates the routes and the one the Diploma will build on. Algebraic fractions are the quiet third: students who manage them in isolation and fail when they appear inside a larger problem, which traces to incomplete fluency rather than to the topic.

In the sciences each strand loses marks differently. Chemistry loses them on calculations that depend on a correct balanced equation written first, so a Year 3 gap becomes a Year 4 ceiling. Physics loses them on unit discipline and on reading meaning from a gradient or an area under a graph. Biology loses them on criterion C: students describe their results and do not evaluate the reliability of their own method, which is also the lowest-scoring criterion for most students in the Diploma internal assessment.

In language and literature the loss is structural. Criterion B, organising, becomes decisive once essays are sustained rather than paragraph-length, and a student with sharper individual observations arranged badly scores below one with ordinary observations held in a clear line of argument. In individuals and societies the loss is at the start: a research question that is too broad or not answerable from available sources makes every subsequent criterion harder to score, and nothing downstream can repair it.

sections.heading: What Year 4 support costs in Dubai, planned over two years
paragraphs: Market rates for a qualified subject tutor working online in Dubai run AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Bestimate's published Dubai 2026 monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. These are market figures with their sources named rather than a price list of ours.

The Year 4 planning question is different from earlier years because the cycle is two years long. A family deciding to support one subject should decide for the cycle rather than the term, which makes the total visible and the decision honest. At the mid-band that is a meaningful commitment, and it is better faced in September of Year 4 than discovered in instalments.

Against that, three places where Year 4 money works unusually hard. Investigative independence work is cheap to buy now and expensive later, because the same skill bought in DP1 sits in the exam-year band. Personal Project process coaching is a handful of sessions in Year 4 that prevents a term of Year 5 being lost to a restart. And a securing block on a Year 3 gap — chemistry balancing, formula rearrangement — is four to six sessions that raise the ceiling on a whole subject.

One context figure for a Dubai budget: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. With the fee held flat, tuition is the variable line, and in Year 4 the question is less whether to spend than which of the four purchases above to spend on first.
