sections.heading: Online or in the room at fourteen
paragraphs: At fourteen the argument for a person in the room is weaker than it was at eleven and has not disappeared. Attention is easier to hold face to face, and a student who is reluctant to say they do not understand may say it more readily to someone sitting beside them. Those are genuine and this page will not pretend otherwise.

The Year 4 requirement, though, is unusually specific. What this student needs is someone who will refuse to supply the answer: a tutor who makes them form the research question, defend the investigation design and evaluate their own result. That is a teaching disposition rather than a location, and the pool of people who hold it for MYP criterion work, in one Dubai community, at the hour the student is home, is narrow. Over video it is not.

There is a cost point too. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor. The gap buys the commute. In Year 4, where a family may be funding a two-year commitment in one subject, that difference compounds into real money for no additional expertise.

IB Gram's position is fixed rather than a preference. All UAE tuition is one-to-one, live over video, on Gulf Standard Time, and we do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we offer only in India. If physical presence in Dubai is what you want for a fourteen-year-old, we are not the right provider and will say so plainly.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in the year independence is the point
paragraphs: Year 4 is the year the programme starts asking students to work alone, which makes it the year adult help is most tempting and most damaging. The MYP's academic honesty rules apply throughout, and the Personal Project in particular is an artefact that cannot be meaningfully ghostwritten without defeating its entire purpose.

What a tutor may do is substantial, and in Year 4 it is mostly asking rather than telling. They may teach the content, explain criterion descriptors letter by letter with the marks attached, model how a piece of that type is structured using a different problem, interrogate the student's research question, challenge an investigation design, read the student's own draft or journal entry and say what is missing against the criterion, and teach notation and referencing.

What a tutor may not do is write any part of a submitted piece, dictate the general rule or the evaluation, design the investigation, produce the process journal, or correct a draft into a finished state. The practical test for everything in Year 4 is whether the student could explain every decision in the work unaided, to their teacher, without notes. If not, the work is not theirs and the feedback that would have helped has been removed.

On materials: we do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. We reference them and link the official source. At Diploma level this road ends with operators selling completed Internal Assessments, which is an IB malpractice trigger where the consequence falls on the student, not the seller. Establishing the boundary at fourteen is considerably easier than defending it at eighteen.
bullets: Allowed: descriptors explained, questions interrogated, designs challenged, drafts read
Not allowed: writing, dictating an evaluation, designing the investigation, producing the journal

sections.heading: The Dubai calendar and the KHDA layer in Year 4
paragraphs: A Grade 9 student in a Dubai private school is carrying eight MYP subject groups with a heavier load inside each, plus the UAE mandatory subjects. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements due for implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year.

KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. It specifies Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic as the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies. It also requires that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval.

On time, KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that any mandatory subject lesson should be at least 25 minutes. On content, the use of any different or additional content for these subjects without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited, which is why support for them works from the school's own material.

On scheduling, the UAE working week runs Monday to Friday with a Saturday-Sunday weekend, so Friday evening is a school night. During Ramadan the school day shortens and the productive window moves, for many families to after Iftar; in Year 4 the better response is usually to reduce frequency for the month rather than push a loaded student later. The weeks after a long break, before assessments restart, are the best window in the year for independence work, because it needs time rather than urgency.

process.title: Establish which track your child is actually on
process.description: Some Dubai schools run MYP and an IGCSE track in parallel through the middle years, so two students in the same Grade 9 can be on different assessment paths. Ask in writing which one your child is in and what the Year 5 destination is, because the planning differs substantially.

process.title: Read criterion B and C before criterion A
process.description: Topic-test performance mostly shows criterion A, which is the least diagnostic in Year 4. Criterion B and C scores tell you whether the student can form a question, design an investigation and evaluate honestly — the four skills the next four years will actually assess.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the matched tutor
process.description: One session, no charge. By the end of it the tutor should be able to say which of the four independence skills is weakest and what the next step on it is. If the match is wrong, you say so and we match again before any payment is made.

process.title: Test the Personal Project goal early
process.description: Before time is invested in it. A viable goal is narrow enough to finish, resourced from what the student will actually have, specifiable, and genuinely interesting for a year. Most unviable goals fail the first two tests, and discovering that in Year 4 saves a term of Year 5.

process.title: Plan the subject slot for the cycle, not the term
process.description: Grades 9 and 10 are one assessment cycle. Where a subject needs ongoing support, decide for two years with a review at the end of Year 4. That makes the real cost visible in September rather than discovered in instalments, which is the honest way to make the decision.

process.title: Do the options work in the second half of Year 4
process.description: Two or three sessions comparing what the Diploma and the A Level route actually assess, read against the student's own criterion evidence. Route constraints in mathematics and languages are still movable this year and largely are not next, which is why the timing matters.

whyPoints.title: We plan across the cycle, not the term
whyPoints.description: Grades 9 and 10 are a single MYP assessment cycle and almost every Year 5 problem starts in Year 4. Planning for two years with a review at the end of the first makes the real commitment visible, which is how a family should be asked to make this decision.

whyPoints.title: Independence is taught by refusing to supply
whyPoints.description: The four skills Year 4 rehearses — form a question, design an investigation, evaluate honestly, sustain an argument — cannot be taught by demonstration. The tutor interrogates rather than answers, which is slower and less comfortable and is the only thing that works.

whyPoints.title: The Personal Project goal tested before the year is spent
whyPoints.description: Most lost Personal Project terms trace to an unviable goal chosen enthusiastically in Year 4. Testing it against four plain criteria takes one session and is the highest-return piece of work available in this year.

whyPoints.title: The fork judged on fit, not on reputation
whyPoints.description: Strong criterion A with weaker B and C often fits an examination-led A Level route; strong B and C fits the Diploma even where topic tests are unremarkable. We will say which the evidence suggests, including when it is the route the family was not expecting.

whyPoints.title: Honesty where independence is the point
whyPoints.description: The Personal Project and criterion B work cannot be ghostwritten without destroying their purpose. The test is whether the student could explain every decision unaided, without notes, and that standard is on the page rather than buried in terms.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what we are not
whyPoints.description: No home visits anywhere in the UAE, no KHDA approval or regulator accreditation, no UAE office. Every AED figure is attributed to whoever published it, no IB exam date is published anywhere on these pages, and where we cannot match a subject at a workable hour we say so.

faqs.question: Is Grade 9 a serious year in the MYP or a quiet one before Grade 10?
faqs.answer: It is the first half of a two-year assessment cycle, which makes it serious in a way that is easy to miss. Scaffolding on criterion B investigations is withdrawn permanently in Year 4, the Personal Project is chosen and begun, and the school starts generating the evidence it will use when advising on the Diploma or an A Level route. None of that has an immediate consequence, which is exactly why families conclude there is nothing to do. The report looks like a Year 3 report while the student is being formed into next year's candidate.

faqs.question: When does the MYP Personal Project actually start?
faqs.answer: In Year 4 in most Dubai schools, with the goal chosen and a process journal begun, and it is submitted in Year 5 against checkpoints the school sets internally. The single most useful Grade 9 action is testing the goal before time is invested: a viable goal is narrow enough to finish, depends only on resources the student will actually have, can be specified so it can be evaluated, and holds their interest for a year. Most unviable goals fail the first two tests, and discovering that in Year 5 costs a term.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child suits the IB Diploma or A Levels?
faqs.answer: Read the criterion profile rather than the grade average. A student whose criterion A scores are strong while criterion B and C lag is often better served by an examination-led A Level route, because criterion A is closest to what examinations test. A student with strong criterion B and C — who forms good questions, designs sound investigations and evaluates honestly — is a natural Diploma candidate even if topic tests are unremarkable, because that is what internal assessments and the Extended Essay reward. Neither profile is better; the match is what matters.

faqs.question: Why has my child's criterion B score dropped in Grade 9?
faqs.answer: Usually because the scaffolding was removed rather than because anything about the child changed. Until Year 4, investigations typically arrive with a question provided and often a method suggested. In Year 4 the student is expected to form the question and design the investigation themselves, and a student who was never taught how reads as having got worse. The fix is practice at exactly that, repeatedly, with a tutor who interrogates the question rather than supplying one. It is slower than content teaching and it is what the next four years assess.

faqs.question: Can my child still change maths route in Grade 9?
faqs.answer: This is the last realistic point. By Year 5 the standard and extended routes have diverged in content rather than only in pace, and most schools decline moves on those grounds rather than on ability. The evidence that moves a decision is criterion B work in which the student states and justifies a general rule, plus criterion C work with correct notation. Ask the school how and when the route decision for Year 5 is taken, because there is no value in building evidence for a review that happens after the decision.

faqs.question: What does my child need to be able to do by the end of Year 4?
faqs.answer: Four things, and they matter more than any topic. Form a research question that is narrow enough to answer from available sources. Design an investigation, including saying which variables were controlled and why. Evaluate their own work honestly — what limited the result, why it mattered, what would improve it. And hold a line of argument across a multi-page essay. Those four are the Diploma internal assessment skill set in miniature, they are assessed in Year 4 at low stakes, and they are far cheaper to learn now than in DP1.

faqs.question: My child is fine on tests but weak on investigations. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It matters for the route decision more than for this year's grades. Strong test performance mostly reflects criterion A, which examinations reward, so that profile often fits an A Level route well. Weak criterion B and C means the independent and investigative side is undeveloped, and that is what the Diploma assesses in every subject through internal assessment plus the Extended Essay. Neither is a problem in itself. The problem is choosing the Diploma on prestige grounds with that profile and meeting six internal assessments at once in DP1.

faqs.question: Where do Grade 9 chemistry marks go missing?
faqs.answer: On calculations that depend on a correct balanced equation written first. Year 4 brings quantitative chemistry properly — reacting masses, rates, energy change — and every calculation assumes the student can balance confidently. A student who never secured balancing in Year 3 hits a ceiling here that no amount of revising reaction types will lift, because the gap is procedural rather than conceptual. Four to six sessions taking balancing to automaticity is usually the correct intervention, and it raises the ceiling on the whole strand rather than on one topic.

faqs.question: How much does Grade 9 MYP tutoring cost in Dubai over two years?
faqs.answer: Market rates for a qualified subject tutor working online run AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150, and Bestimate's published Dubai monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240-600 at the budget end and AED 600-1,200 in the middle. Because Grades 9 and 10 are one cycle, the honest way to decide is for two years with a review at the end of Year 4, which makes the real total visible in September rather than discovered in instalments across twenty-four months.

faqs.question: What exactly may a Year 4 tutor do on the Personal Project journal?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the useful help is mostly questions. A tutor may explain each criterion letter by letter with the marks attached, test whether a goal is viable, ask the questions that sharpen a specification, read the student's own journal entries and report drafts and say what is missing against the criteria, and teach referencing. A tutor may not write the report, produce the journal, design the project or correct a draft into a finished state. The test is whether the student could explain every decision in the project unaided, to their supervisor, without notes.

faqs.question: Is Grade 9 too late to fix a Year 2 or Year 3 gap?
faqs.answer: No, and it is often the highest-return work available. Year 4 content assumes earlier fluency: quadratics assume algebraic manipulation, chemistry calculations assume balancing, physics assumes formula rearrangement. Four to six sessions on one of those earlier skills frequently recovers more Year 4 marks than twenty sessions of Year 4 content, because the Year 4 work was being attempted on an insecure foundation. The diagnosis is quick — can the student do the earlier skill unprompted, cold, two weeks after being shown it?

faqs.question: Does my child's MYP language phase still matter in Grade 9?
faqs.answer: Yes, as a constraint rather than as a grade. Language Acquisition is assessed against phase descriptors, phase movement typically happened around Year 2, and by Year 4 the phase is settled for most students. What it determines is which Diploma language routes are realistically open at options — and in Dubai it interacts with the KHDA Arabic streams, where separate classes are required for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language. A direct question to the school this year is still useful; next year it mostly is not.

faqs.question: How should Grade 9 sessions be scheduled around sport and activities?
faqs.answer: Deliberately, because Year 4 is where committed activities and a heavier academic week first collide properly. Fix the slot with the sport timetable in front of you rather than around it afterwards. The realistic weekday start depends on the community: 4.30pm from Dubai Hills Estate with schooling inside it, 5pm or later from Arabian Ranches along the Al Khail corridor, and 6pm or later from Dubai Marina. Remember the UAE week runs Monday to Friday with a Saturday-Sunday weekend, so Friday evening is a school night.

faqs.question: What is the single best use of a Dubai school holiday in Grade 9?
faqs.answer: Independence work, because it needs time rather than urgency. Forming a research question, designing an investigation and learning to evaluate one's own method are slow, uncomfortable activities that do not fit well into an hour squeezed after a long school day. The two or three weeks after a long break, before assessments restart, allow longer sessions with nothing competing. It is also the right window for a prior-year securing block, since taking a skill to automaticity benefits from consecutive days rather than weekly instalments.

faqs.question: Do you tutor the UAE mandatory subjects at Grade 9 level?
faqs.answer: Yes, from the school's own material and the official curriculum. KHDA states that for the mandatory UAE subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so no parallel scheme is introduced. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, specifies the language of instruction for each stream, and requires that school teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education hold appropriate KHDA approval — a fair question to put to the school.

faqs.question: Which exam series will a Dubai student sit if they move to IGCSE after Grade 9?
faqs.answer: June or November with Cambridge International, and May/June or November with Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. The Cambridge February/March series is offered to India only and is not available to a UAE candidate, which matters because families arriving from India sometimes plan around it. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam through using the wrong zone timetable, so work from the live official timetable for your school's zone rather than a restated date.

dubai/grade-9-ib-myp-tutor.closingHeading: Treat Year 4 as the first half of the work
dubai/grade-9-ib-myp-tutor.closingBody: Almost every Grade 10 problem in the MYP starts in Grade 9 and looks harmless at the time: a Personal Project goal that cannot be finished, a research question nobody taught the student to form, an evaluation habit never built, a maths route left unchallenged in the last year it could be. The useful work now is narrow — test the project goal, build the four independence skills, and read criterion B and C rather than the topic tests. Book a free trial lesson and bring two pieces of marked investigative work. Sessions are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time; we do not send tutors to UAE homes.

intro.heading: The part of the course a school cannot teach, and the market that exploits it
paragraphs: Green Community sits inside Dubai Investments Park: low-rise apartments, townhouses and villas arranged around planted courtyards, with an IB continuum school inside the development and the rest of the Dubai Investments Park school cluster a few minutes away. The households here are long-stay rather than transient, which means the enquiries we get are about whole courses rather than about next week's test, and more of them are about coursework than about lessons.

That reflects how the programmes are built. An IB Diploma student produces an internal assessment in every subject, a four-thousand-word Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, and a CAS record. An MYP student finishes with a Personal Project assessed on their own process journal. Some IGCSE subjects carry coursework components. In each case the school teaches the surrounding content and then supervises work the student must produce independently.

Supervision is deliberately limited. Schools cap the number of formal meetings for an Extended Essay, require a process journal for a Personal Project, and ask the supervisor to confirm the submitted work is the candidate's own. The design is sound. The side effect is a gap that a parent can see and cannot fill: a teenager with four unfinished components, a supervisor they are allowed to meet three times, and six weeks to go.

Into that gap has grown a market. The research behind these pages found a Dubai site advertising finished internal assessments at AED 3,750 each. That is not tutoring. It is an academic-integrity breach with a student's diploma attached to it, and the person who carries the consequence is the sixteen-year-old whose name is on the submission, not the operator who took the payment. Several ranking pages in this search cluster sit uncomfortably close to that line in how they describe coursework support.

It is worth being clear about why a tutoring company would write this page at all, since the obvious commercial move is to say nothing and let a parent assume the most generous interpretation. The reason is that the alternative is worse for everyone involved. A family who buys the wrong kind of help exposes their own child to a process that can end a diploma, and a provider who allows the ambiguity to stand is relying on that confusion to make a sale. Stating the boundary in public costs us a small number of enquiries and removes the argument from the point at which it usually happens, which is late at night, two days before a deadline, with a frightened teenager in the room.

So this page is about the boundary rather than about subjects. It covers what the IB treats as malpractice, how authentication actually works in a school, where generative AI and translation tools sit, exactly what a tutor may and may not do, how to recognise an operator selling the other thing, what honest supervision costs in this market, and the referencing mechanics students get wrong without any dishonest intent at all. Every lesson described runs online, one-to-one. IB Gram does not visit homes in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India.

dubai/green-community.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects most often requested here, described by the independent component each one carries and where its marks are decided.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The individual investigation needs a measurable variable, a repeatable method and real statistical treatment. Most lost marks sit in analysis and evaluation rather than in the biology, and a student who collects data before defining the hypothesis has already lost them.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Investigations fail on scope more than on technique: a question broad enough to be interesting is usually too broad to measure with school equipment. Energetics, kinetics and organic mechanisms carry Higher Level difficulty in the papers.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Uncertainty propagation and error analysis are examinable, rarely taught deliberately and heavily rewarded in the investigation. At IGCSE the recurring loss is circuit reasoning when conditions change rather than recall of definitions.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The exploration must contain genuine mathematics rather than the application of a formula, and choosing a topic that permits real manipulation is most of the work. In the papers, reasoning marks dominate and unjustified answers score a fraction of what is available.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology use. Explorations here commonly repeat a textbook procedure instead of interpreting a result, and papers lose marks where a test is presented without its hypothesis, assumptions or a conclusion in context.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper one is unseen guided analysis, so rereading set texts does not prepare it. The individual oral requires a global issue and two extracts prepared months ahead, and Higher Level adds an essay that must argue rather than summarise.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The historical investigation is where referencing and source evaluation are assessed most directly, and where unintentional plagiarism most often occurs. Paper marks follow command terms and the discipline of using evidence rather than narrating it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The internal assessment depends on an organisation that will supply usable figures, and that choice has to be made early. In the papers, a framework named but not applied to the stimulus loses most of the available analysis credit.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition of three objects with a written commentary. Marks go to precise claim and counterclaim structure, which is coachable, and the component fails most often because it is left until the term everything else is due.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab pupils. Translation tools make this subject the one where the honesty line is crossed most casually and most often.

sections.heading: Where the integrity question actually comes from
paragraphs: Almost nobody sets out to cheat. The breaches that get students into trouble in Dubai schools are mostly produced by pressure and poor technique rather than by intent. A student with four unfinished components and three weeks left makes a decision at midnight that they would not make in September. A student taking notes without separating quotation from paraphrase ends up with sentences in a draft that are not theirs and cannot say where they came from. A student whose Arabic is weak runs a paragraph through a translation tool and submits it without thinking of it as dishonest.

The structural cause is the one described at the top of this page. The independent components are substantial, the supervision is deliberately rationed, and the deadlines cluster. A parent who understands that is in a position to intervene early, which is the only intervention that works. A parent who discovers it in the final fortnight is choosing between a poor submission and a dishonest one, and a market exists to make the second option easy.

The second cause is that nobody states the rules plainly to the student. Schools publish academic-honesty policies, and most students have signed one without reading it. They know plagiarism is wrong. They are far less clear about collusion, about submitting the same work twice, about whether a parent may proofread, about whether a tutor may suggest a structure, and about where a language tool sits. Those are the grey areas where real cases arise.

This page sets the boundary out explicitly because that is more useful than a reassurance. A student who knows exactly what is permitted works more confidently, asks better questions of their supervisor, and does not reach the midnight decision in the first place. It also makes a tutor's role clearer: the help that is legitimate is substantial, and knowing its shape is what stops a family buying the wrong thing in a panic.

sections.heading: What counts as malpractice, in the categories schools actually use
paragraphs: School and board policies tend to describe four or five categories rather than one. Plagiarism is representing someone else's words, ideas or data as your own, including from a website, a textbook, a sibling's old work or a generative tool, and including when it is accidental. Collusion is supporting another candidate in presenting work that is not their own, which catches the student who shares a completed answer as well as the one who copies it.

Duplication of work means submitting the same piece for two different assessments, which students do innocently when a topic suits both an essay and an investigation. Fabrication of data covers inventing results or adjusting them to fit a hypothesis, which happens quietly in science investigations where an experiment went wrong and the deadline did not move. Misconduct during an examination covers unauthorised material and disruption, and is a separate matter handled by invigilation rules.

The consequences are set by the board and the school rather than by any tutor, and they are proportionate to the component. A finding against a Diploma component can mean no grade awarded in that subject, which can mean no diploma. The point worth making to a sixteen-year-old is not the severity but the asymmetry: the operator who sold the work faces nothing, and the candidate faces the outcome.

What protects a student is evidence of process. A dated process journal, draft versions saved as they were written, notes that record where each source came from, and a supervisor who has seen the work develop. Students who keep those things are rarely in difficulty even when a similarity report flags something, because they can show how the work came to exist. Students who produce a finished document from nowhere have no defence available to them.

sections.heading: Authentication: what a supervisor is actually confirming
paragraphs: When a component is submitted, the supervisor confirms it is the candidate's own work. That confirmation is not a formality and it is not based on trust alone. Supervisors are expected to have seen the work develop, which is why schools require meetings at specified points, why a Personal Project is assessed partly on a journal kept during the project, and why a supervisor who has never seen a draft is in a difficult position when something looks wrong.

The checks available are more varied than students assume. Similarity-detection software compares a submission against published sources and against other submissions. Supervisors compare a written component against the student's classwork, and a sudden change in vocabulary, syntax or confidence is visible to anyone who has marked that student for a year. Where doubt remains, a supervisor can question a student about their own work, and a candidate who cannot explain their own method or defend their own argument has answered the question.

That last mechanism is worth describing to a student explicitly, because it reframes the whole issue. The risk is not being caught by software. It is being unable to discuss your own work with the person who knows your writing best. A student who has done the work can talk about it for an hour; a student who has not cannot manage five minutes, and nobody needs a tool to tell the difference.

For a family, the practical implication is about record-keeping rather than suspicion. Keep the drafts. Keep the dated journal. Keep notes with sources attached. Our supervision sessions produce a written record of what was discussed and what the student agreed to do next, and we will release it to the school on request. That record exists to protect the student, and it is one of the reasons online supervision has an advantage over a conversation at a kitchen table.

sections.heading: Generative AI, translation tools and the line nobody has written down
paragraphs: This is the live question in every Dubai staff room and the one competitor pages avoid entirely. The honest position is that policies vary by school and are still moving, so the first and most important step is to read your own school's written policy and ask the department what it expects. What follows is a general framing, not a substitute for that policy, and where the two differ the school's rules govern.

The useful distinction is between a tool that helps a student think and a tool that produces the output being assessed. Using a search tool to find a paper, a calculator or spreadsheet to process data a student collected, a spellchecker, or a grammar prompt that flags an error for the student to fix, sits comfortably inside normal practice. Asking a model to draft a paragraph, to generate an argument, to summarise a source the student has not read, or to translate their own sentences into fluent English or Arabic, does not: the assessed output stops being theirs.

In between sits a genuine grey zone that needs declaration rather than avoidance. Using a model to explain a concept the student then writes about themselves, to suggest search terms, or to generate practice questions is usually acceptable and worth mentioning to a supervisor. Using one to check a reference format is low risk. The rule that holds across all of it: if a student could not reproduce the thinking without the tool, the tool produced the work.

Language subjects are where this bites hardest, and Arabic as an additional language is the specific case in this community. A student submitting translated text is submitting someone else's language, which is precisely what is being assessed. The legitimate route is slower and actually works: build vocabulary, practise the script, write badly in Arabic and improve it with a teacher. We will not supply translated text, and we will tell a student plainly that using a tool for it defeats the only purpose the subject has.

sections.heading: Exactly where a tutor's help stops
paragraphs: The legitimate scope of tutoring on an independently produced component is wide, and families who do not know that often either buy nothing or buy something they should not. A tutor may teach the underlying content, which is the bulk of the work. A tutor may read out the assessment criteria and explain what each strand actually rewards, which most students have never had done properly. A tutor may interrogate a research question until it is narrow enough to answer, which is the single highest-value hour available.

A tutor may show how a comparable published investigation was structured, as an example of form rather than content. A tutor may read one draft the student has written and respond with questions: what is your claim here, where is the evidence, why this method rather than that one, what would change your conclusion. A tutor may check that length, formatting and referencing meet the requirements in the current subject guide. All of that improves work without any of the tutor's words entering it.

What a tutor may not do is produce the output. Not write, not rewrite, not edit a draft into a finished state, not supply text, data, structure to be copied, or a model answer that could be submitted. Not translate. Not run a model and hand over the result. Not complete a section the student has left blank because they ran out of time. These are refusals rather than preferences, and we make them clear to the student in the first session so that nobody is negotiating them at midnight.

There is one further thing a good tutor does that is rarely mentioned: say no out loud, with a reason, in front of the student. A teenager who hears an adult decline to cross a line, and explain why in terms of the risk to them rather than to us, learns something more useful than a policy document. It also means that when the request comes from a stressed parent rather than from the student, the answer has already been given.

sections.heading: How to recognise an operator selling the thing you should not buy
paragraphs: This market is visible to any parent searching in Dubai, and it presents itself as tutoring. The research behind these pages found a site advertising finished internal assessments at AED 3,750. Others are less explicit and no different in substance: they promise a completed component by a stated deadline, quote a fixed price per piece of work, and describe the service in language borrowed from editing and proofreading.

There are reliable signals. A fixed price per component rather than an hourly rate for teaching is the clearest, because teaching time cannot be priced per document. A promised turnaround measured in days. A grade attached to the offer. No named tutor, or a named tutor who never speaks to the student. An emphasis on confidentiality rather than on learning. And a refusal to put the scope of work in writing, which is the question that ends most of these conversations.

The second thing to look at is what happens to the student. An honest arrangement produces a student who can discuss their own work, because they did it. A purchased component produces a student who will be asked about their own method by a supervisor who has marked their writing for a year, and who cannot answer. The risk is not primarily detection software; it is the five minutes of conversation that any experienced teacher can conduct.

Parents occasionally ask whether a heavy proofread is a safe middle route. It is not, and it is the most common way an honest family ends up on the wrong side of a line. Correcting spelling is fine. Rewriting sentences for fluency changes the assessed output, especially in language subjects where expression is the thing being marked. If an adult's rewriting materially improved the text, the text is no longer the student's, whatever the intention was.

sections.heading: What honest supervision costs in this market
paragraphs: Supervision is priced differently from weekly teaching, and the difference is worth understanding before you compare quotes. Weekly teaching is an ongoing hourly arrangement. Supervision is a small number of sessions placed at specific points in a component's life: question design, method or structure review, a response to a draft the student has written, and a final check against criteria and formatting. Four hours placed well beat twelve bought in the final fortnight.

The figures below are Dubai market rates collected in October 2026, each attributed to whoever published it. They are market rates rather than an IB Gram price list, and they exist on this page because three of the six agency pages ranking for these searches publish no price at all. Use them to judge whether a quote you have received is normal, and to notice when a price is attached to a document rather than to time.

Note what the last row in the table is doing there. A price per finished component is not a tutoring rate at all; it is the price of a risk transferred to your child. It appears in this market at a figure comparable to several months of honest weekly teaching, which is the comparison worth making. The same money buys a term of work that improves a student and leaves no exposure.

One more number for context. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package worth AED 1.5 billion. Tuition is the movable part of the education budget this year, and for a Diploma household the highest-return use of it is a handful of supervision hours placed early in the first Diploma year rather than a block of hours bought under deadline pressure in the second.

sections.heading: Referencing, note-taking and the mistakes made without any intent
paragraphs: A large share of honesty cases come from technique rather than from decisions. The most common mechanism is note-taking that does not distinguish between what was quoted, what was paraphrased and what the student thought themselves. Three weeks later the notes are the only record, the distinctions have gone, and sentences that came from a source arrive in a draft looking like the student's own. The student is not lying; they genuinely cannot tell any more.

The fix is a habit rather than a tool, and it takes one session to install. Quotations go in quotation marks with the source and page recorded at the moment they are written down. Paraphrase gets a marker and a source. The student's own thoughts get a different marker. Everything carries a reference from the first note onwards, not added at the end from memory. Students who work this way produce cleaner drafts and finish faster, because they are never hunting for where something came from.

Referencing style matters less than consistency. Schools and subjects differ, and the requirement in most cases is to use one recognised style properly throughout. The errors that cost marks are mechanical: a bibliography that does not match the in-text citations, sources listed that were never cited, a web page referenced with no access date, a data set used with no attribution at all. None of those is dishonest, and all of them are visible to a marker.

Similarity reports deserve a word, because students panic at them. A similarity percentage is not a plagiarism verdict; a well-referenced history investigation with substantial quotation can report high similarity and be entirely honest. The useful way to read a report is item by item, checking that each flagged passage is quoted and cited or genuinely the student's own phrasing. We teach students to do exactly that, and to use the report before submission as a check rather than after it as an accusation.

sections.heading: Getting started from Green Community
paragraphs: Send a component list rather than a request for a tutor: each subject and level, which independently produced components are outstanding, the school's own internal deadline for each, and the criteria document or task sheet the school issued. Add the most recent marked piece of work. A supervision plan is built backwards from those dates, and sending them turns the first hour into work rather than into an interview.

The first session establishes which of four situations you are in, because they need different responses: a question that is not yet answerable, data collected that will not support the required analysis, a draft that answers a different question from the one asked, or a component simply not started. The first three are fixable with a small number of hours. The fourth sometimes needs a conversation with the school about timing rather than a tutoring purchase, and we will say so.

The boundary conversation happens in that first session, with the student present. The tutor says what they will do, what they will not do, and why the line sits where it does in terms of the risk to the student. That removes the midnight negotiation entirely, which is the single most useful thing a provider can do for a Diploma household. We also keep a written record of each session and will release it to the school on request.

Three limits stated before any payment. We do not promise grades or points. We do not send tutors to homes in the UAE, as every lesson is one-to-one online. And we will not write, rewrite, translate, edit to completion or supply any part of an assessed component, however late the deadline is, however the request is phrased, and whoever is asking.

process.title: Send the component list
process.description: Subjects and levels, every outstanding independently produced component, the school's internal deadline for each, and the criteria or task sheet the school issued. Those dates, not the board's, are what a supervision plan is built around.

process.title: Diagnostic hour
process.description: One online session establishing which problem exists in each component: an unanswerable question, unusable data, a draft answering the wrong question, or nothing started. You receive a written summary naming the situation and the sequence that follows from it.

process.title: The boundary conversation
process.description: In the first session, with the student present, the tutor states exactly what they will and will not do with assessed work and why. Having that conversation early removes the pressured request later, which is when most honesty problems actually begin.

process.title: Hours placed early
process.description: Question design first, then method or structure, then a response to a draft the student has written, then final checks on criteria and formatting. The draft-response session is scheduled after the draft exists, not before, so it has something real to work on.

process.title: Record and release
process.description: Each session produces a written note of what was discussed and what the student agreed to do next. The notes stay available to you and to the school on request, which is useful evidence of process if any question of authenticity ever arises.

whyPoints.title: The line is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: Your child hears in the first session what a tutor will and will not do with assessed work, and why. That is protection for the candidate, because an authentication finding falls on them rather than on whoever took the payment.

whyPoints.title: A written trail of process
whyPoints.description: Every supervision session leaves a note of what was discussed and what was agreed. Evidence that work developed over time is what protects a student when a similarity report or a supervisor's question raises a doubt.

whyPoints.title: Help that is genuinely substantial
whyPoints.description: Teaching content, explaining criteria strand by strand, interrogating a research question and questioning a draft is a great deal of legitimate help. Families who do not know its shape either buy nothing or buy something they should not.

whyPoints.title: Figures and sources you can check
whyPoints.description: Every AED rate names its publisher and the month collected, including the price one Dubai site charges for a finished component. Nothing here is asserted without a source, and where something could not be verified the page says so.

whyPoints.title: Refusals we will make out loud
whyPoints.description: We will not write, rewrite, translate, edit to completion or supply any part of an assessed component, under deadline pressure or otherwise. No grade promises, no invented statistics, and no claim of accreditation from any regulator or examination board.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an internal assessment without it becoming malpractice?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the legitimate scope is wide. A tutor can teach the underlying content, read out each assessment criterion and explain what it rewards, interrogate the research question until it is narrow enough to answer, show how a comparable published investigation was structured, read one draft the student has written and respond with questions, and check length and formatting against the current subject guide. What a tutor cannot do is write, rewrite, edit to a finished state, translate, or supply data or text. The boundary protects the candidate, not the tutor.

faqs.question: Is it acceptable for me to proofread my daughter's essay?
faqs.answer: Correcting spelling and pointing out a typo is normal parental help. Rewriting sentences for fluency is not, and it is the most common way an honest family crosses a line without meaning to. Expression is part of what is being assessed, particularly in language subjects, so an adult's rewriting changes the assessed output. The safe version is to read it and ask questions: is this what you meant, I did not follow this paragraph, what is your claim here. That improves the work without any of your words entering it.

faqs.question: What does a supervisor actually check before signing work off?
faqs.answer: More than a similarity report. Supervisors are expected to have seen the work develop, which is why schools require meetings at set points and why a Personal Project is assessed partly on a journal kept during the project. They compare a submission against the student's classwork, where a sudden change in vocabulary or confidence is visible to anyone who has marked that student for a year. Where doubt remains they can question the student about their own method and argument, which is the check nobody can prepare for without having done the work.

faqs.question: Can my son use an AI tool to help with his research?
faqs.answer: Read your school's written policy first, because policies differ and are still changing, and where they differ from any general advice the school's rules govern. The workable distinction is between a tool that helps a student think and one that produces the assessed output. Using a model to explain a concept he then writes about himself, or to suggest search terms, is usually acceptable and worth mentioning to his supervisor. Asking it to draft paragraphs, generate arguments or summarise sources he has not read is not, because the output stops being his.

faqs.question: Why is using a translation tool for Arabic homework a problem?
faqs.answer: Because expression in Arabic is precisely what the subject assesses. A student who writes in English and translates is submitting a tool's language rather than their own, which makes the mark meaningless even where no policy is breached. It also prevents the only thing that actually works, which is writing badly in Arabic and improving it with a teacher. We will not supply translated text, and we tell students plainly that the shortcut removes the subject's entire purpose while leaving the examination still to come.

faqs.question: What happens if a component simply is not finished in time?
faqs.answer: Talk to the school immediately rather than solving it privately. Schools deal with late and incomplete work regularly and have processes for it, including internal extensions in some circumstances, and a supervisor told early can advise on what to prioritise. A late or incomplete honest submission is recoverable; a dishonest complete one is not. The worst outcome comes from families who try to protect a deadline at midnight, which is the exact decision this market is built to serve.

faqs.question: How do I spot an operator selling completed coursework?
faqs.answer: Look for a price per document rather than an hourly rate for teaching, because teaching time cannot be priced per piece of work. Other signals are a promised turnaround in days, a grade attached to the offer, no named tutor or one who never speaks to the student, an emphasis on confidentiality rather than on learning, and a refusal to put the scope of work in writing. That last question ends most of these conversations, and asking it costs nothing.

faqs.question: Does a high similarity score mean my child plagiarised?
faqs.answer: No. A similarity percentage is not a verdict. A well-referenced history investigation with substantial quoted material can score high and be entirely honest, while a paraphrased piece can score low and still be plagiarised. The report should be read item by item: is each flagged passage quoted and cited, or is it genuinely the student's own phrasing. We teach students to run that check before submission as a diagnostic rather than meeting it afterwards as an accusation.

faqs.question: Can two friends work on the same investigation topic?
faqs.answer: Usually yes on the topic, with care about the execution. Discussing method, sharing reading and arguing about an idea is normal academic practice. Exchanging text, data or a finished answer is collusion, which catches the student who gives as well as the one who receives. The practical rule is that conversation is fine and documents are not. If two students in the same class are working closely, both supervisors should know, which removes any ambiguity if the submissions resemble each other.

faqs.question: Can my daughter reuse one topic for two different components?
faqs.answer: Not without checking, because submitting the same work for two assessments is duplication of work, and students do it innocently when a good topic suits both an essay and an investigation. Related but genuinely distinct pieces are sometimes permitted; identical or substantially overlapping ones are not. The answer depends on the subjects and the school, so ask both supervisors before any work begins rather than afterwards, when the only remedy is to start one of them again.

faqs.question: What should a student keep in case their work is questioned?
faqs.answer: Evidence that the work developed over time. Dated draft versions saved separately rather than overwritten, a process journal where the component requires one, notes with sources attached from the moment they were written, and a record of supervisor meetings. Students with that material are rarely in difficulty even when something is flagged, because they can show how the work came to exist. Our supervision sessions add a written record of what was discussed, which we release to the school on request.

faqs.question: Do tutors visit homes in Green Community?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs only in India; every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video. For component supervision the screen is a genuine advantage rather than a compromise: the criteria, the draft, the data file and the subject guide are visible to both people at once, and each session leaves a written record. A conversation across a table leaves nothing, and for work that may need to be defended as the student's own, that record is worth having.

faqs.question: How many hours of supervision should we expect to pay for?
faqs.answer: Four to six per component, placed at the right moments, is usually sufficient. One hour narrowing the question until the variables are nameable, one on method or structure before data is collected, one responding to a draft the student has written, and one on final checks against criteria and formatting. Hours bought in the last fortnight achieve far less, because the data and the question are fixed by then and only the writing can change, which is the part a tutor must not touch.

faqs.question: Who is legally allowed to tutor privately in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Private tuition runs on a MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered at government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing with a two-working-day completion time. Operating without a permit exposes an individual to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: What would IB Gram refuse even if we insisted?
faqs.answer: Writing, rewriting, translating, editing to a finished state or supplying any part of an assessed component, whatever the deadline and whoever asks. We will say so to the student as well as to you, because that is what removes the pressured request later. We also make no promises about grades or points totals, publish no success statistics without a sample size and method, claim no accreditation from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and operate no UAE office.

dubai/green-community.closingHeading: Buy the hours that improve the work, not the ones that replace it
dubai/green-community.closingBody: If your child has independently produced components outstanding, the useful first step is a list: each component, the school's own deadline, and the criteria sheet the school issued. One diagnostic hour online will tell you whether each one needs a narrower question, a usable method, a response to a draft, or a conversation with the school about timing. Four well-placed hours per component is the normal honest answer, and it costs a fraction of what this market charges for a finished document while leaving your child with work they can defend and knowledge they actually have. Where a component needs the school rather than a tutor, we will say that instead.

dubai/hor-al-anz.tutorsIntro: Hor Al Anz families ask for mathematics, the sciences, accounting and English, usually for a Year 10 or Year 11 student whose classwork looks fine and whose paper marks do not. The tutors below work on the written technique that converts knowledge into marks, which is the thing a large class cannot supply per student.

intro.heading: Knowing it and scoring it are two different skills
paragraphs: Hor Al Anz is dense, long-settled and almost entirely apartments, running inland from the Deira coast road towards Abu Hail and Al Qusais. It is one of the most heavily populated parts of Dubai, with a large South Asian community and schools within a few minutes that between them run Indian, British and IB curricula. Indian curricula accounted for 26 per cent of Dubai's private school enrolment in 2024-25, and in this district the share is far higher.

The academic pattern here is distinctive and it is not about effort. Students from this community are, on average, taught a great deal of content and taught it thoroughly. What they often have not been taught is how a Cambridge or Pearson mark scheme awards marks, which is a separate skill with its own rules. The result is a student who can do the physics and loses a third of the available marks on how the answer is written, and a family who reasonably concludes the child needs more physics.

The second factor is class size. Deira's established schools have large year groups, and a teacher with thirty students in a room can deliver content efficiently, set work and mark it. What no timetable allows is individual correction of extended written answers for thirty students every week, which is precisely the activity that fixes the technique problem. That is a structural limit, not a failing, and it is the clearest case anywhere for one-to-one work.

The third factor is transfer. A significant number of students in this district move from CBSE or ICSE into Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE at Year 9 or Year 10, and the direction of the gap surprises families. In mathematics and the sciences the incoming student is frequently ahead on content and behind on written technique and command terms. That is good news, because technique responds to focused work in weeks where missing content takes terms.

This page is written around that diagnosis. It covers what a class of thirty can and cannot do, how the transfer from an Indian board actually behaves subject by subject, what a raw mark converts into and why boundaries move, what the different support formats cost per outcome rather than per hour, how to build a retrieval routine across nine subjects, and what to ask the exams officer. Lessons are delivered online, one to one, over live video, and IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai, which is a service offered only in India. Every AED figure below is a market rate attributed to the provider that published it in October 2026, and every board date comes from Cambridge or Pearson directly. No grade boundary is presented as fixed, because boundaries are set after a paper has been marked and change from series to series.

dubai/hor-al-anz.programmesIntro: What matters in this district is how each qualification is marked, because that is where the marks are being lost. The notes below describe each programme in terms of what its assessment actually rewards.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Terminal papers across eight or nine subjects, with coursework in some. Marks are awarded for specific creditable statements and specific method steps rather than for the overall quality of an answer, and Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended with Core capping the grade. A student who writes a good answer in the wrong form collects a fraction of what was available.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge and Pearson are separate qualifications with different codes, papers and tiering rules, and Deira schools use both alongside Indian boards. The syllabus code is the quick check: 0580 and 0625 are Cambridge Mathematics and Physics, 4MA1 and 4PH1 the Pearson equivalents, and support aimed at the wrong code wastes its opening sessions.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Internal assessment carries roughly a fifth to a quarter of each subject grade and is marked against published criteria letter by letter. A student used to content-led examination finds the criterion marking unfamiliar, and the unfamiliarity itself costs marks.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in the Deira and Al Garhoud schools sit the May session. The deadlines that bind hardest are the school's internal ones for each internal assessment and the Extended Essay, held by the IB coordinator. No IB session or results date appears on this page, because the IB's own site could not be confirmed directly for this project.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8 and converted to a 1-7 grade through school-set boundaries. Process is credited in a way that content-led systems do not credit it, which means a student transferring in can produce correct work and score in the middle band because the criterion was about method rather than answer.
programmes.countryNote: For a family moving from an Indian board into an IB continuum school, the MYP report is the hardest document to read, because a criterion score of 4 out of 8 maps onto no scale the family has used before. Ask the school which subject-specific boundaries it applies, since those are set at school level.

dubai/hor-al-anz.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Hor Al Anz families ask about most. Each note names where the marks are actually going, which in this district is more often the written form of the answer than the understanding behind it.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: Transferring students are often ahead on technique in algebra and arithmetic and lose marks on method presentation, on multi-topic questions, and on showing the working a mark scheme awards credit for. A Core tier placement caps the grade, so the Year 10 tier decision matters more than the Year 11 revision.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and the practical and data questions generate most enquiries. Marks go on stated reasoning and correct units rather than on the final number, and a confident student who writes only the answer loses the method marks that were the larger share.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, rates and the qualitative analysis questions. Transferring students generally know the chemistry and lose marks on command terms and on stating observations in the form the scheme requires, which is correctable in a handful of focused sessions.

subjects.name: IGCSE Biology
subjects.description: The highest-volume science and the most command-term sensitive: an outline answered as a description, an explain answered as a list. The content is rarely the problem for students from a content-heavy background; the instruction word is.

subjects.name: IGCSE English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Distinct from first-language English and frequently the correct entry. Marks sit in reading comprehension technique and in the structure of the writing tasks rather than in vocabulary breadth, so targeted practice against the criteria outperforms general reading.

subjects.name: IGCSE Accounting
subjects.description: Heavily rewarded for layout and convention as well as for arithmetic. Students who can calculate correctly lose marks on presentation of statements and on the narrative explanation questions, which is a learnable and fast correction.

subjects.name: IGCSE Information and Communication Technology
subjects.description: A theory paper where precise terminology earns the marks, and practical papers where following the task instruction exactly matters more than producing a good-looking result. Able students routinely under-score for ignoring a specified step.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with the calculator assumed throughout. Marks leak where an answer arrives with no stated assumption or a correlation with no comment on its limits. Check destination prerequisites before assuming it is the easier route.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case application rather than recall, with the Higher Level paper adding extended response under tighter time. Defining a term instead of applying it to the stimulus organisation is the single most common way an able student scores in the bottom band.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Higher Level extensions assume the Standard Level material is automatic rather than recalled, so organic mechanisms and energetics generate most of the requests. The scientific investigation is marked on research design before anything else, which catches strong practical students.

sections.heading: Thirty in a class: what that actually does to feedback
paragraphs: This has to be said precisely, because the honest version is useful and the lazy version is an insult to good teachers. A teacher with thirty students in a Deira classroom can explain content clearly, demonstrate worked examples, set written work and mark it. Several of the schools in this district have been doing that successfully for decades and their results reflect it. What a timetable with thirty students per class cannot produce is weekly, individual, line-by-line correction of extended written answers for every student.

That specific activity is the one that fixes a technique problem. Not a mark and a comment at the end of a piece, which is what marking at scale realistically allows, but sitting with one student's answer and showing them that the paper asked for an evaluation, that the mark scheme awards two marks for a judgement they never made, and that the method step they skipped was worth more than the correct final answer. It takes fifteen minutes per student per piece, and thirty students make that impossible.

The table below sets out the arithmetic rather than arguing about it. The consequence column is the one families recognise: a student whose classwork and homework are consistently fine and whose paper marks are consistently lower, with nobody able to explain the mismatch. That gap is stable across papers because the cause is stable, which is why it reads as a ceiling on ability rather than as a correctable fault.

The implication for how a Hor Al Anz family spends is clear. One-to-one work here should be spent on correction, not on explanation. A tutor who re-teaches the topic is duplicating something the school already did competently to thirty students. A tutor who marks the student's own attempt against the published scheme is doing the thing the school structurally cannot, and that is the hour worth paying for.

sections.heading: From CBSE or ICSE into IGCSE: ahead on content, behind on technique
paragraphs: This transfer happens constantly in Hor Al Anz and is almost always described the wrong way round. Families expect their child to be behind, because the new school is a different system and the vocabulary is unfamiliar. In mathematics and the sciences, the incoming student is frequently ahead on content, sometimes by a year, and well drilled in routine procedures. The marks go missing somewhere else entirely.

They go missing in the form of the answer. Cambridge and Pearson mark schemes award credit for named steps and specific statements, and they tie the demand to a published command term. A student trained to produce a correct final answer efficiently will write a correct final answer, skip the intermediate reasoning, and collect a minority of the marks. The same student, shown the mark scheme once, usually corrects it faster than anybody expects.

The second place marks go missing is in the extended written subjects, and here the direction reverses. English, business and the humanities in IGCSE demand analysis and evaluation sustained over a longer answer, against criteria, and students arriving from a system that rewards accurate recall find the switch genuinely hard. That part takes longer than the mathematics correction, and it should be started in Year 9 rather than in Year 11.

The table below maps the transfer subject by subject, with an honest estimate of how long each gap takes. It is written for the direction this district actually moves in. The practical first step for any transferring family is to obtain the new school's syllabus codes and a copy of one past paper with its mark scheme, and to sit with the student while they attempt one question against it. Most of the diagnosis is available in that single hour.

sections.heading: What a raw mark actually converts to, and why boundaries move
paragraphs: Families in this district ask more often than most how many marks a grade needs, which is a sensible question with an uncomfortable answer: it is not fixed. Raw marks on a paper are converted through a boundary that is set after the examination has been sat and marked, and the boundary reflects how demanding that particular paper turned out to be. A grade is a judgement about standard, not a fixed percentage.

The consequence is that chasing a specific percentage is the wrong target. What a student can control is the proportion of available marks they collect from what they can genuinely do, and in this district the usual loss there is large. A student who understands eighty per cent of the content and collects sixty per cent of the marks on that content has a technique problem worth more than any further content coverage.

The second thing worth understanding is where marks are available within a paper. Component weightings differ by subject and level, and papers are not equally rich in easy marks. The early questions in most papers are the cheapest marks on offer, and students who begin at the start, work slowly and run out of time are leaving the most expensive marks unattempted. That is a timing decision, not an ability one.

The table below explains the vocabulary, because families are routinely given a mark, a grade and a percentage and left to work out how the three relate. Published boundaries for past series are available from the boards, and your school's exams officer can also explain how the school converted a mock. What should be treated with suspicion is any tutoring page that publishes a boundary table as though it were fixed, or that offers board mark schemes and boundary documents as downloads, which is a copyright matter rather than a service.

sections.heading: Cost per outcome: groups, centres and one-to-one in Deira
paragraphs: Hor Al Anz and the surrounding districts have a dense supply of tuition centres and group classes, often at a materially lower unit cost than one-to-one, and families here are right to weigh them seriously. The honest answer is that the formats are good at different things, so the comparison should be per outcome rather than per hour. The table below is built that way.

The market bands for reference: a budget online tutor, generally a university student, runs AED 45-150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor online is AED 150-300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. A specialist is AED 200-450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Published packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, which works out at roughly AED 100 an hour. All market figures, gathered October 2026, attributed to those providers and not IB Gram prices.

For a content gap, the group format is excellent value in this district and should be used. A student who genuinely missed a topic because they were absent, or who has arrived mid-syllabus, can have it delivered again in a group of eight at a fraction of the one-to-one cost, and the delivery is the same delivery. Spending specialist money on content redelivery is the most common way a family here overpays.

For a technique problem, the group format cannot work, and this is worth being blunt about. Correction of one student's recurring error pattern requires that student's own paper, and seven other students in the room have different patterns. A group class fixing written technique is really a group class explaining written technique, which is a useful lecture and not the same activity. The distinction is the whole of the spending decision in this district.
