sections.heading: Nine subjects, one fortnight: a revision plan that survives
paragraphs: A Year 11 student in this district commonly carries eight or nine IGCSE subjects. The natural way to revise that is in sequence, finishing one subject before starting the next, and it is the pattern that guarantees failure in June. Whatever is revised first decays while everything else is covered, so the subject that received the most attention arrives at the examination in the worst condition.

The alternative feels less satisfying and works considerably better: every subject touched every fortnight, with short retrieval sessions rather than long review blocks. Twenty minutes of producing content from blank paper beats an hour of rereading notes, and the discomfort of not being able to recall something is the signal that the method is working. Most students resist this precisely because it feels like failing, which is why it needs to be explained once and then scheduled.

Spacing is the second element and it costs nothing. A topic revisited after a day, then a week, then a month is retained at a different level from a topic revisited three times in one evening. Families do not need an app or a system for this; a sheet of paper with subjects down one side and fortnights across the top is enough, and the act of ticking boxes is what keeps it running when nobody is supervising.

The third element is where this district's strength becomes a weakness. Students from a content-heavy background are often very good at diligent, sustained work, and they will do what is set for as long as it is set. The risk is that diligence applied to an ineffective method produces long hours with poor returns, and nobody questions it because the student is visibly working hard. Redirecting those existing hours is usually more valuable than adding new ones.

sections.heading: Second-language English against first-language English
paragraphs: This decision matters a great deal in Hor Al Anz and it is frequently taken by default. Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language and first-language English are different qualifications with different demands, and a student entered for the wrong one either struggles against a standard designed for native speakers or coasts below their potential. Both outcomes are avoidable and both are common.

The second-language route is not a lesser option and should not be treated as one by a family. It assesses reading comprehension, listening where that component is taken, and structured writing to defined tasks. Marks sit in technique: reading a question for exactly what it asks, locating evidence precisely, and following the structure each writing task requires. A student with strong English who has never been taught that technique can score surprisingly low.

The first-language route demands analysis of how a text is constructed and extended writing with control of register and structure. For a student whose education has been in English throughout, it is usually the correct entry and it carries more weight for some sixth-form and university purposes. The question is not pride; it is what the student can produce under time against the published criteria, which a single marked timed piece will reveal.

There is a related point about equivalency worth noting here. The British-track Ministry of Education requirement counts five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, so the English entry is one of the five regardless of which route is taken. What matters is the grade rather than the route label, which is a relief to most families once stated plainly.

sections.heading: Exam entry: what the centre owns and what a family must ask
paragraphs: Entry decisions are made by the school as the examination centre, and most families never see the process. That is usually fine and occasionally expensive, because two of the decisions involved cap outcomes permanently. The tier for a Cambridge subject sets the highest reachable grade. The entry deadline closes months before the paper. Neither is reversible afterwards, and neither is announced to parents in those terms.

The Pearson International GCSE November 2026 series is the useful worked example of the timescales, because its dates are published in full: the final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results reach students in the January that follows, the way the November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. Entries for a series like that close in the summer before it, months ahead of the first paper. A Cambridge candidate in this part of Deira sits the June series or the November series, and the same logic applies on a different footing: entries in the spring for June papers, forecast grades weeks before the first one, results in August. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November each year, the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so the live official PDF is the only version worth planning against. Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, with November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026.

The table below lists what to ask and when. None of it requires a confrontation with the school; it is five questions by email in September, answered by the exams officer in a few lines. The families who send that email are the ones who never discover in March that a tier was set in October, and in a district where a single capped entry can undo two years of work, it is the highest-value email of the year.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in a market that sells finished coursework
paragraphs: This has to be addressed directly because the market is active in this part of Dubai. Research for this project found a provider selling finished Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. Services offering completed coursework, assignments and projects circulate widely, and they are most persuasive to a family whose child is capable, busy and two weeks from a deadline. The transaction looks like buying time. It is not.

Under IB rules, submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice. The investigation falls on the candidate, and the consequence can reach the whole Diploma rather than one subject grade. For IGCSE coursework components, the school declares authenticity, which means a submission that is not the student's work implicates them with their own school as well as with the board. The provider who supplied the document carries none of that.

The legitimate alternative is specific and worth stating so it can be checked. A tutor may explain what each published criterion rewards and the marks it carries. A tutor may interrogate a research question until it can produce usable data in the weeks available. A tutor may teach how a reflection, an evaluation or an argument should be structured, and may read a draft the student has produced and say in writing where it falls short. The student writes every word.

There is a parent test that needs no subject knowledge: ask whether your child could discuss the method, the choices and the limitations of the work with their teacher for ten minutes. A student who did the work can. A student handed a document cannot, and teachers in large Deira year groups encounter this market often enough to recognise the difference quickly. A provider offering to produce the work is giving you the reason to decline.

sections.heading: Checking that a tutor may legally teach in the UAE
paragraphs: The supply of private tutoring in this district is large and much of it is informal, so this is worth a paragraph of real detail rather than a line. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years.

The eligible categories are deliberately broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee, gives a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws.

No fine amount appears here. Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, and figures circulating online could not be verified against any official source. A page quoting a number is not working from a source, and that is itself useful information about the page.

Two further points. The permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, so hiring your child's own teacher is the arrangement these rules exist to prevent. And a tuition centre with premises in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which licenses an organisation rather than conferring approval on any individual tutor. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation and runs no UAE office.

process.title: Send the marked paper first
process.description: Before anything else we want the most recent marked mock or unit test. In this district the diagnosis is almost always in the margins of that paper rather than in a conversation about the subject, and two students with the same grade in the same class lose their marks in different places.

process.title: Get the losses categorised honestly
process.description: Every lost mark on that paper gets classified as knowledge, technique or timing. If the technique share is large, which it usually is here, the plan is mark-scheme work rather than content coverage, and that is both faster and cheaper than the alternative.

process.title: Confirm the board and code
process.description: Ask the exams officer which board and syllabus code each subject is entered for, and whether any Cambridge subject sits at Core. Support aimed at the wrong code wastes its first sessions, and a Core entry caps the grade regardless of how good the tutoring is.

process.title: Trial on an unseen question
process.description: The trial session is spent on a question the student has not seen, marked live against the published scheme. That shows you what the sessions will actually consist of, which is a better test than a discussion of the tutor's experience.

process.title: Review at the next marked assessment
process.description: Progress is judged against the named question types at the next marked paper, not on how the sessions felt. If those types are still failing, the approach changes or the tutor does, and that judgement is only possible because the targets were written down.

whyPoints.title: We do the thing a class of thirty cannot
whyPoints.description: Line-by-line correction of one student's written answers against the published mark scheme takes fifteen minutes per piece. For thirty students that is not available in any timetable, and it is exactly the activity that closes a technique gap.

whyPoints.title: We expect transfer students to be ahead, not behind
whyPoints.description: Students arriving from CBSE or ICSE into IGCSE are frequently ahead on content in mathematics and the sciences and behind on mark-scheme form. Treating them as behind wastes a term; showing them the scheme once usually fixes more than a term of coverage.

whyPoints.title: We will tell you when a group class is better value
whyPoints.description: For a genuine content gap, a published package at roughly AED 100 an hour delivers the same explanation as a specialist at three times the rate. Spending specialist money on content redelivery is the commonest way a family here overpays.

whyPoints.title: No boundary tables presented as fixed
whyPoints.description: Grade boundaries are set after a paper is marked and vary by series, so a page publishing them as fixed is misleading. We explain what is controllable, which is the share of available marks a student collects from what they can already do.

whyPoints.title: Five questions for the exams officer, in writing
whyPoints.description: Board and code, tier, entry deadline, Cambridge zone and internal coursework dates. One email in September prevents most of the avoidable damage in a school year, and it is the highest-value thing a parent here can send.

whyPoints.title: We never supply work that must be the student's own
whyPoints.description: There is an active market in finished coursework in this part of Dubai, and one provider found in research sells completed internal assessments. We teach criteria, question designs and give written feedback on the student's own draft, and nothing else.

faqs.question: My child knows the subject but loses marks in Hor Al Anz school exams. Why?
faqs.answer: Because knowing the content and collecting the marks are separate skills. Cambridge and Pearson schemes award credit for named method steps and specific statements tied to a published command term, so a correct final answer with the reasoning skipped collects a minority of what was available. Students from content-heavy backgrounds are especially prone to this. The fix is line-by-line correction of their own answers against the published scheme, which is fast once started and almost never happens in a class of thirty.

faqs.question: Is a class of thirty a problem for my child's results?
faqs.answer: For content delivery, no; one good explanation serves the whole room, and several Deira schools have done this well for decades. For individual correction of extended written work, yes, because fifteen minutes per student per piece is not available in any timetable. The consequence is the familiar pattern of consistent classwork and lower paper marks with nobody able to explain the gap. That gap is correctable, and one-to-one correction is the only format that addresses it.

faqs.question: We are moving from CBSE to Cambridge IGCSE. Will my child be behind?
faqs.answer: Usually not on content in mathematics and the sciences, where incoming students are often ahead and well drilled in procedures. The marks go missing in the form of the answer: method steps skipped, units omitted, command terms unmet and working not shown. That takes four to eight weeks of mark-scheme work rather than a term of content. The genuine content and skill gap is in extended written subjects such as English and the humanities, which is why that work should start in Year 9.

faqs.question: How many marks does my child need for a grade 7 at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: There is no fixed figure, which is the uncomfortable answer. Raw marks are converted through a boundary set after the paper has been sat and marked, reflecting how demanding that particular paper proved to be. Published boundaries exist for past series and are available from the boards, but they vary. Treat any tutoring page presenting a boundary table as fixed with suspicion. What a student controls is the share of available marks collected from the content they already know, and in this district that share is usually well below what it could be.

faqs.question: Which schools near Hor Al Anz do your students attend?
faqs.answer: The nearest cluster spans Hor Al Anz, Abu Hail and Al Qusais and includes Dubai Scholars Private School, The Westminster School, Al Diyafah High School, The Elite English School and Deira Private School. The second cluster, towards Al Garhoud and Oud Metha, includes The Indian High School, Our Own English High School Dubai, Al Mawakeb School Al Garhoud, Deira International School and St Mary's Catholic High School. Year groups here are large, which is the structural reason written technique goes uncorrected. Named as context only.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class in Deira good value?
faqs.answer: For a content gap, genuinely yes, and families here should use it. A published monthly package of AED 799 for eight sessions works out at roughly AED 100 an hour, and a topic missed through absence can be delivered again in a group as effectively as one to one. For a technique problem it cannot work, because correcting one student's recurring error pattern requires that student's paper while seven others in the room have different patterns. Match the format to the problem.

faqs.question: Should my child take English as a Second Language or first-language English?
faqs.answer: Decide it from a marked timed piece rather than from pride. The second-language route assesses reading comprehension and structured writing to defined tasks, with marks sitting in technique, and a strong English speaker who has never been taught that technique can score low. The first-language route demands analysis of how a text is built and control of register across extended writing. For the Ministry's equivalency count the English entry counts as one of the five either way, so the grade matters more than the route label.

faqs.question: How should a Year 11 student revise nine subjects at once?
faqs.answer: Touch every subject every fortnight rather than finishing one subject before starting the next. Revising in sequence guarantees that whatever was covered first decays most, so the subject that received the most attention arrives in June in the worst condition. Use short retrieval sessions from blank paper rather than long review blocks, and space each topic across a day, a week and a month. A sheet with subjects down one side and fortnights across the top is enough structure.

faqs.question: My child works hard for hours with no improvement. What is wrong?
faqs.answer: Probably the method rather than the effort, which is a common pattern among diligent students from content-heavy backgrounds. Rereading notes, highlighting and redoing questions already mastered all feel productive and return very little. Replace them with retrieval from blank paper, interleaved topics so cross-topic questions stop surprising, spaced review, and unseen questions attempted without a worked example. Redirecting hours already being worked is usually more valuable than adding new ones to a full week.

faqs.question: What should I ask my child's exams officer in September?
faqs.answer: Five things: which board and syllabus code each subject is entered for, whether any Cambridge subject is entered at Core rather than Extended, what the entry deadline is for the series, which Cambridge administrative zone the centre sits in, and what the internal coursework deadlines are. The entry deadline is the one that bites. A Cambridge June entry closes in the spring, months before the papers, and a November entry closes over the preceding summer, so a tier conversation started in the exam term has started too late. A Core entry caps the grade permanently. One email answers all five.

faqs.question: Why does the Cambridge zone matter to a Deira student?
faqs.answer: Because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states plainly that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. A revision plan built from a timetable found online can therefore be wrong by days. Ask the exams officer which zone the school is in and use the school's own version. Pearson revises provisional timetables, so use its live official PDF.

faqs.question: Someone has offered to complete my child's coursework. Should we?
faqs.answer: No. Research for this project found a provider in this market selling finished internal assessments at AED 3,750. Submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice under IB rules, the investigation falls on the candidate, and the consequence can reach the whole Diploma. For IGCSE coursework the school declares authenticity, so it implicates the student with their own school too. A ten-second test: could your child discuss the method and limitations with their teacher for ten minutes?

faqs.question: Can a tutor give my child past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: A tutor can work with you from the boards' own published materials and point you to the official pages, which is where past papers, mark schemes and syllabus documents should be obtained. What a credible provider will not do is reproduce or distribute board syllabus documents, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as its own downloads, which is a copyright matter. Ask your school for the official access route; most schools provide it, and the material is the same material.

faqs.question: Do informal private tutors in Deira need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE's service page stating a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website and e-services. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published.

faqs.question: Can a tutor visit our apartment in Hor Al Anz?
faqs.answer: No. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered online, one to one, over live video, and IB Gram does not make home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service offered only in India. The in-home market in Dubai charges roughly AED 180-500 an hour with travel priced in, against AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor. In a district this dense, with the metro Green Line running through it, the travel premium buys nothing the online format does not already provide.

dubai/hor-al-anz.closingHeading: Bring the marked paper, not the worry
dubai/hor-al-anz.closingBody: If your child is working hard in a Deira school and the paper marks do not match the classwork, the problem is almost certainly in the margins of the last marked script. Send that paper with the school, the year group and the syllabus code, and you will get every lost mark sorted into knowledge, technique or timing, plus a short list of recurring question types to close and a date to review it. Where a group class would do the job more cheaply, we will say so. Lessons run online, one to one, over live video.

dubai/ib-7-in-maths-coaching.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Mathematics at the top of the range, where the marks sit in the final parts of long questions and in the exploration. Each marks written work against published criteria and reports honestly on what is still missing.

intro.heading: A grade 7 in Mathematics is a paper-by-paper problem
paragraphs: There are four IB Mathematics courses and they behave differently. Analysis and Approaches rewards algebraic fluency, proof and abstraction. Applications and Interpretation rewards modelling, statistics and interpretation in context. A student can be strong at one and mediocre at the other, and a plan written for the wrong one wastes months. The first thing we establish is the exact course and level, because every later decision depends on it.

The second is which paper is losing the marks, and this is where most Dubai students surprise their families. At Standard Level there are two papers; at Higher Level there are three, with the third a shorter extended-response paper. One of the two main papers is sat without a calculator and the other with a graphic display calculator. Students who describe themselves as weak at Mathematics very often have a paper-specific problem: fluent with technology and lost without it, or the reverse, able to manipulate algebra but unable to use the calculator efficiently enough to finish.

The third is the exploration, which is the internally assessed component and carries 20 marks across five criteria, lettered A to E. It is marked by the teacher against published descriptors and moderated by the IB. We treat it as a separate project with its own plan, because it is the one part of the grade where the student controls the conditions entirely: topic, timeline, depth, and how carefully the criteria have been read. Confirm the current weightings and criteria with your child's teacher or the current subject guide, since the IB revises its documents and the school's copy is the authoritative one.

Dubai adds the usual pressures. Mathematics is the subject Dubai families most often seek help with across both the IB and IGCSE, which means specialist availability tightens sharply when every school's mock window lands between late November and early February. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is the single hardest match to make in the emirate during those weeks, and families who wait until January to look are choosing from whoever is left rather than from the right person.

One more distinction is worth drawing before any plan is written. A student at a 6 who wants a 7 and a student at a 4 who wants a 6 are not doing the same work, even in the same class. The first is recovering the last marks of long questions and polishing an exploration; the second is closing genuine content gaps in functions or calculus and will need months rather than weeks. Families sometimes arrive with the first label and the second problem, and saying which one the script actually shows is part of the job rather than a sales objection.

All our UAE sessions run one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For Mathematics the online format has a practical edge beyond reach: working on a shared screen means the tutor sees the student's actual written method as it is produced, which is precisely where the method marks are won and lost.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Four courses: Analysis and Approaches at Higher and Standard Level, and Applications and Interpretation at Higher and Standard Level. Two papers at Standard Level, three at Higher, plus the exploration as the internally assessed component across all four routes.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools do not all offer all four routes. Some run Analysis and Approaches only at Higher Level, or Applications only at Standard, which means a student's choice is partly determined by their school's staffing. Families moving between Dubai schools mid-Diploma occasionally find the course they were taking is not offered at the new school, which is worth checking before a transfer rather than after.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment across four criteria rather than papers. Extended mathematics is offered in the later years and is the usual preparation for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. The lack of timed external papers is the main gap students carry into DP1.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students coming into the Diploma from MYP rather than IGCSE frequently lose their first DP1 Mathematics marks to exam technique rather than content. The algebra is there; the ability to produce it under a clock, on paper, with method shown, is not yet. That is a few weeks of work if it is diagnosed early and a persistent handicap if it is not.

programmes.name: IGCSE into Diploma Mathematics
programmes.description: Most Dubai students reach the Diploma via Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1, sometimes with Additional Mathematics 0606 or Further Pure 4PM1 alongside. Students who took the additional course arrive with a real advantage in Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level.
programmes.countryNote: The clearest predictor we see of a comfortable start in Analysis and Approaches HL among Dubai students is whether they sat Additional Mathematics or Further Pure at IGCSE. Students who did not can still succeed, but usually need a bridging block over the summer before DP1 covering calculus foundations and algebraic fluency.

programmes.name: The exploration and the core
programmes.description: The Mathematics exploration is an individual piece of written mathematics, marked against five criteria worth 20 marks in total and moderated externally. It sits alongside the Diploma core of Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, each with its own deadlines.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai internal deadlines for the exploration cluster in the same months as mock exams and other subjects' Internal Assessments, which is why so many explorations are written in a rush against a teacher's extended deadline. Starting the topic conversation a term early is the cheapest intervention available in this subject.

dubai/ib-7-in-maths-coaching.subjectsIntro: A grade 7 in Mathematics is built out of specific competences rather than topics. Below are the ones that decide the grade, with where each is assessed.

subjects.name: Algebraic fluency without a calculator
subjects.levels: AA HL and SL, assessed on the non-calculator paper
subjects.description: Manipulating expressions, solving exactly, and producing surds and logarithms correctly under time. Students who rely on a graphic display calculator in class arrive at this paper unable to work by hand, and the loss is uniform across the whole paper rather than concentrated.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.levels: AA HL and SL, with HL extension topics
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration techniques, then their application in optimisation and kinematics. At Higher Level the extension material is where the final marks of long questions sit, which makes it the most common gap between a 6 and a 7.

subjects.name: Proof and reasoning
subjects.description: Proof by induction, contradiction and counterexample. Rarely a large number of marks and frequently the difference at the top, because it is the part of the paper most students have practised least and it cannot be improvised in the exam.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: All four courses, weighted towards AI
subjects.description: Distributions, hypothesis testing and conditional probability. The AI courses go further, and the losses there are nearly always interpretation: the correct test performed and no conclusion written in the context of the question.

subjects.name: Modelling
subjects.description: Choosing a function to fit a situation, justifying the choice, and judging the model's limitations. Marks come from the justification and the critique, not the fitting, which is why strong calculator users still lose marks here.

subjects.name: Graphic display calculator technique
subjects.levels: All four courses, on the calculator paper
subjects.description: Solving numerically, using statistical functions, reading intersections and storing values accurately. Speed matters: students who work slowly on this paper run out of time on the later questions, and that is a technique problem rather than a mathematics one.

subjects.name: Vectors, matrices and complex numbers
subjects.description: Content that is taught late in DP2 in many Dubai schools and is therefore thin at mock time. A low mock mark in these topics usually reflects teaching order rather than ability, and the right response is to note it and plan for it.

subjects.name: The exploration
subjects.levels: All four courses, 20 marks across five criteria
subjects.description: Criteria A to E cover presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. The last of these carries the largest single allocation, and students routinely lose it by choosing a topic that cannot sustain mathematics at the level of their course.

subjects.name: Paper 3 extended response
subjects.description: Two long investigation-style questions that build across multiple parts. Students lose marks by treating each part as separate rather than following the structure the question is setting up, and that pattern is learnable with practice.

subjects.name: Command terms and method presentation
subjects.description: Method marks are awarded for working that is written down, and 'hence' means the previous result must be used. Dubai mock scripts are full of correct answers with no visible method, and recovering those marks is the fastest improvement available in this subject.

sections.heading: The four courses and their papers, side by side
paragraphs: Families frequently arrive asking for help with 'IB Maths', which is four different requests. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic and analytic route, expected by most engineering, physics, mathematics and many economics programmes. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling and statistics route, suited to students heading for business, social sciences, design and many life science programmes. Both exist at Higher and Standard Level, and the Higher Levels are substantial courses by any measure.

The assessment shape is what drives a revision plan. Standard Level students sit two papers; Higher Level students sit three, the third being a shorter extended-response paper built from long multi-part investigations. The exploration is internally assessed in all four routes and carries 20 marks against five criteria. The weightings below are the shape as taught in Dubai schools at the time of writing; confirm them against your child's current subject guide, because the IB revises documents and the school's copy governs.

What matters practically is that one paper is sat without a calculator and one with it, which splits the subject into two different skills. A student who has done all their classwork on a graphic display calculator can appear competent all year and then lose a third of the available marks on the paper that takes the calculator away. The reverse happens too: students who are strong algebraically but slow with technology run out of time on the calculator paper and leave later questions blank.

That split is why we diagnose by paper before anything else. Two students with the same grade 5 may need opposite work, and the only way to know is to look at both papers' scripts. Where a school has only set one paper in a mock, the diagnosis is incomplete and we say so rather than guess.

sections.heading: The exploration criteria, letter by letter
paragraphs: The exploration is the one part of a Mathematics grade where the student sets the conditions, and it is also the part most often written in a hurry against an extended internal deadline. It is marked out of 20 across five criteria, lettered A to E, and the allocations are not equal. Knowing which criterion carries the most marks changes how a student spends their time, and almost no student we meet has read the descriptors before choosing a topic.

The table below sets out the criteria and what each rewards. Verify the current mark allocations against your child's subject guide, since the school's copy is authoritative and the IB does revise its documents. The important structural point holds regardless: the use of mathematics criterion carries the largest single allocation, which means the topic has to be capable of sustaining mathematics at the level of the course. A beautifully presented exploration built on arithmetic cannot score well in a Higher Level course, however much personal engagement it shows.

The commonest failure we see in Dubai explorations is topic choice made for interest alone. A student passionate about football chooses a football topic, discovers after three weeks that the available mathematics is descriptive statistics, and cannot reach the level required. Testing the topic against criterion E before any writing begins takes one session and prevents a term of wasted effort. That single conversation is the highest-value hour in the whole subject.

The second commonest failure is reflection treated as a conclusion. The reflection criterion wants the student to evaluate their own mathematics, acknowledge limitations and consider extensions, which is a different activity from summarising what was done. It is a small allocation, but it is routinely scored at zero or one by students who wrote a competent exploration and then stopped.

sections.heading: Where the last marks go on each paper
paragraphs: Students aiming at a 7 in Mathematics usually lose marks in four identifiable places, and none of them is a topic. The first is unwritten method. Method marks exist for working that appears on the page; a correct answer with no working earns the answer mark alone, and a wrong answer with no working earns nothing at all. Dubai mock scripts routinely show a student who understood the question and scored two marks out of six for it.

The second is the final parts of long questions. Questions are built to escalate, and the last part often requires the previous result. The word 'hence' is an instruction, and ignoring it costs the marks even when the answer arrives by another route. Students who stop when the routine work runs out are leaving a predictable number of marks on the table in every paper they sit.

The third is calculator efficiency, and it is almost invisible until it is measured. On the calculator paper, speed determines how many later questions get attempted. A student who takes four minutes to set up a statistical calculation that should take one is losing marks at the end of the paper for a reason that has nothing to do with mathematics. Timed practice with the specific model of calculator fixes this faster than anything else on this list.

The fourth is exact-value discipline on the non-calculator paper: surds left unsimplified, logarithms evaluated approximately, answers given as decimals where an exact form was required. Each individual loss is one mark. Across a paper it is a grade. All four of these are diagnosable from a marked script in one session, which is why we ask for the script before the first lesson rather than during it.

sections.heading: What Mathematics coaching costs in Dubai, cheapest first
paragraphs: Taking the market from the bottom up rather than the top down is more useful here, because Mathematics is the subject where the cheapest options are most heavily advertised. At the budget end of the published Dubai market, read in October 2026, Tutopiya lists from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Those rates buy homework support from a capable graduate, and for a Standard Level student who needs someone to keep them working through exercises, that may be exactly the right purchase.

The next band up, qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300 an hour, is where syllabus-specific teaching starts. Unitors publishes from AED 200 for IB. At this level a tutor knows the paper structures and the mark schemes, which is the minimum for work aimed at a 7. Above that, IB specialists are published at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate reaching AED 450 and above, and one premium provider publishing AED 650.

In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 an hour, with the travel inside the rate. Monthly comparisons in the market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work.

For Mathematics specifically, the band that matters depends on the job. A student needing content coverage can be well served in the middle band. A student at a 6 trying to reach a 7, or one writing a Higher Level exploration, needs the specialist band, because the work is criteria-level and paper-specific. We publish no rate card on these pages; the figure depends on course, level and whether the exploration is in scope, and it is confirmed after the free trial lesson.

sections.heading: Why Mathematics works well on a shared screen
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject where the objection to online tutoring is heard most often and holds least. The work is written, step by step, and the question is whether the tutor can see the student's writing as it happens. On a shared screen with a writing tablet or a document camera, they can, and they can annotate it in the same moment. What the tutor is watching for is precisely what a parent cannot see: whether the method is being written down, whether the notation is consistent, whether the student jumps to an answer.

The second advantage is the record. Every annotated page is saved, so by the spring of DP2 a student has a file of their own corrected long questions with the specific error marked on each. For a subject where the losses are habitual rather than topical, that archive is more useful than any textbook, and it does not exist when the work is done on paper in a kitchen.

In-home Mathematics tutoring in Dubai is a large market with published rates of roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour. Part of that is travel. The structural limit is the pool: a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches specialist who can mark Paper 3 is a narrow category, and the subset of that category willing to drive to a specific Dubai community at 6pm is narrower still. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India, and all UAE sessions are one-to-one over live video.

The honest exception is younger children, for whom physical presence does real work in keeping attention on task. A Diploma Mathematics student is not in that category. What they need is someone who knows where the marks are, available at a time that fits a Dubai school week, and able to see their written method as they produce it.

sections.heading: The exploration and academic honesty
paragraphs: The exploration must be the student's own work, and in Mathematics the temptation to cross that line is unusually strong because the output is a document. The IB's position is clear and so is ours. A tutor may discuss a topic, point out whether the mathematics can reach the level of the course, explain what each criterion rewards, teach a technique the student needs, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write it, produce the mathematics for it, or edit it into shape.

There is a specific market reason to be explicit. At least one provider ranking for UAE IB queries sells completed Internal Assessments, at around AED 3,750. A student who submits purchased work risks a malpractice finding, which can cost the Diploma rather than the subject grade. In Mathematics the risk is compounded because the mathematics itself is traceable: an exploration using techniques the student cannot explain is identifiable in a two-minute conversation with a teacher.

A practical test for parents: ask the student to explain, without notes, why their exploration uses the method it uses and what its limitations are. That is the reflection criterion restated as a question, and a student who has done their own work answers it easily. A student who cannot answer it has a problem that no grade compensates for.

On materials, we link to official IB documents and publishers rather than redistributing subject guides, mark schemes or grade boundary tables. The school's own copies of the subject guide and criteria sheets are the authoritative versions, and the subject teacher is the right route to them.

sections.heading: Starting Mathematics work, course and paper first
paragraphs: Send four things: which course, which level, the most recent marked paper, and whether the exploration has been started. Those four answers determine everything. Without the course and level we cannot even tell you whether the right specialist exists; without the script we cannot tell you which paper is costing the marks; and the exploration question frequently changes the priority order entirely, because an unstarted exploration with a deadline in six weeks outranks paper practice.

Availability is worth saying plainly. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is the tightest match we make in Dubai, and it tightens further between late November and early February when every school's mock returns at once. If the specialist is not free, we will tell you the realistic wait rather than offer a Standard Level tutor for Higher Level work. Where a tutor outside the UAE covers the course at the same online format and Gulf-time scheduling, we say so, because concealing where a tutor sits is a trust failure common in this market.

The trial lesson is free and the only condition is finding a time. For Mathematics we use it on a real question from the student's own marked paper, with the shared screen and writing tablet set up, because that also tests the practical side: whether the student can work comfortably in that format. Most can within ten minutes; a few prefer a different setup, and it is better to discover that in a free hour.

After that the plan is built around the paper diagnosis and the exploration deadline, reviewed at week three against new marked work, and narrowed as the predictable losses disappear. We will tell you when the remaining gap is content that needs the school's teaching rather than more tutoring, which happens most often with topics taught late in DP2 such as vectors or complex numbers.

faqs.question: What is the difference between IB Maths AA and AI for a Dubai student?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic and analytic route, built around functions, calculus and, at Higher Level, proof. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling and statistics route, built around fitting models to situations and interpreting them in context. Most engineering, physics and mathematics degrees expect Analysis and Approaches; business, social science and design programmes commonly accept either. Both exist at Higher and Standard Level. A student can be genuinely strong at one and ordinary at the other, which is why a revision plan written for the wrong course wastes months of work.

faqs.question: Which paper should we focus on to move from a 6 to a 7?
faqs.answer: Whichever one the marked scripts say, and the answer is often the opposite of what the family expects. One paper is sat without a calculator and one with it, and those are different skills. Students who do all their classwork on a graphic display calculator can lose a large share of the non-calculator paper, while strong algebraists sometimes run out of time on the calculator paper because setup is slow. At Higher Level, Paper 3 is a third distinct skill: long investigations that build across their parts. We diagnose by paper before planning anything.

faqs.question: How is the Mathematics exploration marked?
faqs.answer: Out of 20 marks across five criteria, lettered A to E: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. The allocations are not equal, and use of mathematics carries the largest single share, which is why the topic has to be capable of sustaining mathematics at the level of the course. Your child's subject guide holds the current descriptors and allocations, and the school's copy governs. Testing a topic against those criteria before any writing begins is the single most useful session available in this subject.

faqs.question: My child chose an exploration topic they love but the maths is thin. What now?
faqs.answer: Change the topic or change the angle, and do it immediately rather than after another draft. The use of mathematics criterion carries the largest allocation, and a topic that only supports descriptive statistics cannot score well in a Higher Level course however engaged the student is. Often the subject can be kept and the question narrowed to a part that admits real mathematics: optimisation, a modelled relationship, a probability structure. One session is usually enough to find that angle, and the alternative is a term of work capped at a low band.

faqs.question: Can my child reach a 7 if they are currently at a 5?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the script decides. A 5 made up of unwritten method, calculator slowness and missed final parts of long questions is largely technique, and technique moves quickly. A 5 made up of genuine content gaps across functions and calculus is a longer piece of work, usually a year rather than a term. The useful answer comes from looking at both papers rather than from the grade, and we would rather tell you the realistic target from the evidence than attach an ambitious label to the work.

faqs.question: How much does IB Maths tutoring cost in Dubai at each level of the market?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates read in October 2026 start at the budget end with Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Qualified online subject tutors run AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing from AED 200 for IB. IB specialists are published at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and one premium provider at AED 650. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the rate. Those are other providers' figures; ours depends on course, level and whether the exploration is in scope.

faqs.question: Is the cheapest band ever the right choice for Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Yes, for a specific job. A Standard Level student who understands the content but will not sit down and work through exercises is well served by an affordable tutor who keeps them working, and paying specialist rates for that is waste. The budget band stops being appropriate the moment the work is about mark schemes, paper technique or the exploration criteria, because those require someone who knows the assessment rather than the mathematics alone. Matching the band to the job is most of the value in this decision, and most pages in this market never mention it.

faqs.question: Does a graphic display calculator model matter for practice?
faqs.answer: It matters more than families expect. Speed on the calculator paper determines how many of the later questions get attempted, and speed is model-specific: menu paths, statistical functions and storing values all differ. A student who practises on a different model from the one they will sit the exam with loses time on the day for no mathematical reason. Sessions therefore use the student's own model, and part of the early work is often timing routine setups until they take seconds rather than minutes.

faqs.question: My child's mock covered vectors and they scored nothing. Should we panic?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Vectors, matrices and complex numbers are taught late in DP2 at many Dubai schools, so a mock that included them tested content the student had barely met. The mark understates the position. The right response is to confirm with the subject teacher when those topics are being taught and to plan tutoring around that schedule rather than to pay for pre-teaching the whole topic. Where the school's sequence leaves a topic very late, a short block just after it is taught is better value than a block before.

faqs.question: How does online Maths tutoring handle written working?
faqs.answer: Through a shared screen with a writing tablet or a document camera, so the tutor watches the method being produced rather than seeing a finished answer. That matters because the largest recoverable loss in Dubai Mathematics scripts is correct thinking with no working written down, and it is only diagnosable by watching. Every annotated page is saved, so across the Diploma a student accumulates a file of their own corrected long questions with the specific error marked on each, which is a better revision resource than a textbook.

faqs.question: Do you send a Maths tutor to our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE tutoring one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. For Mathematics the limiting factor is the pool: a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches specialist who can mark Paper 3 to criteria is a narrow category, and the subset willing to drive to a given Dubai community in the early evening is narrower still. In-home rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour also carry travel inside them, which buys movement rather than teaching.

faqs.question: When should we start thinking about the exploration?
faqs.answer: A term before the school's internal deadline, and earlier than most Dubai students do. Internal deadlines cluster in the same months as mocks and other subjects' Internal Assessments, which is why so many explorations are written against an extended deadline in a rush. The early work is cheap and decisive: read the criteria, test two or three candidate topics against the use of mathematics criterion, and pick the one that can sustain course-level mathematics. That is one or two sessions, and it prevents the most expensive failure in the subject.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Mathematics and Physics for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it can work well because the two subjects share technique: data handling, unit discipline, method presentation. The caution is depth at Higher Level. A tutor strong in Higher Level Mathematics and generally capable in Physics is not the same as a Higher Level Physics specialist who can handle the option topic and Paper 3 data analysis. For boundary work we would rather use two specialists than one generalist, and for content coverage one tutor across both is often the better use of a budget.

faqs.question: What should we ask the Maths teacher after a disappointing paper?
faqs.answer: Four questions. Which paper lost the most marks, and was it method or content? Were marks lost for working that was not shown? Which topics in this paper are still to be taught properly? And is the exploration on track against the internal deadline? Also ask for the mark scheme alongside the script, which is a normal request. Those answers tell an outside tutor more than any report comment, and they frequently reveal that the problem is habitual rather than topical, which is the cheaper problem to fix.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level Maths manageable for a student who took ordinary IGCSE Maths?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a bridging block and realistic expectations. The clearest predictor of a comfortable start in Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level among Dubai students is whether they sat Additional Mathematics 0606 or Further Pure 4PM1 alongside their main IGCSE. Students who did not can still succeed, but usually need work over the summer before DP1 on algebraic fluency and calculus foundations, and a standing weekly hour through DP1 rather than a repair block in DP2. Starting early is both cheaper and more effective here than catching up later.

dubai/ib-7-in-maths-coaching.closingHeading: Tell us the course, the paper and the exploration
dubai/ib-7-in-maths-coaching.closingBody: Four facts shape everything in this subject: which of the four Mathematics courses, which level, which paper is costing the marks, and where the exploration stands. Send those with the most recent marked script and we will tell you whether the right specialist is free, what the plan should contain, and in what order. Each one works live online with Dubai students and is matched to the course your child's school has entered them for.

intro.heading: Three Arabic courses, three very different hourly rates
paragraphs: Parents in Dubai who ask what an IB Arabic tutor costs are usually given a single number, and that single number is the reason so many first bookings go wrong. Arabic inside the Diploma Programme is not one subject. A child who arrived in Dubai at thirteen with no Arabic sits ab initio, where the work is script, high-frequency vocabulary and five hundred words of controlled writing. A child who has had Arabic as an additional language since Year 2 sits Arabic B, where the listening paper punishes a weak ear far more than a weak grammar table. A child from an Arabic-speaking household sits Arabic A: Language and Literature, where the examiner wants a reading of a text, not evidence of fluency. The tutor who is excellent at the first of those three is often the wrong person for the third, and the hourly rate moves with the scarcity of the skill rather than with the hours in the week.

That is why this page leads with money. Market rates in Dubai for Arabic support run roughly AED 150 to AED 250 an hour online for ab initio and MYP phase work, AED 200 to AED 350 for Arabic B at Higher Level, and AED 250 to AED 450 where the course is Arabic A and the tutor has to be literate in classical and modern literary registers. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts specialist IB and IGCSE tuition at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350, and TutorChase publishes AED 270 for its own tutors. Unitors is the only researched agency that prints a floor at all, at AED 200 for IB. Those are the figures a Dubai parent is actually comparing, and they are quoted here with the provider named rather than dressed up as our own price list.

The second thing that moves the number is the part of the course being taught. An hour spent drilling Paper 2 listening is cheaper to deliver than an hour of oral rehearsal, because oral work needs a tutor who can respond in Arabic at speed and then switch into English to explain why the answer lost marks. Internal assessment and Extended Essay supervision in Arabic is scarcer again. Dubai has a deep pool of Arabic teachers and a thin pool of Arabic teachers who have examined or taught the Language A literature course, and the price follows that thinness rather than any claim about quality.

There is also a layer most tutoring pages ignore completely. Every private school in Dubai, whatever curriculum it is licensed for, must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies under KHDA requirements, with those requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA counts mandatory-subject time in forty-minute lesson units, requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibits combined classes for the two groups. So an IB student in Dubai often carries two Arabic obligations at once: the Diploma course they are graded on and the school subject the regulator requires. Families routinely book tuition for the wrong one.

IB Gram delivers all of this as one-to-one tuition over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. The argument for online here is not a cost argument alone. A Jumeirah family that insists on someone at the door is choosing from the Arabic A specialists who happen to live within a thirty-minute drive on a weekday evening. Online, the same family chooses from everyone who can teach that course at all, and pays for teaching rather than for Sheikh Zayed Road at six o'clock.

dubai/ib-arabic-tutor.programmesIntro: Arabic runs through every IB programme a Dubai school offers, and it changes character at each transition. The four blocks below set out what Arabic looks like in each one and what that means for a family deciding whether to buy tuition hours now or in two years.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Arabic in the Diploma sits in Group 1 or Group 2. Group 2 holds Arabic ab initio at Standard Level and Arabic B at Standard and Higher Level; Group 1 holds Arabic A: Language and Literature and, in a handful of Dubai schools, Arabic A: Literature. The assessment split is published by the IB per course, and under the current language syllabuses a Language B candidate faces a writing paper, a combined listening and reading paper and an individual oral, while a Language A candidate faces guided textual analysis, a comparative essay and an oral on a global issue.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Group 1 Arabic cohort is small at most schools, which has two consequences for a parent. Class teaching is often shared across SL and HL in one room, and a weak reader is harder to spot early. Tuition hours at this level are the most expensive Arabic hours in the market, roughly AED 250 to AED 450 online, because the person has to be comfortable with literary criticism in Arabic and able to explain it in the language of the school's report card.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Arabic is organised as Language Acquisition in six phases, or as Language and Literature for students working at first-language standard. Phases are not year groups: a student can sit in Phase 2 for three years if nothing changes. Assessment runs on four criteria, with comprehension of spoken and written text weighted alongside production, so a student who speaks confidently but cannot handle an unseen written passage will see criterion marks that look inconsistent to a parent.
programmes.countryNote: Phase placement is where Dubai families lose the most ground. A child placed in Phase 2 in Year 7 because the family speaks Arabic at home, then never moved, arrives in DP1 with a spoken register and no academic reading. MYP Arabic tuition in Dubai runs roughly AED 120 to AED 200 an hour online, which is the cheapest point in the whole sequence to fix a problem that costs three times as much to fix in Year 12.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: PYP Arabic is taught as an additional language for most non-Arab students and as a first language where the school streams for it. There is no external assessment, which makes progress hard for a parent to read. The useful markers at this stage are script fluency, whether the child can decode unfamiliar words rather than recognise memorised ones, and whether listening comprehension is keeping pace with spoken production.
programmes.countryNote: Because KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups in Arabic as a first language, a Dubai primary child may be streamed on arrival into a group that does not match their actual level, particularly if the household language is Arabic but the previous school was English-medium. A short block of tuition at PYP rates, around AED 120 to AED 180 an hour, is usually spent on evidence for a re-streaming conversation rather than on content.

programmes.name: Mandatory UAE subjects alongside the IB
programmes.ageRange: All year groups in Dubai private schools
programmes.description: Separate from the IB course, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided weekly totals are met, and the guidance advises no mandatory lesson should be shorter than twenty-five minutes. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited.
programmes.countryNote: This matters to a Dubai parent in one concrete way: a tutor cannot invent a syllabus for these lessons. Support has to work from what the school is teaching, because the content is set and the school is accountable for it. We treat mandatory-subject tuition as exam-technique and comprehension work on the school's own material, and we say so before the first session rather than after it.

dubai/ib-arabic-tutor.subjectsIntro: Arabic tuition is only useful when it is matched to the exact course. These are the Arabic and Arabic-adjacent courses Dubai students bring to us, with what each one actually assesses and the point at which marks usually leak away.

subjects.name: Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: For students with little or no prior Arabic. Three prescribed themes, controlled writing tasks and a listening paper built on slow, clearly enunciated audio. Marks are lost on script accuracy, on confusing the sun and moon letters in reading aloud, and on writing that answers the prompt in the wrong text type.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Writing, a combined listening and reading paper and an individual oral based on a visual stimulus. The listening component is the single biggest source of unexpected low marks for Dubai students, because classroom Arabic is slower and more forgiving than examination audio.

subjects.name: Arabic A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided analysis of an unseen literary or non-literary text, a comparative essay on studied works and an oral on a global issue. Fluent speakers lose marks here for describing a text rather than analysing how it produces meaning, and for quoting at length without commentary.

subjects.name: Arabic A: Literature
subjects.description: Offered by a smaller set of Dubai schools. Works in translation sit alongside Arabic originals, and the HL essay demands a sustained line of argument over 1,200 to 1,500 words. Tutors here are scarce in the UAE market, which is visible in the rate.

subjects.name: MYP Arabic Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Four assessment criteria covering listening, reading, speaking and writing. The common pattern in Dubai is a strong speaking criterion mark propping up a weak reading mark, which masks the gap until DP entry testing exposes it.

subjects.name: MYP Arabic Language and Literature
subjects.description: For students at first-language standard. Analytical writing about texts, in Arabic, with criteria that reward structure and terminology. This is the natural feeder to Arabic A, and a student who has not written analytically here will find DP1 brutal.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first language (KHDA mandatory)
subjects.description: Required of Arab students in Dubai private schools and taught in separate classes from non-Arab groups. Standard Arabic is the language of instruction. Report grades here are a school judgement rather than an external one, which makes them easy for parents to misread.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language (KHDA mandatory)
subjects.description: Required of non-Arab students in Dubai private schools. Weekly time is counted in forty-minute units. Tuition here is about keeping pace with the school's own scheme of work, since additional content needs Ministry of Education permission.

subjects.name: Islamic Education
subjects.description: Taught in Standard Arabic for Arab students and in the school's curriculum language for non-Arab students. KHDA requires separate classes for the two groups and requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the relevant approval from KHDA to teach these subjects.

subjects.name: UAE Social Studies and Moral Education
subjects.description: Arabic is the primary language of instruction for Arab students; non-Arab students follow Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the curriculum language. Content is fixed, so support is comprehension, vocabulary and structured written answers rather than new material.

subjects.name: Arabic for the Extended Essay
subjects.description: An essay written in Arabic, or about an Arabic text, needs a supervisor who can read the sources. Our role is question framing, source evaluation and feedback on the student's own successive drafts, with the student as sole author throughout.

subjects.name: Arabic oral and interview preparation
subjects.description: Structured rehearsal for the individual oral: stimulus description, unprepared follow-up questions, register control. Recorded so the student hears their own hesitation markers, which is the fastest fix available in oral assessment.

regions.note: The heaviest concentration of Arabic A demand in the city, from Emirati and Arab expatriate households whose children need literary Arabic rather than conversational. Local in-home quotes here sit at the top of the Dubai band, AED 300 and above, partly because the pool of Language A specialists is small.

regions.note: Dense with large international schools and with non-Arab families who need ab initio and additional-language support rather than literature. Rates quoted locally are nearer the AED 150 to AED 250 online band, and the common booking is a short Phase 2 to Phase 4 catch-up block.

regions.note: Strong Arab-expatriate enrolment, so first-language streams are full and competition for Arabic A tuition hours is real in exam term. Families here are the most likely to be choosing between the school's mandatory Arabic grade and the DP course grade, and to need both explained.

regions.note: Apartment living and long commutes make in-home Arabic tuition expensive in practice: a tutor crossing from Deira at 6pm is charging for the car as much as the lesson. This is where the online argument lands hardest, and where ab initio is the dominant request.

sections.heading: What an IB Arabic tutor in Dubai actually costs, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Online one-to-one Arabic tuition in Dubai is quoted at roughly AED 150 to AED 450 an hour as of October 2026, and the single biggest determinant is the course rather than the tutor's seniority. Ab initio and MYP phase work sits at the bottom of that band. Arabic B at Higher Level sits in the middle. Arabic A: Language and Literature sits at the top, because the person has to be able to analyse a literary text in Arabic and then explain the analysis in the language of the school report. Nothing else about the booking changes the price as much as that one fact, which is why a quote given before the course is identified is close to meaningless.

Three other variables move the number in Dubai specifically. Format: in-home one-to-one across the city is quoted at AED 180 to AED 350 by Bestimate's 2026 rate table and up to AED 500 by individual home tutors, and a meaningful part of that premium is travel rather than teaching. Timing: the 4.30pm to 7.30pm window is the one every family wants, so the scarcest tutors price it accordingly, and a 9am Friday slot is routinely cheaper for the same person. Season: demand concentrates in the eight weeks before the May session, and the Arabic A pool in the UAE is small enough that late bookings simply do not get the specialist they wanted at any price.

What does not move the number, despite being sold hard, is package length. A twenty-hour block at a discount is only cheaper if all twenty hours get used, and families who buy before a diagnostic frequently find that six of those hours should have gone to the oral component and fourteen to reading. We quote the market bands here because no competitor in this search result publishes an AED figure at all: three of the six ranked pages show no price, and the two that do quote in US dollars. A parent comparing options in Dubai is comparing dirhams, so the dirham figures belong on the page with the provider named.

sections.heading: Which Arabic course is your child actually sitting?
paragraphs: This is the question that determines everything else, and a surprising number of Dubai families cannot answer it with certainty in October of DP1. The school knows, the student half knows, and the parent is often working from a timetable line that just says Arabic. Before buying a single hour, get the course name and level in writing from the school: Arabic ab initio SL, Arabic B SL, Arabic B HL, Arabic A: Language and Literature SL or HL, or Arabic A: Literature. The difference between the second and the fifth of those is not a matter of difficulty. They are different disciplines with different examiners looking for different things.

The routing is partly about prior learning and partly about household language, and the two often disagree. A student from an Arabic-speaking family who attended English-medium schools from Year 1 may speak at near-native level and read at Phase 3 level. Put that student into Arabic A and the oral goes well and the guided textual analysis collapses. Put them into Arabic B HL and the listening paper is trivially easy while the writing task exposes a register problem nobody has ever corrected. Neither placement is wrong in principle; both need to be made with evidence, which means an unseen reading passage and a timed written response, not a conversation.

Switching is possible but it is expensive in hours rather than in fees. A move from Arabic A to Arabic B in DP1 means learning a different set of text types and a different oral format with eighteen months to go. A move from Arabic B HL to SL reduces the reading load but not the listening demand. Our first session on any Arabic booking is a diagnostic for exactly this reason, and if the diagnostic says the school's placement is right, that is a useful hour too: it stops the family from spending a term on the wrong fix.

sections.heading: The Arabic a Dubai school must teach, and the Arabic the IB grades
paragraphs: Dubai is unusual among IB markets because the regulator sets a parallel Arabic requirement. Under KHDA's mandatory-subjects guidelines, Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with the requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, and April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. The guidance counts instructional time in forty-minute lesson units, allows schools to vary lesson length provided weekly totals are met, and advises that no mandatory-subject lesson should run shorter than twenty-five minutes.

Two of KHDA's rules have direct practical consequences for tuition. The first is streaming: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, and combined classes for the two groups are prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. The second is content: for the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited. A tutor who promises a better syllabus for these lessons is describing something a Dubai school cannot accept.

So a family can end up holding two Arabic grades that tell different stories. The mandatory subject grade is a school judgement against a set national curriculum, delivered in Standard Arabic for Arab students and in the school's curriculum language for non-Arab students in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies. The IB grade is an external judgement against a published assessment model. A student can be comfortable in one and in trouble in the other, and the honest answer to which one to tune is usually the one with the external examination attached, because that is the grade that travels. KHDA also requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the relevant approval from KHDA to teach those subjects, which is a credential question worth asking your school directly.

sections.heading: Where Arabic marks actually leak away
paragraphs: In Arabic B and ab initio the loss is concentrated in listening. Classroom Arabic is slower, repeated, and supported by a teacher's face and gesture. Examination audio is none of those things, and a student who has only ever listened to their own teacher will hear the first thirty seconds and then lose the thread. The fix is mechanical rather than clever: listen at full pace from the first tutoring session, pause nothing on the first pass, and build vocabulary from the words that were actually missed instead of from a printed list. Six weeks of that moves a listening mark more reliably than a term of grammar.

In Arabic A the loss is interpretive. A fluent speaker reads the unseen passage, understands every word, and writes a summary. The examiner wanted an account of how the text produces its effect: the choice of register, the structure, the imagery, the implied reader. Fluency is what makes this trap so effective, because the student feels successful while writing the wrong kind of answer. The remedy is a repeated drill on the gap between what a text says and how it says it, with the student's own paragraphs marked against the published criteria rather than against a model answer.

In the oral, across every course, the loss is in the unprepared section. Students rehearse the stimulus description until it is fluent and then fall apart on the examiner's follow-up questions, which are the part that cannot be scripted. The intervention that works is uncomfortable and quick: unprepared questioning from session one, recorded, with the student listening back to their own hesitations. The third variety of loss is pure process, and it costs more marks in Dubai than anyone admits. Mandatory-subject deadlines, school internal assessment dates and the DP timeline collide in DP1, and the student who is behind on a school Arabic project borrows time from DP preparation. Sequencing that calendar is part of what a tutor is for.
