sections.heading: The Diploma Arabic year, counted backwards
paragraphs: Nobody in this search result publishes a calendar, which is strange, because every decision a family makes about Arabic tuition is a decision about timing. The IB's own session dates and results dates are published by the IB and should be confirmed with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org before you plan around them; this page deliberately does not restate an IB date it cannot verify. What can be set out is the sequence, counted backwards from the May session that Dubai schools sit, because the sequence is stable even when the dates move.

Working back from the examinations themselves: the final weeks are paper practice at speed, not content. Before that sits the window where the school's predicted grades are formed, and a student whose listening mark is weak should have fixed it before that judgement is made rather than after. Before that sit the internal deadlines for the oral components and for any Group 1 or Group 2 coursework, which in most Dubai schools fall in the first half of DP2. Before that, in DP1, sits the only comfortable window there is for a course change, and the only cheap window for fixing a reading gap carried up from MYP.

The practical consequence is a buying pattern, not a sales pitch. Families who book Arabic support in DP1 buy one hour a week for a long time and spend less in total. Families who book in the February before the examinations buy two or three hours a week for eight weeks, pay a premium for scarce specialists, and get a smaller improvement because the components that respond fastest to tutoring are the ones already assessed. For Cambridge and Pearson candidates in the same household the pattern is documented more precisely, and it is worth reading across. A UAE Cambridge candidate sits the June series, with the November series available as the resit route; entries for the June papers close in the spring, several months before the first paper, and the exact deadline reaches the family on the centre's statement of entry rather than being something to guess at. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after working from the wrong zone timetable, so which version of the timetable the school used matters as much as the date printed on it.

sections.heading: Online versus in-home Arabic tuition in Dubai, honestly compared
paragraphs: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, so take the comparison below as a comparison of models rather than an advertisement. In-home Arabic tuition is a real and reasonable choice, especially for younger children and for students who need the physical presence of an adult to stay on task. It is quoted in Dubai at roughly AED 180 to AED 350 an hour by Bestimate's rate table, with individual home tutors quoting up to AED 500, and monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions advertised around AED 1,599 to AED 1,799.

What a Dubai family is actually buying with that premium is proximity, and proximity has a cost that does not appear on the invoice. The tutor who can reach Jumeirah Lake Towers at 6pm on a Tuesday is selected from the people who live near enough to do it, which for Arabic A: Language and Literature may be a pool of a handful across the whole emirate. Travel time also sets the session length: a tutor who has driven forty minutes will not sell a forty-five minute session, so families buy ninety minutes whether or not ninety minutes is the right dose for oral work.

Online, the selection constraint disappears and the scheduling constraint loosens. Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time, forty-five or sixty or ninety minutes as the work requires, with screen-sharing for annotated text work and recording for oral components. The real trade-offs are worth naming rather than hiding: a younger child needs a parent in earshot for the first few sessions, handwriting practice in Arabic script needs the student to photograph their work, and a weak internet connection ruins a listening exercise faster than anything else. Our position is simply that for a scarce, course-specific skill like Arabic A, choosing the teacher beats choosing the postcode.

sections.heading: What an Arabic tutor may and may not do with assessed work
paragraphs: This matters more in Arabic than in most subjects, because the language barrier makes it easy for a family to lose sight of who is producing the words. The IB's academic honesty rules make the student the sole author of every assessed piece, and a tutor who supplies sentences for an oral script, corrects a draft into fluency the student cannot reproduce, or supplies a ready-made commentary on a set text is creating a malpractice risk for the student rather than a grade advantage. The consequences land on the candidate, not on the tutor.

The boundary is workable and we state it plainly before the first session. A tutor can teach the assessment criteria and what each one rewards. A tutor can discuss the suitability of a global issue or an Extended Essay research question. A tutor can read the student's own draft and say where the argument is thin, where the register slips, where a quotation is unsupported by commentary. A tutor can model analysis on a different text entirely, so the technique transfers without the content being handed over. A tutor can mark a timed practice answer against the published descriptors.

What a tutor must not do is become the author. No supplied paragraphs, no translation of the student's English thinking into Arabic prose that becomes the submitted work, no line-by-line rewriting that leaves the student unable to explain their own choices. One of the pages competing for this search sells finished Internal Assessments outright at an advertised price; that is an integrity breach and we will not imitate it. If a family wants that, we are the wrong platform, and we would rather say so on the page than in a refund conversation. The practical test we use with Arabic students is simple: could the student defend every sentence, in Arabic, to their own teacher without notes?
bullets: Allowed: teaching the criteria, feedback on the student's own drafts, modelled analysis on other texts
Allowed: research-question framing, source evaluation, timed practice marked to the descriptors
Not allowed: supplied sentences, rewriting to completion, any form of authored submission
Our test: the student can defend every line of the work to their teacher, unaided

sections.heading: Arabic, MoE equivalency and the five-subject rule
paragraphs: Families in Dubai often assume Arabic is the gatekeeper for UAE university entry, and for the British curriculum track the published rule says something more specific. For equivalency of secondary certificates, students on the British track must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for that count.

That exclusion is worth reading twice, because it is the opposite of what most parents expect, and because a competing page in this cluster publishes a six-subject requirement that does not match the reported rule. It does not make Arabic optional in any practical sense: the subject is required in Dubai schools by the regulator, it appears on the school report, and it carries weight with the schools themselves. It simply means a family choosing between an extra IGCSE and an Arabic resit should know which one the equivalency count recognises before they spend tuition money on it.

For the IB track specifically, no points threshold is published on this page, because the figures circulating for IB equivalency could not be verified against a Ministry of Education source. Check moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority directly, and treat any tutoring provider quoting an IB equivalency number without a citation with caution. The American-track requirements are documented: English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics through at least 450 in the SAT Math test. Equivalency is a process the authority runs, not a service a tutoring platform performs, and no tutoring is required for it.

sections.heading: Ramadan, prayer times and when an Arabic session actually happens
paragraphs: The Dubai school year has rhythms that a generic tutoring timetable ignores, and Arabic is the subject most affected, partly because of who studies it and partly because of when it gets studied. During Ramadan, school days shorten, energy in the late afternoon drops sharply, and the productive window for a demanding oral session moves to after Iftar. Families who try to hold a 5pm slot through Ramadan usually lose three or four sessions to fatigue and rescheduling, which is money spent on a calendar rather than on teaching.

The practical answer is to move the slot rather than pause the work. Post-Iftar sessions, typically between 8.30pm and 10pm, work well for oral rehearsal and reading, and less well for timed writing. Early morning weekend sessions are the other option, and a 9am Saturday hour is often easier to protect than a weekday evening in any season. Because tuition runs online, moving a slot is a calendar change rather than a renegotiation with someone's driving schedule, which is one of the quieter advantages of the format.

The rest of the year has its own pinch points. The long summer break creates a three-month gap in which listening skill degrades faster than anything else; two short sessions a month through July and August hold it in place at low cost. The weeks around National Day and the winter break collide with school internal assessment deadlines. Mid-term breaks are when families travel, and a tutor who can follow a student across time zones for two weeks is worth more than a cheaper tutor who cannot. We ask about the family's travel pattern before setting a schedule, because a slot that survives the year is worth more than a slot that looks ideal in October.

process.title: Send the course name, not just the subject
process.description: Tell us the exact course and level from the school: Arabic ab initio SL, Arabic B SL or HL, Arabic A: Language and Literature SL or HL, or the MYP phase. Add the school's own Arabic stream if the student carries a mandatory-subject grade too. This one detail determines the tutor, the plan and the rate band.

process.title: A trial lesson before any payment
process.description: The first session is a trial with a course specialist, run live online at a time that suits the family. It is a working lesson rather than a sales call: an unseen reading passage, a short timed write and a few minutes of unprepared speaking, so both sides can see where the student actually stands.

process.title: Diagnostic report and an hours estimate
process.description: After the trial you get a short written diagnosis: which component is weakest, whether the school's course placement looks right, and how many hours the fix plausibly needs. If the honest answer is six focused hours rather than a year of weekly sessions, that is what the note says.

process.title: Weekly sessions with written notes
process.description: Sessions run to the agreed slot on Gulf Standard Time, with a short note after each one covering what was done, what was marked and what to practise before the next. Recordings of oral work go to the student. Nothing about the schedule depends on traffic, so a changed week is a calendar edit.

process.title: Review at the point it matters
process.description: We review before the school forms predicted grades, and again six to eight weeks out from the live session, because those are the two moments when changing the plan still changes an outcome. If a different tutor is a better fit by then, we say so and arrange the switch rather than defend the original match.

whyPoints.title: Priced as the market, with the source named
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is a market band attributed to the provider or research that published it, not an IB Gram price list. Three of the six pages ranking for Dubai tutoring queries publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. A family comparing dirhams deserves dirhams and a citation.

whyPoints.title: Matched by Arabic course, not by language
whyPoints.description: An Arabic A: Language and Literature specialist and an ab initio teacher are doing different jobs, and the wrong match wastes a term before anyone notices. We route on the course code and level the school confirms, and we run a diagnostic in the first session to check that the school's own placement holds up.

whyPoints.title: The regulator's requirements treated as fact, not decoration
whyPoints.description: KHDA's mandatory-subject rules shape what Arabic tuition in Dubai can and cannot do: separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups, set content that cannot be substituted without Ministry permission, and forty-minute lesson units. We work inside those rules and explain them rather than selling around them.

whyPoints.title: Clear boundaries on assessed work
whyPoints.description: We teach the criteria, give feedback on the student's own drafts and mark timed practice. We do not supply sentences, rewrite work to completion or hand over a commentary. One page competing for this query sells finished Internal Assessments; the student carries that risk, which is reason enough never to copy it.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, and in-home tuition is a service we run only in India. Saying so on the page means no family discovers it after booking, and it is why the comparison table above includes formats we do not sell.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built around the Dubai year
whyPoints.description: Post-Iftar slots through Ramadan, Friday and weekend mornings when weekday evenings are full of sport, short holding sessions through the summer so listening does not decay, and a schedule that follows a travelling family across time zones. The slot that survives the whole year is the one that produces the grade.

faqs.question: How much does an IB Arabic tutor in Dubai charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai run roughly AED 150 to AED 450 an hour for online one-to-one Arabic tuition as of October 2026, and the course drives the figure more than the tutor's seniority does. Ab initio and MYP phase work sits near the bottom, Arabic B HL in the middle, and Arabic A: Language and Literature at the top because literary analysis in Arabic is a scarcer skill. In-home rates across Dubai are quoted at AED 180 to AED 350 by Bestimate's 2026 table, with some individual home tutors at AED 500. Those are market bands with the publisher named, not an IB Gram price list; our own terms start with a trial lesson.

faqs.question: Why does Arabic A: Language and Literature tuition cost more than ab initio?
faqs.answer: Because the two jobs need different people. Ab initio asks a tutor to build script, high-frequency vocabulary and controlled writing from a low base, which many competent Arabic teachers can do well. Arabic A asks for analysis of an unseen literary or non-literary text in Arabic, with the reasoning explained in the language of the school's report card, and for comparative essay work on studied authors. The UAE pool of teachers who can do that fluently is small, and the price reflects scarcity rather than a claim that one tutor is better than another. Expect roughly AED 250 to AED 450 an hour online for Arabic A against AED 150 to AED 250 for ab initio.

faqs.question: My child's Dubai school already teaches Arabic. Why would we pay for more?
faqs.answer: Often you should not. The school's Arabic lessons are a KHDA requirement with set content, and extra hours on the same material rarely change much. The cases where tuition earns its fee are narrower: the Diploma course grade is diverging from the school Arabic grade, the listening component is the weak link and nobody is drilling it at examination pace, the course placement looks wrong, or the oral is weeks away and the unprepared section has never been rehearsed. Our diagnostic session exists to tell you which of those applies, and it is a legitimate outcome for that session to conclude that no weekly tuition is needed.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the individual oral without scripting it for my child?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the distinction matters. A tutor can teach what the oral rewards, build a bank of stimulus material, rehearse the unprepared follow-up questioning that most students never practise, and record sessions so the student hears their own hesitation. What a tutor must not do is supply sentences for the student to memorise, because the student becomes unable to handle any question off the script and because authored material in an assessed component is a malpractice risk under IB rules. The work that actually raises an oral mark is unscripted practice under time pressure, which is also the work students avoid without a tutor in the room.

faqs.question: Is Arabic counted among the subjects the UAE Ministry of Education asks for in equivalency?
faqs.answer: For the British curriculum track, reported equivalency requirements say students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. A further Advanced Level subject at E, or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, is also required. That does not make Arabic optional, since Dubai schools must teach it under KHDA rules, but it changes the arithmetic for a family deciding where to spend tuition hours. Verify the current wording on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority before acting on it.

faqs.question: My child is Arab but has only been schooled in English. Which Arabic course fits?
faqs.answer: This is the single most common placement problem in Dubai, and it cannot be settled by household language. A student in this position usually speaks at a high level and reads several phases below it. Placed in Arabic A, the oral goes well and the guided textual analysis collapses; placed in Arabic B HL, the listening is easy while the written register exposes gaps nobody has corrected. The decision needs evidence rather than instinct: an unseen reading passage, a timed written response and a few minutes of analytical talk about a text. Our first session produces exactly that, and the written diagnosis is something you can take back to the school.

faqs.question: How many weekly Arabic sessions do Dubai Diploma families usually start with?
faqs.answer: One hour a week is the common starting point in DP1, and it is usually the right one, because the gains in Arabic come from steady reading and listening rather than from intensity. Families starting in DP2 with an examination in sight more often take two sessions a week, split so that one is component drilling and one is marked written work. Before the live session, six to eight weeks at two or three hours a week is a recognisable pattern. The honest caution is that the February sprint costs more per mark gained than the DP1 hour did, because the components that respond fastest to teaching have already been assessed by then.

faqs.question: Can Arabic lessons move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we recommend planning for it rather than reacting to it. School days shorten during Ramadan and late-afternoon concentration drops, so a 5pm slot usually bleeds into cancellations. Sessions between roughly 8.30pm and 10pm after Iftar work well for oral rehearsal and reading, while timed writing is better moved to a weekend morning. Because lessons run online, changing a slot is a calendar edit rather than a renegotiation around someone's travel. We ask about Ramadan timing, family travel and sports fixtures before setting a schedule, since a slot that survives the whole year is worth more than one that looks ideal in October.

faqs.question: Do sessions teach Modern Standard Arabic or Gulf dialect?
faqs.answer: Assessment work is in Modern Standard Arabic, because that is what the IB courses examine and what KHDA specifies as the language of instruction for Arabic as a first language and for Islamic Education for Arab students. Dialect still appears in sessions where it is useful: listening components sometimes carry regional colour, and a student living in Dubai hears Gulf and Levantine Arabic daily, which can interfere with written register. A good tutor names the difference explicitly rather than letting a student discover in an examination that the phrasing they use at home is not the phrasing the paper wants. Dialect coaching for family or social reasons is a different service and we say so.

faqs.question: What should an Arabic Extended Essay supervisor expect a tutor to do?
faqs.answer: The supervisor is the school's; a tutor works alongside that relationship, not instead of it. Useful tutor input is narrowing a research question until it is answerable in the word limit, judging whether the Arabic sources are substantial enough to sustain an argument, teaching how to handle quotation and translation, and giving feedback on the student's own successive drafts against the published criteria. What a tutor must not do is author or rewrite the essay, because the student must be the sole author of assessed work and the student carries the consequence if that is not true. A fair test: can the student explain every choice in the essay, in Arabic, without notes?

faqs.question: Is online Arabic tuition workable when the course is so oral-heavy?
faqs.answer: The oral components are the ones that transfer best to video, which surprises families. Recording is trivial online, so the student can hear their own filler words and self-corrections, and that single feedback loop moves an oral mark faster than anything else available. Screen-sharing suits annotated text work for Arabic A, and listening practice runs at genuine examination pace through headphones rather than through classroom speakers. The real constraints are worth naming: a weak connection ruins a listening exercise, handwriting practice in Arabic script needs the student to photograph their work, and a child under about ten needs a parent in earshot for the first few sessions.

faqs.question: Does an Arabic tutor in Dubai need a MoHRE private tuition work permit?
faqs.answer: An individual providing private tuition in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through MoHRE's smart app, website or e-services system, and MoHRE's own service page lists a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted here. Ask any tutor directly about their permit position.

faqs.question: What does Arabic support cost a Dubai family across the two Diploma years?
faqs.answer: Take the arithmetic rather than a package price. One hour a week of online Arabic B tuition at the mid-market band of roughly AED 250 an hour, across about 36 teaching weeks a year, is in the region of AED 9,000 a year before any exam-term intensification. Arabic A at AED 350 an hour on the same pattern runs materially higher; ab initio at AED 180 runs lower. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions in Dubai are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Those are market figures, not our quote.

faqs.question: What happens if no Arabic A specialist is free in Dubai evening hours?
faqs.answer: We tell you, before you pay, rather than substituting a general Arabic teacher and hoping. The Arabic A pool is genuinely small, and in the eight weeks before a live session it can be fully booked. The realistic options are then a different slot, often a weekend morning or an early evening before the peak window, a tutor in a different time zone whose availability fits a Dubai morning, or a shorter diagnostic-plus-marking arrangement where the student does the volume of work and the tutor marks it against the criteria. If none of those fits, that is a no from us, and we would rather say it than take the booking.

faqs.question: Can my child move from Arabic B HL to SL in DP1, and what does the switch cost in hours?
faqs.answer: Moving down a level inside the same course is the cheapest of all the switches, because the text types, the oral format and the paper structure stay familiar; what changes is reading volume and the literary works studied at Higher Level. Expect a handful of catch-up hours rather than a term. Moving between Arabic A and Arabic B is the expensive change, since the assessment model itself is different, and it is only comfortable in the first two terms of DP1. Any change is the school's decision under IB registration rules, so start with the coordinator, and get the diagnostic evidence first so the conversation is about the student's work rather than a preference.

dubai/ib-arabic-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the course code, then the rate
dubai/ib-arabic-tutor.closingBody: Send us the exact Arabic course and level your child's Dubai school has entered them for, along with the MYP phase or school Arabic stream if that is also in play. We will match a specialist in that course, run a trial lesson live online at a Gulf Standard Time slot that works around school, sport and Ramadan, and send a short written diagnosis of which component is weakest and how many hours the fix plausibly needs. If the honest answer is fewer hours than you expected, or a different course placement, that is what the note will say. Every AED figure on this page is a market band with its source named, so you can compare the Dubai market before you commit to anything.

dubai/ib-biology-ia-help.tutorsIntro: The tutors below supervise Biology investigations and work in the specialist band, because the service is statistical judgement rather than syllabus revision. Each will say in the first session whether a proposed design can support a test, and how many replicates that test will need.

intro.heading: In Biology the statistics decide the mark, and the sample size decides the cost
paragraphs: A Diploma Biology student submits one scientific investigation of up to about 3,000 words, marked out of twenty-four across four criteria of six marks each, worth roughly a fifth of the subject grade. The criteria are the same as in Physics and Chemistry. What is not the same is where the marks are actually won and lost, and in Biology that is almost entirely in how variation is handled.

Living material varies. Two leaves from the same plant, two seedlings from the same packet, two people's reaction times: the spread between them is often larger than the effect the student is trying to measure. That means a Biology investigation cannot reach a defensible conclusion by measuring carefully. It reaches one by measuring enough times, reporting the spread, and applying a test that says whether the difference observed is bigger than the variation would produce by chance.

This has a direct financial consequence, which is why this page leads with it. A student who designs with three replicates per level has produced data no test can carry, and the fix is not a tutoring session. It is another laboratory booking, another week, and in a Dubai school where individual investigation time competes with timetabled practicals, that may not be available before the deadline. The cheapest hour a family can buy on a Biology investigation is the one spent on design, before anything is grown, cut, timed or counted.

The market in Dubai prices this work in the specialist band for a reason that is about scarcity rather than branding. A great many tutors can teach the Biology syllabus well. Considerably fewer can look at a proposed design and say that it needs a chi-squared rather than a t-test, that five levels with five replicates will do and three will not, and that the error bars should show standard error rather than range. That second skill is what moves the mark, and it is what the specialist band is paying for.

Published Dubai rates, read in October 2026: Tutopiya from AED 33-52 an hour, EdFlik from AED 45-65, Unitors from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB, TutorChase at AED 270, Bestimate's specialist IB and IGCSE band at AED 200-450 and above, in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 with independent home tutors up to AED 500, and BartyED at AED 650. Monthly packages in the market include AED 799 for eight online sessions. None of those is our price list; they are what the market publishes, and a family should budget a Biology investigation as a four to six session block against those figures.

Delivery for UAE families is online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family's address is a service we run only in India. For statistical work the online format is better as well as cheaper, because the session is a spreadsheet and a test output on a shared screen, and the in-home band prices a commute into every hour of that.

dubai/ib-biology-ia-help.programmesIntro: Biology runs through the IB continuum, and the cost of supporting it tracks how scarce the needed skill is at each stage rather than how advanced the biology is.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Biology at standard or higher level, with the same scientific investigation at both and the same four criteria shared across the sciences. Statistical treatment is what separates a middling investigation from a strong one, and higher level adds syllabus content rather than a different task.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma Biology investigation support prices in Bestimate's specialist band of AED 200-450 and above in Dubai, because statistical judgement is the scarce component. A family comparing quotes should ask which test the tutor would propose for their child's design, and treat a vague answer as the answer.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Sciences assesses inquiring and designing and processing and evaluating across four criteria. Investigations are shorter and the statistics usually stop at means and ranges, so the skill required is more widely available.
programmes.countryNote: MYP science support sits closer to the general qualified-tutor band in Dubai, broadly AED 150-300 by Unitors' and Bestimate's published figures. Paying specialist rates for MYP investigation help is usually paying for scarcity that does not apply at that level.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A CP student taking Diploma Biology submits the same investigation against the same criteria, with the same statistical demands and therefore the same support cost. The core differs, with a reflective project instead of TOK and the Extended Essay.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is a minority route in Dubai. Where Biology is taken within it, budget as for a Diploma subject; the internally assessed requirement and its statistical demands do not reduce because the programme differs.

dubai/ib-biology-ia-help.subjectsIntro: Investigation topics differ enormously in how much laboratory time and how many replicates they need, and that is what determines the real cost of supporting them. These are the areas Dubai Biology students use most.

subjects.name: Enzyme activity and rate studies
subjects.description: Cheap, fast and repeatable, which makes adequate replication affordable. Catalase or amylase work gives enough data in one laboratory session to support a proper test, and the marks then hinge on controlling pH and temperature rather than mentioning them.

subjects.name: Osmosis and water potential
subjects.description: Inexpensive and slow: samples need hours in solution, so planning matters more than apparatus. Mass change data is easy to collect well and the standard error across replicates is usually small enough to produce a clean conclusion.

subjects.name: Photosynthesis and light intensity
subjects.description: Reliable with pondweed or algal beads and a lamp. Bubble counting is noisy, so replication is essential; students who count for longer intervals and repeat more often get data that a test can actually use.

subjects.name: Transpiration and plant water loss
subjects.description: Suits local conditions, where humidity and temperature gradients are easy to create. Plant-to-plant variation is the dominant source of spread, which is a genuine evaluation point rather than an excuse.

subjects.name: Seed germination and growth
subjects.description: The cheapest route to large sample sizes, because seeds are plentiful. Needs a week or more of elapsed time, so it is only viable if started early, which makes it a design decision rather than a late option.

subjects.name: Human physiology and reaction time
subjects.description: Requires informed consent and careful ethics, and sample size is limited by how many volunteers a student can recruit. Between-person variation is large, so paired designs where each person is their own control are far more powerful.

subjects.name: Antimicrobial and inhibition studies
subjects.description: Depends on what microbiological work the school permits, which varies across Dubai schools. Where allowed, zone-of-inhibition measurements give clean numerical data suited to a straightforward comparison of means.

subjects.name: Ecology and field sampling
subjects.description: Possible in Dubai with urban and coastal sites, and the sampling design is the whole investigation. Quadrat and transect work generates frequency data that suits a chi-squared or a correlation rather than a comparison of means.

subjects.name: Respiration in germinating or exercising systems
subjects.description: Equipment-dependent and sensitive to temperature drift. Good for students who can commit to several short sessions rather than one long one, because the measurements are quick and benefit from repetition.

subjects.name: Food and consumer biology
subjects.description: Popular for its real-world framing and risky because sample variability between batches often swamps the effect. Controlling the material source is the difference between a usable dataset and an unusable one.

dubai/ib-biology-ia-help.regionsIntro: What a family pays depends more on how they buy and how early they start than on where they live, but laboratory access and growing space do vary by community. These are the Dubai areas we hear from.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Sufouh
regions.note: The densest IB cluster in the emirate, with good laboratory provision. Blocks here run short because the design is usually sound and the work is test selection and evaluation.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and The Meadows
regions.note: Established IB provision beside British schools. Transition students from IGCSE Biology have rarely met a significance test, so their blocks include one extra session on statistics.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Meydan
regions.note: Large continuum schools where individual investigation time is contested. Design sessions pay for themselves most clearly here, because a second laboratory booking may simply not be available.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Continuum schools with small higher level sets. Few peers means few comparators, so families more often pay for a draft review they would not need in a large cohort.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Sobha Hartland
regions.note: Newer Diploma cohorts with modern laboratories and thin exemplar bases. Ambitious designs taken from online lists, then found to be under-powered, are the characteristic local cost.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Jumeirah Golf Estates
regions.note: Villa communities where garden space makes germination and transpiration work practical at home, which reduces dependence on contested school laboratory time.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: Apartment living limits home growing experiments, so students here lean towards enzyme and osmosis work that can be completed in school within one or two sessions.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and Umm Al Sheif
schoolClusters.note: Dubai's thickest concentration of IB World Schools, generally with strong laboratory and technician provision. Support blocks from this cluster are typically short and statistics-focused.

schoolClusters.note: Continuum and Diploma schools across the eastern and southern communities. Contested laboratory time and small higher level sets are what most often turn a four-session block into six here.

modes.title: Design and power session, bought first

sections.heading: Why sample size sets the bill in a Biology investigation
paragraphs: Every other cost in this project is downstream of one decision: how many measurements the student takes. A design with five levels of the independent variable and five replicates at each gives twenty-five data points, enough spread to compute a standard error at each level and enough structure for a test to say something. A design with three levels and two replicates gives six points, and no amount of careful processing turns six points into a defensible conclusion.

That is a financial fact, not just a methodological one. If the design is inadequate, the remedy is to collect the data again, which in a Dubai school means requesting another individual laboratory session in competition with timetabled practicals, sourcing material again, and finding a week in a calendar that may not have one. Families routinely discover this three weeks before a deadline, at which point there is no purchasable solution.

By contrast, a single session spent on design before data collection costs one hour at the specialist band and reliably prevents the problem. This is the clearest example in the whole Diploma of support that is cheaper the earlier it is bought, and it runs directly against how families actually buy, which is when a draft is written and worries start.

sections.heading: Choosing the test before collecting the data
paragraphs: Students pick a statistical test after collecting data, usually the one they have seen before, and that ordering causes most of the lost data-analysis marks in Biology. The test has to suit the design, and the design has to be built to feed the test. Deciding in advance costs nothing and determines whether the numbers will mean anything.

The choice is not difficult once the question is stated precisely. Comparing the means of two groups calls for a comparison-of-means test, and if each subject appears in both groups a paired version is far more powerful. Looking for a relationship between two continuous variables calls for a correlation, with the choice between a parametric and a rank-based version depending on the data. Comparing counts or frequencies across categories calls for chi-squared. Comparing more than two groups needs either a test designed for that or a design simplified to two.

What earns the band is not running the test but stating and checking its assumptions, and then interpreting the result biologically. A student who reports a significant difference and stops has done the arithmetic. A student who says what the result means for the biology, acknowledges the assumption that may not hold, and notes what the sample size does to the strength of the claim has written a strong data analysis and set up a strong evaluation.

The table maps question types to tests and names what each one needs. Confirm against the Biology subject guide and the school's own guidance, which is the authority on what is expected and what software or tables are permitted.

sections.heading: Ethics approval: the step that can stop an investigation dead
paragraphs: Biology is the one science where an investigation can be stopped on ethical grounds after the student has planned it, and that is a cost nobody mentions when quoting an hourly rate. The IB's own policy on animal experimentation constrains what may be done with living organisms, school policies add their own limits, and work involving human participants requires informed consent and careful handling of personal data.

The practical rules a Dubai student should check with their teacher before planning anything are straightforward. Investigations causing pain, distress or harm to vertebrates are not acceptable. Work with human participants needs informed consent, with parental consent where participants are minors, and the right to withdraw. Collecting biological material from people, including anything involving bodily fluids, is restricted in most school settings. Microbiological work is permitted only within the school's own containment rules, which differ considerably between schools in this city.

Data protection is the part students overlook. An investigation recording participants' reaction times, heights, dietary habits or exercise patterns is collecting personal data about identifiable people, often classmates and often minors. The student should record only what the investigation needs, keep it unidentifiable where possible, state in the method what was collected and why, and delete it afterwards. That is both good practice and consistent with the UAE's personal data protection framework.

None of this needs to be an obstacle. Paired designs using classmates with proper consent are among the most statistically powerful investigations available to a Biology student, and plant and microbial work avoids the vertebrate question entirely. What causes real cost is discovering the constraint after the design is fixed, so the ethics conversation belongs in the same week as the design conversation.
bullets: No investigation causing pain or harm to vertebrates
Informed consent for human participants, parental where minors
Bodily fluids and human tissue are restricted in school settings
Microbiological work only within the school's containment rules
Collect the minimum personal data, state its purpose, delete it after
Check all of this with the teacher in the design week, not later

sections.heading: What a session costs against what a redo costs
paragraphs: This is the arithmetic that should drive when a family buys help. A session at the specialist market band is AED 200-450. Redoing data collection costs no money at all in tutoring terms and a great deal in the currency that matters near a deadline, which is time the student does not have and laboratory access the school may not be able to grant.

Put concretely: a four-session block bought at the right moments, design, statistics, criterion review and evaluation, is roughly AED 800-1,800 at market rates and produces a defensible investigation. The same four sessions bought after inadequate data has been collected produces a well-processed account of inadequate data, which caps data analysis and conclusion whatever the processing quality. The money spent is identical. The outcome is not.

There is a third scenario worth naming because it is common. A family buys a monthly weekly-tutoring arrangement in the hope it covers everything, at Bestimate's estimated AED 600-2,000 or more a month, and the investigation is discussed in the last fifteen minutes of each session. Over three months that is a substantial sum for roughly one session's worth of focused investigation work. Where the student genuinely needs the syllabus taught, the monthly arrangement is right and the investigation work should be bought as an additional block, not folded in.

The honest summary is that Biology investigation support is inexpensive relative to the rest of the Diploma and almost worthless if bought late. We would rather tell a family that in advance than take four sessions of fees for processing data that cannot support a conclusion.

sections.heading: Where Biology investigations lose marks in Dubai schools
paragraphs: Insufficient replication comes first, for all the reasons above, and it shows up as a graph of means with no error bars or with error bars so wide that the levels overlap entirely. A reader can spot it without knowing any biology: if the bars overlap across the whole range, the investigation has not established a difference and the conclusion cannot claim one.

Second is the wrong test, or a test reported without its assumptions. A comparison-of-means test applied to frequency data, a correlation quoted as though it demonstrated causation, or a significant result reported with no mention of what the sample size does to confidence are all common and all cost data analysis marks. The fix is a single session and has to happen before the write-up is finished.

Third is a conclusion that outruns the data. Biology students are taught to explain mechanisms, so a conclusion often explains a biological mechanism in detail when the data showed only a weak and barely significant trend. The band descriptors reward a conclusion proportionate to the evidence, which sometimes means writing that the data is consistent with a mechanism without claiming to have demonstrated it.

Fourth is evaluation treated as a list, exactly as in the other sciences, but with a Biology-specific twist: the limitation is almost always biological variation, and students write that as though it were an unavoidable fact rather than something quantifiable. Reporting the actual spread, saying which level was noisiest and proposing a replication number that would have resolved it is a specific, quantified evaluation and it is what the top band asks for.
bullets: Too few replicates, visible as overlapping or absent error bars
A test that does not match the design, or assumptions unexamined
A conclusion stronger than the statistics support
Biological variation named but never quantified
Ethics or consent problems discovered after the design was fixed

sections.heading: Online, in-home and group compared on cost and fit
paragraphs: Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one tutoring in Dubai at AED 180-350 an hour and independent home tutors at up to AED 500, against a specialist online band of AED 200-450. The ranges overlap, so the question is not which is cheaper in the abstract but what each buys for a task that consists of a spreadsheet, a test output and a graph.

For Biology investigation work the in-home premium buys a commute. The student and tutor look at one laptop instead of at a shared screen, and the annotated spreadsheet does not stay with the student unless somebody emails it. The in-home option also restricts the tutor pool to those who can reach the family's community at the hour the child is free, which for a specific statistical skill in a small higher level set may mean nobody suitable at all.

Group classes and centre provision are cheaper per hour and structurally unsuited to this task, because every student's design, data and problems differ. A group class on statistical tests in general is useful; a group class on five different investigations is five conversations in one hour.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending tutors to a family's address is a service we run only in India. For this component that is not a limitation to apologise for, and we would rather say it plainly than let a family book expecting something we do not sell.

sections.heading: What we will not sell at any price
paragraphs: Completed Internal Assessments are sold in this market, in one documented case at several thousand dirhams, and Biology is a frequent target because the statistics intimidate students. A family weighing that option should understand exactly what is being purchased: a document the student did not produce, submitted under an academic honesty declaration they must sign personally, with the consequences of a malpractice finding falling on the student rather than on the seller. The risk is the Diploma, not the grade.

Supplying processed data is the same thing in a less obvious form. If a tutor runs the test, builds the spreadsheet and hands back the output, the data analysis criterion is marking somebody else's work. We teach the student to run the test on their own numbers, in their own spreadsheet, and we flag errors for them to find rather than correcting them.

The boundary in practice is wide and useful. We can explain what standard error means and why it is the right thing to put on an error bar. We can say that a design needs five replicates rather than three. We can tell a student their chosen test does not suit frequency data. We can read a draft and report the band each criterion sits in. All of that is support a student may legitimately receive and should acknowledge, and all of it is what good IB departments do when they have the hours.

This is also where price and integrity intersect honestly. A four-session block on the student's own investigation costs less than a purchased document and puts nothing at risk. Any provider whose pricing only makes sense if they are producing the work should be asked directly what they are producing.
bullets: No finished or part-finished investigations, at any price
No processed data, spreadsheets or graphs handed over
Errors flagged for the student to find and correct themselves
Explaining tests, replication and criteria is legitimate and encouraged
A coaching block costs less than a purchased document and risks nothing

faqs.question: How much does Biology IA support cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates read in October 2026 run from AED 33-52 at Tutopiya and AED 45-65 at EdFlik at the budget end, through Unitors at AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB, TutorChase at AED 270, and Bestimate's AED 200-450 and above for specialist IB and IGCSE support, reaching AED 650 at BartyED. Biology investigation work sits in the specialist band because statistical judgement is scarcer than syllabus teaching. These are market figures rather than an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: How many replicates does a Biology IA actually need?
faqs.answer: As a working minimum, five levels of the independent variable with five replicates at each, giving twenty-five data points. That is enough to compute a standard error at each level and support a test. Count-based designs such as seed germination need far more individuals per level, commonly twenty or more, because the measurement is a proportion. Human studies are limited by recruitment, which is why paired designs where each participant is their own control are much more powerful for the same number of volunteers.

faqs.question: Why is starting early cheaper for a Biology investigation?
faqs.answer: Because the expensive failure is a design that cannot support a test, and the remedy for that is collecting the data again rather than buying another tutoring session. In a Dubai school, a second individual laboratory booking competes with timetabled practicals and may not be available before the deadline. One session on design before anything is grown, timed or counted costs AED 200-450 at market rates and reliably prevents an outcome that no amount of later spending fixes.

faqs.question: Which statistical test should my child use?
faqs.answer: It depends on the design, which is why the test should be chosen before data collection. Comparing two groups calls for a comparison of means, and a paired version if the same subjects appear in both. A relationship between two continuous variables calls for a correlation. Counts across categories call for chi-squared. More than two groups need a test built for that or a simplified design. What earns marks is stating and checking the assumptions and interpreting the result biologically, not merely running it.

faqs.question: Do error bars have to be on every Biology IA graph?
faqs.answer: Any graph of means should carry them, and what they represent must be stated. Standard error is usually the right choice because it indicates the precision of the mean, whereas range shows only the extremes and overstates uncertainty. Overlapping bars across every level are a visual signal that the investigation has not established a difference, and a conclusion claiming one will be marked accordingly. A graph of means with no bars at all loses data analysis marks regardless of how clean the numbers look.

faqs.question: What ethical restrictions apply to a Biology investigation?
faqs.answer: Investigations causing pain, distress or harm to vertebrates are not acceptable. Work with human participants requires informed consent, with parental consent where participants are minors, and a right to withdraw. Collecting human tissue or bodily fluids is restricted in school settings, and microbiological work is limited by the school's own containment rules, which differ across Dubai schools. Any personal data collected about participants should be minimal, purposeful and deleted afterwards. Check all of this with the teacher during the design week.

faqs.question: Can my child use classmates as participants?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, with informed consent and the school's agreement, and it is often the best statistical option because a paired design where each person is their own control is far more powerful than comparing two separate groups. The requirements are consent that is genuinely informed, parental consent where participants are minors, the ability to withdraw at any point, and collecting only the personal data the investigation needs. Record what was collected and why in the method, and do not retain it afterwards.

faqs.question: Is a monthly tutoring package worth it for a Biology IA?
faqs.answer: Only if the student also needs the Biology syllabus taught. Market monthly figures include AED 799 for eight online sessions, and Bestimate estimates AED 600-1,200 for mid-range weekly tutoring and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. For the investigation alone, a three or four session block bought at the right moments costs less and finishes when the investigation is submitted. Where both are needed, buy them as two things rather than hoping one covers the other.

faqs.question: Why does in-home tutoring cost more for this kind of work?
faqs.answer: Because travel is priced into every hour. Bestimate quotes in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350, with independent home tutors up to AED 500, against an online specialist band of AED 200-450. A Biology investigation session is a spreadsheet, a test output and a graph on a screen, so the premium buys a commute rather than a better session. It also limits the tutor pool to whoever can reach your community at your child's free hour, which for a specific statistical skill is a real constraint.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to homes in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service we offer only in India; in the UAE every lesson is delivered one-to-one online over live video with a shared screen. We state that plainly because the phrase parents search is a home tutor, and the honest answer for investigation work is that the online format suits it better. The student shares their spreadsheet, the tutor annotates it live, and the annotated file stays with the student for revision afterwards.

faqs.question: How much of the Biology grade comes from the investigation?
faqs.answer: Roughly a fifth at both standard and higher level. It is marked out of twenty-four by the school teacher across four criteria of six marks each, and the IB moderates a sample of each school's marking, so the mark has to be defensible against the band descriptors rather than simply generous. That makes it the most controllable part of the course and the best candidate for a small, well-timed spend. Confirm the exact weighting in the current subject guide.

faqs.question: Why did a well-written Biology investigation score in the middle?
faqs.answer: Most often because the data could not support the claim. Too few replicates, no error bars or bars that overlap across every level, and a conclusion explaining a mechanism the statistics only weakly suggest, are the recurring pattern. The second common reason is a test that does not match the design, or one reported without its assumptions. Neither reflects the quality of the writing or the effort in the laboratory, and both are design decisions that were made months before the draft.

faqs.question: Will a Biology tutor process the results spreadsheet for us?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider who offers to is offering something that puts the Diploma at risk. Data analysis is one of the four marked criteria, so a spreadsheet somebody else built would mean the school marking work that is not the student's. What a Biology tutor can legitimately do is explain what standard error measures, teach which test suits the design, demonstrate the arithmetic on a practice dataset, and flag that a cell contains an error for the student to locate and correct.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest useful thing to buy if money is tight?
faqs.answer: One session, bought as early as possible, on the design. At market specialist rates that is AED 200-450 and it settles the number of levels, the replicates, the control and the test the data will support. That single hour prevents the only genuinely unrecoverable outcome in this project, which is data that cannot carry a conclusion. If the design is already fixed and data collected, buy one diagnostic session on the draft instead and expect to be told plainly whether more is warranted.

dubai/ib-biology-ia-help.closingHeading: Buy the design hour, not the panic hour
dubai/ib-biology-ia-help.closingBody: If your child has not yet collected data, the most valuable session available is the one that settles levels, replicates, control and test, and it is also the cheapest because it prevents the one failure nothing later can fix. If the data is already in, send the spreadsheet and the first session will say what it can honestly support and where each of the four criteria sits. The trial is free, it uses your child's own work, and we will give you an estimate of the whole block at market rates before you commit to anything.

Before any plan is quoted, they say which parts of the problem belong at the lower tier and can be done without them, because a biology plan that buys everything at the specialist rate is a plan that wasted money.

intro.heading: Buy biology from the bottom of the market upwards
paragraphs: Biology is the best-supplied Diploma science in Dubai, which makes it the subject where the price range matters most. Published hourly rates in this emirate, read in October 2026, run from AED 33-52 at Tutopiya and AED 45-65 at EdFlik at the budget end, through AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online with Unitors listing IB from AED 200, up to AED 270 at TutorChase for specialist work, AED 200-450 and above for IB and IGCSE specialists per the Bestimate survey, and AED 650 for a premium named tutor at BartyED. That is a twentyfold spread for a subject taught from one guide.

The spread is only irrational if every biology problem is the same problem. They are not. A student who cannot recall the stages of a process needs retrieval practice, which is a low-skill, high-frequency task that works perfectly well at the bottom of the market or with no tutor at all. A student whose investigation research question cannot generate quantitative data needs someone who can read it against four assessment criteria, and that is not available at AED 45 an hour. Matching the task to the tier is the whole of cost control in this subject, and it is a judgement nobody in this market has an incentive to help a parent make.

Biology also has a specific trap that makes families overspend. The content volume is large, students feel behind, and the instinctive response is to buy more hours. More hours of explanation does not fix a volume problem; spaced retrieval does, and spaced retrieval is something a student largely does to themselves. The marks that actually need a specialist are concentrated in two places: command-term discipline on Paper 2, which is 44 per cent of the grade, and the investigation, which is 20 per cent.

That leaves a surprisingly cheap plan available to a Dubai family who sequences it properly. Retrieval practice at the bottom tier or self-directed. Command-term marking at the qualified tier for a limited block, because the fix is a habit change measurable within weeks rather than a term of teaching. Investigation coaching at the qualified tier, block-booked at three or four sessions against the school's deadlines. Total hours are modest and most of them sit mid-band rather than at the top.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For a cost-led plan the arithmetic is straightforward: the Bestimate survey puts qualified in-home one-to-one in Dubai at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for comparable work online. The premium buys a drive. In a well-supplied subject like biology, it buys nothing else.

dubai/ib-biology-tutor.programmesIntro: Biology reaches a Dubai Diploma classroom from several starting points, and what a student arrives with changes which tier of support they need rather than how many hours.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences, Years 4 and 5
programmes.description: Criterion-assessed science covering knowledge, inquiry and design, processing and evaluating, and reflection. Students arrive well prepared for the Diploma investigation and usually unpractised at the volume of recall Diploma biology assumes, because MYP assessment rewards process over coverage.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai's full-continuum IB World Schools this route feeds straight into Diploma biology. The characteristic first-term problem is coverage rather than comprehension, which means the cheapest tier of support is often the correct one for the first few months.

programmes.name: IGCSE Biology into Diploma biology
programmes.description: Cambridge 0610 or Edexcel 4BI1 leaves a student practised at structured written questions and at command-term compliance. What transfers less well is independent experimental design, since IGCSE practical questions supply the method rather than asking for one to be constructed.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools dominate Dubai enrolment, so many Diploma biologists arrive from IGCSE. They are frequently the group that needs the fewest hours, because the technique is already there and only the content volume and the investigation are new.

programmes.name: IB Biology Standard Level
programmes.description: Two written papers plus the internally assessed investigation at 20 per cent. Paper 1 combines multiple-choice with a data-based section; Paper 2 is extended response and carries the largest weighting. Accepted by a range of health, environmental and social-science routes, and frequently chosen alongside two other sciences.
programmes.countryNote: Standard Level biology is the most commonly requested science in this emirate, which means supply is good and rates sit lower than the equivalent physics request. A family shopping for Standard Level biology has genuine choice, which is not true at Higher Level physics.

programmes.name: IB Biology Higher Level
programmes.description: The same structure with substantially more content and longer papers. Expected or preferred by many medicine, dentistry, veterinary, biomedical and life-science routes. The additional content is largely more of the same kind of material, which makes Higher Level biology a volume challenge above all else.
programmes.countryNote: Higher Level biology demand in Dubai concentrates among students targeting medicine, and so does Higher Level chemistry demand. Families often buy both at the specialist tier when only one of them needs it, which is one of the most common overspends in this market.

subjects.name: Molecular biology and biochemistry
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Water, carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, enzymes and metabolism. Heavy on precise terminology, which makes it a retrieval problem first. The marks that need a specialist are in enzyme-kinetics data questions rather than in the recall itself.

subjects.name: Cells and cell processes
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Cell structure, membranes, transport, division and respiration. Diagram labelling and process sequencing dominate, both of which respond to self-testing. Osmosis and water-potential questions are where calculation-type marks appear.

subjects.name: Genetics and inheritance
subjects.levels: SL and HL, substantially extended at HL
subjects.description: Inheritance patterns, gene expression, mutation and biotechnology. The one topic in biology where a student can be defeated by the logic rather than the volume, particularly on dihybrid crosses and linkage at Higher Level, and that is worth mid-band time.

subjects.name: Physiology and body systems
subjects.levels: SL and HL, substantially extended at HL
subjects.description: Gas exchange, transport, homeostasis, neurones and the immune response. The largest body of content in the course. A volume problem almost entirely, which means it is the cheapest part of the syllabus to address properly.

subjects.name: Ecology and ecosystems
subjects.description: Energy flow, nutrient cycling, population dynamics and conservation. Frequently the source of investigation research questions, and frequently the source of questions whose output is a description rather than a measurement.

subjects.name: Evolution and biodiversity
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Natural selection, speciation, classification and phylogenetics. Marks go to explanation structured as a causal chain rather than as a narrative, which is a command-term discipline rather than a knowledge issue.

subjects.name: Paper 1
subjects.description: Multiple-choice questions plus a data-based section. The data section is where biology students lose marks they did not know were available: quoting the figure, reading the axis correctly, and distinguishing correlation from the causal claim the question did not make.

subjects.name: Paper 2
subjects.description: Extended response across the syllabus and the largest component in the course. Command-term discipline decides the band here more than coverage does, which is why a block of marking-led work at the qualified tier is the highest-value biology purchase.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.levels: SL and HL · 20 per cent · 24 marks
subjects.description: An individual investigation with a 3,000-word ceiling, assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at six marks each. In biology the usual failure is biological variability treated as experimental error, and insufficient replication to say anything about it.

subjects.name: Retrieval practice
subjects.levels: Not a syllabus topic, and the largest single lever in biology
subjects.description: Spaced self-testing against the syllabus statements, scored and repeated. It solves the volume problem, which is most of the biology problem, and it is the one intervention a student can run alone or at the bottom tier of the market.

dubai/ib-biology-tutor.regionsIntro: Delivery is online, so the rate does not change across the emirate. What changes is the in-home quote a family is comparing against, and how long a Diploma student has been awake by the time a session starts.

regions.name: Dubai Marina, JLT and Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: Well supplied by in-home tutors and therefore the smallest travel premium in the emirate. Even so the published in-home band sits above the online one, and tower access adds time at both ends that nobody itemises.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches, Mudon and Damac Hills
regions.note: The largest in-home premium, because a tutor commits an hour of driving either side of the lesson. For a well-supplied subject like biology, paying that premium buys nothing the online market does not already offer.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Several IB World Schools within a short radius and large biology cohorts. Demand here is high but supply in biology is good, so families in this cluster usually have real choice even in the spring term.

regions.name: Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim and Al Safa
regions.note: Established Diploma programmes with equipped laboratories and often a biology garden or field site, which widens the range of viable investigation questions. Support here is better spent on replication design than on apparatus workarounds.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais
regions.note: More price-sensitive on average and more likely to be comparing a tuition-centre group class. For biology content coverage a group class is a defensible purchase; for the investigation and Paper 2 marking it is not the same thing.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Close to the universities, so undergraduate tutors at the budget band are easy to find. For retrieval practice and content review that is the right tier; for criterion-referenced investigation feedback it is not.

regions.name: Al Furjan, Discovery Gardens and Dubai South
regions.note: Newer Diploma provision with smaller biology cohorts. Travel quotes to this corridor are among the highest in the emirate, which makes the published online band the clearly better value for a subject with good online supply.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai IB schools with large biology cohorts
schoolClusters.note: Mature Diploma programmes running biology at both levels with separate teaching groups. Families here typically need a short block of marking-led work plus investigation coaching rather than sustained teaching, which keeps the total hours low.

schoolClusters.city: Newer Diploma biology provision
schoolClusters.note: Smaller cohorts, sometimes with both levels taught together for part of the course. The useful first check is confirming which content is assessed at the student's own level, which costs almost nothing and removes a common source of misplaced panic.

schoolClusters.city: IGCSE biology feeder schools
schoolClusters.note: British-curriculum schools whose Year 11 biologists join Diploma programmes elsewhere in the emirate. This group usually needs the fewest paid hours, because command-term technique is already established from two years of structured written papers.

dubai/ib-biology-tutor.modesIntro: Three purchases cover almost every biology need, and they sit at different tiers. Buying all three at the top tier is the most common way a Dubai biology budget disappears without changing a grade.

modes.title: Retrieval practice, bottom tier or self-run
modes.description: Short frequent self-testing against the syllabus statements, scored and repeated at increasing intervals. It solves the content-volume problem, which is most of the biology problem. A student can run it alone with a well-made question bank, or at the bottom of the market with someone to administer and score it.

modes.title: Command-term marking block, mid tier
modes.description: Six to eight sessions at the qualified band, built entirely around marking Paper 2 style questions to the published scheme. The object is a habit change, not content coverage: describe, explain, deduce, outline, distinguish and suggest each buy something different, and the loss stops once the habit changes. Measurable within three weeks.

modes.description: Three or four sessions placed against the school's internal deadlines. Research-question feasibility first, with biological variability and replication addressed before data collection, then a draft read against the four criteria with six marks named against each. The student designs, collects and writes; the tutor questions and marks.

sections.heading: What AED 45 an hour buys in Dubai biology, and what it does not
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the published range rather than the top, because for biology the bottom is genuinely useful. EdFlik publishes online tuition from AED 45-65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. At that tier the realistic product is content explanation, worked examples and supervised question practice, usually delivered by a university student. For a Diploma biology student whose problem is recalling the stages of a process or the structure of a membrane, that is sufficient, and paying four times more for it is a straightforward waste.

What the budget tier reliably cannot do is mark against published criteria. Reading a Paper 2 answer and identifying that the student described where the question asked them to deduce requires familiarity with the mark scheme's conventions. Reading an investigation draft against research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation requires knowing what each of those four criteria rewards and what each is worth. Neither is available at AED 45 an hour, and a family who buys criterion-referenced work at that tier is paying for something they are not receiving.

The qualified band at AED 150-300, with Unitors listing IB specifically from AED 200, is where criterion-referenced marking and investigation coaching sit. The specialist band at AED 200-450 and the premium band above it exist for scarcity and for component-level depth. Biology is the best-supplied Diploma science in this emirate, which means a family rarely needs to go above the qualified band and should ask what the extra is for if quoted higher.

The table below sorts the tiers by what they can and cannot do rather than by adjectives. All figures belong to the providers who published them, read in October 2026. Those bands are the market's, not IB Gram's, and the free 30-minute trial lesson with no card details taken is where a plan with a stated hour count gets quoted.

sections.heading: Biology is a volume problem, and hours are the wrong answer
paragraphs: Diploma biology carries a large body of content and comparatively little calculation, and that combination produces a specific failure mode. A student reads the material, understands it, feels reasonably confident, and then cannot retrieve it four months later under time pressure. The felt experience is of understanding biology and being bad at biology exams, and the instinctive family response is to buy more explanation.

More explanation does not fix it, because the problem is not comprehension. Retrieval is a separate skill from understanding and it is built by testing rather than by reading or listening. The intervention is spaced self-testing against the syllabus statements: twenty to thirty minutes, three or four times a week, scored, with the interval between repetitions increasing as recall becomes reliable. It is tedious and it is the single largest lever available in this subject.

The cost consequence is substantial. Retrieval practice requires administration and discipline rather than subject expertise, which means it sits at the bottom of the market or at no cost at all if a student will run it themselves. A Dubai family who buys retrieval practice at the specialist band is paying AED 270 an hour for someone to read questions aloud, and that is the most common overspend in Diploma biology.

The corollary is where the paid hours should go. Two places: command-term discipline on Paper 2, which is 44 per cent of the grade and where the marks lost are technique rather than knowledge, and the investigation, which is 20 per cent and cannot be done well without criterion-referenced reading. Together they account for nearly two thirds of the grade and require perhaps ten to twelve paid hours across a Diploma year at the qualified band.
bullets: Retrieval is a separate skill from understanding and is built by testing
Twenty to thirty minutes, three or four times a week, scored and spaced

sections.heading: Where biology marks go: command terms and the data question
paragraphs: The largest single category of lost marks in Dubai biology scripts is command-term misreading, and it is cheap to fix because it is one habit rather than many gaps. State wants a fact with no justification. Describe wants observable detail. Explain wants a causal chain. Deduce wants a conclusion derived from information given in the question. Outline wants a brief account. Distinguish wants both sides placed against each other. Suggest wants applied reasoning on unfamiliar material. A student who writes a description every time loses marks on both papers at once.

The fix is enforcement rather than instruction. The concept takes twenty minutes to explain. Changing the habit takes about three weeks of every answer being marked against its verb, with the loss tagged by command term so the pattern is visible in the record. After six to eight marking-led sessions the student is reading the verb before the content, and the gain shows up across every topic simultaneously because the habit is topic-independent.

The second category is the data question, and it is where biology students lose marks they did not know were on offer. Paper 1's data-based section and many Paper 2 questions supply a table or a graph, and the mark scheme requires the figure to be quoted. A biologically correct answer that does not cite the data earns less than a thinner answer that does. The related trap is the causal claim: a question asking what the data show is not asking why, and students who explain mechanism where description was requested lose the mark for the right reason badly applied.

The third is specificity of terminology. Biology mark schemes frequently require a precise term rather than a correct paraphrase, and a student who writes 'the thing that carries the signal' when the scheme wants 'neurotransmitter' has demonstrated understanding and not earned the mark. This is a retrieval problem again, which puts it back at the bottom tier, and it is the clearest illustration of why the two kinds of work need separating.
bullets: Command-term discipline is one habit, worth marks across every topic
Three weeks of verb-tagged marking changes it; explanation alone does not
Data questions require the figure to be quoted, not just understood
