dubai/ib-cas-guidance.programmesIntro: Service learning and creative and physical engagement run across the IB continuum in different forms, and Dubai families moving between schools meet each version. Here is what each stage asks for.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: CAS runs for the duration of the Diploma as one of the three core elements. The student maintains a portfolio of evidence against seven learning outcomes, completes at least one collaborative CAS project of a month or more, and meets their coordinator or adviser for three formal interviews. There is no grade and no points, and completion is required for the Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools vary considerably in how tightly they run CAS. Some use a structured platform with deadlines and assigned advisers; others leave it to the student with three interviews as the only checkpoints. The second model produces most of the late-stage emergencies, and a family should find out early which model their school uses.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP core includes service learning rather than CAS, alongside personal and professional skills, a language development portfolio and the reflective project. Service learning is structured around identifying a need and responding to it in a sustained way, with reflection throughout.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Dubai school offers the CP, families should be clear that service learning and CAS are different requirements with different documentation. A student transferring between the two programmes cannot simply carry a CAS portfolio across, and the coordinator should be consulted before assuming any evidence transfers.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Service as action runs throughout the MYP, with students expected to engage in service and reflect on it, and the Personal Project in the final year providing a sustained independent undertaking with a process journal.
programmes.countryNote: Continuum students in Dubai arrive at the Diploma already used to logging service and writing reflections, which is a substantial advantage. Students joining at Year 12 from a system with no service requirement often have eighteen months of CAS to construct from a standing start, and that is the group most likely to need early planning help.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Action is one of the essential elements of the PYP, with students encouraged to respond to their learning through genuine initiative, culminating in the Exhibition in the final year. There is no portfolio requirement of the CAS kind.
programmes.countryNote: The PYP layer in Dubai is deep because many families arrive mid-primary. For parents it is the first sight of how an IB school treats student-initiated action, which is the same instinct CAS will later ask the student to document formally.

dubai/ib-cas-guidance.subjectsIntro: CAS experiences are grouped under creativity, activity and service, and most good ones sit in more than one strand. These are the kinds of commitment Dubai students use most, with what each tends to evidence well.

subjects.name: Instrumental music and ensemble playing
subjects.description: Strong for commitment and perseverance because progress is slow and visible, and strong for collaboration where an ensemble is involved. Weak on initiating unless the student organises something rather than attending something.

subjects.name: Visual art, film and design projects
subjects.description: Good for identifying strengths and for developing new skills, particularly where the student works outside their comfortable medium. Needs a defined outcome to avoid becoming an unevidenced hobby.

subjects.name: Theatre, debate and public speaking
subjects.description: Covers collaboration naturally and often engages with ethical issues, which is the hardest outcome to evidence. Debating in particular produces genuine material on the ethics of issues of global significance.

subjects.name: Competitive and team sport
subjects.description: Reliable for commitment and for collaboration, and often the easiest strand for a Dubai student to sustain because school sport is well organised. Rarely evidences initiating or ethics without deliberate effort.

subjects.name: Individual fitness and endurance goals
subjects.description: Good for challenge and new skills if the goal is genuinely new, and excellent for perseverance because the record of training is itself evidence. Needs a clear starting point so progress can be shown.

subjects.name: Coaching or officiating younger children
subjects.description: One of the most efficient CAS commitments available: it spans two strands, evidences collaboration and responsibility, and schools in Dubai usually have an internal route to it that needs no external arrangement.

subjects.name: Tutoring and peer academic support
subjects.description: Valuable and frequently mishandled, because it must be genuine service with a real need rather than an arrangement that benefits the student's own revision. Works well where a school runs a structured peer support scheme.

subjects.name: Environmental and sustainability initiatives
subjects.description: Well suited to local conditions and to the ethics outcome, particularly around water, waste and energy use. Strongest where the student measures something rather than raising awareness in the abstract.

subjects.name: Work with registered charities and community organisations
subjects.description: The core of most service strands in Dubai, arranged through registered organisations and school-approved partners. Students should confirm the route with the CAS coordinator before committing, since schools maintain their own approved lists.

subjects.name: Student-led societies and school initiatives
subjects.description: The best route to the initiating outcome, because founding or running something generates evidence nothing else does. Also the most common place students claim an outcome they cannot actually demonstrate.

dubai/ib-cas-guidance.regionsIntro: CAS looks different across Dubai because communities and schools offer different access, and travel time across the city is a real constraint on sustained weekly commitment. These are the areas we hear from.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Sufouh
regions.note: The densest IB cluster in the emirate, where several schools run structured CAS platforms with assigned advisers. Students here more often need outcome mapping than activity finding.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Meydan
regions.note: Large continuum schools with well-developed internal service programmes. The common gap here is the initiating outcome, because so much is organised for students already.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and The Springs
regions.note: Established provision beside British schools. Students who joined at Year 12 from a non-IB route are concentrated here and often start CAS with nothing logged at all.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Continuum schools with strong community links. Service access is good, and the recurring issue is reflections written as attendance records rather than as evidence.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Sobha Hartland
regions.note: Newer schools with young Diploma cohorts and CAS programmes still being built. Fewer established partnerships means students have to initiate more, which is useful for outcomes and harder logistically.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Jumeirah Golf Estates
regions.note: Villa communities where sport and outdoor activity are easy for much of the year and where cross-city travel to service commitments is the practical limit on frequency.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: Apartment living with excellent access to organised city-wide activities and limited space for anything self-organised at home. Students here lean towards institution-based service and creativity.

regions.name: Dubai Festival City and Al Jaddaf
regions.note: Diploma provision on the Creek side with good access to community organisations. Evening commitments are constrained by the homeward commute, so weekend service blocks are more common.

sections.heading: The seven learning outcomes and the evidence each one needs
paragraphs: Everything in CAS reduces to these seven outcomes. The student must demonstrate all of them through evidence in their portfolio, and the coordinator decides whether they have. Students generally evidence three or four without trying, because ordinary school life produces them, and then struggle with the remaining three because those require deliberate choices.

The outcomes that come free are usually identifying strengths and areas for growth, demonstrating skills while undertaking new challenges, and showing commitment and perseverance. Any student who plays a sport and learns an instrument has those. The outcomes that do not come free are initiating and planning a CAS experience, engaging with issues of global significance, and recognising and considering the ethics of choices and actions. Those three need a student to start something, to connect it to something larger, and to think about it honestly.

The table below sets out all seven with the kind of evidence each actually requires. Read it as a checklist rather than as a description, because that is how the coordinator will read the portfolio. An outcome is not evidenced because a student believes they displayed it; it is evidenced because something in the portfolio shows it, in a reflection, a photograph with a caption, a supervisor's note or a documented plan.

Confirm the current wording of the outcomes with the CAS coordinator, since the IB publishes the authoritative version and the school applies it. The substance below is stable but the exact phrasing matters when a student is writing a reflection that is meant to address one of them specifically.

sections.heading: The CAS project: the requirement most students leave too late
paragraphs: At least one CAS project is required, it must last at least one month, and it must involve collaboration. That is a short specification and it is the single requirement most Dubai students have not met when their second interview arrives. The reason is simple: everything else in CAS can be accumulated from activities the student was already doing, and the project cannot.

What counts is broader than students assume. A project does not have to be a charitable fundraiser, and fundraising is in fact one of the weaker options because it often involves little sustained collaboration and generates thin reflection. A sports coaching programme run over a term, a student-founded society with a defined aim, an environmental audit of a school building with recommendations, a performance or exhibition organised from nothing: all of these are projects, and all of them generate the initiating, collaboration and ethics evidence that is otherwise hardest to find.

The month matters and it is a minimum rather than a target. A project that runs across a term produces a sequence of reflections showing how the plan changed, which is far better evidence than a single intense week. Collaboration also has to be real: a project where the student did everything and others helped occasionally will be visible as such in the reflections, because there will be no disagreements, no shared decisions and no division of work to write about.

The practical advice is to decide the project in the first year, not the second, and to choose something that overlaps with a commitment the student already has. A student who already coaches a junior team can turn that into a project by planning and running a tournament. A student who plays in an ensemble can organise a performance for a community audience. The project is then an extension of something sustainable rather than an addition to an already full second year.
bullets: At least one month, as a minimum rather than a target
Genuine collaboration, with roles and decisions to reflect on
Fundraising is permitted and usually weaker than the alternatives
The project is the best source of initiating and ethics evidence
Decide it in the first year and build it on an existing commitment

sections.heading: Reflections that work as evidence
paragraphs: The portfolio is evidence and reflections are most of it, so the quality of reflection is what determines whether a coordinator can sign CAS off. The commonest form a student submits is an attendance record: what happened, when, and that it was enjoyable or tiring. That is a diary. It evidences nothing except presence.

A reflection that works does three things. It names what happened specifically enough that it could not be any other occasion. It says what the student thought, decided or found difficult, including when the answer is unflattering. And it connects to an outcome explicitly, so the coordinator can see which box it fills. Three sentences doing those three things is more useful than five hundred words of narrative.

Reflections should be written close to the event and they should not all be prose. A photograph with a caption explaining what the student was deciding at that moment is a reflection. A short voice note transcribed is a reflection. A supervisor's note confirming a role is evidence. A planning document with crossings-out shows initiating better than a paragraph claiming it. Variety is explicitly encouraged and almost nobody uses it.

The hardest reflections to write are the ones that earn the ethics outcome, because they require admitting that a decision was difficult or that something was handled badly. A reflection describing a moment when the student realised their service work was more useful to them than to the people they were serving is genuinely strong evidence. A reflection asserting that helping people is good is not. Coordinators in Dubai read hundreds of these and the distinction is immediately apparent.
bullets: Name the occasion specifically; a diary entry evidences nothing
Say what was thought, decided or found difficult
Connect each reflection to a named outcome
Use photographs, captions, notes and plans, not only prose
Write close to the event rather than in a final-week batch
Honesty about difficulty is what earns the ethics outcome

sections.heading: The three interviews and what the coordinator is checking
paragraphs: A CAS programme includes three formal interviews with the coordinator or an assigned adviser, and students treat them casually because nothing is marked. They are in fact the only checkpoints in the entire eighteen months, and what happens in them determines whether a problem is found with a year to fix it or with a month.

The first interview, near the start, is about the plan: what the student intends to do, which strands it covers, and whether the balance across creativity, activity and service is plausible. The useful preparation is to arrive with the outcome map rather than with a list of activities, because the coordinator's question is which outcomes the plan will evidence.

The second, roughly in the middle, is the one that matters most. It checks progress against the plan, and it is the last point at which a missing CAS project or an unevidenced outcome can be addressed comfortably. A student who arrives with reflections organised by outcome, and who can name the two outcomes still unevidenced, will leave with a workable plan. A student who arrives with an undated activity list will leave with a warning.

The third, near the end, confirms completion. By then the evidence either exists or it does not. The specific thing to avoid is discovering at this interview that reflections are too thin to evidence an outcome the student genuinely achieved, which is the most frustrating failure in CAS because the work was done and only the record is missing. Writing reflections as the programme runs is the entire defence against it.
bullets: Three interviews are the only formal checkpoints in CAS
First: the plan, and which outcomes it will evidence
Second: progress, and the last comfortable chance to fix gaps
Third: completion, by which point evidence must already exist
Bring reflections organised by outcome, not an activity list

sections.heading: Planning eighteen months around a Dubai school year
paragraphs: CAS spans roughly eighteen months and a Dubai calendar does not offer eighteen usable ones. Outdoor activity is impractical through the hottest months, the long summer break removes most families from the city, the second Diploma year is dominated by internal assessment deadlines and then examinations, and in years when Ramadan falls in term time the rhythm of the school day changes for a month. A plan that assumes a uniform eighteen months will fail in the second year.

The workable shape front-loads. The first Diploma year is where sustained weekly commitments should be established and where the CAS project should run, because that year has fewer competing deadlines than any other period. The summer between the two years is good for an intensive block, particularly for students travelling to family in another country, where service with a local organisation produces genuinely distinctive reflections. The second year should be maintenance and documentation, not new initiation.

Local specifics are worth planning around rather than lamenting. Indoor and early-morning activity carries the hot months. Ramadan creates real service opportunities around community meals and charitable distribution, which is also a period when reflection on ethics and global significance comes naturally. Cooler months are when outdoor environmental and sporting commitments should be concentrated.

The table maps a typical Dubai Diploma calendar to what CAS work suits each phase. Treat it as a planning template to take to the coordinator, who will have the school's own deadlines and approved partner arrangements and whose version takes precedence over any general plan.

sections.heading: Where CAS goes wrong in Dubai schools
paragraphs: The missing CAS project is first, for the reasons above. It cannot be accumulated from existing activity, it needs a month, and it needs other people, so it is the one requirement that has to be deliberately started. Students who have not begun one by the end of the first Diploma year are usually in difficulty, because the second year has no comfortable month in it.

Second is unevidenced outcomes that were genuinely achieved. A student who founded a society, argued with their committee, changed the plan twice and made a difficult decision about who to include has evidence for initiating, collaboration and ethics, and none of it is in the portfolio because they never wrote it down. This is the most common and most avoidable failure in CAS, and it is purely a documentation habit.

Third is an unbalanced programme. Some students do a great deal of activity and almost no creativity, or treat service as a single week of volunteering. The strands do not require equal time but they do require genuine engagement, and a coordinator reading a portfolio that is twelve months of football and one afternoon at a charity event will say so.

Fourth is the student who joined at Year 12 from a system with no service requirement, has eighteen months of CAS to build from nothing while also meeting a new course load, and does not realise until the first interview that CAS is a Diploma requirement rather than an extracurricular suggestion. In Dubai, where lateral entry into DP1 from British and other streams is common, this is a sizeable group and the fix is almost entirely about starting early.
bullets: No CAS project started by the end of the first Diploma year
Outcomes achieved in reality and absent from the portfolio
A programme heavily weighted to one strand
Late entrants treating CAS as optional extracurricular activity
Reflections written in a final-week batch and reading like it

sections.heading: What CAS guidance costs, and what cannot be bought
paragraphs: CAS guidance is the cheapest support in the Diploma because the useful work is short. One mapping session and one reflection session covers most students, with a third on the CAS project where that has not started. At published Dubai market rates read in October 2026, which run from AED 33-52 at Tutopiya and AED 45-65 at EdFlik at the budget end, through Unitors at AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB, TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's AED 200-450 and above for specialist IB support, with BartyED at AED 650, a two or three session block is a modest one-off cost.

What cannot be bought is the CAS itself, and a family should be suspicious of anything that implies otherwise. No provider can complete a student's activities, write their reflections, or determine that their CAS is complete. That last point is worth emphasising: the school's CAS coordinator is the sole authority on completion, and no external service can override, substitute for or guarantee their judgement.

Nor should anyone pay for access to service opportunities as part of a tutoring arrangement. Service in Dubai generally runs through registered organisations and school-approved partners, the school's coordinator holds the relevant list, and a student should go through that route rather than through a paid intermediary. Where an opportunity requires a formal arrangement or permission, the coordinator is the person who knows what applies.

The honest summary is that CAS support is advice, and its value is almost entirely a function of when it is bought. A single session in the first term of DP1 prevents nearly every problem described on this page. The same session in the final term can only triage. We would rather tell a family that than sell four sessions to a student with eight weeks left.

process.title: Send the activity list and the year group
process.description: Everything the student currently does, in or out of school, and whether they are in the first or second Diploma year. If a coordinator has already flagged a gap, say which. That is enough to tell whether this is a one-session mapping job or something more urgent.

process.title: We map it against the seven outcomes
process.description: The first session produces a written map: which outcomes are evidenced, which are partial, which are untouched, and which existing activities could cover the gaps with small adjustments. The student takes that map to their coordinator, who remains the authority on whether it is sufficient.

process.title: A free trial that produces the map
process.description: The first session is free and its output is concrete. Most families need nothing beyond it, particularly in the first Diploma year when the gaps are still easy to close. If the honest answer is that the student is in good shape and should simply write better reflections, that is what we will say.

process.title: One or two follow-up sessions where there is a real gap
process.description: A session on scoping the CAS project where none has started, and a session on reflection where the portfolio reads as an attendance record. Beyond that there is little an external adviser can usefully add, and we will not book sessions to pad a short piece of work.

process.title: The student does everything, and the coordinator decides
process.description: No activity is arranged for the student, no reflection is written for them, and nothing we say determines whether their CAS is complete. The school's coordinator holds that judgement, and our role ends at helping the student arrive with a portfolio that makes the decision easy.

whyPoints.title: We tell families CAS is a Diploma requirement
whyPoints.description: No marks, no grade, and incomplete CAS means no Diploma. That sentence is the whole reason this page exists, and it is said at the top rather than buried, because students who join at Year 12 from other systems routinely do not know it.

whyPoints.title: Mapping first, activities second
whyPoints.description: The useful work is identifying which of the seven outcomes are unevidenced, then adjusting existing commitments to cover them. Adding new activities to an already full Diploma is the expensive answer and usually the unnecessary one.

whyPoints.title: We push the CAS project forward a year
whyPoints.description: It needs a month and real collaboration, so it belongs in the first Diploma year. Almost every late CAS emergency in Dubai is a project that was never started, and the advice is the same every time: start it before the second year begins.

whyPoints.title: Reflections treated as evidence
whyPoints.description: A diary entry evidences nothing. We teach the three things a reflection must do, have the student rewrite one of their own in the session, and leave the writing entirely with them.

whyPoints.title: Short blocks, honestly ended
whyPoints.description: One to three sessions covers CAS guidance for nearly every student. We say so rather than constructing a programme, because the value here is in timing and advice rather than in hours.

whyPoints.title: The coordinator's authority is respected
whyPoints.description: No external service can decide that CAS is complete, arrange approved service placements in place of the school's own route, or guarantee any outcome. We say what applies and point the student back to their coordinator.

faqs.question: Does CAS affect my child's IB points total?
faqs.answer: No. CAS produces no marks, no grade and no points towards the 45. What it does carry is a completion requirement: a candidate who has not completed CAS to the school's satisfaction does not receive the Diploma, regardless of their subject points or their core points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. That combination, no reward for doing it well and a serious penalty for not finishing, is why it is the most under-managed part of the Diploma.

faqs.question: How many CAS hours does my child need?
faqs.answer: Hours are not the requirement. Older guidance attaching an hour count to CAS no longer governs, and what matters instead is evidence of all seven learning outcomes, at least one CAS project of a month or more involving collaboration, and sustained engagement across roughly eighteen months. Some Dubai schools still set an internal hours expectation as a management tool, so ask the coordinator what the school requires, but hours alone will not satisfy the outcomes.

faqs.question: What exactly are the seven CAS learning outcomes a Dubai DP student has to evidence?
faqs.answer: In substance: identifying strengths and areas for growth; undertaking new challenges and developing skills; initiating and planning an experience; showing commitment and perseverance; working collaboratively with others; engaging with an issue of global significance; and recognising and considering the ethics of choices and actions. All seven must be evidenced in the portfolio. Students usually evidence the first, second and fourth without trying, and struggle with initiating, global significance and ethics, which require deliberate choices rather than ordinary school life.

faqs.question: What exactly is the CAS project?
faqs.answer: At least one project lasting a minimum of one month and involving collaboration with others. It is the requirement most commonly left too late, because everything else in CAS can be accumulated from activities a student was already doing and the project cannot. It does not have to be a fundraiser, and fundraising is often a weaker choice because it generates thin collaboration evidence. A coaching programme, a founded society, an environmental audit or an organised performance all work better.

faqs.question: When should the CAS project start?
faqs.answer: In the first Diploma year, ideally in its second term. The second year has internal assessment deadlines, the Extended Essay and examinations, and no comfortable month for a collaborative project. Starting in DP1 also means the project can be built on a commitment the student already has, which makes it sustainable rather than an addition to a full year. A student who has not begun one by the end of DP1 is usually in genuine difficulty.

faqs.question: What makes a CAS reflection count as evidence?
faqs.answer: Three things. It names the occasion specifically enough that it could not be any other one. It says what the student thought, decided or found difficult, including when that is unflattering. And it connects explicitly to one of the seven outcomes so the coordinator can see what it evidences. Three sentences doing those is worth more than five hundred words of narrative. Photographs with captions, planning documents and supervisor notes all count as reflection evidence too.

faqs.question: Can my child's existing hobbies count towards CAS?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they should, provided the engagement continues during the Diploma and is documented. What an existing hobby cannot do is evidence the new challenges outcome, because the challenge has to be genuinely new. The productive approach is to keep the existing commitments for commitment and perseverance, and then extend one of them into something unfamiliar: a player who starts coaching, a musician who organises a performance, a swimmer who trains for a distance they have never attempted.

faqs.question: What happens if CAS is not completed in time?
faqs.answer: The school cannot confirm completion, and incomplete CAS is a failing condition for the Diploma, so the candidate does not receive it. Schools work hard to avoid that outcome and will usually escalate well in advance, which is what the three formal interviews exist for. The danger case is a student who did the activities but documented nothing, because the remedy then is reconstructing evidence under time pressure, and reconstructed reflections are visibly thin to an experienced coordinator.

faqs.question: How do Dubai students find service opportunities?
faqs.answer: Through the school in the first instance. Service in the UAE generally runs through registered organisations and school-approved partners, and the CAS coordinator holds the list of routes the school recognises. Going through that channel also handles whatever permissions or arrangements apply, which an informal arrangement may not. Students should not pay an intermediary for access to placements as part of a tutoring arrangement; the school's own route exists and is the one the coordinator will accept.

faqs.question: How does the Dubai climate affect a CAS plan?
faqs.answer: Substantially, and it is entirely foreseeable. Outdoor activity is impractical through the hottest months, so outdoor sporting and environmental commitments should be concentrated in the cooler part of the year and indoor or early-morning alternatives planned for the rest. The long summer break removes most families from the city and pauses school-based routes, which makes it good for an intensive block elsewhere rather than for sustained local commitment. Plan the eighteen months around those two facts from the start.

faqs.question: Can service done abroad during the summer count?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, subject to the coordinator's approval and proper documentation, and it often produces the most distinctive reflections a portfolio contains. A student spending a summer with family in another country and working with a local organisation has material on global significance and ethics that school-based service rarely generates. Agree it with the coordinator before travelling, arrange for a supervisor to confirm the engagement in writing, and write the reflections while abroad rather than afterwards.

faqs.question: What are the three CAS interviews for?
faqs.answer: The first, near the start, reviews the plan and whether it will evidence the outcomes. The second, roughly mid-programme, checks progress and is the last comfortable opportunity to fix a missing project or an unevidenced outcome. The third, near the end, confirms completion. Students treat them casually because nothing is marked, but they are the only formal checkpoints in eighteen months. Arrive with reflections organised by outcome rather than with an undated activity list.

faqs.question: My child joined DP1 from a British school with no service requirement. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It is a common situation in Dubai and manageable if addressed immediately. The student has the full CAS requirement to build while also adjusting to a new course structure, so the risk is not capability but late realisation that CAS is a Diploma requirement rather than an optional extra. A mapping session in the first term, an early decision on the CAS project, and a reflection habit established from the start handles it. Left until the second year, it becomes genuinely difficult.

faqs.question: Can anyone guarantee that my child's CAS will be signed off?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider suggesting otherwise should be avoided. The school's CAS coordinator is the sole authority on whether CAS has been completed to the school's satisfaction, and no external service can override, substitute for or promise that judgement. What outside help can legitimately do is make the decision easy: map the outcomes, identify gaps early, explain what the project requires, and teach the student to write reflections that evidence what they actually did.

dubai/ib-cas-guidance.closingHeading: Map it in the first term, not the last
dubai/ib-cas-guidance.closingBody: The single most useful hour in CAS is the one where a student lists everything they already do and finds out which of the seven outcomes are unevidenced, because in the first Diploma year those gaps can usually be closed by adjusting commitments they were keeping anyway. The trial session is free, runs over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and ends with a written outcome map to take to the school's coordinator. If your child is already in good shape and simply needs to write better reflections, that is what we will tell you.

dubai/ib-chemistry-ia-help.heroSubtitle: IB chemistry IA help in Dubai, costed openly before anything else. Market rates in Dubai run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 at the premium examiner-branded end, and a Chemistry investigation is a four to six session block rather than a monthly subscription. This page sets out what moves that number and what each dirham actually buys.

dubai/ib-chemistry-ia-help.tutorsIntro: The tutors below supervise Chemistry investigations and quote within the specialist band rather than the generalist one, because the skill being bought is the ability to judge whether a procedure will produce data worth analysing. Each works on the student's own method and results.

intro.heading: Price the help first, because that is the question parents actually ask
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranked pages for tutoring queries in this market publish no price at all, and two of the rest quote in US dollars, which is not what a Dubai family transacts in. One publishes a rate in its structured data that contradicts the figure on the page. So this page starts with money, in dirhams, attributed, and then explains what the money buys.

The ranges, all read in October 2026 from the providers' own pages: Tutopiya advertises from AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65 at the budget online end. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost tables put specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level support at AED 200-450 and above, in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180-350, and independent home tutors at up to AED 500 once travel is priced in. BartyED sits at AED 650 for premium examiner-branded work. Monthly packages seen in the market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

None of those is an IB Gram price list. They are the market, and they matter because a Chemistry investigation is a defined piece of work rather than an open-ended tutoring need, so a family should be able to estimate the whole cost before starting. Four to six sessions is the usual shape: one on procedure feasibility, one on uncertainty and processing, one or two criterion reviews of the student's own draft, and one on evaluation. At mid-range market rates that is a project cost in the high hundreds to low thousands of dirhams, not a monthly subscription.

What the money is buying is a specific competence rather than general chemistry teaching. The investigation is marked out of twenty-four across four criteria of six marks each, and the two that cost Dubai students most are data analysis and evaluation. Both turn on whether the student can carry a burette's uncertainty through to a final enthalpy or rate constant, and whether they can say what an uncontrolled variable did to that number. A tutor who knows the syllabus thoroughly but has never read an investigation against the criteria cannot do that, at any hourly rate.

There is a second reason to be explicit about price here. Chemistry investigations are frequently commissioned rather than coached in this market. Finished Internal Assessments are sold openly, in one documented case at several thousand dirhams, and a student who submits one is risking the whole Diploma rather than a grade. The honest comparison is between a few hundred dirhams of coaching on the student's own work and a few thousand spent on something that could end the Diploma, and it is worth making plainly.

Delivery for UAE families is online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family's address is a service we run only in India. For this task that is also the cheaper and better format, because the session is a spreadsheet, a titration table and a graph on a shared screen, and the in-home market prices a car journey into every hour of exactly that work.

dubai/ib-chemistry-ia-help.programmesIntro: Chemistry appears across the IB continuum and the cost of supporting it changes with the stage, because the scarcity of the required skill changes. Here is how that works at each level.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Chemistry at standard or higher level, with the same scientific investigation required at both and the same four criteria shared with Physics and Biology. Roughly a fifth of the subject grade sits in the investigation, teacher-marked and externally moderated by the IB.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma Chemistry support sits in the specialist market band in Dubai, AED 200-450 and above by Bestimate's figures, because the pool able to supervise an investigation is narrower than the pool able to teach the syllabus. Families comparing quotes should ask specifically whether the tutor has read investigations against the criteria rather than whether they know Chemistry.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Sciences is assessed on four criteria including inquiring and designing and processing and evaluating. The investigations are shorter and the chemistry simpler, but the structure is the same, which is why continuum students arrive at the Diploma already able to write a method that someone else could follow.
programmes.countryNote: MYP science support prices closer to the general qualified-tutor band, around AED 150-300 by Unitors' and Bestimate's published figures, because a wider pool can do it competently. A family paying specialist rates for MYP science investigation help is usually paying for scarcity that is not there.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: CP students taking Diploma Chemistry submit the same investigation against the same criteria, so the support requirement and therefore the cost are unchanged. The core differs, with a reflective project in place of TOK and the Extended Essay.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is a minority route in Dubai and Chemistry is not a common part of CP packages. Where it is taken, families should budget as for a Diploma subject rather than assuming the career-related route reduces internally assessed work or its support cost.

dubai/ib-chemistry-ia-help.subjectsIntro: Cost per mark varies by investigation type, because some chemistry produces analysable data cheaply and some needs equipment and time the school may not have. These are the areas Dubai students choose from, with the practical economics of each.

subjects.name: Acid-base titration studies
subjects.description: The cheapest reliable route to good data. Burette and pipette uncertainties are easy to state and propagate, equipment is universal, and repeats are quick. Marks are decided by whether concordant titres are achieved and by how uncertainty reaches the final concentration.

subjects.name: Enthalpy and calorimetry
subjects.description: Inexpensive and leaky. Heat loss dominates and must be quantified or modelled rather than noted. Investigations that measure the loss separately, or extrapolate a cooling curve, move from a middling evaluation to a strong one without any extra apparatus.

subjects.name: Rates of reaction and order determination
subjects.description: Good value because timing data is cheap and the analysis is genuinely demanding. Initial-rate methods with a clear linearisation support strong data analysis marks; continuous monitoring without a plan for processing usually does not.

subjects.name: Arrhenius and activation energy
subjects.description: Higher level ground with a clean linearisation: the logarithm of the rate constant against the reciprocal of temperature. Needs reliable temperature control, which in a school laboratory means a water bath and patience rather than money.

subjects.name: Colorimetry and the Beer-Lambert relationship
subjects.description: Depends on a colorimeter or spectrophotometer being available, which varies across Dubai schools. Where available it produces excellent linear data with small uncertainties, which shifts the marking pressure onto evaluation.

subjects.name: Equilibrium and solubility studies
subjects.description: Conceptually strong and practically slow, because systems need time to reach equilibrium and repeats multiply the laboratory hours required. Worth it only where laboratory access is genuinely available for multiple sessions.

subjects.name: Organic synthesis and percentage yield
subjects.description: Expensive in reagents and technician time, and the yield depends on steps a student cannot fully control. Attractive to students and often a poor economic choice unless the school has already indicated the apparatus is available.

subjects.name: Electrochemistry and cell potentials
subjects.description: Equipment is usually present and the measurements are quick, but drift and electrode condition introduce systematic effects that must be identified. Those systematic effects are an opportunity for evaluation marks rather than a problem.

subjects.name: Buffer capacity and pH studies
subjects.description: Cheap, repeatable and underused. The pH meter's calibration becomes a genuine uncertainty discussion, and the relationship between added acid and pH change supports a defensible quantitative conclusion.

subjects.name: Food and consumer chemistry investigations
subjects.description: Popular because the context feels real, and risky because sample variability is often larger than the effect being measured. Only sensible with a clear plan for controlling the material before data collection begins.

dubai/ib-chemistry-ia-help.regionsIntro: What a family pays is affected less by where they live than by how they buy, but laboratory access and the local school mix shape the shape of the block. These are the Dubai areas we hear from most.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Sufouh
regions.note: The densest IB cluster in the emirate, with well-equipped laboratories. Blocks here are usually short, three or four sessions, because the data is already good and the work is processing and evaluation.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and The Meadows
regions.note: Established IB provision alongside British schools. Transition students from IGCSE Chemistry need an extra session on reporting conventions, which is the main reason a block runs to six rather than four.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Meydan
regions.note: Large continuum schools where laboratory time for individual investigations is contested. Families here benefit most from a feasibility session, because an unavailable procedure is the costliest mistake in the whole project.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Continuum schools with small higher level Chemistry sets. With few peers to compare against, families often pay for a draft review they would not have needed in a larger cohort.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Sobha Hartland
regions.note: Newer Diploma cohorts with new laboratories and thin exemplar bases. The common pattern is good equipment, an ambitious procedure chosen from an online list, and a feasibility problem discovered late.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Mixed British and IB provision along the coast. Evening slots dominate, and data processing work fits that hour better than conceptual teaching, which keeps blocks efficient.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Motor City
regions.note: Villa communities feeding established Diploma schools. The in-home market quotes a premium to reach these communities at peak hours, which is the clearest local argument for working on screen.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and Umm Al Sheif
schoolClusters.note: Dubai's thickest concentration of IB World Schools, generally with good chemistry facilities and technician support. Support blocks from this cluster tend to be short and focused on processing rather than on procedure.

schoolClusters.city: Nad Al Sheba, Mirdif, Dubai Hills and Al Jaddaf
schoolClusters.note: Continuum and Diploma schools across the eastern and southern communities. Competition for laboratory time and small higher level sets are the two features that most often lengthen a support block here.

sections.heading: What Chemistry IA support costs in Dubai, in dirhams
paragraphs: Here is the whole market in one table, with each figure attributed to the provider that published it and dated to when it was read. The pattern across the Dubai tutoring market is a wide budget tier, a broad middle, and a premium tier defined mostly by branding rather than by a different service. Chemistry investigation support sits in the specialist band because the required skill, judging and processing uncertainty and reading a draft against the criteria, is scarcer than subject teaching.

A family should read this as an upper and lower bound on a block rather than as a rate card. Four sessions at AED 200 is AED 800. Six sessions at AED 350 is AED 2,100. That range covers almost every Chemistry investigation arrangement a Dubai family will need, and anything materially above it should prompt the question of what additional service is being supplied.

What should not be read into these figures is a quality ranking. The premium band buys brand and sometimes examiner experience; it does not automatically buy somebody who has read Chemistry investigations against the four criteria. The budget band occasionally includes someone who has, usually a working teacher supplementing income. The reliable filter is not the price but the question in the next section.

One note on comparing quotes. Published hourly rates in this market frequently exclude written feedback between sessions, which for investigation work is a material part of the service. A quote of AED 250 with written criterion notes included can be better value than AED 180 without them, because the notes are what the student revises from.

sections.heading: The five things that actually move the number
paragraphs: Families assume level drives price, and it does not much. A standard level Chemistry investigation and a higher level one are marked against the same four criteria and take similar support. What moves the number is scarcity of the specific skill, how the hours are bought, and what is bundled in.

Scarcity first. Anyone can teach titration calculations. Fewer people can look at a set of titres, judge whether they are concordant, propagate the burette and pipette uncertainties to a final concentration and then say what the evaluation has to quantify. That second skill is what the specialist band prices, and it is the skill that moves the marks.

Second, how the hours are bought. Block and single-session purchases cost more per hour and less in total than a monthly arrangement, because an investigation does not need weekly contact for a year. Third, what is included: written criterion feedback between sessions, draft turnaround time and whether a diagnostic report is supplied all vary and are rarely stated in a headline rate. Fourth, timing: demand concentrates in the weeks before internal deadlines, and availability at those hours is tighter.

The fifth factor is the one families control most. A student who arrives with clean data, a stated procedure and a complete results table needs three sessions. A student who arrives with a procedure that cannot produce analysable data needs a feasibility conversation, a repeat laboratory session and then the three. The single cheapest intervention in the whole project is therefore the earliest one, and the most expensive mistake is starting support after the laboratory work is finished.

sections.heading: What twenty-four marks are being bought
paragraphs: Value only means something against what is being purchased, so here is the thing itself. The Chemistry investigation is up to about 3,000 words, marked out of twenty-four across four criteria worth six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The school teacher marks it, the IB moderates a sample, and it carries roughly a fifth of the subject grade at both levels.

In Chemistry specifically, the marks concentrate in two places. Data analysis demands that uncertainties from glassware, balances and probes are carried through the calculation to the final quantity, which for a titration means the burette's uncertainty counted at both the start and the end reading, combined with the pipette and the balance, and expressed as a range on the final concentration or enthalpy. Evaluation demands that each limitation carries a magnitude and a direction, so heat loss is not merely mentioned but estimated.

Research design in Chemistry is mostly about controlling variables that are chemically significant rather than obviously so. Temperature matters because rate constants depend on it. Concentration of a supposedly excess reagent matters if it is not genuinely in excess. The age of a solution matters where it decomposes. A method that controls the obvious and ignores the chemically consequential is the characteristic weak design in this subject.

Confirm the current criteria and the word limit in the Chemistry subject guide your child's teacher is working from. The IB publishes the authoritative version, revises guides on a cycle, and the guide in use at the school governs.

sections.heading: Where the money earns marks in a Chemistry investigation
paragraphs: If a family is paying for four sessions, the highest-return allocation is clear from the pattern of Dubai drafts. One session on the procedure before laboratory work, one on uncertainty arithmetic, one reading the draft criterion by criterion, and one rebuilding the evaluation. That ordering matters: a procedure session after data collection cannot fix a procedure, and an evaluation session before the data exists has nothing to evaluate.

The procedure session pays because unanalysable data is unrecoverable. A student who runs a reaction at room temperature without recording it, or whose titres never converge, has produced an investigation with a ceiling regardless of how well it is written up. Thirty minutes checking the method against the question would have prevented it.

The uncertainty session pays across three criteria at once, exactly as in Physics but with different arithmetic: the burette read twice, the pipette's tolerance, the balance resolution, and in calorimetry the temperature probe, all combined and then carried to the final value. Once that is in place the conclusion can state whether a literature value falls inside the experimental range and the evaluation can rank limitations by size.

The evaluation session pays because it is the weakest criterion in most drafts and the easiest to improve without new data. Converting a list of five weaknesses into three quantified effects with one targeted improvement is an evening's work for the student and usually moves a band. It is the single clearest example in this task of a mark gained by thinking rather than by spending.

sections.heading: Hidden extras in the Dubai tutoring market
paragraphs: Headline rates in this market are frequently incomplete, and the gaps are consistent enough to list. Written feedback between sessions is the biggest one: for investigation work the criterion notes are what the student revises from, and some providers charge for them separately or not at all. Ask whether they are included in the quoted figure before comparing two quotes.

Second, session length. A quoted hourly rate sometimes refers to a fifty-minute session, and sometimes a provider's minimum booking is ninety minutes, which changes the real cost of a short diagnostic conversation. Third, cancellation and rescheduling terms, which matter in a city where travel and school events disrupt plans frequently. Fourth, whether a free trial is genuinely free or conditional on a subsequent booking; if a condition applies it should be stated on the same screen as the offer.

Fifth, tax. Ask any provider whether the figure quoted is the amount that will be charged, including any applicable tax, and get the answer in writing. We make no claim here about how tuition is treated for value added tax purposes, because that is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority rather than for a tutoring page; the practical point is simply that a quote should be the final number.

Sixth, and most important for Chemistry specifically, ask what the provider will and will not do with the investigation itself. A provider willing to supply processed data, write sections or hand over a finished document is offering something that puts the Diploma at risk, and the price of that is not the price of tutoring. The correct answer is that the tutor teaches, questions and marks, and the student writes.

sections.heading: What the in-home travel premium actually buys
paragraphs: Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one tutoring in Dubai at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoting up to AED 500, against an online specialist band of AED 200-450. Those overlap, which means the honest comparison is not simply cheaper against dearer. It is about what the premium at the top of the in-home range buys for this particular task.

For a Chemistry investigation it buys very little. The work is a results table, a propagation calculation and a graph, all on a screen. An in-home tutor and the student look at one laptop; an online tutor and the student look at the same document with live annotation and the student keeps the file. The in-home option additionally constrains who is available to whoever can reach your community at the hour your child is free, which in a small higher level Chemistry set is a severe restriction.

Where in-home genuinely helps is with younger children, with students who need physical presence to stay on task, and with practical demonstrations. None of those describes a seventeen-year-old processing titration data. The travel premium in this market is a real cost that buys a real benefit for some tasks, and this is not one of them.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; tutors travelling to a family's address is a service we run only in India. That is stated plainly rather than hidden, because the phrase parents search is a home tutor and the honest answer for this component is that the online format is better as well as cheaper.

sections.heading: Budgeting a Chemistry IA from start to submission
paragraphs: A worked budget is more useful than a rate, so here are three realistic shapes. The minimum arrangement is one diagnostic session on the draft, which at the specialist band is AED 200-450 and frequently enough for a student who is competent and merely uncertain. The standard arrangement is a four-session block covering procedure, uncertainty, a criterion review and the evaluation, which lands at roughly AED 800-1,800 in total at market rates.

The extended arrangement, six sessions, applies where the student is also weak on the underlying chemistry, where the procedure needs redesigning after a failed laboratory session, or where a transition student needs reporting conventions taught from scratch. That reaches roughly AED 1,200-2,700 at market rates. Beyond six sessions the honest diagnosis is usually that the student needs syllabus teaching rather than investigation coaching, and that should be bought as what it is.

Set against the alternatives, those numbers are modest. Bestimate's monthly estimate for specialist exam-year weekly tutoring is AED 1,000-2,000 a month, so a complete investigation block costs about what one month of weekly subject tutoring does. The in-home monthly packages seen in this market, AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour sessions, cost more than a full investigation block for eight hours of someone's time plus their travel.

The comparison nobody makes openly is with buying a finished investigation, which is available in this market at several thousand dirhams. That spend purchases a document the student cannot defend, submitted under an academic honesty declaration they have to sign, with the Diploma itself at risk if it is detected. A four-session block on the student's own work costs less and puts nothing at risk, and that is the comparison a family deserves to see written down.

faqs.question: How much does Chemistry IA help cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates read in October 2026 run from AED 33-52 at Tutopiya and AED 45-65 at EdFlik at the budget end, through Unitors at AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB, TutorChase at AED 270, and Bestimate's AED 200-450 and above for specialist IB and IGCSE support, up to AED 650 at BartyED. Chemistry investigation work sits in the specialist band because judging and propagating uncertainty is scarcer than syllabus teaching. These are the market's figures, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: What should a whole Chemistry investigation block cost?
faqs.answer: At market specialist rates, a four-session block covering procedure feasibility, uncertainty arithmetic, a criterion review and an evaluation rebuild comes to roughly AED 800-1,800 in total. A single diagnostic session is AED 200-450 and is often enough. Six sessions, where reporting conventions or a procedure redesign are needed, reaches roughly AED 1,200-2,700. Beyond that the real need is usually syllabus teaching rather than investigation coaching, and it should be bought as that instead.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper tutor worse value for an IA?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, but the filter is not the rate. The question is whether the person has read Chemistry investigations against the four criteria and can propagate a burette's uncertainty through to a final concentration. Someone at AED 150 who has done that is better value than someone at AED 400 who has not, and both exist in this market. Ask the question directly before booking. A tutor who answers in general terms about knowing the syllabus is answering a different question.

faqs.question: Does the price change between standard and higher level Chemistry?
faqs.answer: Much less than families expect. The investigation is marked against the same four criteria at both levels and takes similar support, so the rate is driven by the tutor's criterion experience rather than by the level. What does change the total is the complexity of the procedure: an Arrhenius study or an organic synthesis needs more laboratory time and more processing support than a titration study, which can add a session or two to the block.

faqs.question: Are monthly tutoring packages good value for a Chemistry IA?
faqs.answer: Usually not, because an investigation is a defined piece of work with a deadline rather than an ongoing need. Market monthly packages include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, and Bestimate estimates AED 600-2,000 or more a month for weekly tutoring. A monthly arrangement makes sense where the student needs the Chemistry syllabus taught; for the investigation alone, a four-session block costs less and finishes.

faqs.question: What hidden charges should I ask about before booking?
faqs.answer: Six things. Whether written criterion feedback between sessions is included in the quoted rate, because for investigation work that is what the student revises from. Whether a session is sixty minutes and what the minimum booking is. The cancellation and rescheduling terms. Whether a free trial carries any condition, which should be stated alongside the offer. Whether the quoted figure is the final amount charged including any applicable tax. And what the provider will refuse to do with the student's own work.

faqs.question: Why is in-home Chemistry tutoring more expensive in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because travel is priced into every hour. Bestimate quotes in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors up to AED 500, against an online specialist band of AED 200-450. For a Chemistry investigation the premium buys little, since the work is a results table, a propagation calculation and a graph on a screen. It also limits the tutor pool to whoever can reach your community at your child's free hour, which in a small higher level set may be nobody suitable.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; tutors travelling to a family's address is a service we run only in India. UAE tuition is delivered one-to-one online over live video with a shared screen. For investigation work that is the better format as well as the cheaper one, because the session is a shared document with live annotation and the student keeps the annotated file for revision afterwards.

faqs.question: How much of the Chemistry grade does the investigation carry?
faqs.answer: Roughly a fifth, at both standard and higher level. It is marked out of twenty-four by the school teacher across four criteria of six marks each, research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and the IB moderates a sample of each school's marking. That makes it the most controllable part of the course, which is the case for spending a few hundred dirhams on it rather than on additional examination practice. Confirm the weighting in the current subject guide.

faqs.question: Where do Chemistry investigations lose the most marks?
faqs.answer: In data analysis and evaluation. Glassware uncertainties get recorded in the table and then vanish from the calculation, so the final concentration or enthalpy is quoted with a precision the data cannot support. Evaluation is then written as a list of weaknesses with no magnitudes, when the criterion asks what each one did to the number and in which direction. Heat loss mentioned is worth little; heat loss estimated and shown to account for a stated share of the discrepancy is worth a band.

faqs.question: Can we buy a finished Chemistry IA instead?
faqs.answer: Operators in this market sell completed Internal Assessments, in one documented case at several thousand dirhams, and a student who submits one is risking the entire Diploma rather than a grade. Both student and supervisor sign academic honesty declarations, and malpractice consequences fall on the student. IB Gram declines that work at any price. A four-session block coaching the student's own investigation costs considerably less and puts nothing at risk, which is the comparison worth having in front of you.

faqs.question: When is the cheapest time to start getting help?
faqs.answer: Before the laboratory work. A thirty-minute check on whether the procedure can produce analysable data is the single cheapest intervention in the project, and the most expensive mistake is starting support after data collection, when an unworkable method can no longer be changed. Families who book one session at the procedure stage frequently need only one more later; families who book after the draft is written often need three or four because the data constrains everything.

faqs.question: Which Chemistry investigation topics are cheapest to support?
faqs.answer: Titration studies, calorimetry, buffer and pH work and simple rate experiments, because the equipment is universal in Dubai school laboratories, repeats are quick and the uncertainty arithmetic is standard. The expensive end is organic synthesis, which consumes reagents and technician time and depends on steps a student cannot fully control, and equilibrium studies, which need multiple laboratory sessions for systems to settle. Ask the Chemistry teacher what can actually be booked before committing to a topic.

faqs.question: Is one session ever enough?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and we will say so when it is. A competent student with clean data and a complete draft often needs nothing more than a single diagnostic hour that places each of the four criteria and names the two jobs that matter, which at market specialist rates is AED 200-450. Families who are told after one session that no further sessions are warranted have had good value from that hour, and a provider who always finds more to sell should be treated with some scepticism.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Chemistry to Dubai students on live video at Standard and Higher Level. Each marks to the published scheme rather than to impression, writes feedback against named criteria, and keeps the record so a parent can compare October with March instead of relying on a recollection of either.

intro.heading: What the record shows, and what it stops you believing
paragraphs: Chemistry is a subject in which a student can feel competent and score in the middle for two years, and the reason is that the feeling and the mark measure different things. Understanding why a reaction proceeds is pleasant and insufficient. Producing the correct quantity of product to three significant figures, from a balanced equation and a mass that needed converting first, is what the mark scheme pays for. A record of marked work is the only thing that distinguishes the two, which is why every session on this plan produces one.

The record is deliberately plain. A dated list of topics with a mark against each from a timed question, an annotated script showing where each lost mark went, and for the investigation a versioned draft so that the research question's narrowing is visible rather than asserted. Parents receive it the same evening. Nobody enjoys reading it and it answers the only question that matters: is this moving, and in which direction. It is also the only document in the file that a school will engage with seriously, because it is written in the school's own currency: a mark, against a question, from a published scheme. A parent arriving at a subject meeting with four dated scripts is having a different conversation from a parent arriving with a worry.

The first entry in the file is always the mole. Mole calculations carry into concentration and titration, into electrolysis and Faraday relationships, into enthalpy calculations per mole, into equilibrium expressions and into every yield question in organic chemistry. A student who is slow or unreliable on moles is losing marks across six topics for one reason, and that pattern is invisible in a report card and obvious in a marked script. Measuring it takes twenty minutes.

The second entry is command-term discipline. Chemistry mark schemes pay for specific verbs: state, describe, explain, deduce, justify, outline and distinguish each buy something different, and a student who answers everything as a description loses marks across both papers simultaneously. It looks like a chemistry problem and is a habit, and the record shows it because the same category of loss repeats week after week until the habit changes.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For a record-based plan that is an advantage: the annotated script, the marked calculation and the commented draft all exist as files rather than as paper that leaves the house, so March can be compared with October directly. A Dubai family in Mirdif or Dubai Hills also gets a Chemistry specialist at the right level rather than whichever science tutor is within a short drive.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor.programmesIntro: Chemistry arrives in a Dubai Diploma classroom from several directions, and the record a student brings with them, or does not, determines what the first month of support is spent on.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences, Years 4 and 5
programmes.description: Criterion-assessed science covering knowledge, inquiry and design, processing and evaluating, and reflection. Students arrive well prepared for the Diploma investigation and frequently light on calculation volume, because MYP assessment does not demand repeated quantitative work under time pressure.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai's full-continuum IB World Schools this is the standard route into Diploma chemistry, and the first marked timed paper is usually where the calculation gap appears. It is a gap in practice rather than in understanding, which is why it closes faster than families expect once it is measured.

programmes.name: IGCSE Chemistry into Diploma chemistry
programmes.description: Cambridge 0620 or Edexcel 4CH1 leaves a student with solid qualitative chemistry and partial quantitative fluency. Moles appear at IGCSE but at a level that permits workarounds, and those workarounds fail at Diploma level where multi-step stoichiometry is routine rather than exceptional.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools dominate Dubai enrolment, so many Diploma chemists arrive from IGCSE. The specific carry-over problem is a student who passed 0620 by learning reaction facts and avoiding calculation questions, a strategy that produced a good grade and no transferable fluency.

programmes.name: IB Chemistry Standard Level
programmes.description: Two written papers plus the internally assessed investigation at 20 per cent. Paper 1 combines multiple-choice with a data-based section; Paper 2 is extended response and carries the largest weighting. Required by some life-science and medical routes without Higher Level, and not a soft option.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Dubai school teaches both levels together for part of the course, Standard Level students sometimes meet Higher Level material and conclude they are behind. Confirming which content is assessed at their own level is a short conversation with a real effect on both confidence and revision efficiency.

programmes.name: IB Chemistry Higher Level
programmes.description: The same structure with substantially more content and longer papers, extending organic chemistry, equilibrium, acid-base theory, energetics and electrochemistry. Expected by most medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and chemical engineering routes, which makes the level decision a university decision as well as an academic one.
programmes.countryNote: Higher Level chemistry demand in this emirate concentrates among students targeting medicine, which means the same weeks of the final year see the same surge in requests. The record built in Diploma Year 1 is what makes the Year 13 plan short rather than exploratory.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor.subjectsIntro: Chemistry support is organised by topic for teaching and by component for marks. These are the units a plan is built from, with what the record typically shows about each.

subjects.name: Moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: The load-bearing calculation of the entire subject. Mass to moles, moles to volume, limiting reagent, percentage yield and atom economy. A weakness here reappears in titration, electrolysis, energetics, equilibrium and organic yield questions, which is why it is the first entry in the record.

subjects.name: Bonding and structure
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Ionic, covalent and metallic bonding, intermolecular forces and molecular geometry. Marks go to explanations that name the specific force and relate it to the observed property, rather than to a correct general statement about strength.

subjects.name: Energetics and thermochemistry
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Enthalpy changes, calorimetry, Hess's law and at Higher Level entropy and spontaneity. Every calculation is per mole, so the mole weakness surfaces here first. Sign conventions are the second most common loss in marked scripts.

subjects.name: Kinetics
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Rate, collision theory and catalysis, with rate equations, orders and mechanisms at Higher Level. Graph interpretation is decisive: reading an initial rate from a tangent, determining an order from concentration data, and relating a mechanism to a rate-determining step.

subjects.name: Equilibrium
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Dynamic equilibrium and Le Chatelier at both levels, with equilibrium constant calculations at Higher Level. The common script failure is predicting a shift correctly and then explaining it in terms of the constant changing, which it does not.

subjects.name: Acids, bases and redox
subjects.levels: SL and HL, substantially extended at HL
subjects.description: Titration, pH, buffers at Higher Level, oxidation states, electrochemical cells and electrolysis. Two of the subject's most calculation-heavy areas sit here, and both run on mole work plus careful unit handling.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry
subjects.levels: SL and HL, substantially extended at HL
subjects.description: Functional groups, reaction types and at Higher Level mechanisms, stereochemistry and synthetic routes. Students who learn reactions as isolated facts stall at Higher Level; the ones who hold reagent and condition together with the transformation can construct a route they have never seen.

subjects.name: Paper 1
subjects.description: Multiple-choice plus a data-based section, with the data booklet available. The data section discriminates: reading a spectrum, using tabulated values correctly, and identifying what a plotted line actually represents. Drilling multiple-choice alone leaves it untouched.

subjects.name: Paper 2
subjects.description: Extended response across the syllabus and the largest component in the course. This is where command-term discipline and multi-step calculation decide the grade, and where the weekly marked script does most of its work.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.levels: SL and HL · 20 per cent · 24 marks
subjects.description: An individual investigation with a 3,000-word ceiling, assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at six marks each. In chemistry the usual failure is a question whose measurable output is qualitative, which leaves the data analysis criterion nothing to reward.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor.regionsIntro: Online delivery means the record travels and the tutor does not. What the postcode changes is when a session can start and whether a timed paper can realistically be sat on a weekday evening.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JLT
regions.note: Short commutes and apartment study space. Timed chemistry papers need a clear desk and ninety uninterrupted minutes, which in these buildings is easier at five in the afternoon than at eight in the evening.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Several IB World Schools within a short radius and large chemistry cohorts, often with separate Standard and Higher Level groups. Internal rankings here say little about the paper itself, which is what makes an independently marked script useful.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches, Mudon and Damac Hills
regions.note: Long bus routes and heavy after-school commitments. Sessions run at 6.30pm or later, so the timed paper is set for a weekend morning and the session is spent on the marked version of it.

regions.name: Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim and Al Safa
regions.note: Established Diploma programmes with well-equipped laboratories, so chemistry investigations here are usually limited by the research question rather than by apparatus. Support is better spent on design and uncertainty than on logistics.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais
regions.note: A high share of students arriving from IGCSE chemistry, typically strong on reaction facts and partial on stoichiometry. The mole diagnostic matters most in this cluster because the IGCSE grade frequently conceals the gap.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Short commutes make a 4.30pm chemistry slot realistic, which is the best time of day for calculation work. Families here often run a Diploma student and an IGCSE sibling in consecutive slots.

regions.name: Al Furjan, Discovery Gardens and Dubai South
regions.note: Newer Diploma provision with smaller chemistry cohorts and sometimes one teacher across both levels. With no parallel group to benchmark against, the external marked record is often the only independent data a family holds.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai IB schools with separate Higher Level chemistry groups
schoolClusters.note: Mature Diploma programmes where Standard and Higher Level run as distinct teaching groups with established laboratory routines. Families here usually want an independent mark rather than teaching, particularly in the medicine-targeting cohort.

schoolClusters.city: Newer Diploma chemistry provision
schoolClusters.note: Smaller cohorts, sometimes with both levels taught together for part of the course. The common first need is confirming which content is assessed at the student's own level, which is a cheap intervention with a measurable effect.

schoolClusters.city: IGCSE chemistry feeder schools
schoolClusters.note: British-curriculum schools whose Year 11 chemists join Diploma programmes elsewhere in the emirate. Cambridge 0620 and Edexcel 4CH1 leavers arrive with different balances of qualitative knowledge and calculation practice.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor.modesIntro: Three shapes of work produce three different kinds of record, and a chemistry plan usually needs two of them running at once.

modes.title: Weekly marked-script session
modes.description: Sixty minutes a week built around a timed question sat between sessions and marked to the published scheme before the next. Twenty minutes reviewing the marked work, thirty teaching what it exposed, ten setting the next task. The annotated script and the updated topic record go to the parent the same evening.
