modes.title: Calculation fluency block
modes.description: Thirty-minute sessions two or three times a week for a few weeks, on moles, concentration, limiting reagent, yield and unit conversion. Measured by timed sets of twenty items counted week to week. It contains no new chemistry and it routinely produces the largest single movement on Paper 2.

The student designs, collects and writes every word; the tutor questions and marks, and every version is kept.

sections.heading: What an IB chemistry tutor in Dubai should leave behind
paragraphs: An IB chemistry tutor in Dubai should be judged by the file, not by the session. A session can be enjoyable, well explained and entirely undirected. A file cannot: it either shows marks against dated topics moving in one direction or it does not. The three documents that make up the file are an annotated script per session, a topic record updated and dated each time, and for the investigation a versioned draft. Nothing else is required and nothing less is sufficient.

The reason this matters in chemistry specifically is the gap between comprehension and performance. Chemistry rewards explanation, and a student who can explain why an equilibrium shifts feels, correctly, that they understand the chemistry. The mark scheme asks them to calculate the new concentration to three significant figures having first converted a volume. Comprehension and performance diverge quietly, and only a marked script catches it.

The second reason is that chemistry failures are categorical rather than scattered. Marked scripts sort losses into a small number of recurring types: a mole conversion done late, a sign convention reversed, an explanation given where a deduction was asked, a significant-figure convention ignored, a graph read without units. Those categories repeat, which means the record predicts. After four weeks the file says what the next four weeks should contain without anyone guessing.

The third is the parent's position. A Dubai parent who was not in the room has three sources of information about their child's chemistry: the child, the school report, and a tutor's summary. The first two are compressed and the third is interested. An annotated script with a mark on it is none of those things, which is why it goes out the same evening rather than being described in a monthly call.
bullets: Three documents: annotated script, dated topic record, versioned draft

sections.heading: The chemistry record, week by week
paragraphs: A record only works if it is collected to a schedule, so here is the schedule. Week one is diagnostic and contains no teaching: a mole fluency set, a timed structured question on recently taught content, and a short unit-conversion set. Those three produce the baseline. Weeks two to five run the weekly cycle: a question sat between sessions, marked before the session, reviewed in the first twenty minutes. Week six is a comparison week, in which the week-one diagnostics are re-sat and the two results placed side by side.

The six-week cycle then repeats, which gives a Dubai family three or four comparison points across a Diploma year. That is enough to see a trend and few enough that the student is being taught rather than tested. Between the formal points the weekly marked question feeds the topic record continuously, so a topic that moves from amber to green has a date and a script behind it.

The investigation runs on a separate track with its own record, because its deadlines belong to the school rather than to the tutoring plan. Each session on it produces a commented version of the student's own document, and the versions are kept. A research question that started broad and ended answerable has a visible history, and that history is itself evidence that the thinking was the student's.

The table below is the schedule as used. Dubai school calendars differ, and the comparison weeks are better placed just after a long break than just before one, because a re-sat diagnostic after the December break measures retention rather than recency and retention is the more useful number.

sections.heading: The mole is the first thing the record measures
paragraphs: Mole calculations are the load-bearing arithmetic of Diploma chemistry, and a weakness in them is not contained. Concentration and titration run on moles. Electrolysis and Faraday relationships run on moles. Enthalpy changes are quoted per mole. Equilibrium expressions are built from concentrations derived from moles. Percentage yield and atom economy in organic chemistry are mole ratios. A student unreliable on the conversion is losing marks in six topics for one reason, and in a report card that appears as general weakness in chemistry.

The diagnostic is twenty items, timed, with no context: mass to moles and back, concentration to moles given a volume in the wrong unit, limiting reagent in a two-reactant equation, moles of gas at a stated condition, and percentage yield from an actual and theoretical mass. Count the correct answers and record the time. A student who is accurate but slow has a different problem from one who is fast and wrong, and the two need different interventions.

The intervention for slowness is frequency rather than duration: thirty-minute sessions two or three times a week, twenty items each, counted and compared. It contains no new chemistry, which has a useful consequence for a Dubai family's budget — this work does not require a specialist rate, because the content is not Diploma-specific. Buying it at the specialist band is a waste, and buying Diploma content teaching before fixing it is a larger one.

The re-measurement is the part that makes it a record rather than an exercise. The same twenty items, re-sat four weeks later, with both scores in the file. Movement on that number is the most reliable predictor of movement on Paper 2 that this subject offers, and it is available for an outlay that sits at the bottom of the published market range rather than the top.
bullets: Moles carry into concentration, titration, electrolysis, energetics, equilibrium and yield
Twenty timed items, scored and timed, separates slow from inaccurate

sections.heading: Organic chemistry: facts against routes
paragraphs: Organic chemistry is where a Dubai Diploma student's method of learning becomes visible. Students who learned IGCSE chemistry as a set of reaction facts can usually recall that an alcohol oxidises to a carboxylic acid. Asked to construct a three-step route from an alkene to an ester, they stall, because the route requires holding reagent, condition and transformation together rather than recalling a pair.

The fix is structural and it shows up in the record quickly. Build the reaction set as a table rather than a list: starting functional group, reagent, condition, product, and the transformation type. Once the same information is organised by transformation, a student can read a route backwards from the target, which is how synthesis questions are actually answered. At Higher Level the mechanism layer sits on top of the same organisation, and students who built the table first find mechanisms considerably easier than students who learned reactions as isolated facts.

The second organic failure is notation. Marks go for structures drawn with the correct number of bonds, for naming that follows the convention rather than approximates it, and for mechanisms with arrows that start from the right place. Those are precision errors rather than understanding errors, they are visible on a marked script immediately, and they repeat until someone enforces them in marking. A student losing two marks a paper to arrow placement is losing a grade boundary's worth across the course.

The third is stereochemistry at Higher Level, where the common loss is describing a relationship correctly in words and failing to represent it. Drawing practice is unglamorous, it is the thing students most readily skip in favour of reading, and it is the only thing that moves the mark. The record makes skipping it visible, because the same category of loss keeps appearing in the weekly script.

sections.heading: The investigation, drafted on the record
paragraphs: The internally assessed investigation carries 20 per cent of the chemistry grade, has a 3,000-word ceiling, and is marked out of 24 across four criteria at six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. A fifth of the grade is awarded for work done without time pressure, which makes it the most recoverable portion of the course and the portion most often left until the term when every other Diploma deadline arrives.

In chemistry the dominant design failure is a research question whose output is qualitative. A colour change observed, a precipitate formed, a reaction that went faster — none of those gives the data analysis criterion anything to reward. The question has to produce numbers, enough of them, across enough values of a genuinely variable independent quantity. Testing that before any apparatus is booked is the single highest-value hour in the process, and it is also the hour that most often results in the question being rewritten.

Uncertainty is the second. Chemistry investigations involve measuring instruments with stated uncertainties, and the data analysis and evaluation criteria both depend on those uncertainties being recorded during collection, propagated through the calculation, and then used to say something specific about the reliability of the conclusion. Reconstructed afterwards it is obvious, and it reads as the afterthought it was. Taught before collection it is straightforward.

The boundary is firm, and stating it protects the student. A tutor may teach experimental design, question whether a question can generate usable data, teach uncertainty treatment, name the criteria and their marks, and give written feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not design the experiment, supply data, or write any part of the report. Work that is not the student's own produces a malpractice finding against the student rather than against whoever sold it. One UAE-facing site advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, which is the clearest example in this market of a thing to refuse.

sections.heading: Higher and Standard Level chemistry, decided from the file
paragraphs: Both levels share the component structure and the four investigation criteria. Higher Level adds substantial content, concentrated in organic chemistry, equilibrium constants, acid-base theory including buffers, energetics including entropy and spontaneity, and electrochemistry. Papers are longer. The additions are calculation-heavier than the shared content, which is why the mole and fluency record predicts Higher Level success better than any report grade.

The level conversation should therefore be read off the file rather than discussed in the abstract. Losses concentrated in two or three named topics indicate content, and content responds to teaching across eighteen months. Losses spread evenly across every topic and question type, with the calculation fluency score flat across two comparison points, indicate that the level is the issue. That is an uncomfortable reading and it is better delivered in the first term of Diploma Year 1 than in the second term of Year 13.

University requirements are the other input and they are published by the universities themselves. Most medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and chemical engineering routes expect Higher Level chemistry; some biological and environmental science courses accept Standard Level; a few state a chemistry requirement without specifying level. Reading the actual requirement for the actual courses on a student's list is an afternoon's work and it settles more of the decision than any amount of discussion.

One cheap and frequently overlooked check belongs here. Where a Dubai school teaches both levels in the same room for part of the course, confirm which content is assessed at the student's own level. Standard Level students who have sat through Higher Level buffer calculations and concluded they cannot do chemistry are commoner than they should be, and the remedy is a syllabus comparison rather than a term of tutoring.

sections.heading: Cost, regulation and the Dubai chemistry context
paragraphs: Published rates in this emirate, read in October 2026: Unitors lists IB tuition from AED 200 an hour and IGCSE from AED 150, TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist work, and the Bestimate rate survey puts IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above, with premium named listings reaching AED 650 at BartyED. Budget online provision starts at AED 33-52 at Tutopiya and AED 45-65 at EdFlik. Chemistry is better supplied in this market than Higher Level physics, which usually places it mid-band rather than at the top.

A record-based plan has a useful cost property: it tells you when to stop. Where the comparison week shows the calculation score has risen and the weekly losses have moved from calculation to content, the drilling block ends. Where the topic record goes green across the board, the frequency drops. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240-600 at the budget tier, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work, and the point of the record is to spend as little time in the upper band as the evidence permits.

Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects annually against six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. The sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25 offering 17 curricula, with seven new schools approved for the 2026-27 intake, three of them International Baccalaureate, adding 16,846 places. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for 2026-27.

Three points of record. The mandatory subjects — Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral studies — are taught in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and the use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education prohibited. Private tutoring requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. And IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, the Ministry of Education or the International Baccalaureate, operates no UAE office, and references rather than reproduces IB syllabus material.

process.title: Send the level and the last marked paper
process.description: The useful opening message says Standard or Higher Level, names the topics currently taught, and attaches a photograph of the most recent marked paper. The script is the start of the record. Without it the first session is spent generating evidence the student has already produced once.

process.title: Free 30-minute trial lesson, one per family
process.description: Live video with the matched tutor, no card details taken, no obligation. It is spent on one structured question marked live against the published scheme, with the withheld mark explained. That shows the marking standard that will populate the record, which is the thing being bought.

process.title: The three baseline diagnostics
process.description: A twenty-item mole fluency set, a timed structured question on taught content, and a short unit-conversion set. Scored and timed. Those three decide whether the plan opens with drilling at the lower band or with Diploma content at the specialist band, and that sequencing decision is usually worth more than the choice of tutor.

process.title: Weekly cycle, marked before the session
process.description: A timed question sat between sessions and marked to the published scheme before the next slot, so every session opens with current evidence. The annotated script and the dated topic record go to the parent the same evening, with each lost mark categorised rather than merely counted.

process.title: Comparison week every six weeks
process.description: The baseline diagnostics are re-sat and the two results placed side by side. Movement on the same instrument is the only honest measure of progress. Where there has been none, the plan changes rather than continuing, and that conversation happens on the evidence.

process.title: Investigation track, versioned separately
process.description: Sessions booked against the school's own deadlines, each producing a commented version of the student's own document. Versions are kept, so the narrowing of the research question and the development of the analysis are both part of the record rather than claims about it.

whyPoints.title: The file, not the session, is the product
whyPoints.description: An annotated script, a dated topic record and a versioned draft after every session. A parent who was not in the room can read what happened, and progress becomes a comparison between two documents rather than an opinion about a term.

whyPoints.title: Moles measured before anything is taught
whyPoints.description: Twenty timed items in the first session, scored and timed, then re-sat at six weeks. Mole weakness costs marks across six topics simultaneously, and it is the one chemistry problem that can be fixed with cheap, short, frequent drilling rather than specialist teaching.

whyPoints.title: Losses categorised, not just counted
whyPoints.description: Every lost mark on every script is sorted into content, calculation, command term or timing. Three of those four categories move in weeks rather than months, which is why a mid-range chemistry mark is often cheaper to lift than it appears.

whyPoints.title: Organic taught as transformations
whyPoints.description: Reaction sets are built as tables organised by transformation rather than learned as pairs of facts, because that is what makes a synthetic route readable backwards from the target. Higher Level mechanisms then sit on an organisation that already exists.

whyPoints.title: Investigation criteria named with their marks
whyPoints.description: Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each, named in every piece of feedback, with uncertainty taught before data collection rather than reconstructed afterwards. No competing page found in this market names a single criterion.

whyPoints.title: The record tells you when to stop
whyPoints.description: When the comparison week shows the fluency score has risen and losses have shifted to content, the drilling ends. When the topic record goes green, the frequency drops. A plan whose own evidence can end it is a different product from a rolling monthly subscription.

faqs.question: What should an IB chemistry tutor in Dubai actually hand over each week?
faqs.answer: Three things, and nothing else is required. An annotated script from the question sat that week, showing where each mark went and why. A dated topic record with a status against each topic taught so far. And, where the investigation is in progress, a commented version of the student's own draft. Those arrive the same evening as the session. The reason to insist on them is that they are comparable: October against March on the same instrument is evidence, while a monthly phone call describing progress is a report from an interested party.

faqs.question: Why do mole calculations matter so much in IB chemistry?
faqs.answer: Because the weakness is not contained to one topic. Concentration and titration run on moles. Electrolysis and Faraday relationships run on moles. Enthalpy changes are quoted per mole. Equilibrium expressions are built from concentrations derived from moles. Percentage yield and atom economy are mole ratios. A student who is slow or unreliable on the conversion loses marks across six topics for a single reason, and on a school report that appears as general weakness in chemistry. Twenty timed items with no context identify it in one session, and the fix is short frequent drilling rather than more chemistry teaching.

faqs.question: My child understands chemistry but the marks do not reflect it. What is happening?
faqs.answer: Comprehension and performance diverge in this subject, and the gap is measurable. Understanding why an equilibrium shifts is genuine knowledge; the mark scheme asks for the new concentration to three significant figures having first converted a volume. The usual loss categories in marked Dubai scripts are a mole conversion done late in a multi-step calculation, a sign convention reversed in energetics, an explanation written where a deduction was asked, and a significant-figure convention ignored. None of those is a gap in understanding, and all of them are visible on a script and invisible on a report card.

faqs.question: How does a Dubai student get better at organic chemistry?
faqs.answer: By reorganising it rather than revising it again. Students who learned chemistry as reaction facts can recall that an alcohol oxidises to a carboxylic acid and stall when asked to construct a three-step route to an ester. The fix is to build the reaction set as a table holding starting functional group, reagent, condition, product and transformation type together. Once organised that way, a route can be read backwards from the target, which is how synthesis questions are answered. At Higher Level the mechanism layer sits on the same organisation, and students who built the table find mechanisms notably easier.

faqs.question: What are the four criteria for the IB chemistry investigation?
faqs.answer: Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each for a total of 24, with the component carrying 20 per cent of the subject grade and a 3,000-word ceiling. Research design rewards a focused question with a genuinely variable independent quantity and controlled variables. Data analysis rewards correct processing, graphing and uncertainty treatment. Conclusion rewards a reading of the results related to accepted chemistry. Evaluation rewards identifying which specific source of uncertainty dominated and how it propagated, rather than a generic list of improvements beginning with better equipment.

faqs.question: Why do chemistry investigation questions fail in Dubai schools?
faqs.answer: Most often because the output is qualitative. A colour change observed, a precipitate formed, a reaction that proceeded faster — none of those gives the data analysis criterion numbers to reward, which caps the piece however well it is written. The question has to produce measurements, enough of them, across enough values of a genuinely variable independent quantity. The second common failure is apparatus the school does not hold. Both are detectable in a single session before anything is booked, which is why feasibility work is the highest-value hour in the whole process.

faqs.question: How is progress in chemistry measured across a Diploma year?
faqs.answer: On the same instrument, repeatedly. The baseline is a twenty-item mole fluency set, a timed structured question and a unit-conversion set, all scored and timed in week one. Those are re-sat every six weeks and the results placed side by side. Between comparison points the weekly marked question feeds a dated topic record, so a topic moving from amber to green has a date and a script behind it. Four comparison points across a year is enough to see a trend and few enough that the student is being taught rather than examined.

faqs.question: Should the comparison test come before or after a school break?
faqs.answer: After, and this is more than a scheduling detail. A diagnostic re-sat just before Dubai's long December break measures recency: the material was taught last month and is still warm. The same diagnostic re-sat in the second week of January measures retention, which is the number that predicts examination performance. A student whose score holds across a break has learned the material; a student whose score falls has met it. Those two need different plans, and only the post-break measurement distinguishes them.

faqs.question: Does IB Chemistry Higher Level need more tutoring hours than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Usually, and the reason is calculation volume rather than conceptual difficulty. Higher Level adds content concentrated in organic chemistry, equilibrium constants, acid-base theory including buffers, entropy and spontaneity, and electrochemistry, and those additions are calculation-heavier than the shared content. That is why the mole fluency record predicts Higher Level performance better than any report grade does. A Higher Level student with a flat fluency score across two comparison points needs the drilling block before the content teaching, and reversing that order is the most common way hours get spent without effect.

faqs.question: Is Standard Level chemistry enough for medicine applications?
faqs.answer: Read the requirement for the actual courses on the student's list, because it varies and it is published by each university rather than inferable. Most medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and chemical engineering routes expect Higher Level chemistry. Some biological, environmental and health-science courses accept Standard Level. A few state a chemistry requirement without naming a level. That afternoon of reading settles more of the level decision than any discussion, and it is the one input to the decision that cannot be revised after the fact. Tutoring is not a requirement for any admission process.

faqs.question: What do Dubai providers charge per hour for IB chemistry support?
faqs.answer: Published rates read in October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors listing IB tuition from AED 200 and TutorChase quoting AED 270 for specialist work. The Bestimate survey places IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above, and premium named listings reach AED 650. Budget online provision starts at AED 33-52 at Tutopiya and AED 45-65 at EdFlik. Chemistry is better supplied in this emirate than Higher Level physics, which usually places it mid-band. Calculation drilling can sensibly be bought at the lower band, because the content is not Diploma-specific.

faqs.question: Can online chemistry tuition handle a subject with laboratory work?
faqs.answer: The laboratory work happens at school in either case, so the question is what support it needs. Investigation coaching is design, uncertainty treatment and draft review, all of which happen on documents, tables and graphs, and all of which are better on a shared screen where annotations are saved and versions kept. What online delivery cannot do is stand beside a student while they take a reading. What it can do is ensure the readings they plan to take will produce data the criteria can reward, which is where investigations are actually won or lost.

faqs.question: Is a home chemistry tutor in Dubai worth the extra cost?
faqs.answer: The published numbers put qualified in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour in this market, with independent home tutors at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for comparable work online, and the premium rises with distance from the central tutoring clusters. The premium is a commute. For a record-based chemistry plan there is also a practical argument: annotated scripts and commented drafts stay in a file that can be re-read in March, whereas work marked on paper at a kitchen table is gone by the following week. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with a chemistry investigation, and what may they not?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach experimental design, question whether a research question can generate usable quantitative data, teach uncertainty treatment and propagation, name the four criteria and their six marks each, and give written feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not design the experiment, supply data, or write any part of the report. Work that is not the student's own produces a malpractice finding against the student rather than against the provider who sold it. One UAE-facing site advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, and the outcome at stake there is the Diploma itself.

faqs.question: What happens if no chemistry specialist is available at the level we need?
faqs.answer: You get told, with the options stated. Higher Level chemistry demand in this emirate concentrates among students targeting medicine, which means the same weeks of the final year see the same surge in requests. The honest choices are a wait with a date attached, a tutor based outside the UAE delivering on the same live video platform and on Gulf Standard Time, or a referral elsewhere. A general science tutor placed into Higher Level buffer calculations or Higher Level organic mechanisms is the thing to refuse. No competitor page found in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor.closingHeading: Start the file with twenty mole questions
dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor.closingBody: The first useful chemistry document is not a revision plan. It is twenty timed mole items, scored, dated and kept, alongside one timed structured question marked against the published scheme. Those two pages say whether the problem is calculation fluency, content or technique, and the three have different fixes at different costs. Send the level, the topics currently taught and the last marked paper, take the free 30-minute trial lesson, and insist on the annotated script the same evening. If the fluency score comes back strong, the plan should be shorter and cheaper, and it will be.

intro.heading: Chemistry is the subject where the month matters most
paragraphs: Of the three Diploma sciences, chemistry punishes a late start hardest. The reason is structural rather than conceptual. Chemistry content is strongly sequential: bonding underpins structure, structure underpins reactivity, moles underpin every quantitative topic, and energetics and kinetics both assume the quantitative work is secure. A student who leaves the first term with shaky mole calculations does not have a mole problem. They have a problem that will reappear, in a different costume, in every subsequent topic.

That is why this page is organised around the calendar rather than around a syllabus list. The useful question for an Al Barari parent is not whether their child needs a chemistry tutor but what the term they are currently in has to deliver before the next one starts, and what the remaining weeks can honestly reach. The answer in the first Diploma term is different in kind from the answer in the final one, because by the final term the investigation mark has already been submitted and only the written papers are still in play.

Al Barari adds a scheduling constraint to this. There is no school inside the community, so every pupil commutes out — north to Nad Al Sheba, west towards Motor City and the Arabian Ranches, or across towards Al Barsha South. Those schools run different internal calendars, so two neighbouring households can have students at quite different points in the same course. Weekday sessions realistically begin at five once the commute is done, which matters for chemistry because multi-step calculation is precision work and a tired student makes arithmetic errors rather than conceptual ones.

The investigation deserves its own paragraph because its timing is the single most consequential thing in this subject. It carries 20% of the chemistry grade and is marked out of 24 across four criteria. The mark is largely decided at the design stage, before any solution is made up, by whether the chosen variable produces a measurable change with school apparatus. A student who begins in the first Diploma year has a straightforward route to a good mark. A student who begins in the second has a problem that no amount of later writing solves.

So what follows is a term-by-term planning frame, the paper structure and weightings, the investigation broken down criterion by criterion, where chemistry marks actually go topic by topic, and the Dubai market rates in dirhams with their sources. There is also an honest section on what practical chemistry a tutor can and cannot contribute when lessons are online.

One statement of fact. IB Gram delivers chemistry tuition to Al Barari as live one-to-one lessons over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Chemistry teaching is a shared screen, a worked calculation with every line visible, a marked mechanism and a conversation about an investigation design, none of which needs anyone in the room.

programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each out of eight, with processing and evaluating among them. programmes.countryNote: Several Dubailand schools run the full IB continuum, so a reasonable share of Al Barari chemistry students come this way. programmes.name: IGCSE chemistry into the Diploma
programmes.description: Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1 students arrive with good coverage of bonding, moles and qualitative analysis, and with a short-answer habit. The gap is depth: Diploma organic chemistry demands mechanism reasoning rather than product recall, and Diploma energetics expects quantitative treatment rather than qualitative description.
programmes.countryNote: Most British-curriculum schools near Al Barari use this route. A pupil who sat the Extended or Higher tier arrives prepared; one who sat Core or Foundation has a genuine content gap in the quantitative topics and should address it before Year 12 rather than during it.

Confirm the current weightings and durations with your child's teacher.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May session. No IB exam or results dates appear on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated verification and an unverified date a parent acts on is worse than none. programmes.description: Medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, veterinary science and chemical engineering routes commonly require Higher Level chemistry, often with a minimum grade. Requirements are published by each university and vary by course and year, so they should be read on the institution's own course page rather than inferred from a school's general advice.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-barari.subjectsIntro: These are the chemistry topics Al Barari families ask about, with where the marks actually go. Note how many of them depend on the quantitative work, which is why a first-term gap is so expensive.

subjects.name: The mole concept and stoichiometry
subjects.description: The load-bearing topic of the whole course. Concentration, limiting reagents, percentage yield and gas volumes all rest on it, and every error here propagates. Students lose marks less to the concept than to unit discipline: moles per cubic decimetre against moles per cubic centimetre decides more questions than understanding does.

subjects.name: Atomic structure and periodicity
subjects.levels: HL and SL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Electron configuration, ionisation energy trends and periodic behaviour. Marks go to students who explain trends from shielding and nuclear charge rather than reciting them. Higher Level adds transition metal chemistry, which is self-contained and therefore unusually responsive to focused tutoring.

subjects.name: Bonding and structure
subjects.levels: HL and SL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Ionic, covalent and metallic bonding, intermolecular forces and molecular geometry. Shape and polarity questions are routinely lost by students who know the theory and do not count lone pairs. Higher Level hybridisation and formal charge are precise topics where notation matters as much as reasoning.

subjects.name: Energetics and thermochemistry
subjects.levels: HL and SL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Enthalpy changes, Hess cycles, bond enthalpies and, at Higher Level, entropy and Gibbs free energy. Sign conventions are where the grade is decided: a correctly calculated magnitude with the wrong sign loses the mark. Hess cycle questions reward drawing the cycle before attempting arithmetic.

subjects.name: Chemical kinetics
subjects.levels: HL and SL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Rate, collision theory, activation energy and, at Higher Level, rate laws, orders of reaction and the Arrhenius treatment. Determining order from data is a procedure that can be taught once and then relied on, and it is a common source of recoverable marks late in the course.

subjects.name: Equilibrium
subjects.levels: HL and SL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Dynamic equilibrium, Le Chatelier reasoning and, at Higher Level, equilibrium constant calculations. Written answers lose marks by stating that the equilibrium shifts without naming which change drives it. Calculation questions lose marks to assumptions that are not stated.

subjects.name: Acids and bases
subjects.levels: HL and SL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Strength against concentration, pH scales and, at Higher Level, weak acid calculations, buffers and titration curves. The strength and concentration distinction is the most common conceptual confusion in the whole course, and it survives into Higher Level if nobody addresses it directly.

subjects.name: Redox and electrochemistry
subjects.levels: HL and SL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Oxidation states, half-equations, electrochemical cells and, at Higher Level, cell potentials and electrolysis calculations. Balancing half-equations in acidic or basic conditions is a procedure, not an insight, and it is reliably learnable in a session or two.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry
subjects.levels: HL and SL, substantially extended at HL
subjects.description: Functional groups, reaction pathways and, at Higher Level, mechanisms including nucleophilic substitution and electrophilic addition. The commonest request from Dubai students, and the commonest mistake is memorising products instead of reasoning from electron movement, which fails as soon as an unfamiliar molecule appears.

subjects.name: Spectroscopy and structure determination
subjects.description: Mass spectrometry, infrared and nuclear magnetic resonance used together to deduce structures. A reliable source of accessible marks because the reasoning is systematic, and reliably skipped in revision because students treat it as an add-on rather than a method.

subjects.name: Uncertainty and data processing
subjects.levels: HL and SL, examined and assessed internally
subjects.description: Absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation through calculations, and judgement about significant figures. Examined in the data section of the written papers and central to the investigation, so time spent here is paid for twice. Almost always under-taught.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.levels: HL and SL, 20% of the grade
subjects.description: An individual investigation marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. In chemistry the design trap is a reaction whose measurable change is too small or too fast for school apparatus, which cannot be rescued once the data exists.

sections.heading: The chemistry calendar, counted backwards
paragraphs: This is the section competitors do not write, and it is the reason to read this page. The Diploma is not two years of study followed by exams. It is a sequence in which marks are banked at intervals set by your child's school, and in chemistry the sequential nature of the content means an early gap compounds rather than sits still.

Work from the end. In the final weeks before the session, the investigation mark is already submitted and only the written papers remain, so tutoring is paper technique and targeted topic repair. In the term before that, investigation drafts and a mock series usually collide, which is the most congested point in the two years. In the first year, everything is still available: content can be secured as it is taught, the investigation design can be chosen well, and the quantitative fluency that carries the whole course can be built rather than patched.

The table below is a planning frame rather than a set of IB dates. No IB exam or results date appears on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated verification and publishing an unverified date to a parent who will act on it is worse than publishing none. The school-side milestones are the ones a tutor plans against anyway, and your child's Diploma coordinator can supply them in a single email.

Use it in one specific way. Write your child's own internal deadlines into the right-hand column, then count the weeks between today and the nearest one. That count, rather than a general sense of concern, is what should decide whether you book one session a week or two and whether the first target is content, the investigation or paper technique.

sections.heading: The papers, the weightings and the eight-week reality
paragraphs: The current IB Chemistry guide sets two written papers at each level alongside the internally assessed scientific investigation, which carries 20% of the grade at both Standard and Higher Level. Paper 1 pairs multiple-choice questions with a data-analysis section; Paper 2 is extended response and carries the largest single share. Confirm the exact weightings and durations for your child's cohort with their teacher, because the IB revises subject guides periodically.

Families in Al Barari frequently arrive eight weeks before a mock or a paper, so it is worth being specific about what that window does. Eight weeks of two sessions a week is roughly sixteen taught hours plus set work. That is enough to do three things well. Diagnose properly, by working a full paper under timing and marking it against the published scheme, which usually relocates the problem. Repair the three or four topics producing the largest share of lost marks. And fix technique: working shown for method credit, unit discipline, and answering the command term rather than writing everything known.

What eight weeks does not do is teach the sequential spine of a two-year chemistry course to a student who never secured it. If mole calculations are unreliable, every quantitative topic is unreliable, and that is a holiday block of volume rather than eight weeks of explanation. Nor can eight weeks touch an investigation mark already submitted, which is why a first-year booking has a materially higher ceiling than a final-term one with the same tutor and the same effort.

There is one thing eight weeks reliably changes that is hard to measure. A student who has been quietly avoiding chemistry revision because they do not know where to start will do the work once someone has broken it into a sequence. That shift usually happens by the third session, and for some students it is the whole of the gain.

sections.heading: The investigation, criterion by criterion, and when to start it
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market names a single investigation criterion or its marks, which is striking for a component worth a fifth of the grade. In the current science guides the individual scientific investigation is marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Confirm these with your child's teacher, as the IB revises its guides.

In chemistry specifically, research design is where most of the eventual mark is won or lost, and the trap is measurability. A student picks a reaction that is interesting and then discovers the colour change is too subtle, the reaction too fast, the temperature change within the uncertainty of a school thermometer, or the yield too small to weigh reliably. The data then shows nothing and no amount of careful writing recovers it. A tutor's single most valuable hour on this component is spent asking, before any apparatus is booked, whether the proposed change can actually be measured with the equipment available.

Data analysis rewards correct processing, appropriate graphing and genuine uncertainty treatment — propagation through the calculation and a statement of how uncertainty affects the conclusion. Conclusion rewards answering the stated research question, justified by the data and compared with accepted chemistry. Evaluation rewards identifying specific methodological weaknesses and proposing realistic improvements, not generic statements about human error. Conclusion and evaluation together carry twelve of the twenty-four marks and are the cheapest to improve, because they reward thinking rather than apparatus.

The timing conclusion follows directly. A student who chooses a measurable question in the first Diploma year has a straightforward route to a strong mark, with time to repeat a trial that went wrong. A student who starts in the second year is choosing under pressure, has no time to repeat anything, and is usually writing up data that does not support a clean conclusion. The difference between those two students is often four or five marks out of twenty-four, which is a meaningful fraction of a grade.

sections.heading: Where chemistry marks actually go
paragraphs: Mark a chemistry paper rather than asking the student and four patterns appear in nearly every cohort. Three are habits and respond within weeks; one is structural and takes a term.

The first is unit and concentration discipline. Moles per cubic decimetre against moles per cubic centimetre, grams against kilograms, and the conversion between them decide more chemistry questions than conceptual understanding does. It bleeds a mark at a time and concentrates in titration and solution questions. The second is compounding error in multi-step calculation: a rounding decision taken at step one survives to the final answer, and because mark schemes credit the steps, a student who shows no working loses everything rather than most of it.

The third is sign convention in energetics. A correctly calculated enthalpy magnitude with the wrong sign loses the mark, and students who draw the Hess cycle before calculating almost never make the error while students who work algebraically frequently do. That is a habit change rather than a knowledge change and takes a fortnight of deliberate practice.

The fourth is structural: organic chemistry memorised rather than reasoned. A student who has learned the products of named reactions performs well until an unfamiliar molecule appears, at which point they have nothing. Reasoning from electron movement — where the nucleophile attacks, why that carbon is electrophilic, what the intermediate looks like — transfers to anything. Rebuilding that takes a term and is the commonest reason a capable Dubai student requests Higher Level chemistry support in the second year.

sections.heading: Practical chemistry when the tutor is on a screen
paragraphs: A straight answer rather than reassurance. Practical chemistry happens at school. Your child's school has the reagents, the fume cupboard, the balances and the supervision, and it runs the laboratory sessions in which the investigation data is collected. No tutor in any delivery format runs experiments for a student, and an in-home tutor arriving at an Al Barari villa with a burette is not what in-home tutoring looks like either.

What a tutor genuinely contributes divides into three things, all of which work on a shared screen. The first is design, which in chemistry means measurability: can the proposed change be detected with school apparatus, how many concentrations are needed and over what range, what has to be controlled, and whether a trial should be run before committing. That conversation determines the research design mark and it is talk rather than practice.

The second is uncertainty and data treatment. Propagating uncertainty through a multi-step calculation, deciding significant figures consistently, plotting with error bars and judging whether a gradient means anything is all better on a shared spreadsheet than across a dining table, because both parties see the same cells and the same graph. This is also the work that pays twice, since the data-analysis section of Paper 1 examines the same skills.

The third is the writing, which is identical in any format: the tutor reads the student's own draft, says what is not working and why, and the student rewrites. Where a screen genuinely loses something is laboratory intuition — knowing what a reaction looks like when it has gone wrong, how a burette actually behaves, why a reading drifted. The school provides that and a tutor cannot substitute for it. What a tutor can do is send the student into a laboratory session with a plan, which is more useful than it sounds given how many students arrive with none.

sections.heading: What chemistry tutoring costs across two years
paragraphs: Hourly rates obscure the decision a family is actually making, which is a two-year one. So here are the market bands and then the two-year arithmetic. Read in October 2026: EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour, Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52, Unitors from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB, TutorChase at AED 270, BartyED at AED 650. Bestimate's Dubai table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 and IB or IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with monthly estimates of AED 240 to AED 600 budget, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Now the calendar-led version. A family that starts in the first Diploma year typically runs one session a week for three terms, adds a holiday block, then two sessions a week through the final two terms. A family that starts in the final term runs two or three sessions a week for eight to twelve weeks. The second pattern costs less in total and reaches a lower ceiling, because the investigation mark is already submitted and the quantitative spine cannot be rebuilt in eight weeks. The first costs more and buys a fifth of the grade that the second cannot touch at all.

That is the honest comparison, and it is worth making explicitly because the cheaper option looks more attractive at the moment of decision. Spread across two years at the mid band, weekly chemistry support is a recurring monthly line of the kind a Dubai household can plan around. Compressed into a final term at the specialist band it is a larger monthly number for a shorter period, aimed at a smaller share of the grade.

For context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for Dubai private schools for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. The school bill is flat; the tutoring decision is the variable. sections.heading: Ramadan, holidays and when revision actually happens
paragraphs: The Dubai academic calendar shapes chemistry revision more than families plan for, and two features of it are worth building into a plan rather than reacting to. The first is the long school breaks, which are the only time a student can run four or five sessions a week. For a sequential subject like chemistry that is not merely more tutoring; it is the only realistic way to rebuild a quantitative spine, because fluency comes from volume rather than from being explained again.

The summer between the two Diploma years is the single most valuable block in the programme. Nothing is being banked, no deadlines are running, and a student can cover ground that term-time cannot touch. A family who uses it well arrives in the second year with the first year's content secure and the investigation already designed, which changes what the final year is for. A family who does not spends the second year carrying first-year gaps into harder topics.

The second feature is Ramadan. School hours shorten and the usable part of the evening moves, so sessions shift to the earlier afternoon or to a post-Iftar slot. The adjustment that works is a shorter session at the same frequency rather than skipped weeks, because chemistry is sequential and a fortnight's gap costs more than two shortened sessions would. Where Ramadan falls close to a mock series or an investigation deadline, plan the block before it begins rather than improvising week by week.

An online slot is considerably easier to move than a tutor's drive across Dubai, which is one of the quieter practical advantages of the format in this emirate. A post-Iftar session at nine in the evening is a reasonable ask of a tutor on video and an unreasonable one of a tutor who would have to drive to Al Barari and back.

sections.heading: Honesty, permits and what we will not supply
paragraphs: The investigation is individual assessed work and there are providers in this region selling completed internal assessments at a published price. Submitting one is academic misconduct and the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller. So the boundary belongs on the page, and we state it to the student rather than only to the parent.

A tutor may teach any chemistry the investigation requires, test whether a design is measurable, explain each criterion and what its descriptors mean, teach uncertainty propagation, and read the student's own draft and say what is not working. A tutor may not write any part of it, supply data, choose the research question outright, or edit a draft into something the student did not produce. Where a draft needs changing, the tutor names the problem and the student rewrites. That is slower and it is the only version that is both lawful and effective, because conclusion and evaluation reward thinking the student actually did.

On materials: syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, and reproducing or distributing them is copyright infringement. A tutor works from legitimately obtained material and teaches the student to read the assessment criteria themselves. We also do not describe tutors as IB examiners where current status cannot be evidenced, and examiner experience gives no access to marking, boundaries or unseen paper content in any case.

On regulation: private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years to teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Those operating without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so distrust any page quoting an amount. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from the IB, KHDA, ADEK or the Ministry of Education.

process.title: Tell us the term and the investigation stage
process.description: Which Diploma year and term your child is in, and whether the investigation has no topic yet, a topic but no data, data collected, or a draft written. Those states need entirely different first sessions, and the earlier one is in that list the more a tutor can affect the twenty per cent the component carries.

process.title: A diagnostic that tests the quantitative spine
process.description: The first session works mole, concentration and multi-step calculation questions deliberately, separately from the conceptual topics, because a chemistry problem is frequently a quantitative-fluency problem wearing a topic label. If the spine is shaky, the plan is a holiday block rather than six weeks on energetics.

process.title: A free first lesson with the named tutor
process.description: One full lesson, no charge, with the person who would continue. Ask them to name the four investigation criteria and their marks, and to talk through whether a proposed design is measurable with school apparatus. A genuine chemistry specialist does both immediately; much of this market cannot.

process.title: Pick a slot where arithmetic is reliable
process.description: Chemistry calculation is precision work and a tired student makes arithmetic errors rather than conceptual ones. From Al Barari the realistic weekday start is five o'clock after the commute, so where a family can manage it we recommend a weekend morning for calculation-heavy work and a shorter weekday slot for content.

process.title: Working shown, every time
process.description: Each session enforces visible working, because mark schemes credit the steps and a student who shows nothing loses everything when a multi-step calculation compounds an error. Problem sets go out and are marked at the start of the next session. The written note records what was set and whether it came back.

process.title: Reassess at each school milestone
process.description: Reports, mocks and investigation drafts are the checkpoints where the plan is tested against evidence rather than renewed by habit. If the level looks wrong we will say so and hand you a marked paper to take to the school. If the subject is secure we will say that and end the block rather than roll it forward.

whyPoints.title: Planned from your school's calendar, not a scheme of work
whyPoints.description: Chemistry is sequential, so the month a tutor starts changes what tutoring can achieve. We plan from your child's own internal deadlines, which means each session has a target that sits between today and the next fixed date rather than following a generic topic order.

whyPoints.title: The investigation started early and coached by criterion
whyPoints.description: Four criteria, six marks each, with the outcome largely decided at the design stage by whether the chosen change can be measured at all. We run the viability conversation before any apparatus is booked, which is the single most valuable hour available on a component worth a fifth of the grade.

whyPoints.title: The quantitative spine tested separately
whyPoints.description: Moles, concentration and multi-step calculation carry the whole course, and a school report cannot tell you whether a topic problem is really a fluency problem. We test them apart, because telling a family their child needs a holiday block of volume is more useful than selling them six weeks of equilibrium.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what a screen cannot do
whyPoints.description: Practical chemistry and laboratory intuition happen at school and no tutor substitutes for them in any format. We say so, then describe the three things a tutor genuinely contributes, all of which work better on a shared spreadsheet than across a dining table.

whyPoints.title: Two-year costs shown, not just hourly rates
whyPoints.description: This page sets out what starting in the first year costs against a final-term rescue, and what each can reach. The cheaper option looks better at the moment of decision and reaches a lower ceiling, and a family deserves to see both numbers before choosing.

whyPoints.title: Clear about the limits
whyPoints.description: No part of an investigation written by a tutor. No home visits in the UAE. No distribution of IB papers or mark schemes. No examiner claims we cannot evidence. No guaranteed grades. No approval or accreditation from the IB, KHDA, ADEK or the Ministry of Education, because we hold none.

faqs.question: When in the Diploma should chemistry tutoring start?
faqs.answer: The first year, if the choice is available, because chemistry content is sequential and an early gap compounds rather than sits still. Mole calculations underpin every quantitative topic, so a student who leaves the first term shaky will meet the same weakness again in energetics, kinetics, equilibrium and acids. A first-year start also keeps the scientific investigation in play, and that component carries twenty per cent of the grade. By the final term the investigation mark is submitted and only the written papers remain.

faqs.question: Why does organic chemistry collapse for students who revised it?
faqs.answer: Because they memorised products rather than reasoning from electron movement. A student who has learned what named reactions produce performs well on familiar molecules and has nothing when an unfamiliar one appears, which is exactly what the Higher Level paper does. Reasoning from where the nucleophile attacks, why a particular carbon is electrophilic and what the intermediate looks like transfers to anything. Rebuilding that takes a term rather than a fortnight, which is why it is the commonest second-year request from capable Dubai students.

faqs.question: How is the chemistry investigation marked?
faqs.answer: Out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each in the current science guides: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, scaled to twenty per cent of the final grade. Confirm the allocations with your child's teacher, since the IB revises its guides. In chemistry the decisive criterion is research design, and the decisive question is measurability: whether the chosen change is large enough and slow enough to detect with school apparatus. A reaction that is too fast or a temperature change inside the thermometer's uncertainty produces data that cannot be rescued.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a chemistry tutor to an Al Barari address?
faqs.answer: No. All UAE tuition is delivered live and one-to-one over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are a service we run only in India and no tutor is sent to any UAE address. For chemistry the cost is minimal, because the work is a shared screen, a calculation with every line visible, a marked mechanism and a shared spreadsheet of uncertainties. The gain is a shortlist of people who actually teach the course at your child's level rather than those who will drive to a villa community at five.

faqs.question: What can eight weeks of chemistry tutoring realistically achieve?
faqs.answer: Three things, done well. A proper diagnosis from a full paper worked under timing and marked against the published scheme, which usually relocates the problem. Repair of the three or four topics producing most of the lost marks. And technique: working shown for method credit, unit discipline, and answering the command term. What it cannot do is rebuild the quantitative spine of a two-year course, which needs a holiday block of volume, or change an investigation mark that has already been submitted.

faqs.question: Which chemistry topics do Dubai Diploma students lose most marks on?
faqs.answer: Concentration units above everything: moles per cubic decimetre against moles per cubic centimetre decides more questions than conceptual understanding does, and it bleeds a mark at a time through titration and solution work. Then sign conventions in energetics, where a correct magnitude with the wrong sign scores nothing and drawing the Hess cycle first almost eliminates the error. Then acid strength against concentration, the most persistent conceptual confusion in the course, which survives into Higher Level if nobody addresses it directly.

faqs.question: Can practical chemistry be supported over video?
faqs.answer: The practical work itself happens at school, with the school's reagents, balances and supervision, and no tutor in any format substitutes for that. What a tutor contributes works on a screen: testing whether an investigation design can be measured with available apparatus, teaching uncertainty propagation and significant-figure discipline on shared data, and giving feedback on the student's own draft. What a screen loses is laboratory intuition, which the school provides. A tutor can at least send a student into a practical with a plan.

faqs.question: How should we use the summer between the two Diploma years?
faqs.answer: It is the most valuable block in the programme and most families waste it. Nothing is being banked, no deadlines are running, and a student can run four or five sessions a week, which is the only realistic way to rebuild quantitative fluency. Used well, a student arrives in the second year with first-year content secure and the investigation already designed, which changes what the final year is for. Used poorly, first-year gaps get carried into harder topics where they cost considerably more.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan affect chemistry revision in Dubai?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten and the usable part of the evening moves, so sessions shift to the earlier afternoon or to a post-Iftar slot. For a sequential subject the adjustment that works is a shorter session at the same frequency rather than skipped weeks, because a fortnight's gap in chemistry costs more than two shortened sessions. Where Ramadan falls close to a mock series or an investigation deadline, plan the block before it starts. An online slot is far easier to move than a tutor's drive across the emirate.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level chemistry worth it if the degree does not require it?
faqs.answer: Check the requirement before deciding rather than after. Medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, veterinary science and chemical engineering routes commonly expect Higher Level chemistry, sometimes with a minimum grade, and the requirement is published by each university and varies by course and year. Read it on the institution's own course page. If no intended course requires it, Higher Level chemistry is a substantial time commitment — roughly half again the hours of the Standard Level version — spent on something nothing depends on.

faqs.question: What does IB chemistry tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026 run from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour for budget and student tutors, AED 150 to AED 300 for qualified subject tutors online, and AED 200 to AED 450 or above for IB specialists, with in-home visits at AED 180 to AED 500 including travel. Monthly, at one session a week, that is roughly AED 240 to AED 600, AED 600 to AED 1,200, or AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above. Those are published market numbers rather than IB Gram prices, and the first lesson is free.

faqs.question: My child shows no working and gets the right answers. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: Yes, and chemistry punishes it harder than most subjects. Mark schemes credit the steps, so a correct final figure with nothing written scores below a wrong figure with sound working. In multi-step calculations the effect compounds: a rounding decision taken at the first step survives to the end, and a student who showed nothing loses the whole question rather than one mark. The pupils most affected are the quick ones who have been praised for mental arithmetic for years, and two to three weeks of enforced working fixes it.

faqs.question: Should we book one session a week or two?
faqs.answer: Count the weeks to your child's next fixed deadline — an investigation draft date, a mock window, a report — and let that decide. One session a week through the first Diploma year is usually right if it starts early, rising to two in the terms before mocks and the exam session. Beyond two in term time the limiting factor becomes whether the problem sets get done, and the problem sets are where the improvement happens. If three subjects need attention, sequence them across terms rather than running them together.

faqs.question: Do science tutors in the UAE need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule is published, so be sceptical of pages quoting amounts. Ask to see the permit rather than accepting a verbal assurance, and ask any agency the same.

faqs.question: What happens if the investigation data does not work?
faqs.answer: This is precisely why starting early matters. A student in the first Diploma year who collects data that shows nothing has time to change the design and repeat, which is a normal part of experimental work and no barrier to a strong mark. A student in the second year has no time to repeat and ends up writing up data that will not support a clean conclusion, losing marks on the conclusion and evaluation criteria as well as on analysis. The viability conversation before any apparatus is booked is what prevents it.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-barari.closingHeading: Find the next date, then count the weeks
dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-barari.closingBody: Ask your child's chemistry teacher two things: when the investigation topic has to be approved, and when the internal draft and final submission dates fall. Then count the weeks between today and the nearest of them. That number decides whether you need one session a week or two, and whether the first target is the quantitative spine, the investigation design or paper technique. If the investigation has no topic yet, that is the work to do first, because it carries twenty per cent of the grade and the mark is set before any data exists. Al Barari sessions run live and one-to-one over video at Gulf Standard Time. Practical work stays at school, we make no home visits in the UAE, and we promise no grades.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-barsha.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma Chemistry at Higher and Standard Level across the Al Barsha corridor, covering Paper 1 and Paper 2 technique, organic mechanisms, the calculation set and the scientific investigation.

intro.heading: Four neighbourhoods, one chemistry course
paragraphs: Parents in this part of Dubai compare neighbourhoods constantly, and with reason: Al Barsha, Al Barsha South, Al Quoz, Al Sufouh and the communities around them have genuinely different school gates, different commutes and - this is the part that surprises people - noticeably different quoted tutoring rates for the same work. So a family naturally asks whether a chemistry tutor from one area is better placed than one from another, and whether the local market they are in explains the grade their child is getting.

The honest answer is that almost nothing that matters differs. Diploma Chemistry is one course with one assessment structure: in the current guide, Paper 1 carries 36% and includes a multiple-choice section and a data-based section, Paper 2 carries 44%, and the scientific investigation carries 20% and is marked out of 24 across four criteria of 6. A student at a gate in Al Barsha 2 and a student at a gate in Al Barsha South sit the same papers against the same mark schemes. Organic mechanisms fail in the same way for both. Hess cycles go wrong in the same place. The investigation collapses for the same five reasons.

What does differ is worth knowing precisely, because it is short. School internal deadlines differ, sometimes by weeks, and those deadlines govern the investigation. Laboratory access and the amount of practical time a school gives differ, which affects how prepared a student is to design an investigation. Commute times differ by twenty minutes or so, which changes the start time of a session and nothing else. And quoted rates differ by area, which is a fact about local market expectation rather than about teaching.

This page therefore spends most of its length on the chemistry and a short section on the comparison. There is the component structure, the organic mechanism trap, the calculation set that decides Higher Level grades, the specific ways chemistry investigations fail, the two things that genuinely vary between these neighbourhoods, and an explanation of why the same tutor is quoted differently in Emirates Hills and Al Quoz.

On delivery: IB Gram teaches students across this corridor one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer in India only. For chemistry the trade is favourable - a mechanism drawn live on a shared screen is clearer than one drawn upside down on a kitchen table, and a titration data set is easier to interrogate in a shared spreadsheet - and it removes the one variable that genuinely does differ by neighbourhood, which is who happens to be within driving distance. That is worth stating as a choice rather than a limitation, because across this corridor the in-home option is perfectly practical and plenty of families use it. The argument for working over video here is not that driving is hard; it is that the person who can mark a nucleophilic substitution mechanism properly at Higher Level is in short supply across the whole emirate, and requiring them to be in your neighbourhood as well is a filter that removes capability without adding anything.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-barsha.programmesIntro: Chemistry sits in a two-year programme and follows from two different routes in. Both routes leave characteristic gaps, which is worth knowing before deciding what tuition is for.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Scored out of 45 points. Chemistry is assessed through Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44% and the scientific investigation at 20%.
programmes.countryNote: Across the Al Barsha corridor Chemistry at Higher Level is most often taken by students heading for medicine, dentistry, engineering or chemical sciences, which means the target grade is usually a 6 or 7 and the margin for a weak investigation is small. That shapes where tuition should go.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria out of 8. The Sciences criteria - inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating - prepare a student directly for the Diploma's scientific investigation, which is why continuum students often find the investigation familiar in shape.
programmes.countryNote: Several campuses in this corridor run the MYP into the Diploma. A student arriving in DP1 Chemistry from a strong MYP Sciences profile has met controlled variables, repeats and evaluation before. One arriving with weak MYP Criterion C and D marks will meet the investigation as something genuinely new.

programmes.name: IGCSE Chemistry, Years 10-11
programmes.description: The other common route in, usually Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1. Cambridge 0620 carries a practical component worth 20% of the grade, which is reasonable preparation for Diploma practical write-up; Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers instead.
programmes.countryNote: An IGCSE Chemistry student moving into Diploma Chemistry at Higher Level in this corridor typically finds the mole calculations familiar and the energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanism work genuinely new. The gap is conceptual depth rather than content volume, and it shows up in the spring of DP1.

programmes.name: International A Level Chemistry
programmes.description: The alternative post-16 route, offered by several schools in this cluster, going deeper in chemistry and narrower overall than the Diploma, without Theory of Knowledge or an Extended Essay competing for time.
