dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-barsha.subjectsIntro: The chemistry below is grouped by where grades are decided rather than by syllabus order. Each note names the specific failure, because the content is in the textbook and the failure is not.

subjects.name: Atomic structure and periodicity
subjects.description: Electron configuration, ionisation energy trends and periodic patterns. Marks are lost explaining trends rather than stating them: the mark scheme wants nuclear charge, shielding and atomic radius in the same sentence, and students give one of the three.

subjects.name: Bonding and structure
subjects.description: Ionic, covalent and metallic bonding, intermolecular forces, and shapes of molecules. Predicting shape and bond angle requires counting electron domains including lone pairs, and students count bonds. Comparing boiling points requires naming the specific intermolecular force.

subjects.name: Stoichiometry and the mole
subjects.description: The calculation spine of the whole course: moles, limiting reagents, percentage yield, atom economy, titration calculations and gas laws. Familiar from IGCSE and examined at greater depth, with marks lost to unit conversion and to not identifying the limiting reagent.

subjects.name: Energetics and thermodynamics
subjects.description: Enthalpy changes, Hess cycles, bond enthalpy calculations, and at Higher Level entropy, Gibbs free energy and Born-Haber cycles. Sign errors in Hess cycles are the most reliable loss in the subject; bond enthalpy questions lose marks because bonds broken and formed get reversed.

subjects.name: Kinetics
subjects.description: Rate, collision theory, activation energy, and at Higher Level rate equations, orders of reaction and the Arrhenius relationship. Determining order from data is a Paper 1B and Paper 2 staple and requires reading a table rather than recalling a fact.

subjects.name: Equilibrium and acids and bases
subjects.description: Le Chatelier, the equilibrium constant, pH and the strength of acids and bases, and at Higher Level Ka, Kb, pKa, buffers and titration curves. Buffer calculations and interpreting a titration curve's equivalence and half-equivalence points separate 6s from 7s.

subjects.name: Redox and electrochemistry
subjects.description: Oxidation states, half-equations, voltaic and electrolytic cells, and at Higher Level electrode potentials and the feasibility of reactions. Balancing half-equations in acidic conditions requires water and hydrogen ions, and that step is where students stop.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry
subjects.description: Functional groups, reaction types, and at Higher Level nucleophilic substitution, electrophilic addition and reaction mechanisms with curly arrows. The largest single source of lost Higher Level marks and the most teachable, because mechanisms are rule-governed rather than conceptual.

subjects.name: Paper 1B: data-based questions
subjects.description: Part of the 36% Paper 1 weighting. Tests graph and table interpretation, uncertainty handling and whether a conclusion is supported. Rule-governed, fast-moving and almost never revised separately from the chemistry.

subjects.name: Paper 2: extended response
subjects.description: The 44% paper, where reasoning chains and mechanisms must be written out in full. Students who understand the chemistry lose marks by stating products without conditions, omitting state symbols or skipping the steps that carry the marks.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.levels: HL and SL, 20% of the grade
subjects.description: A single independent investigation marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each out of 6. Chemistry investigations fail in five characteristic ways, all of which are design problems rather than writing problems.

subjects.name: Uncertainty and apparatus precision
subjects.description: Reading uncertainty from apparatus, propagating it through a calculation, and knowing which piece of glassware limits precision. Required throughout the investigation, examined in Paper 1B, and the skill most often missing in otherwise competent chemistry students.

sections.heading: What actually differs between these neighbourhoods, and what does not
paragraphs: An IB chemistry tutor in Al Barsha and one in Al Barsha South are, for all practical purposes, doing the same job. The useful thing is to be precise about which variables genuinely change across these areas, because the list is short and three of the four items on it are not about teaching at all.

Four things differ. Internal deadlines: schools set their own draft and final dates for the scientific investigation, and across this corridor those can sit weeks apart, which is the single most important local fact for anyone planning investigation work. Laboratory time: schools allocate different amounts of practical work, and a student with more bench experience arrives at the investigation better equipped to design one. Commute: twenty minutes or so of difference, which changes the start time of a session and nothing else. Quoted rates: real, and discussed in its own section below, and a fact about neighbourhood expectation rather than about anybody's chemistry.

Everything else is the same. The course is one course. Paper 1 carries 36% and includes multiple-choice and data-based sections; Paper 2 carries 44%; the scientific investigation carries 20% and is marked out of 24 across four criteria of 6. The mark schemes are the same mark schemes. A Hess cycle sign error costs the same marks in Al Quoz as in Emirates Hills. An organic mechanism without curly arrows loses the same credit at every gate in the corridor.

Which is why the answer to the neighbourhood question is the same in all of them: choose for whether the tutor can teach mechanisms and the calculation set and can read an investigation design, and treat location as a scheduling detail. IB Gram delivers across this corridor over live video and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE - home visits are an India-only service - and the practical effect is that the one variable we remove is the one that was never worth optimising.

sections.heading: The organic mechanism trap, identical in every postcode
paragraphs: Organic chemistry is the largest single source of lost Higher Level marks in Diploma Chemistry and the most teachable, which is an unusual and useful combination. It is teachable because mechanisms are rule-governed. A nucleophilic substitution has a defined sequence, a defined set of arrow origins and destinations, and a defined way of showing charge. A student who learns the rules can draw a mechanism they have never seen. A student who memorises examples cannot.

The characteristic failures are specific. Curly arrows drawn from the wrong place: an arrow must start at a lone pair or a bond, not at an atom, and marks are lost for an arrow starting on a carbon rather than on the bond. Arrows pointing to the wrong destination: to an atom rather than to the position where the new bond forms. Missing partial charges on a polarised bond, where the mark scheme wants them shown. Intermediates omitted entirely, so a two-step mechanism is drawn as one step. Charges not conserved across the mechanism, which is a quick self-check almost nobody is taught.

Beyond mechanisms, organic marks go on reagents and conditions. A reaction identified correctly but written without the reagent, the solvent or the temperature loses the condition marks, and those marks are available on nearly every organic question. Students learn reactions as pairs - this becomes that - and the mark scheme wants the full set: what it becomes, with what, under what conditions.

The reason this section sits on a comparison page is that it is the clearest demonstration of the argument. There is no local variation in any of it. A student in Al Barsha South drawing an arrow from a carbon atom loses the same mark as a student in Al Sufouh doing the same thing, and both are fixed by the same three or four sessions of drilled practice with a tutor who marks to the scheme. Choosing a tutor by neighbourhood cannot touch this; choosing one who can mark a mechanism can.

sections.heading: The calculation set that decides Higher Level grades
paragraphs: After organic, the calculations. Diploma Chemistry has a finite set of calculation types, and a Higher Level student who can do all of them reliably has secured a large share of Paper 2 regardless of how the written questions fall. The set is learnable in a defined block, which is why we recommend a block rather than an open-ended arrangement for it.

Energetics first, because the losses there are the most reliable in the subject. Hess cycles go wrong on signs: a reaction used in reverse changes the sign of its enthalpy change, and students carry the original sign through. Bond enthalpy calculations go wrong because bonds broken and bonds formed get reversed, which flips the answer's sign and loses the accuracy mark while the method mark survives. At Higher Level, Born-Haber cycles compound both problems, and Gibbs free energy questions lose marks on unit consistency between enthalpy in kilojoules and entropy in joules.

Then equilibrium and acids. The equilibrium constant expression must match the balanced equation, including powers, and Le Chatelier answers must state the direction of shift and the reason. At Higher Level, Ka and pKa calculations and buffer questions are what separate a 6 from a 7, and titration curve interpretation - identifying the equivalence point, the half-equivalence point and what each tells you - is examined directly and often never practised. Then kinetics: determining order from a data table is a reading exercise with a method, not a recall question.

Finally stoichiometry, which looks familiar from IGCSE and is examined at greater depth. Limiting reagent questions require the comparison to be shown, not assumed. Titration calculations lose marks on dilution factors. Gas law questions lose marks on unit conversion, particularly temperature in kelvin and volume in cubic decimetres. None of this is conceptually hard and all of it is drilled rather than understood, which means it responds to a few weeks of focused practice at any point in the two years.

sections.heading: Why chemistry investigations fail, and they fail the same way everywhere
paragraphs: The scientific investigation carries 20% of the chemistry grade and is marked out of 24 across four criteria of 6: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. In chemistry specifically it fails in five characteristic ways, and all five are design decisions made in the first week rather than writing problems in the last.

First, too few variations of the independent variable. A credible investigation uses at least five values across a meaningful range, and students collect three because three was quicker. No amount of analysis rescues three points. Second, a single trial at each value, which makes uncertainty impossible to estimate and means the data analysis criterion cannot be satisfied. Third, apparatus precision ignored: a student records a volume to the nearest cubic centimetre from a measuring cylinder and then quotes a result to four significant figures, and the investigation's limiting uncertainty is never identified.

Fourth, a question that cannot produce analysable data. This is the expensive one. Investigations built around a vague comparison - which brand of something contains more of something - frequently yield a result that cannot be graphed, cannot be compared against theory, and therefore cannot earn conclusion marks. The question has to produce a relationship, and that should be settled before any chemicals are measured. Fifth, evaluation written as a list of limitations with safety included: the criterion wants each limitation's impact on the result judged and specific realistic improvements proposed, and 'I would repeat it more times' earns nothing.

All five are the same in Al Barsha, Al Barsha South, Al Quoz and Al Sufouh, because the criteria are the same criteria. What differs by school is the deadline and how much laboratory time the student had beforehand. That makes the timing of help local and the content of help universal - which is the argument of this whole page, stated in the component that carries a fifth of the grade.

sections.heading: The two local facts that do matter: deadlines and bench time
paragraphs: Having argued that most neighbourhood comparison is beside the point, it is worth being exact about the two local variables that genuinely affect a chemistry grade, because both are checkable and neither appears on any tutoring page in this market.

The first is the school's internal deadline calendar. Schools set their own dates for the investigation's research question approval, first draft and final submission, and across this corridor those can differ by weeks between gates a short drive apart. The investigation is the only block of marks with a hard local expiry, so the deadline list is the single most useful administrative document a Diploma chemistry family can hold. Ask the IB coordinator for it at the start of DP1 and plan everything, including whether to buy tuition at all, from that list rather than from the external session.

The second is practical time. Schools differ in how many laboratory sessions a Diploma chemistry student gets before designing their own investigation, and the difference is real. A student who has run a dozen practicals knows what a measuring cylinder's uncertainty looks like, has seen a titration go wrong, and will design a feasible investigation. A student with fewer will design something elegant and unworkable. Ask the school how many practicals precede the investigation, because the answer tells you whether design support is likely to be needed.

Neither of those is something a tutor's postcode affects, and both are things a parent can establish in one email. That is the practical recommendation of this page: spend the effort on the two variables that matter and stop comparing the ones that do not. A tutor cannot change your school's deadline or give your child bench time - the school does the second and should - but a tutor who knows the deadline and knows how much practical experience the student has can plan around both.

sections.heading: Why the same work is quoted differently in different parts of this corridor
paragraphs: Families comparing neighbourhoods notice something real: quoted tutoring rates vary across this corridor for identical work, with Emirates Hills and The Meadows at the top and Al Quoz and Al Barsha Heights lower. That variance is about local market expectation rather than about teaching, and the way to test it is against the published market bands rather than against what a neighbour paid.

The published Dubai figures, read during the October 2026 research round, run as follows. Budget online tuition starts at AED 33-52 an hour from Tutopiya and AED 45-65 from EdFlik. A qualified subject tutor working online runs AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists sit at AED 200-450 and upwards, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's guidance putting specialists at AED 200-450 or more. In-home one-to-one with travel included runs AED 180-500, Bestimate quoting AED 180-350. Premium named or examiner-led tutors reach AED 500-650, with BartyED publishing AED 650. Monthly, a weekly hour runs AED 240-600 budget, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

For Higher Level chemistry the specialist band is often what the subject costs, because mechanisms, Born-Haber cycles and buffer calculations need somebody who has taught them repeatedly. But an area-driven quote above that band is worth questioning, and a quote below the mid band is worth questioning differently - at AED 60 an hour nobody is marking an organic mechanism against a scheme. The useful questions before agreeing anything: the rate per 60 minutes, whether VAT is included, the cancellation terms in writing, which guide version the tutor teaches from, and their position on the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years.

For household context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that Dubai private-school fees would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. School fees are capped by policy and tutoring is not, which is why an area-inflated rate compounds quietly across two years. All figures above are other providers' published rates quoted as market context, not as an IB Gram price list; our own arrangement starts with a free trial lesson.

sections.heading: Starting anywhere in this corridor, and the limits
paragraphs: Send five things: the level, the current predicted grade, where the scientific investigation stands, your school's internal deadline for it, and the most recent marked paper. The deadline is the item that changes the plan most, which is why it is on the list alongside the chemistry. We then match a tutor who teaches chemistry at that level, you take a full-length trial lesson at no cost on your child's own work, and you decide.

Sessions run weekly in Gulf Standard Time. Across this corridor the honest start times are 5:00pm for a student at a local Al Barsha gate and 5:15pm for a commute from Al Sufouh, Jumeirah Village or Emirates Hills, because Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road take the whole corridor's traffic at release. A fixture in Al Quoz removes that evening entirely. Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar timing, and weekend mornings suit investigation work and timed papers, which need more than an hour.

What we would tell you not to buy. If the investigation deadline has closed at a reasonable band and the papers are strong, there may be nothing worth purchasing. If the marked paper shows losses concentrated in organic mechanisms and the calculation set, buy a finite block rather than a standing weekly arrangement, because both are rule-governed and finish. If a student is not doing work between sessions, more sessions is the wrong purchase. And if a quote in your area sits above the published specialist band with no scarcity explanation, ask why before paying it.

The fixed limits. No home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. No claimed approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the IB, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson - the IB authorises schools rather than tutors and IB Gram holds nothing from any of them. No writing, drafting, restructuring or editing of a scientific investigation, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or any assessed work. No supplied or reproduced past papers, mark schemes or subject guides; we reference the official sources and work from your school's copies. No IB session or results dates published here; confirm them on ibo.org or with your coordinator. And no statistics about our own results, because we cannot publish the sample, date and method that would make them mean anything.

faqs.question: Is a chemistry tutor in Al Barsha better placed than one in Al Barsha South?
faqs.answer: No, and being precise about why is useful. Four things differ across this corridor: school internal deadlines for the scientific investigation, which can sit weeks apart; how much laboratory time a school gives before the investigation; commute time, worth about twenty minutes; and quoted rates, which vary by neighbourhood expectation. Everything that decides the grade is identical - Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44%, the investigation at 20% marked out of 24 across four criteria of 6, the same mark schemes and the same failure modes in organic and energetics. Choose for mechanism and calculation teaching, not postcode.

faqs.question: Why do organic chemistry marks disappear even when my child understands the reactions?
faqs.answer: Because mechanisms are marked on drawing conventions, not on understanding. An arrow must start at a lone pair or a bond, never at an atom, and must point to where the new bond forms rather than at an atom. Partial charges must be shown on polarised bonds. Intermediates must be drawn, so a two-step mechanism is not collapsed into one. Charge must be conserved throughout. Separately, organic questions award marks for reagent, solvent and conditions, and students who have learned reactions as pairs - this becomes that - lose those marks on nearly every question.

faqs.question: Which chemistry calculations separate a 6 from a 7 at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Ka and pKa work, buffer calculations and titration curve interpretation, in that order. Buffers lose marks when approximations are applied where they do not hold; titration curves lose marks because the half-equivalence point is never identified or used. Before those, Hess cycles are the most reliable loss in the whole subject - a reaction used in reverse changes the sign of its enthalpy change and students carry the original sign through - and Born-Haber cycles at Higher Level compound the same error. All of these are drilled rather than understood, which is why a finite block works.

faqs.question: Why do chemistry investigations lose marks so consistently?
faqs.answer: Five characteristic reasons, four of them decided in the first week of planning. Too few values of the independent variable: three instead of at least five across a meaningful range. A single trial at each value, which makes uncertainty impossible to estimate. Apparatus precision ignored, so the limiting uncertainty is never identified. A research question that cannot produce a graphable relationship, which is the expensive one because no writing repairs it. And an evaluation written as a list of limitations rather than a judgement of each one's impact with specific realistic improvements proposed.

faqs.question: Should we get help with the investigation before or after collecting data?
faqs.answer: Before, and it is not a close call in chemistry. Four of the five characteristic failures are design decisions: the number of values, the number of trials, the apparatus choice and whether the question yields a relationship at all. A tutor consulted before any chemicals are measured can prevent all four. A tutor reading a finished draft can improve the evaluation and the write-up and cannot fix a data set with three points and one trial each. One session on the research question and the variable range is worth several on the draft, and families almost never book it because nothing appears wrong yet.

faqs.question: What exactly may a tutor do on the chemistry investigation?
faqs.answer: Teach the four criteria in the IB's own terms, challenge the research question and the variable range, explain uncertainty and apparatus precision, read a draft and name which criterion it falls short of and why, and ask the questions the supervisor will ask. A tutor may not design the investigation, write, draft, restructure or edit any part of it. The work is submitted under your child's name with their supervisor's authentication, so the malpractice consequence falls on the student. Agree this boundary explicitly in the first session, and expect a tutor to state it before being asked.

faqs.question: Why is the same tutoring work quoted at different rates in different parts of this corridor?
faqs.answer: Local market expectation. Quoted rates in Emirates Hills and The Meadows sit above those in Al Quoz and Al Barsha Heights for identical work, which is a fact about neighbourhoods rather than about teaching. Test any quote against the published bands instead: budget online AED 45-150, qualified subject tutor online AED 150-300 with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200, specialists AED 200-450 and upwards with TutorChase at AED 270, in-home AED 180-500, premium AED 500-650 with BartyED at AED 650. A quote above the specialist band needs a scarcity explanation; one far below it is buying something else.

faqs.question: How many of the chemistry marks are still available eight weeks out?
faqs.answer: More than families expect, if the work is ordered properly. Paper 1B data technique moves fastest because its marks go to conventions. Organic mechanisms are rule-governed and respond to three or four sessions of drilled practice. The calculation set is finite and each type has one reliable error to fix. Paper 2 structure - writing out the reasoning chain rather than stating the conclusion - improves in two to four weeks. What cannot be done in eight weeks is learning energetics, equilibrium and organic from nothing, and the honest plan in that case secures what is reachable rather than attempting everything.

faqs.question: Does my child's school's laboratory time affect the chemistry grade?
faqs.answer: Indirectly but genuinely, which is one of only two local variables worth checking. Schools in this corridor allocate different numbers of practicals before students design their own investigation. A student who has run a dozen knows what a measuring cylinder's uncertainty looks like, has seen a titration go wrong and will design something feasible. A student with fewer tends to design something elegant and unworkable. Ask the school how many practicals precede the investigation; the answer tells you whether design support is likely to be needed before data collection.

faqs.question: Which internal deadline should we be planning around?
faqs.answer: Your own school's, not the area's. Schools set their own dates for the investigation's question approval, first draft and final submission, and across this corridor those can differ by weeks between gates a short drive apart. The investigation is the only chemistry block with a hard local expiry, so that list is the most useful administrative document a Diploma chemistry family can hold. Ask the IB coordinator for it at the start of DP1. External session and results dates should be confirmed on ibo.org rather than taken from any tutoring page, including this one.

faqs.question: My child came from IGCSE Chemistry and is struggling in DP1. What is the gap?
faqs.answer: Conceptual depth rather than content volume, and it usually shows in the spring of DP1. Mole calculations feel familiar because they are. Energetics, equilibrium, kinetics at Higher Level and organic mechanisms are genuinely new in their demands, and they assume mathematical handling - rearrangement, logarithms, unit consistency between kilojoules and joules - that IGCSE did not require. The cheapest intervention is a weekly hour through DP1 on exactly that, which is both earlier and smaller than what most families end up buying in DP2 after the problem has compounded.

faqs.question: Is Paper 1B worth revising separately from the chemistry?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is routinely never done. The data-based section of Paper 1 tests graph and table interpretation, uncertainty handling and whether a stated conclusion is supported by the data shown. Those marks go to conventions rather than to chemical insight, which makes them fast to secure and makes the skills transferable to the investigation's data analysis criterion and to Paper 2 questions on experimental data. Students treat it as part of the chemistry and revise the chemistry instead. A few sessions on it alone typically return more than the same hours on content.

faqs.question: What time should a chemistry session start for a family in this corridor?
faqs.answer: 5:00pm at a local Al Barsha gate and 5:15pm if the commute runs to Al Sufouh, Jumeirah Village or Emirates Hills. Secondary release across this cluster is tightly bunched between roughly 2:45pm and 3:15pm, and Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road absorb the whole corridor at once, so arrival is typically between 3:40pm and 4:35pm. Allow for changing and food. A fixture in Al Quoz removes the evening entirely because of the double journey. Weekend mornings are better for investigation work and timed papers, which need more than an hour.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover chemistry and biology, or chemistry and physics?
faqs.answer: Chemistry and physics is the stronger pairing, because the overlap is mathematical handling, uncertainty and graph work, and a tutor can teach those inside whichever subject the student meets them in. Chemistry and biology overlap in the organic and biochemical content and in command-word discipline, which is also real. Beyond adjacent pairings the claim gets thin: a tutor offering several Higher Level sciences is claiming something improbable. Matching should still be on level as strictly as on subject, because Higher and Standard Level chemistry are different teaching jobs even where the content overlaps.

faqs.question: When would you tell us not to buy chemistry tuition at all?
faqs.answer: Several situations. If the investigation deadline has closed at a reasonable band and the papers are already strong, there may be nothing worth buying. If the marked paper shows losses concentrated in mechanisms and the calculation set, buy a finite block and let it end rather than committing to a weekly arrangement, because both are rule-governed and finish. If the student is not doing work between sessions, that is a supervision problem and more sessions make it worse. And if a local quote sits above the published specialist band with no scarcity reason, the right next step is a question, not a payment.

intro.heading: The Diploma chemistry year has five pressure points, and only one of them is the exam
paragraphs: Chemistry is the subject where Diploma students most often feel they are keeping up and then discover they are not. The reason is structural rather than intellectual. Content arrives in a sequence set by the school, assessment arrives in a sequence set by the IB, and those two sequences do not align. A student can be fluent in bonding in November and still be in trouble, because the Scientific Investigation draft is due in three weeks and the practical work behind it was never properly planned.

There are five points in the two-year course where a chemistry student either gains ground or loses it. The first is the transition in, usually from MYP Sciences or IGCSE, where the jump is in quantitative reasoning rather than in content. The second is the choice between Higher and Standard Level, which has to be made before the student has seen enough HL material to judge it. The third is the Scientific Investigation: twenty per cent of the final grade, a single piece of work, and the only component where the student controls the timeline. The fourth is mock examinations, which for most Dubai schools land in the winter and are the first honest signal of where the grade actually is. The fifth is the final series itself.

A tutor arriving at each of those points should be doing something different. At the transition, the work is mole calculations, unit handling and the habit of showing a quantitative method - skills carried over from mathematics rather than from science. At the level decision, the work is a diagnostic: one HL-only topic taught properly and tested, so the choice rests on evidence instead of ambition. At the Investigation, the work is method, variables, uncertainty and evaluation, done by asking questions rather than supplying answers. After mocks, the work is paper-by-paper triage. In the final stretch, it is past papers against the data booklet and the mark scheme.

Dates are where tutoring pages in this market go wrong, and it is worth being explicit about why this one does not quote IB dates. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no exam-session or results date in our research is confirmed from the IB itself. What is safe to say, and what every Dubai Diploma family already knows, is that UAE schools enter the May session, that the Investigation deadline is set by the school well before it, and that the school's DP coordinator holds the authoritative version of every date that matters. Ask them, write the dates on one sheet, and plan backwards from there. Any tutor who hands you an IB calendar they have not sourced is guessing on something you will act on.

What follows is the chemistry year read backwards from the May session, with the work each phase actually needs. Al Barsha South families tend to arrive at this page in one of three states: Year 12 in autumn with time to build, Year 13 in winter after disappointing mocks, or Year 13 in spring with eight weeks left. The honest plan looks completely different in each case, and the first session exists to work out which one you are in.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-barsha-so.programmesIntro: Al Barsha South sits beside a cluster of schools running both the Diploma Programme and British alternatives, so a chemistry plan here has to know what the student did before Year 12 and what they are heading into. These are the programmes that feed the same chemistry classrooms.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Chemistry
programmes.description: Standard Level across 150 taught hours, Higher Level across 240. The guide is organised into Structure 1 to 3 and Reactivity 1 to 3, with Tools and the inquiry process running through all of it. Assessment is Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44% and the Scientific Investigation at 20%. A data booklet is supplied in both papers, which changes what is worth memorising.
programmes.countryNote: International Baccalaureate students are 7% of Dubai's private-school enrolment, and the 2026-27 intake adds three new IB schools among seven new private schools creating 16,846 places. For Al Barsha South that means more Diploma places within a short drive each year, and a growing number of students whose chemistry teacher is new to the current guide.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: The route most Diploma chemistry students in this cluster arrive from. MYP Sciences assesses four criteria out of 8 each - knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science - which builds strong investigation instincts and leaves quantitative fluency thinner than Diploma chemistry assumes.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students moving into DP Chemistry in a Dubai school usually find the inquiry side familiar and the mole calculations unfamiliar. The gap shows up in the first term of Year 12 as a confident student who cannot finish a stoichiometry question, and it closes faster with targeted arithmetic work than with more chemistry.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson International GCSE Chemistry
programmes.description: The other main entry route, through Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1, or through a double-award science course. IGCSE chemistry covers much of the same territory at lower depth and with far less emphasis on uncertainty, error and evaluation, which is precisely where the Diploma's Investigation marks sit.
programmes.countryNote: Many Al Barsha South students sit IGCSE at a British-curriculum school and then move into a Diploma Programme elsewhere in Dubai for Year 12. That move, made in a single summer, is the most common reason a Year 12 chemistry student needs support in their first term, and it is a transition problem rather than an ability problem.

programmes.name: A Level Chemistry
programmes.description: The alternative post-16 chemistry route offered by most British-curriculum schools near Al Barsha South. A Level goes deeper into fewer areas and assesses practical skills separately, where the Diploma folds investigation into a single internally assessed piece. Families comparing the two usually want to know which suits a medicine application.
programmes.countryNote: Both routes are accepted by UAE and overseas universities, and the choice in this cluster is usually driven by what the school offers rather than by the subject. A student weighing HL Chemistry against A Level Chemistry should look at how each school timetables practical work, since that is where the real difference in experience lies.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-barsha-so.subjectsIntro: Chemistry is the subject on this page, and these are the areas of the current guide where Diploma students in Dubai most often lose reachable marks. Each entry names what the component is actually testing rather than restating a topic title.

subjects.name: Structure 1: models of the particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: The mole, molar mass, concentration, limiting reagents and percentage yield. Almost every quantitative error later in the course traces back to a shaky method here, and the fix is arithmetic discipline rather than more chemistry.

subjects.name: Structure 2: models of bonding and structure
subjects.description: Ionic, covalent and metallic models, intermolecular forces, and the HL extension into formal charge and expanded structures. Students lose marks explaining a physical property without naming the specific force responsible.

subjects.name: Structure 3: classification of matter
subjects.description: Periodic trends and the chemistry of organic functional groups, plus HL spectroscopic identification. Trend questions need a reason stated in terms of nuclear charge and shielding, not a restatement of the trend itself.

subjects.name: Reactivity 1: what drives chemical reactions
subjects.description: Enthalpy, Hess cycles, bond enthalpies, entropy and Gibbs energy at HL. Sign conventions account for more lost marks here than any concept, and they are fixable in a single session.

subjects.name: Reactivity 2: how much, how fast and how far
subjects.description: Rate, rate equations and mechanisms at HL, plus equilibrium and the equilibrium constant. Le Chatelier answers fail when the student predicts a shift without saying which quantity the system is opposing.

subjects.name: Reactivity 3: mechanisms of chemical change
subjects.description: Acid-base behaviour, pH and buffers, redox, electrochemistry, and organic mechanisms at HL. Buffer calculations and electrode-potential sign handling are the two reliable HL marks sinks.

subjects.name: The Scientific Investigation
subjects.levels: SL and HL, 20% of the grade
subjects.description: One piece of work, up to 3,000 words, assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at 6 marks each. The marks lost are almost always in evaluation, where students list limitations without explaining their effect on the result.

subjects.name: Uncertainty, error and data treatment
subjects.description: Propagating uncertainty, choosing significant figures honestly and distinguishing random from systematic error. Examined in Paper 1B data-based questions and central to the Investigation, and taught thinly in most schools for time reasons.

subjects.name: Using the data booklet under time pressure
subjects.description: A supplied booklet changes the skill from recall to navigation. Students who have not practised finding a value fast lose minutes per paper, and minutes are marks in Paper 1.

subjects.name: Extended response technique in Paper 2
subjects.description: Paper 2 is 44% of the grade and rewards structured explanation with chemical terms used precisely. The common failure is a correct idea written in everyday language that the mark scheme cannot credit.

subjects.name: Organic synthesis routes
subjects.description: Multi-step conversions requiring reagents and conditions at each stage. Students who learn individual reactions and never practise chaining them cannot answer the question as asked.

subjects.name: Linking Tools and inquiry across topics
subjects.description: Experimental technique, technology and mathematics are woven through the guide rather than taught as a unit, so gaps hide easily. A diagnostic across all three usually explains a student whose topic tests look fine and whose papers do not.

sections.heading: The chemistry year counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Every useful chemistry plan in a Dubai Diploma school is built backwards. The fixed point is the May session that UAE schools enter. Everything else is positioned relative to it, and most of the dates that matter are set by the school rather than by the IB: the Investigation proposal, the practical window, the draft deadline, the final submission, and the mock examinations. A family who writes those five school dates on one sheet has a better planning document than any generic revision timetable.

A word on the dates we do not publish. The IB's own website returns an automated-access block, so no IB exam-session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Secondary sources circulate windows and results dates, and they may well be right, but a date a parent acts on should come from the authority that sets it. Ask your school's Diploma coordinator for the session window, the results release arrangement and the internal upload deadlines, and confirm them against ibo.org. A tutoring page that prints an IB date it has not verified is handing you a liability dressed as a service.

Working backwards from the session, the useful structure is four phases. Phase one, roughly the first Diploma year, is content and quantitative fluency, and it is the only phase where learning new material is genuinely efficient. Phase two, spanning the end of Year 12 into Year 13, is the Scientific Investigation, which has to be fitted around content rather than bolted on after it. Phase three is the post-mock window, where triage replaces teaching. Phase four is the final stretch, where nothing new goes in and everything is timed. Students who try to run phase one work in phase four are the most common avoidable failure in this subject.

sections.heading: What eight weeks can actually achieve in IB Chemistry
paragraphs: Families in Al Barsha South frequently arrive with roughly two months left and a specific question: is it worth starting. The answer is yes, with a reshaped plan, and the honest version of what two months buys is narrower than most tutoring pages imply. Eight weeks will not deliver a syllabus. It will reliably deliver three things: technique on the paper formats, recovery of marks currently being lost to presentation and timing, and genuine improvement on two or three high-yield topics chosen for mark value rather than for comfort.

Here is how a realistic eight weeks divides. Weeks one and two are diagnosis and the cheapest wins: a full Paper 1 and a Paper 2 section sat timed, marked against the mark scheme, with lost marks sorted into causes. Presentation and precision errors usually surface immediately, and those are recoverable in days rather than months. Weeks three to six are two or three targeted topics, chosen because they carry weight in both papers - Reactivity 1 enthalpy work and Reactivity 3 acid-base behaviour are common picks - taught then immediately tested on past-paper questions. Weeks seven and eight are entirely timed papers and data-booklet speed.

What eight weeks cannot do is close an Investigation that has not been started, or rescue a student who has not met half the HL extension material. In those cases the honest advice differs: speak to the school about the Investigation timeline before paying for tutoring, because an internal deadline is a school matter and no tutor can move it. And where the content gap is genuinely large, the better use of eight weeks is to secure the achievable grade band firmly rather than to chase a band that the calendar has already closed. A tutor who agrees to cover two years of chemistry in eight weeks is telling you something about their honesty, not their ability.

sections.heading: The Scientific Investigation, and where its marks are actually lost
paragraphs: The Scientific Investigation is twenty per cent of the chemistry grade, up to 3,000 words, and assessed on four criteria worth six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. It is the only part of the course where the student sets the pace, which is both the opportunity and the problem. Students who start late lose marks in a predictable order, and the order is useful to know in advance.

Research design marks go missing when the question is not actually answerable with the equipment available, or when the variables are named but not controlled in any described way. Data analysis marks go when uncertainty is ignored, when significant figures are carried inconsistently, or when a graph is drawn without considering whether the relationship is linear. Conclusion marks go when the student states a result without comparing it to accepted values or to the theory the investigation was testing. Evaluation is where most of the loss sits: students write a list of limitations - time, equipment, temperature - without saying what effect each one had on the result and in which direction. The criterion rewards the effect, not the list.

What a tutor may do here is strictly bounded, and the boundary is worth stating plainly because competitors in this market cross it. We question the method, point out an uncontrolled variable, ask what the uncertainty on a measurement is and why, challenge whether the conclusion follows from the data, and read a section the student has written to tell them which criterion it is not yet meeting. We do not write any part of the report, redraft it, supply a research question, or edit it towards submission. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments. That is an academic-integrity breach, the consequences fall on the student rather than the seller, and it is not available from us at any price.
bullets: Four criteria, six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion, evaluation

sections.heading: What IB Chemistry tutoring costs in this part of Dubai
paragraphs: Budgeting is easier monthly than hourly, so start there. Packages visible in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 monthly estimates for a single weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. A Year 13 chemistry student on one specialist session a week therefore sits in that top band for the exam year, which is a real line in a household budget and a smaller one than most families fear before they look.

The hourly figures behind those monthly numbers, each published by the provider named: Tutopiya advertises online sessions from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, generally university-student tutors. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with home tutors to AED 500, and IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. BartyED publishes AED 650 for premium examiner-led work. None of those are IB Gram prices; they are what each of those providers states publicly, as of October 2026.

Reading the bands as a market, the step worth paying for in Diploma chemistry is the one into genuine subject specialism, because the current guide is recent enough that a generalist science tutor may be teaching an older structure. The step above that buys scarcity rather than quality and should be checked rather than assumed, particularly where examiner status is claimed: that claim is only worth something if it can be evidenced, and it should never be used to imply access to marking or boundary information. Worth holding in context too: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. IB Gram publishes no rate card here; the free trial lesson exists so the teaching is seen before money is discussed.

sections.heading: Online, in-home or group for a Diploma chemistry student here
paragraphs: To be unambiguous: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. UAE lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, and visiting tutors are a service we operate only in India. That belongs near the top of a page a parent reached by looking for someone local, and the comparison that follows is not a defence of a limitation - for Diploma chemistry specifically, the online case is the stronger one on its merits.

The reason is the match, not the medium. A Diploma chemistry student needs someone who knows the current guide, the Investigation criteria by letter, and the difference between what Paper 1B and Paper 2 reward. In a radius of a few kilometres around Al Barsha South, the number of people who fit that description and are free between 4.30pm and 7pm is small. Widen the pool past the drive and it is not small. A family choosing in-home is choosing geography first and specialism second, and in a subject this specific that trade is expensive in a way the hourly rate does not show.

The in-home advantages are genuine and worth naming: physical presence keeps a tired student at the desk, and a tutor in the room can see a page and a face at once. Video covers more of that than sceptics expect, because chemistry work is written and diagrammatic, and a shared whiteboard with the data booklet open side by side is closer to the in-room experience than a conversation-based subject would be. Sessions can also be recorded, so a student can rewatch a Hess cycle worked through at the point they lost it, which no in-home lesson provides. What video asks of a family is a desk, a door left open and a charged device.

sections.heading: KHDA, inspection reports and what they say about a school's science teaching
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described by u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a report per school across six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. For a family in Al Barsha South trying to understand whether a chemistry problem belongs to their child or to the teaching, that report is the only independent evidence available and it is free to read.

Read past the headline band. Reports break attainment and progress down by subject and phase, so a school rated Good overall may be rated Acceptable for post-16 science attainment. They also comment on teaching quality and on assessment, and an inspection note that internal assessment data does not align with external outcomes is a direct explanation for a predicted grade that keeps not arriving. None of this means a school is letting a student down; it tells a family which gap they are considering paying to cover, which is a different and more useful question.

The scale context matters because it explains staffing. Dubai had 387,441 private-school students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum on 37% of enrolment, Indian on 26%, US on 14% and International Baccalaureate on 7%. Seven new private schools open for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three IB, adding 16,846 places, after six opened during 2025-26 with enrolment up 6%. A Diploma chemistry department in a school that opened eighteen months ago is, by definition, teaching the current guide for the first or second time. That is not a criticism. It is a reason a specialist second opinion on the Investigation criteria can be worth having.

sections.heading: Permits, ethics and who may legally tutor your child in Dubai
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The official route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Because the permit is free and quick, there is no reasonable explanation for a working tutor not holding one. u.ae states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE will be subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount can honestly be quoted, and figures circulating online could not be verified. Ask to see the permit rather than a listing or a screenshot of one.

The ethics layer is separate and matters specifically in chemistry, where a student's own teacher also supervises their Investigation. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's own school. Those are press-reported positions and should be checked against the current policy document, but the direction is clear enough to act on: hiring your child's own chemistry teacher privately is the wrong move even where it looks convenient. A separate point for completeness: an operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram operates no UAE centre and holds no approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in a Diploma timetable
paragraphs: A scheduling fact that surprises families new to Dubai: the mandatory UAE subjects run alongside the Diploma Programme, not instead of parts of it. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose academic year starts in April. The federal position behind this is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations.

The organisational rules are precise. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students; and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Schools must ensure all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

The reason this sits on a chemistry page is time. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, permits schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Those periods come out of the same timetable as six Diploma subjects, the core, and practical chemistry. A Dubai Diploma student is carrying a heavier week than the same student would elsewhere, which is why the question is never whether a child has an hour free but which hour a weekly session displaces. For tutoring in the mandatory subjects themselves, note that using any different or additional content without prior MoE permission is strictly prohibited, so support there stays within the school's own material.

sections.heading: Starting mid-year, and what we will tell you honestly
paragraphs: The first step is a free trial lesson, and for this subject the trial starts with paperwork rather than chemistry. We ask for the level, the school's Investigation deadlines, the most recent marked assessment and the mock result if there is one. Then the session works a section of a past paper live with the data booklet open, and the tutor marks it against the mark scheme while the student watches. What a parent has at the end is a position on the calendar, a list of topics by confidence band, and a view on whether one session a week or two makes sense from here. No card is required and nothing continues if the match is wrong.

Matching for Diploma chemistry takes a few days rather than minutes, because the match is to the current guide and to the Investigation criteria rather than to the word chemistry. The pool for HL and SL chemistry is reasonable, so most requests fill quickly. The exception we will tell you about rather than paper over: a request that combines a niche Investigation context with a narrow evening slot during the busiest weeks of Year 13 sometimes has no genuine specialist free. In that case the options are to wait, to move the slot, or to begin with a strong generalist on a stated interim basis - and we will say which one it is.

After the first month the plan is tested against evidence. A fresh paper section is sat timed and the lost marks are classified the same way as in the trial. If precision and timing have improved and content has not, teaching takes a larger share of the sessions; if content is closing and timing is not, the balance moves to timed papers. Sessions pause for school assessment weeks and for travel, and the slot is held. Nobody here will promise a 7, because no tutor can deliver a grade. What a chemistry tutor can deliver is a student who knows which paper is costing them marks and why, eight weeks before anyone else notices.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 13 and mocks went badly. Is there still time for chemistry?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a reshaped plan. After mocks the efficient work is triage rather than teaching. The first session marks a full Paper 1 and a Paper 2 section against the mark scheme and sorts every lost mark into a cause: content gap, imprecise wording, timing, or misread command. Precision and timing losses usually recover within a few weeks because they are habits. Content gaps are prioritised by mark yield across both papers rather than by what the student finds least unpleasant. What the remaining weeks will not do is teach the whole Higher Level extension, and a tutor who claims otherwise is selling.

faqs.question: How is IB Chemistry assessed at Standard and Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 carries 36% and combines multiple-choice questions with data-based questions, running longer at Higher Level. Paper 2 carries 44% and uses short and extended response questions. The Scientific Investigation carries the remaining 20% and is marked internally against four criteria. A data booklet is supplied in both papers, which shifts the skill from recall towards navigation and application. Higher Level is 240 taught hours against 150 at Standard Level, and the difference is depth within the same Structure and Reactivity themes rather than a separate list of extra topics.

faqs.question: Which Investigation criterion costs chemistry students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Evaluation, by a clear margin. The four criteria - research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation - are worth six marks each. Students handle design and data reasonably and then write evaluation as a list: not enough time, limited equipment, room temperature varied. The criterion does not reward the list. It rewards saying what effect each limitation had on the result and in which direction, with a suggested improvement that would actually address it. Conclusion marks are the second most common loss, usually because a result is stated without being compared to an accepted value or to the theory being tested.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help write my child's Chemistry Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: No, and anyone who offers to should be avoided. A tutor may question the research question, point out an uncontrolled variable, ask how an uncertainty was arrived at, challenge whether the conclusion follows from the data, and read a section the student has written to say which criterion it is not yet meeting. A tutor may not supply a research question, write or part-write the report, or edit it towards submission. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright. The malpractice consequences of that fall on the student, not the seller, and it is not something IB Gram offers at any price.

faqs.question: When are the IB exams, and why does this page not give the dates?
faqs.answer: UAE Diploma schools enter the May session. This page deliberately publishes no specific IB exam or results date, because the IB's own site returns an automated-access block and no date in our research could be confirmed from the IB itself. Secondary sources circulate windows, and they may be accurate, but a date a family schedules around should come from the body that sets it. Ask your school's Diploma coordinator for the session window, the internal upload deadlines and the results arrangements, then confirm against ibo.org. Any tutoring page printing an unverified IB date is passing you a risk.

faqs.question: Should my child take Chemistry at Higher or Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Decide it on tested evidence rather than on ambition or on a university wish list alone. The useful diagnostic is to teach one Higher-Level-only element properly - the Reactivity 1 entropy and Gibbs energy work is a good choice - then test it under timed conditions. A student who handles that comfortably can carry 240 hours of depth. A student who handles it only with heavy support will likely carry it at the cost of their other five subjects. The decision sits with the school within IB registration rules, so bring marked evidence to that conversation rather than a preference.

faqs.question: What does IB Chemistry tutoring cost monthly around Al Barsha South?
faqs.answer: Monthly is the easier frame. Bestimate's Dubai 2026 estimates for one weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, which is the band a Year 13 chemistry student falls into. Packages visible in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are other providers' published figures, not ours. IB Gram runs a free trial lesson first and discusses cost once you have seen the teaching.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a chemistry tutor to our home in Al Barsha South?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. UAE lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For Diploma chemistry the online case is genuinely strong rather than a compromise: the binding constraint is finding someone who knows the current guide and the Investigation criteria, and within a few kilometres of Al Barsha South the number of such people free between 4.30pm and 7pm is small. Widening past the drive widens the specialism available.

faqs.question: My child came from MYP Sciences and is struggling in Year 12 chemistry. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always a quantitative gap rather than a chemistry one. MYP Sciences builds strong inquiry and design instincts, assessed against four criteria out of eight each, and rather less fluency in the arithmetic Diploma chemistry assumes: moles, concentration, limiting reagents, unit conversion and significant figures carried through a multi-step calculation. The student understands the chemistry and stalls in the middle of the working. The remedy is short, targeted quantitative drill separated from conceptual teaching, usually a few weeks of it, not a general chemistry course from the beginning.

faqs.question: How many chemistry sessions a week does a Dubai Diploma student usually need?
faqs.answer: One is the normal starting point and two is the exception rather than the default. One weekly session is enough to work slightly ahead of the class on quantitative topics and behind it on gaps, provided the student does the set work between sessions. Two becomes justified in three situations: a large content gap carried into Year 13, Higher Level alongside a second demanding science, or a short intensive block around the Investigation deadline. We would rather start with one and add a second on evidence than book two and discover the student had no time to use either.

faqs.question: How do I tell a real chemistry specialist from a general science tutor?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions before the first paid session. Which themes does the current guide use to organise content, and the answer should be Structure 1 to 3 and Reactivity 1 to 3. What are the four Investigation criteria and what is each worth, with six marks each as the answer. What is the difference between what Paper 1B and Paper 2 reward. A specialist answers all three without hesitation. A general science tutor usually answers the first and hesitates on the second, which tells you they will be learning the Investigation alongside your child.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan or around school assessment weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they routinely do. Sessions shift to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan for families who prefer it, and the slot is held rather than lost. We also pause during school assessment weeks, because a student sitting internal examinations does not benefit from a tutoring session the same evening. Travel breaks work the same way: the slot stays reserved. For Year 13 students the one period we advise against pausing is the eight weeks before the session, since timed-paper practice loses its value when it becomes occasional rather than weekly.

faqs.question: Is a KHDA inspection report useful for judging a school's chemistry teaching?
faqs.answer: More useful than most parents realise, provided you read past the overall band. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a report per school on six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak, broken down by subject and by phase, so a school rated Good overall can be rated Acceptable for post-16 science attainment. Reports also comment on assessment quality, and a note that internal data does not align with external outcomes explains a predicted grade that never arrives. With seven new private schools opening in Dubai for 2026-27, three of them IB, department-level variation is normal and worth checking.

faqs.question: What happens if no current-guide chemistry specialist is free when we want to start?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than placing someone and describing them as a specialist. For Higher and Standard Level chemistry the pool is reasonable and most requests fill within a few days. The requests that stall are narrow combinations: an unusual Investigation context, or a single fixed evening slot during the busiest weeks of Year 13. The honest options are to wait a week, to move the slot, or to start with a strong generalist on a clearly stated interim basis. No competitor in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is exactly why we do.

faqs.question: Do the mandatory UAE subjects affect how much chemistry time my child has?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth factoring in before adding a weekly session. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and KHDA calculates their instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit with a recommended minimum of 25 minutes per lesson. Those periods share the week with six Diploma subjects, the core and practical science, so a Dubai Diploma student carries a fuller timetable than the same student elsewhere. The real question is not whether an hour exists but which hour the session displaces.

The free trial lesson then marks a real past-paper section with the data booklet open and places the student on the calendar, with a written list of topics by confidence band. Lessons run live online, one to one, on Gulf Standard Time. No IB dates we have not verified, no grade promises, and a straight answer if the specialist you need is not free this week.

intro.heading: Buy components, not hours
paragraphs: Chemistry is the Diploma subject where spending decisions are made worst, because the hourly rate is the only number most families compare. The useful question is which components are worth paying to support. In IB Chemistry there are three with a clear answer: organic mechanisms, where marks are lost for notation that can be taught in a few sessions; energetics, where sign conventions cost marks across every paper; and the Scientific Investigation, which carries twenty per cent of the grade on its own.

That last figure reframes the whole budget. Twenty per cent of a subject grade sits in a report of up to three thousand words, written at home, decided largely by the research question and the quality of the data collected. Both of those are fixed months before the writing. A family that spends nothing until the spring of Diploma 2 is buying help for the remaining eighty per cent, at a higher rate, in a tighter market.

The Dubai market itself is knowable. Published online rates for a qualified subject tutor run AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one including travel runs AED 180 to 350 per Bestimate's Dubai table, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. Specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650 at the examiner end. All read in October 2026.

Al Furjan sits awkwardly in that market. The community is residential, between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Yalayis Road, and Chemistry Higher Level is one of the scarcer specialisms in the Jebel Ali and Dubai South corridor. So the travel premium here buys the smallest possible pool: the tutor who will drive into the villa districts for 17:00 is frequently comfortable to Standard Level and no further. That is a more expensive mistake than any hourly rate.

IB Gram runs every UAE lesson one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time between 15:30 and 21:30, and no tutor attends a UAE address; home visiting is a service we offer only in India. Removing the drive removes the premium and widens the pool at the same time, which is the only way a Masakin or Quortaj family reliably reaches a Higher Level chemistry specialist.

The rest of this page sets out what the current syllabus actually contains, where chemistry marks go, what each component costs in hours rather than in rhetoric, and where families in this corridor overspend. Our own rates are not on this page, because a price without a subject, a level and a number of weeks attached is a number that misleads. They get discussed after the free trial, when there is a component, a level and a timeframe to attach them to.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-furjan.programmesIntro: Chemistry spending behaves differently at each stage, because what the money protects changes. These are the stages an Al Furjan family will pass through.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme sciences
programmes.description: Assessed on criteria A to D on an eight-point scale, with processing and evaluating data the strand that most consistently costs marks. Chemistry content at this stage is light relative to Diploma demands, so the valuable work is not more content but the quantitative habits the Diploma assumes: moles arithmetic, significant figures, and writing a method with controlled variables named.
programmes.countryNote: This is the cheapest stage to buy and the one skipped most often in Al Furjan. Middle Years students here are home between 15:40 and 16:30, so a 17:00 session fits easily. A weekly session in MYP 4 and 5 costs a fraction of a Diploma 2 rescue block and decides whether Chemistry Higher Level is a realistic choice two years later.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Chemistry
programmes.description: Organised around structure and reactivity rather than a numbered topic list, with continuous reference to the data booklet provided in the exam. Assessment is Paper 1, split into multiple choice and a data-based section, Paper 2 with short and extended response, and the Scientific Investigation at twenty per cent. Higher Level deepens the same framework rather than adding separate topics.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students from Al Furjan travel to the Al Barsha or Al Khail corridor for school, so chemistry sessions here usually start at 18:00 or later. Higher Level Chemistry is among the scarcer specialisms in this part of Dubai, which is why in-home hiring in the villa districts so often produces a tutor working one level below the student.

programmes.name: The Scientific Investigation
programmes.description: One independent investigation reported in up to three thousand words, assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and worth twenty per cent of the grade. In chemistry the commonest failure is a question whose chemistry is sound and whose measurement is impossible with school equipment, which produces data too scattered to support any conclusion.
programmes.countryNote: The cost pattern here is stark. One early session on the research question costs an hour; rebuilding an investigation in the final term costs several and still scores lower, because the data cannot be recollected. Tutors read the criteria with the student, question the design, teach the uncertainty treatment, and give written feedback on the student's own drafts. Nothing is written by the tutor.

programmes.name: From IGCSE Chemistry into the Diploma
programmes.description: IGCSE Chemistry builds recall, equations and single-step moles calculations. The Diploma expects confident stoichiometry under time pressure, formal energetics with sign conventions, mechanism notation, and extended written explanation. The gap is quantitative and notational rather than conceptual, which means targeted work closes it quickly and general revision does not.
programmes.countryNote: Four to six summer sessions is the normal size of this block and the best-value purchase in the sequence. It matters particularly in this corridor because families usually change schools for the Diploma, given the limited full Diploma provision nearby, so a new school and unfamiliar quantitative demands would otherwise arrive in the same term.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-furjan.subjectsIntro: Chemistry support requests from this corridor cluster in a few predictable places. These are the components and neighbouring subjects, with a note on what each costs in hours when it is weak.

subjects.name: Chemistry HL
subjects.description: The structure and reactivity framework at greater depth, with longer quantitative chains and extended explanations built from a named principle. The scarcest chemistry specialism in this part of Dubai, so the component where online matching earns the most. Usually needs a weekly session across both Diploma years rather than a block.

subjects.name: Chemistry SL
subjects.description: The same framework with reduced depth and the identical Scientific Investigation at twenty per cent. Families often under-buy here on the assumption that Standard Level is light; the investigation and the data-based paper make the same demands, and most Standard Level marks are lost in exactly those places.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry and mechanisms
subjects.description: The single best-value block in the subject. Marks go to notation as much as to understanding: curly arrows drawn from the right place, lone pairs shown, intermediates represented properly. Four to six sessions typically converts a student who understands mechanisms into one who scores on them.

subjects.name: Energetics and thermodynamics
subjects.description: Enthalpy, entropy and Gibbs energy, where sign conventions cost marks across every paper and in the investigation. A student who is confident with the chemistry and careless with signs loses marks consistently and invisibly, and the fix is drilled convention work rather than more theory.

subjects.name: Stoichiometry and quantitative chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, concentration, limiting reagents, percentage yield and gas calculations. Everything else in chemistry routes through this, which makes a weakness here expensive: it shows up as poor marks in topics the student actually understands. Usually two to four sessions of pure arithmetic practice.

subjects.name: Reaction kinetics and equilibrium
subjects.description: Rate expressions, orders of reaction, equilibrium constants and Le Chatelier reasoning. Higher Level adds depth that catches students who learned the ideas qualitatively. The reliable loss is explaining a shift without naming which quantity changes and in which direction.

subjects.name: Acids, bases and redox
subjects.description: pH calculations, buffers, titration curves and electrochemistry. Titration curve questions reward reading the graph rather than recalling a shape, and redox questions reward systematic half-equation work. Both are procedural and respond quickly to practice with marked feedback.

subjects.name: The Scientific Investigation
subjects.description: Twenty per cent of the grade, up to three thousand words, assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The research question and the data decide the mark. Four to six sessions, and the earliest of them is worth more than all the rest combined.

subjects.name: Paper 1B: data-based questions
subjects.description: A written examination of experimental skill: processing data, plotting, interpreting gradients, handling uncertainty and using the data booklet. Students revise content and leave this to chance, which makes it the most recoverable set of marks in the subject for a modest number of hours.

subjects.name: Mathematics for Chemistry
subjects.description: Logarithms for pH, rearrangement, standard form and proportional reasoning. Where a student understands the chemistry but stalls on the arithmetic, the correct purchase is mathematics support rather than more chemistry, and one session with a marked paper distinguishes the two.

subjects.name: Physics and Biology alongside Chemistry
subjects.description: Both share the investigation structure and the same uncertainty demands, so families frequently arrange two sciences. Where one tutor genuinely covers both to the level needed that is efficient; where they do not, two specialists outperform one generalist and we will say which applies.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Chemistry
subjects.description: Four thousand words of supervised independent research. Chemistry essays fail on access to equipment and on scope rather than on ambition, and that is diagnosable in one early session. Support is questioning the question and feedback on the student's own drafts, never drafting.
