sections.heading: What each chemistry component is worth paying to support
paragraphs: Rather than quote an hourly rate and leave a family to guess, it is more useful to say which components repay support and roughly how many hours each takes. Chemistry divides neatly here. Some areas are notational and fix fast. Some are arithmetic and need drilling. One carries twenty per cent of the grade and is decided months before it is written. A budget built on that map goes further than one built on a rate comparison.

The best return in the subject is organic mechanism notation. Students who understand mechanisms perfectly well lose marks for arrows drawn from the wrong place, missing lone pairs, and intermediates represented loosely. Four to six sessions typically converts understanding into marks, and at the published mid-market online band of AED 150 to 300 an hour that is a known and modest total for a visible gain across every paper.

The second best is the data-based section of Paper 1, which is effectively a written practical: processing, plotting, gradients, uncertainty and using the data booklet. Students revise content and leave this to chance. Three or four sessions of pure data work usually moves more marks than the same hours spent on any single area of content, because the skills recur in the investigation as well.

The most consequential is the Scientific Investigation at twenty per cent. The cost asymmetry here is extreme: one early session on the research question and the measurement plan, against several late sessions that cannot recover data already collected badly. Any chemistry budget that does not include that early hour is mis-sequenced, whatever the hourly rate attached to it.

sections.heading: Structure and reactivity: what the current syllabus actually looks like
paragraphs: IB Chemistry is no longer organised as a numbered topic list. The course is built around two organising ideas: structure, covering models of the particulate nature of matter, bonding and classification; and reactivity, covering what drives reactions, how much and how fast and how far they go, and the mechanisms by which they happen. Higher Level deepens the same framework rather than appending separate higher-level topics.

This matters when hiring, because a tutor working from an older guide plans revision against a structure the school no longer uses. The symptom is subtle: the content taught is correct, the sequence does not match the school's scheme of work, and the student ends up holding two mental maps of the same subject. Asking a tutor to describe the course's organisation takes ten seconds and settles it.

The framework also changes what good revision looks like. Because bonding and structure underpin reactivity, revising them as separate blocks produces a student who can describe a bond and cannot predict a reaction. The questions on the papers routinely require both at once. Cross-cutting work on why a structure produces a particular reactivity is what the assessment rewards, and it is rarely how a topic-based plan is built.

One further feature worth knowing is the data booklet. Chemistry is examined with a data booklet provided, containing constants, values and spectroscopic information. Students who meet it for the first time in the exam waste minutes locating entries. Using it in every session from the start costs nothing and saves time under pressure, which is why a tutor should have it open routinely rather than occasionally.

sections.heading: Where chemistry marks actually go
paragraphs: Chemistry grades are rarely lost to ignorance of content. They are lost to four specific behaviours, and a parent paying for support should know which of the four they are buying a fix for. The first is sign conventions in energetics: enthalpy and Gibbs energy calculations where the chemistry is understood and the sign is wrong, which costs the mark every time and is almost never noticed by the student.

The second is describing where the paper asked for explaining. A trend stated without its cause earns little. Periodicity questions, bonding and property questions and equilibrium shift questions all reward naming the mechanism or the quantity that changes. This is a command-term problem rather than a chemistry problem, and the fix is written answers marked against the command used, then rewritten once.

The third is mechanism notation. Curly arrows starting from the wrong place, lone pairs omitted, charges unassigned and intermediates drawn loosely. Students find this unfair because they understand the chemistry, and the marker is not assessing understanding in the abstract. It is the most quickly fixable loss in the subject and therefore the best value for a short block of sessions.

The fourth is chemical tests and observations, inherited from IGCSE habits. The paper asks what would be seen and what that shows, and the answer awards credit for the observation and for the conclusion separately. A student who learned the tests as a memorised list produces one of the two. Together these four behaviours account for most of the gap between what a Dubai chemistry student knows and what they score.

sections.heading: The Scientific Investigation, and the price of starting late
paragraphs: The Scientific Investigation is one report of up to three thousand words, worth twenty per cent of the Chemistry grade at both levels, assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The cost argument on this page rests on a single fact about it: the mark is largely determined by the research question and the quality of the data, and both are fixed long before any writing happens.

In chemistry the usual failure is specific. A student chooses a question with sound chemistry behind it and no realistic measurement route using school equipment. Concentration changes too small to detect, reaction times too fast to time by hand, or temperature changes within the noise of the thermometer. The chemistry is right and the data is unusable, and no amount of good writing at the end recovers it.

That is why the cost comparison is so lopsided. One session before the question is fixed, spent asking what will be measured, with what precision, over what range, and with how many repeats, costs an hour at market rates. Rebuilding an investigation in the final term costs five to eight hours, cannot recollect the data, and still scores below what the early hour would have secured. Families in this corridor regularly discover this in Diploma 2.

The boundary on help is absolute and stated at the first session. A tutor may read the four criteria with the student, question the design and the measurement plan, teach the uncertainty and graphical treatment the data needs, show how published work structures an analysis, and give written feedback on the student's own drafts. A tutor may not write the report, process the data, supply the analysis, or outline it for the student to complete. At least one provider in this market sells completed internal assessments; the malpractice exposure from that falls on the student.

sections.heading: The free things to use before paying for anything
paragraphs: Three useful resources in this subject cost nothing, and a family that uses them buys tutoring more precisely afterwards. The first is the data booklet. It is provided in the examination and contains the constants, values and spectroscopic data students waste time hunting for. Working with it open from the first week of the course is free and removes a real source of lost time in the exam room.

The second is the school's own subject clinic. The teacher who set and marked the assessment is better placed than anyone to explain the marking of it, and in most Dubai schools that time exists and is under-used. It is limited and rarely diagnostic across a whole syllabus, but for a specific question about a specific marked answer it is both free and immediate.

The third is the KHDA inspection report for your child's school. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and publishes reports naming subject-level strengths and weaknesses rather than a single verdict. If science attainment is flagged across the school, you are buying support for a structural problem; if the department is strong, the diagnosis is individual. That changes how you brief a tutor.

Only after those three does paid chemistry support become a well-specified purchase: you know the component, the behaviour losing the marks, and whether the school can address it. That is what we ask for at the start, and it is why the free trial is built around a marked paper rather than a general conversation about how your child is finding chemistry.

sections.heading: A two-year chemistry plan against a six-week rescue
paragraphs: The arithmetic that matters to a household is the total, not the hourly rate, so here it is both ways. At the published mid-market online band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, one weekly session across a thirty-six week year costs roughly AED 5,400 to 10,800. Across both Diploma years in chemistry alone that is AED 10,800 to 21,600, and it protects the investigation marks as well as the written papers.

The alternative pattern most families default to is nothing until the spring of Diploma 2, then twenty hours in six weeks at specialist rates of AED 300 to 450, which is AED 6,000 to 9,000. The spend is lower. The ceiling is lower with it, because twenty per cent of the grade has already been submitted and cannot be touched, and because stoichiometry fluency cannot be rebuilt in six weeks while also revising content.

Between those sits the pattern we see work best in this corridor: a weekly session through Diploma 1 at mid-market rates, a defined organic mechanisms block, an early investigation design session, and two shorter sessions a week through the mock window. Sixty to eighty hours over two years, somewhere between AED 9,000 and AED 24,000, with the hours placed where they protect marks rather than where panic puts them.

Context is worth stating too. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's economic incentives package. A family planning chemistry support is working against a stable fee base this year, which makes a planned two-year commitment easier to carry than an unplanned emergency one.

sections.heading: Is there a Higher Level chemistry tutor near Al Furjan?
paragraphs: The honest answer is that Higher Level chemistry is one of the thinner specialisms in this part of Dubai, and a family should not build a plan on the assumption of a local match. Al Furjan is residential, and the Diploma chemistry teachers in the city work near the schools that run the programme, which in the Jebel Ali and Dubai South corridor are fewer than in Al Barsha, Al Khail or Jumeirah.

Requiring Higher Level specifically, in a fixed evening slot, within a reasonable drive of the villa districts, reduces the pool to a handful of people who are generally already committed. What families then do is take the nearest competent science tutor. At Standard Level that sometimes works. At Higher Level the gap appears within two sessions, usually on extended response marking or on energetics sign discipline.

This is also where the travel premium becomes an actively bad purchase rather than a neutral one. Paying AED 150 extra an hour for a tutor who can reach Al Furjan by 17:00 is paying to shrink the pool you are choosing from. In a scarce specialism that is the wrong direction, and it is the single clearest cost argument for online delivery on this page.

IB Gram matches by subject and level and teaches one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time between 15:30 and 21:30. No tutor attends a UAE address, since home visiting is an India-only service. Where we cannot cover a request we say so rather than substituting a Standard Level tutor. Availability tightens in January and February, when every Diploma 2 family in Dubai wants the same evening slots.

sections.heading: What no amount of money should buy
paragraphs: There is one purchase available in this market that a family should refuse. At least one UAE provider advertises completed internal assessments at a fixed price. The transaction looks like a shortcut and is a transfer of risk: the IB treats submitted work that is not the student's own as malpractice, and the exposure falls on the student and their Diploma rather than on the seller.

The legitimate alternative is not a weaker version of the same thing. A tutor can read the assessment criteria with the student, interrogate the research question and the measurement plan, teach the uncertainty and graphical treatment the data requires, show how published work structures an argument, and give written feedback on the student's own drafts against each criterion. Most of the recoverable marks live inside that list.

We also do not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Those are cited and linked, and sessions work from what the school has issued to the student. For published documents that is a copyright matter, and for unreleased material it is a malpractice exposure for the student, so neither risk is worth taking to save a download.

Two further limits. We do not predict or guarantee grades, for chemistry or anything else; a promised grade is a sales device rather than a teaching plan. And we do not describe tutors as IB examiners without evidence of current status, nor use examiner status to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content, because it confers none of those things.

faqs.question: What does IB chemistry tutoring cost for a family in Al Furjan?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates, read in October 2026, put a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one including travel runs AED 180 to 350 per Bestimate, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. Specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650. Those are other providers' figures, not an IB Gram price list, which is discussed after the free trial.

faqs.question: Which chemistry component gives the best return on a small budget?
faqs.answer: Organic mechanism notation. Students who understand mechanisms lose marks for arrows drawn from the wrong place, missing lone pairs, unassigned charges and loosely drawn intermediates. Four to six sessions typically converts understanding into marks, and at the published AED 150 to 300 band that is a known total of roughly AED 600 to 1,800 for a gain visible across both written papers. The second best is the data-based section of Paper 1, which three or four sessions of pure processing work usually improves.

faqs.question: Why is starting chemistry support in the spring of Diploma 2 expensive?
faqs.answer: Because twenty per cent of the grade has already gone. The Scientific Investigation is submitted months before the papers, and its mark is set by the research question and the quality of the data, neither of which can be recollected. A twenty-hour spring block at specialist rates of AED 300 to 450 costs AED 6,000 to 9,000 and can only address the remaining written marks. A weekly session from Diploma 1 at mid-market rates costs more in total and reaches everything.

faqs.question: How is IB Chemistry organised now?
faqs.answer: Around two organising ideas rather than a numbered topic list: structure, covering particulate models, bonding and classification; and reactivity, covering what drives reactions, how much and how fast and how far they go, and the mechanisms involved. Higher Level deepens the same framework instead of adding separate topics. Ask a tutor to describe that organisation. One working from an older guide will teach correct content in a sequence that does not match the school's scheme of work, which leaves the student holding two maps of one subject.

faqs.question: What is the commonest way a chemistry investigation fails in Dubai schools?
faqs.answer: A question with sound chemistry and no realistic measurement route using school equipment. Concentration changes too small to detect, reactions too fast to time by hand, temperature changes inside the thermometer's noise. The chemistry is right and the data is unusable, and good writing at the end cannot recover it. One session before the question is fixed, asking what will be measured, how precisely, over what range and with how many repeats, prevents nearly all of these.

faqs.question: Where do Dubai chemistry students lose marks they should have kept?
faqs.answer: Four places. Sign conventions in energetics, where the chemistry is understood and the sign is wrong, which costs the mark silently every time. Describing a trend when the command term asked for an explanation. Mechanism notation. And chemical tests answered as a memorised list rather than as an observation plus a conclusion, which is an IGCSE habit carried forward. Together those four account for most of the gap between what a student knows and what they score, and all four are fixable.

faqs.question: Is the data booklet worth using in every session?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it costs nothing. Chemistry is examined with a data booklet provided, containing constants, values and spectroscopic information, and students who meet it for the first time in the exam lose minutes locating entries under pressure. Having it open in every session from the start of the course makes it familiar by the time it matters. A tutor who only produces it occasionally is leaving free marks on the table, and it is a fair thing to ask about at the trial.

faqs.question: Does a visiting chemistry tutor in Al Furjan cost more for the same teaching?
faqs.answer: It costs more and in this subject often buys less. Published in-home rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 online reflect the drive rather than teaching quality. The problem specific to chemistry is that Higher Level is one of the scarcer specialisms in the Jebel Ali and Dubai South corridor, so requiring a tutor who can reach the villa districts by 17:00 shrinks the pool you are choosing from. Paying to narrow the choice is the wrong direction.

faqs.question: Is Standard Level chemistry worth paying to support?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and families routinely under-buy here. The Scientific Investigation is the same twenty per cent at Standard Level, with the same four criteria and the same three thousand word limit, and the data-based section of Paper 1 makes the same demands. Most Standard Level marks are lost in exactly those places rather than in advanced content. Assuming Standard Level needs little support is how a student who could have scored well ends up with a grade shaped by an unsupported investigation.

faqs.question: Is my child's chemistry problem actually a maths problem?
faqs.answer: One session with a marked paper will tell you. Logarithms for pH, rearrangement, standard form and proportional reasoning are routine demands, and a student who explains the chemistry well then stalls on the arithmetic needs mathematics support rather than more chemistry. Stoichiometry is the particular case: everything in the subject routes through moles arithmetic, so weakness there shows up as poor marks in topics the student genuinely understands. Two to four sessions of pure arithmetic practice usually settles it.

faqs.question: What should I do before paying for any chemistry tutoring?
faqs.answer: Three free things. Ask the school for the paper-level breakdown of the last mock, so you know which component is actually losing marks. Use the school's subject clinic for specific questions about specific marked answers, since the teacher who marked it explains it best. And read the KHDA inspection report for the school, which names subject-level strengths and weaknesses, so you know whether you are buying help for an individual gap or a departmental one. Then the purchase is well specified.

faqs.question: How many hours does a full two-year chemistry plan take?
faqs.answer: Sixty to eighty in the pattern that works best in this corridor: a weekly session through Diploma 1, a defined organic mechanisms block, an early investigation design session, and two shorter sessions a week through the mock window. At the published AED 150 to 300 mid-market band that is roughly AED 9,000 to 24,000 over two years. The point is not the total but the placement: hours put where they protect marks rather than where panic puts them in the final term.

faqs.question: Can a tutor process my child's investigation data if the chemistry is correct?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor may teach the uncertainty and graphical techniques the data requires, explain what each criterion rewards, question whether the processing answers the research question, and give written feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not process the data, supply the analysis, write or rewrite the report, or outline it for the student to fill in. That boundary is stated at the first session of any investigation block and the feedback is given in writing so the school can see its nature.

faqs.question: Is an AED 650 an hour chemistry tutor ever the right purchase?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and almost never before the final two terms. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the examiner-experienced end of the Dubai market, and that depth has a use for a student already scoring well who needs component-level insight for the last few marks. For a student with a notational or arithmetic gap, the same money buys three times as many hours at the published AED 150 to 300 band, and hours are what closes a gap. We also do not describe tutors as examiners without evidence of current status.

faqs.question: When can chemistry sessions run for a Diploma student in the villa districts?
faqs.answer: Usually 18:00, and 19:00 on a day with a fixture or a CAS commitment. Diploma students from Al Furjan mostly travel to the Al Barsha or Al Khail corridor for school, so they are not home before 16:30. Students at Dubai Investments Park or Green Community schools are home by 15:40 and can start at 15:50, which suits Middle Years science. Sessions run to 21:30 Gulf Standard Time, and a session missed to a late bus moves to the next evening rather than the next week.

faqs.question: Will more hours guarantee a better chemistry grade?
faqs.answer: No, and we do not guarantee grades in any subject. Hours placed badly change very little: twenty hours of content revision will not fix sign conventions, mechanism notation or an investigation already submitted. Hours placed well change a great deal, which is why this page is organised by component rather than by rate. Ask any provider which component their hours will address and how they know. A plan that cannot answer that is selling time rather than teaching chemistry.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-garhoud.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma Chemistry to Al Garhoud and wider Deira-side families: Higher and Standard Level theory, the data booklet and organic mechanisms, past-paper technique, and process coaching on the student's own investigation.

intro.heading: Price the whole Diploma, not the first hour
paragraphs: Chemistry tutoring is sold by the hour and bought by the term, and that mismatch is where Al Garhoud families lose money. A parent compares two quotes, picks the lower one, and discovers eighteen months later that the cheaper tutor needed twice as many hours to cover the same ground. The useful unit of comparison is not AED per hour. It is the total cost of carrying a Diploma chemistry student from the start of DP1 to the final paper, and what that total buys at each price point.

Start with the honest arithmetic. A Diploma subject taken seriously with weekly support over two years runs to somewhere between 60 and 90 tutored hours, depending on where the student starts and whether the Scientific Investigation needs a dedicated block. At the budget end of the Dubai market, advertised from around AED 45 to 150 an hour by providers including EdFlik at AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from about AED 33 to 52, that is a modest line in a family budget. At the specialist band of AED 200 to 450 and above, quoted by TutorChase at AED 270 and shown in Bestimate's 2026 rate table as AED 200 to 450 or more, it is a substantial one. The decision deserves more than a glance at the hourly figure.

The second thing to price is what the hours are spent on. Chemistry divides cleanly into content a student can learn from a textbook and content that genuinely needs a teacher. Memorising the solubility rules does not need paid hours. Learning to see why a particular organic mechanism proceeds the way it does, or why an enthalpy cycle has been set up in the direction it has, does. Families who buy twenty hours of re-teaching bonding have bought something available free; families who buy ten hours of mechanism reasoning and mark-scheme work have bought the thing that moves the grade.

The third is the shape of the spend across the two years. Diploma chemistry does not need the same intensity throughout. DP1 rewards steady low-volume work that keeps the student level with the school's sequence. The investigation needs a short concentrated block timed to an internal deadline that sits months before the examination session. DP2 needs a thin maintenance pattern followed by a dense run-in. Spreading the same budget evenly across twenty-four months is the most common planning error, and it costs more than it looks because the heavy hours land where they do the least good.

Lessons here are delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India, and the pricing consequence is worth stating plainly: published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor working online, and a large part of that gap is the car crossing the Creek at 17:00. For an Al Garhoud family that difference, paid weekly across a two-year Diploma, is a meaningful number of additional teaching hours.

programmes.name: The investigation block and the final run-in
programmes.description: Two discrete purchases rather than a continuation of the weekly pattern. The investigation block is three to five sessions timed to the school's internal deadline. The run-in is two or three sessions a week for six to ten weeks before the examination session, built entirely around timed papers and mark schemes. Pricing these separately makes the two-year total predictable.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-garhoud.subjectsIntro: Not every chemistry topic justifies a paid hour. These are the strands Al Garhoud families actually buy time on, with a note on whether the money is well spent there.

subjects.name: Moles, stoichiometry and limiting reagents
subjects.description: The foundation everything quantitative rests on, and genuinely worth paid hours early because an insecure mole concept quietly corrupts titration, energetics and equilibrium work for two years. Three or four sessions in DP1 is a better investment than twenty in DP2.

subjects.name: Atomic structure and periodicity
subjects.description: Mostly learnable from a textbook and rarely worth many paid hours. The exception is explaining trends rather than stating them: a mark scheme wants the named reason, and students who can recite the trend still lose the explanation marks.

subjects.name: Bonding, structure and intermolecular forces
subjects.description: Cheap to teach and expensive to leave vague. Questions ask students to justify a physical property from a structure, which is reasoning rather than recall. One or two targeted sessions usually close the gap for good.

subjects.name: Energetics and thermochemistry
subjects.description: Worth paying for. Enthalpy cycles require students to set up a route rather than apply a formula, and the sign conventions defeat a large share of candidates. Higher Level extensions here add entropy and spontaneity, which carry their own set of reliable losses.

subjects.name: Chemical kinetics and rate
subjects.description: Standard Level work is manageable independently. The Higher Level rate-law and mechanism material is not, because it requires interpreting data to propose a rate-determining step. This is a strand where a specialist earns the rate in two sessions.

subjects.name: Equilibrium and the equilibrium constant
subjects.description: Le Chatelier questions look easy and are marked strictly: a direction of shift without the reason earns little. Higher Level calculations with equilibrium constants demand confident algebra, and that algebra is often the real obstacle rather than the chemistry.

subjects.name: Acids, bases, pH and buffers
subjects.description: High-yield paid hours. Weak acid calculations, buffer behaviour and titration curve interpretation appear reliably and reward precise method. Students routinely lose marks by using the strong acid approach on a weak acid question without noticing the difference.

subjects.name: Redox, electrochemistry and cells
subjects.description: Half-equation balancing in acidic and basic conditions is drillable and worth drilling. Electrode potential questions require a convention applied consistently, and inconsistent sign handling is the single most common source of lost marks in the topic.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry and reaction mechanisms
subjects.description: The topic Al Garhoud families buy the most hours for, and usually correctly. Mechanisms cannot be memorised at Higher Level volume; they have to be reasoned from structure and electron movement. Expect this strand to absorb a quarter of the two-year total.

subjects.name: The data booklet and the periodic table provided
subjects.description: A skill rather than a reference habit, and almost never taught deliberately. Students lose minutes hunting for values and misuse constants whose units differ from their classroom notation. Twenty minutes of practice pays for itself inside one paper.

subjects.name: Uncertainties, error analysis and graph work
subjects.description: Carries marks on the papers and underpins the investigation, so work here counts twice. Percentage uncertainty propagation and deciding what a gradient physically represents are the two specific skills, and both are quick to teach.

subjects.name: Extended-response and command-term technique
subjects.description: The cheapest grade movement available in the final two terms. Longer questions are marked against named points, so writing the required reason matters more than writing at length. Distinguishing state, describe, explain, deduce and evaluate is an hour's work with permanent value.

sections.heading: A two-year chemistry budget in dirhams, phase by phase
paragraphs: Here is the spend laid out the way a family actually encounters it. The figures use the published market bands, so they describe what a Dubai family would pay a specialist at the going rate rather than any price IB Gram sets. Take the specialist band at AED 200 to 450 an hour, which TutorChase publishes at AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 table shows as AED 200 to 450 or more, and apply it to the phase structure that Diploma chemistry actually needs.

The headline is that the two-year total is dominated by DP1, not by the run-in, even though the run-in feels like the expensive part. Thirty-four weekly hours across DP1 at a mid-specialist rate is a larger number than twenty intensive hours in DP2. That is the opposite of how most families plan, which is to economise through DP1 and then buy heavily in the final term. The economising is false, because the DP1 gaps are what make the DP2 block long.

The second thing the table shows is how cheap the investigation block is relative to its weight in the grade. The Scientific Investigation is assessed internally against four criteria totalling 24 marks and forms part of the final subject grade, and three to five sessions is enough to make the difference between a student who understands what each criterion rewards and one who does not. Per mark, it is the best-value purchase in the two years.

The third is that the bridging block before DP1 barely registers in the total and prevents a disproportionate share of the later spend. Six sessions on moles, concentration and stoichiometric reasoning in the summer before the Diploma starts costs a fraction of the term of remedial work it replaces. Nothing else on this page has that ratio.

sections.heading: Tutoring in context: where it sits in a Dubai education budget
paragraphs: A tutoring figure means nothing without the rest of the budget beside it, and Dubai gives an unusually clear reference point. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. School fees are the largest line in most families' education spending and they are, for this year, frozen. Tutoring is the line that is still moving.

That changes the planning question. A family whose fees are flat has a clearer view of what discretionary spending is available, and the sensible response is to plan the tutoring total deliberately rather than let it accumulate hour by hour. The monthly packages advertised in the Dubai market make this easier to think about: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a single weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Those monthly figures expose the in-home premium more starkly than hourly rates do. Four two-hour in-home sessions at AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month is eight hours of teaching; AED 799 a month buys eight online sessions. The difference per month, sustained across a two-year Diploma, is a substantial number of additional teaching hours, and a good portion of what the premium covers is a car crossing the Creek in peak traffic rather than anything that happens in the lesson.

The scale of the sector gives the last piece of context. Dubai reported 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen curricula, with UK-curriculum schools at 37 per cent of enrolment and the IB at 7 per cent. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. A growing Diploma cohort means growing demand for Diploma chemistry specialists, which is a reason to settle the arrangement early in DP1 rather than in the term before the papers.

sections.heading: Provider models compared, and what the cheapest one leaves out
paragraphs: There are six realistic ways to buy chemistry support in Dubai and they differ in more than price. The comparison that matters is not which is cheapest per hour but which includes the things a Diploma chemistry grade needs: a tutor who can read a mark scheme, continuity with one person across two years, a defined position on the investigation, and a way out if the match is wrong.

The budget online tier, advertised from around AED 45 to 150 an hour, is genuinely useful for MYP sciences and for IGCSE chemistry catch-up. For Higher Level Diploma chemistry it tends to omit the specific thing you are paying for, which is diagnosis. A tutor who re-teaches bonding to a student whose problem is organic mechanism reasoning has delivered an hour of teaching and no progress, and the hour was cheap in isolation and expensive in aggregate.

Tuition centre group classes work on content coverage and cannot work on an individual's loss points, which is the entire purpose of chemistry tutoring in DP2. They also reintroduce a journey into an afternoon that was already tight, and the journey is the thing an Al Garhoud family was trying to avoid. In-home one-to-one, quoted across Dubai at AED 180 to 500 with Bestimate's common range at AED 180 to 350, carries the travel inside the rate; it is not a service IB Gram provides in the UAE, and the table includes it as the comparison it is.

The table also includes a column nobody in this market publishes: what happens if the match is wrong. That matters financially. A family that has paid for a term in advance and discovers in week four that the tutor cannot diagnose has lost the term, not the hour. A free trial before any payment, and a stated process for changing tutor, are worth more in expected cost than a twenty per cent difference in hourly rate.

sections.heading: Organic chemistry: where the hours actually go
paragraphs: If a chemistry budget overruns, organic chemistry is almost always the reason. It is the strand Al Garhoud families buy the most hours for, and in Higher Level it is the strand where memorisation stops working. Students arrive having learned a list of reactions as facts, and the questions ask them to reason from structure and electron movement to a product they have not seen before. That gap cannot be closed by repetition, which is why it absorbs hours.

The expensive mistake is treating it as a volume problem. A student who does fifty mechanism questions without understanding why a nucleophile attacks where it does has reinforced a pattern-matching habit that will fail on an unfamiliar substrate. The cheap version is slower and shorter: four or five sessions spent on electron movement, on why a particular carbon is electron-poor, and on what a reagent is actually doing, after which the fifty questions become useful practice rather than a substitute for understanding.

Higher Level extends this material significantly, and the extensions are where the mark differences open up between a 5 and a 7. Synthetic routes, spectroscopic identification and the reasoning behind reaction conditions all appear, and all reward a student who can argue rather than recall. The data booklet and the spectroscopic data provided in the examination are part of this: a student who has practised using them reads a spectrum in a minute, and a student who has not loses five.

For budgeting purposes, allocate roughly a quarter of the two-year total to organic chemistry and expect to spend it in two concentrated phases rather than spread thinly. One phase in DP1 when the functional group work begins, one in DP2 when the Higher Level extensions and synthesis questions arrive. Spread across twenty-four weekly lessons it achieves less for the same money, because the reasoning has to be built in a run rather than revisited monthly.

sections.heading: Three places Al Garhoud families waste chemistry money
paragraphs: The first is paying for content coverage that the school is already providing competently. A Diploma chemistry teacher in a Dubai IB school is teaching the course to a class five times a fortnight. Paying a tutor to deliver the same content again, a week behind, is the most common form of waste in this market and it is easy to detect: if the tutor's lesson plan is the textbook chapter order rather than your child's specific loss points, you are buying a second lecture.

The second is buying intensity instead of diagnosis. Three sessions a week in DP1 feels like seriousness and usually is not, because the limiting factor at that stage is how much independent work the student does between lessons. A student doing one lesson a week and one timed past paper a fortnight will outperform a student doing three lessons and no independent work, at a third of the cost. Intensity earns its keep in the final six to ten weeks and rarely before.

The third is leaving the investigation to chance and then paying to rescue it. The Scientific Investigation is internally assessed on four criteria totalling 24 marks, and a student who has never had the criteria explained is guessing at what is being rewarded. Three sessions before the work starts is cheap. A panicked block in the week before the internal deadline is expensive, less effective, and the point at which families are most likely to be offered help that crosses the academic-honesty line.

Behind all three is the same error: buying hours rather than buying a plan. The question to ask any tutor before paying is not how many sessions they recommend but what the first three sessions will diagnose and how the plan changes depending on what they find. A tutor who answers that in specifics is worth the specialist band. A tutor who answers it with a number of sessions is selling hours.

sections.heading: The investigation: a defined block, a defined limit
paragraphs: Diploma chemistry includes an internally assessed Scientific Investigation, assessed against four criteria totalling 24 marks. Treat it as a separate purchase with a defined scope, because that is both the cheapest way to buy it and the clearest way to keep the academic-honesty boundary visible.

What the block legitimately contains: each criterion explained with its mark allocation, so the student knows what is being judged; a research question interrogated until the student can defend it; a challenge to whether the variable control does what the student claims; an explanation of what good uncertainty treatment and good evaluation look like, demonstrated on a different investigation; and written feedback on a draft the student has written. Three to five sessions covers all of it.

What the block cannot contain, at any price: designing the investigation, supplying the research question, writing any section, or redrafting the student's text to completion. The submission must be the student's own work. A breach is academic malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student's award. This search results set includes an operator selling completed Internal Assessments outright at a fixed price, which is the offer to refuse however difficult the term has become.

Scheduling is the free part of the saving. Investigation deadlines are set internally by the school, usually months before the examination session, and in most Dubai Diploma timetables they land near the mock examinations. A block placed before that collision costs the same as one placed inside it and achieves considerably more, because the student is not choosing between two deadlines. Ask the school for the internal date in September and book around it.

sections.heading: Receipts, VAT, permits and what to ask before paying
paragraphs: A few practical questions are worth asking before any money moves, and they take two minutes. The first is whether the quoted rate is per hour or per session, because a 45-minute session quoted at an hourly-sounding figure is a different price. The second is what happens to a cancelled or missed session and how much notice is required. The third is whether the rate is fixed for the year or revised mid-term, which matters over a two-year Diploma more than over a single term.

On tax, the honest position is narrow. This page makes no statement about how UAE VAT treats tuition fees, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation and a tutoring site is not the place to read one. What a family can reasonably ask of any provider is simply whether a quoted figure includes VAT, and to get that answer in writing before paying. A provider who cannot answer that clearly is a provider to be careful with for other reasons too.

On permits, private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists it as private tutor licensing with no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule is published, any page quoting an amount is quoting something unverified.

Finally, two claims to discount when comparing quotes. Regulator approval: KHDA issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises, and a platform without one is not approved by anybody. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE premises, and claims no accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. And review ratings: pages in this search publish self-asserted star ratings, in one case two conflicting figures on the same page, which tells a parent nothing about whether a tutor can teach Higher Level organic chemistry.

sections.heading: What an Al Garhoud parent can verify for nothing
paragraphs: Before spending anything, there are four checks that cost nothing and remove most of the risk from the decision. They are all things a parent can do without knowing any chemistry.

Read the school's inspection report on the regulator's own site. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai and inspects schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. The report tells you how the school's science provision is actually judged, which is useful context for deciding whether the problem you are solving is your child's or the class's. Ask the school for the Diploma chemistry scheme of work at the same time; a tutor working to it is worth more than one working to a textbook.

Use the free trial as an assessment rather than an introduction. Send a photograph of a recent marked chemistry test beforehand and ask the tutor to come with a view. By the end they should be able to name two or three specific loss points: a mechanism answer that did not show electron movement, an equilibrium calculation where the algebra failed rather than the chemistry, a command term answered as describe when it asked for explain. Three statements of that kind mean the diagnosis is real and the specialist band is justified.

Then watch your child for the last ten minutes of the trial. A chemistry student who is being taught well is doing most of the talking and getting stuck in public. If the tutor is explaining and your child is nodding, the lesson is a lecture, and lectures are free. Finally, ask directly what the tutor will not do with the Scientific Investigation. An answer with a clear limit in it is a good sign about everything else, and an offer to look over and improve the write-up is the answer to walk away from.

process.title: Send the marked script and the school's scheme of work
process.description: A photograph of a recent marked chemistry test, the year group, the level and the school. With the scheme of work alongside it, the first lesson diagnoses instead of introducing, and the two-year plan can be shaped around the school's actual sequence.

process.title: Free trial run as a diagnosis
process.description: No payment, and the test is specificity. The tutor should finish able to name two or three loss points: a mechanism without electron movement, an equilibrium calculation where the algebra failed, a command term answered wrongly. General reassurance is a failed trial.

process.title: Agree the phase plan and the total, not just the rate
process.description: Bridging block if needed, weekly intensity through DP1, the investigation block timed to the school's internal deadline, maintenance through DP2 and the run-in. Knowing the shape of the spend in September prevents it accumulating by accident.

process.title: Weekly lessons with a written note each time
process.description: One lesson in the agreed slot, one past-paper question marked against the published mark scheme, and a short note afterwards naming what was missed and what comes next. The note is how progress stays visible without sitting in on lessons.

process.title: Reassess at the mock and adjust the spend
process.description: After mocks the script is reviewed and the remaining plan rewritten around what it showed. If the student needs fewer lessons and more independent past-paper work, or a different specialist for the run-in, that is said plainly rather than left to run.

whyPoints.title: A total, not an hourly rate
whyPoints.description: Diploma chemistry taken seriously runs 60 to 90 tutored hours across two years. Planning the phases in September gives a family a number to decide about, instead of a spend that accumulates one session at a time until it is larger than anyone intended.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published and attributed
whyPoints.description: Three of the six most visible competitor pages in this search publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars. Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider or dataset that published it, so a quote you receive can be measured against the band it belongs to.

whyPoints.title: The travel premium named for what it is
whyPoints.description: In-home rates in Dubai are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 online. Online delivery removes the Creek crossing from the bill, and across a two-year Diploma that difference converts into a meaningful number of extra teaching hours.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before hours
whyPoints.description: The expensive skill in chemistry is reading a mark scheme and naming what is missing. Buying hours from someone who cannot do that means re-teaching content the student already has, which costs the specialist budget anyway and arrives at the paper with the same problem.

whyPoints.title: A defined, limited investigation block
whyPoints.description: Three to five sessions, timed to the school's internal deadline, covering the criteria, the design and feedback on the student's own draft. Not designing it, not writing it, not redrafting it to completion, because the award at risk is the student's.

whyPoints.title: Free trial before anything is paid
whyPoints.description: The judgement about whether a tutor can diagnose is made by watching one lesson, which costs nothing. A family that pays for a term in advance and finds out in week four has lost the term; a free trial converts that risk into an hour.

faqs.question: What does a full two years of IB chemistry tutoring cost for an Al Garhoud family?
faqs.answer: At published Dubai specialist rates of AED 200 to 300 an hour, a planned two-year Diploma chemistry programme of roughly 71 to 81 hours comes to about AED 14,200 to 24,300 in total. That covers a short bridging block before DP1, weekly lessons through DP1, a three-to-five session investigation block, lighter maintenance through DP2 and a six-to-ten week run-in. The figures use the rate band that TutorChase and Bestimate publish rather than any IB Gram price. The point of the breakdown is that DP1, not the final term, dominates the total, which is the opposite of how most families plan it.

faqs.question: How many tutoring hours does a Diploma chemistry grade actually take?
faqs.answer: Between 60 and 90 across the two years for a student taken seriously with weekly support, depending on the starting point and whether the Scientific Investigation needs a dedicated block. Standard Level sits at the lower end, around 50 to 65, because the usual problem is pace rather than depth. Higher Level sits at the upper end because the extensions in organic chemistry, equilibrium and energetics absorb a disproportionate share. A student who does one timed past paper a fortnight independently needs materially fewer tutored hours than one who does none.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to hire a chemistry tutor who comes to our villa in Al Garhoud?
faqs.answer: No, and it is not a service IB Gram offers. Published in-home rates across Dubai run AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's 2026 table showing AED 180 to 350, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor working online. Monthly packages make the gap starker: around AED 799 a month buys eight online sessions while AED 1,599 to 1,799 buys four two-hour in-home sessions. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is an India-only service, and a good part of the premium pays for a car crossing the Creek at 17:00.

faqs.question: Should we spend more in DP1 or save the budget for the final term?
faqs.answer: Spend steadily in DP1. It feels prudent to economise early and buy heavily before the papers, and it is usually false economy, because the gaps left in DP1 are exactly what make the final block long. A student who stayed level with the school's sequence needs sixteen to twenty intensive hours in the run-in; a student who did not can need twice that and still arrive short. The cheapest version of the two-year plan is a low weekly intensity through DP1 that catches misconceptions in the week they form, plus a dense run-in.

faqs.question: Where do Dubai families most often waste money on chemistry tuition?
faqs.answer: Three places. Paying for content coverage the school is already delivering competently, which shows up as a tutor whose lesson plan follows textbook chapter order rather than your child's loss points. Buying intensity instead of diagnosis, since three lessons a week in DP1 achieves less than one lesson plus independent past-paper work. And leaving the Scientific Investigation to chance and then paying to rescue it in the week before the internal deadline, which is both expensive and the moment a family is most likely to be offered help that crosses the academic-honesty line.

faqs.question: Why does organic chemistry absorb so many tutoring hours?
faqs.answer: Because at Higher Level it stops being memorisable. Students learn reactions as a list of facts, and the questions ask them to reason from structure and electron movement to a product they have not met before. Doing fifty mechanism questions without that reasoning reinforces pattern-matching that fails on an unfamiliar substrate. The cheaper route is four or five sessions on electron movement and on what a reagent is actually doing, after which practice becomes useful. Budget roughly a quarter of the two-year total here, in two concentrated phases rather than spread thinly.

faqs.question: Is a budget chemistry tutor at AED 60 an hour ever the right choice?
faqs.answer: For MYP Sciences or an IGCSE chemistry catch-up, often yes. Budget online tutoring in Dubai is advertised from around AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from about AED 33 to 52, and for foundational content that band can be entirely adequate. For Higher Level Diploma chemistry it usually is not, because what it tends to omit is diagnosis. An hour spent re-teaching bonding to a student whose problem is mechanism reasoning is cheap in isolation and expensive in aggregate, and the aggregate is what you pay.

faqs.question: How much does the Scientific Investigation block cost, and what does it include?
faqs.answer: Three to five sessions, which at the published specialist band of AED 200 to 300 an hour is roughly AED 600 to 1,500 as a one-off. It includes each of the four criteria explained with its mark allocation, the research question interrogated until the student can defend it, a challenge to whether the variable control does what the student claims, an explanation of good uncertainty treatment using a different investigation as the example, and written feedback on a draft the student wrote. Per mark it is the best-value purchase across the two years.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help write my daughter's chemistry investigation if we pay more?
faqs.answer: No, at any price. The submission must be the student's own work, and a breach is academic malpractice under IB rules with the consequence falling on her award rather than on the tutor. What a tutor can legitimately do is explain what each criterion rewards, question her research design, challenge her variable control, show what good evaluation looks like on a different investigation, and give written feedback on a draft she has written herself. This search results set includes an operator selling completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price; that is the offer to refuse.

faqs.question: Does a quoted chemistry tutoring rate in Dubai include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider and get the answer in writing before paying. This page makes no statement about how UAE VAT treats tuition fees, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation and a tutoring site is not a source for tax treatment. What is reasonable to expect is a clear answer to a simple question: is the figure quoted inclusive or exclusive. While you are asking, settle two more: whether the rate is per hour or per session, and what notice is required to cancel. A provider who cannot answer those plainly is worth being careful with.

faqs.question: How does the Dubai school fee freeze affect what we should spend on tutoring?
faqs.answer: It makes the budget easier to plan rather than larger. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. With the largest line in the education budget flat, the sensible response is to decide the tutoring total deliberately in September rather than let it accumulate session by session. Tutoring is now the line that moves, which means it is the line worth planning.

faqs.question: Is a group chemistry class in Deira better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes, because the cost is shared. The question is what the hour achieves. A group class works on content coverage and cannot spend twenty minutes on your child's specific problem with equilibrium algebra, which is usually the reason you started looking. It also puts a journey back into an afternoon that was already tight, and the Creek crossing at 17:00 is exactly what you were avoiding. Many Al Garhoud families use a group class or school support for coverage in DP1 and buy one-to-one time for diagnosis and the run-in.

faqs.question: What should I ask a chemistry tutor before paying for a term?
faqs.answer: Not how many sessions they recommend. Ask what the first three sessions will diagnose and how the plan changes depending on what they find. A tutor who answers in specifics, naming the strands they would test and the question types they would use, is worth the specialist band. One who answers with a session count is selling hours. Then ask directly what they will not do with the Scientific Investigation. A clear stated limit is a good signal about everything else, and an offer to look over and improve the write-up is the answer to walk away from.

faqs.question: Do chemistry tutors in Dubai need a permit, and does it cost anything?
faqs.answer: They do, and it is free. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists the route as private tutor licensing, with no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, but no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: How do I judge whether a chemistry tutor is worth the specialist rate?
faqs.answer: Run the free trial as an assessment. Send a photograph of a recent marked test beforehand and ask the tutor to come with a view on it. By the end they should name two or three specific loss points: a mechanism answer that did not show electron movement, an equilibrium calculation where the algebra failed rather than the chemistry, a command term answered as describe when the question asked for explain. Then watch your child for the last ten minutes. If the tutor is explaining and your child is nodding, you are paying for a lecture.

faqs.question: When should chemistry tutoring start if my son begins the Diploma next September?
faqs.answer: In the summer before DP1, with a short bridging block of around six sessions on moles, concentration and stoichiometric reasoning. At published specialist rates that is roughly AED 1,200 to 1,800, and nothing else on a two-year plan has that return, because an insecure mole concept quietly corrupts titration, energetics and equilibrium work for two years afterwards. Students arriving from MYP Sciences usually need the quantitative work; students arriving from a British-curriculum Year 11 more often need experimental design. The diagnosis in the free trial tells you which.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-garhoud.closingHeading: Decide the total in September, not in April
dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-garhoud.closingBody: An IB chemistry tutor in Al Garhoud is a two-year purchase, and the families who spend least are the ones who plan the phases before DP1 starts rather than buying hours as problems appear. Send a photograph of a recent marked script with the school, year group and level, and ask the school for the chemistry scheme of work. The first lesson is free and is used to find the two or three places marks are actually going, which is also the test of whether a tutor is worth the specialist band. Nobody can promise a grade, and the published AED figures on this page belong to the providers that published them, not to us.

They work from where your child is in the year rather than from the front of the syllabus, because in chemistry the calendar decides what is worth teaching almost as much as the diagnosis does.

intro.heading: The Diploma chemistry year, and the four points at which families call
paragraphs: Chemistry requests from Al Habtoor City cluster at four predictable moments. The first is October of the first Diploma year, when a student who was comfortable in MYP or IGCSE science meets mole calculations in volume and discovers that arithmetic they thought was secure is not. The second is February of that year, when bonding and energetics arrive together and a weak foundation stops being survivable. The third is the start of the second year, when the organic mechanisms begin and the investigation deadline appears on the same page of the school calendar. The fourth is the term before the papers, when a mock result makes the gap numerical.

Knowing which of those four you are in matters more than any general description of chemistry tutoring, because the right purchase is different in each. In October the correct intervention is small and cheap: four to six sessions on quantitative chemistry, done properly, and the rest of the year gets easier. In February it is content teaching alongside the school. At the start of the second year it is project management as much as chemistry. In the final term it is paper technique and the elimination of repeated errors, and adding new content actively hurts.

The current chemistry guide organises everything under two ideas, Structure and Reactivity, each with three topics. Structure covers the particulate nature of matter, models of bonding and structure, and the classification of matter. Reactivity covers what drives reactions, how much and how fast and how far, and the mechanisms of chemical change. HL students study the same six with additional material inside each. That matters for revision planning: there is no separate HL block to be left until last, so HL content has to be listed explicitly or it is quietly skipped.

The scientific investigation carries twenty per cent of the final grade under the current guide, and it is the part of the course families most often ask for the wrong help with. A tutor can teach a student how to narrow a research question, how to control variables, how to handle uncertainty and how to write an evaluation that engages with what actually went wrong. A tutor must not write it, draft it, or improve the text into something the student did not produce. One provider in this market advertises completed internal assessments openly; buying that is a malpractice risk that falls on the student.

Al Habtoor City is a vertical neighbourhood of towers and hotels on Sheikh Zayed Road, with the Canal on one side and Al Safa behind it. No school sits inside the development, so Diploma students here commute to Al Barsha, Al Sufouh, Umm Suqeim, Jumeirah or Nad Al Sheba and arrive home in the late afternoon. IB Gram works with these families online, one-to-one, over live video. We do not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. For chemistry the screen is a real advantage, because a mechanism drawn live and a recorded explanation of an equilibrium shift are both better than a half-remembered whiteboard.

sections.heading: The chemistry year, term by term, and what support should be doing in each
paragraphs: A Diploma chemistry course is two years long and the work changes character roughly every term. Treating it as one undifferentiated subject is the reason families sometimes buy the right number of sessions at the wrong time. The first term of Year 12 is foundational and quantitative. The second is where bonding, structure and energetics arrive and where a shaky foundation becomes visible. The third is usually consolidation and the beginning of investigation planning. In Year 13 the organic and mechanistic material lands alongside the investigation deadline, and the final term belongs entirely to papers.

The table below sets out that shape with what a tutor should be doing in each window and what a parent can check without being a chemist. Dates vary by school and should be confirmed against your own school's calendar; the sequence is what is stable. Two things in it are worth flagging. The investigation deadline is set internally by the school and almost always bites earlier than families expect. And the mock series in Year 13 is the diagnostic that should drive the final-term plan, which means the marked mock papers matter more than the mock grade.

Reading the year this way also prices it properly. A family that intervenes in the first term of Year 12 with a short quantitative block is buying four to six sessions. A family that waits until the second term of Year 13 is buying a longer programme to fix the same underlying problem, with less time and more pressure. The arithmetic is uncomfortable but it is the honest version, and it is why the useful question is not how good is the tutor but how early is the start.

Where a student has joined a Dubai school mid-course, which is common in Al Habtoor City given how much of the population arrives mid-phase, the sequence has to be rebuilt from what the previous school covered rather than assumed. That audit takes one session and prevents a term of teaching material the student already has.

sections.heading: Structure and Reactivity: how the current guide is actually organised
paragraphs: The chemistry guide is built around two organising ideas rather than a numbered topic list. Structure deals with what matter is made of and how it is held together: models of the particulate nature of matter, models of bonding and structure, and the classification of matter. Reactivity deals with change: what drives a reaction, how much and how fast and how far it goes, and the mechanisms by which change happens. Six topics in total, with HL material included inside each rather than appended at the end.

That structure is pedagogically tidy and practically demanding, because the dependencies run in both directions. Bonding explains reactivity, and reactivity motivates bonding. A student who has a gap in the structure material will find the reactivity material arbitrary, and a student who memorises reactivity without the structural reasoning will cope until the question changes shape. In marked scripts the two most common deep gaps are an incomplete picture of bonding and an inability to reason about equilibrium position rather than recite the rule.

The HL interleaving deserves specific attention in revision planning. Because there is no separate HL block, HL content tends to be taught at the end of a topic and then never revisited, which is exactly how it ends up under-rehearsed in the final term. A revision plan that lists topics without separating the HL extensions will skip them by default. We build the coverage map with HL material on its own lines for that reason.

The table maps the six topics to what they demand and where students get stuck. Treat the final column as a diagnostic list: a parent who recognises two of those descriptions in their child has identified the next month of work without needing to understand the chemistry.

sections.heading: Where chemistry marks are actually lost
paragraphs: The largest recoverable category in marked chemistry scripts is quantitative method. Not the arithmetic, which calculators handle, but the decision about which method a question needs. A student who can perform a mole calculation when told to perform one, and cannot recognise that a question requires it, has a method-selection problem rather than a knowledge problem. The repair is mixed practice: sets where the student must choose the approach, not apply a given one. It takes a few weeks and the gain is large.

The second is the data booklet. Candidates are given it in the examination and a surprising number of students have never practised navigating it under time pressure. Constants, formulae and reference data sit in a known structure, and a student who is fluent with it saves minutes and avoids recall errors. Treating booklet navigation as an examinable skill in its own right is a small intervention with a direct mark return.

The third is notation, which in chemistry carries marks that look like presentation and are not. State symbols omitted from an equation, charges left off ions, a mechanism arrow starting in the wrong place, an organic structure drawn ambiguously: each of these is marked as wrong rather than untidy. Students find this frustrating and the fix is mechanical, which is good news, because mechanical fixes hold under examination pressure.

The fourth is command-term discipline, shared with every other Diploma science. The verb sets the answer. State wants a fact, explain wants a chain of reasoning, deduce wants a conclusion drawn from given information, and determine wants working followed by a value with units. A capable student who answers at the wrong length loses marks in both directions: content that earns nothing, and time taken from questions that would have.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation and the deadline the school sets
paragraphs: The investigation is the largest block of marks a chemistry student controls directly, assessed against published criteria and marked internally. For most families the binding constraint is not the chemistry but the calendar: the school sets internal deadlines for a proposal, a draft and a final submission, and those dates usually fall in the busiest term of Year 13. Getting them in writing early is worth more than any amount of later rescue work.

The most common fatal flaw is a research question that cannot be answered with the equipment and time available. A question about an effect too small to measure reliably in a school laboratory produces data that supports nothing, and no amount of good writing recovers it. The second is a data set too thin for the analysis the student then attempts. The third is an evaluation that lists apologies rather than identifying which limitation actually mattered and what would be done differently. All three are planning problems, and all three are addressable before any data is collected.

The limits on support are firm and we state them on every page. A tutor may teach how a question is narrowed, how variables are identified and controlled, how uncertainty is estimated and propagated, how an analysis is structured and how an evaluation argues. A tutor may read a draft the student wrote and reply with the questions an examiner would ask. A tutor may not write any part of it, draft a section, rewrite the student's text, or supply data. The practice of selling completed internal assessments exists in this market and the consequences of buying one fall on the student, not the seller.

Practically, we plan the investigation backwards from the school's internal deadline, keep the heavy weeks clear of the mock series where the calendar allows, and set the expectation that the write-up takes longer than the experiment. Students almost always underestimate the analysis stage, and the time pressure at that point is what produces the thin evaluation that costs criterion marks.

sections.heading: Mocks, the May session and the route if the grade is not there
paragraphs: The mock series in Year 13 is the most useful diagnostic in the course and the most commonly wasted one. Families read the grade and file the paper. The paper is the valuable object: a marked script shows whether marks were lost to method selection, to notation, to command terms, to the data booklet or to time, and those five lead to five different final terms. Our first request after any mock is the script rather than the result.

UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session. We deliberately do not publish IB examination or results dates on these pages, because the International Baccalaureate is the authoritative source and its own site or your school's IB coordinator should be the reference. What we do say is that the dates governing a student's term are usually internal rather than external, and that planning around the school's own deadlines produces a calmer year than planning around the board's.

If the grade after the papers is not what a university offer needs, the options are narrower in the Diploma than in a modular system and they are worth understanding before results day rather than after. A retake session exists, an enquiry upon results process exists, and both have deadlines. The school's coordinator is the person who can explain which applies to your child's situation, and the conversation is much easier if it starts before the result arrives. For students holding university offers, the admissions office's own deadlines are the binding constraint.

For families in Al Habtoor City with children in two different schools, which is common here, the mock calendars rarely align. That is worth knowing in advance because it affects which weeks a household can realistically sustain two tutoring schedules. We plan around the busier child's calendar rather than pretending both are flexible.

sections.heading: Chemistry on screen: what the session actually looks like from a tower apartment
paragraphs: Chemistry is the Diploma science that people assume needs a room, and in practice it is the one where the screen helps most. A mechanism drawn live, arrow by arrow, with the student asked to predict the next step, is clearer on a shared whiteboard than on a crowded page. An equilibrium shift explained with a diagram that can be rebuilt three times in two minutes is better than one drawn once. And a recorded session means a student revisiting organic mechanisms in the final term can re-watch the explanation at the moment they need it.

What the household needs is modest. A hard surface, the student's own calculator rather than a phone, the data booklet printed or open on a second device, squared paper for graph work, and headphones so the rest of the apartment is not part of the lesson. The camera is angled at the page rather than the face, because the whole diagnostic value of a chemistry session is in watching the working appear. Ten minutes of setup before the first lesson prevents most of the friction families anticipate.

Timing in Al Habtoor City is set by the school run rather than by preference. Diploma students here leave the towers each morning for schools in Al Barsha, Al Sufouh, Umm Suqeim or Nad Al Sheba, and the afternoon return along or across Sheikh Zayed Road puts most of them home between 15:45 and 16:45. A chemistry session starting at 17:30 or later holds through a term. One starting at 16:30 is rescheduled by the third week, and a rescheduled session in a sequential subject costs more than the hour it lost.

Ramadan reshapes a few weeks each year and Dubai schools adjust their hours. We agree a revised timetable before the month starts, usually fewer and shorter sessions moved into the late morning or the post-Iftar window, and we lighten the work set between them. For a Year 13 student those weeks often sit close to a mock series, which makes planning the shift more useful than improvising through it.
