sections.heading: Schools, the regulator and what an inspection report tells you about science
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes judgements on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. The equivalent bodies elsewhere are ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Knowing the right body tells you where the report lives.

The reports are more useful than their headline letters. A school judged Outstanding overall can still have a science department flagged for attainment or progress in a particular phase, and the published report breaks judgements down by subject and phase. If secondary science is the area identified for improvement, that is a legitimate reason to put support in place before a mock result rather than after one. It is also a fairer basis for a conversation with the school than a parent's impression.

Context on scale: KHDA figures for 2024-25 record 387,441 students across 227 private schools in Dubai offering seventeen curricula, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for about seven per cent of enrolment and UK-curriculum provision the largest share. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK and three IB, creating 16,846 new places. KHDA also confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for 2026-27 under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion.

Alongside the licensed curriculum, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for the two groups strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Those requirements sit on the same timetable as Diploma chemistry, which is part of why a Year 13 week has so little slack in it.

sections.heading: What we do not claim, and what to verify yourself
paragraphs: IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform. We hold no accreditation, approval, licence or partnership from the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education, and no page on this site will suggest otherwise. We operate no office, centre or branch in the UAE. We do not administer examinations, we do not perform Ministry equivalency, and we do not sell home visits anywhere in the Emirates. Each of those sentences exists because a competitor in this market implies the opposite.

Private tutoring itself is regulated and permitted. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and the application runs through its smart app, website and e-services system. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted amount as unverified.

On materials, we reference and link official syllabus, specimen and timetable documents rather than reproducing them, and we do not supply board-owned papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Your child's school has legitimate access through its own subscriptions. On statistics, every figure on this page carries a source and a date, and we publish no success rates, satisfaction scores or star ratings, because we cannot produce the underlying data for any of them and a number without a method is just decoration.

What is worth verifying independently, in every case: the examination session and its dates with the school's IB coordinator and the board's own site; the school's inspection report on the regulator's site rather than from a summary; Ministry equivalency requirements on the Ministry's own channel; and any tutor's permit status directly. We would rather be the page that tells you where to check than the page that asks you to take its word.

process.title: Tell us where in the year you are
process.description: The most useful first message names the year group, the level, the school and the term. Those four facts tell us whether the right purchase is a short quantitative block, weekly topic teaching, investigation coaching or final-term paper work. They also tell us what not to sell you, which is the part most enquiries never get.

process.title: Free trial lesson on real questions
process.description: The first session is free and runs on past-paper questions rather than a conversation about services. The tutor watches the working appear, which is where method-selection problems become visible. You receive a short written note naming what is costing marks and in what order to address it, and the note is yours regardless of what you decide.

process.title: Ask the school for two documents
process.description: The department's scheme of work and the internal investigation deadlines. With the first, a tutor can sequence sessions to reinforce rather than compete with the school. With the second, the project gets planned backwards from a real date. Both are routine requests and both change the quality of the plan more than anything we can do alone.

process.title: Fix a slot after the drive home
process.description: We set one weekly time in Gulf Standard Time, deliberately after the return to the towers. For Al Habtoor City that usually means 17:30 or later. In a sequential subject like chemistry a cancelled session is not a lost hour, it is a lost week, so the slot that survives a bad traffic day is worth more than the slot that looks ideal.

process.title: Re-mark and review at week four
process.description: A second paper is sat and marked at week four and the error tally compared with week one. If the pattern has not shifted, we change the method or the tutor rather than defending either. If the evidence says the plan needs to change for the next term, that is said while there is still a term to change it in.

whyPoints.title: The year is planned around the school's dates, not ours
whyPoints.description: Internal investigation deadlines and the department's scheme of work drive the plan. A tutor teaching energetics while the class is doing organic chemistry is working against the student, and that mismatch is one of the most common reasons families change tutor in this subject.

whyPoints.title: Quantitative method taught as method
whyPoints.description: Each calculation family gets a written approach the student follows until it is automatic, then mixed sets so they have to choose rather than apply. Method selection is the largest recoverable loss in marked chemistry scripts, and it responds to a few weeks of the right practice.

whyPoints.title: A firm line on the investigation
whyPoints.description: We coach the research question, variable control, uncertainty treatment and evaluation argument, and we answer drafts with the questions an examiner would ask. We never write, rewrite or supply work or data. The limit matters in a market where completed internal assessments are openly advertised.

whyPoints.title: Every figure carries a source
whyPoints.description: Where this page names a market rate, a school count or a regulatory rule, it names where the figure came from and when. We publish no success rates or satisfaction scores, because we could not produce the data behind them and a statistic without a method is decoration.

whyPoints.title: Matched on who has taught the course
whyPoints.description: Online matching selects on teaching history rather than on who can reach a tower in the evening peak. For HL Chemistry, and particularly for mechanism-heavy material, that is the difference between a tutor who can explain a step and one who can only name it.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the limits of what we are
whyPoints.description: A tutor-matching platform with no board or regulator approval, no UAE office, and no home-visit service in the Emirates. Where this page names KHDA or MoHRE it is to explain what they do and point you at their own pages, never to borrow their authority.

faqs.question: What should an Al Habtoor City family expect to pay for IB chemistry tuition?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates put a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150-300 an hour, with IB specialists quoted from about AED 200 to 450 or more and one premium provider publishing AED 650. Monthly estimates from the Bestimate Dubai table run about AED 600-1,200 for mid-band weekly support and AED 1,000-2,000 or more in an examination year. In-home visits are quoted at roughly AED 180-500 an hour because the fee carries the journey. Those are market figures with sources attached, not our price list. We quote after the free trial lesson, when we know whether you need four sessions or a term.

faqs.question: Do you send chemistry tutors to homes in Al Habtoor City?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs in India only. Chemistry sessions for families in these towers are delivered one-to-one online over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. For this subject the format is a genuine advantage: mechanisms are drawn live on a shared whiteboard and can be rebuilt as many times as needed, the data booklet sits open beside the question, and every session is recorded so an organic mechanism can be re-watched in the final term. There is also no second car journey on Sheikh Zayed Road at the worst hour of the day.

faqs.question: How is the current chemistry guide organised into Structure and Reactivity?
faqs.answer: Six topics under two organising ideas. Structure covers models of the particulate nature of matter, models of bonding and structure, and the classification of matter. Reactivity covers what drives chemical reactions, how much and how fast and how far they go, and the mechanisms of chemical change. HL students study the same six topics with additional material inside each rather than in a separate block at the end. That interleaving matters for revision: HL content tends to be taught last within a topic and then never revisited, so a plan that does not list it separately will skip it by default.

faqs.question: Why does a strong chemistry student still drop marks across both papers?
faqs.answer: Four things account for most of it. Method selection, where a student can perform a calculation when told to but does not recognise that a question needs it. Data-booklet navigation, which is given in the examination and rarely practised under time. Notation, where a missing state symbol, an omitted charge or a mechanism arrow starting in the wrong place is marked as wrong rather than untidy. And command-term length, where explaining a question that asked for a statement costs time while adding nothing. All four are mechanical, which means they respond quickly to the right practice.

faqs.question: When is the cheapest time to start chemistry support in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: The first term of Year 12. A short block of four to six sessions on quantitative method at that point prevents the compounding problem that otherwise surfaces in February, and it costs a fraction of what the same repair costs in Year 13. The next best moment is the summer before the course starts, bridging from MYP or IGCSE with work on ratio, proportion, standard form and unit conversion. The most common actual start is after the first serious internal assessment, which is still early enough. Starting in the final term is possible, but the work changes to paper technique and error elimination rather than content.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the chemistry investigation an Al Habtoor City student is writing?
faqs.answer: Yes, within limits we state plainly. A tutor can teach your child how to narrow a research question until it is measurable with school equipment, how to identify and control variables, how to estimate and propagate uncertainty, how to structure an analysis, and how an evaluation identifies which limitation actually mattered. A tutor can read a draft your child wrote and reply with the questions an examiner would ask. A tutor cannot write it, draft a section, rewrite the text or provide data. Completed internal assessments are sold in this market; buying one is an academic-malpractice risk that falls on your child.

faqs.question: How much extra does HL Chemistry demand compared with SL?
faqs.answer: The HL course covers the same six topics with additional material inside each, so the difference is depth, volume and rehearsal time rather than a different syllabus. In marked work the HL extensions are where most HL marks go missing, and the reason is usually scheduling rather than difficulty: HL material is taught at the end of a topic and the class moves on before it is practised. Mechanism-heavy HL content suffers most from this. A revision plan that lists HL items on their own lines, and revisits them deliberately, removes most of the problem.

faqs.question: Which subjects do Dubai students usually take alongside HL Chemistry?
faqs.answer: Biology is the standard pairing for medicine applications, and Physics or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches for engineering and the physical sciences. The practical issue with any science pairing is that two scientific investigations run in the same term, each with its own internal deadlines, and students consistently underestimate the write-up stage of both. Coordinating those two calendars saves more stress than extra content teaching does. Check the published entry requirements for the universities your child is aiming at, since medical and engineering courses frequently specify which subjects must be at higher level.

faqs.question: What is the data booklet and why does it matter so much in sessions?
faqs.answer: It is the reference document candidates are given in the chemistry examination, containing constants, formulae and reference data in a fixed structure. Students who have not practised using it lose time hunting and sometimes fall back on half-remembered values instead. We keep it open in every session so navigation becomes automatic, because fluency with it is a mark-earning skill in its own right rather than a convenience. It also changes how revision should work: there is no value in memorising what the booklet supplies, and real value in knowing exactly where each thing sits.

faqs.question: Our child joined a Dubai school mid-course. How do you handle the gaps?
faqs.answer: With an audit rather than an assumption. In the first session we establish what the previous school actually covered, topic by topic and including HL extensions, and compare it with the current department's scheme of work. That usually reveals a short list of genuine gaps rather than the broad weakness families fear, and it prevents a term spent teaching material the student already has. Al Habtoor City has a high proportion of families who arrived mid-phase, so this is routine work here. The audit takes one session and is the best-value hour in the whole arrangement.

faqs.question: How do you plan around the school's internal investigation deadlines?
faqs.answer: Backwards from the date, which means we ask for it in writing at the start. Schools set internal deadlines for a proposal, a draft and a final submission, and these usually fall in the busiest term of Year 13, often near the mock series. We map the heavy weeks away from mocks where the calendar allows, set the expectation that analysis takes longer than data collection, and build the research question early enough that a flawed one can be replaced rather than rescued. The internal dates govern a student's term far more than any external window does.

faqs.question: Can chemistry sessions be rescheduled around Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we agree the change before the month starts rather than improvising through it. Dubai schools adjust their hours during Ramadan, and most families want fewer, shorter sessions rather than the same timetable pushed later. Late-morning slots suit students whose school day has been compressed; the post-Iftar window suits households that prefer the evening. We also lighten the work set between sessions. For a Year 13 student these weeks often sit close to a mock series, which is exactly why planning the shift in advance is worth the conversation.

faqs.question: What does a marked mock paper tell you that the mock grade does not?
faqs.answer: Where the marks went, which decides the entire final term. A script shows whether losses sit in method selection, in notation, in command-term length, in data-booklet use or simply in running out of time, and those five point to five different plans. The grade tells you none of that. Our first request after any mock is the script rather than the result, and we categorise every lost mark into a tally. Across two or three papers the tally stops being anecdotal and starts being a work plan, which is what makes it worth the effort.

faqs.question: What if we need an HL Chemistry tutor at a time nobody is free?
faqs.answer: We tell you instead of filling the slot. SL and mainstream HL matching is usually quick. Narrower requests, such as HL mechanism work or a specific Reactivity extension, draw on a smaller group, and the honest options are a different time, a short wait for the right person, or a script-marking clinic in the meantime so the weeks are not wasted. We also tell you where a tutor is based before you book. Placing a generalist on specialist HL material a term before the papers is how families end up paying to be told what they already knew.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-habtoor-c.closingHeading: Tell us the term, and we will tell you what to buy
dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-habtoor-c.closingBody: Chemistry support is priced by timing more than by anything else. Four sessions on calculation method in the first term of Year 12 do what a whole programme cannot do in the final term of Year 13, and knowing which of those situations you are in is the useful first step. Send us the year group, the level, the school and where the class has reached, and we will say honestly whether the answer is a short block, weekly teaching, investigation coaching or paper technique. The trial lesson is free and runs on real past-paper questions. Everything is delivered one-to-one, online, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, at a time that works after the drive back into Al Habtoor City.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-jaddaf.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach DP Chemistry at Higher and Standard Level, including the organic mechanisms and energetics work that decides most grade movements. Profiles name the topics each has taught most and their experience with the internally assessed investigation, so a match can be judged before a single session is paid for.

intro.heading: Price the year, not the hour
paragraphs: Hourly rates are how the Dubai tutoring market talks about money and they are almost useless for planning. A quote of AED 220 an hour means nothing until you know whether that is thirty hours or ninety, whether anything gets marked between sessions, and whether the two months that actually decide the Chemistry grade are inside the arrangement or outside it. Al Jaddaf families routinely agree an hourly rate and then discover the annual figure by accident, three invoices in.

So this page works in months and terms. The monthly packages currently circulating in the Dubai market start around AED 799 for eight online sessions, and run to AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. The Bestimate rate survey for Dubai estimates monthly spend on weekly one-hour sessions at AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are market numbers from named sources, not an IB Gram price list.

Chemistry has a particular cost shape that physics and maths do not share, and it is worth understanding before you commit a term. Most of the grade movement in DP Chemistry happens in two places: organic chemistry, which arrives late and compounds, and the internally assessed investigation, which carries 20 per cent and is marked out of 24. A family that spends evenly across the year usually underspends on both and overspends on stoichiometry, which the student had already understood by October.

Al Jaddaf itself shapes the logistics rather than the teaching. The neighbourhood sits on the creek between Dubai Healthcare City and Ras Al Khor, with Culture Village to the north and Festival City across the water. Families here draw from a scatter of campuses rather than one, so there is no single school bell that sets the evening schedule. What there is, consistently, is a narrow window between arriving home and losing the student's concentration, and the sessions that survive a whole term are the ones booked inside it.

Below: the annual arithmetic, what organic chemistry costs to fix and why waiting makes it dearer, the investigation boundaries under IB academic-honesty rules, how group and centre provision compares on price, and the order to spend in if the budget is fixed. There is also the Ministry of Education equivalency rule for the British track, stated with the correct subject count, because a provider ranking well for these queries currently publishes the wrong one and families act on it. None of it assumes a particular budget. Several of the most useful moves in a Chemistry year cost nothing at all: reading the school's own inspection report, asking the subject teacher which topics remain unscheduled, and having a marked script read before any hours are agreed. Teaching is delivered one to one over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-jaddaf.programmesIntro: Chemistry shows up at three stages of an IB school career in Dubai, and the cost of support at each stage is wildly different. What follows is what each stage demands and what money buys there.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Chemistry
programmes.description: Two years at Higher or Standard Level, built around structure and reactivity: particulate models, bonding, classification of matter, energetics, chemical kinetics, equilibrium, acids and bases, redox, and organic chemistry. Assessment runs across Paper 1, split into multiple choice and a data-based section, Paper 2 of extended response, and the scientific investigation common to all DP sciences. HL content sits inside each topic rather than as a separate block.
programmes.countryNote: The practical issue for an Al Jaddaf family is sequencing. Organic chemistry and the harder equilibrium work land in DP Year 2 at most schools near the creek, often in the same term as the investigation deadline and the mock window. That collision is why Chemistry tutoring demand in this corridor spikes in the autumn of Year 13, and why the tutors who can teach it are already booked by then.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Chemistry sits within MYP Sciences, assessed against four criteria each marked out of eight: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Mole calculations, balancing and the beginnings of bonding appear here, along with the first formal expectation that a student designs a fair test and evaluates its reliability.
programmes.countryNote: MYP Chemistry support is the cheapest money an Al Jaddaf family will ever spend on this subject, and the least often spent. A student who leaves MYP uncertain about moles carries that uncertainty into every DP calculation, where it is no longer a topic but a permanent tax on every paper. Four sessions on mole arithmetic in Year 10 replaces a term of DP rescue work at double the rate.

programmes.name: IGCSE Chemistry as the DP entry route
programmes.description: Many creek-side students reach DP Chemistry from Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1. Both cover the particulate model, bonding, stoichiometry, acids and bases, electrolysis, rates and basic organic families. Neither asks for the mechanistic reasoning, the energy-cycle construction or the quantitative equilibrium treatment that the Diploma expects from the first term.
programmes.countryNote: An A* at 0620 is routinely read as a signal that no DP support is needed, and it is the wrong signal. IGCSE rewards recall and single-step calculation; DP Chemistry rewards explanation of why a reaction proceeds. Six sessions in the summer between Year 11 and Year 12 on bonding explanations and energy cycles costs a fraction of the term of remedial work that otherwise starts in November.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-jaddaf.subjectsIntro: DP Chemistry is one course, but tutoring hours get allocated by topic, and the price of a fix varies enormously between them. Here is what each area assesses and what it costs to repair.

subjects.name: Stoichiometric relationships
subjects.description: Moles, concentration, limiting reagents, percentage yield and gas calculations. Cheap to fix and usually fixed too late. The classic loss is a correct method applied to an unbalanced equation, which costs every subsequent mark in the question even when the arithmetic is flawless.

subjects.name: Atomic structure and periodicity
subjects.description: Electron configurations, ionisation energy trends and periodic patterns, with HL extending into successive ionisation energies and transition-metal behaviour. Trend questions ask for explanation, not description; candidates who state that ionisation energy increases across a period without naming nuclear charge and shielding score half.

subjects.name: Bonding and structure
subjects.description: Ionic, covalent and metallic bonding, intermolecular forces, shapes of molecules and hybridisation at HL. Marks drain away on boiling-point comparisons where a student names hydrogen bonding but never says between which molecules, which is the part the mark scheme is actually looking for.

subjects.name: Energetics and thermochemistry
subjects.description: Enthalpy changes, calorimetry, Hess cycles and, at HL, Born-Haber and entropy with Gibbs free energy. Sign errors dominate. A student who builds a correct cycle and then adds where they should subtract loses the whole question, and no amount of content revision prevents it without drilled practice.

subjects.name: Chemical kinetics
subjects.description: Rate measurement, collision theory and activation energy, with HL adding rate laws, orders of reaction and the Arrhenius treatment. Order-determination questions are reliably answerable once a student stops reading a table left to right and starts holding every variable but one constant.

subjects.name: Equilibrium
subjects.description: Dynamic equilibrium, Le Chatelier reasoning, and quantitative equilibrium constants at HL. The expensive error is explaining a shift by saying the equilibrium moves to oppose the change without ever naming which side and which species, which is the marked content.

subjects.name: Acids, bases and redox
subjects.description: pH, strong and weak behaviour, titration curves, buffers at HL, oxidation states, half-equations and electrochemical cells. Titration-curve questions carry a lot of marks for relatively little content, which makes them unusually good value for a short tutoring block.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry
subjects.description: Functional groups, reaction pathways, mechanisms, isomerism and, at HL, nucleophilic substitution routes, stereochemistry and synthetic sequences. This is the topic that consumes tutoring budgets, because it compounds: a student who missed the first mechanism cannot reason about the fourth.

subjects.name: Measurement, analysis and uncertainty
subjects.description: Percentage uncertainty, significant figures, spectroscopic interpretation and graphical analysis. Assessed in the data-based section of Paper 1 and in the investigation, and almost never taught as a distinct skill in a crowded school scheme of work.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: The internally assessed report, 20 per cent of the grade at both levels, marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The costliest error is choosing a reaction whose rate cannot be measured reliably with school apparatus, which no later editing repairs.

sections.heading: Organic chemistry is where a Chemistry budget disappears
paragraphs: Every DP Chemistry topic can be fixed. Organic chemistry is the one that gets dearer the longer it waits, and that single property explains most of the money Al Jaddaf families lose on this subject. The reason is structural rather than mysterious: organic chemistry is cumulative in a way that energetics is not. A student can miss Hess cycles entirely, learn them in a fortnight, and be fine. A student who never understood why a nucleophile attacks a particular carbon cannot reason about elimination, cannot predict a product, and cannot follow a synthetic route, because each of those depends on the one before.

Schools in this corridor generally teach organic late. At most campuses near the creek it arrives in DP Year 2, frequently in the same term as the investigation deadline and the mock window. By the time a mock grade reveals the problem, the student has perhaps twelve weeks, the topic has four or five layers of dependency, and the tutors who teach it well are already holding full evening schedules. That is why a January enquiry costs more in total than an October one at the same hourly rate.

The diagnosis is easy to make early and nearly impossible to make from a conversation. Ask the student to predict the product of a reaction they have not seen and explain why. A student who can name the mechanism but not say which atom is electron-deficient has a gap that will widen with every subsequent lesson. That is a six to eight session block in DP Year 1, or a term of expensive remedial work in Year 13, and it is the same gap either way.

There is a related trap on the spending side. Organic chemistry rewards practice with a pen more than explanation, so sessions that consist entirely of a tutor talking through mechanisms are poor value however good the talking is. The useful shape is short explanation, then the student drawing mechanisms while the tutor watches and interrupts. Ask any prospective tutor what proportion of a session the student spends writing. A tutor who has taught this topic will have a number ready.

sections.heading: HL or SL Chemistry, and what the wrong choice costs
paragraphs: The HL and SL decision is made in the first weeks of the Diploma and it is the largest single determinant of what Chemistry will cost a family over two years. HL carries additional content inside every topic rather than as a separate bolt-on, which means the extra load is distributed and therefore easy to underestimate when the choice is made. A student who takes HL because a university prospectus mentioned it, without having tested whether they can hold quantitative equilibrium and mechanistic reasoning together, may spend two years buying support for a decision made in a fortnight.

The reverse error is real too and less discussed. A student who drops to SL to protect their overall points, and later finds that a competitive course expects HL Chemistry, has closed a door that tutoring cannot reopen. This is where a tutor is genuinely useful before any teaching starts: an experienced DP Chemistry teacher can look at a student's MYP or IGCSE work and say honestly whether HL is a stretch or a wall. That conversation costs one session.

What the table below sets out is the comparison that matters for planning, rather than a list of topic headings. Both levels sit the same style of paper and both carry the investigation at 20 per cent, which surprises families who assume the internal assessment is lighter at Standard Level. It is not. The difference is in the depth of the content each paper draws on and in the reasoning the extended responses expect.

Nothing on this page should be read as a claim that tutoring is required for a particular level, a university course or Ministry of Education equivalency. It is not. Plenty of students take HL Chemistry with no outside support at all. The argument here is narrower: if you are going to spend, the level decision changes what the spend should be aimed at, and making it deliberately is free.

sections.heading: The Chemistry investigation: 24 marks, and a hard limit on help
paragraphs: A fifth of the DP Chemistry grade comes from the scientific investigation, marked out of 24 against research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. For a family budgeting a Chemistry year it is the best-value block available, because it happens in ordinary weeks, on the student's own timetable, and the marks are no less real than exam marks. It is also the block most often postponed until the deadline is close enough to make calm work impossible.

Chemistry investigations fail at the design stage more than physics ones do, because reactions are messier than motion. A rate experiment whose temperature drifts, a titration with too few repeats, a reaction monitored by eye rather than by a measurable quantity: each of these produces data that cannot support a conclusion, and no amount of careful writing afterwards fixes it. A tutor who reads the proposal in week one is worth several who read the draft in week ten, and costs the same per hour.

The boundary on a tutor's involvement is firm and non-negotiable. Under IB academic-honesty rules the investigation must be the student's own work. A tutor may teach uncertainty propagation, ask whether a variable is genuinely controlled, explain what the evaluation criterion rewards, and give written feedback on a draft the student has produced. A tutor may not write any section, supply or adjust data, or edit the report into its final state. Providers in this market sell completed internal assessments; that is a malpractice trigger for the student, not a shortcut.

Say that boundary out loud to any tutor before hiring them, and listen carefully to the reply. A tutor who explains where the line sits and how they work inside it has supervised real Diploma students. A tutor who promises a polished report has told you something important about what they are selling, and the risk falls entirely on your child.

sections.heading: Group classes and centres compared on cost per useful hour
paragraphs: Tuition centres in Dubai price group Chemistry classes well below any one-to-one rate, and for some students that is the correct purchase. The question is not whether group teaching is cheaper per hour, because it plainly is. The question is cost per useful hour, and that depends almost entirely on whether the student's problem is shared with the rest of the group.

Group provision works when the gap is content coverage. A class of eight students who all need equilibrium taught properly can be taught equilibrium properly, and each family pays a fraction of a private rate. Group provision fails when the gap is individual: a student whose Hess cycles always carry a sign error, or who cannot explain which atom a nucleophile attacks, needs somebody watching them write. In a group of eight, nobody is watching any individual write for more than a couple of minutes an hour, so a two-hour class may deliver fifteen useful minutes at a very attractive hourly rate.

The in-home option occupies a different position again, and it is the one Al Jaddaf families are most often quoted without an alternative. Bestimate records in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. Set against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor working online, the difference is travel. A tutor reaching the creek for 17:00 spends roughly three hours of their day on one paid hour, and the rate carries that. It also narrows your choice to whoever will make the journey.

To be unambiguous about what is on offer here: IB Gram does not provide home visits in the UAE. Teaching for UAE families runs one to one over live video, screen-shared, with tutor and student annotating the same mechanism or the same titration curve. In-home visiting is a service we operate only in India. The AED 180 to 500 band above is the market's published rate, quoted for comparison rather than offered.

sections.heading: Ramadan, holidays and the cost of a lost term
paragraphs: The UAE academic calendar interacts with Chemistry revision in ways that are easy to plan around and expensive to ignore. Ramadan brings shortened school days and a very different household rhythm, and a weekly session fixed at 17:00 will not survive it. Families who plan for that keep continuity; families who do not usually lose four to six weeks, and in a cumulative subject like organic chemistry those weeks compound rather than simply disappear.

The workable adjustment is to move rather than pause. Sessions shifted to after iftar, or consolidated into weekend blocks, keep the thread intact. Where a student is fasting, shorter and more frequent is better than long and heavy, because concentration rather than willingness is the constraint. A tutor who has taught through Ramadan in the Gulf will propose this without being asked; one who has not will keep the 17:00 slot and then wonder why attendance collapsed.

The long summer break is the other calendar feature with a direct cost consequence, and for Chemistry it cuts both ways. Students travelling for six or eight weeks lose material, and the transition points suffer most: the gap between IGCSE and DP Year 1, and the gap between DP Year 1 and Year 2. Online delivery means a family in Europe or South Asia over the summer can keep a weekly session running in a different time zone, which turns the most dangerous break in the calendar into the cheapest teaching weeks of the year.

One honest note about exam timing, because this market is full of confidently wrong dates. IB Diploma candidates in the UAE sit the May session, with November available as an alternative. Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June and November series; the February and March series is offered to India only, so any Dubai provider quoting February dates is working from the wrong country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May or June and in November. We do not publish specific IB session or results dates here, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and an unverified date on a parent-facing page is worse than no date at all.

sections.heading: Chemistry, medicine and Ministry of Education equivalency
paragraphs: A sizeable share of the DP Chemistry enquiries from this corridor come from families whose child is aiming at medicine or another competitive science route, and the Chemistry grade carries real weight there. What matters for planning is that university requirements are published by the universities themselves and vary considerably, so the only reliable source is the named course's own entry page. Higher Level Chemistry is commonly expected for medicine and for chemistry degrees; that is a pattern worth knowing, not a rule to assume.

Separately from university admission sits Ministry of Education equivalency, which is the process by which a UAE certificate equivalency is issued for an international qualification. For the British track the requirements are published and specific: a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor in this market publishes a six-subject figure, which is wrong.

For the American track, English proficiency is met by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB there is no points threshold published in the source we read, and we will not invent one. Any IB equivalency figure should be confirmed on moe.gov.ae or with the relevant attestation authority directly.

IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency or attestation for any family, and nothing about tutoring is required for it. The process belongs to the Ministry and to the attestation authority, and the official channel is the only one that can give you a binding answer about your child's documents. What a tutor can do is make sure the grades the process looks at are the best the student can produce.

sections.heading: Spending in the right order when the budget is fixed
paragraphs: Most families have a number in mind rather than an open budget, and the order of spending decides how much of the grade that number buys. The order that works for DP Chemistry is counter-intuitive, because it puts the cheapest and calmest work first and leaves the most expensive weeks for the thing that genuinely needs them.

First purchase: a diagnosis. Send a marked Chemistry paper and have a tutor read it before buying any hours. Patterns show up immediately and they are specific. Correct method on an unbalanced equation is one problem. Hess cycles with inverted signs is another. Bonding explanations that name hydrogen bonding without naming the molecules is a third. Each has a different fix of a different length, and guessing between them is what turns a four-session need into a twelve-session invoice.

Second purchase: investigation design, early in DP Year 1. Twenty per cent of the grade, in calm weeks, at the ordinary hourly rate. Third purchase: organic chemistry, as soon as the school starts it and ideally a little before. This is the block that becomes dearer with every week of delay, and the only one where early spending reliably reduces total spending. Fourth purchase: timed Paper 2 practice with every script marked, booked in the autumn even though it is used in the spring, because availability rather than price is the binding constraint by then.

What this leaves out matters as much as what it includes. General revision across the whole syllabus is the most commonly bought and least effective Chemistry purchase in this market. It feels thorough and it is mostly re-covering what the student already knows, at AED 200 an hour or more. If a tutor proposes it before reading a marked script, that is useful information about the tutor.

faqs.question: What does a full year of IB Chemistry tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: At one session a week across a school year, budget online tutoring totals roughly AED 1,400 to 2,600 using Tutopiya's AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik's AED 45 to 65 published rates. A qualified subject tutor at Unitors' published AED 150 to 200 and upward lands between AED 5,400 and 10,800. Specialist IB rates of AED 200 to 450, including TutorChase at AED 270, run from AED 7,200 upward. The monthly packages circulating locally give the clearest comparison: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four in-home visits.

faqs.question: Why do people say organic chemistry is the expensive topic?
faqs.answer: Because it compounds. A student who misses Hess cycles can learn them in a fortnight and be fine, since nothing later depends on them. A student who never understood why a nucleophile attacks a particular carbon cannot then reason about elimination, predict a product or follow a synthetic route, because each step rests on the one before. Most schools near the creek teach organic in DP Year 2, so the problem surfaces with twelve weeks left and four layers of dependency. The same gap costs six to eight sessions in Year 1 and a whole term in Year 13.

faqs.question: Should an Al Jaddaf family take the AED 799 monthly package or pay per session?
faqs.answer: It is, once the need is established and the tutor is proven, and poor value before either. AED 799 a month for eight online sessions works out near AED 100 a session, well below the AED 150 to 300 a qualified subject tutor normally commands, and that discount is bought with commitment. The sensible order is a free trial lesson, then a short block with a stated end point and marked evidence, then a package if the evidence supports it. Committing to a term before anyone has seen the student work is how tutoring money gets stranded.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my daughter needs HL or SL Chemistry?
faqs.answer: Ask an experienced DP Chemistry teacher to look at her actual work rather than her grades. HL adds content inside every topic rather than as a separate block, so the extra load is spread out and easy to underestimate when the choice is made in the first weeks. The practical test is whether she can hold quantitative reasoning and mechanistic reasoning together under time pressure. Also check the entry requirements of the specific courses she is considering, since Higher Level Chemistry is commonly expected for medicine and chemistry degrees but requirements are set by each university.

faqs.question: Exactly what may a paid tutor touch on the Chemistry investigation report?
faqs.answer: Yes, inside clear limits. A tutor may help narrow a research question until the measurement is reliable, teach uncertainty propagation, question whether a variable is genuinely controlled, explain what the evaluation criterion rewards, and give written feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write any section, supply or alter data, or edit the report into final form. The investigation is 20 per cent of the grade at both levels, marked out of 24, and it must be the student's own work. Any provider offering a finished report is offering a malpractice finding.

faqs.question: Are group Chemistry classes at a centre worth the saving?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether the problem is shared. Group teaching works well for content coverage: eight students who all need equilibrium taught properly can be taught it properly at a fraction of a private rate. It works badly for individual technique faults. A student whose Hess cycles always carry a sign error needs somebody watching them write, and in a class of eight nobody watches any individual write for more than a couple of minutes an hour. A cheap two-hour class can deliver fifteen useful minutes, which is not a saving.

faqs.question: Will a weekly Chemistry slot survive the shortened Ramadan school day?
faqs.answer: Move them rather than pause them. A slot fixed at 17:00 will not survive shortened school days and a changed household rhythm, and families who simply suspend usually lose four to six weeks. In a cumulative subject those weeks compound. Sessions shifted to after iftar, or consolidated into weekend blocks, keep the thread intact. For a fasting student, shorter and more frequent beats long and heavy, because concentration rather than willingness is the limit. A tutor who has taught through Ramadan in the Gulf will suggest this without being asked.

faqs.question: Does my son need Higher Level Chemistry for medicine?
faqs.answer: Commonly, yes, but the requirement belongs to each university rather than to a general rule, so the only reliable source is the entry page of the specific course. Higher Level Chemistry is widely expected for medicine and for chemistry degrees, and dropping to Standard Level to protect overall points can close doors that cannot be reopened later. Equally, nothing about tutoring is required for admission anywhere; plenty of students take HL Chemistry with no outside support. Check the named courses first, then decide on level, then decide whether support is needed.

faqs.question: What are the UAE equivalency rules for an IGCSE student?
faqs.answer: For the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking provider in this market states six subjects, which is wrong. For the IB no points threshold appears in the source we read, so confirm any IB figure on moe.gov.ae. IB Gram does not perform or guarantee equivalency; the authority's own channel is the only binding one.

faqs.question: Can online teaching work for a subject with so much practical work?
faqs.answer: For the assessed parts of DP Chemistry, yes. Nothing in Paper 1, Paper 2 or the investigation report requires the tutor to be physically present. Screen-sharing a mechanism, annotating a titration curve together and working through percentage uncertainty line by line is often clearer on a shared screen than across a table. Practical work itself happens at school, where the apparatus and the technician are. What online delivery changes is choice: an Al Jaddaf family can work with a tutor who teaches HL organic well rather than one who happens to drive past the creek.

faqs.question: Which Chemistry topics give the best return for a short block?
faqs.answer: Titration curves and acid-base reasoning carry a lot of marks for relatively little content, which makes them unusually efficient for a four to six session block. Energetics sign discipline is similar: the content is small, the losses are large and drilled practice fixes it. Order-of-reaction determination responds quickly once a student learns to hold every variable but one constant. Organic mechanisms are the opposite case: high value but slow, and best started early rather than compressed. General revision across the whole syllabus is the least efficient purchase available.

faqs.question: My child understands chemistry but writes short answers. What is that?
faqs.answer: That is a command-term problem and it is the cheapest fix in the subject. Describe, explain, deduce, state and justify each ask for a different amount of writing, and a candidate who writes one line for a four-mark explain question loses marks they fully understood. It is invisible in conversation and obvious on a marked script, which is exactly why a tutoring arrangement without marked papers is a weak purchase. Four sessions spent matching answer length to mark allocation, with every attempt marked, usually moves more marks than a term of content revision.

faqs.question: When should we book if exams are the target?
faqs.answer: Earlier than feels necessary, because what runs out is availability rather than affordability. The hourly rate does not rise as the exam series approaches, but the DP Chemistry tutors who teach HL organic well have full evening schedules in Gulf Standard Time by then, and that window is the one every UAE family wants. A parent who fixes a weekly slot in the autumn pays the same as one who fixes it in the spring and chooses from a much better set. If a final-stretch block is coming, reserve it while there is still a choice.

faqs.question: What if you have no Chemistry specialist free for our slot?
faqs.answer: Then we say so. Most providers in this market disclose no coverage limit at all, and the usual quiet substitute is a general science tutor at a specialist rate, which costs a family a term as well as the fees. When no suitable DP Chemistry tutor has a slot in the Gulf evening window, we will normally offer a different time, a tutor in another time zone whose availability overlaps the UAE evening, or a start a fortnight or so out. Occasionally the honest answer is that we cannot cover it this term.

intro.heading: Three failure points carry most of the lost marks
paragraphs: Diploma chemistry has an unusual property: a very large share of its lost marks concentrate in a small number of places, and the places are the same from student to student. The first is the mole and everything downstream of it. The second is organic chemistry, specifically mechanisms and the precision of naming. The third is energetics and thermodynamics, where sign conventions and the direction of a definition decide whether an otherwise correct calculation scores.

The mole is the gatekeeper because so much of the subject chains from it. A question gives a mass, asks for a concentration after a reaction, and the route runs mass to moles, moles through a balanced equation, moles to concentration. Every step depends on the one before, and the commonest single destroyer of a chemistry question is an unbalanced equation feeding the second step. The student does three correct calculations on the wrong coefficients and loses the lot.

Organic chemistry fails differently. The content is learnable and the assessment is precise. A mechanism drawn with an arrow starting in the wrong place, or without the curly arrow showing where the electron pair comes from, loses marks the student conceptually understood. Naming is marked exactly: a locant in the wrong position or a missing stereochemical descriptor costs the mark. Students treat organic as memorisation and it is closer to a notation discipline.

Energetics is the third and it is almost entirely about conventions. An enthalpy change is defined in a direction; bond enthalpies are for breaking; a Hess cycle gives the right magnitude and the wrong sign if the arrows are read backwards. Entropy and Gibbs energy at Higher Level add their own sign traps. A student who has never been made to state the convention explicitly before calculating will keep making the same error because nothing in their method catches it.

Underneath all three sits the data booklet, which every IB chemistry examination supplies along with the periodic table. That changes what revision should be: not memorising constants and values, but knowing what is provided, where, and how to use it quickly. Students who have never worked through the booklet deliberately lose time hunting and sometimes memorise things they are given.

And then the internally assessed investigation, which carries a published share of the grade. In chemistry the viability question is sharper than in most sciences, because many interesting questions cannot be answered safely or with school apparatus, and a question whose measurement is unreliable caps the analysis regardless of care. The design stage is where that grade is largely decided. A family can see most of this for themselves before paying anybody. Take the last marked paper and count the questions where a balanced equation was needed, where a mechanism was drawn, and where a sign was involved. The distribution of the lost marks across those three usually names the problem without a tutor in the room, and it tells you which kind of help to buy.

sections.heading: The mole, and why one unbalanced equation costs a whole question
paragraphs: Quantitative chemistry is built as a chain. A typical question supplies a mass or a volume and a concentration, and asks for something several steps away: a yield, a final concentration, a limiting reagent, an empirical formula. The route passes through moles, and from moles it passes through the balanced equation's coefficients. Every subsequent step inherits whatever happened at that point.

That structure has a brutal consequence. A student who balances the equation incorrectly, or does not balance it at all because the question gave them something that looked balanced, proceeds to do two or three arithmetically perfect calculations on the wrong ratio. The final answer is wrong, the method marks for the later steps may survive depending on the scheme, and a question the student fully understood produces a fraction of its marks.

The repair is procedural rather than conceptual, which is why it works quickly. Balance the equation and check it, atoms and charge, before writing any numbers. Write the mole calculation for the given quantity on its own line. Apply the ratio explicitly, stating which species you are converting between. Then convert to the quantity asked for. Four lines where a confident student writes one, and each line is a place the mark scheme can award credit.

The same discipline fixes a cluster of related losses. Limiting reagent questions are lost by students who calculate moles of both reactants and then forget to divide by the coefficients before comparing. Percentage yield questions are lost by comparing the wrong pair of quantities. Empirical formula questions are lost at the final simplification. In every case the error is a missing explicit step rather than a missing understanding, and making the steps visible catches it.

Molar mass computed from the wrong formula
Write the formula out before summing

sections.heading: Organic chemistry is a notation discipline
paragraphs: Students treat organic chemistry as the memorisation part of the course and then lose marks for reasons that have nothing to do with memory. Mechanisms are marked on what is drawn: where each curly arrow starts, whether it originates from a bond or a lone pair, where it points, and whether intermediates carry the correct charges. A student who can describe nucleophilic substitution fluently in words and draws the arrow from the wrong place does not get the mark.

The arrow conventions are short enough to list and are rarely taught as conventions. An arrow represents the movement of an electron pair. It starts at the electron pair, which means at a lone pair or at the centre of a bond, never at an atom as such. It ends where the pair goes, at an atom or at a position between atoms where a bond is forming. Charges on intermediates have to be shown. Once a student has drawn eight or ten mechanisms marked strictly on those rules, the notation becomes automatic.

Naming is the other half and is marked exactly. The locant has to be the lowest possible set, the functional group priority decides the suffix, substituents are alphabetical, and where stereochemistry matters the descriptor is required. These are rules rather than judgements, which makes naming unusually responsive to drilling: twenty compounds named and corrected in a session produces a reliable improvement, and the gain shows up across every organic question.

Isomerism sits alongside and causes a specific confusion. Structural isomers, stereoisomers, cis and trans arrangements and optical activity each have precise conditions, and students who learned them as a list of examples rather than as criteria cannot classify an unfamiliar compound. Teaching the criteria, then testing on unfamiliar structures, is the difference between recognising examples and answering the question.

sections.heading: Energetics: conventions before calculation
paragraphs: Energetics questions are lost on signs far more often than on arithmetic, and the cause is consistent: the convention is left implicit. An enthalpy change is defined for a specified direction and for specified states. Bond enthalpies refer to breaking bonds, so forming bonds releases that energy and the sign flips. A Hess cycle read in the wrong direction produces the right magnitude with the wrong sign, which the mark scheme treats as wrong.

The repair is to state the convention on the page before calculating. Writing out the definition being used, or annotating a Hess cycle with the direction of each arrow and what it represents, takes fifteen seconds and makes the sign error visible to the student rather than invisible. Students who are simply told to be careful with signs keep making the error, because nothing in their method catches it.

At Higher Level, entropy and Gibbs energy add their own traps. Entropy has units that differ from enthalpy's by a factor of a thousand, so a Gibbs energy calculation mixing them without conversion is wrong by three orders of magnitude. The temperature term must be in kelvin. And the interpretation mark asks what a negative Gibbs energy means for spontaneity, in context, which is a written answer rather than a number.

There is a related pattern in the Born-Haber and lattice enthalpy material at Higher Level, where the number of steps makes an unannotated cycle almost impossible to check. Drawing the cycle with each step labelled and its sign stated is slower and is the only reliable way to arrive at the right answer, and the labelling itself attracts credit in many mark schemes.

Cycle read in the wrong direction
Annotate every arrow's direction and meaning

sections.heading: The data booklet, the periodic table and what revision should actually be
paragraphs: Every IB chemistry examination supplies a data booklet and a periodic table. That fact should reshape revision and usually does not. A student who knows what the booklet contains stops memorising constants, standard values and relationships and starts practising selection and application. One deliberate pass through the booklet with the syllabus beside it, annotating which topic each section serves, is half an hour that pays back repeatedly.

The periodic table supplied is a working tool rather than a reference. Molar masses come from it, so a student computing a molar mass should be reading values rather than recalling them, and reading them accurately. Group and period position supports periodicity answers. Students who have practised with the supplied version rather than a differently laid-out classroom poster waste no time orienting themselves.

The booklet also contains material students routinely do not know is there, which means they either memorise it unnecessarily or fail to use it. Working through it once removes both problems. It is the single cheapest piece of preparation in the subject and it takes one session, which is why it belongs early in any plan rather than in the week before a paper.

What the booklet cannot supply is the chemistry reasoning, the command-term discipline or the notation conventions. Used as a crutch, hunting for a value before thinking about the chemistry, it slows a student down. The order that works is to decide what chemistry applies, then find what the booklet provides for it, then calculate, writing each step. That sequence also produces the working the mark scheme pays for.

sections.heading: Command terms in chemistry, and the answers they will not accept
paragraphs: Chemistry marks are lost at the verb more often than students believe. The IB publishes its command terms with definitions, and the definitions carry mark expectations. State wants a short factual answer and gives nothing for a supporting argument. Describe wants an account without reasons. Explain wants reasons or a causal chain and credits nothing for a description. Deduce requires a conclusion reached from given information. Evaluate and discuss require weighed judgement.

The pattern that follows is predictable. A student who knows a topic thoroughly answers an explain question with a detailed description, receives roughly half the marks, and concludes they need more content knowledge. They revise more content, meet the next explain question, and answer it the same way. The problem was never the chemistry. Sorting past questions by command term and writing only the first two sentences of each answer makes it visible in a session.

Chemistry has a particular version of this in its comparison questions. Asked to compare two species' properties, a student frequently describes both in turn without a single comparative statement, and comparative language is what the mark scheme credits. Phrases that explicitly set one against the other, higher than, because the ionic radius is smaller, are what collect the marks.

There is also a context requirement in the data-based questions. A conclusion drawn from a data set is expected to refer to the data and to the chemistry, not simply assert a trend. A student who writes the rate increases without saying what in the data shows it, or what in the chemistry explains it, loses the credit for both halves of the expected answer.

table.caption: COMMAND TERMS AND WHAT THEY REQUIRE
rows: Describe the trend down the group
Explain why the boiling point rises
An answer from memory ignoring the data
Compare the acidity of the two species

sections.heading: The chemistry investigation: viability is the whole game
paragraphs: Chemistry has a harder investigation design problem than the other sciences, and families rarely anticipate it. Many genuinely interesting chemical questions cannot be answered in a school laboratory, either because the reagents are unavailable or unsafe, or because the measurement available is too crude to show the effect being looked for. A student who chooses a question on enthusiasm and discovers this during data collection has lost weeks.

The viability test is therefore the first piece of work, and it has three parts. Can the reaction or property be set up safely with the apparatus the school actually has. Can the dependent variable be measured with enough resolution to show a trend across the achievable range. And can the controlled variables be controlled, which in chemistry often means temperature, concentration and the purity of what was supplied. A preliminary run answers all three in an afternoon.

Where chemistry investigations then separate is in the treatment of uncertainty and in the evaluation. Each measurement carries an uncertainty from the instrument's resolution, and a titration volume, a mass and a temperature change each contribute differently to the uncertainty in a final result. A student who can say which measurement dominated the uncertainty and why has the material for a strong evaluation. One who writes a general list of things that could have gone better does not.

The honesty boundary is firm. A tutor can teach the chemistry, question whether the design can produce a measurable trend, discuss safety and apparatus realistically, explain each published criterion, and give feedback on drafts the student has written. A tutor cannot design the investigation, process the data, write any part of it or edit it to completion. Operations selling completed Internal Assessments exist in the Gulf market, and the malpractice consequence falls on the student.

Will the measured quantity change enough to see?

Widen the range or change the measured quantity
Can temperature, concentration and purity be held?
List each variable and how it is fixed
Add a control or acknowledge it as a limitation
Can each measurement carry an estimated uncertainty?
The evaluation criteria cannot be reached
Is there time for repeats within the deadline?

sections.heading: Higher Level chemistry, and the subject's stakes for medicine applications
paragraphs: Higher Level Chemistry carries additional content and a larger paper load than Standard Level, and it is also the Diploma subject with the highest external stakes for a particular group of students. Medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, veterinary science and chemical engineering commonly require it at Higher Level. A student who needs one of those routes cannot treat Chemistry Higher Level as optional, and a student who does not need them should think carefully before carrying it.

The Higher Level extensions are where trouble usually sits. The quantitative treatment of equilibrium, the acid-base material including buffers and titration curves, redox and electrochemistry taken further, the thermodynamic content around entropy and Gibbs energy, and the extended organic mechanisms. All of it arrives later in the two years, is taught at pace, and assumes the shared content is secure.

That produces the familiar pattern. A student comfortable through Year 12 struggles in Year 13 with what looks like a general collapse and is in fact a gap in two or three extension topics. Listing the extension content from the syllabus and attempting one question on each identifies the gaps in a session, and a block aimed at those is far more efficient than open-ended revision across the whole course.

The honest exception matters here more than in most subjects, because of those entry requirements. A student carrying Chemistry Higher Level who is weak across the shared content as well, alongside two other demanding Higher Levels, has a load problem. Raising that in term one of Year 12 keeps options open; raising it in Year 13 does not, and the university consequences of a low Higher Level Chemistry grade for a medicine applicant are worse than those of a strong Standard Level grade in a different plan.

sections.heading: Cost, bands and what each one buys in chemistry
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates split into bands and for chemistry the right band depends on which of the failure points is active. At the budget end, Tutopiya advertises online tutoring from around AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Qualified subject tutors working online are published at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at around AED 270, and BartyED charges AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home one-to-one is AED 180 to 500 with travel included.

For stoichiometry and naming drills, the mid band is sufficient: the work is procedural and does not need deep assessment familiarity. For mechanisms marked to IB conventions, for Higher Level thermodynamics, and for investigation design and evaluation, the specialist band earns its premium, because those are the places where a tutor unfamiliar with the published expectations teaches a defensible version that does not match what is credited.

Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-band and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages in the market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. All published by the providers themselves rather than by us.

The efficient shape for chemistry is a short procedural block early, stoichiometry chains and the data booklet, then investigation viability coaching before data collection, then Higher Level extension work and paper technique in Year 13. Front-loading the procedural work matters because everything quantitative in the subject chains from it, and a student whose mole work is unreliable will keep losing marks in topics that look unrelated.

sections.heading: Chemistry over video, and what the format does well
paragraphs: Chemistry transfers to video better than most people assume, for a specific reason: a large share of the subject's marks turn on what is drawn and written. A mechanism is drawn, and on a shared surface the tutor watches each arrow appear and can stop at the one that started in the wrong place. A stoichiometry chain is written line by line, and the tutor sees the unbalanced equation at the moment it is used rather than reconstructing the error from a wrong answer.

The data booklet and periodic table are documents, and having both open on screen for both parties is more practical than passing a paper copy across a table. A data set from the student's own investigation can be annotated live. A titration curve can be drawn and discussed with the axes visible to both. For the written and drawn parts of chemistry, which is most of the assessment, the format is at least as good as sitting side by side.

The apparatus-dependent part stays at school, which is where it belongs. What a student usually lacks is not laboratory time but help with the design decisions, the uncertainty estimates and the evaluation, and all three are conversations. A tutor can ask whether a preliminary trial showed a measurable change, or whether the titration volume or the mass dominated the uncertainty, without being in the room.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and no tutor will arrive at an address in Al Khail Gate or anywhere else in the Emirates. All UAE lessons are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time. The published in-home band in Dubai is AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 online, and for a Higher Level chemistry specialist the online pool is substantially larger than the pool willing to cross the Al Khail interchange at five in the afternoon.
