sections.heading: What chemistry tuition costs around Al Nahda, and what the specialist premium buys
paragraphs: Start at the top of the market rather than the bottom, because the interesting question is not what the cheapest option costs but what the expensive one is selling. A named or examiner-badged tutor in Dubai is advertised at around AED 650 an hour by BartyED. Immediately below that sits a band of subject specialists at roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour, which is where TutorChase's published AED 270 falls and where Bestimate's 2026 rate survey places IB and IGCSE specialist work. Step down again and qualified online subject tutors run about AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. At the bottom, budget and university-student tutors advertise from AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52.

What the premium buys, when it buys anything, is diagnostic speed. A specialist watching your child attempt an equilibrium question identifies the actual fault in one attempt rather than three, and spends the rest of the hour fixing it. That is the whole of the value proposition, and it is why a smaller number of expensive hours frequently outperforms a larger number of cheap ones in a subject with this much interlocking structure. Where the premium buys nothing is in general revision company, and parents in Al Nahda do sometimes pay specialist rates for supervised homework.

The in-home comparison is the one most relevant to this search. In-home one-to-one visits in Dubai are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors, and monthly packages of four two-hour in-home sessions are advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799. Online monthly packages of eight sessions appear at around AED 799. The gap is the travel premium, and in a district on the Sharjah boundary during the evening peak that travel is not nominal. sections.heading: Tutor coverage on the Sharjah border, and what happens when nobody covers Higher Level
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market publishes a coverage limit, and that silence is worth noticing. Tutoring supply is not uniform across subjects. Diploma chemistry at Standard Level is reasonably well covered in Dubai; Higher Level with a specific extension need, or chemistry combined with an unusual second subject, is not. The honest position is to tell a parent that before they book, not after.

Our rule is simple and we state it on every UAE page. If a UAE-based tutor covers the subject and level, that is the match, because the term calendar, the school culture and the time zone are already aligned. If no UAE-based specialist is available for a niche requirement, we say so and offer a tutor from our wider pool, working Gulf Standard Time, at the same rate band. We do not quietly route a UAE family to a tutor in another time zone and let them discover it in the first lesson, which is a pattern visible elsewhere in this market behind a non-UAE contact number.

sections.heading: What an Al Nahda parent can verify for nothing before paying anybody
paragraphs: Four checks cost nothing and take under an hour, and together they rule out most of what goes wrong in this market. The first is the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and it is applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own service, listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing with a two-working-day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you are quoted with suspicion. Ask the tutor whether they hold the permit; the answer costs you nothing and tells you a lot.

The second check is the school's own position. Your child's IB coordinator will confirm which chemistry guide the cohort is on, when the mocks fall, and when internal deadlines for the Scientific Investigation sit. That is three facts, free, from the one source that cannot be wrong. Any tutoring plan built without them is guessing.

The third is the regulator. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, and publishes inspection outcomes for schools on its own site. If your child attends school in Sharjah, as some Al Nahda families do, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education there and also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Read the current rating on the regulator's site rather than on an agency's page, including ours.

The fourth is the claim check. Nobody in this market is accredited, approved or licensed by KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson to tutor your child, and a service that says it is has told you something you can test. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with physical premises, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no regulator accreditation and does not operate a UAE centre. If a page tells you otherwise about anyone, ask for the permit number.

faqs.question: Is there an IB Chemistry tutor based in Al Nahda itself?
faqs.answer: Possibly, but it is the wrong thing to search for. The number of students sitting Diploma chemistry at Higher Level across all of Dubai in a given year is small, so a genuine specialist is unlikely to be concentrated in any single district, Al Nahda included. What you will reliably find locally is a general science tutor with Indian-curriculum strength. Our approach is to match on the syllabus and deliver one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so the tutor is chosen for knowing the current chemistry guide rather than for living within a fifteen-minute drive of Al Nahda 2.

faqs.question: How can I tell whether a chemistry tutor really knows the current IB guide?
faqs.answer: Ask five questions. Which guide do they teach, how many written papers are there now, what is the Scientific Investigation worth, what is the difference between deduce and explain, and what would they check first if your child failed an equilibrium question. A tutor who teaches this course weekly answers all five without pausing: the guide first assessed in May 2025, two papers with Paper 1 split into multiple choice and data-based, about a fifth of the grade for the investigation, and a clear distinction between reaching a conclusion from given information and giving reasons for one.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a chemistry tutor to our apartment in Al Nahda?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we run only in India. Chemistry tuition for an Al Nahda family is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for mechanisms, spectra and worked calculations. The trade is deliberate. Dropping the travel requirement is what makes it possible to put a Higher Level chemistry specialist in front of your child at seven on a Tuesday evening, which no catchment-limited service on the Sharjah boundary can realistically offer.

faqs.question: What has changed in IB Chemistry since my older child took it?
faqs.answer: A great deal, if your older child finished before 2025. The course was rewritten with first assessment in May 2025. The Options are gone, Paper 3 is gone, and content is now organised under two headings, Structure and Reactivity, rather than as a numbered topic list. The practical scheme has been replaced by a single Scientific Investigation worth about a fifth of the grade at both levels. A tutor still working from the previous guide will teach material that is no longer examined, so this is the first thing to check.

faqs.question: How much of the chemistry grade comes from work done outside the exam hall?
faqs.answer: About a fifth, through the Scientific Investigation, at both Standard and Higher Level. That makes it the largest single assessment object in the course, and it is also the one most families treat as a side project. Two consequences follow. First, it is worth timetabling properly rather than squeezing into the week before an internal deadline. Second, the support available for it is strictly bounded: a supervisor may question the design and give feedback on the student's own drafts, but any arrangement where somebody else produces the work is malpractice.

faqs.question: My daughter understands chemistry in class but drops marks in Paper 2. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always command terms and question order rather than content. Paper 2 asks students to deduce, outline, state, explain, compare and contrast, and each verb has a defined expectation marks are allocated against. A student who writes an essay when the paper said state spends time they then do not have for the final question, and loses marks twice. This is quick to fix. Four to six sessions of timed questions marked against the published criteria, with the verb circled before the answer is written, usually produces a visible change by the next mock.

faqs.question: Why does organic chemistry feel so much harder than the rest of the course?
faqs.answer: Because most students learn it as a list of thirty unrelated reactions rather than as a map. Held as a list, every synthesis question is a new memory test. Held as a map, with functional groups at the nodes and reagents on the arrows between them, a multi-step synthesis becomes route-finding, which students are far better at. Building that map takes roughly three sessions and maintaining it takes five minutes a week. The second half of the problem is mechanism arrows, which must start at a lone pair or a bond, never at an atom.

faqs.question: Where exactly does the honesty line sit on my son's chemistry investigation?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary is clear. A tutor may question the research question until it is answerable with school apparatus, challenge an uncontrolled variable, teach uncertainty propagation and graphing conventions in general, and give feedback on the student's own draft, including flagging claims the data do not support. A tutor may not supply a method, process data the student did not collect, or write or rewrite any part of the report. We explain this to students directly, because a malpractice finding can cost the whole Diploma rather than a few marks.

faqs.question: What do chemistry tutors actually charge in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market figures, read in October 2026 and attributed to whoever published them, run as follows. Budget and university-student online tutors advertise from AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors sit around AED 150 to 300, Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. IB and IGCSE specialists run about AED 200 to 450, TutorChase at AED 270. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 500. IB Gram does not publish an hourly price list here; the trial lesson is free.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper tutor at AED 60 an hour ever sensible for Diploma chemistry?
faqs.answer: For some jobs, yes. Keeping practice ticking over between specialist sessions, supervising homework so it gets done, and drilling recall are all tasks a careful budget tutor can handle. What a budget rate rarely buys is diagnosis. The value of a specialist is identifying the actual fault in one attempt instead of three and spending the rest of the hour repairing it, which matters in a subject this interlocked. Many families get the best result by mixing the two, rather than by buying the cheapest hours or the most expensive ones throughout.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit, and should I ask about it?
faqs.answer: Yes to both. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own service for private tutor licensing, which lists a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so ignore any specific figure quoted at you.

faqs.question: My son is in DP1 and has not started his investigation. When should he?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most schools' internal deadline implies, because the slowest part is narrowing the question rather than running the experiment. Ask the IB coordinator for the school's own internal deadlines, then work backwards: a fortnight to settle a question that is genuinely answerable with the apparatus available, time to trial the method and find the variable nobody controlled, then collection, processing and writing. Families who start at the deadline end up with a literature summary and a few measurements attached, which is the most common reason a competent student scores poorly on this component.

faqs.question: Does it matter that our school is in Sharjah while we live in Al Nahda?
faqs.answer: For tutoring planning, yes, in one practical way. Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA; Sharjah private education is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. The two emirates do not run identical term calendars, so mock windows and half-term breaks can fall in different weeks. Tell us which school your child attends and the plan is paced to its dates. A tutor working mostly with schools on the other side of the boundary may otherwise revise to the wrong week.

faqs.question: Which chemistry topics are worth paying a specialist to teach?
faqs.answer: Four, on the evidence of where marks are lost. Energetics, because sign conventions in a Hess cycle need a mechanical rule installed rather than more theory. Equilibrium, because the habit of stating a direction before justifying it has to be taught. Organic chemistry, because it needs restructuring from a list into a map. And the data-based section of Paper 1, because it is almost never drilled separately in school and students describe unfamiliar data instead of using it. Those four are where an expensive hour pays for itself most reliably.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram approved by KHDA or by the IB to teach chemistry?
faqs.answer: No, and neither is anyone else offering you private tutoring. IB Gram holds no accreditation, approval, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no UAE centre. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with physical premises, requiring initial approval first and annual renewal at least thirty days before expiry. If a tutoring page claims regulator approval, ask for the permit number. We name regulators to explain what they do, not to borrow authority we do not hold.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does Diploma chemistry usually need?
faqs.answer: One weekly session suits a student who is coping but losing marks on technique; it gives space to practise between lessons, which is where the learning actually happens. Two sessions a week suit a student with a real content gap, or a Higher Level student whose Standard Level foundation needs repair before the extensions can land. Short dated blocks of three or four sessions work well before a mock, aimed at a single paper. More than two hours a week rarely helps, because the limiting factor becomes independent practice rather than teaching time.

intro.heading: Comparing Al Quoz with the corridor, and finding the comparison cuts the other way

Al Quoz has housing in Al Quoz 1, 2 and 3 inside a district given mostly to warehouses, workshops, showrooms and the Alserkal Avenue arts spaces. The inference drawn is that the better-served district has better options, and for chemistry the inference runs the wrong way.

Here is why. Diploma chemistry cohorts vary sharply in size between schools, and Higher Level chemistry cohorts vary most of all. In a large cohort a school can run separate Higher and Standard Level teaching, assign a specialist to each, and offer structured revision sessions. In a small cohort the two levels are sometimes taught together, and one mid-year staffing change leaves a Higher Level group with a gap that is nobody's fault and still has to be filled from outside.

So the district comparison that actually matters is not about tutor supply. It is about what your own school's chemistry cohort can and cannot do, and that question is answered by the subject teacher rather than by a map. A family in a well-served district with a small Higher Level group may need more outside support than a family in Al Quoz with a large one.

What does not vary by district is the chemistry. Higher Level marks go, in order, to organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium, and the investigation at 20 per cent. That hour decides whether a second weekly session in a pre-session block fits on a weekday or moves to the weekend, and it is worth planning deliberately rather than discovering in week three.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-quoz.programmesIntro: Chemistry support in Al Quoz is requested at four points in the IB continuum, and each has a different shape. Below, each is described by what the assessment demands.

programmes.name: Chemistry, Higher Level
programmes.description: Substantially greater depth across the course, with organic chemistry, energetics and equilibrium carrying the most additional demand, plus the internal investigation at 20 per cent of the grade. The characteristic Higher Level failure is a mechanism drawn with the right products and the wrong arrows, which the scheme does not reward because the arrows are the chemistry.
programmes.countryNote: Higher Level chemistry is the most common Diploma science request from Al Quoz families, and the pattern repeats: a student who found IGCSE chemistry straightforward meets mechanism work in DP1 and discovers that memorising products no longer works. It is a technique problem and it is cheapest to fix in the first DP1 term.

programmes.name: Chemistry, Standard Level
programmes.description: The same thematic structure at reduced depth, with the investigation carrying the same proportional weight. Standard Level students often survive on recall and stoichiometric routine, which caps them: the marks that separate a five from a seven are in explanation and in data treatment rather than in content coverage.
programmes.countryNote: A frequent Al Quoz pattern is Standard Level chemistry taken as a sixth subject behind two heavier Higher Levels, receiving the least preparation time of the six. Four targeted sessions on explanation structure and data handling usually move it more than a term of content revision.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria, including inquiring and designing and processing and evaluating, which are the direct ancestors of the Diploma investigation. A Year 10 student who learns to control variables deliberately and quantify uncertainty writes a far better investigation two years later, at no additional cost.
programmes.countryNote: This is the cheapest chemistry intervention available in Dubai and almost nobody buys it, because in MYP nothing is yet at stake. Schools in the Al Barsha and central corridor clusters run their MYP assessment calendars differently, so the pressure points vary by school.

programmes.name: IGCSE to Diploma chemistry transition
programmes.description: IGCSE chemistry rewards knowing what happens; Diploma chemistry rewards explaining why, in mechanism and in energetics. The content overlap is real and the assessment shift is sharp, which is what produces the DP1 grade fall in students who were previously comfortable.
programmes.countryNote: A summer block of four to six sessions between Year 11 and DP1, spent on bonding, electron movement and the language of mechanisms, prevents most of that fall. It is the best available use of a holiday for a prospective Higher Level chemistry student in Dubai.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-quoz.subjectsIntro: Chemistry is best organised by where the marks go rather than by chapter order. Below are the areas Al Quoz students most often need, each with the error that recurs in marked work.

subjects.name: Stoichiometry and the mole
subjects.description: The arithmetic underneath everything else. Errors are rarely conceptual: they are limiting reagent ignored, a molar ratio inverted, or units dropped halfway through a multi-step calculation that was otherwise correct from start to finish.

subjects.name: Atomic structure and bonding
subjects.description: Electron configuration, ionisation trends and intermolecular forces. The recurring failure is an answer that names a force without saying why it is stronger here than there, which forfeits the explanation mark even when the identification was right.

subjects.name: Energetics and thermochemistry
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Enthalpy changes, Hess cycles, bond enthalpies and at Higher Level entropy and Gibbs free energy. Sign conventions cause more lost marks here than any concept; a correct magnitude with the wrong sign is treated as a chemistry error, not a slip.

subjects.name: Chemical kinetics
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Rate expressions, collision theory and at Higher Level rate-determining steps and mechanisms consistent with an experimental rate law. Students lose marks by proposing a mechanism that does not actually match the given rate expression.

subjects.name: Equilibrium
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Le Chatelier reasoning and at Higher Level equilibrium constant calculations. The characteristic error is predicting the correct shift and explaining it by restating the shift, instead of by reference to the change in the system that caused it.

subjects.name: Acids, bases and redox
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: pH calculations, buffers, titration curves and electrochemical cells. Higher Level adds weak acid and base calculations where students apply strong acid arithmetic and arrive confidently at an answer several pH units out.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry and mechanisms
subjects.levels: SL and HL, substantially extended at HL
subjects.description: Functional groups, reaction pathways and at Higher Level full mechanisms with curly arrows. This is where most Higher Level marks are lost, and the reason is specific: students learn products and are examined on electron movement.

subjects.name: Data processing and uncertainty
subjects.description: Percentage uncertainty, propagation, significant figures and graph interpretation. The technique list is short and finite, it transfers directly into the investigation, and it is almost always taught in a hurry alongside everything else.

subjects.name: Explanation structure
subjects.description: Writing an answer that states the chemistry, applies it to the specific case and reaches the conclusion the question asked for. Students who know the chemistry and write in the wrong structure lose marks consistently, which looks like weakness and is not.

subjects.name: The chemistry investigation
subjects.levels: SL and HL, 20 per cent of the grade
subjects.description: Internally assessed individual work marked against lettered criteria and moderated. The commonest structural failure is a research question that cannot be measured precisely enough with school glassware, which caps the analysis criteria before any data exists.

The first question is the level, and it matters more in chemistry than in most subjects. Higher Level chemistry is not Standard Level with additional chapters; the extra depth lands disproportionately on organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium, and the reasoning demanded in those areas is different in kind rather than in quantity. A tutor comfortable with Standard Level who has not taught Higher Level mechanism work will teach pleasantly and miss the problem.

The second question is where the investigation stands, because 20 per cent of the grade is sitting in it and the window for useful help closes early. Before data collection, a tutor can save a student six weeks by establishing that the research question cannot be measured precisely enough with school glassware. After the data is collected, nobody can fix that, and the ceiling is already set.

The third question is what the marked scripts show. Chemistry mark loss is strikingly concentrated: sign conventions in energetics, molar ratios inverted, Le Chatelier answers that restate the shift instead of explaining it, strong acid arithmetic applied to weak acids, and mechanisms with correct products and wrong arrows. Each of those is a short targeted fix. Guessing between them is a term.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level, properly compared
paragraphs: Almost every competitor page in this market mentions Higher and Standard Level in a single sentence and moves on. The difference deserves a table, because families choose between them on reputation and then meet the consequences for two years.

The additional Higher Level content is not spread evenly. Organic chemistry gains full mechanisms with electron movement. Energetics gains entropy and Gibbs free energy. Equilibrium gains quantitative treatment. Kinetics gains rate-determining steps that must be consistent with an experimental rate law. A student who copes with Standard Level by recall meets four areas at once where recall does not help.

The investigation carries the same proportional weight at both levels, which has a counter-intuitive consequence: it is proportionally the best-value work a Standard Level student can do, because the marks are available on the same terms and the content demand is lower. Standard Level students who treat the investigation as the subject's main opportunity rather than as an obligation routinely gain more from it than their Higher Level peers do.

On choosing the level, the honest test is a timed Higher Level question on mechanisms or energetics, attempted now. A student who can reason through electron movement is in the right place. A student who produces correct products with no mechanism is not yet, and has time to get there in DP1 if the gap is named. Confirm current content and weightings with the subject guide your child's school holds, since the IB revises its science guides and we do not reproduce their documents.

sections.heading: The three areas that cost the most marks
paragraphs: Marked chemistry scripts from Dubai schools are remarkably consistent. Three areas account for most of the recoverable loss at Higher Level, and knowing which one is costing your child decides the length of the plan.

Organic mechanisms come first by a clear margin. The reason is a mismatch in what students practise and what is examined. Students revise by learning which reagent gives which product, because that is what a textbook table presents. The examination asks for the electron movement that produces it, and a mechanism with correct products and incorrect arrows earns very little, because the arrows are the chemistry being tested.

Energetics comes second, and almost entirely through sign conventions. An exothermic change with a positive enthalpy value is not a careless slip in the scheme's view; it is a chemistry error, and it frequently invalidates the rest of a Hess cycle built on it. This is a two-session fix with a rule and a habit, and it is one of the cheapest grade movements available in the subject.

It is worth noticing what these two have in common, because it changes how a family reads a disappointing grade. Neither is a gap in chemistry. Both are habits in how chemistry is written down, and habits are short work: a rule, a deliberate check, and enough marked practice for the check to become automatic.

Equilibrium comes third, through a specific pattern of explanation. A student predicts the correct direction of shift and then justifies it by restating the shift, which is circular and earns the prediction mark only. The scheme wants the change in the system named and its effect on the position of equilibrium derived from it. Again a technique fix rather than a content one, and again short.

sections.heading: Organic mechanisms: what actually fixes them
paragraphs: Mechanism work is the one place in Diploma chemistry where the common study method is actively counterproductive. A student who memorises a table of reagents and products builds a structure that collapses as soon as an unfamiliar substrate appears, and unfamiliar substrates are precisely what the examination uses to separate grades.

What works instead is reasoning from electron density. Where are the electrons, where are they attracted, what breaks, what forms, and in which order. A student who can answer those five questions about an unfamiliar molecule can construct a mechanism they have never seen, which is the actual skill being assessed. A student who cannot is dependent on recognition, and recognition fails at exactly the wrong moment.

Teaching it has a specific shape, and it is why a shared screen helps. The student draws the mechanism, the tutor corrects the arrow as it is drawn rather than afterwards, and the correction lands at the moment the error is being made. Done on paper between two people in a room, half the arrows are drawn upside down from the tutor's viewpoint. Done on a shared annotated screen, both people see the same molecule the same way up.

Expect four to six sessions for most Higher Level students, with the test of completion being an unfamiliar mechanism constructed and justified without prompting. That is a defined block with a visible end point, which is how chemistry support should be bought, rather than as a standing weekly arrangement that nobody reviews until the May session has already happened.

sections.heading: The investigation, and the AED 3,750 problem
paragraphs: One operator researched for these pages sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. It is worth naming the price because it tells you what the market looks like from a student's point of view: there is a product, it is advertised, and a stressed DP2 student in February can find it in a minute. Buying one is an academic honesty breach that can cost the entire Diploma, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the seller.

IB Gram does not write, complete, edit to completion or supply coursework of any kind, and no tutor working through us is permitted to. What a tutor does instead is teach the investigation. That means explaining each criterion in the IB's own terms, testing whether the research question can be measured precisely enough with the glassware a school actually has, demonstrating uncertainty technique on unrelated practice data, reading the student's own draft and saying which criterion it fails and why, and teaching whatever skill the draft reveals is missing.

The structural failures are predictable and they are all front-loaded. A research question that depends on measuring a change too small for school equipment to detect caps the analysis and evaluation criteria before any data exists. A single run per condition makes an uncertainty analysis impossible to produce afterwards. A dependent variable chosen because it is easy to observe rather than because it answers the question produces data that cannot support a conclusion. All three are one-session problems at the design stage and unfixable later.

The practical test for any family: after a session, could your child explain and defend every change to their own work, in their own words? If yes, that was teaching. If no, the line has been crossed, and the school's academic honesty policy is the document that will decide what happens next.

sections.heading: Chemistry Higher Level and what universities ask for
paragraphs: Chemistry at Higher Level is requested more often than any other Diploma science in Dubai, and the reason is usually a medical or related application. That makes the subject choice consequential, and it also makes it a place where tutoring pages tend to overpromise, so here is the careful version.

Medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine, pharmacy and many biomedical courses commonly expect chemistry at Higher Level, frequently alongside biology. Engineering routes more often expect physics and mathematics at Higher Level, with chemistry optional. Those are patterns rather than rules, and the only reliable source is the individual programme's own published requirements, including those of UAE universities, which differ from each other and change.

Two things follow for an Al Quoz family. First, verify the requirement for the specific programmes on your child's list before DP1 subject choices are confirmed, because a Higher Level requirement discovered in DP2 cannot be met. Second, remember that no amount of tutoring makes a subject choice reversible, so the one or two sessions spent checking this at the end of Year 11 are worth more than a term of support later.

What tutoring cannot do is also worth stating. Tutoring is not required for university admission, for Ministry of Education equivalency or for school progression, and any provider implying otherwise is making a false claim about a regulatory process. Nobody can promise a grade, a point total or an offer, and nobody should be asked to.

faqs.question: My child finds organic chemistry impossible. Is that fixable before the session?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and faster than families expect, because the problem is almost always method rather than ability. Students revise by memorising which reagent gives which product, and the examination asks for the electron movement that produces it, so a mechanism with correct products and wrong arrows earns very little. Teaching reasoning from electron density takes four to six sessions, and the test of completion is an unfamiliar mechanism constructed and justified without prompting rather than a recognised one reproduced.

faqs.question: Does an IB chemistry tutor visit our home in Al Quoz?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Chemistry is taught one-to-one into Al Quoz homes over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with working shared and annotated on screen, and we send no tutors to UAE addresses; in-person home visits are an India-only service for us. For mechanism work the shared screen is a genuine advantage: the student draws the arrow, the tutor corrects it as it is drawn, and both see the same molecule the same way up rather than from opposite sides of a notebook.

faqs.question: Where exactly does the extra Higher Level chemistry content land?
faqs.answer: Not evenly, which is why the step feels so sudden. The additional depth lands on organic mechanisms with full electron movement, entropy and Gibbs free energy in energetics, quantitative equilibrium work, rate-determining steps in kinetics, and weak acid and buffer calculations. A student who copes at Standard Level by recall meets four or five areas at once where recall does not help. The internal investigation carries the same proportional weight at both levels.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks in energetics when the numbers are right?
faqs.answer: Sign conventions, almost certainly. An exothermic change reported with a positive enthalpy is treated by the scheme as a chemistry error rather than as a presentation slip, and it frequently invalidates a Hess cycle built on top of it. Students find this harsh, which is why it survives: they treat each instance as carelessness instead of fixing the underlying habit. It is a two-session correction with a rule and a deliberate check, and one of the cheapest grade movements in the subject.

faqs.question: What makes a good chemistry investigation research question?
faqs.answer: One that can be measured precisely enough with the glassware your child's school actually has. The commonest failure is a question depending on a change too small for school equipment to detect, which caps the analysis and evaluation criteria before any data exists. Also decide the uncertainty treatment before the laboratory session rather than afterwards, because a single run per condition makes an uncertainty analysis impossible to produce later. Both are one-session problems at the design stage and unfixable afterwards.

faqs.question: Someone offered to supply a completed IB Internal Assessment. Should we consider it?
faqs.answer: No, under any circumstances. One operator researched for this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, and buying one is an academic honesty breach that can cost the whole Diploma. The consequence falls on your child, not on the seller. A tutor may teach the criteria, test the research question, demonstrate technique on unrelated data and comment on your child's own draft. The test after any session is whether your child could explain and defend every change themselves.

faqs.question: Does living in Al Quoz rather than Sobha Hartland limit our chemistry options?
faqs.answer: Not through us, because lessons are delivered online and both families reach the same specialists. What genuinely differs is in-school provision: districts with larger Diploma science cohorts tend to have schools that can run Higher and Standard Level separately and offer structured revision, while smaller cohorts sometimes teach both levels together. So the useful question is about your own school's chemistry group rather than your postcode, and the subject teacher is the person who can answer it.

faqs.question: How many chemistry sessions a month should we budget for?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which problem you have, which is why diagnosis comes first. A sign-convention fix is two or three sessions in a month, roughly AED 600 at mid-market rates. A Higher Level mechanism block is four to six across six weeks, in the AED 600 to 1,200 monthly range. Investigation coaching is four to six across a term. Examination-year weekly support with a targeted block runs AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more monthly, per Bestimate's 2026 estimates.

faqs.question: Why do weak acid calculations go so badly wrong at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Because students apply strong acid arithmetic out of habit and arrive confidently at a pH several units from the correct value. The error is systematic rather than random, which is good news: it means a short, deliberate block on the distinction, with practice at recognising which case a question presents, usually ends it in two or three sessions. It also tends to indicate that buffer questions are being answered the same way, so the two are worth fixing together.

faqs.question: Is Standard Level chemistry worth supporting if it is a sixth subject?
faqs.answer: Often yes, briefly, and the best value is usually the investigation. It carries the same proportional weight at Standard Level as at Higher Level while the content demand is lower, so the marks are available on easier terms and the work can be done to a high standard with time rather than brilliance. Beyond that, four sessions on explanation structure and data handling typically move a Standard Level grade further than a term of content revision, because content was rarely the problem.

faqs.question: Should we take chemistry at Higher Level for a medical application?
faqs.answer: Medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine, pharmacy and many biomedical courses commonly expect chemistry at Higher Level, often alongside biology, but those are patterns rather than rules. Verify the published requirement for each specific programme on your child's list, including UAE universities, which differ from one another and revise requirements. Do it before DP1 subject choices are confirmed at the end of Year 11, because a Higher Level requirement discovered in DP2 cannot be met afterwards by any amount of tutoring.

faqs.question: How early should we book Higher Level chemistry support before the May session?
faqs.answer: Earlier than feels necessary. Higher Level chemistry and physics are the hardest specialisms to cover at a specific early-evening hour, and those slots fill first across the corridor around Al Quoz, where the largest Diploma science cohorts sit. If you know a block is likely after mocks, agreeing the pattern in advance costs nothing and secures the time. When nothing is available we say so and give a realistic date rather than offering a generalist instead.

faqs.question: Do you supply chemistry past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider advertising them as a feature is distributing someone else's property. IB past papers, mark schemes, grade boundary tables and subject guides are the organisation's copyright, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure in addition. We reference them, cite the official source, link to it, and work from what your child's school legitimately provides. The subject teacher also remains the authority on exactly what this cohort sits, since the IB revises its guides.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover chemistry and biology for a DP2 student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the overlap in data handling and command term technique is real, so the same uncertainty work pays in both. The test is still component-level competence in each subject separately, including each investigation, which have different criteria and different practical constraints. If a tutor is strong on chemistry mechanisms but vague about statistical treatment in a biology investigation, two specialists serve your child better than one convenient diary.

intro.heading: The school run decides when Chemistry tuition actually happens
paragraphs: Al Quoz 4 has almost no secondary schools inside it. Children living here travel out — west to Al Safa, Al Manara and Jumeirah, north-west along Al Khail Road to Al Barsha and Al Sufouh, or south towards Dubai Hills. That geography produces a long bus day. A student whose school sits in Al Barsha South is usually the last few stops on a route that began somewhere else, and the practical result is a front door at a quarter past four rather than half past three.

This matters more for Chemistry than for most subjects, because Chemistry homework is cumulative and the sessions that actually work are the ones that happen every week without negotiation. A tutoring arrangement that collapses in week six does so almost always for a logistical reason, not an educational one: the slot was too early, a sibling's activity moved, or the tutor's own journey made 17:00 into 17:35 twice in a row.

The honest position on in-person tutoring: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. That is an India-only service. Chemistry lessons for Al Quoz 4 families run live over video, one-to-one. For a scheduling problem this is the whole answer, because the thirty to forty minutes a tutor would spend driving across Dubai in the late afternoon is removed from the arithmetic entirely, along with the risk that an accident on Sheikh Zayed Road eats half the lesson.

What the schedule has to accommodate changes through the year. In the autumn term of Year 13 the pressure point is the scientific investigation, which usually needs two sessions in some weeks and none in others. Through the spring it is Reactivity content and timed papers. During Ramadan many families move sessions after Iftar, and schools shorten the day, which makes earlier slots briefly possible. A plan that assumes one fixed hour for two years will be wrong by November.

Parents here also juggle siblings. Where two children in the same household need support, back-to-back slots on the same evening are usually easier to hold than two separate evenings, and because nobody is travelling it costs nothing to arrange. Those are the kinds of details that decide whether tuition lasts a term or a year, and they are worth settling before the first lesson rather than after the third missed one.

There is one more scheduling fact worth stating plainly, because it shapes what a family can realistically be offered. The hours between five and seven on a weekday evening are the busiest two hours in UAE tutoring, and they are busy for every subject at once. A household that can use a Saturday morning, or a weekday at half past seven, has a materially wider choice of Diploma Chemistry specialists than one that needs Tuesday at five o'clock and nothing else. That is not a sales line; it is arithmetic about a small pool of people teaching a minority subject, and a family that knows it early can trade an inconvenient hour for a better-matched tutor.

sections.heading: The Al Quoz 4 afternoon, hour by hour
paragraphs: A workable Chemistry slot for this neighbourhood starts at 17:00. That is the answer, and the reasoning is worth seeing because it changes what a family should ask for. Al Quoz 4 contains little secondary provision of its own, so students board a bus to Al Safa, Al Barsha, Al Sufouh or Jumeirah, and the return leg is a route with multiple stops rather than a direct journey.

Schools in this part of Dubai typically finish between 14:30 and 15:15 for secondary year groups. Add the bus route and arrivals into Al Quoz 4 spread between roughly 15:00 and 16:15, with the Al Barsha and Al Sufouh routes consistently at the late end. Then add the part families forget: a Year 13 who walks in at 16:10 is not ready to think about equilibrium at 16:15. Twenty minutes and something to eat is not indulgence, it is the difference between a productive hour and a wasted one.

That puts the first genuinely reliable slot at 17:00 and the comfortable one at 17:30. Later than 19:00 and the quality drops again for most students, which leaves a two-hour usable window on a weekday. This is precisely why removing the tutor's journey matters: when a lesson can only sit inside a two-hour window, a tutor arriving late twice has used up the family's patience and the term's momentum.

Friday and the weekend are the pressure release. Many Al Quoz 4 families put the longer ninety-minute Chemistry session on a Saturday morning, where organic mechanisms or a full past paper can be worked without a school day pressing on either side, and keep a shorter weekday slot for consolidation. That split is the single most common successful pattern we see in this area.

sections.heading: Which schools this neighbourhood feeds, and what that means for Chemistry
paragraphs: Al Quoz 4 students are spread across three school clusters, and the spread has a real consequence: there is no shared Chemistry timetable in this neighbourhood. Two students on the same street can be eleven weeks apart in the same syllabus, one midway through Reactivity 2 while the other is still finishing Structure 3. Group tuition organised by postcode founders on exactly this.

The Al Safa, Al Manara and Jumeirah cluster is the closest and the most mixed. It contains British-curriculum schools running IGCSE into A Level alongside full IB continuum schools, which means some students in it are not taking DP Chemistry at all and the ones who are sit in small cohorts. A small cohort is a double-edged thing: more teacher attention, but almost nobody to compare a confusing homework question with.

The Al Barsha and Al Sufouh cluster carries several IB Diploma schools and, in our experience of their calendars, some of the earliest internal investigation deadlines in the city. For an Al Quoz 4 family whose child attends here, the autumn of Year 13 is the busy term and the spring is comparatively calm — the opposite of what families expect, and a reason to start Chemistry support in September rather than January.

Umm Suqeim and the coastal schools sit a short run west and draw on the villa communities around Umm Al Sheif and Al Manara. Diploma Chemistry cohorts there are small, and Higher Level cohorts smaller still. Ask the school how many students are taking Chemistry HL in your child's year; the answer tells you a great deal about how much individual attention is available and where tuition genuinely adds something.

sections.heading: Structure and Reactivity: what the current Chemistry syllabus asks
paragraphs: DP Chemistry is now organised around two ideas rather than a long topic list. Structure covers models of the particulate nature of matter, models of bonding and structure, and the classification of matter — atomic structure, the periodic table, ionic, covalent and metallic bonding, intermolecular forces, and the organic and spectroscopic classification work. Reactivity covers what drives chemical reactions, how much and how fast and how far, and the mechanisms of chemical change — energetics, entropy, kinetics, equilibrium, acids and bases, redox and organic mechanisms.

The reorganisation is not cosmetic. It means a question can legitimately draw on bonding and energetics together, and that students who learned topics as separate boxes struggle with linked questions even when they know both halves. The useful tutoring response is to teach across the boundary deliberately: explain a solubility observation using intermolecular forces and then the thermodynamics, in the same session, so the link is built rather than discovered in an exam.

Assessment is Paper 1, which carries a multiple-choice section and a data-based section, Paper 2 with short and extended response questions, and the scientific investigation at 20% of the grade. Higher Level sits the same structure with additional content and longer papers. The data booklet is provided and students are expected to use it fluently; a surprising number of marks are lost by candidates hunting for a value they could have found in ten seconds with practice.

The two reliable mark-losers are organic mechanisms and equilibrium. Mechanisms fail on notation — curly arrows starting from the wrong place, lone pairs omitted, intermediates not shown — which is a drawing discipline more than a conceptual one. Equilibrium fails on interpretation: students can state Le Chatelier's principle and still misread which way a system shifts when two changes are applied at once. Both respond well to short, repetitive practice rather than re-reading notes.

sections.heading: The Chemistry investigation against the school's own calendar
paragraphs: The internal assessment is one scientific investigation, up to 3,000 words, marked out of 24 across four criteria worth six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. It is 20% of the final grade. Because the deadline is set internally, the single most important piece of information a tutor needs from an Al Quoz 4 family is not the syllabus level but the date the school wants the report.

Working back from that date produces a sequence. The research question has to be settled well before data collection, because an unviable question is the failure mode that cannot be recovered. Collection needs lab access, which means fitting around the school's own schedule and often around other students using the same apparatus. Processing and writing then need a clear fortnight, and students almost never give themselves one.

In Chemistry specifically, the design trap is choosing a reaction whose rate or yield cannot be measured accurately enough with school equipment to show a relationship. A student who titrates to a colour change by eye and reports differences smaller than their own uncertainty has done real work with no analysable outcome. Spotting that before the practical, not after, is the whole value of a feasibility conversation.

The boundary is firm and it is stated to the student on day one. A tutor may teach experimental design, ask whether a method will produce usable data, explain uncertainty and significant figures, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write, draft or restructure the investigation, the Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay. The IB treats that as malpractice and the consequence falls on the candidate.

sections.heading: What an evening of Chemistry costs in this market
paragraphs: Take the cheapest end first, because that is where most families start looking. Budget online tuition from university-student tutors is advertised in Dubai from around AED 33 to AED 65 per hour — Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52, EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65 — and sits in a band running up to roughly AED 150. At that price a session is homework supervision. It will keep a student moving through set work and it will not, as a rule, diagnose why their Reactivity 2 answers are losing marks.

One step up, a qualified subject tutor working online is published at around AED 150 to AED 300 per hour, with Unitors quoting IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. This is the band where a DP Chemistry specialist becomes realistic for Standard Level topic teaching. Above that, IB and IGCSE specialists run roughly AED 200 to AED 450 and beyond, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate putting the specialist exam-year band at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Premium named provision reaches AED 650, as BartyED publishes.

In-home visits are a separate band: Bestimate puts them at AED 180 to AED 350 per hour and independent home tutors at AED 200 to AED 500. Monthly packages circulating in this market include online bundles near AED 799 for eight sessions and in-home bundles of AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Compare the in-home and online figures at the same quality tier and the difference is the journey.

For an Al Quoz 4 household the practical question is what the weekly evening is worth. One session a week at mid-market online rates is roughly AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month on Bestimate's estimates; specialist exam-year support runs AED 1,000 to over AED 2,000. None of these are IB Gram prices — we start with a free trial lesson and price the actual requirement afterwards. Knowing the bands first means a quote can be judged rather than accepted.

sections.heading: Ramadan, mock weeks and the holidays nobody plans for
paragraphs: A Chemistry plan that runs from September to the May session will meet three interruptions, and all three are predictable. The first is the mock window, when schools pull students out of normal teaching for a week or two of papers. Tuition during mocks is usually wasted on new content and valuable on technique, so the sensible move is to pause topic work and spend the sessions reviewing scripts as they come back marked.

The second is Ramadan. School days shorten, routines move, and many families in Al Quoz 4 prefer sessions after Iftar. Tutors working online can accommodate a later evening without the journey that would make it impractical in person. The useful planning point is that the shortened school day frees up earlier afternoon slots too, so a family that normally sits at 17:00 sometimes gains a 15:30 option for a few weeks.

The third is the term break and the long summer. Breaks are where the heavy lifting fits: organic mechanisms, a full past paper under timed conditions, the sustained catch-up that cannot be done in a Tuesday hour. Families who use one week of a break for three ninety-minute Chemistry sessions usually gain more than from a month of term-time evenings, simply because the student is not tired.

For students sitting Cambridge or Pearson qualifications on the way into or alongside the Diploma, the series matter. Cambridge International runs June and November for UAE candidates — the February and March series is offered to India only and has no place in a UAE plan. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. Check the live official timetable; entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers.

sections.heading: KHDA, mandatory subjects and the rest of your child's timetable
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes reports on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. For a Chemistry question the useful part is never the headline band but the subject-level commentary, which sometimes says plainly that science teaching is stronger in some year groups than others.

KHDA also sets requirements that sit alongside the licensed international curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes for both groups prohibited. Instructional time for mandatory subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met.

This matters to a Chemistry schedule in a mundane way: these subjects occupy real timetable space, and a DP student carrying them alongside six Diploma subjects and the core has less homework capacity than a parent assumes. When a family tells us their child has no time for Chemistry practice between sessions, the timetable is often the reason rather than motivation.

On context for spend: Dubai's private sector had 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, and KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year. IB accounts for 7% of private enrolment in the emirate, which is why Diploma Chemistry specialists are a thin market locally. IB Gram holds no status with KHDA or any other regulator, and no tutoring service should suggest otherwise.

sections.heading: Permits, and four questions to ask before you agree a slot
paragraphs: Tutoring in the UAE requires a permit. The private tuition work permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is handled by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its app, website or e-services. Eligible applicants range from registered school teachers and government or private-sector employees to unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18.

Those offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published — Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify amounts — so a figure circulating online should be treated as unverified. The permit also carries a code of conduct, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school.

Four questions are worth asking any Chemistry tutor before agreeing an evening. Which groupings have you taught at Higher Level, and how recently? How would you check whether my child's investigation can produce measurable results? What will you do with a draft, and what will you refuse to do? And do you hold the MoHRE private tuition permit? Clear answers to those four tell you more than any testimonial.

Our own honest caveat concerns availability. The 17:00 to 19:00 weekday window is the busiest two hours in this business, and a narrow request — Higher Level organic mechanisms, Tuesdays only, starting next week — sometimes cannot be met immediately. We say so rather than filling the slot with a generalist, and the free trial lesson exists so that the judgement about fit sits with the parent after watching a tutor teach.

faqs.question: What time can Chemistry lessons start on a school night in Al Quoz 4?
faqs.answer: Seventeen hundred is the earliest reliably workable slot, and 17:30 is more comfortable. Buses into Al Quoz 4 arrive between roughly 15:00 and 16:15 depending on whether the school sits in Al Safa, Jumeirah, Al Barsha or Al Sufouh, with the Al Barsha routes consistently latest. A student who walks in at 16:10 needs twenty minutes and something to eat before equilibrium calculations are worth attempting. Because lessons are delivered live online, there is no tutor journey to add on top, so the agreed slot stays the actual slot.

faqs.question: Will a Chemistry tutor come to our home in Al Quoz 4?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service is available only in India. Chemistry sessions for Al Quoz 4 families are delivered live over video, one-to-one, with a shared whiteboard and a camera on the student's written working. For a scheduling-led problem this is the advantage rather than the compromise: the thirty to forty minutes a tutor would spend crossing Dubai in the late afternoon disappears, along with the risk of losing half a lesson to traffic.

faqs.question: Which schools do Al Quoz 4 students usually attend?
faqs.answer: Three clusters. The nearest is Al Safa, Al Manara and Jumeirah, which mixes British-curriculum schools running IGCSE into A Level with IB continuum schools. The second is Al Barsha and Al Sufouh, reached along Al Khail Road or Sheikh Zayed Road, which carries several IB Diploma schools. The third is Umm Suqeim and the coast, a short run west. The practical consequence is that there is no shared Chemistry timetable in this neighbourhood, so group tuition organised by location rarely works.

faqs.question: How is DP Chemistry organised in the current syllabus?
faqs.answer: Around two ideas rather than a topic list. Structure 1 to 3 covers models of the particulate nature of matter, models of bonding and structure, and classification of matter including organic families and spectroscopy. Reactivity 1 to 3 covers what drives reactions, how much and how fast and how far, and the mechanisms of chemical change. Assessment is Paper 1 with a multiple-choice and a data-based section, Paper 2, and the internally assessed scientific investigation worth 20% of the grade at both levels.

faqs.question: Marks keep going on curly-arrow notation in Reactivity 3 — is that fixable?
faqs.answer: Usually notation rather than understanding. Curly arrows drawn from the wrong origin, lone pairs left off, intermediates not shown, charges omitted — each costs marks even when the student can describe the mechanism correctly out loud. It is a drawing discipline and it responds to short repeated practice rather than re-reading notes. A tutor marking ten mechanisms against the published expectations in one session usually produces more improvement than a month of reading, because the errors are specific and repeat.

faqs.question: When should we start working on the Chemistry investigation?
faqs.answer: Earlier than feels necessary, and the date to work back from is the school's internal deadline rather than anything the IB publishes. Schools around Al Quoz 4 set that deadline weeks apart, with the Al Barsha-direction schools often earliest. The research question needs settling well before data collection, because an unviable question is the one failure that cannot be recovered. Collection depends on lab access, and processing and writing need a clear fortnight that students rarely allow themselves.

faqs.question: Is cheap online tutoring worth trying for DP Chemistry first?
faqs.answer: It depends what the problem is. Budget online tuition in Dubai is advertised from around AED 33 to AED 65 an hour by Tutopiya and EdFlik, in a band reaching roughly AED 150. At that rate you are buying homework supervision, which genuinely helps a student who is capable but disorganised. It will not usually diagnose why Reactivity 2 answers are losing marks. If the mock came back below the predicted grade, the specialist band at AED 200 to AED 450 is where the diagnosis lives.

faqs.question: Does the Ramadan timetable shift our Chemistry slot later in the evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the clearer advantages of online delivery. School days shorten through Ramadan, routines shift, and many Al Quoz 4 families prefer a post-Iftar slot. With no tutor journey involved, a later evening costs nothing to arrange. The shortened school day also frees up earlier afternoons for a few weeks, so some families temporarily gain a mid-afternoon option they do not have in a normal term. We agree the Ramadan pattern in advance rather than improvising week by week.

faqs.question: Can a tutor check my child's investigation before submission?
faqs.answer: A tutor can read a draft the student has written and give feedback on it, criterion by criterion, in writing the student can take to their school supervisor. What a tutor cannot do is write, draft or restructure the report, and the same applies to an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay. That line is stated to the student in the first session. IB academic-honesty rules treat a breach as malpractice, and the consequence falls on the candidate, not the tutor.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does DP Chemistry usually need?
faqs.answer: One standing weekly session suits most of the year, with bursts of two when the investigation needs attention or mocks are close. The pattern that works best for Al Quoz 4 families is often a ninety-minute weekend session for mechanism work or a full timed paper, plus a shorter weekday hour for consolidation. Weeks where the student is collecting data in the school lab sometimes need none at all. A plan that bends at those points survives; a rigid one quietly stops.

faqs.question: Does the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education timetable affect Chemistry time?
faqs.answer: It affects homework capacity, which parents often overlook. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA calculates mandatory instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit with separate classes required for Arabs and non-Arabs in several of them. A Diploma student carrying these alongside six subjects and the core has less free study time than a timetable summary suggests. When a student seems not to be practising, the schedule is often the reason.

faqs.question: Is online Chemistry teaching a problem for practical work?
faqs.answer: Not for the parts a tutor contributes. The practical itself happens at school with the school's apparatus, and no visiting tutor brings a laboratory either. What a tutor adds is experimental design, a judgement on whether a measurement can produce an analysable range, uncertainty treatment, and processing the raw data. All four work better on a shared spreadsheet and whiteboard than on a dining table. A camera on the student's written calculations covers the rest.

faqs.question: Which documents help a Chemistry tutor most in week one?
faqs.answer: A marked topic test or mock, the school's topic list or scheme of work, the investigation deadline if one is set, and your child's realistic arrival time home. The marked script matters most, because it shows whether marks went on content, on arithmetic, on command-term reading or on timing, and those need four different plans. The arrival time matters second, because it determines which tutors can be offered at all for a weekday slot.

faqs.question: Which exam series applies if my child also sits Cambridge subjects?
faqs.answer: June and November. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only, so it has no place in a UAE plan. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November; its November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Every Cambridge centre sits in one of six administrative zones and must use its own zone's timetable.

intro.heading: Is there anybody near Al Qusais who actually knows this course? The honest answer
paragraphs: Parents in Al Qusais do not usually start by asking about pedagogy. They ask a supply question: is there someone within twenty minutes of Damascus Street who genuinely knows IB Diploma Chemistry, as opposed to someone who can explain chemistry. The two are not the same, and the gap between them is where most of the money spent on chemistry tutoring in this city disappears. So this page answers the supply question directly, gives you the means to test any tutor you find, and states what happens when the right person is not available.

The honest position is this. Chemistry is a common enough subject that general science tutoring is easy to buy anywhere in Dubai. Chemistry at Diploma Higher Level, under the guide whose first examinations fell in 2025, taught by someone who has marked a scientific investigation against the published criteria and worked through organic reaction mechanisms with a Year 13 - that is a narrower pool than any area-based search will show you. Filter by distance from Al Qusais and you are choosing from whoever lives nearby. Filter by course and level, and the pool is the whole Gulf evening.

There is a specific reason the course knowledge matters more in chemistry than in most subjects right now. The current guide reorganised the whole syllabus into six themes - three under Structure and three under Reactivity - replacing the older numbered topic list that almost every set of notes, revision site and second-hand resource on the internet is still written against. A tutor can explain bonding beautifully and still be navigating by a map that no longer matches your child's assessment. The content is not wrong; the organisation, the emphasis and the paper structure are.

The second reason is the investigation. A fifth of the chemistry grade is a single piece of coursework the student designs, runs and writes, marked against four criteria. A tutor who has never seen one marked gives generous, encouraging feedback on a draft that would score in the middle band, and the student finds out in Year 13. Asking whether a tutor has marked against the descriptors is a more useful question than asking about their degree, and it is the one almost nobody asks.

IB Gram delivers chemistry to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India, and we say so before anybody spends anything rather than afterwards. What that buys an Al Qusais family is a match on the level and the component rather than on driving distance - and a stated answer, with a date, if the right specialist is not free in your window.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-qusais.subjectsIntro: Families looking for an IB chemistry tutor in Al Qusais describe one of a handful of problems once a tutor is on the call. These are the ones that come up most, and how hard each is to staff.

subjects.name: Models of the particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Atomic structure, electron configurations, ionisation energy trends and the mole concept. Easy to find help for and easy to teach badly: students who can recite configurations often cannot explain a first ionisation energy anomaly, which is exactly what Paper 2 asks them to do in words.

subjects.name: Models of bonding and structure
subjects.description: Ionic, covalent and metallic bonding, intermolecular forces, VSEPR shapes and hybridisation at Higher Level. The marks sit in justification rather than identification - naming a shape earns little without the electron-domain reasoning that produced it.

subjects.name: Classification of matter
subjects.description: Periodicity, the behaviour of metals and non-metals, and an introduction to organic structure and spectroscopy. Students treat this theme as revision of IGCSE and then lose marks on trend explanations that require the bonding model from Structure 2 to be applied properly.

subjects.name: What drives chemical reactions?
subjects.description: Enthalpy, Hess cycles, bond enthalpies, entropy and Gibbs energy at Higher Level. Sign errors in energy cycles are the most predictable mark loss in the whole course, and they respond to drilling rather than to re-teaching the theory.

subjects.name: How much, how fast and how far?
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, yield, rates, equilibrium, acids and bases, and the quantitative treatment of each at Higher Level. This theme carries the heaviest calculation load on the course and rewards method discipline: unrounded intermediate values, units carried through, and a stated assumption.

subjects.name: What are the mechanisms of chemical change?
subjects.description: Redox, electrochemistry and organic mechanisms, extended substantially at Higher Level. This is the hardest theme to staff properly, because teaching nucleophilic substitution as a diagram to memorise rather than as a sequence with reasons is the default failure of a non-specialist.

subjects.name: Organic reasoning and synthesis routes
subjects.description: Functional group interconversion, reagent and condition selection, and multi-step synthesis. Students lose marks by producing a correct product with impossible conditions. A tutor who cannot explain why a particular reagent is chosen will not fix this, and most generalists cannot.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: One investigation worth a fifth of the grade, marked against research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. A tutor may teach the criteria, interrogate the research question, flag an unpropagated uncertainty and mark a draft against the descriptors. A tutor may not design it, write it or supply data.

sections.heading: What chemistry coverage really looks like from Al Qusais, including the fallback
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is why it is worth publishing one. Tutoring supply is not uniform across levels and components. Standard Level chemistry content is widely available and easy to staff at short notice. Higher Level content is narrower. Higher Level organic mechanisms and investigation marking are narrower again, and those two are precisely what families in Al Qusais most often need by Year 13.

The distortion that distance-based searching introduces is worth naming. Al Qusais sits on the Deira side, a long way from the parts of New Dubai where most independent tutors advertise, and the evening traffic between them is the worst in the week. So a parent filtering by proximity gets a short list that is short for geographic reasons rather than because the city lacks chemistry teachers. Filtering by level and component instead produces a longer list, all of it reachable over video at the time the family actually has.

Our commitment is to state the position at the match stage. If a Higher Level specialist who has marked investigations is free in your window, you get one. If not, you are told at that point, before any payment, with three options set out: a different time slot with the right specialist, a tutor with adjacent expertise starting now while we hold the specialist slot, or a wait with a date against it. Every one of those is better for a family than a confident match that quietly is not one.

What we will not do is place a Standard Level generalist with a Higher Level student, or a biology graduate with a chemistry mechanism problem, and allow a term to pass before anybody notices. That failure is invisible for weeks - the lessons feel fine, the student is busy, nothing is obviously wrong - and it surfaces in a mock. sections.heading: Ten questions that reveal whether a tutor knows this chemistry course
paragraphs: Use these on any chemistry tutor in Dubai, including ours. They take ten minutes on a first call and they are far more informative than a list of qualifications, because each one has an answer that only somebody who has taught the current course recently can give. None of them requires you to understand chemistry yourself - you are listening for specificity and for willingness to say what they do not know.

Start with structure. Which of the six themes have you taught most recently? A tutor working from the current guide will name them as Structure and Reactivity themes; one working from older material will talk about numbered topics and options. Then: how is the course assessed? The answer should include two papers, with data-based questions inside Paper 1 and the investigation at a fifth of the grade. Then: what do you do differently for Higher Level? Depth within each theme rather than extra topics at the end is the right shape.

Move to the investigation. Have you marked a draft against the published criteria, and what band did it score? A tutor who has will immediately talk about research design and evaluation as the weak points; one who has not will talk about how good the student's writing was. Then ask what they would refuse to do on an investigation. The right answer is explicit: they will not design it, write it, supply data or rewrite it to completion, because the work must be the student's own.

Finish on teaching. How would you teach nucleophilic substitution to a student who has memorised the diagram but cannot predict a new case? Ask them to explain a first ionisation energy anomaly in words. Ask what they do about sign errors in Hess cycles. Ask what they would do in week four if nothing had shifted. And ask whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit - it is granted free of charge for two years, so there is no cost reason for a working tutor not to have one.
