sections.heading: The six themes, mapped: where an Al Qusais student is most likely to be losing marks
paragraphs: The current chemistry guide organises everything into three Structure themes and three Reactivity themes, and the reorganisation is more than cosmetic. Structure 1 covers models of the particulate nature of matter - atomic structure, electron configuration, ionisation energy and the mole. Structure 2 covers models of bonding and structure, from ionic and covalent through intermolecular forces to shapes and, at Higher Level, hybridisation. Structure 3 covers classification of matter: periodicity, metals and non-metals, and the entry point to organic structure and spectroscopy.

Reactivity 1 asks what drives chemical reactions - enthalpy, energy cycles, and at Higher Level entropy and Gibbs energy. Reactivity 2 asks how much, how fast and how far: stoichiometry, yield, kinetics, equilibrium, and acids and bases with their quantitative treatment. Reactivity 3 asks what the mechanisms of chemical change are, covering redox, electrochemistry and organic mechanisms, with substantial Higher Level extension.

Marks cluster predictably. Sign errors in energy cycles under Reactivity 1 are the most repeatable loss on the whole course and respond to drilling rather than explanation. Justification marks under Structure 2 are lost by students who name a shape without the electron-domain reasoning. Calculation discipline under Reactivity 2 - unrounded intermediates, units carried, assumptions stated - costs marks on every paper it touches. And Reactivity 3 organic work separates students who learned mechanisms as sequences with reasons from those who learned them as pictures.

One marked paper usually identifies which of those four is the dominant problem, and it is rarely all of them. That is why we open a chemistry engagement with a diagnostic rather than with a plan, and why the written list that comes out of it is worth keeping whoever teaches afterwards. Confirm the current syllabus structure with your child's IB coordinator, who holds the published guide; we do not reproduce or supply board documents, past papers or mark schemes.

sections.heading: Organic chemistry: the theme that decides a Higher Level grade
paragraphs: If an Al Qusais family is going to buy specialist rather than general chemistry tutoring, this is the theme to buy it for. Organic chemistry under Reactivity 3 is the clearest dividing line between a tutor who knows the course and one who knows chemistry, because the default non-specialist approach - present the mechanism as a diagram, have the student reproduce it - produces a student who can answer the question they have seen and nothing else.

What the examination actually rewards is prediction. Given an unfamiliar substrate and a reagent, what happens and why? That requires the student to hold three things together: what makes a site electron-rich or electron-poor, what the reagent is capable of, and what the conditions permit. A student taught the reasoning can handle a case they have never met. A student taught the picture cannot, and no amount of additional diagrams fixes it.

The second common loss is synthesis routes. Students produce a target molecule by a sequence that is chemically sensible on paper and impossible in practice, usually because a condition would destroy a functional group introduced two steps earlier. Teaching route planning as a backwards exercise from the target, with conditions checked at each step, is a specific skill and takes a handful of sessions rather than a term.

The third is nomenclature and structural drawing under time pressure. Marks lost to an ambiguous skeletal structure or a mislabelled stereocentre are not conceptual failures, and they are among the cheapest marks on the paper to recover. Together, those three - reasoning rather than recall, route planning backwards, and clean drawing under time - usually account for most of the gap between a 5 and a 7 in Higher Level chemistry for the students we see from this part of Dubai.

sections.heading: The investigation, the honesty boundary, and what this SERP is selling
paragraphs: A fifth of the chemistry grade is one investigation the student designs, runs and writes, marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. In chemistry specifically the most common fatal error happens before any writing: a research question whose independent variable cannot be varied meaningfully with school equipment, or whose dependent variable cannot be measured with an uncertainty small enough to reveal the relationship. Titration-based investigations fail this way constantly, and so do rate studies with no reliable way to fix temperature.

Screening the question is therefore the highest-value hour on the component, and it costs one session at the start of the process rather than a rescue in Year 13. After that, the pattern of lost marks is consistent: uncertainties recorded but never propagated into the processed results, conclusions that restate the trend without comparing it against accepted chemistry, and evaluations that list generic apologies about human error rather than identifying the limitation that actually mattered.

The boundary a tutor holds is not a technicality. Under IB academic-honesty rules the investigation must be the student's own work. A tutor may teach the criteria, interrogate the research question, explain why an uncertainty must be propagated, point out that a conclusion is unjustified, mark a draft against the descriptors and say plainly that a section is below standard. A tutor may not design the investigation, write any part of it, produce data, or redraft it to completion.

This matters because the search result you arrived from contains sellers who do otherwise. Research into this market found a provider offering completed Internal Assessments at a published price. That is an academic-integrity breach and an IB malpractice trigger, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the seller - potentially the loss of the diploma. We will not do it, we will say so to a student who asks, and we think a parent is entitled to know that the option exists in this market so they can recognise it.

sections.heading: What it costs, and what the cheap end of this market cannot do for chemistry
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates give a parent something checkable to reason from. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted across the market at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB tuition from AED 200. Named IB specialists sit higher - roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai table putting specialist exam-year support in the same region - and BartyED published AED 650 at the premium end. All figures were read in October 2026 and belong to the providers that published them.

The budget end deserves a specific warning on a chemistry page. Platforms staffed largely by university students advertise from the low double digits: Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52 an hour, EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. For IGCSE chemistry revision or Structure 1 content that can be reasonable value. For Higher Level organic mechanisms, or for marking an investigation against descriptors, it generally is not, because those are not things a capable chemistry undergraduate has necessarily done.

In-home visits are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel, with Bestimate showing AED 180 to 350 and independent tutors asking AED 200 to 500. The structural problem for an Al Qusais family is not the rate but what the rate implies about choice: at that price, the tutor has to be someone willing to drive to Al Qusais in the evening peak, and that constraint has nothing to do with whether they know Reactivity 3.

None of these are our prices and we publish no rate card on these pages, because the honest number depends on the level, the component and the weeks remaining. The free trial lesson is one lesson with the matched tutor, fee discussed afterwards. For chemistry we would spend that lesson on a mechanism the student has not seen or a draft section of the investigation, because that is where the difference between a specialist and a generalist becomes visible in twenty minutes.

sections.heading: Verification: permits, the own-teacher boundary, and what the regulator does
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permit-regulated, and a parent in Al Qusais is entitled to ask about it before paying anybody. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published - Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties - so treat any figure circulating online as unverified. A tutor who becomes evasive on this question has given you useful information at no cost.

There is a second boundary that families sometimes walk into innocently. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct has been reported as barring the same arrangement. Verify the current wording against the authority's own policy document, but the principle holds across the Emirates: paying your child's own classroom teacher privately is the wrong arrangement however convenient it looks.

Dubai's private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific authorisation with initial approval, a completion window and annual renewal. IB Gram holds no such permit and no approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. We describe what these bodies do; we do not claim their endorsement.

Taught that way, a student handles cases they have never met. It usually takes a handful of sessions rather than a term, and it is worth buying a specialist for.

faqs.question: What is the most common reason a chemistry investigation scores badly?
faqs.answer: A research question that cannot produce usable data, chosen before anyone checked. If the independent variable cannot be varied meaningfully with school equipment, or the dependent variable cannot be measured with a small enough uncertainty to reveal the relationship, no amount of good writing recovers it. Titration-based studies and rate studies with no reliable temperature control fail this way constantly. Screening the question in one session at the start of the process is the highest-value hour on the entire component.

faqs.question: Can a tutor legally help with my child's chemistry Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the four assessment criteria, interrogate the research question before any data is collected, explain why an uncertainty must be propagated into the processed results, point out that a conclusion is not justified by the data, mark a draft against the published descriptors and say plainly that a section is below standard. A tutor may not design the investigation, write any part of it, produce data or rewrite it to completion. The work must be the student's own under IB academic-honesty rules, and a breach puts the student's diploma at risk.

faqs.question: Some Dubai providers offer finished Internal Assessments. Why not use one?
faqs.answer: Because the consequence lands on your child rather than on the seller. Research into this market found a provider publishing a price for completed Internal Assessments. Submitting work that is not the student's own is an academic-integrity breach under IB rules and a malpractice trigger, with outcomes that can include the loss of the diploma. The fact that it is openly for sale in this search result does not make it survivable. We will not provide it, and we tell students who ask exactly why.

faqs.question: What should an Al Qusais family expect to pay for IB chemistry support?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates, read in October 2026: a qualified subject tutor online is quoted at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IB tuition from AED 200. Named IB specialists run roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 at the premium end. In-home visits are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel. Those belong to the providers that published them; we quote against level, component and weeks remaining rather than from a rate card.

faqs.question: Is a budget online chemistry tutor ever the right choice?
faqs.answer: For some things, yes. Platforms staffed largely by university students advertise from around AED 33 to 65 an hour, and for IGCSE revision, Structure 1 content or supervised practice that can be sensible value. For Higher Level organic mechanisms or for marking an investigation against descriptors it generally is not, because a capable chemistry undergraduate has not necessarily done either. Spend the budget band on volume and the specialist band on the two or three things that actually decide the grade, rather than averaging across everything.

faqs.question: We came from Coordinated Sciences rather than separate chemistry. Is Higher Level realistic?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, with the gap named at the start rather than discovered in November. A Coordinated Sciences student has met less chemistry content and fewer practicals than one who sat 0620 or 4CH1 separately, so the bridging job is larger but still a defined size - typically mechanism-level organic reasoning, quantitative work with uncertainty, and the written justification the Diploma expects. The summer before Year 12 is the right window for it. Tell us which route your child took in the first message and we plan against it.

faqs.question: What happens if no Higher Level chemistry specialist is free in our slot?
faqs.answer: You hear it at the match stage, before any payment, with three options set out. A different time slot with the right specialist, which usually means moving an hour earlier or later in the Gulf evening. A tutor with adjacent expertise starting now while we hold the specialist slot for you. Or a wait with a date attached, so you can decide rather than guess. Demand concentrates in the same two evening hours and fills before mocks and around investigation deadlines, so the honest answer is sometimes a wait.

faqs.question: Do you provide in-home chemistry tutoring in Al Qusais or anywhere in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. Every UAE lesson we arrange is one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service we operate only in India. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch in the Emirates. The Dubai market does supply in-home chemistry tutors at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the fee. The trade-off worth seeing clearly is that at that price the tutor must be someone willing to drive to Al Qusais in the evening peak, which has nothing to do with whether they know Reactivity 3.

faqs.question: Should I ask a chemistry tutor in Dubai about their tutoring permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the answer should be straightforward. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with a two-working-day completion time through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service. Because it costs nothing, a working tutor has no financial reason to be without one. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so disregard any specific amount you see quoted online.

intro.heading: Chemistry is the subject the school run punishes most
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject suffers from a tired student, but chemistry suffers worst, and it is worth being precise about why. Chemistry is a two-layer subject: a conceptual layer that has to be understood, and a computational layer that has to be practised until it is automatic. Mole calculations, equilibrium expressions and energetics arithmetic are not things a student thinks through from first principles in an examination. They are things a student does, quickly, while thinking about something else. That kind of fluency is built by frequent short practice, and frequent short practice is exactly what a long school run destroys.

Al Rashidiya makes that concrete. The district sits between Dubai International Airport, Al Garhoud and Nad Al Hamar, and it contains no secondary school. Its Diploma students travel: a short run north into the Garhoud cluster, or east along Algeria Street and Tripoli Street towards Mirdif, where the nearest IB continuum provision sits. The eastern bus routes collect across several communities before heading back, and forty minutes once school finishes is an ordinary outcome rather than a bad day. A student home at 4.15pm, hot and hungry, is not going to balance a redox equation at 4.30pm.

So the scheduling question is not when is the tutor free. It is what the evening can actually hold. For most families on the eastern routes that means a lesson at 5.30pm or later, with the practice it sets placed on a different evening rather than on the same one. For Garhoud-direction families a 4.30pm slot is genuinely holdable. Getting this right is worth more to a chemistry grade over two years than any difference in tutor rate.

IB Gram's contribution is to take its own travel out of the equation. Lessons are one to one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, so nobody is leaving Mirdif at 4pm hoping to reach your gate by 4.30pm. Home visits are a service offered only in India; there is no UAE version. That removes the half of the scheduling problem that is nobody's to control and leaves the half you can measure with a stopwatch for a week.

There is a second reason the hour matters in chemistry specifically. The subject is sequential in a way that is unusually unforgiving: bonding sits on atomic structure, energetics sits on the mole, equilibrium sits on rates, and organic mechanisms sit on everything before them. A fortnight lost in October is not a fortnight of content to recover later; it is a foundation the next three topics are built on, and by February the student cannot tell you where the trouble started. A weekly hour that reliably happens is therefore worth far more than a longer hour that happens when the evening allows it.

The rest of this page covers what the current chemistry course actually contains, what an evening in this district can realistically absorb, the five kinds of mole calculation and where each one fails, the scientific investigation and when it has to start, and what the Dubai market charges with every figure attributed so you can check it.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-rashidiya.programmesIntro: Chemistry trouble usually arrives in one of two places: the mole, or the transition from a recall-based course to one that asks why. These are the stages we cover either side of Diploma chemistry.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Chemistry
programmes.description: Available at Standard and Higher Level. The current guide is organised around Structure, covering the particulate nature of matter, bonding and structure, and classification of matter, and Reactivity, covering what drives reactions, how much and how fast and how far, and the mechanisms of chemical change. Assessment is written papers plus a scientific investigation carrying twenty per cent. Confirm current detail with your school's IB coordinator.
programmes.countryNote: An Al Rashidiya student sitting DP chemistry is most likely in the Garhoud or Mirdif clusters, where Diploma cohorts are small by Dubai standards. One chemistry teacher commonly carries both levels, which gives continuity and leaves very little room to recover a topic missed during a travel week. That is the specific gap weekly one-to-one support fills in this district.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Chemistry taught inside an integrated sciences course in most schools, assessed against criteria A to D. MYP builds investigation design and evaluation well, and builds the quantitative habit less well, because criterion-based tasks rarely demand the kind of repeated calculation Diploma chemistry assumes from the first weeks of DP1.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-DP chemistry step is the commonest reason a confident middle-school scientist stalls in DP1 locally. The content is reachable; the arithmetic is not, because converting between mass, moles and concentration at speed was never drilled. A short bridging block in the summer before DP1 is worth more than a term of content teaching afterwards.

programmes.name: IGCSE Chemistry into Diploma Chemistry
programmes.description: The crossing most Dubai students make, given that UK-curriculum schools dominate enrolment. Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 leave students solid on the reactivity series, on tests for ions and on standard equations, and short on equilibrium reasoning, on energetics as a quantitative subject and on explaining a mechanism rather than reciting a product.
programmes.countryNote: A student moving from a British-curriculum school in Mirdif or Al Qusais into a Diploma Programme in Al Garhoud is a routine local case. The three things that reliably need building in that first term are moles at speed, the language of equilibrium, and the discipline of explaining why a reaction goes rather than stating that it does.

programmes.name: Medicine, dentistry and science routes
programmes.description: What Higher Level chemistry is usually for. Medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, biochemistry and chemical engineering commonly expect it, frequently alongside biology or mathematics at a specified level. Requirements vary between universities and between admission cycles, so the only reliable method is reading each specific course page rather than relying on a general rule.
programmes.countryNote: Check requirements directly with every university your child is considering, UAE institutions included, rather than trusting a summary. IB Gram does not perform, guarantee or accelerate Ministry of Education equivalency, and no verified IB points threshold for equivalency is published on ministry sources, so ask moe.gov.ae or your school registrar rather than any tutoring page.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-rashidiya.subjectsIntro: Chemistry marks leave from a short list of identifiable places, and most of them are computational rather than conceptual. These are the areas Al Rashidiya families ask about most.

subjects.name: Structure 1: models of the particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: The mole, atomic structure, electron configuration and the ideal gas treatment. This is where a Diploma chemistry grade is quietly decided, because every later calculation sits on mole fluency, and a student who is slow here is slow everywhere afterwards.

subjects.name: Structure 2: models of bonding and structure
subjects.description: Ionic, covalent and metallic bonding, intermolecular forces and the structure-property link. Students lose marks by naming a force without explaining its consequence, and at Higher Level by not distinguishing clearly between the strength of a bond and the strength of the forces between molecules.

subjects.name: Structure 3: classification of matter
subjects.description: Periodicity, trends down a group and across a period, and the chemistry of transition elements at Higher Level. Reliable marks are available here because the patterns are finite, and they are routinely lost to explanations that describe a trend rather than accounting for it.

subjects.name: Reactivity 1: what drives chemical reactions
subjects.description: Energetics and thermodynamics: enthalpy changes, Hess cycles, bond enthalpies and, at Higher Level, entropy and spontaneity. The common loss is sign errors in a Hess cycle, which is an arithmetic discipline rather than a conceptual gap and responds quickly to practice.

subjects.name: Reactivity 2: how much, how fast and how far
subjects.description: Reaction rates, equilibrium and acid-base chemistry, with equilibrium constants and buffers treated far more quantitatively at Higher Level. Equilibrium is the single biggest conceptual hurdle in the course, because it requires reasoning about a dynamic system rather than a fixed outcome.

subjects.name: Reactivity 3: mechanisms of chemical change
subjects.description: Redox, electrochemistry and organic mechanisms. Organic chemistry rewards memory and pattern recognition; redox rewards a method followed every time. Students who half-learn both lose marks in two places rather than one, so sequencing matters here.

subjects.name: Mole calculations at speed
subjects.description: Mass to moles, moles to concentration, gas volumes, limiting reagents and percentage yield. Five related calculations that must become automatic. This is the highest-yield tutoring work in the subject and the part students most consistently decline to practise.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry and mechanisms
subjects.description: Functional groups, reaction types and, at Higher Level, curly-arrow mechanisms and stereochemistry. Marks are lost to incomplete arrows and to missing intermediates rather than to not knowing the product, which makes it a drawing discipline as much as a chemical one.

subjects.name: Data analysis and uncertainty
subjects.description: Percentage uncertainty, propagation through a titration calculation, and significant figures justified rather than copied. Examined inside the papers and central to the investigation, and taught properly by neither IGCSE nor either mathematics course.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: An independent piece of experimental or data-based chemistry carrying twenty per cent of the grade, assessed against published criteria. A tutor may teach the criteria, question a draft and point out an unsupported conclusion. A tutor may not write, draft or complete any part of it.

subjects.name: Extended-response technique
subjects.description: Answering the command term, writing an explanation rather than a description, and using chemical language precisely. A term of weekly correction here moves marks without covering any new chemistry, which makes it the cheapest work available late in the course.

subjects.name: IGCSE chemistry foundations
subjects.description: Where a DP1 problem usually began. Mole arithmetic that was always done with a calculator and a formula triangle, and equations balanced by inspection rather than by method, are the two habits most often worth unpicking in the first three sessions.

sections.heading: What a forty-minute bus actually does to a chemistry evening
paragraphs: Take a student at a Mirdif school, living in Al Rashidiya, on a collecting bus. School finishes, the bus loads, it works its way through several communities and back along Algeria Street, and the student is dropped near home somewhere around four. Add the walk and the bag on the floor and it is 4.15pm. That is the actual start of the evening, and everything a family schedules has to fit after it.

What a fifteen-year-old can absorb in the first half hour of that evening is close to nothing, and chemistry is the subject least tolerant of being attempted there. A balanced redox half-equation or a limiting-reagent calculation needs working memory, and working memory is the first thing a hot bus takes. A lesson that begins at 4.30pm spends its first ten minutes on the student arriving in the room rather than in the chemistry, and over a term that is real money.

The table below is the version we schedule from. Notice what it does not say: it does not say teenagers are lazy or that families should try harder. It says an evening has a shape, and a chemistry plan that respects the shape delivers more than one that fights it. Garhoud-direction families get the easy version of this and should take it; eastern-route families should accept a later slot rather than a failing earlier one.

The honest conclusion for some households is that weekday evenings do not work at all. If your child is on an Al Warqa or Al Khawaneej route and home at half past four flattened, a weekend morning is the right purchase and the cost is a piece of the weekend. Most long-route families reach that conclusion anyway, usually after a term of trying the alternative.

sections.heading: What is actually in the chemistry course now
paragraphs: The current IB Chemistry guide is organised into two halves rather than the numbered-topic-plus-options arrangement some tutors will remember. Structure covers the particulate nature of matter, bonding and structure, and the classification of matter. Reactivity covers what drives chemical reactions, how much and how fast and how far, and the mechanisms of chemical change. Higher Level depth runs inside those topics rather than sitting in a separate block.

That structural point is the first test of a tutor. Somebody who has taught this course describes it in those terms without hesitating. Somebody working from an older syllabus describes numbered topics and an options paper, which will still be chemistry and will still spend your child's revision time on a structure they are not examined against.

Read the table with your child's current marks in mind. Strong on Structure and weak on Reactivity 2 is not a weak chemist; it is a student who has hit equilibrium, which asks for reasoning about a dynamic system rather than a fixed outcome and is the single biggest conceptual hurdle in the subject. That is specific and teachable, and a six-to-ten session block on it is a defensible purchase.

Confirm the current structure, topic content and weightings with your school's IB coordinator before planning around them. Subject guides are revised and a tutoring page is not a syllabus. We also do not reproduce or supply IB subject guides or past papers; those belong to the IB and reach you properly through the school.

sections.heading: The five mole calculations, and where each one fails
paragraphs: If a parent takes one practical thing from this page, take this. Almost every disappointing Diploma chemistry mark traces back to mole arithmetic that is understood but not automatic. The student can explain the method and cannot execute it in forty seconds, so a four-mark calculation eats three minutes and the paper runs out before the extended responses.

There are five related calculations that have to become reflexive, and they are listed in the table with the specific failure attached to each. The failures are not conceptual. They are procedural: a unit not converted, a ratio read off the wrong species, a yield compared against the wrong theoretical mass. Each one responds to repetition and to nothing else.

This is why the weekly rhythm on this page separates the lesson from the practice. Twenty minutes of mixed mole questions on a Tuesday and a Thursday builds fluency; ninety minutes the night before a test does not. A tutor can teach the method once and then spend a term checking that the practice is happening and correcting the pattern in the errors, which is unglamorous work and the highest-yield work available in the subject.

Ask any prospective chemistry tutor how they handle this. The answer tells you whether they have taught the course under examination conditions or only explained it. Somebody who has will talk about timing and about mixed practice sets. Somebody who has not will offer to explain moles again.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, and the term it has to start in
paragraphs: The investigation carries twenty per cent of the chemistry grade and is assessed against published criteria. The mark is largely decided before any writing happens, by the research question: one with too little chemistry in it, or with variables that cannot be measured properly in a school laboratory, has no route to the higher bands however well the report is written.

The timing matters more in this district than most, because the households here travel. A family with a parent on airport-adjacent shifts or frequent trips will lose a fortnight somewhere, and a fortnight lost from a last-minute investigation is fatal where the same fortnight lost from an early one is survivable. Starting the criteria conversation in DP1 is both cheaper and more robust.

Four sessions typically cover it: what the criteria actually reward, how to choose a question with measurable variables and real chemistry in it, how to treat uncertainty honestly rather than decoratively, and how to write an evaluation that identifies genuine limitations. After that the student works and the tutor responds to drafts with questions.

The boundary is absolute. A tutor may explain criteria, model method on a different investigation, question a draft and point out an unsupported conclusion. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or edit to completion any part of the submission. One page in the researched competitor set sells completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price; that is a malpractice route and the student carries the finding, not the seller. Ask to see the feedback: questions your child must answer are correct, sentences they could paste in are not.
bullets: The research question sets the mark ceiling; the writing cannot raise it afterwards

sections.heading: What a Diploma chemistry hour costs in this market
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages on these searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. Here is the dirham version, with each figure read on the provider's own public page so you can open it and check rather than take our word for it.

A parent choosing on budget usually works upward from the bottom. EdFlik advertises budget online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya's published panel starts lower again, which is a genuine service for MYP science consolidation and thin for Higher Level chemistry. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Named IB and IGCSE specialists run roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai table reaching the top of that band. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end.

The in-home band is separate and higher for a reason that has nothing to do with chemistry: AED 180 to 500 an hour, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor working online, because the rate carries a round trip through the Garhoud interchange or Algeria Street in the afternoon. Monthly packages seen locally run around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four in-home sessions of two hours, and those two numbers describe different products rather than different prices.

None of this is an IB Gram rate and we publish no rate card on these pages. The number for your child's level and arrangement comes out of the free trial lesson and the conversation after it. What the table gives you is a way to tell whether the quote in your inbox is inside the market or outside it.

sections.heading: Laboratory work, and what a tutor adds either side of the bench
paragraphs: Chemistry involves apparatus, and parents reasonably ask how that is handled when lessons are online. The answer is that the apparatus was always the school's responsibility. Your child's practical work, reagents, safety supervision and recorded results come from the school, and nobody is setting up a titration in an Al Rashidiya villa.

A tutor's contribution sits before and after. Before: designing a method that will actually produce usable data, deciding which variables to control and why, choosing a concentration range that gives readings worth plotting. After: handling the uncertainty, propagating it through the calculation, interpreting the gradient, and writing an evaluation that identifies real limitations instead of ritual ones. Both halves are screen work and both are better with the student's own data open on a shared screen.

The data-analysis part of the written assessment makes this concrete, because it asks students to work with experimental data they did not collect. A student who has spent a term interpreting results on a shared screen has exactly the habit that section rewards, which is one of several places where online delivery is an advantage rather than a compromise.

Where physical presence genuinely matters is a student with a diagnosed need requiring hands-on support. We will say so rather than take the booking and will point you towards a local provider with a verifiable MoHRE private tuition permit. IB Gram does not place tutors in UAE homes under any circumstances; home visits are an India-only service.

sections.heading: The calendar: Ramadan, holidays and travel weeks
paragraphs: A chemistry plan that ignores the shape of the UAE academic year loses weeks it never budgeted for, and in a fluency subject those weeks cost more than the sessions missed. Three periods need planning rather than improvising.

During Ramadan school days are shortened and household routines move towards the evening. A 5.30pm slot that works in October is usually wrong then, and a post-iftar lesson is usually right. Because no tutor is travelling, the change costs a message. Families who agree the shift before Ramadan starts keep their continuity; those who improvise tend to lose three or four weeks and restart from a worse position.

School holidays cut differently. A weekly slot limping through a holiday week with a travelling student is worth less than a short defined block on one topic used while there is no homework competing. For a DP1 student the strongest use of a Dubai winter or spring break is three or four sessions on equilibrium or on mole fluency, finished before term resumes.

Travel is a standing feature of this district, given how many households are airport-adjacent or travel frequently. Online lessons follow a student to another time zone if the slot moves, which no arrangement tied to an address can do. Send the dates in advance and sessions are moved rather than missed; the thing to avoid is letting a trip turn into a four-week gap, because in chemistry the restart costs more than the gap.

sections.heading: Starting, and the availability we will not pretend about
paragraphs: Send four things: the level, Standard or Higher; which topics the school has covered so far; a photograph of a marked test or mock; and the time your child is realistically through the door on a bad traffic afternoon. The fourth is the one families omit and the one that decides whether the arrangement is still running in February.

The trial lesson is free, runs about forty minutes on a past question, and is a lesson rather than a sales call. Your child works, the tutor teaches, and afterwards you receive a written read on whether the problem is mole fluency, a conceptual gap in a specific topic, or extended-response technique, with the number of weeks each implies. No card details are taken and nothing is owed if you stop there.

Sometimes the slot you need does not exist. Late-evening Gulf Standard Time hours fill first, weekend mornings fill during exam terms, and a Higher Level organic mechanisms specialist requested a fortnight before final papers may genuinely not be free. We will give a realistic match time rather than filling the hour with a general science tutor, because the wrong tutor in the right slot costs the fee and the weeks.

What we ask for is limited to what matching needs: level, topics covered, school if you want its sequence followed, and a contact for scheduling. We do not need a photograph of your child or a full grade history across every subject. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 governs the data we hold, and the privacy link on this page sets out what is kept and how to have it removed.

process.description: The lesson is one day and the twenty minutes of calculation practice is another, chosen because it is genuinely free. Chemistry fluency comes from frequency, so this step does as much work as the lesson itself and costs nothing.

faqs.question: What time can a chemistry lesson start if my child buses back from Mirdif?
faqs.answer: Plan 5.30pm. A collecting bus from a Mirdif school works through several communities and back along Algeria Street, so thirty-five to forty-five minutes once school finishes is ordinary and a student is home around 4.15pm. Add food and half an hour of decompression and a 4.30pm chemistry lesson is being taught to somebody whose working memory has not arrived yet. Families travelling the short run north to Al Garhoud are the exception and can usually hold 4.30pm through a full term.

faqs.question: Why does chemistry suffer more than other subjects from a late finish?
faqs.answer: Because it has a computational layer that has to be automatic rather than thought through. Mole conversions, equilibrium expressions and energetics arithmetic are executed under time pressure while the student is thinking about something else, and that kind of fluency needs working memory and frequent short practice. A tired student can still absorb a history argument; they cannot reliably balance a redox half-equation. That is why the slot and the separate practice evening matter more in this subject than in most.

faqs.question: How much practice does Diploma chemistry need between lessons?
faqs.answer: Twenty to thirty minutes of mixed calculation work on two separate evenings, rather than one long session before a test. Fluency comes from frequency, and mole arithmetic in particular only becomes automatic through repetition. The practice should be named specifically in the tutor's written note after each lesson, so it is checkable rather than aspirational, and it should sit on evenings that are genuinely free: not after a long fixture, not on the heaviest homework night of the week.

faqs.question: My child understands chemistry but runs out of time in the paper. What is wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost always mole fluency. A student who can explain the method but takes forty-five seconds rather than fifteen on each conversion spends three minutes on a four-mark calculation, and the extended responses at the end never get written. It presents as a time problem and it is a practice problem. Mixed sets of mass-to-moles, concentration, gas volume, limiting-reagent and percentage-yield questions, twice a week for a term, is the whole intervention, and it is unglamorous and reliable.

faqs.question: Which chemistry topic causes Higher Level students the most trouble?
faqs.answer: Reactivity 2, and equilibrium within it. Equilibrium asks a student to reason about a dynamic system where the forward and reverse processes continue, rather than about a reaction that finishes, and a great many students quietly carry a static mental model through the whole course. At Higher Level the quantitative treatment of equilibrium constants, buffers and pH work then compounds the problem. It is a specific, teachable hurdle rather than general weakness, and a six-to-ten session block on it is a defensible purchase.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a chemistry tutor knows the current course?
faqs.answer: Ask them to describe how the guide is organised. Somebody who has taught it will say Structure 1 to 3 and Reactivity 1 to 3, with Higher Level depth inside the topics. Somebody working from an older syllabus will describe numbered topics and an options paper. Both are chemists; only one is teaching the course your child is examined on. Then ask how they build mole fluency, and listen for whether the answer mentions timing and mixed practice sets or just offers to explain moles again.

faqs.question: Can chemistry really be taught well without a tutor in the laboratory?
faqs.answer: Yes, because the laboratory was always the school's job. Your child's practical work, reagents, safety supervision and recorded results come from school, and no tutor is running a titration in a Dubai villa. A tutor's value sits either side of the bench: designing a method that produces usable data and choosing what to control, then propagating uncertainty, interpreting the gradient and writing a real evaluation. Both halves are screen work, and the written assessment specifically rewards analysing data a student did not collect.

faqs.question: When should the chemistry investigation start?
faqs.answer: In DP1, not in the term it is due. The mark is largely decided by the research question: one with too little chemistry, or with variables a school laboratory cannot measure properly, cannot reach the higher bands however well it is written. Four early sessions cover the criteria, question choice, honest uncertainty treatment and how to evaluate a method's limits. That is especially worth doing in this district, where households travel often and a fortnight lost from a late investigation is fatal where the same fortnight lost early is survivable.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help my child finish the chemistry investigation report?
faqs.answer: Not finish it, no. A tutor may explain the criteria, model method on a different investigation, ask questions about your child's draft and point out where a conclusion is not supported by the data. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or edit to completion any part of it. The test for a parent is the feedback itself: questions your child has to go and answer are correct, sentences they could paste in are not. One page in this search result sells completed Internal Assessments, and the student carries the malpractice finding.

faqs.question: What does Higher Level chemistry tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates, each read on the provider's own page: AED 45 to 65 an hour at EdFlik for budget online tutoring, from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB at Unitors, AED 270 at TutorChase, AED 200 to 450 and above in Bestimate's specialist band, and AED 650 at BartyED's premium tier. In-home one to one is quoted at AED 180 to 500 because the rate carries the drive. None of those is an IB Gram price, and we publish no rate card; the figure for your child comes from the trial lesson conversation.

faqs.question: Is a weekend chemistry lesson better than a weekday one for us?
faqs.answer: If your child is on an Al Mizhar, Al Warqa or Al Khawaneej route, very probably. The comparison is not hour against hour but a rested student against a flattened one, and chemistry's computational work is unusually sensitive to that. A Saturday or Sunday morning lesson leaves weekday evenings for school homework and the short calculation practice, and it is easier to protect through mock windows. The cost is a piece of the weekend, which most long-route families decide is the right trade after a term of trying evenings.

faqs.question: My child is coming from IGCSE Chemistry 0620. What needs building first?
faqs.answer: Three things: mole arithmetic done at speed and without a formula triangle, the language of equilibrium as a dynamic process, and quantitative energetics including Hess cycles with their signs handled correctly. Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 leave students strong on the reactivity series, on ion tests and on standard equations, and short on all three of those. A six-to-ten session block in the summer before DP1 removes most of the first-term shock and costs considerably less than the November remediation block.

faqs.question: Do you provide chemistry past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No. IB subject guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, and reproducing or distributing them is not ours to do. We teach against the course your child is registered for and point you to the official route through the school or the IB's own site. That is the more useful answer as well as the lawful one, because official material is current while a file circulating in a parent group is frequently from a superseded guide and will quietly waste revision time.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor take chemistry and biology for my child?
faqs.answer: Usually we would rather two specialists. Diploma chemistry and Diploma biology are different subjects with different failure modes, and a tutor strong in one is frequently average in the other; the combination tends to be a scheduling convenience rather than a teaching advantage. Where both subjects genuinely need help and the household can only hold one weekly slot, fix the one blocking a university route first, review at six lessons against marks, then decide. Splitting a single hour between two sciences moves neither.

faqs.answer: Four things. The level, Standard or Higher. How far the school has reached through Structure and Reactivity. A photograph of a marked test or mock, which shows a specialist the pattern faster than any description. And the time your child is realistically through the door on a bad traffic afternoon, which sets the slot. We do not need a photograph of your child or a full grade history; UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 governs what is held and the privacy link explains it.
